 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Cayetano said several people had approached him, claiming they felt caught in the middle of the pressure.

He alleged that Lacson, his staff and lawyers associated with them had prepared affidavits and were pressuring some contractors to sign the documents.

He did not identify the contractors.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

“If there is nothing wrong, why would you sign? They are being threatened, and there are consequences,” Cayetano said.

“Not everyone has the courage, stamina, patience or guts to stand up for what is right, especially when going up against very high-ranking officials in this highly charged atmosphere. But having said that, how can our country change?” he added.

The senator linked the dispute to the broader investigations into alleged irregularities in government infrastructure and flood control projects.

Cayetano cited Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon, who earlier said that there were no ghost projects in the Laguna Lakeshore area of Taguig.

*   ![Image 2: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

He also questioned the activities of the Laguna Lake Development Authority and the Public Reclamation Authority in areas along the lake in Rizal and Laguna, contrasting them with projects in Taguig.

Cayetano urged government personnel involved in the controversy to focus on evidence and their responsibilities rather than take sides.

“This is not about following Senator Lacson or Senator Alan. No. Do what is right,” he said.

Lacson has yet to respond to Cayetano’s latest allegations.

*   ![Image 3: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

In an earlier statement, Lacson said anomalies he found in flood control projects last year prompted him to dig deeper, eventually leading him to deliver two privilege speeches on alleged corruption involving projects in Bulacan and Oriental Mindoro.

As chairman of the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee at the time, Lacson said hearings uncovered additional evidence that eventually led to cases against several individuals.

He said he would continue to answer Cayetano’s allegations with documents and other evidence.

“I’m just responding. Whenever he speaks, I respond with the receipts," he said.

title: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’
summary: THE House prosecution on Friday questioned Vice President Sara Duterte’s public image of simple living as its final witness presented financial findings that included P11.35 million in checks allegedly paid to her dentist and estimated P817
content:
THE House prosecution on Friday questioned Vice President Sara Duterte’s public image of simple living as its final witness presented financial findings that included P11.35 million in checks allegedly paid to her dentist and estimated P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income.

Financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera, a certified public accountant and lawyer, estimated that Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, had P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income from 2022 to 2025.

Among the transactions highlighted in Cabrera’s report were check payments totaling P11.35 million to Lourdes Lebosada, identified during the hearing as Duterte’s dentist.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

He also flagged P299,142 in Nike purchases at SM Davao Annex in a single day.

The prosecution said Cabrera tied together bank records, statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALNs), corporate filings and audited financial statements to support its allegations under Article II of the impeachment complaint, which covers unexplained wealth, inaccurate financial declarations and prohibited business interests.

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

House prosecutor and Bicol Saro Party-list Rep. Terry Ridon pointed to the gap between Cabrera’s estimate and Duterte’s declared net worth of about P98 million.

“I think the numbers are staggering today. More than P800 million in supposed unexplained wealth, as stated by the expert witness, against a SALN of P98 million,” Ridon said.

The financial findings have renewed scrutiny of the Duterte family’s public image of living like ordinary Filipinos.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

House prosecution spokesperson Ace Barbers earlier questioned that image, citing the family’s portrayal of sleeping under mosquito nets and eating at roadside eateries.

“But now, there are financial records that need to be explained. The image is no longer enough. The documents must speak,” Barbers said.

In a statement Friday after the prosecution concluded its presentation, Barbers expressed confidence that the evidence could support Duterte’s conviction.

“We’re confident that the evidence that we presented in the impeachment court will perhaps merit a conviction,” he said.

*   ![Image 2: Dunning-Kruger effect in PH government](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Dunning-Kruger effect in PH government](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/dunning-kruger-effect-in-ph-government/2442749)

**Remarkable clarity**

Senator-Judge Panfilo Lacson on Saturday praised House prosecutor Chel Diokno for presenting the alleged unexplained wealth of Vice President Duterte with “remarkable clarity, precision, and coherence,” but emphasized that the prosecution’s financial evidence remains open to challenge by the defense.

Lacson said the prosecution appeared to have connected the key issues under Article II of the impeachment complaint, which accuses Duterte of unexplained wealth, while emphasizing that the Senate impeachment court must withhold judgment until the defense has had an opportunity to scrutinize the testimony of prosecution expert witness Alexander Cabrera.

“Without intending to prejudge the outcome, and subject to any convincing rebuttal the defense may present during the cross-examination of prosecution expert witness Alexander B. Cabrera, congressman Chel Diokno appears to have tied up the issues under Article II (Unexplained Wealth) with remarkable clarity, precision, and coherence,” Lacson said in a post on X.

*   ![Image 3: Parts of Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite to have water interruptions this week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254622.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Parts of Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite to have water interruptions this week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/parts-of-metro-manila-rizal-cavite-to-have-water-interruptions-this-week/2443226)

Diokno questioned Cabrera during Friday’s proceedings, focusing on the financial analysis presented by the prosecution to support its allegations against the vice president.

Cabrera’s testimony, however, has yet to undergo cross-examination, which is expected to begin next week.

Lacson said the defense must be given a full opportunity to challenge the expert’s findings, test the assumptions behind his analysis and expose any weaknesses that could affect the prosecution’s case.

While expressing respect for Cabrera and his professional credentials, Lacson said he would not treat the expert’s testimony as conclusive before hearing the defense’s arguments and any countervailing evidence.

He also pointed out that the defense could present its own expert witness and financial analysis, leaving the senator-judges to determine which side has the more convincing evidence.

“After the defense has its chance to present its own expert and analysis, we as senator-judges will weigh which of the testimonies are more meritorious,” Lacson said.

The next phase of the proceedings will be crucial in determining whether the prosecution’s financial analysis can withstand scrutiny from the defense.

Public prosecutor Rep. Terry Ridon said that after the defense completes its cross-examination of Cabrera, followed by any re-direct examination and re-cross-examination, the prosecution will offer its evidence to the impeachment court.

During Friday’s hearing, Lacson also made light of the presentation, joking that both Diokno and Cabrera had voices suited for FM radio.

He added that he did not feel sleepy during their exchanges.

The lighthearted remark notwithstanding, Lacson’s assessment underscored the distinction between the prosecution’s presentation and the court’s ultimate evaluation of the evidence.

As senator-judges, Lacson and his colleagues must assess the competing claims and supporting evidence before deciding whether the allegations against Duterte have been established under the impeachment process.

The defense’s forthcoming cross-examination of Cabrera is expected to test the foundation of the prosecution’s unexplained wealth allegations and provide the impeachment court with a clearer basis for evaluating the competing financial analyses.

**Review of anti-graft laws**

House prosecution lead counsel Gerville Luistro on Saturday called for a review of the country’s anti-graft, tax, money laundering and procurement laws following impeachment trial findings of about P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income involving Duterte and her husband.

The Batangas 2nd District representative said Congress should determine whether existing laws need amendments or stricter enforcement to address possible financial misconduct and conflicts of interest involving public officials.

“We need to revisit, if not amend, laws such as the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, or Republic Act 3019; the Anti-Money Laundering Act; the Procurement Law; Republic Act 6713, or the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees; and perhaps include the Securities Regulation Act and Commission on Audit rules,” Luistro said at the Saturday News Forum in Quezon City.

The House Committee on Justice chairman made the observation after 37 days of impeachment proceedings against Duterte, whose trial includes allegations of unexplained wealth under Article II of the impeachment complaint.

Luistro questioned why no tax evasion complaints had been filed despite financial discrepancies presented by prosecution forensic expert Alexander Cabrera.

“I find it strange. Why has no tax evasion case been filed?” she said.

She cited P101 million in allegedly undeclared personal income, P142 million involving Cale88 Foods Corp. and Metro City Chow Food Corp., and P212 million involving GenCorp Industries Inc. The companies were linked to Duterte and Carpio in the prosecution’s presentation.

“The amount is substantial. Have we filed a tax evasion case? Have we reached the threshold?” Luistro asked.

She said lawmakers should examine the National Internal Revenue Code to determine whether clearer guidelines are needed to investigate potential tax violations.

Luistro also called for stronger coordination among the Bureau of Internal Revenue, the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), the Office of the Ombudsman and the Department of Justice when financial investigations uncover possible offenses.

She said the AMLC’s responsibilities should be clarified, particularly regarding when financial findings warrant complaints or referrals to prosecutors.

Beyond the financial discrepancies, Luistro questioned 19 Davao City government contracts worth about P34 million awarded to GenCorp, in which Duterte allegedly declared a business interest. The city government was headed by her brother, Mayor Sebastian Duterte.

“We saw during the presentation of evidence that Vice President Duterte declared a business interest in GenCorp. But look what happened: 19 contracts worth around P34 million were awarded by none other than the Davao City government, headed by her own brother,” Luistro said.

She also raised discrepancies between Duterte’s statements of assets, liabilities and net worth and GenCorp’s corporate filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Luistro said Congress should review safeguards under RA 12009, or the New Government Procurement Act, to prevent conflicts of interest in government contracts.

She also sought clearer SALN disclosure guidelines under RA 6713 and a review of securities regulations and Commission on Audit rules.

Cabrera testified Friday that his analysis identified about P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income involving Duterte and Carpio from 2022 to 2025.

The prosecution presented the findings to support its allegations of unexplained wealth.

Luistro said, however, that the problem may lie not in the absence of laws but in their implementation.

“Implementation may be what is lacking. The laws may be sufficient, but implementation is what is lacking,” she said.

title: 《坚不可摧》感動德國藝術家：自由需共同捍衛

content:
【大紀元2026年10月11日訊】（大紀元記者王亦笑德國多特蒙德報導）當純善純美的藝術面臨強權的跨國威脅，神韻藝術家選擇用勇氣與堅韌照亮世界。2026 年 10 月 9 日（週五）晚，揭示中共對神韻藝術團進行跨國鎮壓的紀錄片《堅不可摧》（Unbroken: The Untold Story of Shen Yun）在德國多特蒙德（Dortmund）著名的 Schauburg 電影院放映。

這部震撼人心的影片吸引了不少多特蒙德藝術界人士前來觀看，他們都對中國傳統文化以及真正的藝術非常感興趣。在隨後的座談會上，一位神韻演員與其父母，還有一位神韻主持人與現場觀眾驚喜連線。神韻演員分享了他們的訓練日常，並講述在逆境中復興傳統文化的不凡經歷。

這種無懼打壓、堅守使命的精神，引發了在場觀眾對維護人權與信仰自由的強烈反響，許多觀眾表示今晚的經歷讓他們深受啟發，「自由並非理所當然，無論何時何地都需要大家共同捍衛和守護。」還有的觀眾感謝神韻演員的付出並認為，「在謊言與暴力的陰影下，真理與藝術的力量更顯耀眼。」

### 視覺藝術家：這部影片對德國觀眾同樣重要

[![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867757-Unbroken_Dortmund_20261009-0014-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867757-Unbroken_Dortmund_20261009-0014.jpg)

2026年10月9日晚，紀錄片《堅不可摧》在多特蒙德的Schauburg電影院放映。（張清颻/大紀元）

當晚，德國視覺藝術家伊姆加德·曼茨（Irmgard Manz）和朋友、小提琴演奏者弗洛里安（Florian W.）及其母親伊姆特勞特（Irmtraut W.）一起觀看了影片《堅不可摧》，他們都非常感動。

伊姆加德·曼茨是德國北部多個重要藝術家協會的成員，她的個人展覽也受到媒體和觀眾的好評。她表示，「這樣的影片非常重要，應該多多放映，讓更多的人看到。」

一同來觀看影片的朋友、小提琴演奏者弗洛里安（Florian W.）認同道，「是的，這非常重要，也希望該影片能在更多電影院放映，甚至如果可能的話，做一些相關活動讓更多人知道這個影片。」

弗洛里安的母親、對中醫頗有研究的 Irmtraut W.也表示，「這部影片非常有啟發性，對我們很有幫助，因為我們之前並沒有注意到這些情況。現在我們也明白了，這些針對這些舞蹈演員的操作背後的動機是什麼。我還想對他們進一步了解。」

弗洛里安補充說，「影片太棒了，非常好，內容很豐富。而且，能夠聽到來自該藝術團體如此多樣且直接的聲音，這一點非常重要。因為如今在媒體上，報導往往非常失真，正如我們對許多話題所了解的那樣。」

曼茨強調，這部影片對德國觀眾同樣重要，「因為我們也面臨類似的問題，只是不太為人所知。而且，得知美國國內有此類調查揭露了這些問題，這也很有啟發性，這一點非常重要。」

通過此次座談會，曼茨還了解到由於中共的施壓，導致很多德國的劇院無法上演神韻，也包括 多特蒙德劇院在內。她對此感到震驚，「多特蒙德劇院竟然會屈服於（中共的）威懾，這讓我感到震驚。我沒想到竟然會這樣，我不敢相信他們會這麼做。」

他們都認為，自由並非理所當然，需要大家來共同捍衛。曼茨說，「我們現在也正親眼目睹，在民主體制內部，一些我們根本不希望看到的力量正在蔓延，實際上我們所有人都面臨著這種現象的威脅。」

影片中呈現了紐約時報如何針對神韻炮製虛假新聞，曼茨表示，「德國也面臨同樣的問題。有很多媒體，它們為虛假信息和假新聞提供了太多傳播途徑。操縱！操縱的可能性已經大大增加。還有誹謗，以及污名化。」

她強調，「我們認為這是我們社會的一個根本性問題。」

弗洛里安馬上說，「但這部影片（《堅不可摧》）給了大家勇氣，這次活動也鼓舞人們重新團結起來，共同抵制虛假信息並傳播正確信息。」

作為小提琴演奏者，弗洛里安對神韻藝術家所展現的藝術表達深感共鳴，「他們通過藝術向人們傳遞美好的信息和生活的真諦，這是一件很美妙的事。他們通過美妙的方式在舞台上傳達這些內容，這樣既全面又直抵人心。」

同樣從事藝術行業的曼茨馬上說，「是的，這 在電影裡表現得非常有說服力。我從（神韻）舞蹈演員身上感受到，這確實是一種發自內心的表達，是的，這非常美妙！」

他們都表示一定會去觀看神韻演出的。弗洛里安希望把祝福送給神韻演員，「請繼續、繼續、繼續這樣做下去，保持這份初心，永遠充滿勇氣、充滿喜悅、充滿信心。只要真誠且發自內心，就會受到庇佑，一切都會順利。始終懷著美好的信念，事情自然也會順利。懷著純淨的心，觀眾也能感受到的。是的，這（神韻）就是最大的禮物。」

### 前芭蕾舞演員：真正的藝術如同信仰一樣

[![Image 2](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867759-Unbroken_Dortmund_20261009-0016-e1791688516335.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867759-Unbroken_Dortmund_20261009-0016-e1791688516335.jpg)

前芭蕾舞演員Tatjana Mironova。（張清颻/大紀元）

從事醫藥行業的塔季揚娜·米羅諾娃（Tatjana Mironova）觀看《堅不可摧》後對神韻藝術家非常欽佩，她表示，「我完全明白這是怎麼回事，我自己也曾是一名舞蹈演員，曾在俄羅斯芭蕾舞團跳舞，而且我來自吉爾吉斯斯坦。」

吉爾吉斯斯坦是前蘇聯的加盟國之一，1991年 蘇聯解體後才 獨立，同樣經歷過共產主義獨裁統治的米羅諾娃表示，「我很清楚影片所講述的意味著什麼。文化是相當重要的，但當（共產主義）政權主導一切時，它們（獨裁者）自然會向文化界人士施壓。」

「中國走的也是前蘇聯的路，蘇聯已經解體 30 年了。誰知道中國還要持續多久？共產主義政權會慢慢瓦解的！只是也許中國人更加能夠忍耐。」她說，「（由於中共的禁錮）中國人就像生活在飼養箱裡一樣，這意味著他們過著截然不同的人生。但我注意到，中國人已經做好了（爭取自由的）準備。」

最後，米羅諾娃表達了自己對神韻藝術家的敬意，「我也曾是舞蹈演員，我知道這是多麼辛苦的工作。請繼續堅持下去，因為藝術，真正的藝術如同信仰一樣，這是一項艱辛的內心修行，堅持走下去的人，終將開闢出一條道路！」

### 前程序開發員：紐約時報的操作讓人感到震驚

烏蘇拉·君特（Ursula Günther）退休前是位程序開發員，但她一直對中國傳統文化和芭蕾舞很感興趣，所以看到影片《堅不可摧》的介紹，她馬上決定要來觀看。看過後她表示自己的心情非常複雜，很感動，但也很震驚。

君特說，「影片非常感人，而且讓人了解到東方文化、冥想修煉和不同的生活方式，我感到很受啟發。」

「但我也感到震驚，同時也產生一個疑問。」她說，「紐約時報究竟擁有怎樣的權力，竟能撰寫並發表這樣的宣傳文章，去詆毀這些舞蹈演員。」

她搖搖頭說，「我得說，如今這（不實報導）幾乎成了常態，但一家如此世界聞名的報紙竟做出這種事，還是讓人感到震驚！」

能夠通過影片了解到中共跨國鎮壓的種種行徑，君特認為這特別重要，對於德國人也意義重大。「這絕對很重要，無論世界上的哪個角落，我們都應該更加警惕背後發生的事情。像這樣的電影，確實有助於引起人們對人權問題的關注。」

最後，君特也表達了自己想要觀看神韻演出的願望，「非常感謝讓我們有機會了解這一切，我會關注的，找個機會一定要完整地觀看（神韻演出）。」

### 神韻觀眾：影片讓我更加了解神韻藝術家

[![Image 3](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867774-Unbroken_Dortmund_20261009-0034-e1791689040427.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867774-Unbroken_Dortmund_20261009-0034-e1791689040427.jpg)

斯特凡·罗斯（Stefan Rose）曾在法蘭克福觀看過神韻演出。（張清颻）

斯特凡·羅斯（Stefan Rose）曾經觀看過神韻演出，至今都感到震撼。「幾年前，我曾在法蘭克福看過神韻演出，哇，那真是讓我大開眼界，至今難忘！」他說，「現在了解到這些藝術家曾面臨什麼樣的困境，真的心情複雜。我認為這部影片非常有意義，還了解到中共政府試圖通過什麼手段來取締這種信仰（法輪功），這其實才是關鍵所在。」

當晚，羅斯偕女友和幾個朋友一起來觀看影片《堅不可摧》，他們都深受觸動。羅斯的女友說，「對我來說，這非常發人深省，我覺得非常非常引人入勝。發生的這一切（中共的跨國鎮壓）非常令人悲傷，中國發生的事情讓我感到非常難過。我簡直無言以對。我覺得了解這些非常非常重要。我也想進一步了解情況。我還很想觀看一下神韻演出。」

羅斯的朋友也表示，「我眼含熱淚看完了影片，深受感動，也深受觸動。我肯定會向別人推薦這部電影，是的，希望儘可能多的人能看這部影片，也希望德國的記者們能看到。」

他強調，「因為人們正在遭受苦難並被殺害，不幸的是，這發生在中國，太可怕了。那（中共）不是一個政府，而是一個政權，一個恐怖政權。而且，這是人類歷史上最惡劣的政權，遺憾的是事實確實如此。我們德國也曾有過非常惡劣的政權，但中國的政權（中共）要糟糕得多。因為納粹時期，相對來說時間很短，但中國的政權已經持續了很長時間，長達數十年之久。他們有這麼長的時間去破壞、殺戮並摧毀文化。這當然非常、非常令人悲痛。」

羅斯還非常想對神韻藝術家說，「你們的表演獨一無二，請繼續保持，你們的初衷非常了不起，我覺得這太了不起了。不要被那些試圖打壓你們的人影響。」他的女友也補充說，「他們（神韻藝術家）傳達的信息非常美好。」

責任編輯：周仁

title: Over 28,000 villages declared stable, peaceful — NTF-Elcac
summary: **MANILA, Philippines —**A total of 28,415 barangay (villages) in 60 provinces have been declared under Stable Internal Peace and Security (SIPS), reflecting the government’s efforts to curb communist insurgency and expand development in co
content:
**MANILA, Philippines —**A total of 28,415 barangay (villages) in 60 provinces have been declared under Stable Internal Peace and Security (SIPS), reflecting the government’s efforts to curb communist insurgency and expand development in conflict-affected communities, the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-Elcac) said.

NTF-ELCAC Deputy Director for Operations Rodrigo “Rhod” Lutao presented the figures during the Major Island Group Action Planning Workshop for Mindanao, where he reported on the implementation of the National Action Plan for Unity, Peace and Development (NAP-UPD).

The workshop brought together government communicators and partners from Regions 9, 10, 11 and 12, the Caraga region and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

*   [‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

The task force said 21,614 barangay in 45 provinces are covered by SIPS declarations that have attained the status while 6,801 villages in 15 provinces are covered by provincial SIPS declarations in regions still working toward full regional coverage.

The NTF-Elcac said the figures reflect a shrinking area of communist armed influence and a transition toward civilian governance, peaceful political participation and development.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The task force previously described the spread of SIPS as a “historic rejection” of the Communist Party of the Philippines–New People’s Army–National Democratic Front of the Philippines violence, pointing to communities emerging from decades of insurgency and choosing to secure peace.

The transformation accelerated in 2026, with SIPS milestones in Central Luzon, Cagayan Valley, Calabarzon, Western Visayas, Caraga and the Cordillera Administrative Region.

These declarations add to earlier gains and demonstrate that the reduction of communist armed influence is no longer confined to individual barangay or provinces but, in many areas, encompasses entire regions.

*   ![Image 1: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

Lutao said that the expanding SIPS map cannot be separated from the government's development offensive in communities previously affected by armed conflict.

As of Sept. 29, the Barangay Development Program (BDP) has reached 5,638 formerly conflict-affected villages, backed by P44.90 billion in development investments benefiting an estimated 16.03 million Filipinos.

These investments, he said, have translated into concrete interventions on the ground: 955 classrooms, 1,587.02 kilometers of farm-to-market roads, 23,681 streetlights, 1,169 water and sanitation systems, 9,264 electrification projects, and 547 health and medical stations.

The government has sustained that approach in 2026, with P8.08 billion appropriated for projects in 808 cleared barangay, including roads, schools, water systems, health stations and electrification.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The government is seeking to consolidate peace by bringing roads, electricity, potable water, education, health services, livelihoods and economic opportunities into communities previously vulnerable to conflict.

The decline of the armed movement is also reflected in the number of individuals leaving it.

Lutao said that 50,907 individuals surrendered to authorities from 2019 to 2025, while P984 million in assistance was extended under the Enhanced Comprehensive Local Integration Program (E-CLIP), covering 33,627 immediate, livelihood and firearms-remuneration grants to former rebels.

He also reported 13,647 amnesty applications, alongside the formation of 4,008 people's organizations and the establishment of the Buklod Kapayapaan Federation.

*   ![Image 3: Lacson threatening contractors with plunder charges — Cayetano](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254606.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson threatening contractors with plunder charges — Cayetano](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/lacson-threatening-contractors-with-plunder-charges-cayetano/2443221)

These initiatives, Lutao said, form part of the broader transition from armed conflict toward reintegration, community participation and peaceful development.

Assistant Director General Cornelio H. Valencia Jr., co-chairman of the NTF-Elcac Strategic Communications Cluster, said these gains must now be translated into messages and programs that communities themselves understand and advance.

“Anchored on ‘One message, many voices,’ we will craft plans responsive to local realities — while advancing our shared goals of unity, peace, and development,” Valencia said. “Mindanao is diverse — no single approach fits every area. Our communications must be locally relevant yet anchored on a shared national direction.”

The Strategic Communications Cluster has developed a comprehensive communication plan aligned with NAP-UPD to ensure that national policy is translated into locally meaningful action.

Lutao identified three priorities moving forward: intensifying efforts against the remaining armed threat and expanding SIPS coverage; sustaining BDP gains in roads, classrooms, water systems, electrification and livelihoods while addressing the requirements of communities still affected by conflict; and strengthening accountability through the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning or MEAL Framework.

The Task Force is carrying these gains into its revitalized “Build Peace Better” identity under NAP-UPD, centered on Unity, Peace and Development.

The objective, officials said, is no longer merely to clear communities of armed insurgency, but to make the resulting peace durable by ensuring government presence, responsive institutions and visible development.

content:
【大紀元2026年10月10日訊】（大紀元記者王麗飛紐約報導）青天白日滿地紅旗迎風飄揚，曼哈頓華埠洋溢著喜慶氣氛。10月10日，中華民國迎來115年雙十國慶，來自紐約華埠、法拉盛及新澤西州的各大僑團與僑胞齊聚華埠，以中華公所為中心，舉行升旗、獻花、國慶大會及愛國大遊行，紀念辛亥革命，弘揚民主共和精神，延續海外僑界百餘年的國慶傳統。

[![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867731-195053.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867731-195053.jpg)

10月10日，曼哈頓華埠中華公所大樓前舞獅助興，歡慶中華民國115年雙十國慶。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 2](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867745-195077.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867745-195077.jpg)

10月10日，紐約中華公所門前舉行雙十國慶升旗儀式。（王麗飛/大紀元）

中華公所外牆懸掛著「平等、博愛、正義、和平」及「民主、自由、人權、法治」兩幅醒目標語，中央高懸「中華民國萬歲」條幅，與街頭飄揚的青天白日滿地紅旗相互映襯，格外醒目。

下午1時30分，駐紐約台北經濟文化辦事處處長李志強、中華公所主席伍銳賢率領各大僑團代表及僑胞，在中華公所門前參加升旗典禮。當《中華民國國歌》響起，眾人肅立，注視著青天白日滿地紅旗徐徐升起，在曼哈頓上空迎風飄揚，現場氣氛莊嚴。

升旗儀式結束後，僑界代表前往哥倫布公園，向國父孫中山銅像獻花致敬，緬懷革命先賢。

[![Image 3](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867742-195074.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867742-195074.jpg)

10月10日，紐約僑界代表在華埠哥倫布公園孫中山銅像前合影留念。（王麗飛/大紀元）

[![Image 4](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867743-195075.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867743-195075.jpg)

10月10日，僑界代表在華埠哥倫布公園向孫中山銅像獻花致敬。（王麗飛/大紀元）

下午2時，國慶慶祝大會在中華公所中山紀念大禮堂舉行。典禮在美國與中華民國兩國國歌聲中揭開序幕，各僑團代表齊聚一堂，共慶雙十國慶。

[![Image 5](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867740-195072.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867740-195072.jpg)

10月10日，駐紐約台北經文處處長李志強在中華民國115年雙十國慶慶祝大會上致詞。（王麗飛/大紀元）

[![Image 6](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867741-195073.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867741-195073.jpg)

10月10日，紐約中華公所主席伍銳賢在中華民國115年雙十國慶慶祝大會上致詞。（王麗飛/大紀元）

中華公所主席伍銳賢致詞時回顧紐約華僑支持辛亥革命的歷史，指出海外華僑在中華民國創建過程中扮演重要角色。他表示，中華公所長年堅持舉辦升旗、獻花及國慶遊行，不僅是慶祝國慶，更是為了傳承歷史、紀念先賢。

駐紐約經文處處長李志強接受本報採訪時表示，這已是他今年參加的第五場國慶活動，先後走訪王后區、新澤西州及雪城等地，對各地僑胞持續舉辦慶祝活動深受感動。

「海外僑胞的支持，其實是中華民國最大的動力。」李志強感謝僑胞多年來的熱情與付出，並表示駐紐約經文處將繼續與中華公所及各大僑團合作，為僑胞提供更好的服務。

下午4時30分，國慶愛國大遊行登場。隊伍沿華埠街道前進，青天白日滿地紅旗隨隊飄揚，鑼鼓聲與歡呼聲此起彼落，將節日氣氛推向高潮。

[![Image 7](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867739-195068.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867739-195068.jpg)

2026年10月10日，紐約中華公所主辦中華民國115年雙十國慶大遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 8](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867736-195060.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867736-195060.jpg)

美東聯成公所參加雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 9](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867737-195062.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867737-195062.jpg)

10月10日，紐約台北經濟文化辦事處代表參加曼哈頓華埠雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 10](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867733-195056.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867733-195056.jpg)

10月10日，紐約開平同鄉會成員參加曼哈頓華埠雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 11](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867734-195058.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867734-195058.jpg)

10月10日，美國紐約華人退伍軍人會參加雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 12](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867735-195059.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867735-195059.jpg)

10月10日，朱超然南北醒獅隊伍參加雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 13](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867732-195054.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867732-195054.jpg)

10月10日，紐約華僑學校師生參加曼哈頓華埠雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 14](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867729-195047.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867729-195047.jpg)

10月10日，王后區115年國慶籌備委員會成員參加曼哈頓華埠雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

[![Image 15](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867728-195046.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867728-195046.jpg)

10月10日，大紐約區僑界急難救助協會成員參加曼哈頓華埠雙十國慶遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

對許多老僑胞而言，雙十國慶不僅是節日，更是延續數十年的情感與記憶。

來美52年的台灣僑胞馬佩華表示，今年是她第51次參加華埠雙十國慶，半個多世紀以來僅缺席過一次。她出生於上海，童年時隨家人輾轉香港、台灣，大學畢業後與丈夫移居美國。今年原本打算獨自前來，沒想到兒女和孫子也一同參加，讓這場國慶多了一份三代同堂的溫馨。

[![Image 16](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867748-195080.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867748-195080.jpg)

10月10日，台灣僑胞馬佩華手持青天白日滿地紅旗，參加華埠雙十國慶慶祝活動。（王麗飛/大紀元）

中華民國僑務委員褚月梅參加華埠雙十國慶已有二、三十年。她認為，近年台灣經濟發展及國際能見度不斷提升，而中華公所長年升掛中華民國國旗，更具有特殊的象徵意義。

[![Image 17](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867746-195078.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867746-195078.jpg)

僑務委員楮月梅。（王麗飛/大紀元）

「中華民國的國旗不只在國慶這一天飄揚，而是一年365天都在這裡飄揚。」她說，雖然僑胞身在紐約，但對中華民國的情感始終難以割捨，希望民主、自由的理念及雙十國慶傳統能夠代代相傳。

新州北部美華聯誼會前會長俞莉萍也帶領會員參加慶祝活動。她表示，每年唱起中華民國國歌和國旗歌，總會感動得熱淚盈眶。「我們以這面漂亮的國旗為榮。」她說，能與各地僑胞共同慶祝國慶，感到格外興奮。

[![Image 18](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867744-195076.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867744-195076.jpg)

新州北部美華聯誼會前會長俞莉萍（左一）帶領會員參加慶祝活動。（王麗飛/大紀元）

除了長年參與的老僑胞，今年也有來自中國大陸的新移民加入慶祝行列。

2023年來美的朱國輝，今年首次參加華埠雙十國慶，「我們這些從中國大陸來的人，能夠站在這裡參加雙十國慶活動，真的非常難得。」他表示，能夠公開參與慶祝活動令他感到榮幸，也希望中國大陸民眾未來能享有民主、自由及基本權利保障。

[![Image 19](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867747-195079.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867747-195079.jpg)

來自大陸的朱國輝，今年首次參加華埠雙十國慶。（王麗飛/大紀元）

同樣於2023年來美、來自山東煙台的王莉，今年第二次參加華埠雙十國慶。她自述，過去在中國大陸參與關懷抗戰國軍老兵、記錄老兵歷史的公益活動時曾受到打壓，微信群及社交媒體帳號也多次遭封禁。

王莉說，來到美國後，終於能夠公開表達自己的理念。對她而言，參加雙十國慶不僅是慶祝中華民國的生日，也是表達對民主、自由的嚮往。她希望中國大陸未來也能實行民主選舉，保障人民的言論自由。

[![Image 20](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867738-195067.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867738-195067.jpg)

2026年10月10日，紐約中華公所主辦中華民國115年雙十國慶大遊行。（戴兵／大紀元）

國慶系列活動當晚還安排聯歡餐會。從莊嚴的升旗典禮到熱鬧的街頭遊行，從連續參加半個世紀的老僑胞到首次到場的新移民，不同世代的人們在這一天相聚紐約華埠，共同見證青天白日滿地紅旗再次升起，也讓延續百餘年的中華民國雙十國慶傳統增添新的記憶。

title: Park service could remove more than 500 trees at historic golf course Trump wants to redesign
summary: **WASHINGTON** — The National Park Service has begun a new round of tree-cutting at a historic golf course near the National Mall as the Trump administration proceeds with a plan to renovate the East Potomac Golf Links into a championship-l
content:
**WASHINGTON** — The National Park Service has begun a new round of tree-cutting at a historic golf course near the National Mall as the Trump administration proceeds with a plan to renovate the East Potomac Golf Links into a championship-level course.

More than 500 trees "that do not contribute to the historic landscape will be removed" as part of the rehabilitation project, the National Park Service said in a court filing Friday. "No healthy trees that are contributing features of the historical golf course" — including historic cherry trees — will be removed as part of the project, the park service said.

A total of 169 trees will be removed starting Saturday, with another 90 trees slated for removal later, the agency said.

*   [A tiger kills a man who entered the big cat enclosure at an English wildlife park](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/americas-emea/a-tiger-kills-a-man-who-entered-the-big-cat-enclosure-at-an-english-wildlife-park/2443214)

The tree removals come as President Donald Trump has moved to turn the course into a world-class golf venue — part of his grand vision for Washington, D.C., where he has torn down storied structures, remade or renamed others and deployed the National Guard for more than a year.

Some residents fear the planned changes to the golf course — where Trump has visited with a cabinet member, a well-known golf course architect and blueprints — risk altering the character of a place that has served Washingtonians of all income levels for more than a century. Turning the park into an upscale golf course will mean costlier fees and a likely loss of public space.

The National Park Service confirmed in a filing they had marked over 500 trees for removal as the Trump Administration mulls over a renovation for the golf course. Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Aaron Schwartz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP)

"The National Park Service is finally implementing a 7-year-old plan to address tree overgrowth at East Potomac Golf Course,'' the Interior Department said in a statement Saturday. The department oversees the park service and other agencies that manage federal lands.

*   ![Image 2: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

The renovation work will include selective tree and vegetation work to restore the course, the Interior Department said, adding that the work is intended to "help restore the course's historic character and reopen views toward landmarks, including the Washington Monument, National War College, Potomac River and Washington Channel."

The park service "recognizes the importance of trees to the park and its visitors. This carefully planned work is part of our required stewardship of the park," the statement said.

The golf course will remain open to the public throughout the renovation effort, although individual holes may temporarily close while work is underway, the agency said.

The 106-year-old public course has been embroiled in a lawsuit since February. Plaintiffs including the DC Preservation League say the Trump administration's reconstruction would violate the congressional act that created the park in 1897. The group sought an emergency stop-work order this spring because of concerns that work was expected to begin immediately on the course.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Charles Birnbaum, president of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, a nonprofit that is suing the Trump administration over renovations at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, said the tree removal at the golf course should be subject to review under the National Historic Preservation Act.

"The work is not routine maintenance, and therefore, for a designated property, they need to undertake Section 106," Birnbaum said Saturday, referring to the section of the preservation law that requires federal agencies to consider a project's effects on historic and cultural properties.

Trump, an avid golfer, has posted about the course on social media: "When completed, this Course will have the ability to host Major Golf Tournaments, including The U.S. Open, The Ryder Cup, The PGA Championship, and other top PGA Tour events," he wrote in late June.

It's unclear when the course could host any major tournaments, as locations are chosen several years ahead of the events.

title: Pope Leo declares death penalty 'inadmissible' as his native US plans to livestream execution
summary: **ROME**— Pope Leo XIV on Saturday declared capital punishment ''inadmissible" as he marked the World Day Against the Death Penalty and his native United States announced plans to livestream an execution by firing squad. In a post on X, the
content:
**ROME**— Pope Leo XIV on Saturday declared capital punishment ''inadmissible" as he marked the World Day Against the Death Penalty and his native United States announced plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.

In a post on X, the American pope quoted the revised Catholic teaching on capital punishment ushered in by Pope Francis that the death penalty attacks the inherent dignity of a human being.

"The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment," read the post under Leo's official handle, @Pontifex. "Effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption."

*   [Christa Pike is discharged from a hospital after surviving execution attempt, her attorneys say](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/americas-emea/christa-pike-is-discharged-from-a-hospital-after-surviving-execution-attempt-her-attorneys-say/2443219)

The post ended with the hashtag #NoDeathPenalty.

The U.S. Defense Department announced Thursday that the firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of a 2009 shooting at the Fort Hood military base, will be livestreamed. Hasan, scheduled to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others.

U.S. President Donald Trump said Saturday he would be making a decision ultimately on whether the execution would be livestreamed.

Leo didn't refer specifically to the planned execution, or the botched lethal injection in Tennessee earlier that has revived debate over the death penalty in the United States. Saturday is World Day Against the Death Penalty, and it is common for the pope's official social media accounts to post messages marking such commemorations.

*   ![Image 1: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

[![Image 2: Pope Leo XIV arrives to celebrate a mass in St. Peter's Basilica at the Vatican, Thursday, Oct.8, 2026, for the annual opening of the academic year at pontifical universities, joining Rome's 22 pontifical institutions and numerous others worldwide. (AP Photo/Gregorio Borgia)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254601.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254601.jpg)
Pope Leo XIV arrives to celebrate a mass in St. Peter's Basilica at the Vatican, Thursday, Oct.8, 2026, for the annual opening of the academic year at pontifical universities, joining Rome's 22 pontifical institutions and numerous others worldwide. (AP Photo/Gregorio Borgia)

But Leo's post came just hours after his top deputy, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said explicitly that the planned U.S. public execution was "unacceptable."

Pope Francis declared capital punishment 'inadmissible'

Pope Francis in 2018 amended official Catholic teaching to declare capital punishment "inadmissible" in all circumstances.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Previously, the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the official compendium of church teaching, said the church didn't exclude recourse to capital punishment "if this is the only possible way of effectively defending human lives against the unjust aggressor."

Past popes had upheld that position, though St. John Paul II began urging an end to the practice and stressed that guilty people were just as deserving of dignity as innocent ones.

Like Francis before him, Leo has made visiting prisons a key part of his papal travel in a bid to give a message of hope to inmates and underscore their inherent dignity, that God loves them and that there is always a chance for redemption.

"If any of you fear being abandoned by everyone, know that God will never abandon you, and that the church will stand by your side," Leo told inmates at the notorious Bata prison in Equatorial Guinea during his visit in April. Leo is to visit a prison in Buenos Aires during his upcoming tour through Latin America.

*   ![Image 4: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

Speaking specifically about the United States, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said the planned livestreamed execution was "truly incomprehensible" and "unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle."

"The Church's position is one of total opposition to the death penalty; it is incompatible with human dignity and serves as no deterrent…," Parolin said in comments carried by Vatican News. "It is truly incomprehensible that anyone would want to use this system today — I don't know for what purpose. It is certainly unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle; even if the person is guilty, of course, there are other methods."

The head of the U.S. bishops conference, Archbishop Paul Coakley, expressed "shock" and "great sorrow" at the Pentagon's plans.

"In no way can Hasan's actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered," he said in a statement Friday. "The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people."

title: 12 killed and over 300 hurt in latest attack on Riyadh airport, Saudi authorities say
summary: **CAIRO**— The latest attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital of Riyadh killed 12 people and injured over 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early Sunday, with some in critical condition. A Saudi-led coalition
content:
**CAIRO**— The latest attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital of Riyadh killed 12 people and injured over 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early Sunday, with some in critical condition. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen.

It was the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war, whose fronts have expanded to include the recent surge in fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.

A missile struck a King Khalid International Airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to speak to the media.

*   [A tiger kills a man who entered the big cat enclosure at an English wildlife park](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/americas-emea/a-tiger-kills-a-man-who-entered-the-big-cat-enclosure-at-an-english-wildlife-park/2443214)

The Saudi statement said the dead included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said the injured were being treated at several hospitals.

Footage posted on social media following the attack and analyzed by The Associated Press shows at least one ambulance and another vehicle outside the airport.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

**Trump said he would consider joining strikes against rebels**

The attack — the latest of several in the past week on the airport — is expected to increase Saudi pressure on allies including the United States to provide military support for the kingdom, which has seemingly tried to avoid all-out war with the Houthis.

Shortly after the attack on Saturday afternoon, U.S. President Donald Trump said he was evaluating whether the U.S. should join Saudi strikes against the rebels. "We may. We're going to look at it," he said. "We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."

*   ![Image 1: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

Trump later Saturday said he planned to speak to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and said "what happened in Saudi Arabia is not acceptable." Asked if the U.S. might get involved, Trump responded, "We'll find out."

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged in a social media post that an American citizen had been killed in the attack, which he condemned.

"These reprehensible attacks demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life. They must stop now," he said.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis blamed them for the attack, calling it a "fully-fledged war crime" and vowing a firm response. The airport has no military facilities.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

There was no immediate statement from the rebels, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital.

The Houthis claimed attacks earlier in the week on King Khalid International Airport that killed three Saudis, including a pilot. The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis.

Saudi civil aviation authorities earlier Saturday said airport operations were suspended. The airport had a heavy police presence, with all entrances blocked, and lights around the complex were dimmed. Flights diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the United States, Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport.

Also Saturday, U.S. Central Command said a fighter jet struck and disabled a commercial cargo vessel with a precision munition in the Gulf of Oman, part of U.S. efforts to maintain a naval blockade of Iranian ports. The Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica had departed an Iranian port and did not heed repeated warnings. The ship's crew was unharmed, CENTCOM said.

*   ![Image 3: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

For Iran, the fighting puts pressure on a key US ally

The attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, have rattled markets and the region. And yet the Saudi energy ministry hours after the latest one was still promoting a major international energy conference set to begin in Riyadh on Sunday.

Until recently, the Houthis had been largely on the sidelines of the Iran war. Now the rebels are a way for Tehran to apply pressure on a key U.S. ally.

The Saudis and the Houthis began fighting in 2015 when the kingdom entered Yemen's civil war on behalf of the internationally recognized government. Relative calm after a 2022 ceasefire ended in July when the Houthis resumed attacks, saying the Saudis fired on the Sanaa airport as a plane from Iran was trying to land. That revived anger over the Saudi-led blockade that has largely isolated Houthi-run areas.

Now fighting has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for Yemeni government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea. Those gains gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that is a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

While the Houthis have said they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for the one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked dozens of ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign sharply limited that.

**Saudi Arabia has run low on interceptors, officials say**

Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air defense support to the region, regional officials told the AP last month, with one noting that the U.S. has seen its own stock dwindle during the war with Iran.

Officials have said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive against the Houthis.

On Saturday, Saudi Arabia said its foreign minister and Omani counterpart spoke by phone about the importance of "supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions" in the region. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region.

**Saudi flight disruptions are growing**

The Houthis this week warned global airlines "for the last time" about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theater for their military operations.

Before the latest attack, Air India, FlyDubai, Lufthansa Group and Pakistan International Airlines were among airlines suspending flights to and from Riyadh and other Saudi airports for varying periods.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency had expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis' ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a "greater focus on aviation infrastructure."

The missile and drone attacks and interception efforts "create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft," it said.

Two regional officials said Houthi attacks on the Riyadh airport on Thursday damaged three planes. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to brief the media. The Saudi national carrier said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board.

Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that "filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability."

summary: 【大紀元2026年10月11日訊】（大紀元記者徐曼沅洛杉磯報導）秋高氣爽的10月，好萊塢環球影城旁的山路，青天白日滿地紅的中華民國國旗迎風飄揚，為南加州帶來濃厚的雙十國慶氛圍。駐洛杉磯台北經濟文化辦事處於10月9日（週五）晚間，在洛杉磯環球影城希爾頓酒店（Hilton Los Angeles/Universal City）舉行中華民國115年國慶酒會。約800名美國聯邦國會議員、地方政府官員、多國駐洛杉磯外交使節及僑界代表齊聚一堂共同祝賀，展現出台美關係持續深化與國際社會對台
content:
【大紀元2026年10月11日訊】（大紀元記者徐曼沅洛杉磯報導）秋高氣爽的10月，好萊塢環球影城旁的山路，青天白日滿地紅的中華民國國旗迎風飄揚，為南加州帶來濃厚的雙十國慶氛圍。駐洛杉磯台北經濟文化辦事處於10月9日（週五）晚間，在洛杉磯環球影城希爾頓酒店（Hilton Los Angeles/Universal City）舉行中華民國115年國慶酒會。約800名美國聯邦國會議員、地方政府官員、多國駐洛杉磯外交使節及僑界代表齊聚一堂共同祝賀，展現出台美關係持續深化與國際社會對台灣的堅定支持。

[![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867625-49d1ac8df87fe6a688d76d4d8253517a-600x443.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867625-49d1ac8df87fe6a688d76d4d8253517a.jpg)

2026年10月9日，中華民國國旗迎風飄揚於好萊塢環球影城。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

[![Image 2](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867633-dd075a4aad98caa593c3c00d7a242e37-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867633-dd075a4aad98caa593c3c00d7a242e37.jpg)

2026年10月9日，（左起）駐洛杉磯台北經濟文化辦事處政治組組長方崇宇、處長馬博元伉儷及立陶宛公使銜參贊Agnė Gurevičienė出席雙十國慶酒會。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

駐洛經文處處長馬博元表示，今年適逢美國建國250周年以及台灣首次總統直選30周年；兩地雖然擁有不同的歷史脈絡，卻共享「人民有權決定自身未來」的民主信念。馬博元強調，台灣與美國及國際友人的深厚情誼早已超越傳統外交框架，透過專業人士、觀光、學術及藝術交流，彼此連結日益緊密。去年洛杉磯發生野火期間，台灣人與海外僑胞第一時間伸出援手，支持第一線消防人員與受災家庭，充分展現了堅韌、慷慨與樂於助人的台灣精神。

[![Image 3](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867627-701f7b0023b4a7ab0ec1649121c67c0e-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867627-701f7b0023b4a7ab0ec1649121c67c0e.jpg)

2026年10月9日，駐洛杉磯台北經濟文化辦事處處長馬博元致詞，強調台美共享民主信念。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

馬博元表示，現場來賓雖然來自不同背景，卻都是「台灣隊」（Team Taiwan）的一分子，共同為自由、和平及下一代努力。他並幽默地以「道奇隊加油」（Go Dodgers）向地主隊表達支持，展現融入美國在地文化、與社區建立連結的友好精神。

## 美跨黨派議員發聲：深化經貿合作與維護台灣安全

現場多位美國重量級政要出席致詞，一致盛讚台裔美國人對當地的卓越貢獻，並強調深化台美關係的重要性：

聯邦眾議員趙美心（Judy Chu）祝賀雙十國慶並指出台灣已發展為亞洲重要的經濟力量與民主典範。她表示，台美貿易為加州創造了大量就業機會，未來將積極推動台美自由貿易協定（FTA），並將減輕台美商務人士雙重課稅負擔列為優先議題。

[![Image 4](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867630-b057365e3cac0ef35e603ba834c42f3f-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867630-b057365e3cac0ef35e603ba834c42f3f.jpg)

2026年10月9日，聯邦眾議員趙美心（右）與駐洛杉磯台北經濟文化辦事處處長馬博元伉儷合影。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

聯邦眾議員金映玉（Young Kim）以眾議院外委會東亞及太平洋小組主席身分出席，她強調台灣海峽的安全至關重要，美國國會應持續提供台灣自我防衛所需的工具。金映玉明確表示：「美國對台承諾不僅是因應安全威脅，更因為台灣能為台美關係帶來巨大貢獻，美國與我本人都將持續堅定支持台灣。」

[![Image 5](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867628-1f8d78deb0ebb6f27118510bc490547d-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867628-1f8d78deb0ebb6f27118510bc490547d.jpg)

2026年10月9日，聯邦眾議員金映玉表示，美國對台承諾將持續不變。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

加州州眾議員方樹強（Mike Fong）提到，台灣與加州去年貿易額已達770億美元，對加州經濟發展至關重要。他目前正推動加州第1354號法案（AB1354），旨在將台裔及亞裔美國人的歷史貢獻納入加州中小學課程，讓下一代更瞭解這段歷史。

## 地方交流與外交盟友：共享民主價值與多領域合作

除了聯邦與州級的正面肯定，地方政府與外交使節也展現了對台灣的濃厚情誼。

[![Image 6](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867631-a273a1789a9649f6b6096d7f8c35b67d-600x450.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867631-a273a1789a9649f6b6096d7f8c35b67d.jpg)

2026年10月9日，（左起）維拉公園市市長吳正鵬、爾灣市議員劉令淳、約巴林達市代理市長黃瑞雅出席駐洛經文處雙十國慶酒會，共同慶祝中華民國國慶。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

約巴林達市代理市長黃瑞雅（Peggy Huang）深以台裔身分自豪，並宣布擔任新成立的「台灣友誼聯盟」（Taiwan Friendship Alliance）主席，未來將全力推動南加州地方政府、企業與台灣在商業、文化及民主價值上的深入合作。

爾灣市議員劉令淳（Melinda Liu）、維拉公園市（Villa Park）市長吳正鵬（Jordan Wu）等多位台裔美籍民選官員亦出席參與慶祝雙十酒會。

巴拉圭總領事卡琳娜・達赫（Carina Daher）表示，台巴兩國友誼建立在相互尊重之上，雙方正持續推動青年實習、科技、製造業及蘭花產業等領域交流，期盼在國際環境變化中持續鞏固台巴深厚夥伴關係。

## 文化與美食饗宴 展現台灣多元軟實力

當晚酒會由羅省龍岡親義公所「名義軒」瑞獅團演出揭開序幕，洛杉磯歌劇演員林聖峰領唱中華民國國歌，台裔音樂設計師邱玠韋負責全新編曲並現場演奏。現場首度設置戶外的「台灣美食專區」，包括台灣品牌「啤酒頭」釀造的二十四節氣啤酒「秋分」及台裔經營的Zero Gravitea鹹酥雞餐車，讓來賓體驗台灣飲食文化。

[![Image 7](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867632-5d7a3989be066c938734b66498082415-600x352.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14867632-5d7a3989be066c938734b66498082415.jpg)

2026年10月9日，雙十國慶酒會設置台灣美食專區，提供台灣啤酒及台式鹽酥雞等炸物，讓來賓品嚐台灣特色美食。（徐曼沅／大紀元）

出席賓客還包括洛杉磯縣政委員會執行官嚴志豪（Edward Yen）、貝里斯（伯利茲）總領事金特爾（Yvette Karen Gentle）、瓜地馬拉總領事卡爾德隆（Patricia Nineth Santizo Estrada de Calderón），以及印度、捷克、立陶宛等多國駐外代表與羅省中華會館主席聶澤英、大洛杉磯台灣會館董事陳柏宇等僑界領袖。◇

title: Pag-IBIG, BCDA bring homes closer to offices
summary: THE Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF), also known as the Pag-IBIG Fund, has partnered with the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) to advance the agenda of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa
content:
THE Home Development Mutual Fund (HDMF), also known as the Pag-IBIG Fund, has partnered with the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) to advance the agenda of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino (Expanded 4PH) Program.

Both parties signed a memorandum of agreement on Thursday at the BCDA’s office at Bonifacio Global City in Taguig.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

[![Image 1: NEW WALKABLE CITY A new walkable city is set to rise in Tarlac as Pag-IBIG Fund and the BCDA have partnered to pursue a walk-to-work township in New Clark City and explore development opportunities on other government lands, advancing President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s Expanded 4PH Program. Pictured from left are Pag-IBIG Fund Acting Deputy CEO Marcial Pimentel Jr.; Deputy CEOs Benjamin Felix Jr. and Alexander Hilario Aguilar; DHSUD Secretary and Pag-IBIG Fund Board Chairman Jose Ramon Aliling; Pag-IBIG Fund CEO Marilene Acosta; BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang; Chairman Jerry Marasigan; Executive Vice President and COO Gisela Kalalo; and Board Director Gerard Seno. CONTRIBUTED PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254520.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254520.jpg)
NEW WALKABLE CITY A new walkable city is set to rise in Tarlac as Pag-IBIG Fund and the BCDA have partnered to pursue a walk-to-work township in New Clark City and explore development opportunities on other government lands, advancing President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s Expanded 4PH Program. Pictured from left are Pag-IBIG Fund Acting Deputy CEO Marcial Pimentel Jr.; Deputy CEOs Benjamin Felix Jr. and Alexander Hilario Aguilar; DHSUD Secretary and Pag-IBIG Fund Board Chairman Jose Ramon Aliling; Pag-IBIG Fund CEO Marilene Acosta; BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang; Chairman Jerry Marasigan; Executive Vice President and COO Gisela Kalalo; and Board Director Gerard Seno. CONTRIBUTED PHOTO

Under the memorandum of agreement, both agencies will “pursue housing and other development opportunities on identified BCDA properties, bringing together land, infrastructure, financing and housing expertise to help create quality homes in locations that meet Filipino workers’ needs.”

It added that the partnership between the agencies will initially prioritize about 14 hectares in New Clark City, which will comprise a 10-hectare property in Bamban, Tarlac, and a 4-hectare property in Capas, Tarlac, with the Tarlac property intended to be a government center and other complementary developments.

“The planned housing development in New Clark City is intended for workers and aims to create a walk-to-work township, bringing homes closer to employment opportunities. The parties envision an integrated development that combines housing with commercial areas and facilities for rest, recreation and other daily needs, helping workers and their families enjoy a more convenient and balanced way of life. Set amid mountains and trees, the proposed township also seeks to offer workers a home environment with access to green surroundings while keeping them within reach of their workplaces and essential services,” Pag-IBIG said in a statement on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Camp John Hay in Baguio City, Morong Discovery Park in Bataan, and the Poro Point Freeport Zone in San Fernando, La Union, have also been identified for possible projects.

Pag-IBIG said that their partnership with the BCDA “advances Expanded 4PH’s approach of addressing both sides of the housing equation by increasing the supply of quality homes and matching these with affordable financing.”

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

“Coming as the country celebrates National Shelter Month, the collaboration also aligns with BCDA’s plans to provide affordable and mixed-income housing for workers within reach of New Clark City’s business, industrial and commercial districts,” the Pag-IBIG Fund stated.

Housing Secretary and Pag-IBIG Fund Board Chairman Jose Ramon Aliling said the partnership with the BCDA showed how two government institutions can combine resources in making homeownership more attainable for the Filipino worker.

“President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has directed us to sustain our efforts to provide more Filipino families with access to decent and affordable homes. Through Expanded 4PH, we are bringing together government resources and capabilities to turn that directive into concrete housing opportunities,” Aliling said.

“This collaboration between BCDA and Pag-IBIG Fund puts government land and affordable financing to work toward that goal. We hope to replicate this model with similarly situated institutions in both government and the private sector, making more land available for quality housing and ensuring that more families have the means to own a home,” he added.

*   ![Image 3: Malacañang accepts Aguda resignation – Remulla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254517.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Malacañang accepts Aguda resignation – Remulla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/national/malacaang-accepts-aguda-resignation-remulla/2443171)

Meanwhile, BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang said that their collaboration with Pag-IBIG is seen as a “long-term institutional partnership.”

“As our project areas continue to grow, we want to make sure that our properties are put to productive use and that development keeps pace with the needs of the people. Through this partnership, we aim to advance projects within the Marcos administration’s term that will provide quality housing and help give Filipino families greater opportunities to own a home,” Bingcang said.

Pag-IBIG Fund Chief Executive Officer Marilene Acosta, on the other hand, said the partnership “opens opportunities to make housing more affordable,” while also placing emphasis on how the location of the home affects the life of ordinary Filipino workers.

“Making homeownership more accessible means bringing together affordable financing and quality homes in locations that meet Filipino workers’ needs. Through this partnership, BCDA can provide access to government land, while Pag-IBIG Fund can contribute financing and housing expertise.”

title: Missile strikes a passenger terminal at Riyadh airport and many are wounded, official says
summary: **CAIRO —**The airport in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, was attacked again Saturday and evacuated, two regional officials said, just days after three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, were killed as the kingdom faces an extraordinary ser
content:
**CAIRO —**The airport in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, was attacked again Saturday and evacuated, two regional officials said, just days after three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, were killed as the kingdom faces an extraordinary series of assaults in the new front in the Iran war.

President Donald Trump told reporters he was evaluating whether the U.S. should join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen who have claimed this week's attacks on King Khalid International Airport as well as other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure.

“We may. We’re going to look at it,” Trump said. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”

*   [Taiwan ups defense spending to ‘deter war’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/taiwan-ups-defense-spending-to-deter-war/2443116)

In the latest attack, a missile struck a complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights at the Riyadh airport and many people were wounded, one of the regional officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Several ambulances were seen rushing there.

The surge in attacks has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis. There was no immediate statement from the Houthis, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa International Airport in the rebel-held Yemeni capital.

**Riyadh airport operations have been suspended**

Saudi civil aviation authorities said operations at the airport had been suspended and the number of wounded and damage were being assessed. An official notice to aviators said the suspension was through midnight. The airport had a heavy police presence, with all entrances blocked, and lights around the complex were dimmed.

Flights diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the United States, Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The attacks on airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, has rattled markets and the region. And yet the Saudi energy ministry hours after the latest attack was still promoting a major international energy conference set to begin in Riyadh on Sunday.

Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces in an attempt to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea. Those gains gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that is a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

Though the Houthis have told the AP and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A US bombing campaign sharply limited that.

Saudi Arabia has run low on interceptors, officials say

*   ![Image 2: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air defense support to the region, regional officials told the AP last month, with one noting that the US has seen its own stock dwindle during the war with Iran.

Officials have said US assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive against the Houthis.

The Saudi and Omani foreign ministers spoke by phone about the importance of “supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions” in the region, the kingdom said Saturday. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region.

Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that "filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability.”

*   ![Image 3: DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254558.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

**Flight disruptions are growing**

The Houthis this week warned global airlines “for the last time” about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theater for their military operations.

At least 225 flights at the Riyadh airport had been canceled over the past 24 hours, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware. Air India, FlyDubai, Lufthansa Group and Pakistan International Airlines have been among airlines suspending flights to and from Riyadh and other Saudi airports for varying periods.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis’ ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a “greater focus on aviation infrastructure.”

The missile and drone attacks and interception efforts “create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft,” it said.

Two regional officials said Houthi attacks on the Riyadh airport on Thursday damaged three planes. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to brief the media. The Saudi national carrier said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board.

# DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla

[![Image 14: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/1893_1768618670.jpg)![Image 15: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/1893_1768618670.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/arlie-o-calalo "author image")

[By Arlie O. Calalo](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/arlie-o-calalo "Arlie O. Calalo")

 October 11, 2026

 10

[Resize](https://manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

*   ![Image 16: font icon small](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-small.svg)Small
*   ![Image 17: font icon medium](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-medium.svg)Medium

[![Image 19: Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/google-preferred-source.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=manilatimes.net "Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google")

**MANILA, Philippines —**The Department of Justice (DOJ) confirmed on Saturday that the preliminary investigation into the obstruction of justice complaint filed against Senator Robin Padilla proceeded last Friday, October 9.

Saying that the next hearing has been set on November 6, 2026, Justice spokesperson Polo Martinez said only the senator’s counsel was present during the initial investigation on the complaint.

The Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) on May 28, 2026 lodged an obstruction of justice complaint against Padilla and others before the justice department in connection with the escape of Senator Ronald "Bato" Dela Rosa from the Senate building.

*   [‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

A former PNP chief, dela Rosa has been the subject of an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court for "alleged criminal responsibility as an indirect co-perpetrator" in the crimes against humanity of murder during the Duterte administration's war on drugs.

He sought refuge at the Senate on May 11 after authorities attempted to serve the warrant. He slipped out of the Senate building in the early hours of May 14.

The senator has denied intentionally helping Dela Rosa evade arrest, although he previously acknowledged giving him a ride from the Senate to Makati.

Insisting that the matter should have been handled by the ICC, Padilla maintained that he did not help dela Rosa "escape," insisting that the former police chief had merely asked to hitch a ride with him out of the Senate building.
