title: COA flags Mandaue’s P55M Christmas expenditure
summary: MANDAUE CITY — The Commission on Audit (COA) has questioned this city’s P55.525-million expenditure for its “Gugma sa Pasko (Love at Christmas)” food bundle program, saying the city failed to sufficiently establish how the assistance addres
content:
MANDAUE CITY — The Commission on Audit (COA) has questioned this city’s P55.525-million expenditure for its “Gugma sa Pasko (Love at Christmas)” food bundle program, saying the city failed to sufficiently establish how the assistance addressed specific socioeconomic concerns and development gaps.

In its 2025 audit observations, COA said the city distributed 100,000 Christmas bundles worth P595.25 each in December 2025 to households registered and not registered under the Community-Based Monitoring System.

However, the audit team found that the program’s developmental purpose and contribution to defined objectives remained unclear.

*   [DENR pushes bamboo planting in Tarlac](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/regions/denr-pushes-bamboo-planting-in-tarlac/2443091)

“The developmental value and strategic relevance of the expenditure to the objectives of the 20-percent Development Fund could not be readily established,” the audit report stated.

COA recommended that the city prioritize programs addressing clearly identified social needs and development gaps to ensure public funds generate greater socioeconomic benefits.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

In response, Mandaue City is seeking to revise the program’s guidelines and prioritize vulnerable sectors for its planned distribution in December 2026.

The city council approved on first reading an ordinance establishing the Gugma sa Pasko Mandaue Food Assistance Program, with a proposed P60-million allocation for an estimated 80,000 qualified beneficiaries.

City administrator Gonzalo Malig-on Jr. acknowledged the need to identify specific sectors that the program should serve.

*   ![Image 1: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

“Ang observations sa COA dapat naa gyud targeted nga sectors nga naa gyuy social program nga gi-address (COA’s observations emphasize that there should be targeted sectors served by specific social programs),” Malig-on said.

He explained that last year’s distribution covered around 100,000 households without restricting beneficiaries to specific vulnerable groups.

Mayor Thadeo Jovito Ouano has since asked the city council, through councilor Joel Seno, to establish the program through an ordinance setting clear guidelines and eligibility requirements.

The proposed measure identifies persons with disabilities, senior citizens, solo parents, low-income households and urban poor residents as priority sectors.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The City Social Welfare and Development Office will lead beneficiary screening and validation in coordination with concerned city offices and barangay leaders.

Malig-on said the number of beneficiaries would likely decrease from last year’s 100,000 households if the ordinance takes effect. He noted that Mandaue has more than 33,000 senior citizens and acknowledged that some previous recipients might no longer qualify under the revised guidelines.

“Wa man tay mahimo kay mutuman ra pod ang syudad sa gi-raise sa COA nga concern (There is nothing we can do because the city must comply with the concerns raised by COA),” he said.

Councilor Joel Seno, chairman of the Committee on Education, said the program would provide Christmas bundles to qualified residents across the city.

*   ![Image 3: Mayabang talaga!](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252273.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

The proposed P60-million appropriation would cover an estimated 80,000 beneficiaries, subject to validation, procurement results and fund availability.

“Murag Christmas gift ni Mayor ba para sa tanan, walay pili basta na-belong sa sector (It is like a Christmas gift from the mayor for everyone, as long as they belong to the identified sectors),” Seno said.

The Christmas bundles distributed in 2025 contained 10 items: fruit cocktail, cream, spaghetti noodles and sauce, Chinese luncheon meat, carne norte, sausage, beef loaf, pork and beans and cheese.

Seno clarified that the proposed ordinance would cover the December 2026 implementation only and would not automatically make Gugma sa Pasko an annual program. The city may consider continuing it in subsequent years depending on its implementation and the city administration’s direction.

Malig-on also disputed COA’s reported identification of the funding source, saying the P55.525-million expenditure came from the General Fund rather than the 20-percent Development Fund.

He said the city had already communicated with COA to correct the information in the report.

Despite the audit observation, Malig-on maintained that the program contributed to residents’ general well-being by allowing households to benefit directly from government assistance.

He also cited similar Christmas bundle distribution programs in Metro Manila, including those implemented by Pasig City and Quezon City.

COA said the money could have supported programs addressing identified development concerns, improving public services, strengthening economic productivity or promoting long-term social welfare.

Section 2 of Presidential Decree 1445, or the Government Auditing Code of the Philippines, requires government resources to be managed and used in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, with safeguards against waste and improper disposition.

title: Filipino workers fear speaking up about mental health, Telus index finds
summary: SEVENTY-SEVEN percent of Filipino workers would worry about their career options if their workplace knew about a mental health issue, according to the latest Telus Mental Health Index for the Philippines, released by Telus Health in August.
content:
SEVENTY-SEVEN percent of Filipino workers would worry about their career options if their workplace knew about a mental health issue, according to the latest Telus Mental Health Index for the Philippines, released by Telus Health in August. That is up from 75 percent in 2022, while the share who would feel negatively about themselves rose from 57 to 63 percent.

More than half of workers have no emergency savings to cover basic needs, and half name personal finances as their top source of personal stress. A similar share say their mental health hurts their productivity, and nearly half often end the workday mentally or physically exhausted.

The overall index score is 61.6 out of 100, more than three points lower than in November 2022 and within the range the report labels “strained.”

*   [When security creates friction, employees find workarounds](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/business/sunday-business-it/when-security-creates-friction-employees-find-workarounds/2443042)

The online survey covered 2,000 people in the Philippines who are employed or had a job in the previous six months.

I asked Jamie MacLennan, region head for Asia-Pacific at Telus Health, what reason workers have to ask for help if they believe it could hurt their careers.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“If someone believes asking for help might cost them a promotion, silence can feel like the safer choice,” MacLennan wrote in an email interview. He traced this to Asia’s history of high stigma around mental health, and said the Philippines is similar to other parts of Asia but much worse than Western countries. Employees “look at how a manager responds, whether a conversation stays confidential, and whether someone who asks for help is still considered fairly for opportunities,” he wrote.

“Those experiences shape trust more than any campaign.”

Since 2020, employers in the formal private sector have been required to have a mental health workplace policy and program under Department Order 208 of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), which implements the Mental Health Act (Republic Act 11036). The order bars discrimination in hiring, promotion and other employment benefits because of a worker’s mental health condition, provided it does not interfere with their job performance or unduly affect their safety or that of coworkers, clients and the public. Yet nearly eight in 10 workers in the Telus survey still fear that disclosure could limit their career options.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

I also asked him about money. “When someone is wondering how to pay the next bill or what they would do if a family member became ill, that worry comes to work with them.”

Workers without emergency savings scored 55.5 on the index, against 69.0 for those with savings. Employers “should absolutely make financial well-being part of their mental health strategy,” MacLennan said, and salary alone does not cover it. He said the survey shows workers want financial consultation, education or resources from their employer. Across the region, Telus Health has seen confidential financial counseling and help with budgeting and debt work.

More than eight in 10 workers do their jobs while mentally or physically unwell at least once a week. “Many workers keep going because they feel they have to,” he said, since a day off can mean lost income, unfinished work or more pressure on colleagues.

According to the report, workers who never work while unwell lose 17.3 productivity days a year. Those who do it four or five days a week lose between 64 and 71 days. For employers who still count attendance and hours, MacLennan said “showing up is not the same as being well.”

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

He told managers to watch for an engaged employee who turns withdrawn, has trouble concentrating or misses familiar deadlines. Those changes “should start a private, caring conversation,” he wrote. “People should not have to reach a breaking point before their employer notices.”

Workers under 40 are twice as likely as those over 50 to report constant stress, and 70 percent more likely to end the day exhausted. Younger workers score lower across Asia-Pacific, according to MacLennan, who listed the stressors that have piled up since the pandemic: cost of living, geopolitical risks, housing, job security “and now AI.”

Only six in 10 managers say they would know what to do if they suspected an employee was struggling. More than four in 10 workers say their manager has not told them what programs are available, and only about a third regularly receive clear information about them. More than half cite cost as a barrier to professional help. About a third do not know what type of care fits them, and nearly three in 10 do not know where to go.

MacLennan would start by training every manager. They should be able to tell employees whom to contact, what help exists, what it costs and what stays confidential, and then connect them to qualified support “without trying to be their counsellor.” Employers also need to keep explaining their programs and ask staff if they work.

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

Many of us have worked beside someone who was struggling and never said a word about it. As MacLennan wrote: “The real test is whether an employee facing a difficult day knows where to turn and feels safe taking that first step.”

# India crackdown on youth protesters provokes anger

[![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/861_1632502576.jpg)![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/861_1632502576.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/associated-press "author image")

[By Associated Press](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/associated-press "Associated Press")

 October 11, 2026

[Resize](https://manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/india-crackdown-on-youth-protesters-provokes-anger/2443108)

*   ![Image 21: font icon small](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-small.svg)Small
*   ![Image 22: font icon medium](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-medium.svg)Medium
*   ![Image 23: font icon large](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-large.svg)Large

[![Image 24: Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/google-preferred-source.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=manilatimes.net "Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google")

NEW DELHI— Indian authorities deployed a sweeping security crackdown across New Delhi and detained thousands of protesters on Saturday as India’s youth “Cockroach” movement sought to intensify a nationwide campaign against a contentious voter list revision that has fueled anger at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government and election authorities.

Police intercepted demonstrators before they could reach Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the heart of India’s capital, chasing off some and detaining many others. Some were dragged away before being bundled into police vehicles and taken to temporary detention centers. Several “Cockroach” movement leaders were detained before arriving, effectively crippling the protest ahead of its start.

The crackdown extended beyond the protest venue, with police stopping buses, cars and other vehicles at checkpoints on routes into the capital and searching for demonstrators.

*   [India deploys police forces ahead of huge protest](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/india-deploys-police-forces-ahead-of-huge-protest/2443114)

Jantar Mantar was barricaded, while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear gas launchers were stationed along key routes. Restrictions on mobile internet and access to parts of the city added to the hurdles facing protesters.

Police said on Friday they had denied permission for the protest because the request was submitted late.

The scale of the crackdown underscored the authorities’ determination to disrupt a fast-growing protest campaign that has mobilized thousands of young people, drawn opposition support and intensified scrutiny of Modi. The protests also come at a politically sensitive time, months after demonstrations led by the “Cockroach” movement over exam paper leaks forced Modi’s education minister to resign in July.

Police detain leaders

Advertisement

Leaders of the “Cockroach” movement Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were expected to be at the forefront of the protest, were detained after arriving at Delhi airport from Mumbai on Saturday. A video shared by the “Cockroach Janta Party” on X showed police boarding the aircraft and detaining the three men.

*   ![Image 25: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

“The preplanned interception by Delhi Police aims to cripple the leadership of today’s peaceful demonstrations before they even reach the protest site,” the movement said in a statement.

Loudspeakers around the protest site warned that gatherings of five or more people were banned in parts of New Delhi, as authorities imposed sweeping security restrictions rarely seen in the capital. Journalists also faced restrictions in some areas.

Some protesters nevertheless broke through police cordons, chanting slogans against Modi and election authorities before being detained.

title: India deploys police forces ahead of huge protest
summary: NEW DELHI — India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on Saturday demanding the resignation of the country’s election chief over alleged voter-roll irreg
content:
NEW DELHI — India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on Saturday demanding the resignation of the country’s election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities.

The protests, called by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), are the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilization following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision.

Demonstrations erupted across the country after a newspaper investigation last month alleged misconduct by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

*   [India crackdown on youth protesters provokes anger](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/india-crackdown-on-youth-protesters-provokes-anger/2443108)

The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety in the “special intensive revision”, saying it was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.

Opposition parties and critics say the exercise could disenfranchise voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Tens of thousands of police officers and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across the capital, with multiple layers of yellow metal barricades blocking roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the usual government-designated protest site.

[![Image 1: Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel stand guard ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India�s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged ](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254362.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254362.jpg)
Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel stand guard ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India�s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged "special intensive revision� (SIR) voter-roll irregularities, in New Delhi on October 10, 2026. India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on October 10 demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities. (Photo by Manan VATSYAYANA / AFP)

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Police have not authorized rallies at the site this weekend.

The protests, called by the CJP, are widely seen as a reprise of its mass mobilization in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.

This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign.

‘Cannot detain the movement’

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office.

Authorities have ordered the closure of dozens of metro stations, and cancelled several trains coming to New Delhi.

However, the Supreme Court on Friday said some trains must still run and that there should be no blanket closure of metro stations.

“The dictator would rather shut down the entire national capital and inconvenience millions of citizens than allow a peaceful protest at a designated protest site,” CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said on X.

*   ![Image 4: HEADLINES: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’ | Oct. 11, 2026](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254313.png?width=113&crop=113:85)
[HEADLINES: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’ | Oct. 11, 2026](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/podcasts/headlines-no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes-oct-11-2026/2443086)

“Imagine how many lives would be affected because of this shutdown by Modi.” The CJP, which emerged online as a satirical political movement in May, has accused authorities of intimidating its supporters ahead of the demonstration.

The party has said that “at least 10,000 people”, including protesters travelling to Delhi by train, have been detained across the country.

Some people detained in the central state of Madhya Pradesh were taken to hotels, The Hindu newspaper reported.

Police have not responded to the party’s broader allegations of mass detentions.

“You can detain the people -- you cannot detain the movement,” said Neha Bora, who has emerged as a leading face of the current protest.

The voter list overhaul, which began in 2025, has led to more than 133 million names being excluded from draft rolls.

The exclusions include duplicate entries and people found to have died.

The poll body said the exercise identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from casting ballots.

Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalized and minority communities.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

title: Taiwan ups defense spending to ‘deter war’
summary: TAIPEI— Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defense spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims. Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant thr
content:
TAIPEI— Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defense spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.

Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.

“Our aim by increasing investment in national defense is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war,” Leader Lai Ching-te said in a speech to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.

*   [Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/candidate-named-hitler-mussolini-elected-mayor-in-peru/2443077)

Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion — and to show the United States it is serious about its own defense.

Lai’s government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) in defense spending for 2027, which accounts for more than 3 percent of GDP.

“We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others,” Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei, where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered.

“However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” Lai said, noting that China continued to “apply pressure through military and gray-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.” Lai welcomed talks between the US and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist.” Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have jangled nerves at times.

(Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254374.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254374.jpg)
Taiwan�s President Lai Ching-te gives a speech during the National Day celebrations ceremony at the Presidential Palace in Taipei on October 10, 2026. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP)

‘US support important’

The US switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer.

Trump’s suggestion in May, following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Taiwan is waiting for Trump’s signature on $14 billion worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defense system.

Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Lai’s wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population.

“You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society,” said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances.

Tao Yi-feng, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said Lai’s speech was “relatively moderate” and unlikely to be met with “overt reaction from Beijing.” Saturday’s celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China’s Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China.

*   ![Image 4: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong’s communist fighters.

Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favors closer ties with China, said “US support is extremely important to Taiwan’s security,”but he noted the historical and cultural links with China.

“The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges,” Han said at the National Day event.

title: Chinese linked to POGOs in Bamban, Porac nabbed
summary: COMBINED elements of the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (Paocc) and the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a Chinese citizen linked to human trafficking activities. The Chinese was identified as Huang M
content:
COMBINED elements of the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (Paocc) and the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a Chinese citizen linked to human trafficking activities.

The Chinese was identified as Huang Mingmin, who is wanted in connection with human trafficking activities linked to Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) operations.

The Paocc said Mingmin uses multiple aliases — including “Yang Bin,” “Sy Wang” and “A Bao” — to conceal his identity and evade detection by government authorities.

*   [Cebu ‘unhealthy’ air no longer from Indonesia](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/regions/cebu-unhealthy-air-no-longer-from-indonesia/2442632)

Mingmin was arrested at the K1 Center Building in Barangay Tambo, Parañaque City, on Friday.

The Paocc said Mingmin established a presence within the local business community and has already acquired real estate properties and fishing vessels on Jomalig Island in Quezon province.

The suspect also reportedly operates the Mother’s Wonderland and Sea Horizon Resort in Quezon province, where he was also identified as the owner.

The Paocc also alleged that Mingmin was among the foreigners who supported the broader operations of illegal POGO hubs such as the Baofu Hub in Bamban, Tarlac, and Lucky South 99 in Porac, Pampanga.

The Paocc also said initial investigations point to the subject’s alleged connection to individuals involved in the operations of these hubs, warranting further examination of his role and potential involvement in related activities.

*   ![Image 1: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

Based on court records, the Paocc said the arrested individual identified as alias “Yang Bin” is listed among the persons in control of the subject premises under Search Warrant 41M-M-2024, issued by the Regional Trial Court Branch 81, Malolos City, Bulacan.

He is also one of the persons in control of the premises in connection with an alleged violation of Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code (serious illegal detention); and Search Warrant 42-M-2024 for the violation of Republic Act (RA) 9208, as amended by RA 10364, or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012.

The suspect’s other known alias, “A Bao,” is listed among the individuals with arrest warrants in connection with the operations of Lucky South 99 and Whirlwind Corp. in Porac, Pampanga.

The case involves qualified trafficking in persons under Criminal Case R-PSG-25-01737-CR, pending before the Regional Trial Court Branch 157, Pasig City.

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Mingmin was brought to the CIDG-NCR for booking procedures and the completion of other necessary documentation.

Paocc said the agency, under the leadership of executive director Undersecretary Benjamin Acorda Jr., and law enforcement partners, remain steadfast in strengthening the government’s campaign against organized crime and human trafficking.

Former Paocc spokesman Winston Casio, meanwhile, said the POGOs “never left” the country and are still involve in guerrilla-like operations all over the Philippines.

Meanwhile, Ruperto Cruz, the former landowner, urged the government to clean the surroundings of the Lucky South 99 premises to prevent overgrown bushes from triggering fire. A golf club now operates near the Lucky South 99 property, which is now under the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Arrest warrants had been issue against key personalities in the Porac POGO such as Cassandra Li Ong and Ronelyn Baterna for qualified human trafficking charges, but the two had gone hiding.

The International Criminal Police Organization red notices were also issued against the two in October last year.

title: MGB suggests reducing exploration area
summary: BAYOMBONG, Nueva Vizcaya — A proposal by the Mines and Geosciences Bureau in Cagayan Valley (MGB-2) to substantially shrink a contested exploration permit in the upland town of Kasibu has become the focal point of efforts to ease tensions b
content:
BAYOMBONG, Nueva Vizcaya — A proposal by the Mines and Geosciences Bureau in Cagayan Valley (MGB-2) to substantially shrink a contested exploration permit in the upland town of Kasibu has become the focal point of efforts to ease tensions between the exploration firm and residents maintaining an anti-mining barricade.

The permit in question spans 4,456 hectares and has affected six barangay (villages), prompting protests, legal actions and a series of meetings involving national agencies, provincial and municipal officials, and community representatives.

MGB-2 regional director Mario Ancheta said the bureau intends to recommend that four villages be removed from the coverage of Exploration Permit EP-000029-II issued to North Luzon Mineral Resources Corp. (NLMRC), retaining only the villages of Pao and Kakidugen.

*   [Cebu ‘unhealthy’ air no longer from Indonesia](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/regions/cebu-unhealthy-air-no-longer-from-indonesia/2442632)

The recommendation, he said, directly addresses the geographic scope that has fueled opposition.

Reducing the area to two villages is presented as a way to limit potential disturbance while keeping the exploration process within the existing regulatory framework, Ancheta said.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“The purpose of the current activity is to establish whether commercially viable mineral deposits exist,” he said.

Ancheta appealed to residents at the barricade to allow the firm to finish its technical work, noting that communities would still have a formal avenue to oppose any future mining development through free, prior and informed consent, and through the required concurrence of local legislative bodies.

That distinction is central to the regulatory sequence.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Exploration is treated as preliminary and technical, while any shift to development would require a separate, more stringent layer of social acceptability and clearances, he said.

Limits of local authority

Provincial officials, meanwhile, underscored the limits of local power over permits issued nationally.

Nueva Vizcaya Gov. Jose Gambito cautioned the company against any act that might place residents at the barricade at risk, saying it would be held accountable if harm occurs.

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

At the same time, Gambito acknowledged that local officials do not have the power to unilaterally stop an operation backed by a national permit.

He expressed understanding for residents who oppose large-scale mining but said the authority to order a halt lies beyond the provincial and municipal levels.

Kasibu Mayor Romeo Tayaban shared that assessment, stating that the municipality cannot suspend exploration while a valid national permit remains in effect.

Gambito said he has elevated the concerns of protesters to Malacañang and noted that only President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. can order a halt to mining activities in the province.

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

He added that past administrations in the province have faced similar challenges in stopping large-scale operations, and that he is pursuing all legal and administrative channels available with a clear conscience.

As a possible alternative, Gambito said that if the area is found to be more viable for small-scale operations, he would push for its declaration as a Minahang Bayan, or people’s small-scale mining area, a classification that allows residents to benefit from mineral resources under regulated conditions.

The model offers a different approach to resource use, centered on community participation rather than large corporate development.

Conflicting positions

Despite the proposed reduction in coverage, the barricade group continues to call for a complete withdrawal of the company.

Municipal councilor Anthony Glen Guingayan Sr., speaking for the protesters, said allowing the firm to leave the site would be the most direct way to avoid further confrontation, arguing that its exploration is already close to completion.

Guingayan said operations in Didipio are sufficient and that expansion to other barangay in Kasibu should not be allowed.

He also raised concern over criminal complaints filed against residents who joined the barricade to defend their lands, saying more than 20 individuals, including himself, have been charged and that more cases could be filed.

On the company side, lawyer Ulysses Ordoñez said the blockade has resulted in about P8 million in losses.

Ordoñez said the firm is considering applying for a preliminary injunction to remove the barricade and resume work, but would be willing not to pursue that legal remedy if protesters allow exploration to be completed.

Provincial board member Flodemonte Gerdan, who chairs the Committee on Peace and Order, reiterated the provincial board’s appeal for NLMRC to drop charges against protesters as a sign of good faith toward a peaceful settlement.

Bugkalot lawyer Efraim Osingat, meanwhile, urged those at the barricade to allow exploration to continue on their ancestral land, saying that for the first time a company willing to bring development to that land has come forward.

title: The candidate who isn’t running keeps appearing in the polls
summary: THERE is an unusual character in the early polling for the 2028 presidential election: a candidate who says she is not running. Leni Robredo has said she does not intend to seek national office in 2028. Instead, she expects to seek a second
content:
THERE is an unusual character in the early polling for the 2028 presidential election: a candidate who says she is not running.

Leni Robredo has said she does not intend to seek national office in 2028. Instead, she expects to seek a second term as mayor of Naga City. Yet when pollsters ask Filipinos whom they would choose if the presidential election were held today, many continue to name her.

That is interesting in itself. But Robredo may not be the only number worth watching.

*   [US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

[![Image 1: n CHART FROM THE AUTHOR ](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254437.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254437.jpg)
n CHART FROM THE AUTHOR

In OCTA Research’s first-quarter 2026 survey, Robredo received 21 percent in a 26-name presidential preference question, up from 8 percent in the previous quarter. Bam Aquino was at 4 percent.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

In a separate head-to-head question, Robredo received 35 percent against Sara Duterte’s 46 percent, with 19 percent undecided. By the second quarter, the figures were 34 percent and 43 percent, respectively. The nine-point gap is notable, but it is not, by itself, proof of a decisive political shift.

Other surveys tell a similar broad story. WR Numero’s June survey put Robredo at 20.9 percent. Momentum’s July survey had her at 23.8 percent. Pulse Asia’s late-June/early-July survey placed her at 26 percent in a six-name field.

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

The figures are worth putting beside the 2022 election, but not treating as the same thing.

Robredo received 15,035,773 votes, or 27.94 percent, in that election. Some current hypothetical polling has placed her in roughly the same territory. But today’s surveys ask different questions, offer different candidate lists and measure opinion in a very different political environment.

The safer conclusion is simply that Robredo’s name continues to generate substantial support, even though she says she does not intend to run.

Then there is Bam Aquino.

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

His presidential preference numbers are modest: 2 percent in WR Numero’s November 2025 survey, 4 percent in OCTA’s first-quarter poll, and 2 percent in Momentum’s July survey.

But his actual electoral record is much stronger. Aquino received 20,971,899 votes and finished second in the 2025 Senate race. Pulse Asia’s May 2025 pre-election survey also placed him at 32.8 percent in its Senate preference question.

The distinction matters. Presidential preference, Senate preference and an actual election result are three different things.

OCTA’s second-quarter survey adds another data point: in a hypothetical president-vice president tandem question, Robredo and Aquino received 36 percent against 48 percent for Sara Duterte and Robin Padilla, with 16 percent undecided. The 12-point gap was the narrowest OCTA had recorded between the two tandems. Aquino, however, has said he will not run for vice president in 2028, so the pairing remains hypothetical.

*   ![Image 4: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Kiko Pangilinan provides another useful reminder that political support cannot be measured with one number.

His presidential preference was only 1.6 percent in WR Numero’s November 2025 survey and 1 percent in Momentum’s July poll. Yet Pangilinan received 15,343,229 votes and finished fifth in the 2025 Senate race.

A politician can therefore have substantial demonstrated support for one office without being a leading preference for another.

Taken together, these numbers raise a larger question: how much of the political constituency that emerged around Robredo in 2022 remains visible four years later?

It would be tempting to call this proof that the “Pink” or “Leni” coalition remains intact. The polling does not establish that. We do not have individual-level data showing that the same people moved from Robredo in 2022 to Aquino and Pangilinan in 2025, or that they would support the same candidates in 2028.

What we can say is more modest. Robredo remains a significant name in hypothetical presidential polling. Aquino demonstrated very large actual electoral support in the 2025 Senate race and appears with Robredo in OCTA’s hypothetical tandem question. Pangilinan also demonstrated a substantial national Senate vote.

That is enough to make the persistence of these political figures worth watching, without claiming that they constitute one permanent constituency.

There is another reason to be careful with the numbers: the question matters.

A poll asking respondents to choose among many presidential candidates is not the same as a head-to-head matchup. Neither is the same as a hypothetical tandem question, a Senate preference survey, or an actual election.

So the most useful habit when reading political polls is simple: look not only at the number but also at what voters were actually asked.

For now, we know that Robredo remains a significant hypothetical choice, despite saying she is not running. We know that Aquino and Pangilinan demonstrated substantial electoral support in the 2025 Senate race. And we know that Robredo and Aquino can still appear together in a hypothetical 2028 question.

What we do not know is whether these numbers represent one coherent political constituency.

For now, the numbers can raise that question.

They cannot answer it yet.

Bong Habana Ruado is a former public-sector official whose career has spanned government, politics, public policy, and the private sector. His current interests include public opinion research, governance data, and explanatory journalism, with a particular focus on interpreting political surveys beyond their headline numbers. He holds degrees in political science and law (Juris Doctor) and completed the Strategic Business Economics Program at the University of Asia and the Pacific.

title: Why the NCIP cannot take cognizance of disputes belonging to different Indigenous cultural communities and Indigenous peoples
summary: _**Dear PAO,**_ _**I am a member of a certain tribe in the south. My problem involves my property which is being grabbed by another person belonging to another tribe. I plan to file my complaint with the NCIP since its mandate is to protect
content:
_**Dear PAO,**_

_**I am a member of a certain tribe in the south. My problem involves my property which is being grabbed by another person belonging to another tribe. I plan to file my complaint with the NCIP since its mandate is to protect Indigenous peoples, but one elder persuaded me not to proceed because there are requirements to be followed. What are the requirements that I need to comply, if there is any?**_

_**Kalentong**_

*   [Can overtime work be used to offset an employee’s absence?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/06/legal-advice/can-overtime-work-be-used-to-offset-an-employees-absence/2439267)

Dear Kalentong,

The government agency responsible for the formulation of plans and programs for the protection and promotion of the rights of the Indigenous cultural communities/Indigenous peoples (ICCs/IPs) is the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP). Its primary jurisdiction is specified in Section 66 of Republic Act 8371, or the Indigenous People’s Rights Act of 1997, which reads:

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

_“The NCIP, through its regional offices, shall have jurisdiction over all claims and disputes involving rights of ICCs/IPs: Provided, however, that no such dispute shall be brought to the NCIP unless the parties have exhausted all remedies provided under their customary laws._ For this purpose, a certification shall be issued by the Council of Elders/Leaders who participated in the attempt to settle the dispute that the same has not been resolved, which certification shall be a condition precedent to the filing of a petition with the NCIP.” (Emphasis ours)

A careful reading of the above provision of law shows that the jurisdiction of the NCIP involves disputes between parties belonging to the same ICCs/IPs but not to parties belonging to different groups. This was illustrated in Unduran vs. Aberasturi, GR 181284, April 18, 2017, where the Supreme Court, speaking through Chief Justice Diosdado Peralta, stated that:

_“As held in the main decision, the NCIP shall have jurisdiction over claims and disputes involving rights of ICCs/IPs only when they arise between or among parties belonging to the same ICC/IP group because of the qualifying provision under Section 66 of the IPRA that ‘no such dispute shall be brought to the NCIP unless the parties have exhausted all remedies provided under their customary laws.’ Bearing in mind that the primary purpose of a proviso is to limit or restrict the general language or operation of the statute, and that what determines whether a clause is a proviso is the legislative intent, the Court stated that said qualifying provision requires the presence of two conditions before such claims and disputes may be brought before the NCIP, i.e., exhaustion of all remedies provided under customary laws and the Certification issued by the·Council of Elders/Leaders who participated in the attempt to settle the dispute that the same has not been resolved. The Court thus noted that the two conditions cannot be complied with if the parties to a case either (1) belong to different ICCs/IP groups which are recognized to have their own separate and distinct customary laws, or (2) if one of such parties was a non-ICC/IP member who is neither bound by customary laws or a Council of Elders/Leaders, for it would be contrary to the principles of fair play and due process for parties who do not belong to the same ICC/IP group to be subjected to its own distinct customary laws and Council of Elders/Leaders. In which case, the Court ruled that the regular courts shall have jurisdiction, and that the NCIP’s quasi-judicial jurisdiction is, in effect, limited to cases where the opposing parties belong to the same ICC/IP group.”_

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Applying the above-quoted jurisprudence to your situation, the dispute covering your property involves parties belonging to different ICCs, so the NCIP has no jurisdiction. This is for the reason that parties belonging to different ICCs/IPs have their own separate and distinct customary laws. Remember that every ICC/IP has their own and distinct customary laws, traditions and practices, and it would be contrary to the principle of fair play and due process if the party belonging to other ICCs/IPs will be subjected to customary laws which he/she is not bound to.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice is solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

Thank you for your continued trust and support.

Editor’s note: Dear PAO is a daily column of the Public Attorney’s Office. Questions for Chief Acosta may be sent to dearpao@manilatimes.net.

title: Art, AI, and what it means to be human
summary: THE threat posed by the alarming development of artificial intelligence (AI) has not subsided for some weeks now, as can be observed on social media and attested by major industry players. The mere thought of possible disruptions once AI be
content:
THE threat posed by the alarming development of artificial intelligence (AI) has not subsided for some weeks now, as can be observed on social media and attested by major industry players. The mere thought of possible disruptions once AI becomes unrestrained causes anxiety for many. Some describe this technology as a work in progress toward superintelligence. It is undeniable that the power and reach of this technology are becoming colossal in scale and far beyond what humanity needs.

It is alarming to also realize how AI is affecting art in all its forms, a field within the humanities that has not been spared from the technology’s disruptive presence. But hope is not lost, as long as we remain grounded in our desire for the authentic over the artificial.

A few weeks ago, an international initiative brought together universities from around the globe to form the Catholic Universities Art Triennial, a project dedicated to exploring how art can address the most relevant issues today. As news reports said, “Catholic universities offer art as a way of addressing today’s problems.” Over the coming months, these universities will host exhibitions, commissions, publications and public programs. This major event is promoted by the Dicastery for Culture and Education of the Holy See.

*   [Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

One may ask: “Can art really help solve today’s problems?” The answer is yes, provided that the issue of AI-generated art is addressed first. As the Art Triennial highlights, the primary role of art in higher education is “to promote human relationships and the concept of empathy,” in which AI is devoid of having and doing.

Saving art from AI requires returning to the experience of life’s deeper meaning: the power of inspiration, appreciation, and the freedom to create. These may be considered the fundamentals of human existence.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Tackling this issue is more crucial than ever, especially now that AI is increasingly encroaching upon the domain of art.

Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas” (Magnificent Humanity) points out that AI systems “may simulate empathy and understanding, but they do not understand what they produce, for they lack the affective, relational, and spiritual perspective through which human beings grow in wisdom.”

In contrast to AI-generated works, human art is supposed to transform universities into educational communities that strengthen our capacity to create — to generate new ideas, connect what was previously divided, and imagine new versions of the world. As the Art Triennial emphasizes, artworks “should be seen as invitations to join in an act of ‘co-creation’ instead of simply a technical exercise in repetition.”

*   ![Image 1: US-China war now](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253555.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

Pope Leo has a term for a human process in the act of creating: a divine “spark.” This is found exclusively in human endeavor, not in high technological complexity. Human creation is the locus of inspiration; it touches the soul directly and amplifies a capacity for creativity that no machine possesses.

On the other hand, it is interesting to note that contemporary philosophical thought can also deepen our understanding of genuine art, as opposed to AI-generated outputs.

For instance, the philosopher Hans-Georg Gadamer, a disciple of the phenomenologist Martin Heidegger, explains in his magnum opus, “Truth and Method: Elements of Philosophical Hermeneutics”: “Hermeneutical aesthetics regards aesthetic appearance not as a distraction from the real but as the vehicle through which real subject matters reveal themselves. It overturns the notion that artworks are at one remove from reality.”

An artwork is not a passive object merely installed in a museum; its true existence as a reflection of reality unfolds when it is performed, viewed, or read.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

No matter how elegantly generated an AI piece may be, it remains a shadow of the real art. AI can never present the essence of reality as clearly as a human immersed in the lived experience of everyday life. For example, a masterful portrait does not merely replicate a person’s face; it reveals the intrinsic truth of who that person is and his web of experiences in the world.

Maintaining skepticism toward AI-generated art may feel like a repetitive exercise during these times, but it is necessary in this age of artificial intelligence, where distinguishing human art from machine output has become urgent.

Thus, following Gadamer’s thought, one should ask when standing before a work of art: Does it possess an inner necessity and truth to convey, or is it merely a technical simulation of style?

If AI-produced art functions merely as a prompt-and-output generator for rapid and mass consumption, it risks bypassing the sublime process of internalization that aesthetic truth requires.

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

While there are distinct nuances between the Thomistic understanding of truth and essence and that of Heidegger and Gadamer, that is a topic for a separate discussion. What matters here is that both frameworks ground art in the ontological reality of human existence — a dimension entirely absent from AI and its “works” of art.

_Fr. Jesus “Jay” Miranda Jr., OP, is an organization and leadership studies resource person. He teaches at the University of Santo Tomas Graduate School and the Department of Educational Leadership and Management of the Bro. Andrew Gonzalez, FSC, College of Education of De La Salle University, Manila._

_jaymiranda.op@ust.edu.ph_

title: Make up your mind, Sharon
summary: BEFORE I get into today’s discussion, I need to share a follow-up to my column about the potential problem of the use of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) from last Sunday (“The dirty little problem with energy expansion,” Oct. 4). As I explained,
content:
BEFORE I get into today’s discussion, I need to share a follow-up to my column about the potential problem of the use of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) from last Sunday (“The dirty little problem with energy expansion,” Oct. 4). As I explained, SF6 is commonly used in heavy-duty transmission and distribution equipment, primarily as an insulator and arc-dampener. While it is safe and harmless in every other respect, SF6 unfortunately happens to be one of the most powerful greenhouse gases (GHG) known to man, and so its release into the atmosphere — which is a common enough practice when equipment is being repaired or replaced — is rather problematic.

China is the biggest source of atmospheric SF6, but it is potentially a problem anywhere there is any kind of grid or distribution infrastructure, so I queried both the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) and the Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) about how they handled it, but unfortunately, there was not enough time for either to respond before that column’s deadline. In the interim, however, the NGCP has talked to its engineering people, and provided some clarification, so an update is in order.

The good news is that, despite an utter lack of regulations requiring them to do so, the NGCP already has a procedure for handling SF6 responsibly and safely. A statement forwarded to me said the “NGCP [uses] sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) as an insulating and arc-quenching medium in certain high-voltage substation equipment, including gas-insulated switchgear, circuit breakers, and current transformers. SF6 is handled, monitored, and managed in accordance with applicable operational, safety and environmental requirements. Serviceable gas may be retained for reuse, while contaminated or unusable gas and associated cylinders are managed through appropriate treatment and disposal procedures. Relevant SF6 management guidelines are also undergoing review to further strengthen existing controls.”

*   [Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

So there you go. The NGCP is doing good business with respect to a potential environmental risk, despite the apparent hard-on our Energy Secretary Sharon Garin continues to have for the nation’s grid operator, which, at this point, defies any explanation other than it being a personal vendetta on her part.

In the Oct. 3 hearing of the House Subcommittee on Energy held in Bacolod City, the Department of Energy (DOE) chief seemed to have a hard time making up her mind as to the root problem of the persistent energy shortages in the Visayas. In one breath, she admitted that it was the result of years of poor planning on the part of the DOE to encourage the development of more generating capacity in the Visayas. And in another, she told the subcommittee and the assembled stakeholders and media that “the problem is really transmission,” despite earlier testimony from her and other DOE officials that the Visayas generally had a shortage of baseload capacity, which has been aggravated by six generating plants simultaneously going offline earlier this year.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Make up your mind, Sharon. And make it up the right way because anyone with even a modicum of understanding about how the electricity system works already knows that it is not “really a transmission problem.”

What I find rather frustrating is that Secretary Garin, especially since she seems to be particularly image-conscious, is making a rookie mistake in trying to assign blame that doesn’t hold up to scrutiny, whereas if she stuck to the truth, she could make herself out to be the hero for trying to do what she can with a bad situation she inherited. People in the Visayas, business groups, local governments and energy-sector players themselves have been howling about the impending disaster from insufficient generating capacity for years. In 2024, a casual, back-of-the-envelope assessment by a number of concerned parties that I happened to be privy to came up with a reasonably sound estimate that the region overall would need at least 2,000 megawatts of new generation capacity by 2028 to keep up with its power deficit, and more if it wanted to support future growth.

Perhaps, a fourth of that can be accounted for by inter-island connections between the Visayas and Luzon and Mindanao, but no more, and for Garin to imply that the NGCP is somehow dropping the ball because there are not more lines in place to import power into the Visayas contradicts the Philippine Energy Plan and the Transmission Development Plan. The interconnections are intended for the transfer of surplus power, and are more useful for maintaining grid stability rather than being part of the primary supply for parts of the Visayas. Yet they are still managing to fill that role, which should be a credit to the NGCP for doing a good job of building things.

*   ![Image 1: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

Could the NGCP — or, as an alternative, other third-party grid developers operating under the umbrella of the National Transmission Corp. (Transco) — speed things up? Yes, they probably could, with some assistance, but as has been pointed out ad nauseam, transmission doesn’t create power, but only moves it around. If there is a shortage of supply, nothing is going to solve that problem except the development of more supply.

Again, Secretary Garin had the perfect opportunity to position herself as a leader of energy policy doing her best to solve a problem handed down through three successive national administrations. But instead, for reasons only she can explain, she has spent her relatively short time in office — less than two years — in office taking the low road and looking for someone else to blame. It doesn’t scan and, as a result, simply makes her look foolish, out of touch, and not in control of the important policy area placed under her responsibility.

A couple of months ago, I heard a rumor that Secretary Garin would be shuffled out of her job in “the next couple of months,” which, if that was true, would mean about now. The usual suspects among the self-styled consumer energy advocacy have been calling for her resignation lately, and while those are ordinarily to be disregarded, they might accidentally be on to something this time. On the other hand, an abrupt change in leadership at the DOE with less than two years to go in the current administration would be an undesirable signal of instability to the outside investors the country so desperately needs, so I cannot necessarily endorse it. Thus, the best-case scenario would be for our energy secretary to have a little humility, stop pointing fingers, work with those of us trying to modernize the laws governing the power sector, and address actual problems.

title: Political noise unsettles Big Business, but is liberating for democracy
summary: THE second term of United States President Donald Trump shattered all known guardrails of political and ethical discourse. For the ultrarich — mostly men in technology and finance who gravitated to Trump’s orbit just before and especially a
content:
THE second term of United States President Donald Trump shattered all known guardrails of political and ethical discourse. For the ultrarich — mostly men in technology and finance who gravitated to Trump’s orbit just before and especially after he returned to the White House in January 2025 — the equivalent of an “oligarchy unbound” took place. Elon Musk, the richest person on the planet, once said the word he loathed most was “empathy.” Another tech bro said he could now freely say the word “p*ssy” without fear of being reprimanded.

The attitude behind those statements is in sync with the core policies of Trump: gutting the US Agency for International Development, as well as other programs for the poor; mass deportations of immigrants, especially those of color; and tax cuts for the rich. Also, ending all diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programs and initiatives while loosening all regulatory and environmental regulations that used to moderate the rapacity of the favored oligarchy.

In place of what political scientist Francis Fukuyama has described as the best governing structure and the “most ideal” — which was in reference to democracy — the tech bros around Trump described democracy as “inefficient” and “anti-growth.” Their ideal governing structure, in their own words, is a “benevolent monarchy.”

*   [Virata’s political legacy](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/viratas-political-legacy/2441986)

A minor version of that is taking place in the Philippines. We can call it “Big Business Unbound.”

Recently, prominent people speaking on behalf of Philippine Big Business said in very agitated and audacious tones that the current “political noise” — which broadly covers the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte for violating our laws and the Constitution, the incessant clamor of the Duterte camp for the resignation of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and the deeply polarizing rhetoric from opposing political camps — is unsettling the broader economy. They want the political noise to stop so the nation and the polity can focus on more important things.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Specifically, Big Business claimed that political noise has been discouraging investments. Either companies are holding back on their expansions or expanding at reduced levels. Delays in expansions also hold back the deployment of capital and job hirings, both of which drag on the national economy. Investors are holding back possible investments in “these gems of Philippine companies” because of the political noise and turmoil, said one complaint.

It is safe to say these “gems” being referred to are the publicly listed corporate giants controlled by Big Business. It’s also safe to say the message implied is this: to make these companies more profitable and juice up their already gargantuan profits, the political noise should stop.

All those statements said in audacious and agitated tones were, in reality, not for the broader national good but for the vested interests that would have raked in more investments and reaped jumbo profits had it not been for the recurring political noise. It was never for the country nor the broader good. It was to help the ultrarich climb higher on the lists of the Forbes-ranked global dollar billionaires.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

What good does the political noise serve, and why should the many issues being discussed under such noise get proper closure? Plenty. First and foremost, the political noise that Big Business wants to stop is part and parcel of seeking accountability for alleged acts of official corruption, often done with impunity, which is a primary mandate of a democracy. Public office is a public trust, right, and its holders should conduct themselves in a way that is beyond reproach.

The political noise decried by Big Business, i.e., Duterte’s impeachment trial involves looking into a possibly dark underbelly of official corruption that is beyond the pale, which cannot be left unexamined. A democracy is built on truth and compliance with our laws and the Constitution, and on leaders of integrity. It has to stay true to that mandate, never mind the transitory pains while seeking the truth.

The Constitution vests specific mandates on the two chambers of Congress. The House of Representatives is mandated to impeach top executive and constitutional-body officials on the grounds of high crimes, betrayal of public trust, and violations of the laws and the Constitution. The Senate, under the Constitution, should convene an impeachment court where they will serve as senator-judges to try an impeached official. The climax of a trial is the rendering of a verdict ideally based on verifiable evidence. That, actually, is what is playing out in the Duterte princeling’s impeachment trial. The political noise as the fulfillment of a constitutional mandate.

The big revelations that have come out of the impeachment trial have been shocking: the P4.4 billion in bank transactions of Sara Duterte and her husband Mans Carpio; the allegations of money flowing from China into one of the Duterte-linked companies; the mismatch between the declared income and actual wealth; and the allegation that checks had been issued from the Duterte accounts to a suspected drug lord.

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

The political noise has so far exposed that one of the most powerful political families in the country, with poverty and simple living as their long-running shtick, has been transacting money worth billions of pesos — money transactions definitely beyond their pay grades and in violation of laws and the Constitution.

The norms of democracy are duty-bound to see to it that there is a day of reckoning for such transgressions. In that sense, political noise as an act of truth-seeking and accountability-seeking is liberating.

title: When security creates friction, employees find workarounds
summary: SECURITY is meant to protect the business. But when it gets in the way too much, it can do the opposite. That challenge is becoming increasingly visible across Asia-Pacific, where organizations are embracing AI and digital transformation wh
content:
SECURITY is meant to protect the business. But when it gets in the way too much, it can do the opposite. That challenge is becoming increasingly visible across Asia-Pacific, where organizations are embracing AI and digital transformation while employees face pressure to work faster and smarter.

For many employees, security still feels like something that gets in the way. It might be a password reset at the wrong moment, an approval process that holds up a project, or a blocked app that turns a simple task into a headache. When controls are not built around how people actually work, they can push employees toward the behavior the business is trying to stop.

**Shadow AI: a symptom of workplace friction**

*   [Filipino workers fear speaking up about mental health, Telus index finds](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/business/sunday-business-it/filipino-workers-fear-speaking-up-about-mental-health-telus-index-finds/2443041)

Shadow AI is a clear example. If approved systems are difficult to access, limited in functionality or unclear, people may turn to personal devices, public AI platforms or unsanctioned applications.

In most cases, this is not malicious. Employees are trying to solve a problem, whether that means meeting a deadline, responding to a customer or keeping a project moving. But the same instinct that drives productivity can also create hidden exposure.
