 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Our Digital Friction Report found that 40 percent of employees worldwide admit to using personal devices or apps as a workaround when work technology fails. In APAC, India reaches 66 percent, the highest in the study, while Japan sits at 22 percent, the lowest. Australia is at 38 percent.

The risk is not only unapproved tools. These behaviors also reduce visibility. Organizations cannot govern what they cannot see, and they cannot secure activity outside official systems. When security friction pushes work into unmanaged environments, it can make the business less secure, not more.

Shadow AI is therefore not simply a technology problem. It is also a sign that security, governance and employee experience are not working together. Employees may not know which tools they can use or what information can be entered into an AI platform. In some cases, sanctioned tools simply do not support the way a team needs to work.

*   ![Image 1: 2 LTO employees engaged in ‘fixing’ activities arrested](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254480.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[2 LTO employees engaged in ‘fixing’ activities arrested](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/national/2-lto-employees-engaged-in-fixing-activities-arrested/2443156)

Leaders should treat this as a signal of both a policy and design failure. It shows where employees are experiencing friction and where security may be creating gaps rather than closing them.

[![Image 2: DIGITAL FRICTION Employees may seek workarounds when security measures make routine digital tasks difficult. AI-GENERATED GRAPHICS](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254166.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254166.jpg)
DIGITAL FRICTION Employees may seek workarounds when security measures make routine digital tasks difficult. AI-GENERATED GRAPHICS

**Poor digital experiences create business risk**

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

That friction comes at a real cost. The research found that 80 percent of people lose time to broken IT, around 1.3 workdays a month on average worldwide. Across APAC, India loses the most time at 1.9 days a month, while Japan loses the least, at under a day.

Almost half of respondents globally say digital friction has delayed important projects or operations.

What starts as everyday frustration can become a wider business problem, slowing teams down and weakening trust in workplace technology. The challenge is to make the secure route practical, with controls that support how people work rather than interrupting it.

**Security needs to enable productivity**

*   ![Image 4: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Security should enable productivity, not compete with it. Secure processes need to be clear enough to follow and practical enough to fit into daily workflows.

Trust is central to this. Fifty-seven percent of workers do not trust their IT team to resolve issues quickly or effectively, while 47 percent fear their IT team will not adequately protect personal or work-related data. If employees do not trust official routes to meet their needs, they are more likely to find their own.

**AI governance must be part of daily work**

AI tools can enter an organization through different teams and for different reasons. A small productivity experiment can quickly become part of a core workflow, even if no one has clearly defined who owns the risk.

Businesses need clear responsibility for how AI is used and secured. Security teams have an essential role, but they cannot solve this alone. AI governance has to become part of the organization’s operating model, rather than a separate policy. Responsible AI use needs to become part of everyday decisions and behaviors.

Human oversight is also essential. AI can process information at speed, but it does not understand every business context or reputational consequence. People are needed to challenge AI outputs and take responsibility for decisions that carry real-world impact.

Employees also need practical guidance on approved tools and what information should never be entered into them. A policy that is difficult to find will not change behavior.

Across Asia-Pacific, governments are taking different approaches to AI. While regulations continue to evolve, businesses cannot afford to wait for every rule to be finalized before addressing how AI is used inside their organizations.

**Reducing shadow AI starts with understanding the cause**

Reducing shadow AI starts with understanding why employees are using unsanctioned tools. Leaders need to look closely at where approved systems fall short and where security is being introduced too late.

Too often, security is brought in after a tool or process has already been adopted. By then, controls can feel like an extra layer rather than a natural part of the workflow. A security-by-design approach brings security into the conversation earlier, so risks can be addressed before behaviors become embedded.

Employees are more likely to follow security guidance when they understand why it exists and how it supports the wider business. A policy that simply says “do not use this tool” is unlikely to be enough. People need context and confidence that the approved route will help them do their jobs effectively.

Cybersecurity conversations usually focus on outside threats. But businesses also need to look at risks building up inside their own walls, most of them coming from good intentions, not bad ones.

Shadow AI does not tell us that employees are breaking the rules. It tells us that workplace systems need to keep pace with how people work.

The businesses that succeed will not be those with the strictest rules. They will be the ones that make doing the secure thing the easiest thing to do.

Patricia Leppert is the team manager for Customer Trust & Security at TeamViewer, a global technology company that provides remote connectivity, remote access and digital workplace solutions for businesses and organizations.

赖清德在台北总统府前举行的双十国庆典礼上发表演说。(2026年10月10日)

台湾总统赖清德星期六(10月10日)表示，台湾珍惜和平，但不会放弃自由；台湾愿意交流，但不会接受矮化。

赖清德是在台北总统府前举行的庆祝中华民国115年国庆典礼上致辞时作上述表示的。

“台湾展现决心，不让威权侵蚀民主，不让恐惧取代自由，以坚定而负责任的行动，守护台海与印太的和平稳定现状，”赖清德说。

赖清德表示，台湾不求霸权，也不追求支配他人。台湾深知冲突的代价，因此选择以坚持和平为己任，做国际社会可信赖的稳定力量。

“然而，和平不能只靠愿望，包容也不能成为侵略者得寸进尺的理由，”赖清德说。

中华民国因1911年辛亥革命推翻满清而成立，至今已经115年。由国民党总裁蒋介石领导的民国政府由于在国共内战中失利而于1949年被迫播迁台湾。自此，台湾的中华民国和中国共产党在大陆建立的中华人民共和国便隔海相望，各自为政，互不隶属。

台湾自1980年代起实行全面的民主化改革，并成功进行多次政党轮替。而在中国大陆，共产党仍然一党独大，不容任何异议与杂音。但是北京坚持认定两岸同属一个中国，即使诉诸武力也要实行两岸的统一。近年来，随着中国大陆经济和军事实力飙升，北京对台湾的军事恐吓与威胁也愈演愈烈。

由于赖清德领导的民进党政府坚持台湾的未来只能由2300万台湾人自行决定，北京视民进党为“台独”政党，而视赖清德本人为“顽固的台独分子”。

赖清德在国庆演说中援引基督教《圣经》的说法，强调要把台湾打造成“山巅之城”。

“各位国人同胞，山巅之城必须固若金汤，全民团结一心，是维护印太和平与稳定的关键力量，”赖清德说。

他指责北京持续以“军事与灰色地带行动”施压，“企图改变台海现状”。他强调，“武力不能凌驾规则，强权不能剥夺人民决定未来的权利。”

美国虽然在1979年与北京建交前，在中方坚持下与台北断交，但自那时起一直与台湾保持和发展密切的经济、文化、人文交流和伙伴关系。美国还是台湾最重要的武器供应国。唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统主政以来，美国已经向台湾出售价值110亿美元的武器。另有价值140亿美元的售台武器等待特朗普总统签字。

“我们增加国防投资，不是为了挑衅，而是为了吓阻战争。我们强化自我防卫，不是放弃对话，而是确保对话能够在对等、尊严的基础上进行，”赖清德说。

赖清德自2024年胜选就职以来，已多次呼吁两岸在对等、尊严和不预设前提的情况下进行对话，但是他的提议全都遭到北京方面的拒绝。

台湾最大的在野党中国国民党主席郑丽文当天并未出席台北的双十国庆典礼，而是前往台湾南部重镇高雄举办国民党自己的升旗典礼。

郑丽文在致辞时表示，国民党通过与大陆的对话交流，“让下一代不会成为战场上的炮灰。”她批评民进党让两岸关系陷入紧张，让台湾“空转撕裂”。

北京的国台办也于星期六发表声明，抨击赖清德的双十演说“罔顾事实”、“颠倒是非”，指责他“以武谋独”、“依外谋独”，“搅动两岸对立对抗”，“破坏台海和平稳定”。

title: Chinese V American Views On WAR With Taiwan | Armstrong Economics
summary: Spread the love [![Image 1: China v Taiwan 3](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg) The Center for Stra
content:
Spread the love

[![Image 1: China v Taiwan 3](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg)

The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some [**84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification**](https://chinapower.csis.org/survey-experts-china-approach-to-taiwan/ "84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification") but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.

This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.

The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.

[![Image 2: TaiwanMagnified](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/TaiwanMagnified.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/TaiwanMagnified.jpg)

Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.

Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.

A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.

A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA [**blockade**](https://chinapower.csis.org/data/survey-results-chinas-approach-to-taiwan/ "blockade"), while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.

[![Image 3: Taiwan ECM 2](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Taiwan-ECM-2.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Taiwan-ECM-2.jpg)

This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.

Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.

What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.

This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.

If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

content:
【大紀元2026年10月11日訊】（大紀元記者江寒報導）美國司法部尋求剝奪一名幫助中共國安部在美國監視法輪功學員的男子的公民身分。這是美國一系列反擊中共針對法輪功跨國鎮壓行動的最新一拳。

## 李平監視法輪功學員 遭美取消美籍

10月1日，美國司法部向佛羅里達州中區聯邦地區法院提起訴訟，要求取消李平的美國國籍，理由是他違反了美國法典第18篇第371條和第951(a)條，串謀充當外國政府的代理人，且未事先通知司法部長。

司法部文件說，至少從2012年起，李先生就受中共安全部官員的指示，獲取中共政府感興趣的信息，包括有關中國異見人士和民主倡導者、法輪功成員以及美國非政府組織的信息，並將這些信息報告給國安部。

「李先生的行為初步證明，他入籍時並未認同美國憲法的原則，也無意維護美國的良好秩序和幸福。因此，美國提起一項單項指控，要求撤銷其入籍公民身分，」司法部表示。

此前在2024 年 11 月，李已經以「共謀充當中華人民共和國的未註冊代理人」的罪行被判處48 個月監禁、罰款 25 萬美元，並接受三年監視居住。

當年，司法部披露了李監視法輪功學員的細節。司法部文件說，2012年8月，一名中共國安部官員要求李提供美國境內法輪功學員和民主倡議者的資訊。收到這項要求不到一週，李就提供了居住在佛羅里達州聖彼得堡的一名與法輪功有關的人士的姓名和個人資訊。

法輪功是一門佛家修煉方法，以「真善忍」為原則，在1992年由李洪志先生從中國長春傳出，但是從1999年開始遭到中共鎮壓。李監視法輪功學員的行動只是中共將鎮壓法輪功延伸到海外的一個縮影。

## 鎮壓法輪功延伸到海外

自2024年3月以來，中國境外已有超過154起針對法輪功的威脅事件發生。例如，4月25日，由法輪功學員創立的「全球退黨中心」透過其線上聯絡表單收到炸彈威脅。該中心立即通知紐約警察局，紐約警察局隨後疏散並搜查了辦公大樓。

另一個遭受暴力威脅的目標是神韻藝術團，這是一個由法輪功學員創立的中國古典舞蹈團體。神韻是一個以中國古典舞和傳統音樂為主的表演藝術團體。節目涵蓋中國各朝代與歷史故事、神話傳說，以及展現法輪功修煉者在中國受迫害的現實題材。

2018年，神韻首次在以色列演出。演出前中共大使館聯繫了特拉維夫歌劇院的經理，要求取消演出。由於未能說服經理，大使館又試圖透過地方政府和以色列外交部向劇院施壓。2022年，神韻在墨西哥演出前夕，中共駐墨西哥大使館致函克雷塔羅市政府，要求市長辦公室阻止神韻在該市演出。信函聲稱允許神韻演出將「損害中墨友好關係」。

自2024年12月以來，針對法輪功的威脅頻率顯著增加，達到前所未有的水平。

2025年2月20日上午，華盛頓特區的甘迺迪中心收到匿名炸彈威脅，當時劇院正在為神韻藝術團的一系列演出做準備。威脅稱，如果允許神韻演出，炸彈將被引爆。美國其它地區聖荷西、柏克萊、康乃狄克州沃特伯裡、喬治亞州亞特蘭大、德州聖安東尼奧、波多黎各聖胡安等劇院，以及法國、義大利、英國和波蘭的劇院也收到了類似的威脅。

2026年3月29日，多倫多四季表演藝術中心在神韻演出前收到一封炸彈威脅郵件，導致當日演出被迫取消，中心人員緊急疏散。出於擔憂，劇院還取消了原定於4月1日至5日舉行的剩餘五場神韻演出。

此外，自2025年1月以來，威脅目標還包括支持法輪功的民選代表，以及其他美國官員和機構。

中國共產黨也在美國發起了一場抹黑法輪功的宣傳運動。擁有400萬訂閱者和30億次觀看量的保守派網紅蒂姆·普爾（Tim Pool）在2024年底披露，中國共產黨一直在收買網紅傳播反法輪功的言論。普爾被出價200美元發布一段影片。該影片捏造了對法輪功的攻擊，將其醜化。

所有這些威脅、祕密活動和宣傳都是中國共產黨精心策劃的結果。2024年12月，一群追蹤中共鎮壓法輪功學員的海外研究人員公佈了由中共公安部部長王小洪主持的一次視訊會議的記錄。這些記錄顯示，中共正在醞釀的計劃和策略，旨在加大力度在海外，尤其是在美國，打擊法輪功，其明確目標是「破壞法輪功與美國的關係」。

## 中共為跨國鎮壓推新法律 美國警覺

中共跨境鎮壓的對象除了法輪功學員，還包括維吾爾族人、藏族人、臺灣獨立運動人士以及民主運動人士。自2014年以來，這場運動已顯著升級。根據自由之家統計，從2014年至2023年間，發生了214起由中共發起的攻擊事件。

中共通過的一系列新法律，例如《國家情報法》、《香港國安法》和《資料安全法（草案）》，也為跨國鎮壓提供「合理化」。

例如，《國家情報法》要求中國所有組織和公民支持、協助和配合國家情報工作，給海外中國公司和個人戴上了緊箍咒。《資料安全法》和網路安全法規定在中國境內運營或與中國利益相關的國內外實體必須按照國家安全需要處理數據，將商業數據列為潛在的國家祕密，並授予當局廣泛的數據/加密訪問權限。

香港國家安全法第38條規定，顛覆國家政權、煽動叛亂、共謀叛亂等罪行，無論與香港有無關聯，均應處以刑事處罰。

中共的跨國鎮壓行動引起了美國的高度警覺。美國司法部將跨國鎮壓定義為外國政府「越過國界，傷害、恐嚇、威脅、騷擾或脅迫」政治對手、異議人士、活動家和僑民社區成員的行為。

傳統基金會亞洲研究中心前研究員邁克爾·坎寧安2025年八月撰文說，跨國鎮壓不僅威脅人權，也威脅美國和世界各國的主權。

在中共加大力度鎮壓海外法輪功學員的同時，美國政府也加強了反擊跨國鎮壓的力度。

## 美國對「跨國鎮壓」的系列反擊

2026年10月4日，加州華裔房地產經紀張婉瑩在洛杉磯國際機場準備登機前往中國上海時被聯邦探員逮捕。她被控未依法通知美國司法部長，卻充當外國政府代理人。她被控監視和偷拍台灣總統賴清德的兒子賴廷宇。美國眾議院「對中共委員會」週二（10月6日）發表聲明說，這是中共又一次公然侵犯美國主權。

2026年5月，加州阿卡迪亞市長王愛琳辭職，並承認充當中國政府的非法代理人，進行親北京的宣傳。

2026年2月，南加州居民孫耀寧（Mike Sun）被美國地區法官 R. Gary Klausner判處48 個月聯邦監禁。孫承認在未通知美國司法部長的情況下，充當外國政府的非法代理人。檢方稱孫某在中共官員的指示下工作，影響地方政治，包括幫助南加州市議員當選、宣傳親中共的言論，並在2023年4月台灣地區領導人蔡英文訪問加州期間對其進行密切監視。

2024年9月，紐約州前州長高級助手孫雯因涉嫌充當中共政府的未公開外國代理人而被捕，並被控八項聯邦罪名。今年9月，孫雯案追加洗錢共謀罪，其辯護律師接連退出。

2024年8月，居住在紐約皇后區的唐元雋因涉嫌非法充當中共代理人並向聯邦官員作虛假陳述而被捕。至少從2018年起，唐元雋透過共享電子郵件帳戶、加密聊天、簡訊以及音訊和視訊通話，定期接收來自國家安全的指示，並向其匯報被中共視為可能損害其利益的個人和團體。

同月，紐約皇后區居民王書君被聯邦陪審團裁定犯有一系列罪行，包括充當中共非法代理人、非法使用身分信息以及向執法部門作虛假陳述。王書君是某民主組織的創始人之一，他利用其在海外華人社區的地位和影響力，收集知名活動人士、學者和異見人士的信息，並將這些信息報告給中共政府。

2024年7月，居住在加州洛杉磯的陳約翰（John Chen）和林峰（Lin Feng）認罪。他們承認非法充當中共代理人並賄賂美國國稅局（IRS）官員。根據法庭文件，至少從2023年1月到2023年5月，陳約翰和林峰在美國境內受中共政府指示，協助中共政府鎮壓和騷擾法輪功學員。2024年9月，林峰被判處16個月監禁；2024年11月，陳約翰被判處20個月監禁。

2024年5月，紐約州羅斯林居民安全忠承認非法充當中共代理人。安全忠與中共省委員會辦公室成員一同被控參與中共的獵狐行動，強迫一名居住在美國的中國公民返回中國的計劃。

獵狐行動是中共黨魁習近平在2014年發起的一項旨在追捕並遣返攜帶贓物的腐敗官員和逃犯的國際行動。儘管中共聲稱這項行動是反腐敗努力的一部分，但它的策略、目標和真實意圖受到了美國執法機構和人權組織的密切關注和批評。

據聯邦調查局稱，「獵狐行動」為打擊政治異議人士和採取威脅美國主權的脅迫手段提供了默許的掩護。透過將鎮壓目標列為通緝犯，中共得以堂而皇之地發出紅色通緝令，要求國際刑警組織協助抓捕。

2023年6月，美國司法部再次起訴了三名參與獵狐行動的人。陪審團裁定麥可·麥克馬洪、鄭聰穎和朱勇犯有多項罪行。通過參與獵狐行動，這三人威脅、騷擾、監視和恐嚇一名受害者及其家人，以脅迫受害者返回中國。

2023年5月，馬薩諸塞州布萊頓居民梁立堂（Litang Liang）因涉嫌充當中共的非法代理人而被起訴並逮捕。梁立堂的罪行包括向中共政府官員提供異議人士的照片和訊息，並組織了一場針對支持民主的異議人士的反示威活動。

2023年4月，紐約市居民「哈里」盧建旺（音譯，Harry Lu Jianwang）和陳錦平（音譯，Chen Jinping ）因涉嫌串謀充當中共非法代理人以及妨礙司法公正而被捕並被起訴。盧建旺和陳錦平合謀代表中共公安部福建省福州市分局，在美國設立了首個海外派出所。該派出所的任務之一就是，透過騷擾和暴力威脅等手段逼迫一名被中共追捕的人返回中國。

2023年4月，34名中共公安部官員遭到起訴。他們被控串謀跨州散佈威脅和串謀跨州騷擾。起訴書稱，該集團成員涉嫌在社群媒體上創建數千個虛假身分，透過網路騷擾和威脅來針對中國異議人士。

2023年4月，六名中共公安部官員和兩名中國國家互聯網資訊辦公室官員和一名在中國工作的電信公司員工被起訴。他們協助中共審查居住在美國和其他地區人士的政治和宗教言論。

除了對跨國鎮壓採取執法行動，美國也在地方和聯邦層面展開立法行動。

## 美國對跨國鎮壓採取立法行動

2026年9月28日，美國參議院一致通過了S.4009號法案，即《法輪功和強摘器官受害者保護法案》。該法案規定，對於明知故犯地直接參與或協助在中國進行非自願器官摘取的外國個人，將實施財產凍結和吊銷簽證的製裁。

在德州，《跨國鎮壓法案》要求德州公共安全部（DPS）為警官制定跨國鎮壓方面的培訓計劃，內容包括經常參與此類案件/行動的外國政府和外國恐怖組織，以及這些政府和組織所使用的手段。

2025年3月，科羅拉多州共和黨眾議員加布·埃文斯(Gabe Evans)提出了《執法支持和打擊跨國鎮壓法案》，該法案旨在幫助社區瞭解跨國鎮壓，提高公眾對此類威脅的認知度。

2025年四月，眾議院國土安全委員會通過了美國眾議員塞思·馬加齊納提出的 《加強州和地方打擊跨國鎮壓法案》，該法案旨在培訓州和地方執法部門識別和打擊獨裁政權的跨國鎮壓活動。

2025年7月，參議員默克利提出了《跨國鎮壓政策法案》；該法案經兩次宣讀後提交外交關係委員會。該法案要求保護美國境內的人員以及身處美國境外的美國國民免受外國政府違反國際公認人權的行為侵害；鼓勵與志同道合的外國夥伴合作，以減輕跨國鎮壓。

## 七國集團共同反擊跨國鎮壓

跨國鎮壓的黑手不僅僅伸向美國，還伸向世界其他國家。美國國務院在其2024年度《人權狀況國別報告》中，描述了與51個國家政府相關的跨國鎮壓事件。而根據自由之家的統計，從2014年至2025年間，在100多個國家發生了1375起「直接的跨國人身鎮壓事件」。作為肇事者，中共佔據其中的23%，一共319起，排名第一。

為了應對全球範圍的跨國鎮壓，美國與其他國家政府合作進行多邊努力，包括發表聯合聲明和共同製定關於出口管制和人權的國際行為準則。美國參與了七國集團快速反應機制（RRM）下的跨國鎮壓工作小組，該機制旨在加強七國集團在應對外國對民主國家構成的威脅方面的協調。

七國集團領導人在2025年6月的聲明中承諾採取若干措施打擊跨國鎮壓，包括增進全球對此威脅的瞭解；制定 TNR 韌性和應對框架，透過七國集團風險管理機制啟動數位跨國鎮壓檢測機構，該機構將為七國集團及其合作夥伴提供識別和應對最新威脅的技能和工具。

七國集團還承諾，支持那些可能成為跨國鎮壓攻擊目標的人，以及積極致力於應對這一威脅的民間社會成員。+

[查 看 中 国 议 会 发 展 大 事 记](https://chinacongress.net/archives/category/about/cc_dev_chronicle)

# 什么是中国议会

中国议会是一个面向海内外中国人的民主政治平台，旨在通过一人一票产生议员，实践议会民主，并为未来中国的民主宪政积累制度和经验。2026年1月4日，89.64学运领袖王丹先生在美国洛杉矶发起成立中国议会筹备委员会，将于12月31日之前完成第一届选民登记，并开启第一届中国议会议员选举。

title: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week
summary: **MANILA, Philippines**— The Senate impeachment court will determine on Monday how to proceed with the prosecution’s reported decision to drop Article III of the impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte, with the move poten
content:
**MANILA, Philippines**— The Senate impeachment court will determine on Monday how to proceed with the prosecution’s reported decision to drop Article III of the impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte, with the move potentially affecting the trial calendar and the sequence of presenting evidence.

Senate impeachment court spokesman Regie Tongol said the court had received a formal manifestation seeking to drop Article III, but the matter remains subject to action by the presiding officer, Senator Francis “Chiz" Escudero.

“The manifestation filed with the impeachment court will suffice,” Tongol told reporters during his press briefing following the 37th day of the trial on Oct. 10, adding that the court would await the presiding officer’s action or any questions he might raise on the matter.

*   [Aguda resigns as DICT secretary amid Discord criticism, Ombudsman probe](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/aguda-resigns-as-dict-secretary-amid-discord-criticism-ombudsman-probe/2442996)

House of Representatives lead prosecutor Chel Diokno announced that the prosecution would rest its case on Article II after presenting financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera. Tongol said the prosecution’s next move would depend on the court’s action on the manifestation concerning Article III.

The prosecution has yet to formally rest its case on Article I. Tongol recalled that Diokno had been preparing to do so when the presiding officer raised the possibility of presenting additional witnesses, including Col. Lachica and Maj. Gen. Nolasco.

 delivered to your inbox

The court must therefore await the House prosecution panel’s decision on how to proceed with the remaining article, he said.

Tongol declined to predict whether dropping Article III would alter the trial calendar or when Duterte’s defense could begin presenting evidence. He said the court would have to determine whether to allow a period for the formal offer of prosecution evidence and the defense’s comments, as is customary in ordinary court proceedings.

While expediting the trial remains a priority, Tongol stressed that speed must not come at the expense of due process.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

“The impeachment court will have to consider everything to balance the interests of everyone,” he said, adding that procedural pauses should not automatically be considered unreasonable delays.

The court is also expected to clarify whether the defense must present its evidence in the same sequence as the prosecution’s articles or may choose its preferred order.

Tongol said either approach was possible, but emphasized that the presiding officer would have to rule on the question.

title: 賴清德：打造山巔之城 讓台灣成世界之光

content:
【大紀元2026年10月10日訊】（大紀元記者鍾元台灣報導）中華民國總統賴清德10月10日以「台灣 山巔之城，地上的鹽，世上的光」為題發表國慶演講。他指出，中共持續以軍事與灰色地帶行動施壓，企圖改變台海現狀。面對威權擴張，政府持續推動國防改革，強化不對稱戰力，發展國防自主產業，讓半導體、資通訊與精密製造的優勢，轉化為守護國家的力量。

賴清德提到，「我們也必須指出，要維護區域的安全、和平與穩定，不但要正確理解歷史的發展，絕不容許扭曲二戰歷史，也要尊重台灣人民生存的權利，更要結合印太地區民主國家的共同力量，不讓區域和平穩定的現狀被改變。」

10日上午，賴清德在總統府府前廣場舉行的「中華民國中樞暨各界慶祝115年國慶大會」，發表國慶演講。

賴清德說，大會主席韓國瑜院長、蕭美琴副總統、行政院卓榮泰院長、史瓦帝尼王國恩史瓦帝三世國王陛下、祖瑪王妃殿下、「日本台灣友好議員聯盟」古屋圭司會長、友邦、友好國家的慶賀團團長、各國駐台使節、海內外貴賓，現場以及收看電視和直播的國人同胞，大家好！

他說，「今天我們齊聚在總統府前，一起慶祝中華民國國慶，共同為台灣喝采，祝福國家生日快樂，國運昌隆！此時此刻，無論我們人在台灣，或身處世界不同角落；無論我們來自不同世代、不同職業，抱持不同的政治立場，都立足在台灣；也共同承擔一份責任，就是讓國家更安全、社會更安定、人民生活更美好，讓下一代對未來充滿希望。」

## 國家的主人是人民；台灣的未來，要由台灣人民決定

今年是台灣總統直選30週年。賴清德說，30年前，面對飛彈（大陸稱導彈）威脅，台灣人民依然勇敢走進投票所，完成台灣人民「當家作主」的百年追求，用手中的選票告訴世界：這個國家的主人，是人民；台灣的未來，要由台灣人民自己決定。

賴清德說，「30年來，我們走過民主轉型，經歷政黨輪替，也承受許多挑戰。今天，我們更加確信，自由民主與經濟發展不會背道而馳。台灣越是擁抱民主、迎向世界，就越能創造繁榮，也越有能力為世界做出貢獻。」

## 台灣在世界變局中站穩腳步，展現令人驕傲的韌性

「過去一年，世界並不平靜。」他指出，戰爭與威權持續擴張，全球經濟面臨關稅、能源與紅色供應鏈的多重挑戰。然而，台灣沒有退縮，反而在變局中站穩腳步，展現令人驕傲的韌性。就像台灣健兒在亞運表現精采，讓世界看見台灣的韌性與驕傲。

他感謝百工百業的打拚，經濟表現也非常亮眼。今年，光是上半年，最新的經濟增長率，達到14.15％。而全年的經濟增長率更有望突破11％，創下39年新高；今年，台灣的人均GDP，預估也將達到4萬5,332美元，幾乎是2016年的兩倍。台股指數衝上4萬9千點，成為全球第四大股市。

賴清德說，在外交上，台灣也一步一步走得更遠。今年，他前往史瓦帝尼（陸譯斯威士蘭）王國進行國是訪問，感謝恩史瓦帝三世國王陛下的熱情接待，以及王母陛下與全國人民的熱烈歡迎，見證雙方在能源、農業、醫療、婦女賦權及教育文化上的合作。

此外，他說，副總統蕭美琴訪問帛琉（陸譯帕勞），深化醫療、農漁業、基礎建設及永續觀光的成果，並應邀赴義大利（陸譯意大利）出席文托泰內歐洲自由與民主論壇，讓台灣的聲音在象徵歐洲自由與民主的重要場域被世界聽見。

賴清德說，而在今年瑞士洛桑管理學院的世界競爭力排名中，台灣在「經濟表現」、「政府效能」、「企業效能」與「基礎建設」都名列前茅，一舉衝上全球第四具競爭力的國家，創下有史以來最好的佳績。這些成就，毫無疑問，屬於2,300萬台灣人民；也是政府攜手無數台灣人民，不分領域，共同努力，一點一滴所勤奮打拚的成果。他要邀請所有國人同胞，再次用熱烈的掌聲，為自己喝采。

「在戰爭與威權擴張、全球秩序快速變動的時代，台灣應該成為什麼樣的國家？」賴清德說，他的答案是：勇敢自信的打造「山巔之城」！「這不是對自己的讚美，而是我們對國家未來的期許，也是台灣願意承擔的責任。」

賴清德表示，各位國人同胞，山巔之城，是建造在護國群山之上，是民主治理的美好成果，讓人民在堅實的基礎上安心生活；因此，一座山巔之城不能只有耀眼的天際線，更要有穩固的地基。

「台灣的地基，就是人民的生活。」他說，國家是否進步，不能只看產值與出口，更要看勞工待遇有沒有提高、家庭負擔有沒有減輕、長輩是否受到照顧，以及年輕人是否相信，努力就能創造更好的未來。「因此，我們以務實治理，推動加薪、減稅、增福利、少負擔，讓這個國家裡的每一個人，都能站得穩、過得好。」

賴清德說，面對少子女化，政府在「0到6歲國家一起養」的基礎上，提出「台灣人口對策新戰略—家庭支持篇」，從生育、養育到教育，以加補助、減負擔、多彈性、增照顧，建立更完整的家庭支持。

他說，政府規劃從明年開始，推動0到18歲成長津貼，每個孩子每月5千元，並結合生育給付、人工生殖補助、平價托育、友善職場與婚育住宅，讓工作與家庭，不再成為年輕人被迫二選一的難題。養育孩子，不應是一個家庭孤軍奮戰。支持一個家庭，就是守護台灣的未來。

面對超高齡社會，他說，政府推動「健康台灣」，從癌症篩檢、智慧醫療、在宅照護，到改善醫療工作環境與護理人力，讓國人不只活得長壽，也要活得健康。今年上路的長照3.0，進一步整合醫療、社福、社區與科技，讓長輩在熟悉的生活圈獲得照顧，也讓上有老、下有小的三明治世代，多一分支持，少一分辛苦。

面對居住壓力，他說，政府持續推動「百萬租屋家庭支持計劃」，透過直接興建社會住宅、包租代管、租金補貼，還有都市更新分回及容積獎勵等多元方式增加供給，並調升婚育宅比例、實施青安3.0，提高婚育家庭貸款額度。安居才能樂業，安居也才能讓年輕人勇敢成家，追求夢想。

面對缺工與人才不足，他說，政府推動「跨國勞動力精進方案」，堅持本國勞工為主、跨國勞動力為輔，以加薪連動增聘人力，放寬資深移工轉任技術人力的留用限制，並推動國對國直接聘僱。政府也修正《外國專業人才延攬及僱用法》，擴大國際人才與外籍生來台、留台的機會。讓企業補足人力，也讓勞工提高待遇；讓人才願意來，更願意留下來。社會安全，同樣是這座山巔之城不可動搖的根基。

面對詐騙，他說，政府將行政院打擊詐欺指揮中心列為常設性任務編組，整合內政、法務、數發與金融監理力量，串聯檢察、金融及平台業者，從廣告、通訊、帳戶到金流，阻斷犯罪鏈。

面對毒品與毒駕，他表示，政府持續推動「新世代反毒策略行動綱領」，強化緝毒、驗毒、戒毒與識毒，向上追查毒品來源，並運用唾液毒品快篩加強路檢，即時阻止危險駕駛。人民辛苦累積的財產、每一個家庭珍貴的生命，政府都要全力守護。政府也積極推動修法，毒駕初犯最高罰15萬；拒絕受測，重罰27萬；累犯罰款不設上限，一律吊銷駕照，強制沒入車輛，同車乘客，也將連帶受罰。政府會從嚴執法，絕不寬貸。

面對能源與氣候挑戰，他說，政府以穩定供電、能源安全及淨零轉型為目標，推動多元綠能、儲能、節能與電網強韌建設，也會依科學證據、法定程序及安全標準，務實評估各種能源選項。能源政策不能建立在口號上，必須建立在安全、專業和責任上；我們不為意識形態排除選項，也不會為短期利益犧牲世代永續。

賴清德表示，山巔之城的高度，不是政府自己宣告的，而是由人民的生活，一層一層築起。「我們要讓世界看見，民主不只有選擇的自由，更有解決問題、照顧人民的能力。」

## 台灣守護民主、自由、人權及法治，不讓威權侵蝕珍貴的普世價值

賴清德強調，各位國人同胞，山巔之城，必須固若金湯，全民團結一心，是維護印太和平與穩定的關鍵力量。就像鹽雖微小，卻能調和百味、防腐保鮮。台灣的國土不大，但我們守護民主、自由、人權及法治，不讓威權侵蝕珍貴的普世價值。

「我們不求霸權，也不追求支配他人。我們深知衝突的代價，因此選擇以堅持和平為己任，做國際社會可信賴的穩定力量。然而，和平不能只靠願望，包容也不能成為侵略者得寸進尺的理由。」賴清德說。

## 中共持續以軍事與灰色地帶行動施壓，企圖改變台海現狀

賴清德指出，中共持續以軍事與灰色地帶行動施壓，企圖改變台海現狀。面對威權擴張，台灣的堅持，不只關乎自己的生存，也關乎國際社會是否仍然相信：武力不能凌駕規則，強權不能剝奪人民決定未來的權利。因此，我們持續推動國防改革，強化不對稱戰力，發展國防自主產業，讓半導體、資通訊與精密製造的優勢，轉化為守護國家的力量。

他說，政府也透過全社會防衛韌性的準備，整合中央、地方與民間量能，提升能源、通訊、交通、金融、糧食與醫療的持續運作能力。讓危機來臨時，社會能夠穩定運作，人民知道如何保護自己、協助彼此。他要感謝所有國軍官兵、後備軍人、警察、消防、醫護、民防，以及參與演練的國人。你們每一次認真的準備，都是為台灣的和平，多築起一道防線。

「我們增加國防投資，不是為了挑釁，而是為了嚇阻戰爭；我們強化自我防衛，不是放棄對話，而是確保對話能在對等、尊嚴的基礎上進行。」賴清德說。

賴清德表示，「我們樂見美中透過對話來管理競爭，降低衝突及戰爭的風險，但是，我們也必須指出，要維護區域的安全、和平與穩定，不但要正確理解歷史的發展，絕不容許扭曲二戰歷史，也要尊重台灣人民生存的權利，更要結合印太地區民主國家的共同力量，不讓區域和平穩定的現狀被改變。」

他指出，台灣珍惜和平，但不會放棄自由；台灣願意交流，但不會接受矮化。台灣展現決心，不讓威權侵蝕民主，不讓恐懼取代自由，以堅定而負責任的行動，守護台海與印太的和平穩定現狀。

賴清德說，各位國人同胞，山巔之城，城門要向世界自由開放，讓世界的光照進城裡；城中的光，則以創新、平等與良善，為世界帶來希望。光，不只照亮自己，也讓他人看見方向。「台灣的光，來自人民的智慧與勤奮，來自產業的創新，也來自我們願意與世界分享成果的選擇。」

「從傳統產業到先進半導體，台灣用實力證明，一個資源有限的島嶼，也能成為全球繁榮不可或缺的力量。但我們不會停在今天的成就，行政院正加速推動13項核心戰略產業，涵蓋半導體、人工智慧、軍工、安控、次世代通訊等五大信賴產業；以及矽光子、量子運算、機器人等AI新十大建設所聚焦的三大核心科技。」賴清德說。

賴清德接著說，還有關鍵礦物、生技醫療、亞洲資產管理中心、基礎公共建設及都市更新、文化創意、兆元觀光等六項重點產業，來確保台灣下一個世代的競爭優勢；也透過千億元規模的中小微企業多元振興發展計劃，提供融資、人才培訓、數位轉型、淨零升級與國際通路支持。

他說，科技產業要繼續向前，也要帶著傳統產業一起走；龍頭企業要走向世界，也要帶動供應鏈在台灣扎根。台灣不能只有一座護國神山，而要讓百工百業共同成為護國群山。

## 讓全民共享經濟發展的成果

「經濟的光，也必須照進人民的生活。」賴清德說，「我們連續11年調升最低工資，軍公教10年來5次調薪，也在今年調升專業與主管加給，透過加薪誘因與社會支持，讓成長轉化為更好的待遇、更少的負擔」；政府也規劃在財政穩健的基礎上，普發每人1萬元；老農津貼每人每月1萬元，國民年金每人每月5千元；弱勢家庭等六大社福津貼，也全面提升，讓全民共享經濟發展的成果。

賴清德提到，「在國際上，我們以醫療、農業、能源、科技、教育與永續發展合作，回應夥伴的需要。台灣的專業與善意，化為改善生活的實際行動。」「Taiwan Can Help」，不是一句口號，而是台灣願意分享能力、承擔責任的承諾。台灣的光，要跨越國界，讓更多需要幫助的人，感受到溫暖與希望。

## 台灣將迎來九合一地方選舉 賴清德籲選賢與能 國人團結前行

他說，「再過不久，我們將迎來九合一地方選舉，選賢與能、不受威脅利誘是我們共同的責任；政黨可以競爭，意見可以不同，但我們立足的台灣，不應因此被分割。山巔之城，不是因為沒有分歧才發光，而是因為即使意見不同，我們仍然尊重彼此，相信制度，也願意共同守護國家。」

「總統的權力，來自人民的託付；總統的責任，就是凝聚力量，帶領國家向前。」他會以務實治理，築起山巔之城；以堅定的民主與防衛力量，成為守護和平的鹽；以創新、平等與良善，成為溫暖世界的光。

最後，賴清德說，「各位國人同胞，讓我們團結一起，為下一個30年的台灣：打下更堅實的基礎，更有力的競爭優勢，讓下一代站得更穩、走得更遠。中華民國加油！台灣加油！」

責任編輯：葉紫微#

title: Taiwan needs a 'chain of guardian mountains' across industries: Lai - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) said on Saturday that Taiwan needed many industries across its economy to become a "chain of guardian mountains" to broaden the foundation of its economic strength. In his National Day addr
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) said on Saturday that Taiwan needed many industries across its economy to become a "chain of guardian mountains" to broaden the foundation of its economic strength.

In his National Day address outside the Presidential Office, Lai said leading companies expanding overseas should help their supply chains establish deeper roots in Taiwan.

"We cannot rely on just one guardian mountain; we must ensure that all sectors join together to form a chain of guardian mountains," Lai said.

His statement appeared to refer to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., the world's largest contract chipmaker and a pillar of Taiwan's economy. The United States, Japan and other countries have encouraged it to build factories abroad to strengthen supply security and reduce reliance on Taiwan.

Lai outlined government measures to support that development, highlighting Taiwan's strong economic performance while warning of challenges from tariffs, energy issues and competition from Chinese supply chains.

Taiwan's economy grew 14.15 percent in the first half of 2026, he noted. Full-year growth could exceed 11 percent, which would be the highest rate in 39 years, while per capita gross domestic product was projected to reach US$45,332, almost double its 2016 level.

The benchmark Taiex had reached 49,000 points, Lai said, with Taiwan's stock market becoming the world's fourth largest by market capitalization.

He also cited Taiwan's fourth-place finish in this year's World Competitiveness Ranking compiled by the Swiss-based Institute for Management Development, describing it as the country's best performance to date.

To sustain Taiwan's competitiveness, Lai said the Executive Yuan was accelerating the development of strategic industries and emerging technologies.

He highlighted the government's Five Trusted Industry Sectors -- semiconductors, artificial intelligence, defense, security and surveillance, and next-generation communications -- alongside the three core technologies targeted by its 10 new AI infrastructure initiatives: silicon photonics, quantum computing and robotics.

Technological advances should also benefit traditional industries, Lai said.

Other priorities include critical minerals, biotechnology and healthcare, an Asian asset management hub, public infrastructure and urban renewal, cultural and creative industries, and developing tourism into a trillion-NT-dollar industry.

A separate program for micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, with a scale of NT$100 billion (US$3.13 billion), would support financing, workforce training, digital transformation, net-zero upgrades and access to international distribution channels, Lai said.

To address labor and talent shortages, Lai said the government would maintain Taiwanese workers as the primary workforce, supplemented by workers recruited from overseas.

Measures include linking higher local wages to additional migrant worker quotas, easing retention restrictions on experienced migrant workers transitioning into skilled roles, and promoting direct government-to-government recruitment.

Amendments to the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals would also expand opportunities for international professionals to come to and remain in Taiwan and for foreign students to stay after graduation, he said.

On energy, Lai said the government would pursue stable electricity supply, energy security and a net-zero transition through renewable generation, storage, conservation and grid upgrades.

It would also pragmatically assess different energy options based on scientific evidence, legal procedures and safety standards, he said.

"We will not rule out options solely for ideological reasons, nor will we compromise the sustainability of future generations for short-term gains," he said.

Economic gains must also translate into better living standards, Lai said, citing 11 consecutive years of minimum wage increases, five pay raises for military personnel, civil servants and teachers over the past decade, and increases in professional and supervisory allowances this year.

He also outlined plans for a universal NT$10,000 cash payment and higher welfare benefits.

The goal, he said, was to ensure that prosperity was reflected not only in production and exports, but also in better pay and lighter burdens for families.

(By Chao Yen-hsiang)

Enditem/cs

title: Taiwan president says defence spending boost aims to ‘deter war’
source: 菲律宾在中国紧张局势中加强其最北端的防御
summary: _President Lai emphasises peace and freedom, vows not to tolerate aggression in Taiwan Strait._ Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te has said the island “cherishes peace” and will “not give up our freedom” in a National Day speech outside the Pr
content:
_President Lai emphasises peace and freedom, vows not to tolerate aggression in Taiwan Strait._

Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te has said the island “cherishes peace” and will “not give up our freedom” in a National Day speech outside the Presidential Office in Taipei.

Lai made the remarks on Saturday before thousands of people, including foreign diplomats.

end of list
“We are open to exchanges, but will not accept subordination,” he said. “Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke; rather, it is to deter war.”

Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of the speech.

The holiday marks the 115th anniversary of a 1911 uprising that toppled China’s last imperial dynasty and led to the founding of the Republic of China.

## Pressure from China

Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the [constant threat](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2/us-delivers-f-16v-fighter-jets-to-taiwan-as-island-eyes-threat-from-china) of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory, has never renounced the use of force to take it, and calls Lai a “separatist”.

Beijing has rebuffed his offers of talks.

Lai said China continued to “apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait”.

Grey-zone tactics are actions that stop short of open war. “Peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” he added.

Lai’s government has set aside a record 1.1 trillion New Taiwan dollars ($34.5bn) for defence in 2027, more than 3 percent of gross domestic product.

China held war games around the island shortly after Lai’s first National Day speech in 2024, but not last year. Its last drills near Taiwan were in late December, after news of an $11bn arms deal with Washington, the largest ever US weapons package for the island.

Lai said he welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist”.

Officials in Washington and Taipei have repeatedly said US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump.

In May, after meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, Trump suggested arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China, which set off alarm across the world.

Taiwan is now waiting for Trump to sign off on $14bn worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defence system.

title: The US and China Cannot Slow the AI Race, But They Can Make It Safer
source: 害怕军事上软弱的中国——外交官
summary: The most important shift in artificial intelligence (AI) is not that models are becoming more intelligent, but that they are becoming more capable of acting. Much of the first wave of AI safety governance focused on misinformation, bias, de
content:
The most important shift in artificial intelligence (AI) is not that models are becoming more intelligent, but that they are becoming more capable of acting.

Much of the first wave of AI safety governance focused on misinformation, bias, deepfakes, privacy violations and harmful content. Those risks remain. But increasingly capable AI agents can plan, write and execute code, use tools, obtain credentials, and interact with external systems. [Recent incidents](https://time.com/article/2026/07/24/openai-hugging-face-attack/) in which OpenAI’s autonomous systems slipped past their constraints show that as agents gain tools and autonomy, the boundary between a model and the outside world becomes harder to enforce.

That makes AI safety a collective-action problem. The AI superpowers face a prisoner’s dilemma. If one laboratory slows while competitors continue, it may lose its edge. Disclosure creates a similar tension: reporting failures can make the wider ecosystem safer, but the discloser bears the costs and may expose vulnerabilities to attackers. Governments face the same strategic impasse as the firms. Washington fears that slowing its AI development will allow China to catch up; Beijing fears that doing so will leave it further behind.

Yet cooperation can be narrow on AI safety. The United States does not need to trust China, share frontier models with China, or slow its own AI development to have a national security interest in such cooperation. It has an interest in ensuring that AI-enabled cyber incidents are contained before they cascade through third countries, shared software infrastructure and global supply chains. China has the same systemic interest.

This collective action has significant implications for middle-power countries. Helping others repair a vulnerability can be a form of systemic containment and a public good.

**The Accelerating AI Race**

The AI arms race is intensifying.

U.S. President Donald Trump has rejected calls to slow U.S. AI development, framing continued technological leadership as essential to [winning the AI race](https://apnews.com/article/e560910c897fedb0448eda4cdbfdbaea). On September 29, he convened major technology companies at the White House, where six firms – OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI and Nvidia – signed [a voluntary accord](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/trump-host-zuckerberg-anthropics-amodei-other-ai-titans-tuesday-2026-09-29/) built around four layers of oversight: internal capability assessments, internal audit teams, independent external auditors, and board-level review. His administration ordered federal agencies to replace the term “artificial intelligence” with “[super intelligence](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/09/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence/),” presenting the technology as a source of economic and strategic leadership.

Taken together, these moves point to a U.S. approach combining continued AI power with developer responsibility, voluntary industry controls, external scrutiny, and ex-post legal accountability.

China approaches the problem through a more centrally coordinated system. In May 2026, [guidelines on AI agents](https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-05/08/c_1779979789523320.htm), issued jointly by the Cyberspace Administration of China, the National Development and Reform Commission, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, made “safety and controllability” a baseline requirement for agent development and deployment. Governance is tiered, with tighter filing, testing and recall requirements for agents used in sensitive sectors.

On September 14, [China’s AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0](https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-09/14/c_1791137092283345.htm) reiterated “safety and controllability” while updating its classification of AI risks and associated technical and governance measures.

Despite their institutional differences, the two approaches converge on one point: neither country wants safety policy to halt AI development, and both increasingly recognize that greater autonomy creates new problems of control.

**Common Ground and Shared Risks**

AI systems rest on overlapping technological foundations. [Chinese AI development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437) has relied heavily on U.S. chips and, in some cases, U.S. cloud infrastructure. Export controls may weaken those hardware links, but the stronger case for joint risk management lies in the software and services AI systems share.

Standards, certificates, identity infrastructure, model repositories, and open-source libraries support trust across networks. A compromised root certificate or a maintainer’s credentials can put the entire dependency tree [at risk](https://www.enisa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/all_files/Operation_Black_Tulip_v2.pdf).

AI risks vary along two dimensions: severity of harm and whether responsible actors can recognize it in time. The biggest danger is severe and invisible harm, where nothing visibly breaks for days or weeks, yet time compounds the severity of the incident. An AI agent could quietly corrupt records, act on instructions planted in its memory or in documents it consults, or appear cooperative while accumulating access beyond operator intent. Infrastructure may operate normally while the means to disrupt it are already in place.

The dependencies and shared risks determine which code a system runs, which credentials it accepts, and which updates it trusts. Harm can cross borders quietly even when models and their owners remain separate.

That makes the speed of response critical. Delays in detecting a breach, assigning responsibility or authorizing a shutdown can allow damage to spread. Both China and the United States therefore need warnings to reach personnel with the authority and technical means to respond.

**Make the Race Safer**

There is no obvious diplomatic agreement that can resolve the paradox built into the AI race: it rewards speed and secrecy, while safety depends on collective restraint and disclosure.

China-U.S. cooperation should instead focus on measures that improve safety without requiring either side to slow unilaterally, transfer its most advanced models, or expose commercially and strategically sensitive capabilities. Four areas stand out:

#### _1. Keeping humans in control_

Before the Trump-Xi summit, American and Chinese security experts in a long-running bilateral dialogue [proposed](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-china-security-experts-propose-nuclear-style-safeguards-ai-risks-2026-09-17/) red lines around nuclear systems, human control over consequential cyber operations, and a dedicated mechanism for AI incidents.

When an AI agent can search, authenticate, write code, call external tools, and act within minutes or seconds, where should human intervention occur? Requiring approval for every step would undermine the autonomous value of AI agents; waiting until something goes wrong may make intervention too late.

The harder questions concern permissions, escalation thresholds, shutdown mechanisms and which actions should always require explicit human authorization. Researchers could cooperate on these engineering challenges without sharing model weights, training data, or proprietary frontier capabilities.

#### _2. Test the guardrails, not each other’s secrets_

Sandboxing, monitoring, permission controls, and model-level refusals are often treated as established safeguards.

The underlying technical risk is broad: with appropriate tools and access, advanced models could identify previously unknown vulnerabilities and develop exploits across well-protected systems without step-by-step human direction. The key question is not whether a developer has guardrails, but whether they still work as agents become capable enough to search for ways around them.

While frontier AI labs in the U.S. have voluntarily disclosed instances of their models escaping from sandboxed environments, public reporting from China on comparable containment failures remains limited. This lack of transparency shouldn’t stop the two sides from working together. Washington and Beijing could develop compatible methods for testing sandbox escape, scope violations, unauthorized tool use, shutdown resistance, and failures of human intervention. Independent auditors, potentially from trusted third countries, could help verify the results.

#### _3. Contain first, attribute later with care_

Cyber attribution has always been challenging. AI makes it harder.

A defender discovering unauthorized access may be looking at a state-directed operation, a criminal actor using AI, a human-directed autonomous agent, or an agent that has exceeded its instructions while pursuing a legitimate task.

Between strategic rivals, that ambiguity is especially dangerous when the trust deficit widens. An autonomous system interacting with critical infrastructure could be mistaken for reconnaissance or preparation for attack before either government understands what happened.

American and Chinese experts have already [identified this risk](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-china-security-experts-propose-nuclear-style-safeguards-ai-risks-2026-09-17/): autonomous cyber exchanges could move faster than governments can determine whether an operation was deliberate, accidental, or unauthorized.

Washington and Beijing are unlikely to agree routinely on the attribution of contentious cyber incidents. They could instead develop common technical expectations about the evidence that should be examined before an AI-enabled incident is escalated politically, including agent logs, credential use, tool-invocation records, model provenance, human authorization, and network telemetry. In the first hours of a major cross-border incident, governments and trusted responders should be able to exchange technical indicators, containment measures, and patch information without first deciding who is responsible. Exchanging such information need not imply an admission of responsibility.

#### _4. Close the AI remediation gap_

Cybersecurity has struggled with remediation for decades. Critical infrastructure is fragmented across hospitals, utilities, telecommunications networks, ports, government agencies, and private vendors. A vulnerability may be understood and a patch may exist, yet deployment can still take days or weeks.

AI compresses the time between vulnerability discovery and exploitation. A capable model may identify a weakness, develop a working exploit, and begin using it faster than organizations can patch their systems.

This creates an emerging AI remediation gap: offensive capability increasingly operates at machine speed, while much of the world still responds at the slower pace of human decision-making and institutional coordination across multiple stakeholders.

Most countries will not train the world’s most capable AI models themselves. Their defensive capacity may therefore depend increasingly on capabilities developed in a small number of frontier ecosystems. If frontier defensive capability arrives only at another power’s discretion – or not at all – exposed systems have no reliable recourse in a crisis.

Closing this gap requires extending access to frontier defensive capability to these countries.

An affected operator or national CERT (Computer Emergency Response Team) could provide malware samples, vulnerable code, selected system logs, or configuration information through a trusted technical intermediary. A frontier defensive model could then help analyze the incident, validate vulnerabilities, generate and test patches, and return a remediation package, while the underlying model and its most sensitive capabilities remain with the provider.

The United States and China also have reasons to support such a system out of self-interest. An AI-enabled vulnerability left unpatched elsewhere can spread through open-source software, cloud infrastructure, model re

title: Isaias makes landfall along the US Gulf Coast as a dangerous Category 2 hurricane
summary: **GULF BREEZE, Florida**— Hurricane Isaias crashed into the US Gulf Coast as a dangerous Category 2 storm on Friday, lashing communities with wind and rain and threatening to flood low-lying areas where residents were advised to evacuate ah
content:
**GULF BREEZE, Florida**— Hurricane Isaias crashed into the US Gulf Coast as a dangerous Category 2 storm on Friday, lashing communities with wind and rain and threatening to flood low-lying areas where residents were advised to evacuate ahead of its arrival.

The first hurricane of the Atlantic season made landfall near Destin, Florida, the Miami-based National Hurricane Center said. It had maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (169 kph). The storm weakened to just below major hurricane status before it came ashore.

High winds whipped palm trees and thundering waves crashed along the beaches of the Florida Panhandle and Alabama on Friday as Isaias approached.

*   [Japan protests Russia’s extradition requests for ICC president Tomoko Akane and 8 other court staff](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/world/americas-emea/japan-protests-russias-extradition-requests-for-icc-president-tomoko-akane-and-8-other-court-staff/2442504)

“The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said at a news conference, adding that flash flooding would be a hazard "throughout the region.”

Forecasters warned of a significant storm surge, damaging winds, flooding and possibly even tornadoes before the storm loses steam as it moves inland and delivers strong winds and rain well north into Atlanta.

Hurricane-force winds lashed the Gulf shoreline in the low-lying coastal area known for powdery white sand beaches that are dotted with vacation homes, waterfront bars and seafood shacks.

In Mobile, Alabama, officials reported downed trees and power lines, while Emerald Coast Utilities Authority, which serves parts of Florida, issued a boil-water notice for its customers.

More than 400,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were without power Friday evening, according to poweroutage.com.

*   ![Image 1: Aguda resigns as DICT secretary amid Discord criticism, Ombudsman probe](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253982.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Aguda resigns as DICT secretary amid Discord criticism, Ombudsman probe](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/aguda-resigns-as-dict-secretary-amid-discord-criticism-ombudsman-probe/2442996)

A hurricane warning was in place from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the western Florida Panhandle. Several counties announced mandatory evacuations while Mobile, Alabama, imposed a curfew beginning Friday evening until morning.

Residents in Panama City, Florida, braved the rain while filling sandbags Friday to protect their houses.

“I mean, it’s just the nature of the beast. It’s Florida," said Corliss Stone, who works for the fire department.

**Many will brave Isaias at home**

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

One of the biggest concerns is a storm surge that could be as high as 6 to 9 feet (1.8 to 2.7 meters), according to the hurricane center. Places most at risk include Florida’s Pensacola Beach and the Gulf Islands National Seashore.

Anne Petzold, who lives with her husband in the Florida beach community of Gulf Breeze, said everyone in their neighborhood planned to ride out the storm. The couple installed hurricane shutters and picked up anything in their yard that could turn into a projectile.

“Everybody does what they can do, everybody asks if they need help — they ask for help, they offer help. All good,” she said. “It’s just another adventure.”

Dangerous conditions are expected throughout the western panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi, the National Hurricane Center said.

*   ![Image 3: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

In a sign of how serious the warnings are, dozens of Waffle Houses in the Florida Panhandle were closed, according to the company's website. The beloved Southern breakfast chain is known for staying open through severe weather and often is a measuring stick of a storm’s severity.

Kelsei Frazier, a Florida-native living in Pace who is no stranger to hurricanes, knows all about the Waffle House Index.

“We joke because if Waffle House is still open, then you know it’s not a bad hurricane, but all the Waffle Houses that I know of within at least a normal range from us are closed,” said Frazier. “Which is a pretty big deal.”

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis warned residents to expect power outages, gasoline shortages and closures of bridges and highways.

The state's National Guard deployed about 5,000 soldiers and airmen to help with the response, and search and rescue teams were ready to respond, while some prisons evacuated inmates.

**The whole region could get soaked**

Isaias is expected to weaken and be downgraded to a tropical storm by Saturday afternoon, the center said.

Still, heavy rain is forecast as it moves inland, with 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 centimeters) or even more expected through the weekend from southern Alabama to southwestern Georgia.

Isaias, which is the first hurricane to hit the eastern U.S. since Milton tore up the Gulf Coast of Florida in 2024, also is expected to bring heavy rain and potential flooding to much of the Southeast over the weekend, and then to parts of the Midwest and Northeast into Monday.

Isaias grounds flights but likely to miss oil hubs

The storm grounded most Friday flights at several Panhandle airports, including all flights into and out of Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, scrapped his plans to attend Saturday’s football game between the University of Georgia and the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa. He said he didn’t want to disrupt the emergency response.

Isaias was expected to miss the oil industry’s biggest hubs along the Gulf Coast, but fuel prices could rise if power outages shut down refineries for processing crude, industry experts said.

On Dauphin Island, a barrier island off the Alabama coast, Mayor Jeff Collier said he didn't expect major damage, “but at the same time, these things are very fickle and a little jog here or there, or some last-minute increase in strength — we just have to be prepared for the worst.”

Meanwhile in the Pacific, Hurricane Simon became a Category 2 storm on Friday and was expected to strengthen further before making landfall in Mexico this weekend.

Tropical Storm Rachel was also expected to bring heavy winds and rain to northern Mexico and Southern California over the weekend.

title: Full text of President Lai Ching-te's National Day address - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德), in his National Day address on Saturday, pledged to improve people's well-being, safeguard regional peace and stability, and sustain Taiwan's economic competitiveness. The following is the
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德), in his National Day address on Saturday, pledged to improve people's well-being, safeguard regional peace and stability, and sustain Taiwan's economic competitiveness.

The following is the full English translation of his speech provided by the Presidential Office, titled "Taiwan's Future: A City upon a Hill, the Salt and Light of the World."

National Day Celebration Chairperson Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜), Vice President Bi-khim Hsiao, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰), His Majesty King Mswati III of the Kingdom of Eswatini, Inkhosikati Make Zuma, Japan-Taiwan Diet Members' Consultative Council Chairman Furuya Keiji, heads of delegations from diplomatic allies and friendly nations, members of the foreign diplomatic corps stationed in Taiwan, distinguished guests from home and abroad, and my fellow citizens here in person and watching on TV or online: Good morning.

Today, we are gathered here in front of the Presidential Office Building to celebrate the National Day of the Republic of China, to praise Taiwan, and to wish our nation a happy birthday and continued prosperity.

At this moment, here in Taiwan and in different corners of the world, no matter the generation to which you belong, and no matter your profession or political stance, we are all rooted in the same Taiwan. And we share a responsibility, which is to make our country safer, our society more stable, our lives better, and to give the next generation hope for the future. This year marks the 30th anniversary of Taiwan's first direct presidential election. Thirty years ago, our citizens went to the polls, showing their courage in the face of missile threats, to fulfill their century-long dream of becoming the masters of their own destinies. With the ballots they cast, they told the world: This nation belongs to its people, and the future of Taiwan will be decided by the people of Taiwan.

Over those 30 years, we transformed into a democracy, we saw the peaceful transition of power between political parties, and we endured many challenges. Today, we know with even more certainty that freedom and democracy do not run counter to economic development. As Taiwan more tightly embraces democracy and engages more closely with the world, it is more able to create prosperity and more capable of contributing to the world.

The last year has not been a quiet one for the world. War and authoritarian expansion continue to spread. The global economy underwent a host of challenges, such as tariffs, energy issues, and red supply chains. But Taiwan did not back down; despite the changing circumstances, it stood firm, with a resilience we can be proud of.

Just look at the recent accomplishments of our athletes at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. In soft tennis mixed doubles, Yu Kai-wen (余凱文) and Huang Shih-yuan (黃詩媛) fought for every point to clinch Taiwan's first gold of the games. Swimmer Wang Kuan-hung (王冠閎) powered through the water to realize our 28-year-long hope for gold. Fu Chao-hsuan (傅兆玄) leapt through the pouring rain to win the gold in high jump, Taiwan's first Asian Games men's track and field gold in 60 years. Neither did Lin Yu-ting (林郁婷) disappoint, taking home gold for the second consecutive Asian Games. Taiwan dominated the top two spots in women's tennis doubles, with Hsieh Su-wei (謝淑薇) and Liang En-shuo (梁恩碩) taking gold and Chan Hao-ching (詹皓晴) and Wu Fang-hsien (吳芳嫺) taking silver. I want to thank all our athletes for showing the world Taiwan's resilience and pride.

I would also like to thank the people of Taiwan, in all sectors and professions, for our impressive economic performance. Our most up-to-date economic growth rate for just the first half of the year is 14.15 percent, and we could see a rate exceeding 11 percent for the year as a whole, which would be a 39-year high. Our per capita GDP is projected to reach US$45,332 this year, almost double that of 2016. The TAIEX rose over the historic 49,000-point mark, making Taiwan's stock market the world's fourth biggest in terms of market capitalization.

Taiwan is also going farther, step by step, with our diplomacy.

I made a state visit to the Kingdom of Eswatini earlier this year. I would like to thank His Majesty King Mswati III for the thoughtful reception, and Her Majesty the Queen Mother and all the people of Eswatini for the warm welcome. Together, we witnessed our countries' bilateral cooperation in the fields of energy, agriculture, healthcare, women's empowerment, and education and culture. Also this year, Vice President Hsiao visited the Republic of Palau to deepen our bilateral cooperation in such areas as healthcare, agriculture and fisheries, infrastructure, and sustainable tourism. And just last month, she was invited to speak at the European Conference of Ventotene for Freedom and Democracy in Italy, allowing Taiwan's voice to be heard by the world from a place that is an important symbol of freedom and democracy in Europe.

In this year's World Competitiveness Ranking compiled by the Swiss-based Institute for Management Development, Taiwan placed highly in its four major factors of economic performance, government efficiency, business efficiency, and infrastructure, and it climbed up to fourth globally, our best performance to date.

These achievements, without a doubt, are owed to the 23 million people of Taiwan. They are the result of every ounce of strength given by the government and countless citizens, across all fields, working hand in hand. Let us have another warm round of applause in celebration of your accomplishments.

In this era marked by war, authoritarian expansion, and a rapidly shifting global order, what kind of nation should Taiwan strive to be?

My answer is this: We must become a "city upon a hill," built with courage and confidence.

This is not to sing our own praises, but rather to declare our aspirations for the nation's future. It is also a responsibility Taiwan stands ready to shoulder.

My fellow citizens, this city upon a hill is built atop a chain of guardian mountains. It is the splendid outcome of democratic governance which grants us a solid basis for peace of mind. A city upon a hill, therefore, should have more than just a dazzling skyline; it must stand on a firm foundation.

The well-being of our people is the very foundation of Taiwan. National progress lies not merely in output value and exports, but in increasing benefits and pay for our workers, alleviating the burden on families, providing care for the older generation, and giving our youth the confidence that their hard work will pave the way to a brighter future.

We are therefore taking a pragmatic approach to governance, promoting higher salaries, lower taxes, increased benefits, and reduced burdens so that each and every individual in this nation can stand steady and live well.

To address the declining birthrate, we are building upon our national childcare policy for ages 0-6, and have proposed a new population strategy for Taiwan in the area of family support. This includes increased subsidies, lighter loads, greater flexibility, and expanded care from the stages of childbirth and childrearing to education, making support for families even more comprehensive.

Starting next year, we are on track to launch NT$5,000 monthly allowances for every child, from birth until age 18. By combining this with maternity benefits and subsidies for assisted reproduction, affordable childcare, family-friendly workplaces, and social housing for newlyweds and families of young children, we will ensure that our young people will no longer be forced to choose between work and family.

Families should not have to raise children all on their own. To support a family is to safeguard Taiwan's future.

As we are now a super-aged society, we are advancing the Healthy Taiwan initiative, which ranges from cancer screenings, smart healthcare, and in-home care to improving working conditions for healthcare professionals and increasing the nursing workforce. This way, our people will live not only longer, but healthier.

Our Long-term Care 3.0 plan, which launched this year, further integrates healthcare with social welfare, the community, and technology. This allows older adults to receive care in a familiar setting, and gives the "sandwich generation," who must look after both older and younger family members, greater support and less hardship.

To ease housing pressure, we will continue implementing our program to support 1 million renter households, and will expand supply through a variety of methods, including government construction of social housing, subleasing and management programs, rental subsidy programs, as well as housing units allocated to the government through urban renewal and floor area ratio incentives. We are also increasing the proportion of social housing for newlyweds and families with young children, implementing our Preferential Housing Loans for the Youth 3.0 program, and raising the maximum loan amounts for these families. Stable homes are not only necessary for us to thrive in our careers; they are also what young people need to take the leap in starting families and pursuing their dreams.

To address labor and talent shortages, we have also rolled out the Cross-border Workforce Enhancement Program. We firmly maintain that local workers are our primary workforce, while the cross-border workforce serves in a supplementary capacity. We will increase local employee wages in tandem with migrant worker quotas, allow for greater retention of experienced migrant workers seeking re-designation as skilled foreign workers, and promote direct government-to-government recruitment.

We have also amended the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals, expanding opportunities for international talent and foreign students to come to and stay in Taiwan. This will address corporate staffing shortages while enhancing employee benefits and pay, ensuring that talent is not just willing to come, but willing to stay.

Social safety is likewise part of the unshakeable foundation of this city upon a hill.

To combat fraud, we have made the Executive Yuan's anti-fraud command center a permanent task force. By integrating efforts from the areas of domestic affairs, justice, digital affairs, and financial supervision, and by connecting prosecutors, financial institutions, and digital platform operators, we are severing the chain of crime at all segments, from advertising and communication to accounts and cash flows.

To fight drugs and counter drug-impaired driving, the government continues to advance the New Generation Anti-drug Strategy Guidelines and strengthen drug enforcement, screening, rehabilitation, and education. We are tracing drugs upstream to their sources and using rapid saliva drug tests to step up roadside checks and stop dangerous drivers on the spot. The government will do everything in its power to protect our people's hard-earned property and every precious life in every family.

The government is also actively pushing for legal amendments. First-time drug-impaired driving offenders will face fines of up to NT$150,000, and those who refuse roadside testing will be fined NT$270,000. There will be no cap on fines for repeat offenders; their driver's licenses will be revoked and their vehicles forfeited. Passengers riding with drug-impaired drivers will also be liable to fines. The government will strictly enforce the law and show zero tolerance.

In addressing energy and climate challenges, our goals are a stable power supply, energy security, and the transition to net zero. We are advancing diverse green energy sources, energy storage, energy conservation, and grid resilience. We will also pragmatically evaluate all energy options by drawing on scientific evidence, following due process of law, and applying safety standards.

Energy policy cannot be built on slogans; it must be built on co

title: Protests in New York as Trump admin defends ICE shooting
summary: **NEW YORK**— Protesters gathered in New York on Friday after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers shot a Dominican man in an incident that has provoked a showdown between the city's Democratic mayor and the Trump administrati
content:
**NEW YORK**— Protesters gathered in New York on Friday after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers shot a Dominican man in an incident that has provoked a showdown between the city's Democratic mayor and the Trump administration.

Oscar Bergal, 28, was wounded in the neck during an ICE operation in the Bronx on Thursday, while a five-year-old child who was in his car at the time was physically unharmed.

The shooting drew swift criticism from Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who wrote "Abolish ICE" on X -- a common refrain among the political left opposed to Republican President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

*   [Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/outrage-over-plan-to-livestream-us-military-firing-squad-execution/2442977)

US Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin lashed out in response, telling reporters that Mamdani's words are "dangerous and incite hostility."

"Mayor, if you abolish ICE, who's going to take criminals off the streets of your own town?" Mullin said. "Who's going to take the murderers and the thieves and the gangbangers?"

An AFP journalist saw hundreds of protesters stretching several blocks in Manhattan on Friday chanting "No hate, no fear, immigrants are welcome here" and "No ICE."

New York, a Democratic stronghold, is one of several US cities that bars its police force from assisting with federal immigration enforcement.

Mamdani on Thursday said he was seeking to speak with Trump and would demand that immigration agents be withdrawn from the city.

*   ![Image 1: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

The incident could test the surprisingly warm relationship between the two leaders.

Video of the shooting, shared by US media on Friday, shows what appears to be a plainclothes federal agent rushing toward a silver car with a gun drawn.

The vehicle briefly reverses as the agent punches the driver-side window, before a second plainclothes officer draws a gun.

He points the weapon at the driver as the car pulls away off screen, appearing to collide with the side of a passing vehicle.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

**High-profile shootings**

Mullin said that Bergal had an extensive criminal history and was trying to evade arrest.

"He came to this country legally a few years ago, and ever since he's come in, he's committed crime and crime after crime," the Homeland Security secretary said.

Mullin said ICE officers did not know there was a child in the car when they opened fire.

*   ![Image 3: No first-round bye for projected No. 13 seed Eala at Wuhan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253937.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[No first-round bye for projected No. 13 seed Eala at Wuhan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/sports/no-first-round-bye-for-projected-no-13-seed-eala-at-wuhan/2442979)

Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, told reporters that Bergal had "refused lawful orders to exit his vehicle."

"He then accelerated his vehicle, smashing into two of our government ICE vehicles, and then weaponized his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate, going towards other officers," Charles said.

"Our officers, using their training, and believing that their life and the lives of their partners and general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," he said.

ICE agents, who often wear civilian clothing and cover their faces, have been involved in several high-profile shootings this year.

Ruben Ray Martinez, 23, was shot by ICE in March 2025, in what the Texas Tribune said was the first known killing by immigration agents of an American in Trump's second term.

More recently, a Mexican man, Lorenzo Salgado, died in July after he was shot by an ICE officer in Houston, Texas.

Two Americans — Renee Good and Alex Pretti —were shot and killed by federal immigration agents in separate incidents in Minnesota during a crackdown on undocumented migrants in the northern state earlier this year.

title: Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution
summary: **WASHINGTON, D.C.—** Condemnation of US plans for a public execution by military firing squad escalated Friday, as Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would be livestreamed as proposed and insisted he would not watch if it is.
content:
**WASHINGTON, D.C.—** Condemnation of US plans for a public execution by military firing squad escalated Friday, as Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would be livestreamed as proposed and insisted he would not watch if it is.

Nidal Hasan's execution —scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 —is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945.

Asked about the planned livestream, Vance told journalists he does not "know that that's actually going to happen."

"This is a guy who committed, in my view, the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11," Vance said, but added that if the execution is broadcast live, "I'm not going to be watching it."

Representative Austin Scott of President Donald Trump's Republican Party said he supported executing Hasan but "livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that."

Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Hasan should "face justice" but that public executions are "the kind of thing Iran and the Taliban do. Is this who we want to be associated with?"

A Pentagon official told AFP on Thursday that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public."

But Trump on Friday contradicted Hegseth's confirmation, and said there has been no decision yet on whether to publicly broadcast the execution, which he supports.

"They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed," Trump said. "I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes."

Tech firms YouTube, Meta and X did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether they would allow the execution to be streamed on their platforms.

TikTok directed AFP to its policy banning depictions of "graphic incidents and violence" including "the shooting of an individual."

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the move, saying in a message sent to AFP on Friday that "the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture."
