[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered."

**'Compound the cruelty'**

Hegseth said it would be the military's first firing squad execution since World War II.

"People need to understand that...there's serious consequence for these types of things," Hegseth said in a video shared Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.

The Death Penalty Information Center says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.

According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 -- six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.

Amnesty's Justin Mazzola said Friday that the death penalty is "a violation of human rights," and that streaming Hasan's execution "would only compound the cruelty."

Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralyzed from the waist down.

Hasan chose to conduct his own defense during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges.

He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.

Court-appointed defense attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.

The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military's occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

title: Trump strikes deal with Putin for Russian diesel in sharp reversal of US policy ahead of midterms
summary: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midte
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he was expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter.” Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.

Trump’s shocking announcement comes after he signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law last month that aimed at clamping down on Russia’s energy revenues, among other areas, that fuel its war against Ukraine.

*   [Trump says Putin agrees to major release of diesel to US, global markets](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/trump-says-putin-agrees-to-major-release-of-diesel-to-us-global-markets/2442901)

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it, “a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners," according to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington.

Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to try to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

“I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,” Zelenskyy said.

Trump's move casts doubt on the likelihood of the White House imposing sanctions on Russia this month, given that a bipartisan law passed by Congress directs the administration to target the top importers of Russian oil and gas.

Trump, in his announcement, did not address the sanctions or Russia’s war but said, “Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority.”

[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

#### **Washington and Moscow offer few details on deal**

#### The White House did not immediately respond to questions about who was paying for the diesel from Russia and when the fuel being supplied under the agreement would become available. It also did not clarify whether subsequent supplies of Russian diesel set to come next month would be supplied prior to Election Day on Nov. 3.

Gas prices globally have surged as the war in Iran upends the energy sector. While diesel future prices dipped on the news on Friday, the national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. remained high at $6.28, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on Sept. 22.

A statement from Putin, released by the Kremlin on Friday, said that during their call he and Trump dedicated “significant attention to the prospects of resolving the Ukrainian crisis” and also discussed “the situation around Iran and various aspects of bilateral relations.”

Russia “confirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and global markets,” Putin said. “I am confident that this will have a positive impact on the entire global economy.”

*   ![Image 2: LTO identifies rider in hit-and-run incident involving 'It's Showtime' host](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1249307.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[LTO identifies rider in hit-and-run incident involving 'It's Showtime' host](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/07/news/lto-identifies-rider-in-hit-and-run-incident-involving-its-showtime-host/2440550)

The two leaders agreed to continue contacts, Putin said in the statement.

#### **Trump and Putin's deal draws immediate backlash**

Zelenskyy, in a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, said Russia would repay it “with further terror and perfidy.” He cast it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged.

“It plays into Russia’s hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.

*   ![Image 3: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Rep. Don Beyer, the senior House Democrat on the Joint Economic Committee, called Trump’s announcement “infuriating.”

“This is what we warned anyone who would listen: Trump isn’t the slightest bit trustworthy when it comes to Russia,” Beyer said in a statement on X. “Giving him expanded tariff powers in hopes he would use them to help Ukraine was a mistake. Now he’s lifting sanctions on Russian fossil fuels.”

The law Trump signed last month envisions sanctions on Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers and bans all new U.S. investment in Russia and the handling of sovereign debt.

It also directed Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia’s natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.

The U.S. has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned them because of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

#### **Treasury Department moves to ease diesel sanctions for six months**

Shortly after Trump made the announcement, the Treasury Department said it was immediately issuing a temporary license allowing Russian diesel to be supplied to the global market.

This is the latest in several licenses the U.S. Treasury has issued regarding Russian fuel shipments since the start of the Iran war earlier this year. But it is the first such license to ease sanctions on diesel for a period lasting longer than the standard 30-day window since the start of the Ukraine war.

The new so-called general license means U.S. sanctions will not apply until April 2027 on deliveries of Russian diesel that has been loaded onto tankers as of Friday. The department extended similar easing of sanctions in March and April even though Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had ruled out such a move earlier in the year.

The extensions continue to underscore how the fallout from the Iran war has boosted Moscow’s ability to profit from its energy exports, which had been restrained by the U.S. and other allies since the invasion of Ukraine.

**It’s unclear what kind of impact the move will have on oil prices, given overall global supply shortages.**

“It’s kind of shuffling deck chairs on the Titanic,” said Michael Lynch of the Energy Policy Research Foundation, a non-partisan research institution focused on energy and economics.

“If we get diesel from Russia, basically it means that their existing customers are not going to get it and they’ll have to go somewhere else, and that will keep the price basically where it is now,” Lynch said.

Russia, once a major exporter of diesel, has banned exports since July as it has struggled to meet demand inside the country because of Ukraine’s repeated attacks on Russian oil refineries. The International Energy Agency says Russian diesel output has fallen by about 30%.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told state news agency Tass that Russia is “immediately starting to lift restrictions on diesel exports ahead of schedule.” He said that Moscow could start supplies to the U.S. already in October, and that Russia’s domestic market will be “fully supplied” with diesel, as well.

title: 赖清德会美国会议员，双十节演说将强调台湾强化防卫非挑衅
summary: 华盛顿 — 台湾总统赖清德星期四(10月8日)在台北会见来访的美国参、众议员，就美台关系及地区情势交换意见。赖清德对议员们表示，台海和平稳定攸关第一岛链及印太地区的稳定与发展，台湾有决心强化自我防卫能力，以实力维护和平。赖清德也预计在星期六的双十演说中强调，台湾加强防卫能力并非挑衅，而是要以实力维护人民自由民主的生活。 赖清德在总统府分别会见科罗拉多州民主党籍联邦参议员迈克尔·贝内特(Michael Bennet)，以及由众议院预算委员会民主党首席议员、宾夕法尼亚州联邦众议员
content:
华盛顿 —

台湾总统赖清德星期四(10月8日)在台北会见来访的美国参、众议员，就美台关系及地区情势交换意见。赖清德对议员们表示，台海和平稳定攸关第一岛链及印太地区的稳定与发展，台湾有决心强化自我防卫能力，以实力维护和平。赖清德也预计在星期六的双十演说中强调，台湾加强防卫能力并非挑衅，而是要以实力维护人民自由民主的生活。

赖清德在总统府分别会见科罗拉多州民主党籍联邦参议员迈克尔·贝内特(Michael Bennet)，以及由众议院预算委员会民主党首席议员、宾夕法尼亚州联邦众议员布伦登·博伊尔(Brendan Boyle)率领的代表团，包括同党的俄勒冈州联邦众议员安德烈亚·萨利纳斯(Andrea Salinas)及纽约州联邦众议员蒂姆·肯尼迪(Tim Kennedy)。

台湾总统赖清德在台北总统府会见来访的美国民主党籍联邦参议员迈克尔·贝内特。(2026年10月8日)

参议员贝内特曾在今年3月提出《第一岛链吓阻法》(First Island Chain Deterrence Act)，检视美国对位于第一岛链的日本、台湾及菲律宾军售(FMS)的武器交付议题，以及一旦军售有所延宕对此地区的遏阻有何影响；他也在今年7月联署由参议员匡希恒(John Curtis)先前提出的《对台六项保证法》(Six Assurances to Taiwan Act)，推动将美国对台湾的“六项保证”法制化，由国会审视其执行，以保护台湾不受胁迫。

根据总统府新闻稿，赖清德对贝内特以立法作为来支持台湾表达感谢，更认为贝内特在双十前夕来访意义重大。

“这些行动也传达一个非常重要的讯息，就是台海和平稳定不只是台湾的事情，也攸关整个第一岛链及印太区域的稳定与发展。在台湾国庆前夕，贝内特参议员更亲自来到台湾，以行动证明对台湾的支持，不仅展现对台湾的情谊，也充分表达对台湾的强力支持，对台湾的社会安定有莫大帮助，”他说。

贝内特也在会面中肯定台湾立法院通过超过240亿美元军购特别预算，并表示美国国会对维护台海和平稳定有跨党派支持，包括通过对台出售足以供其自卫的防御性武器，他将持续与国会同事合作，确保国会已经通过和拨款的支持得到落实。他强调，台湾关系法及六项保证依然是美国对台政策的基石和框架，它提供通往台海和平稳定及整个印太地区最稳妥的道路。

“自由与民主并非理所当然，在印太地区尤其是如此。美国人民与台湾站在一起，美国国会两党成员也是如此，他们将持续支持台湾的民主、安全与繁荣。台湾并不孤单，”他说：“他们永远不会孤单。”

在与由众议员博伊尔率领的代表团会面时，赖清德也感谢代表团在台湾庆祝双十国庆前来访，并表示面对中国对台湾的威胁，台湾有决心捍卫台海和平。

“中国今年不断对东海、台海、南海及太平洋周边国家，以军事行动、灰色地带侵扰、长臂管辖、跨国镇压等手段，企图片面改变台海现状，破坏区域和平稳定；民主国家更应团结一致、紧密合作，才能守护赖以生存的民主价值与生活，”他说，台湾位于第一岛链关键位置，有决心捍卫和平，也坚信唯有实力才能确保和平，这也是为什么台湾持续增加国防预算，投入更多资源推动国防自主，也对外进行军事采购，积极强化自我防卫力量。

博伊尔说，此次访团三位众议员都是首次访台，“能在台湾的国庆日前夕来访更是别具意义”，今年是美国建国250周年，过去250年来美国人民努力实践独立宣言所揭示的崇高理想，他们的民主发展也经历了一段漫长的历程。美国与台湾有许多共同之处，台湾的民主也历经一段发展才走到今天这一步。

“美国人民与台湾人民因共同价值观而紧密连结，包括对自由与人权的承诺在内，”他说，“尽管我们的民主体质仍然有不完美之处，但对全世界那些仍然在争取自由的人们，这都是一个值得效法的典范，尤其对亚洲一些国家更是如此。”

台湾预订星期六上午在总统府前广场举行双十典礼，不具名官员告诉媒体，赖清德将在双十演说中回应美中对话，强调台湾加强自我防卫能力并非为了挑衅，而是要以实力维持人民现有的民主自由生活。

这是赖清德自2024年5月就任总统以来第3次发表国庆讲话。官员说，赖清德的演说重点包括民生经济、国际挑战与强化防卫、维护民主。他将在演说中以自信坚定态度回应美中对话，并阐述台湾在国际交流中的角色，并向世界展现位于印太第一岛链的台湾，始终是台海和平稳定的守护者，也是积极贡献国际社会的民主伙伴。

此外，他也将阐述台湾如何强化自我防卫能力，持续投入国防，并增强全社会防卫韧性，并强调“这些努力不是为了挑衅，而是期盼台湾人民能够以实力维持现有的民主自由生活，展现珍惜和平的负责任立场，”中央社的报道说。

中国视民主治理的台湾为其领土一部分，并且不排除以武力强迫实现统一，对拒绝其主权宣示的台湾不断加大施压进行各种军事胁迫。

赖清德多次强调将提升台湾防卫能力，其政府提出的2027年国防预算突破新台币一万亿元(约350亿美元)，创下新纪录，也超过了国内生产总值GDP的百分之3。赖清德还宣示，将在2030年前比照北约标准，让台湾的防卫开支达到GDP的百分之5。

赖清德9日晚上在“115年国庆晚会”上发表演说时表示，把经济成果反映到人民的生活是政府的责任。

他说，在海内外台湾人共同努力下，台湾已一步步站上世界舞台，“越来越多企业选择把信心留在台湾，把下一个世代的关键布局留在台湾”。

“身为总统，我更清楚，国家强、国家好，不只是数字上的表现，而是要反映在人们的生活上。我们有责任把世界对台湾的信任，转换成台湾人民更好的生活，”赖清德说。

title: Trump appoints 'devoted fan' Katie Zacharia as press secretary

content:
WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump on Friday announced the appointment of conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter.

"She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.

"She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" he added, referring to his Make America Great Again movement.

*   [Trump says Putin agrees to major release of diesel to US, global markets](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/trump-says-putin-agrees-to-major-release-of-diesel-to-us-global-markets/2442901)

Zacharia, a lawyer and communications adviser to Trump's media company, will succeed Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public faces of his second administration.

Trump hailed his new spokeswoman's credentials, including her work for his presidential campaigns, and said he was confident she would enjoy a good relationship with the White House press corps.

A graduate of Pepperdine University's law school, Zacharia began her career in Republican politics, working as an intern for the Republican National Committee in 2006, CNN reported.

Trump sought advice from several allies and advisors, including Leavitt, before deciding to offer Zacharia the position, according to CNN.

Her appointment fills one of the White House's most visible positions, with the press secretary responsible for briefing journalists, fielding questions about administration policies and serving as a chief public defender of the president.

Leavitt, who took up the position when Trump returned to power in January 2025, became the youngest White House press secretary in US history at 27.

A staunch Trump loyalist who previously served as press secretary for his 2024 presidential campaign, she left the administration in late August following the birth of her second child.

Fox News announced this week that Leavitt would join the conservative network as an on-air contributor beginning in November.

Trump praised his outgoing spokeswoman, saying she had done a "fantastic job" in the role.

title: New attacks on Riyadh airport kill 3 Saudis
summary: **RIYADH**— Saudi Arabia said on Friday that three people, including a pilot, were killed in attacks on Riyadh’s international airport, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed a series of attacks targeting the gateway. The conflict between the Houthi
content:
**RIYADH**— Saudi Arabia said on Friday that three people, including a pilot, were killed in attacks on Riyadh’s international airport, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed a series of attacks targeting the gateway.

The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has widened, with the Iran-backed fighters staging repeated attacks on Saudi targets since they began a lightning offensive just across the border.

While seizing large swathes of territory along the Red Sea coast in Yemen, the Houthis have also attacked Saudi transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian targets in the world’s largest crude exporter.

*   [Flydubai co-pilot intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, UAE prosecutor says](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/flydubai-co-pilot-intended-to-crash-plane-into-tel-aviv-airport-uae-prosecutor-says/2442894)

The Saudi civil aviation authority said two attacks on King Khalid International Airport and a Saudia Airlines plane there on Thursday “resulted in the martyrdom of three citizens.”

The national flag carrier confirmed the death of the plane’s captain, expressing “profound sadness” and citing an “incident” at the gateway.

Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government forces it backs have struggled to contain the Houthis’ advance, despite a counteroffensive aimed at recapturing territory including the area around the Bab al-Mandab Strait that is crucial to global energy flows.

But a regional source told Agence France-Presse (AFP) on Friday that Riyadh would not bow to the Houthis’ “military blackmail” and would not agree to a truce until the Yemeni government regains all territory it has lost in recent weeks.

The attacks forced diplomats stationed in the Saudi capital to shelter in place and international schools to take safety measures as explosions echoed across the city on Thursday.

Numerous flights at King Khalid airport were delayed or canceled, while the airport advised travelers of the “necessity” to contact airlines before their trips.

The kingdom’s civil defense agency also said “interception debris” had damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh. It did not say if there were casualties there or provide details of the damage.

‘Crisis in everything’

The Houthis, whose heartlands are among the Zaidi Shia Muslims in the northwest, had already controlled the capital Sanaa and most of Yemen’s major population centers since the start of the war in 2014.

Riyadh’s military coalition intervened to support the government the following year.

After declaring their counteroffensive against the Houthis, Yemen’s government claimed to have pushed the fighters out of strategic areas on the Red Sea coast and the port city of Mokha.

*   ![Image 3: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

But the Houthis insist they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched missiles at an airport in Najran and an air base in Khamis Mushait on Thursday.

The Houthis have also warned workers to evacuate Saudi Arabia’s oil facilities, having days before hit a major refinery south of the capital.

Admissions by Saudi authorities of civilian targets being hit are relatively rare. There have been few statements on Houthi attacks in recent weeks.

Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

In Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, ordinary civilians are paying the price for the renewed fighting, with more than 200,000 people displaced since July, according to United Nations data.

In Yemen’s Taiz, the Houthis are laying siege to the government-controlled city in the country’s west, depriving residents of their main supply route to the government’s temporary capital in Aden.

“There is a crisis in everything: water, gas, vegetables, everything essential,” said Um Rian.

title: Road safety is everybody’s business
summary: IMAGINE a plane crash with 36 persons killed. What if this happened every single day for years? It would be a national emergency. It would be on the front page of every newspaper and the top news story every morning. The president would be
content:
IMAGINE a plane crash with 36 persons killed. What if this happened every single day for years? It would be a national emergency. It would be on the front page of every newspaper and the top news story every morning. The president would be calling Cabinet meetings to solve this crisis. Yet comparable numbers die in land transport crashes daily. But is anyone taking notice? Shouldn’t it be a Cabinet-level concern?

The Philippine Statistics Authority recorded 13,125 deaths due to land transport accidents in 2023, an average of 36 daily and 7.2 percent more than in 2022. Behind every number is a family that has lost a loved one, a breadwinner or a future.

The victims include children as well as Filipinos in their prime. Globally, road traffic injuries remain the leading killer of persons aged five to 29. Many survivors face permanent disability. More than half of those killed are pedestrians, cyclists and motorcycle riders. We need to make road safety everybody’s business.

*   [No collection of taxes in BIR’s ‘Oplan Kandado’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/business/top-business/no-collection-of-taxes-in-birs-oplan-kandado/2441215)

Up until now, we have designed our roads and bridges to facilitate faster travel by private motor vehicles, placing the convenience of car-owners above the safety and welfare of the vast majority of Filipinos. When crashes occur, the frequently-cited cause is human error — “kamote” drivers or pedestrians who didn’t follow rules. “Disiplina” is then pushed as the solution. Better enforcement, more driver training and stricter licensing may help, but they are far from sufficient.

The Safe System Approach, promoted by the World Health Organization and the United Nations, begins with the premise that human mistakes are inevitable, even with the best training and incentives. The human body can withstand only limited force. Transport systems should therefore minimize mistakes and ensure that, when they occur, people are not killed or seriously injured. Responsibility is shared by road users, road designers, vehicle manufacturers, transport operators and government decision-makers. Safety must be built into the system.

Get the latest news

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Road safety management is about according road safety the high-level attention and priority that it deserves. It means applying a whole-of-government approach, assigning Cabinet-level accountability and establishing a dedicated coordinating and monitoring unit with permanent staff and sufficient budget. Reliable crash and injury data should guide investments and measure results. National agencies and local governments should have clear responsibilities, deadlines and targets for reducing deaths and serious injuries.

Safe roads means designing roads to be forgiving and prioritizing vulnerable road users. Sidewalks should be spacious, continuous and free of hazards or obstructions. Pedestrian crossings should be at street level, accessible to persons with disabilities, and provided where people need to cross. Traffic signals should give children and the elderly sufficient time to cross safely. Painted bike lanes offer little protection; physical barriers are needed to prevent motor vehicles from entering the space reserved for bicycles.

Safe speeds are fundamental. Where motor vehicles mix with pedestrians and cyclists, speeds should generally be limited to 30 kilometers per hour or less. Higher speeds increase both the likelihood of a crash and the severity of injury. Posting a speed limit is insufficient and ineffective if the road encourages fast driving. Lane narrowing, speed humps, raised crossings and other traffic calming measures should make slower speeds the natural behavior. Around schools and on shared neighborhood streets, even lower speeds (10-20 kph) are appropriate.

*   ![Image 1: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Safe vehicles require rigorous inspection to ensure that brakes, tires, lights and other essential equipment are working. Governance arrangements should make it difficult to circumvent the inspection process. Vehicle standards should protect occupants as well as people outside the vehicle. Better public transport also matters. Safe, sufficient and attractive services can reduce reliance on private motor vehicles. Bus and jeepney operations should eliminate on-street competition for passengers and give drivers dignified and sufficient compensation.

Safe road use involves licensing, driver training, education and consistent enforcement against speeding, drunk driving and distracted driving. Proper helmets, seat belts and child restraints save lives. Camera-based enforcement can improve the certainty of penalties. But responsible behavior also requires supportive conditions: a pedestrian cannot use a sidewalk that does not exist and a cyclist cannot remain safe in a bike lane occupied by parked cars.

Post-crash response means expeditious and effective emergency care, accessible trauma services and rehabilitation. Victims and families also need psychological and economic support. The quality and timeliness of care can determine whether an injured person survives or suffers permanent disability.

In May 2023, the government launched the Philippine Road Safety Action Plan (PRSAP) 2023–2028, seeking a 35-percent reduction in road traffic deaths by 2028. Yet, as reported by the Philippine News Agency in September, the proposed 2027 budget gives the plan zero funding, despite the Department of Transportation’s request for P111.29 million. Congress should correct this omission.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The budget should fund PRSAP activities, with named implementing agencies and measurable results. Safer school zones, dangerous crossing improvements, speed management and emergency response should receive resources commensurate with the scale of this public health emergency.

A plan without a budget is meaningless. If the government leaves its own plan without funding, we need to assign a major part of the blame for the 13,000+ preventable deaths in 2027 to decision-makers who are remiss in their duty to keep Filipino road users safe at all times.

title: SKorea recalls envoy from Ukraine over POW row
summary: **SEOUL** — South Korea said on Thursday it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine in response to a deepening diplomatic row over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to Seoul. The two countries have been at loggerheads sinc
content:
**SEOUL** — South Korea said on Thursday it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine in response to a deepening diplomatic row over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to Seoul.

The two countries have been at loggerheads since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy last month disclosed the prisoner transfer, sparking anger in Seoul, which said it had placed their families in North Korea at risk.

The recall also comes days after a media report alleged more than 176,000 tons of fuel, mostly diesel, had been shipped from South Korea to Russia in July and August, sparking accusations that Seoul was helping alleviate Russian fuel shortages.

*   [Trump: No new Iran attack before midterms](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/trump-no-new-iran-attack-before-midterms/2442642)

"The government has decided to recall its ambassador to Ukraine," South Korea’s foreign ministry said in a statement.

"The government hopes that all outstanding issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably and will continue consultations with the Ukrainian side to that end," it added.

"Despite Seoul's decision to recall its ambassador, Ukraine remains open to restoring a constructive dialogue — even if it takes time," Ukraine's foreign ministry spokesman Georgiy Tykhy told reporters.

Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, North Korea has sent troops to support Moscow's war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology.

South Korea's spy agency estimated last year that around 2,000 North Korean troops had been killed in the war, while a more recent assessment put the number killed or wounded at around 6,000.

Ukraine's hopes of South Korean armament supplies have been complicated by the diplomatic row.

*   ![Image 3: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

South Korea has so far not provided lethal weapons to Ukraine, citing a domestic ban on military aid to countries at war.

Seoul had already summoned Kyiv's ambassador and threatened unspecified "further measures." President Lee Jae Myung has demanded an official apology over the prisoner revelation.

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha has called the incident a "diplomatic misunderstanding."

Fuel shipment allegations

*   ![Image 4: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

A report in the United Kingdom’s Guardian newspaper this week has threatened to deepen tensions, with allegations of fuel shipments to Russia coming as Ukraine has struck refineries deep inside Russia, while Moscow has launched intense missile attacks.

An adviser to Zelenskyy said this week that the alleged diesel shipments stood in "sharp contrast" to South Korea's sanctions policies, remarks Seoul slammed as "factually incorrect" and "inappropriate."

South Korea has been part of a coalition of countries with enhanced export controls on Russia and its ally Belarus since the invasion started.

But Seoul’s foreign ministry issued on Thursday a statement saying that even if the fuel had originated in South Korea — something it argued had not been established — it would not breach the country's export ban.

"Refined petroleum products, including commercial diesel and aviation fuel, mentioned in The Guardian's report, are not subject to South Korea's export controls against Russia," it said, noting that overall exports to Moscow had more than halved since the war started.

title: Trump: No new Iran attack before midterms
summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — United States President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out attacking Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran. Trump’s announcement on his Truth Social p
content:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — United States President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out attacking Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran.

Trump’s announcement on his Truth Social platform followed a surge in oil prices driven by media reports suggesting potential new US strikes prior to the elections.

“I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect ... we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections,” he wrote.

*   [New attacks on Riyadh airport kill 3 Saudis](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/new-attacks-on-riyadh-airport-kill-3-saudis/2442669)

LET’S DANCE United States President Donald Trump dances at a campaign rally at the Freeman Coliseum in San Antonio, Texas, on Oct. 7, 2026. AP PHOTO

“We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he added.

The Atlantic magazine reported on Wednesday that the White House had asked the Pentagon to develop options to strike Iranian targets that could be used before the midterms.

The New York Times said on Thursday the plans were being developed despite Trump’s “ambivalence.”

The surge in crude oil prices has also been fueled by persistent tensions in the Strait of Hormuz -— a strategic choke point for the global oil trade — as well as hostilities between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia.

Polls suggest that American voters are strongly dissatisfied with fuel prices, which have soared since deadly US-Israeli strikes against Iran on Feb. 28 triggered the war.

Putin vows to help

Also on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin promised to “do everything” to help end the Middle East war when he met his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian for talks ahead of a regional summit, Russian media reported.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

“We are ready to do everything that is in our power to contribute to the settlement of this situation,” Putin said after arriving in Turkmenistan for a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) that was to start in the Caspian Sea resort of Avaza on Friday.

He added that Iran had made “real efforts to end the war,” Russian news agencies said.

Russia and Iran have reinforced diplomatic and military links since Moscow’s forces invaded Ukraine in February 2022, becoming increasingly reliant on each other.

Trump has repeatedly insisted in recent weeks that the US has effectively won the Iran war, despite ongoing unrest and a recent security threat that forced the withdrawal of American bombers from a base in the United Kingdom.

*   ![Image 4: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

Pezeshkian insisted that Tehran was “engaged in dialogue, but every time we negotiate with the United States, they attack again,” Iranian state media quoted him as saying at the talks with Putin.

Pezeshkian said the Islamic republic wanted to see a “final framework” to end the war.

But he accused Washington of “trying to impose its policies and views on all countries.”

“If the United States insists on pursuing a unilateral approach, a resolution will not be possible,” state media quoted him as saying.

Approaching election

The midterm elections will shape the final two years of Trump’s second term as his Republican Party risks losing its current grip on Congress.

Although Trump is not on the ballot, he is holding numerous rallies in an attempt to limit the damage or even turn the political tide.

Trump has warned he faces a possible third impeachment if Democrats retake the House of Representatives, and the White House is preparing for a slew of investigations into corruption and abuse of power.

The US president also sought to calm a furor on Thursday over his comments at a rally earlier this week that Iran could “take out” the cities of Los Angeles and San Diego.

The 80-year-old blamed the “fake and artificial news” for misinterpreting the remarks, which Democrats pounced on.

“In actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?” Trump said on Truth Social.

title: US-China war now
summary: IF Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr.’s current moves were to be the gauge, then Taiwan will have to erupt in its destined flash point sooner than we think. First, in May, no less than Teodoro led the raid on the Sanjia Steel Cor
content:
IF Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr.’s current moves were to be the gauge, then Taiwan will have to erupt in its destined flash point sooner than we think.

First, in May, no less than Teodoro led the raid on the Sanjia Steel Corp. inside the 3,000-hectare Philippine Veterans Investment and Development Corp. (Phividec) industrial estate in Misamis Oriental. A year before that, the Pentagon had already decided on the Phividec estate as the site for its planned establishment of a giant fuel hub capable of storing 41 trillion barrels of oil daily for the use of the United States Navy Indo-Pacific Command (Indopacom). Together with the fuel hub is a similar huge establishment of US naval facilities and munitions manufacturing. Then following is the disclosure of the 121-page report of current Indopacom Commander Samuel Paparo submitted to Congress, asking for channeling a huge portion of the $1.5-trillion Trump allotment for military expenditures to manufacture low-cost “quick-sink kits” capable of hitting enemy ships’ keel. The report admits China has outnumbered US vessels capacity 430-291, and the idea of equalizing the discrepancy is no longer constructing naval ships but increasing destructive capabilities, which the proposed “quick-sink” kits are.

On Aug. 3–6, 2026, the 37th annual International Military Law and Operations conference in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, was co-keynote hosted by Secretary Teodoro and Admiral Paparo, in which they shared the paramount concern about deterring China’s dominance in the region.

*   [The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

Then the virtual ratatat by Teodoro: the cleverly-scripted “note passing scenario” at the Seoul Defense Forum, the P80-million port construction at the 7-hectare zero-population, zero-development Lawak Island far out in the South China Sea, and the stupendous Teodoro announcement at the 3rd Balangay Forum held in Makati on Sept. 17, 2026, to expand the Philippine Navy into an “expeditionary navy.”

All these developments compose one single element: preparation for war.

But in each of the cited developments, what are involved are long-term works whose usefulness is in a far perceivable future.

For instance, as of 2026, no completion date is defined for the proposed 300-hectare US naval complex at the Phividec industrial estate.

And particularly striking is the fact that going expeditionary navy, the latest of Teodoro’s braggadocio, necessarily takes at least a decade.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

This means that for the Philippines readiness for war won’t come about until after 10 years. Such must be true, particularly for the US, which calls the ultimate shots.

What do all the above indicate?

That the US won’t be ready to war with China until after 10 years.

And yet for the US, such is unthinkable.

*   ![Image 2: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

The US is deeply in mess with Iran in the Middle East, and there are no indications that it will get out of the trouble in the short run. It direly needs the billions of dollars ready for the taking from Taiwan through their pending arms deal. The only kink hampering that deal is the objection of China. This is to be expected since against who else would Taiwan use those arms but China?

So, no way for the US to get its arms deal with Taiwan done but by forcing it through China.

And that means war, not in the far future but now.

Why then, as Teodoro consistently indicates, make preparations for war that is yet long to come?

*   ![Image 3: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Well, Teodoro has not been appointed to the post of defense secretary twice for nothing.

That he stays in that post only proves he is in the good graces with the real appointing power in the security sector — America.

Everything he does is for the betterment of the US position in its antagonism with China.

Making America appear weak, when in fact it is strong, not ready for war when in fact it can deliver the effective strike anytime it so wishes.

Teodoro has been the effective decoy for America’s real war readiness.

To this column, Teodoro’s moves bring back memories of Operation Overlord, the code name for the covert Allied strategy of retaking France from Nazi occupation in World War II.

All indications were that the allies landing would be at Pas-de-Calais, the nearest point in France across the English Channel. Among the many ploys employed by the allies aside from visible troops and facilities deployment were radio messages deliberately meant for Nazi interception and always identifying Pas-de-Calais as the site of the Allied landing.

Accordingly, all Nazi preparations were geared for the defense of Pas-de-Calais.

But then comes June 6, 1944, the real D-Day. Thousands of Allied paratroopers drop — not at Pas-de-Calais but in Normandy, which turns out to be the real site for the retaking of France, without any Nazi resistance.

From that point onward, the Nazi forces were on retreat back to Germany, culminating in ultimate surrender.

The point being driven here is that Teodoro’s obviously intended media splurge is a decoy for drawing attention away from what is already a US readiness to war with China now.

The recent visit of President Xi Jinping to Washington betrayed a desperation on China’s end to pursue what still could be achieved diplomatically in averting the ultimate catastrophe that could result from a final outburst of the Taiwan flash point. President Trump’s body language betrayed that he was not listening but was sticking to a resolve earlier already reached on the issue.

Notice how Trump was inwardly squeamish from some private shenanigan he was nursing inside while Xi was making a last-ditch attempt to convince him of his oft-repeated imploration that both the US and China would gain from cooperation but lose from confrontation.

But the smirk on Trump’s face betrayed he was actually into one more Operation Overlord.

As Sun Tzu puts it: “Make your plans be as dark as night. And when you move, strike like thunder.”

title: The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte
summary: APPARENTLY, in the Philippines today, even banana chips can become a national security threat — provided the buyer is Chinese and the company selling them has a connection to the Duterte family. Welcome to the latest spectacle in Philippine
content:
APPARENTLY, in the Philippines today, even banana chips can become a national security threat — provided the buyer is Chinese and the company selling them has a connection to the Duterte family.

Welcome to the latest spectacle in Philippine politics, where ordinary commercial transactions become geopolitical intrigue, Chinese corporate ownership becomes a convenient insinuation of foreign interference, and allegations appear as established facts long before the evidence catches up.

At the center of this controversy is CALE88 Foods Corp., a Philippine company previously associated with lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, the husband of Vice President Sara Duterte. In the ongoing impeachment trial against the VP, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records fueled sensational headlines alleging that approximately P319.33 million flowed from China and Hong Kong into CALE88.

The insinuation and narrative from the current political establishment in the Philippines under a Marcos Jr. government were hardly subtle: The headline claimed that Sara Duterte secretly received financing from Beijing. How inventive!

But an explosive allegation is not necessarily a substantiated one. This controversy illustrates how easily legitimate financial scrutiny can become entangled with political rivalry, strategic suspicion and the increasingly fashionable habit of finding Chinese interference wherever the words China and Chinese exist.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The crucial distinction is simple: Money received by a Philippine company from Chinese commercial counterparties is not automatically money from the Chinese government. Neither is corporate revenue automatically money personally received by the vice president. Yet somewhere between the financial records and the political headlines, these distinctions appear to have become inconvenient and blurred.

AMLC executive director Ronel Buenaventura testified clearly that AMLC has no records whatsoever showing that China, as a country, or its government, funneled funds to CALE88. It is on record in the impeachment trial proceedings. When asked whether the AMLC had records identifying how much of CALE88’s transactions benefited the vice president or her husband, he said there were none. Hence, the most politically incendiary accusation against the vice president is unproven.

**From banana chips to China’s alleged political financing**

What makes this controversy particularly revealing is the Oct. 6 Bilyonaryo news channel report, which cites Bureau of Customs records showing that CALE88 exported about P217.3 million worth of products to China, out of P246.6 million in total exports since 2023. Its buyers included 13 Chinese companies, among them Beijing Zhenweifang Food Co. and China National Township Enterprises.

Now, here is a revolutionary lesson in Economics 101 that Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr. and Antonio Trillanes IV might wish to revisit: When a Philippine company exports products to China, Chinese buyers are expected to pay for them, right? Shocking, isn’t it?

But since when does legitimate international trade automatically become clandestine political financing? Does selling banana chips to Chinese companies now constitute foreign interference or treason?

These documented exports fundamentally challenge the insinuation that Chinese remittances necessarily represent political funding. If the prosecution suspects otherwise, produce the invoices, trace the money, identify the beneficiaries and prove the illicit purpose. Commercial exports do not automatically validate every remittance, but neither does a Chinese buyer establish wrongdoing.

Evidence, not geopolitical paranoia and sinophobia. Pointing toward Beijing and shouting “Aha!” is not proof. It is political theater masquerading as investigation.

**Hontiveros insinuations and her usual anti-China antics**

Sen. Risa Hontiveros has raised concerns over CALE88’s transactions with Chinese companies allegedly linked to state-owned enterprises and the Chinese Communist Party, including China National Township Enterprises and firms connected to Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group.

Question: Since when did trading with Chinese state-owned enterprises become evidence of foreign interference?

China’s state-owned enterprises are deeply integrated into its domestic economy and international trade. They operate in agriculture, energy, logistics, infrastructure, manufacturing and numerous other industries. That is hardly a state secret. That is hardly a geopolitical revelation.

Does purchasing agricultural products from a Chinese state-owned enterprise automatically constitute foreign interference? Does selling banana chips to a state-linked company make a Filipino entrepreneur an agent of Beijing? By that absurd logic, would this mean that countless Philippine companies doing business with Chinese state enterprises should be investigated as potential national-security threats?

Hontiveros has every right to scrutinize questionable transactions. But Chinese state ownership is not proof of clandestine political financing, much less evidence that Sara Duterte personally received funds from Beijing. Hontiveros should stop confusing commercial relationships with political conspiracy. Otherwise, this becomes guilt by association, dressed up as national security scrutiny.

**Gibo inserted himself again!**

Defense Secretary Gibo Teodoro warned that allegations of Chinese financing, if substantiated, could have serious national-security implications. Fair enough. But since when should the country’s defense establishment amplify geopolitical suspicion before establishing the facts/evidence?

Where is the evidence of a national-security violation? Was classified information compromised? Was there an agreement to influence Philippine foreign policy? Were illegal political contributions made? Did Beijing issue instructions to Sara Duterte? Any proof of this?

Where is the proof, Gibo? Or are we substituting geopolitical paranoia, imagination and insinuation for hard evidence now?

A defense secretary, of all people, should understand that national security is far too serious to be reduced to political theater, speculation, imagination, hallucination or sinophobia.

Simply invoking China does not magically transform a commercial transaction into espionage, foreign interference or treason. National security demands credible, factual, evidence-based intelligence assessment, not geopolitical hallucinations and bigotry masquerading as intelligence.

**Conclusion**

What Filipinos deserve is accountability, not political theater. AMLC testimony reportedly identified P1.25 billion in aggregate covered and suspicious transactions involving CALE88 between 2022 and 2025. These warrant an investigation. The defense must explain the financial discrepancies, while the prosecution must establish wrongdoing through credible, verifiable evidence.

But investigating questionable corporate transactions is one thing; accusing Vice President Sara Duterte of secretly receiving Chinese government funding is quite another. The latter requires compelling evidence, not political insinuations, sensational headlines or national-security rhetoric. The burden of proof cannot be replaced by geopolitical paranoia or sinophobia.

More troubling is the political climate under the Marcos Jr. administration, where almost anything associated with China increasingly invites suspicion and allegations of sinister intent. Such a mindset risks discouraging legitimate investment, distorting commercial realities and undermining an independent Philippine foreign policy. Nationalism/patriotism should never require compulsory hostility toward China.

The CALE88 controversy involves documented exports, substantial financial transactions requiring reconciliation and corporate relationships deserving examination. What is unproven is the sensational allegation that Beijing secretly financed Sara Duterte.

And here lies the spectacular absurdity of Philippine politics: Marcos Jr.’s government is grappling with allegations of massive corruption, food and energy insecurity, economic uncertainty, strategic dependence and overwhelming American influence, yet somehow finding time to turn banana chips into an international conspiracy! What the hell!?

The greatest irony? While billions in public funds face scrutiny over questionable government flood control and infrastructure projects, some politicians seem remarkably eager to find treason in banana-chip shipments.

That is hardly a serious national security analysis. It is political theater seasoned with geopolitical paranoia and a generous helping of sinophobia. And frankly, the Filipino people deserve far better.

title: Effect of minor discrepancies between testimony in court and affidavit of the complainant
summary: _**Dear PAO,**_ _**I am accused of a certain crime, and the complainant made minor discrepancies between her affidavit and her testimony in court. Am I correct in my assumption that such discrepancies would affect her credibility?**_ _**Kum
content:
_**Dear PAO,**_

_**I am accused of a certain crime, and the complainant made minor discrepancies between her affidavit and her testimony in court. Am I correct in my assumption that such discrepancies would affect her credibility?**_

_**Kumpormae**_

*   [Can overtime work be used to offset an employee’s absence?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/06/legal-advice/can-overtime-work-be-used-to-offset-an-employees-absence/2439267)

**Dear Kumpormae,**

Generally speaking, the qualification of a witness, such as the complainant, is provided under Section 21, Rule 130 of A.M. No. 19-08-15-SC, or the 2019 Revised Rules on Evidence, which reads:

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“All persons who can perceive, and perceiving, can make known their perception to others, may be witnesses.”

Correlative thereto, Section 22 of the said Rules also provides that:

“A witness can testify only to those facts which he or she knows of his or her personal knowledge; that is, which are derived from his or her own perception.”

*   ![Image 1: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

The examination of a witness is to be done in open court. This is in consonance with Section 1, Rule 132 of the same Rules:

“The examination of witnesses presented in a trial or hearing shall be done in open court, and under oath or affirmation. Unless the witness is incapacitated to speak, or the question calls for a different mode of answer, the answers of the witness shall be given orally.”

It may happen that there will be inconsistencies between the testimony in court and the earlier affidavit of the complainant or witness. With respect to minor inconsistencies, the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in Pacu-an vs. People of the Philippines, G.R. No. 237542, June 16, 2021, penned by Honorable Associate Justice Edgardo L. Delos Santos, is very enlightening, viz.:

_“Given the natural frailties of the human mind and its incapacity to assimilate all material details of a given incident, slight inconsistencies and variances in the declarations of a witness hardly weaken their probative value. It is well settled that immaterial and insignificant details do not discredit a testimony on the very material and significant point bearing on the very act of accused-appellants._

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

_In Avelino v. People, the Court reiterated the ruling in Madali v. People and held that “[a]s long as the testimonies of the witnesses corroborate one another on material points, minor inconsistencies therein cannot destroy their credibility. Inconsistencies on minor details do not undermine the integrity of a prosecution witness.” In People v. Manigo, the Court ruled that as between a sworn statement or affidavit and an open court testimony, courts must always give more weight to the open court declarations since “affidavits being taken ex-parte are usually incomplete and inaccurate.” Furthermore, in People v. Dayaday, the Court ruled that sworn statements taken ex parte are, as a general rule, considered to be inferior to the testimony given in open court, to wit:_

_A sworn statement or an affidavit does not purport to contain a complete compendium of the details of the event narrated by the affiant. Sworn statements taken ex parte are generally considered to be inferior to the testimony given in open court.”_

Applying the above-quoted jurisprudence to your situation, minor discrepancies or inconsistencies between the testimony given in open court and the affidavit of the complainant does not discredit her or affect her credibility as long as the testimony can be corroborated in its material points. In fact, minor inconsistencies are even treated as badges of truth instead of an indication of falsehood because it shows that the same was not rehearsed or coached. As between the testimony and the affidavit, the former will be controlling because the complainant-witness was subjected to direct and cross examination.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice is solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

*   ![Image 3: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Thank you for your continued trust and support.

_Editor’s note: Dear PAO is a daily column of the Public Attorney’s Office. Questions for Chief Acosta may be sent to dearpao@manilatimes.net_

title: Is governance a brake or a catalyst?
summary: A WELL-DESIGNED regulatory framework is often described as a “brake” on innovation. Too many rules slow companies down, too much compliance burdens entrepreneurs, and too much uncertainty chases away investment. But that framing is incomple
content:
A WELL-DESIGNED regulatory framework is often described as a “brake” on innovation. Too many rules slow companies down, too much compliance burdens entrepreneurs, and too much uncertainty chases away investment. But that framing is incomplete.

In the digital era, artificial intelligence (AI), data flows, online marketplaces and cybersecurity risks evolve at the speed of software releases. Here, governance must also be seen as a catalyst. It can create the conditions under which innovation becomes safer, faster and more widely shared. When regulation clarifies rights and responsibilities, levels the playing field and establishes trust, innovators can build on something stronger than their own risk models.

Public trust, in turn, enlarges adoption; adoption enlarges markets; markets attract more innovation. In that sense, regulatory frameworks are not merely constraints — they are infrastructure for digital economies.

*   [The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

To make governance both a brake and a catalyst, regulators must master three skills. They must set clear baselines without freezing experimentation, build compliance pathways that are practical for companies of different sizes and enforce rules consistently enough that the marketplace believes they apply to everyone.

This is why “good regulation” cannot be only a legal text. It must also include standards, guidance, supervisory capacity and dispute resolution mechanisms. Otherwise, the rules remain aspirational — ineffective as protection and harmful as uncertainty.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

A regulatory framework promotes innovation when it reduces information asymmetry. Platforms often move faster than consumers, and consumers often cannot evaluate risks, especially in AI-driven systems where decisions are opaque. Regulations that demand transparency, independent audits for high-risk AI use, and clear consumer recourse systems give both innovators and users a shared understanding of how the digital market works. That shared understanding converts vague risk where investment can thrive.

At the same time, regulation strengthens trust by tackling the three trust deficits that repeatedly stall digital adoption: privacy insecurity, fraud and manipulation, and unequal power. Data protection laws, security standards and anti-fraud enforcement build confidence that digital services won’t exploit users. Rules for platform conduct include fair ranking practices, complaint handling and accountability for content harms. They signal that public interests matter, not only engagement metrics.

These ideas connect to the “digital majority” thesis. If digital technology reaches and empowers most people, then the legitimacy of the rules becomes essential. A digital majority cannot be governed by architecture alone. It also requires democratic accountability: regulations that reflect public values, not only corporate incentives. The emerging powers that increasingly design digital ecosystems — across Asia, Africa and Latin America — must therefore craft governance that supports innovation while guarding inclusion.

*   ![Image 1: US-China war now](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253555.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

**Asia: ‘Sandboxing’ and data governance**

In Asia, a recurring regulatory strategy for balancing innovation and trust is the use of regulatory sandboxes and phased compliance. Sandboxes let companies test products with temporary flexibility while regulators learn. That learning loop is the “catalyst” part: It turns enforcement into adaptation rather than surprise crackdowns later.

For instance, the Singapore approach — often referenced in fintech and digital service governance — has long used a risk-based framework that encourages experimentation while requiring safeguards around consumer protection, cybersecurity and compliance reporting. The result is not “no regulation,” but a structure where innovators know the boundaries early.

In South Korea, trust-building for digital markets is often tied to strong consumer protections and enforcement coordination across sectors. Meanwhile, Japan has frequently served as a regional reference point for institutionalizing governance practices relevant to digital technologies, combining regulatory clarity with emphasis on responsible media and public communication.

*   ![Image 2: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Another major Asian theme is data governance. When data protection laws and cross-border transfer rules are comprehensible and predictable, firms can invest in compliance rather than fear sudden enforcement. Frameworks that specify roles help companies design systems correctly from the start. In emerging economies, this clarity is particularly valuable: It allows smaller startups to compete because rules are not applied arbitrarily.

Africa’s digital transformation — especially through mobile money, e-commerce and fintech — has shown how trust can become a competitive advantage. Where financial inclusion depends on digital systems, regulation becomes a direct driver of adoption.

Take mobile money. In many African markets, the speed of growth outpaced early rules. Later regulatory frameworks focused on licensing, interoperability, agent conduct, consumer protection and dispute resolution. When regulators required safeguards, they reduced the uncertainty that prevented mainstream users from trusting digital payments.

A concrete example is Kenya’s mobile money ecosystem. The country’s regulatory evolution demonstrated that payment innovation can scale rapidly when supervision and rules are tailored to real-world usage. Requirements around agent settlement practices, risk management and customer protections transformed mobile money from an experimental service into trusted infrastructure.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

That trust broadened the market — female users, rural users, small merchants and informal-sector workers included. This created a demand for additional fintech innovation such as credit scoring, savings products and digital merchant payments.

In Nigeria, the evolution of digital finance regulation illustrates another balance: promoting innovation while managing systemic risks. Financial regulators have periodically tightened and clarified licensing and compliance requirements to reduce fraud and increase system resilience. While such tightening can feel like a “brake” to startups, clearer licensing criteria and compliance guidance often become a “catalyst” over time by attracting more sustainable investment and reducing risk for legitimate players.

Latin America offers strong lessons on governance for digital trust in environments where inequality, misinformation risk and fraud are significant. Here, regulation often must protect consumers not only from product risks but also from market manipulation.

One area where trust and innovation collide is platform power. When a few platforms dominate distribution, market entry becomes harder. Regulatory frameworks that encourage competition can stimulate innovation by lowering “access barriers.”

Another lesson concerns consumer protection and data privacy. When users fear that personal data will be mishandled — or that digital services will not respond to complaints — adoption slows. Latin American regulators have increasingly focused on data protection implementation and enforcement to build consumer confidence. Where privacy rights are enforceable and institutions are capable, innovators can differentiate through trust rather than through opaque data practices.

Regulation also plays a vital role in managing misinformation and harmful online content. Yet here the “brake vs catalyst” balance is delicate: Heavy-handed approaches that undermine free expression can chill legitimate innovation in media, civic tech and journalism. The best models aim for procedural fairness, include clear standards for removal or restriction, transparency reports, avenues for appeal and platform obligations. They should be measurable rather than arbitrary.

A digital majority implies that digital systems are no longer peripheral; they are civic infrastructure. In that context, regulation is not an obstacle to progress — it becomes the condition for sustainable progress. When governance aligns innovation incentives with public values, it transforms trust into a multiplier. It reduces fraud, improves reliability, strengthens consumer rights and increases adoption. With more users and a more trusted environment, innovation accelerates and becomes more inclusive.

_Danton Remoto is writing a book on the digital majority. His literary books are being sold at Fully Booked, National Bookstore, Shopee, Lazada and Central Books website; Kinokuniya in Asia; and Amazon globally._

title: Chinese teacher recall sparks debate, concern
summary: ​RETIRED US Air Force Col. Ray Powell, director of maritime security initiative SeaLight, said that China has used travel and education warnings to pressure governments in diplomatic disputes. ​This comes as about 150 Chinese volunteer teac
content:
​RETIRED US Air Force Col. Ray Powell, director of maritime security initiative SeaLight, said that China has used travel and education warnings to pressure governments in diplomatic disputes.

​This comes as about 150 Chinese volunteer teachers were abruptly recalled from Philippine schools following security concerns and heightened scrutiny surrounding state-sponsored Chinese influence operations in the country.

​Geopolitical analyst Herman Tiu Laurel, president of the Asian Century Philippines Strategic Studies Institute, dismissed Powell’s allegations as speculative, saying the teachers’ parents sought their return out of concern for their children’s safety amid what he described as persistent anti-China media coverage.

*   [Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

The Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry reportedly said the recall was approved by the organization and the Chinese Embassy in Manila following concerns raised by parents in China.

​The circumstances surrounding the decision, including who ordered the teachers’ return and when, remain unclear.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

​Powell said no teacher, family member, or specific threat had been publicly identified to substantiate claims that the educators were in danger.

​The Chinese Embassy has denounced what it called “malicious smear campaigns” and urged the Philippine government to protect the safety and legitimate rights and interests of Chinese nationals.

​Powell said his concerns centered on the institutions involved in training and deploying the teachers, rather than on the educators themselves.

*   ![Image 1: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

​He cited records showing that Jinan University trained 43 of the 56 Filipino students in the Philippine Chinese Education Research Center’s 2024 teacher-training cohort. The university describes itself as jointly established with the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Committee United Front Work Department.

​Powell noted that China’s volunteer-teacher position list for 2027, published around Sept. 22, contained no Philippine posts, compared with 45 positions for 2025 and 32 for 2026. He said this suggested the program might already have been undergoing a reduction before the recall became public.

​Laurel said the lack of clarity over who ordered the teachers’ return undermined the allegations against Beijing. He maintained that the decision followed appeals from concerned parents worried about what he described as persistent anti-China coverage in Philippine media.

​Powell cited previous disputes to support his argument that China uses travel warnings and restrictions to exert political pressure.

*   ![Image 2: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

​During the 2012 Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) standoff, China issued travel safety advice and Chinese travel agencies suspended tours to the Philippines. Chinese authorities also rejected Philippine banana shipments, citing quarantine concerns.

​He cited China’s restrictions on group tours to South Korea in 2017 following Seoul’s decision to deploy a US-made missile defense system, as well as disputes involving Australia, Turkey, Japan, and Palau.

​Laurel countered that travel advisories are not unique to China. He cited efforts by Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to promote tourism to the Philippines and expand flights by Chinese airlines.

​He claimed Chinese tourist arrivals increased by 64 percent in 2026 but provided no supporting figures in his statement.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

​The reported recall has disrupted Mandarin instruction in some Manila schools, with affected students turning to substitute teachers and online classes.

​Powell maintained that scrutiny of Chinese-linked education programs should not be interpreted as opposition to Chinese teachers or Mandarin instruction, but as an examination of possible political influence behind the programs.

​The Department of National Defense (DND) has also defended scrutiny of foreign state-backed academic and cultural exchange programs, saying transparency is necessary to protect academic integrity and national security.

​Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has raised concerns about Jinan University’s links to Chinese-language teacher training and its academic work questioning Philippine sovereignty over Batanes.

​The DND has denied targeting Chinese schools, saying its concerns involve possible foreign influence rather than Chinese-language education itself.

title: ‘Bird’s-eye view’ enhances disaster response and climate resilience
summary: WHEN a major tropical cyclone tears across the archipelago, roads submerge, bridges collapse, and terrestrial communications often fail. In those critical early hours, emergency responders face a dangerous information void. The quickest way
content:
WHEN a major tropical cyclone tears across the archipelago, roads submerge, bridges collapse, and terrestrial communications often fail. In those critical early hours, emergency responders face a dangerous information void. The quickest way to see that deluge is not by road or air, but from low Earth orbit.

The Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA), satellite data underpins both immediate post-impact emergency operations and multidecade resilience planning. Tasked with managing the country’s Earth observation satellites, PhilSA has evolved from its origins in DOSTled research initiatives, moving beyond experimental scientific pursuits to become an indispensable pillar of the nation’s disaster risk reduction and climate adaptation infrastructure.

While the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) relies on meteorological orbiters to track typhoons, rain bands, and atmospheric dynamics in real time, PhilSA leverages Earth observation imagery to assess ground impact. The agency generates disaster extent maps that delineate the footprint of floods, landslides, volcanic activity, and earthquake damage.

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

A satellite pass offers a panoramic, high-altitude view that ground networks cannot replicate. A single sweep captures entire river basins, provinces, and inaccessible hazard zones, allowing national and local disaster agencies to dispatch relief, position search-and-rescue teams, and allocate capital where damage is concentrated.

“Satellites provide a bird’s-eye view of disasters that groundbased systems cannot, allowing them to monitor large areas in a single pass. This complements ground observations by providing a broader picture of what is happening across provinces, regions, or even the entire country, especially when access on the ground is limited or unsafe,” Gay Jane Perez, Director General of PhilSA told The Manila Times.
