By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Officials in the Pentagon clarified Thursday that the execution will be livestreamed and that more details would follow.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell had said Monday that President Donald Trump had approved the execution of Hasan.

Trump has previously been critical of public executions in Iran, at times using the possibility of protesters being killed by the Iranian government as a possible rationale for military action. Those warnings preceded his ultimate choice to attack Iran at the end of February over its ballistic missiles and the risk of it developing nuclear weapons.

*   ![Image 1: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

“We’ve been told that the killing in Iran is stopping,” Trump told reporters on Jan. 14 of this year. “It’s stopping and there’s no plan for executions.”

He repeated that claim on Jan. 20 at a White House press briefing, saying: “We let them know that if that happens, that will be a very bad day for them. And they decided not to do it. They didn’t hang the people.”

Slightly more than a month later in his State of the Union address, Trump said, “We stopped them from hanging a lot of them with the threat of serious violence.”

**The White House on Thursday immediately referred questions about the plans for the livestreamed execution to the Pentagon.**

*   ![Image 2: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

However, experts on military law said Hasan could choose to resist execution and file a habeas petition in civilian court, which could significantly delay the execution.

“It frankly might outlast the current administration, and who knows if the next one will have the same penchant for executions,” Eugene R. Fidell, a visiting lecturer at Yale Law School specializing in military law.

Hasan, an Army psychiatrist who held the rank of major, walked into a medical building where soldiers were were waiting in long lines to receive immunizations and medical clearance for deployment. He shouted “Allahu akbar” — Arabic for “God is great!” — and opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun.

During the trial it was revealed that Hasan spent weeks planning the deadly attack, and his preparation included videotaping a sales clerk showing him how to change the magazine on the pistol that he purchased. He would later go to a gun range outside Austin and ask for advice on how to reload with speed and precision from an instructor.

*   ![Image 3: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

Soldiers later testified that Hasan’s rapid reloading made it all but impossible to stop the shooting. Investigators recovered 146 shell casings inside the building and dozens more outside, where Hasan shot at the backs of soldiers fleeing toward the parking lot.

Hasan said it was an effort to stop them from going to Afghanistan and killing his fellow Muslims. A military judge barred him from presenting that as a defense during his trial. Hasan made almost no effort to defend himself in court, telling jurors when he acted as his own counsel that evidence would show he was the shooter and describing himself as a soldier who had “switched sides.”

Hegseth said the military hasn’t executed a servicemember by firing squad since World War II. The last military execution took place on April 13, 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was executed by hanging.

title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
summary: [![Image 1](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhyj_ek8VTEYw5CpVqkAK63I01D84oGBvRsHmwpjeAfat3TCDqzhXqRWXWCGkNZKwH3rF0uyeuowCSGcBT-mLkdw-174FA0gGh8ZIVKOXUbXt9w0eTZZTlMGE-ySkZIIkswfxe0-cEU9ww6E8iIpWI2eDQU_NrsezDxIoE2WNB
content:
[![Image 1](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhyj_ek8VTEYw5CpVqkAK63I01D84oGBvRsHmwpjeAfat3TCDqzhXqRWXWCGkNZKwH3rF0uyeuowCSGcBT-mLkdw-174FA0gGh8ZIVKOXUbXt9w0eTZZTlMGE-ySkZIIkswfxe0-cEU9ww6E8iIpWI2eDQU_NrsezDxIoE2WNBt8mDtG6nYeke9Ut17_JY/s1700-nu-rw-lo-l85-e365/china-email.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhyj_ek8VTEYw5CpVqkAK63I01D84oGBvRsHmwpjeAfat3TCDqzhXqRWXWCGkNZKwH3rF0uyeuowCSGcBT-mLkdw-174FA0gGh8ZIVKOXUbXt9w0eTZZTlMGE-ySkZIIkswfxe0-cEU9ww6E8iIpWI2eDQU_NrsezDxIoE2WNBt8mDtG6nYeke9Ut17_JY/s1700-nu-rw-lo-l85-e365/china-email.jpg)

Hackers tied to a Chinese cybersecurity company stole email from government organizations, law enforcement agencies, healthcare systems, and religious institutions in Southeast Asia, the FBI and agencies in 6 other countries said on October 8.

The company, **Integrity Technology Group**, has been sanctioned by the U.S. and the UK. The hackers scanned websites for flaws using a tool containing more than 1,300 scripts, guessed passwords for Microsoft 365 and Exchange accounts, and copied mailboxes using tools designed to collect mail.

The hackers have been breaking into networks since at least mid-January 2021, according to the agencies' [joint advisory](https://www.ic3.gov/CSA/2026/261008.pdf). It describes the hacking in the present tense but provides no date for any theft and does not specify how many organizations were breached.

The same hackers targeted U.S. government services, critical manufacturing, healthcare, and IT organizations, along with U.S. law enforcement, education, and religious groups. Organizations in Southeast Asia, Africa, and North America were also targeted.

The hackers also run a web application that "provides third-party access to stolen email content," the advisory said. It does not identify those third parties.

In September 2024, the FBI [disrupted a botnet](https://thehackernews.com/2024/09/new-raptor-train-iot-botnet-compromises.html), a network of hijacked devices, that the U.S. Justice Department said Integrity Technology Group controlled. It held more than 200,000 routers, cameras, and other consumer devices, and Lumen researchers had named it Raptor Train.

[![Image 2: Cybersecurity](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjVYuoalvwUlwvLZFDideJ8jW4rz-IodX0Lwi7uyP7Ab0wiDeu_BqVhPDdejQQ65MC3p9Xc4MApnHz56NJ5SDc1HMg0DvozkkGYv9TGtDLCh26v1yD5-GyzQxnA5-6A6B4beW96H_6FyrByq22cvU5JDF-i8e5GIfV4wg1SpCvjwAJt74FaqkAb2gzqE7ll/s728-nu-rw-lo-l85-e365/core-d.png)](https://thehackernews.uk/growth-ai-control-d)

The 2024 action dealt with the botnet. The new advisory covers how the hackers get into networks and what they take. It is based on evidence the FBI recovered and observed during several investigations related to the company.

### Who Is Behind It[](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/fbi-says-china-linked-hackers-ran.html#who-is-behind-it)

The agencies describe Integrity Technology Group as "a China-based for-profit company with links to the Chinese government" whose employees build or get cyber tools "for use and sale," host infrastructure, and break into networks.

The advisory uses a single label, "the threat actors," for the company and the hackers it enables. It does not say which of them carried out each break-in.

The U.S. Treasury [sanctioned the company](https://thehackernews.com/2025/01/us-treasury-sanctions-beijing.html) in January 2025 for its role in several computer break-ins against U.S. victims. The UK [sanctioned it](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-clamps-down-on-china-based-companies-for-reckless-and-irresponsible-activity-in-cyberspace) in December 2025.

Christopher Wray, then the FBI director, [said in 2024](https://www.fbi.gov/news/speeches-and-testimony/director-wray-s-remarks-at-the-2024-aspen-cyber-summit) that the company's "chairman has publicly admitted that for years his company has collected intelligence and performed reconnaissance for Chinese government security agencies."

The hackers' methods are "consistent with" activity that security companies track as Flax Typhoon, Ethereal Panda, and RedJuliett, among others, the advisory said. Those names may not match the U.S. government's own tracking one-to-one, and the same hackers may also carry out work unrelated to Integrity Technology Group.

Flax Typhoon is Microsoft's name for a China-based group that it [described in 2023](https://thehackernews.com/2023/08/china-linked-flax-typhoon-cyber.html) as targeting organizations in Taiwan.

Integrity Technology Group rejected the U.S. accusations in January 2025. It told the Shanghai Stock Exchange that the U.S. move had no factual basis, [the Associated Press reported](https://www.clickondetroit.com/business/2025/01/06/china-protests-us-sanctions-for-its-alleged-role-in-hacking-complains-of-foreign-hacker-attacks/). A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson, asked about the sanctions, said China firmly opposed the U.S. action, according to the same report.

### How the Hackers Get In[](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/fbi-says-china-linked-hackers-ran.html#how-the-hackers-get-in)

The hackers look for flaws in networks and web applications with open-source scanners such as Nmap, masscan, and WPScan, the advisory said. Their scans focus on ports 21, 22, 53, 80, 443, and 1080.

"The use of open source tools typically found on GitHub suggests the threat actors tend to look for more vulnerable targets," the agencies said.

The hackers have also used a scanner called MicroScan since as early as 2017. It is a Python web application containing more than 1,300 penetration testing scripts designed to scan websites for specific flaws. The hackers have used the scripts against services including OpenSSL, Oracle WebLogic Server, Rejetto HFS, WordPress, Juniper ScreenOS, Jenkins, and Apache Struts.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre, one of the agencies behind the advisory, said in [its news release](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/news/china-linked-actors-called-out-by-uk-and-international-partners-for-targeting-sensitive-data) that the hackers are "uniquely using AI tools, such as automated scanning." The advisory itself does not mention AI.

The hackers mostly get in with command-line tools built on exploit code written in languages such as Python and Go. The advisory lists 8 known flaws that it says were successfully exploited. The flaws were found in the hackers' penetration testing scripts.

The table shows the affected versions as the advisory gives them and, where one could be confirmed, the release that fixes the flaw.

| Flaw | Product | Affected Versions in the Advisory | Fixed In |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CVE-2014-6278 | GNU Bash | Through 4.3 bash43-026 | Not confirmed |
| CVE-2015-3306* | ProFTPD | 1.3.5 | [1.3.5a](https://github.com/proftpd/proftpd/blob/1.3.5/NEWS) |
| CVE-2015-5477* | ISC BIND | 9.x before 9.9.7-P2 and 9.10.x before 9.10.2-P3 | [9.9.7-P2 or 9.10.2-P3](https://kb.isc.org/docs/aa-01272) |
| CVE-2016-3081* | Apache Struts | 2.3.19 to 2.3.20.2, 2.3.21 to 2.3.24.1, and 2.3.25 to 2.3.28 | [2.3.20.3, 2.3.24.3, or 2.3.28.1](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/WW/pages/62693266/S2-032) |
| CVE-2019-11510 | Pulse Connect Secure | 8.2 before 8.2R12.1, 8.3 before 8.3R7.1, and 9.0 before 9.0R3.4 | 8.2R12.1, 8.3R7.1, or 9.0R3.4, from the advisory's ranges |
| CVE-2021-22205 | GitLab | All versions starting from 11.9 | [13.8.8, 13.9.6, or 13.10.3](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-22205), per its NVD record |
| CVE-2021-3199* | ONLYOFFICE Document Server | 5.1.5 through 5.6.2 | [5.6.3](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer/blob/903fe5ab7a275bd69c3c3346af2d21cf87ebeabf/CHANGELOG.md#563) |
| CVE-2023-22894* | Strapi | Up to 4.5.5 | [4.8.0](https://strapi.io/blog/security-disclosure-of-vulnerabilities-cve) |

The advisory marks 5 of the 8 with an asterisk and describes them as newly added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, the list of flaws that the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) says have been used in attacks. They were not in the [catalog data that CISA publishes on GitHub](https://github.com/cisagov/kev-data) (version 2026.10.04) when The Hacker News checked at 18:05 UTC on October 8.

Strapi's own advisory gives a wider range than the joint advisory. It says versions from 3.2.1 through 4.7.9, but not including 4.8.0, are affected.

Two flaws depend on a setting. The Struts flaw works only when Dynamic Method Invocation is turned on, and Apache says turning it off is an alternative to upgrading. The ONLYOFFICE flaw applies when JWT is used, according to its NVD record.

The BIND flaw is a denial-of-service bug that makes the DNS server exit.

Another way in is a fake login. The FBI recovered a cross-site scripting (XSS) payload that changes a vulnerable web page to show username and password fields.

After a visitor enters any username and password, the page offers a password-protected ZIP file that holds a program named live700_v1.exe. That program starts a process named DiagTrack.exe, the same name as a legitimate Windows program, which sends encrypted traffic to dns.studiocloud[.]xyz.

The FBI attributes that domain to Integrity Technology Group and assesses that the malware likely targets email.

The hackers also use password spraying, which means trying a few common passwords against many accounts. For this, they use EBurst, an open-source Python tool that targets Microsoft 365 and Exchange accounts.

EBurst tries logins through Exchange interfaces that include ECP, EWS, OAB, OWA, RPC, API, MAPI, PowerShell, Autodiscover, and Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync, according to its README file. Defenders should cover these interfaces, the agencies said.

### How They Stay and What They Take[](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/fbi-says-china-linked-hackers-ran.html#how-they-stay-and-what-they-take)

To keep access, the hackers install SoftEther, a legitimate VPN program that security software is less likely to flag, the advisory said. They often rename the installer conhost.exe or dllhost.exe so it looks like a Windows file, and they set the client to reconnect each time the machine starts.

To take credentials, they ran a tool named DC.exe that uses DCSync, a technique that copies data from a domain controller through Active Directory's replication service. It copied account credentials, group membership details, and trust relationships.

For email, the hackers built a bot from a PHP script named Curlc4.txt. It collects mail through Exchange Web Services (EWS), an interface that also gives access to calendars and contacts.

The bot compresses the mail, sometimes encrypts it, and uploads it to a remote server. The script appears to be stand-alone rather than installed on a hacked device, and its main command-and-control domain was natcloudservice[.]com.

A second tool, office-cli, keeps going back to Microsoft 365 accounts to take mail from different time periods. It works from configuration files that hold a client ID, tenant ID, and secret, and it avoids detection by using legitimate access methods, the agencies said.

The FBI also saw the hackers download databases or pull data from victims' email by hand.

[![Image 3: Cybersecurity](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjVV2rRkX8tRMF6gCzemvQNpwFwGxRWxY1cJEYfoLLSj1EZYJOlj5WTR77t0i6kELXujYcaHTpRDqTjCbVHH5Pnh7wzxUiKP5j4dsDkWIMlp2bmpZsL0jeAsA_19pHH5UPtyBvNkZdyGEULOAsXPcraMP5CYjQRFefhXRSdEjYkrdcpUnc4ILcvcdEfAauE/s728-nu-rw-lo-l85-e365/tl-d.jpg)](https://thehackernews.uk/network-defense-d)

In some cases, the hackers limited access to the stolen data to IP addresses in Xiamen, China.

Users of the web application for third parties can view the mail of a specific account by adding arguments to a URL.

### What Defenders Should Do[](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/fbi-says-china-linked-hackers-ran.html#what-defenders-should-do)

# Japan to China: Show ‘respect’ in addressing PM

**TOKYO** — Tokyo has told Beijing to “show appropriate respect” after a Chinese spokesman addressed Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi only by her name with no title.

Japan’s foreign ministry spokesman Toshihiro Kitamura said on Wednesday that Tokyo had relayed its concerns to Beijing after its foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun referred to the Japanese head of government only as “Sanae Takaichi” at a news conference last month.

Historically tense ties between Japan and China have soured further recently, after Takaichi suggested in November 2025 that Tokyo may intervene in an attack on Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its territory.

title: Fiji-based Chinese official paid bribes for Beijing – US
summary: **NADI, Fiji** — The United States on Thursday accused a Fijian citizen working for a Chinese state agency of allegedly paying bribes to advance Beijing’s interests in the Pacific nation. Zhao Fugang, director of the Overseas Chinese Servic
content:
**NADI, Fiji** — The United States on Thursday accused a Fijian citizen working for a Chinese state agency of allegedly paying bribes to advance Beijing’s interests in the Pacific nation.

Zhao Fugang, director of the Overseas Chinese Service Center in Fiji’s capital Suva, engaged in “significant corruption” on behalf of actors in China, Washington claimed.

“Zhao abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance China-based government, business, and criminal interests,” State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott said.

*   [Bear kills man, maims woman in Mongolia](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/world/asia-oceania/bear-kills-man-maims-woman-in-mongolia/2441773)

“His actions constituted significant corruption and adversely affected US interests in Fiji,” he added.

Zhao and his immediate family members will be barred from entering the US as a result, Washington said.

The US embassy in Suva said in a statement on Thursday that Zhao’s actions left the Pacific nation open to “malign foreign influence” by Chinese government, business and criminal actors.

[![Image 1: HEARTBREAK HOTEL? A general view of the Yue Lai Hotel, owned by local businessman Zhao Fugang, in Fiji’s capital Suva on Oct. 8, 2026. AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251244.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251244.jpg)
HEARTBREAK HOTEL? A general view of the Yue Lai Hotel, owned by local businessman Zhao Fugang, in Fiji’s capital Suva on Oct. 8, 2026. AFP PHOTO

*   ![Image 2: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

“Corruption stunts opportunities for foreign investment and foreign assistance, facilitates organized crime, offers a permissive environment for malign actors, drives illegal migration, and undermines citizens’ faith in government,” the statement added.

Zhao, also a prominent local businessman, said in a statement sent to Agence France-Presse (AFP) that he “categorically” denied the allegations.

“They are unsubstantiated,” he said in the statement issued by his lawyers.

“I have not been questioned by any Fijian authority about these matters, and no charge has been laid against me,” he added.

*   ![Image 3: Duterte, Carpio’s combined income below VP’s declared net worth — BIR](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251142.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte, Carpio’s combined income below VP’s declared net worth — BIR](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/duterte-carpios-combined-income-below-vps-declared-net-worth-bir/2441516)

Zhao also said he had written to the US embassy requesting the full details of the allegations against him.

“I respect the laws of Fiji and will cooperate fully with any lawful inquiry by the Fijian authorities,” he said.

An investigation by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project in 2024 alleged Zhao that operated as a key point man for Beijing’s interests in Fiji and was a naturalized citizen of the Pacific nation.

It also reported that Zhao was suspected by Australian law enforcement to be a top player in a transnational syndicate linked to human trafficking, money laundering and drugs smuggling.

*   ![Image 4: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

Zhao’s lawyer Nikheel Nambiar told AFP he denied those claims and that allegations of influence-peddling for Beijing were “false and misleading.”

China’s embassy in Suva did not respond to multiple requests for comment from AFP.

But Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Mao Ning told a regular briefing in Beijing on Thursday that she was not aware of the case, adding: “We have always opposed any slander and smear directed at China.”

Beijing says Overseas Chinese Service Centers help its citizens with administrative issues abroad, like renewing drivers’ licenses.

But rights groups have alleged they are front groups for Beijing to push its interests abroad, including the targeting of dissidents.

China has sought in recent years to deepen its influence among Pacific Island nations, to the consternation of the US and its ally Australia.

Beijing sent waves through the region in 2022 when it signed a secretive security pact with the Solomon Islands, stoking fears it could lead to a permanent military presence one day.

title: Myanmar’s leader to take back migrants from Malaysia
summary: **PUTRAJAYA, Malaysia** — Myanmar will accept more Burmese migrants held in Malaysia “as soon as possible,” the war-torn nation’s leader said on Thursday despite human rights concerns over the opaque repatriation scheme. Min Aung Hlaing mad
content:
**PUTRAJAYA, Malaysia** — Myanmar will accept more Burmese migrants held in Malaysia “as soon as possible,” the war-torn nation’s leader said on Thursday despite human rights concerns over the opaque repatriation scheme.

Min Aung Hlaing made the pledge on a visit to his counterpart in Malaysia as he works to bring his country back into the international fold after staging a coup in February 2021.

Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim invited Min Aung Hlaing, now installed as civilian president, for a two-day visit to discuss the return of thousands of migrants to his country.

*   [Bear kills man, maims woman in Mongolia](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/world/asia-oceania/bear-kills-man-maims-woman-in-mongolia/2441773)

Malaysia has historically offered safe haven to those exiled from Myanmar, hosting 190,000 refugees or asylum seekers from the nation — mostly Rohingya — according to the United Nations.

But Anwar is making a repatriation push amid an uptick of anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia, defying concerns from the UN that his scheme cannot guarantee their safe homecomings to Myanmar.

The country has been wracked by war since Min Aung Hlaing’s putsch, and there are fears the persecuted Rohingya may return to a country where they suffer violent persecution many deem genocide.

“We will take those verified nationals back as soon as possible,” Min Aung Hlaing said at a joint news conference with Anwar in the administrative capital Putrajaya.

‘Enhance collaboration’

*   ![Image 1: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

Min Aung Hlaing has been a pariah in many capitals abroad since his coup unleashed a civil war, but Anwar invited him for talks about returning Myanmar migrants.

Nearly 1,500 migrants arrived in back in Myanmar on Sunday after a five-day navy vessel voyage from Malaysia, where they were being held in detention centers before being shipped out.

[![Image 2: DIPLOMATIC DANCE Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing (left) and Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim shake hands during their meeting in the Malaysian administrative capital Putrajaya on Oct. 8, 2026. PHOTO FROM MYANMAR’S PRESIDENTIAL PRESS INFORMATION BUREAU VIA AFP](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251240.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251240.jpg)
DIPLOMATIC DANCE Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing (left) and Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim shake hands during their meeting in the Malaysian administrative capital Putrajaya on Oct. 8, 2026. PHOTO FROM MYANMAR’S PRESIDENTIAL PRESS INFORMATION BUREAU VIA AFP

*   ![Image 3: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

Anwar announced in July that Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 Rohingya members, but the Malaysian government later said those sent back would be of “various ethnicities,” not only Rohingya.

Myanmar last month pledged “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad, after criticism from the UN and rights groups.

Min Aung Hlaing’s two-day trip also comes as he makes a push for diplomatic recognition after his installation as civilian president in April, following elections branded a charade by democracy watchdogs.

Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) said in July they were seeking “gradual” engagement with Myanmar.

*   ![Image 4: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

The 11-nation organization has frozen Myanmar out of high-level summits since the coup, presenting a united front to pressure its leaders into engaging in its conflict resolution plan.

But analysts say the consensus is now fraying.

Malaysia marks the fifth Southeast Asian nation to host Min Aung Hlaing since he transitioned to ruling the country as its nominally civilian president.

A five-point peace plan adopted by Asean leaders in April 2021, which, among other things, call for an immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar, has shown very little signs of progress.

This was highlighted by a Myanmar military air strike late last month on a market in the country’s west, killing some 50 people — one of the deadliest recent bombings of the civil war.

“We, and [on] our part in Malaysia, will do whatever is possible to make sure that we enhance this collaboration,” Anwar said on Thursday.

The aim ultimately was to “take Myanmar as part of our community of nations without prejudice, and particularly in the context of [the] Asean,” he added.

title: Russia warns of ‘false’ info amid new plague reports
summary: **MOSCOW**— Russia warned on Wednesday against “false” information as reports emerged of a second suspected case of the plague in Siberia, with Washington and Brussels calling for transparency and neighboring Mongolia tightening health surv
content:
**MOSCOW**— Russia warned on Wednesday against “false” information as reports emerged of a second suspected case of the plague in Siberia, with Washington and Brussels calling for transparency and neighboring Mongolia tightening health surveillance.

Russian news outlet People of Baikal reported last Friday that a 28-year-old woman employed at a plague research institute in Siberia’s Irkutsk region had died of the disease, possibly after contracting it from a broken test tube.

International concern has, meanwhile, grown over the death and suspicions that a second employee at the institute fell ill.

*   [‘Church must review attitude to sexuality, intimacy’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/world/americas-emea/church-must-review-attitude-to-sexuality-intimacy/2441776)

The United States, the European Union and the World Health Organization (WHO) have all called on Russia to be transparent about the situation.

Mongolia’s government said on Wednesday that “health surveillance and monitoring measures [were] being implemented at the border” with Russia.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also urged Moscow to clarify “media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause” at the Irkutsk institute.

Russian authorities have played down the reports, determining that the woman died of pneumonia and insisting there was no risk of an outbreak.

Asked about reports of a second case, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that “the vast majority of what the media is reporting regarding this situation is false information.”

*   ![Image 1: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

People should rely solely on official statements from Russian health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor, he insisted.

US President Donald Trump, asked if a “bio-weapon” was involved, told reporters in the Oval Office: “We don’t think so. We’re going to find out soon enough, but we don’t think so.”

“If you listen to them, it’s under control. But you know, people have said that before about other things,” he added.

‘No epidemic risks’

*   ![Image 2: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

The Russian health agency said earlier on Wednesday that it had determined “there are no epidemic risks for the population.”

It said extensive investigations had uncovered “no emergencies” and that the lab had complied with “proper control when working with pathogenic microorganisms.”

“More than 90 percent of contacts have completed medical observation,” it added.

“No health disorders associated with infectious pathology were detected,” it said, adding that “the results of almost 5,000 laboratory tests did not reveal any dangerous pathogenic microorganisms.”

*   ![Image 3: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

[![Image 4: TRANSPARENCY CALL World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus looks on during a press conference on global health issues in the city of Geneva, southwestern Switzerland, on Oct. 7, 2026. AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251252.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251252.jpg)
TRANSPARENCY CALL World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus looks on during a press conference on global health issues in the city of Geneva, southwestern Switzerland, on Oct. 7, 2026. AFP PHOTO

The agency also said the woman had been “vaccinated and had immunity to dangerous infections with which she worked.”

‘False’

Plague is a bacterial disease that can occur in several forms, including pneumonic plague, the most contagious type, which can spread through respiratory droplets.

Bubonic plague is transmitted by infected fleas.

Pneumonic plague can be fatal if not treated early, the WHO said.

Irkutsk Gov. Igor Kobzev said on Monday that an inspection by Rospotrebnadzor had found that the woman died of “pneumonia of undetermined aetiology.”

“No microorganisms linked to the young woman’s professional work were found in her biological samples,” he said, adding that no other staff at the institute had sought medical attention since her death.

In the town of Shelekhov, where she was reported to have died, residents spoke of stepped-up health precautions in place.

“My brother’s in [elementary] school. They’ve already made masks compulsory, so they have to wear them everywhere,” Alina, a 22-year-old Shelekhov resident, told AFP.

Oksana, a 35-year-old manager, was admitted to a maternity ward for observation but said she could not be discharged and spent four days in quarantine.

“In the hospital, people started talking about how a woman had died and they suspected it was the plague,” she said, adding: “They stopped accepting lab samples and wouldn’t let anyone out. So it was very strict.”

Risk ‘low’

Those assurances have done little to quell international concern.

The US made a formal request to Russia for information, a source close to the matter said on Tuesday, while Trump said he had “a call scheduled” with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin and would speak with him “very soon.”

Asked about this, Peskov insisted on Wednesday that he had “no information” regarding a formal US request for clarification, nor about a call scheduled between the two leaders.

European Commission spokeswoman Eva Hrncirova, meanwhile, called on Wednesday for Russia to “share timely and transparent reporting” about the reported plague case.

While determining there were no epidemic risks, Rospotrebnadzor said it had implemented a set of “anti-epidemic measures” as a precaution and in line with sanitary legislation.

It also stressed that it had shared information with the WHO in accordance with international health regulations.

The WHO said on Tuesday that its initial risk assessment, based on available information, was moderate-to-low for Irkutsk, low for Russia as a whole, and very low for Europe.

title: Playing the high-stakes game: The Luzon Economic Corridor
summary: WHEN the Philippines and the United States inked the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) back in 2014, the critics and political commentary class were practically hyperventilating. “Is Manila giving away the farm? Are we turning o
content:
WHEN the Philippines and the United States inked the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) back in 2014, the critics and political commentary class were practically hyperventilating. “Is Manila giving away the farm? Are we turning our front yard into a stage for someone else’s geopolitical drama? Is our sovereignty being bartered away for a pat on the head from Washington?”

For over a decade, the narrative remained stuck in an utterly exhausting binary: You were either a fiercely principled guardian of national pride or a helpless pawn in a Western superpower’s grand strategy. Every joint exercise was parsed like a scandal, every diplomatic statement scrutinized for hints of capitulation and every strategic agreement framed as a zero-sum compromise where Manila inevitably drew the short stick.

Fast-forward to today, and the doomsayers have officially run out of scripts.

*   [Questions on Senator Robin’s questions](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/opinion/columns/questions-on-senator-robins-questions/2440972)

The military alliance didn’t just hold its ground; it expanded with fresh EDCA sites in 2023. More importantly, Manila turned that renewed geopolitical attention into something more concrete: massive economic leverage. That shift is what makes the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) more than another infrastructure slogan. It is the clearest sign yet that routine security dialogues can be converted into a multibillion-dollar development engine.

Because let’s be entirely honest for a moment: defense pacts and security guarantees are necessary, but deepwater port modernizations, high-speed freight railways, semiconductor supply chains and a flood of institutional foreign capital? Now that is how you get everyone’s undivided attention.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

What started as a tight trilateral security partnership among the Philippines, the United States and Japan back in early 2024 has quickly morphed into a heavyweight international club. The G7 economies have stepped up, the European Union is involved, and major global players from Canada and Denmark to Sweden and the United Kingdom have pulled up a seat at the table.

This level of international backing is not something you pull off through wishful thinking or basic geopolitical posturing. Getting the world’s most sophisticated economies to actively line up behind a single regional infrastructure blueprint is a loud, clear vote of confidence. More than a diplomatic win, it shows that the Philippines is no longer merely reacting to regional pressure; it is using its geography, alliances and market potential to set terms and build economic leverage.

That is why the LEC deserves to be read not only as an economic program, but as a legacy-defining strategic wager. Looking at the big picture, it could easily become President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s most enduring structural legacy. The average citizen navigating the daily commute might not feel the seismic shift just yet. High-level infrastructure, policy alignment and mega-corridor planning don’t yield headline results overnight. But a decade from now, as the dust settles and the supply chains click into place, we will likely look back at this precise window as the moment the country stopped playing defensive policy and started building real global leverage.

*   ![Image 1: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

That long-term legacy, however, depends on execution. Grand diplomatic speeches and high-profile international summits do not build freight rails or clear regulatory red tape on their own. Behind every major strategic vision, someone must keep the numbers honest, prepare the institutions and make sure the investment case actually holds up, and that is where Executive Secretary Ralph Recto enters the narrative.

When the initiative was first introduced, Recto, then serving as finance secretary, played the pivotal role of translating high-level diplomatic ambition into hard, bankable reality. While the presidency worked the global stage, Recto focused on the unglamorous mechanics: overhauling fiscal incentives, sharpening the investment climate, aggressively engaging foreign institutional investors and establishing the structural discipline required to handle massive foreign direct investment.

His focus on structural readiness meant that when foreign capital finally arrived, it didn’t hit a wall of bureaucratic inertia. By building a stable, predictable policy framework, he helped ensure the corridor could absorb large-scale foreign capital and convert those paper commitments into real-world domestic growth, high-value manufacturing and expanded tax bases. That is where the story moves from diplomatic architecture to everyday economic consequence.

Those consequences become most visible in the geography of Luzon itself. By physically and economically stitching together Subic, Clark, Metro Manila and Batangas, the LEC creates a hyper-connected economic engine through the absolute heart of Luzon. We are talking about a region that already drives half of the nation’s GDP and handles the overwhelming majority of its trade. Connecting deep-sea ports to international airports, high-tech industrial hubs and clean energy grids means shorter logistics turnarounds, lower operational costs, high-quality jobs in advanced manufacturing and wealth circulating beyond traditional urban bottlenecks.

*   ![Image 2: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

If the corridor is to deliver that payoff, the next challenge is not conceptual but collective. The only missing variable in this entire equation is our own tendency toward skepticism and overthinking good fortune. Opportunities on this scale, backed by an alignment of major global economies, do not knock on the door twice. Wasting time debating yesterday’s political tropes while the rest of the region accelerates is a luxury we simply cannot afford.​

Nation-building at this tier is an all-hands effort. It demands that the state maintains its momentum, the private sector steps up with serious capital, local government units clear the way and the public recognizes the long-game value of what is being built.

*   ![Image 3: Duterte, Carpio’s combined income below VP’s declared net worth — BIR](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251142.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte, Carpio’s combined income below VP’s declared net worth — BIR](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/duterte-carpios-combined-income-below-vps-declared-net-worth-bir/2441516)

Rarely do national strategic interests, domestic economic priorities and global capital line up with this level of precision. The foundation is poured, the partners are at the table and the green light is flashing. It is time to stop questioning our seat at the high table and start driving the momentum forward.

title: Likhang HABI 16
summary: TODAY at One Ayala Space on the fifth floor, the Likhang HABI Fair opens with free admission to the public to see, learn and enjoy Filipino textiles and woven crafts from 100 booths. Likhang HABI is all about Filipino traditional and innova
content:
TODAY at One Ayala Space on the fifth floor, the Likhang HABI Fair opens with free admission to the public to see, learn and enjoy Filipino textiles and woven crafts from 100 booths.

Likhang HABI is all about Filipino traditional and innovative artistry using our natural fibers woven into textiles, mats, baskets, household objects and innovative modern items that fit into our world of the past and the present, and look forward to the future.

It has been a 16-year journey for Likhang HABI, which seems to have taken place in the blink of an eye for those of us who were present at its creation.

*   [Questions on Senator Robin’s questions](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/opinion/columns/questions-on-senator-robins-questions/2440972)

But first, we have to pay tribute to our social events of yesteryears, as well as today, where fashion using traditional Filipino woven textiles was always selected to be at the forefront. We remember the annual Kahirup Ball of the Visayan community, the Mancomunidad Pampangueña Ball and the Club Bulakeño Annual Charity Ball, all of them featuring traditional textiles.

These are piña, the legendary pineapple fiber said to be the queen of them all. Equally well-known is the world-wide-recognized Filipino fiber, abaca, resilient for industrial use, as well as for fashionable clothing. Both these fibers stand out among our many others woven in different ways for different purposes.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

We also pay tribute to the visionaries who put their efforts toward promoting, processing, innovating and bringing them to public attention. There is Patis Tesoro, who has now been conferred National Artist honors, who has devoted her fashion career to piña and Filipino artistry in embroidery and embellishment of piña in colorful, enchanting and useful ways. Former first lady Ming Ramos was the first to give our native fabrics her personal and government support in an organized fashion though other first ladies from previous and post-Ramos administrations also paid attention to them by wearing them and encouraging others to do so. And Lourdes Montinola, who came up with the first Philippine book devoted to piña.

Then there were the fashion designers of yesteryear and today who have brought our fabrics public attention. I will name only those in the past as today there are many, many more, too numerous to enumerate individually, but all promoting Filipino fabrics. Ramon Valera, Ben Farrales, Inno Sotto, Aurelio Alonzo, Pitoy Moreno, Gang Gomez, Joe Salazar, Christian Espiritu are some of them. I am sure I have missed many, but these and all those unnamed were responsible for keeping Filipino fabrics in the public eye, as well as making them aspirational for all who learned of them.

And yet all along, there was no organized Filipino textile group until 2009 when the Philippine Textile Council Inc. was formed after (not before) the Philippines hosted the Second Asean Traditional Textiles Symposium. The first symposium took place in Indonesia spurred by an Asean Foundation grant. Our Indonesian friends then looked toward the Philippines to do the next one. The Philippines did with the assistance of the National Museum under director Cora Alvina and organized by the Museum Foundation of the Philippines with significant help from President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo and a contribution from the National Commission on Arts and Culture, as well as private citizens.

*   ![Image 1: Duterte, Carpio’s combined income below VP’s declared net worth — BIR](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251142.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte, Carpio’s combined income below VP’s declared net worth — BIR](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/duterte-carpios-combined-income-below-vps-declared-net-worth-bir/2441516)

The symposium required a selling exposition. And in the Second Asean Traditional Textiles Symposium, 12 booths managed to be put up to offer Filipino woven products. There was also a fashion show of Philippine fabrics with Filipino designers recruited for the occasion.

The Second Asean Traditional Textiles Symposium was deemed a success despite the absence of a Filipino textile society per se. So, it was inevitable that one had to be organized and thus was born in 2009 the Philippine Textile Council Inc., now all of 16 years old.

It has published five books on Philippine woven arts. The fifth will be launched at this year’s Likhang HABI Fair on Oct. 9. It will be on abaca. We also have three film documentaries, and there will be Kwentong Kultura talks every day during the Fair on various subjects and aspects of Filipino woven arts by experts. There will also be an exhibit of especially curated fashions in Philippine textiles by the Benilde Fashion Museum, which will be interesting, educational and stimulating.

The Likhang HABI Fair also has a competition segment for piña and abaca. They are the Lourdes Montinola Piña Weaving Competition and the Eloisa Hizon Gomez Abaca Weaving Competition. They are very established competitions which have brought up innovative weaves, resurrected long-forgotten traditional weaves and come up with imaginative blends and embellishments. The winning entries will be on exhibit at the fair.

*   ![Image 2: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

The Philippine Textile Council has also become known and respected in other countries beginning with the Asean countries with our Indonesian, Malaysian, Thai, Brunei, Singaporean, Vietnamese, Laotian, Myanmar, Cambodian, Timor-Leste friends whom we meet every two years at the symposium. All advocate their traditional textiles and the traditional way of making them as well as innovations. In this advocacy we are a united brotherhood and sisterhood.

The Philippine Textile Council has also participated in international exhibits and events. Aside from the Asean countries, it has been to the US, Jordan, and lately, the United Nations. This year piña took center stage at the UN Fashion Lifestyle Network annual meeting in September. This event is aligned with New York Fashion Week, and Philippine Textile Council board member Wilma Huang represented the Philippines. Piña was hailed as the revered and legendary Filipino traditional fabric that is an eco-friendly luxury material. And of course, Filipino artistry was the center of attention, particularly for its transition to modern needs, where its qualities of zero waste, biodegradable character, organic breathability and carbon-frugality integral to it were acclaimed.

*   ![Image 3: LTO identifies rider in hit-and-run incident involving 'It's Showtime' host](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1249307.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[LTO identifies rider in hit-and-run incident involving 'It's Showtime' host](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/07/news/lto-identifies-rider-in-hit-and-run-incident-involving-its-showtime-host/2440550)

Yes, at 16 Likhang HABI and the Philippine Textile Council have come a long way in what seems a short period of time. It is because tradition, identity, artistry, craftsmanship and the use of our natural resources have been recognized and valued.

title: Bendalista politics: Requiem for Yellow politics
summary: **Last of a series** FR. Daniel Franklin Pilario, CM, president of Adamson University, was right when he wrote in 2025 that “the [yellow] ribbon and the song (i.e., ‘Tie a yellow ribbon round the ole oak tree’) became a rallying symbol of p
content:
**Last of a series**

FR. Daniel Franklin Pilario, CM, president of Adamson University, was right when he wrote in 2025 that “the [yellow] ribbon and the song (i.e., ‘Tie a yellow ribbon round the ole oak tree’) became a rallying symbol of protest against the repression of Marcos’ martial rule.” He added:

“We wore yellow, but we did not call ourselves ‘dilawan.’ We just wanted to protest against the dictatorship. We just wanted Marcos out. When we shouted ‘Tama na. Sobra na. Palitan na,’ we shouted while wearing yellow. Yellow was a color of resistance.

*   [Questions on Senator Robin’s questions](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/opinion/columns/questions-on-senator-robins-questions/2440972)

It was not only about Cory or Ninoy but about what their lives symbolized — martyrdom, hope and love of country. It was also more against Marcos, against martial law, against the repression — and all that he represented.”

In this honest and succinct summary lies the foundations for the inevitability of the Yellows’ demise.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Yellow politics is not the private inheritance of the Aquinos and their cohorts. It never was. Rather, as Fr. Pilario showed, it drew strength and vitality from the Filipino people’s unquenchable thirst for democratic ideals that serve the interests of the nation, not any partisan political group, whether pro-Marcos or pro-Aquino.

Ferdinand Marcos Sr. was so contemptible because he usurped power from the sovereign democratic Filipino people, exploiting the political instability of his times, magnifying the communist threat and the fractious nature of Mindanao/Muslim secessionism, and installing himself dictator through the Bendalista-style declaration of martial law in 1972.

FM was the OG Bendalista.

*   ![Image 1: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

Still, the Filipino people gave the tyrant a chance to deliver on his bold promise of making the Philippines great again, and to safeguard the security of the nation against threats from within and from without. In time, however, the Marcos conjugal dictatorship of Ferdinand and Imelda unraveled itself through treachery toward the national interest and an unbridled debauchery toward public resources.

Yellow politics never centered around former senator Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino Jr. — or any specific personality — despite the necro-political initiatives of his widow, President Corazon “Cory” Aquino, to self-interestedly brainwash the nation. Ninoy was merely the most visible reminder of the evils of the Marcos dictatorship, for which his clan was handsomely rewarded in the political arena.

Of greater import was the fervent desire of Filipinos to be freed from the shackles and corruption of the conjugal Marcos dictatorship. Yellow politics promised the Filipino people — which Cory Aquino and her political clan want the nation to conveniently forget about — in the words of Andres Bonifacio and the Katipunan 100 years earlier, “kaginhawahan” and “kasaganaan” for the nation once the avarice of the Marcoses was ended.

Freedom, democracy and good governance only made sense to Filipinos as necessary tools to bring about kaginhawahan and kasaganaan for the nation. Without kaginhawahan and kasaganaan, the ideals of freedom, democracy and good governance are hollow and meaningless, drowning in the ocean of vagueness and ambiguity, incorrigibly shielding the bewildered incompetence and perversion of the usurpers of the spirit of EDSA 1986.

*   ![Image 2: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

This is why Yellow politics is on the verge of disintegration.

How can the zealous witch hunt against Vice President Sara Duterte (and the Duterte family, if we are going to be brutally honest) be rationalized vis-à-vis an uncannily nonchalant demeanor toward the multitrillion-peso corruption of the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. administration, the president himself and his rapacious minions?

In the midst of mind-numbing inflation, a nose-diving Philippine peso, spiraling public debt to go with the unrestrained corruption of the Marcos Jr. administration that can rival the great conjugal plunderers of 50 years ago, the current crop of Yellow politicians are tunnel-vision, obsessive-compulsive in derailing Sara Duterte’s 2028 date with destiny in contrast to holding the dictator’s kleptocratic heir and his coterie of ravenous cronies accountable before the bar of justice.

The Yellows try to convince themselves that they can budol-style camouflage their partisan political agenda in Sara’s impeachment trial from the watchful Filipino people. Fellow historian and Manila Times columnist, an August Twenty One Movement stalwart, Dr. Xiao Chua, was forced by nagging questions from the public to address this very issue before mainstream media. It indicates an unsuccessful — pathetic to be sure — attempt to deodorize their stinking self-interested political agenda in the impeachment trial.

*   ![Image 3: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

Chua’s denial was itself anemic, lethargic and impotent against the searing force of our country’s political circumstances.

Based on presidential (and vice presidential) politics of the past decade, the Yellows have not been on the right side of history since 2016 at least. Then-congresswoman Leni Robredo might have (very narrowly) won against then-senator Marcos Jr. in the controversial vice presidential race in 2016, but a large number of Filipinos hold the belief that she won through electoral fraud, whether perpetrated by her or on her behalf. In the 2022 presidential elections, Marcos Jr. — conveniently riding the coattails of then-Davao City mayor Sara Duterte, his running mate — soundly trounced Robredo, who was running as a “pink” candidate; the distinction is actually meaningless, but it is there.

Now, with their partisan interests aligning, Robredo has become a fan of Marcos Jr.’s government.

The 2028 elections are 20 months away but none of the prospective Yellow candidates are doing well in the presidential election surveys of reputable pollsters.

The worst is the unabashed association of the Yellows in Bendalo/Bendalista politics, most prominently in forwarding a perverted interpretation of the two-thirds (of all senators) voting threshold for the impeachment of Vice President Duterte.

Yellow politics was born during the struggle against the Marcos dictatorship in the 1980s. The Marcos conjugal dictatorship was a plunderous regime that advanced an unconscionable perversion, repression and suppression of the sovereign democratic Filipino people through the employment of clever and brutal tactics — and anything in between — to perpetuate its decadence and gluttony.

In spite of a heritage built on a struggle for the ages against the Marcos-style Bendalista usurpation of democracy, self-proclaimed Yellow senators of today have perfidiously and villainously forwarded their own Bendalo/Bendalista bastardization of the 1987 Constitution purposely to deny Sara’s date with destiny in 2028.

That is sure to bring about the irreversible death of the Yellows.

title: Mark Villar joins Senate majority, leads Public Works panel
summary: SEN. Mark Villar joined the Senate majority bloc on Thursday and was elected to the Commission on Appointments (CA), replacing Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri. Villar was also elected chairman of the Senate Committee on Public Wor
content:
SEN. Mark Villar joined the Senate majority bloc on Thursday and was elected to the Commission on Appointments (CA), replacing Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri.

Villar was also elected chairman of the Senate Committee on Public Works, a post previously held by Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III, Zubiri said.

Zubiri confirmed that he gave up his seat in the CA to make way for Villar, describing the move as his gesture to welcome the senator back to the majority.

*   [Mark Villar joins Senate majority](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/mark-villar-joins-senate-majority/2441430)

On the Public Works committee, Zubiri said Sotto had suggested that Villar take over the chairmanship because of Sotto’s other responsibilities, including chairing the committees on National Defense and Ethics, and serving as Senate president pro tempore.

Sotto said Villar’s addition would help ease the workload of the majority, which is handling the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, budget deliberations and regular legislative duties.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“We’re glad because we’re all loaded with work. We have the impeachment, legislative [duties] and budget [deliberations], so it would be better if we have more members,” Sotto said.

Sotto said he learned of Villar’s transfer only on Thursday and that Zubiri coordinated the senator’s move to the majority.

Villar had previously chaired the Public Works committee before moving to the minority.

*   ![Image 1: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

Zubiri said there had been no negotiations over Villar’s return to the majority.

He said Villar himself reached out to the majority and expressed a desire to join the bloc so he could become more productive in the Senate.

Zubiri also said Villar’s previous vote in favor of the majority’s position was a “conscience vote” and was separate from his decision to return to the majority.

He maintained that joining the majority would not necessarily determine how Villar or other senators would vote in the impeachment proceedings.

*   ![Image 2: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

**More senators may follow**

Asked whether other senators from the minority could follow Villar, Zubiri said all minority members were welcome to join the majority.

Sen. Raffy Tulfo also welcomed Villar’s transfer and hinted that another senator or senators from the minority could follow.

“From the minority to the majority, it looks like there may be [someone who will transfer]. I don’t know. I’m not going to tell you because it might preempt the announcement, but I think there probably is,” Tulfo said.

*   ![Image 3: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

“Time will tell,” he added, Villar, a former Public Works secretary, is vice chairman of the Committee on Finance and serves on several committees dealing with infrastructure and government spending.

His return to the majority gives him a key role in the Senate’s oversight of public works and infrastructure spending, including proposed allocations for flood control and other projects.

The CA, composed of members from both chambers of Congress, exercises constitutional authority over the confirmation of presidential appointments.

With Villar’s transfer, the Senate majority has 14 members, while the minority has 10. His sister, Sen. Camille Villar, remains with the minority bloc.

Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano, meanwhile, replaced Sen. Loren Legarda as a member of the CA.

In a statement, Cayetano said political alliances may change but the minority bloc’s principles and commitment to the Filipino people would remain unchanged.

He said the minority would continue to serve as a constructive opposition while defending the rights of Filipinos in accordance with the Constitution and other laws.

Cayetano acknowledged that political considerations can lead lawmakers to realign.

“We understand all too well the circumstances and considerations that lead to changes in political alliances,” Cayetano said. “But regardless of how the political landscape shifts, our duty remains unchanged. We will continue to stand for what is right, uphold our institutions and work for the good of our nation.” Villar’s move to the majority comes as members of his family face separate legal proceedings.

In September, the Office of the Ombudsman filed graft and administrative complaints against Villar, Camille Villar, their parents Manny and Cynthia Villar, brother Paolo Villar and others over allegedly disadvantageous joint venture agreements involving PrimeWater and local water districts. The complaints are undergoing preliminary investigation.

The Villars are also facing a separate Securities and Exchange Commission complaint before the Department of Justice involving Villar Land Holdings Corp. over allegations of market manipulation, insider trading and misleading disclosures.

Mark and Camille Villar have filed counter-affidavits seeking dismissal of the case and have denied wrongdoing.

title: Bamboo-zled by innovation
summary: ADELO Caberte was just looking at his bamboo poles one afternoon when a bright idea lit up. For years, he grew and propagated bamboo in Bohol — that was the plan and always was the plan. But as he stood among the hollow poles in his backyar
content:
ADELO Caberte was just looking at his bamboo poles one afternoon when a bright idea lit up.

For years, he grew and propagated bamboo in Bohol — that was the plan and always was the plan. But as he stood among the hollow poles in his backyard, an instrumental song was playing in his head, and he found himself thinking of a flute.

“Ang unang purpose unta kay maghimo ko’g bamboo straw, unya kadugayan nako’ng tan-aw-tan-aw, pwede himuon man ni nga flute (My first purpose was to make bamboo straws, but after observing them for some time, I realized they could also be made into a bamboo flute),” he said.

*   [Semirara: Revised auction rules unfair](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/business/corporate-news/semirara-revised-auction-rules-unfair/2441199)

From that quiet afternoon, the 50-year-old farmer’s son began producing pan flutes — also called a syrinx — ranging from one to two octaves, with eight to 15 pipe notes each.

Caberte exhibited and sold his bamboo instruments publicly for the first time at the 2026 Bamboo Technology and Innovation Summit organized by the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) in Cebu City. He joined other exhibitors who showcased bamboo-based products — furniture prototypes, a bamboo drum shell called the Solidrum and clothing made from bamboo fibers.

“Nagpasalamat pud ko sa DOST nga usa ko sa gi-invite unya ma-exhibit pud akong product (I am also thankful to DOST for inviting me and allowing me to exhibit my product),” he said.

*   ![Image 1: Virata: Martial law pillar](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252091.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Virata: Martial law pillar](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/opinion/columns/virata-martial-law-pillar/2441990)

Beyond the pan flute, Caberte also displayed a bamboo whistle and a kazoo-type instrument that produces a sound similar to a saxophone. The summit gave him room to learn, network and showcase work he had developed largely on his own.

His bamboo instruments have since caught the attention of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) in Bohol, which recognized their value in showcasing local crafts beyond the province’s usual food products.

Caberte has been invited to DTI events to exhibit the instruments made from poles grown in his backyard — a reflection, he said, of Bohol’s identity as a cradle of music and talent.

Caberte’s journey into bamboo instruments grew out of a deeper advocacy — one that took root after a talk by fellow bamboo advocate Fr. Victor Labao of Kabilin Nature Farms and Bamboo Center broadened his understanding of the plant’s uses and environmental value.

*   ![Image 2: Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1251097.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court eases rules on foreign divorces](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/court-eases-rules-on-foreign-divorces/2441497)

He readily ticks off bamboo’s advantages: fast growth, easy propagation, low maintenance, strong carbon sequestration capacity and versatility across shelter, furniture, textiles and musical instruments.

“Una ang kawayan, paspas kaayo ... in one day motubo og 3 feet, unya in three to five years, maka-harvest na ta (First, bamboo grows very fast ... it can grow 3 feet in a day, and in three to five years we can already harvest it),” Caberte said, recalling Fr. Labao’s observation.

A single bamboo clump, he explained, can produce two to three new shoots per year. A person with 10 clumps can expect 20 to 30 more. Trees, by contrast, can take 10 to 20 years to mature before harvest.

“Ang kawayan, pwede natong himuong alternative sa unsa man pung gipangbuhat nga gamit nato kahoy. Kung moabot ang panahon nga daghan na ta og kawayan, dili na nato kinahanglan putlon ang atong mga kahoy kay kawayan na atong gamiton (Bamboo can be an alternative to many products we currently make from wood. If the time comes that we have enough bamboo, we may no longer need to cut trees because we can use bamboo instead),” he said.

*   ![Image 3: Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/07/1250224.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

He also noted that bamboo releases at least 35 percent more oxygen than an equivalent area of trees — a figure he cites often when encouraging others to plant.

“Only our imagination and creativity limit what we can do with bamboo,” Caberte said, quoting Fr. Labao — a line he has taken to heart.

Caberte is currently about 70 percent finished developing a whistle that mimics the sound of a tarsier — specifically, the call the primate uses to attract a mate, a sound most people do not know it makes. He is also working toward producing wind chimes and an angklung, and plans to request formal training from DOST to sharpen his instrument-making skills.

On the advocacy side, one of his key takeaways from the Cebu summit was the importance of matching bamboo species to local industry needs. Bohol has its own identified priority species suited to its existing industries, just as Cebu has.

“Ingon ta priority species ... lahi diay pud ang industriya diri sa Cebu, lahi pud sa Bohol kay naa may gi-identify nga species sa Bohol nga angay natong itanom (It’s about priority species ... industries differ. Bohol has identified species suitable for its existing industries, while Cebu has its own as well),” he said.

He encourages the public to plant bamboo on idle or unused properties — especially those that generate no income but still require tax payments. Soil type, he said, should not be a concern, as different bamboo varieties thrive in clay, sandy, dry and even waterlogged environments.

Caberte also hopes to see a bamboo processing facility established in Bohol to produce items such as coffee stirrers, barbecue sticks and toothpicks — replacing small plastic items that do not easily degrade. He further envisions a national bamboo inventory system to track which species are in sufficient supply and which are lacking.

With about 50 bamboo species growing in his garden, Caberte now serves as president of the United Bohol Bamboo Advocates Inc., a group of around 40 members contributing independently to the bamboo value chain in Bohol — from propagation and nursery management to harvesting and processing.

What started as an interest in bamboo straws has grown into instruments, advocacy and a community. For Caberte, the plant keeps offering more than he expected.

“Only our imagination and creativity limit what we can do with bamboo.”
