# 美国8月贸易逆差扩大到1056亿美元 对台湾逆差超过中国排第三

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月7日 08:18

美国商务部10月6日公布，8月美国的贸易逆差为1056亿美元，比7月的928亿美元增加13.7%，高于经济学家预期的1021亿美元，是一年多来最大的单月逆差。这直接影响美国的经济增长：贸易已经连续三个季度拉低美国国内生产总值（GDP），经济学家估计，第三季度可能拉低多达2.5个百分点。

按国家和地区分，8月美国商品贸易逆差最大的是墨西哥（277亿美元）、越南（240亿美元）、台湾（183亿美元）、中国（164亿美元）和欧盟（110亿美元）。台湾排在中国前面，是美国第三大逆差来源；美国对台湾的逆差一年前是122亿美元，今年8月比一年前多了61亿美元，增幅50%。对台湾的逆差扩大，和美国建设人工智能（AI）有关：进口增加集中在AI基础设施等资本品上，而芯片仍要从台湾进口。

8月美国商品贸易逆差最大的五个国家和地区（亿美元）

数据：美国商务部10月6日公布的数据

8月美国进口4208亿美元，比前一个月增加4.3%；出口3152亿美元，增加1.4%。进口增加最多的是工业用品和资本品：工业用品增加91亿美元，其中原油增加33亿美元、非货币黄金增加31亿美元；资本品增加62亿美元，主要是半导体和其他机床。第二季度美国国内需求的增长是三年半多来最快的，主要来自消费支出和企业的设备支出，设备大多与AI有关；企业要靠进口来满足需求。特朗普说，他的关税是为了缩小贸易逆差。从全年看，今年前八个月的逆差比2025年同期减少19.9%。

## 茉莉花观察

这一节是茉莉花的看法，依据是上文的事实。

我们的分析 美国对台湾的逆差一年里增加一半、超过对中国的逆差，主要是AI带来的。美国企业建设AI基础设施，要进口大量芯片和设备，而芯片仍要从台湾来；8月资本品进口增加的62亿美元里，半导体占了二十四亿美元。关税意在缩小逆差，但这类进口跟着国内需求走：需求旺盛时，企业就要靠进口来满足。

不同看法 从全年看，逆差在缩小，今年前八个月比去年同期少了19.9%；8月的扩大可能只是AI设备集中进口的一个月，不说明关税没有作用。我们同意全年的逆差在缩小；但对台湾的逆差反映的是AI投资，只要美国企业还在大量建设AI，从台湾进口的芯片就还会增加。

前瞻 美国商务部11月4日公布的9月贸易数据。我们判断，9月美国对台湾的商品贸易逆差仍会大于对中国的逆差。8月对台湾的逆差已经比一年前多了一半，进口增加集中在AI需要的资本品上；8月非国防资本品（不含飞机）的订单和出货也很强，企业的设备投资在第三季度还在继续。

title: Hu Haifeng Draws Attention Ahead of CCP Fifth Plenum as Xi Renews Security Push - Vision Times
summary: The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) will hold the Fifth Plenary Session of its 20th Central Committee from Oct. 26 to 29, according to a [Sept. 21 announcement from Xinhua](https://app.xinhuanet.com/news/article.html?articleId=202609215f91ba7
content:
The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) will hold the Fifth Plenary Session of its 20th Central Committee from Oct. 26 to 29, according to a [Sept. 21 announcement from Xinhua](https://app.xinhuanet.com/news/article.html?articleId=202609215f91ba7df196487ab25232ca078d3ed0&utm_source=chatgpt.com). With the party also moving toward its 21st National Congress in 2027, personnel changes and the future composition of the leadership are drawing growing attention.

Among the officials back in the spotlight is Hu Haifeng, the 53-year-old son of former CCP leader Hu Jintao. Hu appeared at a State Council Information Office briefing on Sept. 23, shortly before Hong Kong media raised fresh questions about whether he could advance further in the party hierarchy.

At the same time, CCP leader Xi Jinping has renewed his emphasis on domestic security, ordering officials to advance the “Peaceful China Initiative” and strengthen the party-state’s capacity to identify and contain risks.

## **Hu Haifeng returns to the spotlight**

Hu has served as vice minister of Civil Affairs since January 2024, when the [State Council announced his appointment](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202401/16/content_WS65a66409c6d0868f4e8e323b.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) after he had spent more than five years as party secretary of Lishui in Zhejiang Province.

On Sept. 23, Hu appeared alongside Civil Affairs Minister Li Changguan and other vice ministers at a government briefing on civil affairs policy under China’s 15th Five-Year Plan. [Xinhua’s account of the briefing](https://www1.xinhuanet.com/politics/20260923/f85fc42f02af4fe887ba39ba45134576/c.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) quoted Hu extensively on children’s welfare, social organizations and charitable organizations.

Hu said authorities plan to expand services for disadvantaged children, including programs covering psychological health, safety and guardianship. He also outlined tighter supervision of social organizations and charities.

The appearance revived interest in Hu’s political future. An [Oct. 1 article in the Hong Kong Economic Journal](https://www.hkej.com/dailynews/cntw/article/4528330/%E8%83%A1%E6%B5%B7%E5%B3%B0%E8%BD%89%E4%BB%9513%E5%B9%B4%2B%E6%9C%89%E6%9C%9B%E6%99%89%E8%BA%AB%E3%80%8C%E5%85%A9%E5%A7%94%E3%80%8D?utm_source=chatgpt.com) noted that speculation over Hu’s career has followed him since he entered politics more than a decade ago and said his prospects are again attracting attention as the CCP approaches another period of leadership reshuffling.

Hu entered government work in Zhejiang in 2013 after holding positions at Tsinghua University-affiliated organizations and security-equipment maker Nuctech. He later served as mayor of Jiaxing and party secretary of Lishui before moving to Beijing as vice minister.

Despite repeated outside speculation about possible promotions, Hu remained a vice minister at the Sept. 23 briefing. There has been no official announcement of a new position.

## **Promotion questions return ahead of 21st Party Congress**

The renewed attention surrounding Hu comes as the CCP begins looking toward its 21st National Congress, expected in 2027.

The Hong Kong Economic Journal said Hu’s potential advancement should be viewed against the wider personnel maneuvering that traditionally precedes a party congress. His family background guarantees unusual scrutiny: Hu Jintao led the CCP from 2002 to 2012, making his son’s career closely watched by China observers.

However, Hu’s recent public appearance by itself does not establish that a promotion is imminent. The Sept. 23 event was an official policy briefing involving the ministry’s senior leadership, and Hu spoke on policy areas falling within his portfolio.

That distinction was largely missing from the original speculation surrounding his appearance. While media coverage may provide clues about an official’s standing, the CCP rarely discloses senior personnel decisions before they are formally approved.

## **Xi puts renewed emphasis on domestic security**

Separately, Xi has issued a fresh directive calling for China’s security apparatus to strengthen what Beijing officially calls the “Peaceful China Initiative.”

According to the [Chinese government’s account of the Sept. 28 directive](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202609/28/content_WS6aba4404c6d00ca5f9a0d7fe.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Xi ordered officials to pursue a “holistic approach to national security,” strengthen the party’s leadership over security work and “prevent and mitigate all kinds of risks.” He called for efforts to make the country safer, society more orderly and governance more effective.

The initiative dates to the early years of Xi’s leadership and combines public security, social governance, legal controls and increasingly technology-based risk monitoring.

The timing has attracted attention because the directive comes as the CCP approaches another major leadership transition. The [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3369101/xi-jinping-demands-safer-china-communist-party-prepares-leadership-reshuffle?utm_source=chatgpt.com) described the order as a renewed focus on domestic stability ahead of the 21st Party Congress and noted that it followed Xi’s recent visit to the United States.

That context makes the coming Fifth Plenum particularly significant. Rather than proving the existence of a specific internal crisis, the simultaneous focus on personnel positioning and domestic security shows that Beijing is already preparing for a politically consequential period leading into the CCP’s next national congress.

title: African Vector of Global Politics: Interests of Key Actors and Opportunities for Ukraine
summary: ## Authors: **Marta Oliynyk-D’omochko, Yurii Oliinyk, Anatolii Maksymov** Experts of the Center for African Studies [Audio 3](https://www.kas.de/documents/270026/47150255/%D0%A6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%80+%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%B4%D
content:
## Authors:

**Marta Oliynyk-D’omochko, Yurii Oliinyk, Anatolii Maksymov**

Experts of the Center for African Studies

[Audio 3](https://www.kas.de/documents/270026/47150255/%D0%A6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D1%80+%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%B4%D0%B6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BD%D1%8F+%D0%90%D1%84%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B8_ENG.mp3/5bcdce7c-7b59-f990-b17c-a7aeedcae9ca?version=1.0&t=1791195066878)

Audio:African Vector of Global Politics: Interests of Key Actors and Opportunities for Ukraine

_The full analytics is available for download as a PDF on the right panel of the page._

## Summary

In 2026, Africa became the main arena of competition between global centers of influence. The countries of the continent are adapting to this struggle, balancing among the interests of external players for the sake of their own development. This brief analyzes the strategies of the United States (US), the European Union (EU), the United Kingdom, China, and Russia, and identifies opportunities for strengthening Ukraine’s presence in the region.

### Transformation of American Strategy in Africa

As of 2026, US policy in Africa has transformed into a “transactional model” based on pragmatic exchange: support for investment and security in return for access to critical resources and loyalty in the global confrontation. This shift is reinforced by a change in the institutional architecture, notably the restructuring of the United States Agency for International Development and the abandonment of “non-reciprocal preferences” in the trade regime of the African Growth and Opportunity Act. At the same time, the toolkit is oriented toward direct returns for the American economy.

In the extractive sector, the implementation of this strategy proceeds through a “dealmaking approach” aimed at deconstructing the monopoly of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Washington acts as a diplomatic mediator in conflicts in order to unlock access to strategic assets for American companies. A similar strategy of flexible pragmatism is also applied to South Africa, where Washington is purposefully consolidating control over extractive chains, minimizing the space for Beijing’s expansion.

With the same aim, Washington pragmatically weaves national interests into the global architecture of the Group of Seven (G7), notably the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII) initiative, while securing control over key nodes for American corporations. The flagship project in this context is the Lobito Corridor – the modernization of 1,300 km of railways and port infrastructure in Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Zambia for the export of minerals. In addition, the US is implementing its strategy of influence in Africa through a number of other programs in the areas of the “green” energy transition (South Africa, Kenya) and institutional facilitation (through support for the Africa Virtual Investment Platform).

Washington’s systematic activity is underpinned by the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, whose portfolio focuses on hub countries: Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa, and Kenya. Beyond these countries, by investing in energy (Sierra Leone, Gabon) and logistics, the corporation integrates American capital into key network assets, turning them into a platform for the dominance of American standards. Strategic investments in regional digital platforms allow the US to introduce its own technological standards and control key data transmission nodes, limiting the influence of competitors.

At the same time, three factors constrain the US strategy. The first is high political dependence on the situation in Washington: changes of administration or shifting priorities often lead to the freezing of projects, which reduces the trust of African partners. The aggressive rhetoric of certain political leaders is an additional destabilizing factor. The second is strict compliance requirements and regulatory restrictions, which narrow access to tenders for external players and slow project implementation compared with the PRC’s directive methods. The third is that the US role in Africa has been reduced to attempts to seize the initiative from competitors. This puts Washington in a weaker position: instead of setting the rules of the game, it is forced to “embed itself” in systems where China has already established its logistical and technological standards.

The changing political situation in the Sahel and the arrival of the Trump administration have driven a number of key changes in the US military sphere in Africa. The first concerns the scaling up of counterterrorism operations under the United States Africa Command, particularly in Somalia and Nigeria. The second change concerns the relocation of infrastructure and part of the activity to Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, and Nigeria after the loss of access to bases in the Sahel. In addition, the completion in January 2026 of the expansion of the Manda Bay base (Kenya) has substantially strengthened US capabilities for air monitoring and power projection in East Africa. The third change is that the US actively uses military diplomacy – from joint exercises with representatives of the opposing sides in Libya to non-public contacts of the Africa Command in the Sahel – in order to seize the initiative from competitors and restore influence over the region’s security architecture.

Given strict US protectionism, Ukraine’s direct integration into African projects through official tenders is rather unlikely due to regulatory restrictions on the origin of services. A realistic strategy for Ukraine lies in positioning itself as an engineering subcontractor for American prime contractors, particularly at the stage of calculating and designing complex mining and beneficiation processes. Another possible option is engaging Ukrainian specialists with experience in operating critical infrastructure under conditions of security instability. Their unique experience of working in a high-risk environment gives projects high operational resilience, making it possible to maintain critical infrastructure amid acute instability of logistics and communications.

### Infrastructure and Security Architecture of EU Policy in Africa

For the EU, the African vector is critical for ensuring security and social stability on its own southern flank. Brussels’ toolkit is aimed at eliminating the root causes of migration – the absence of legal economic opportunities and constant security threats – notably through Global Gateway investments and financial support under the European Peace Facility. These measures also serve the function of geopolitical deterrence and the strengthening of the EU’s own positions.

The Global Gateway initiative is positioned as a high-quality alternative to Chinese expansion. Thanks to its financial architecture and the Team Europe approach, Brussels is mobilizing up to €150 billion, using risk-guarantee mechanisms. The strategic focus is concentrated on four key modules: digitalization, climate and energy, transport, and healthcare and education, which strengthen the EU’s humanitarian influence.

The EU’s orientation toward energy, logistics, and critical resources is a strategic response to the monopolization of these areas by the PRC, which threatens Europe’s industrial future and the success of the “Green Deal”. For example, in the energy sphere, the Africa–EU Green Energy initiative is being implemented with the aim of reaching 50 gigawatts of renewable energy sources by 2030. Through the creation of transregional energy systems, the EU seeks to integrate Africa’s energy potential into its own grid, turning the continent into a stable supplier for European industry. This is a way to offset dependence on external energy sources and to entrench the region’s technological attachment to EU standards.

However, the EU seeks to implement an approach distinct from the simple export of raw materials. The EU offers countries (for example, Namibia, the DRC, Zambia, and Rwanda, with which relevant memoranda have been concluded) an alternative, focusing on building up local processing industries. This allows African countries to retain a share of added value within their economies, which corresponds to the goals of the continent’s countries.

In the infrastructure sphere, the EU’s cooperation with the African Union on 12 strategic corridors is a key instrument for entrenching European capital in the continent’s logistics. The development of such facilities as the Lobito Corridor and the Abidjan–Lagos corridor is a priority direction of this expansion.

Despite the EU’s technological advantage, the strategy’s implementation is being slowed by two critical factors. The first is procedural slowness. Bureaucratic donor coordination and the dragging out of the feasibility-study stage reduce the speed of implementation, making the EU less competitive compared with actors that act directively. The second lies in the realm of security challenges. High risks make investment projects too expensive and risky for private capital. Accordingly, the key task becomes creating conditions under which European corporations can implement capital-intensive projects without waiting for the full stabilization of the region, relying instead on the systemic support of state financial institutions.

However, financial guarantees are insufficient where security stability is absent, which makes EU–Africa military cooperation necessary. Since 2022, the EU’s key security instrument has been the European Peace Facility (EPF), through which Brussels implements a “stabilization donor” model, focusing mainly on the supply of non-lethal equipment and the professional training of local security forces. The differentiated geography of assistance covers countering jihadism in West Africa, ensuring freedom of navigation in East Africa, and localizing conflicts in the center and south of the continent. The prioritization of partners’ requests and the shift to bilateral agreements allow the EU to respond promptly to challenges, avoiding the bureaucratic delays of collective cooperation formats.

At the same time, EU security policy faces a funding deficit due to the prioritization of Global Gateway economic projects. On the other hand, in Africa, Brussels is increasingly becoming hostage to a conflict between political principles and economic interests. A vivid example is the financing of the Rwandan contingent in Mozambique to protect the assets of TotalEnergies. By choosing Kigali as the executor, the EU finds itself in a trap: on the one hand, Rwandan forces effectively secure energy facilities, while on the other, support for Rwanda, which is destabilizing the neighboring DRC, substantially complicates pan-European efforts to settle regional conflicts and undermines trust in the European peacekeeping strategy.

Ukraine’s integration into EU projects in Africa requires a shift to a subcontracting model within consortia with European engineering, procurement, and construction contractors, which would allow Ukrainian business to bypass regulatory barriers and insurance restrictions. The key niches for cooperation are engineering and technical audit, the implementation of government technology solutions, and equipment service support, where experience of working under high-risk conditions becomes a competitive advantage. To this end, the state needs to shift its focus from political lobbying to institutional support, establishing systematic communication with European business and financial institutions in order to integrate Ukrainian companies into tender consortia.

### United Kingdom’s New Approach to African Continent

title: Congress Moves to Break China Rare Earth Grip Before November Deadline
summary: Hector RETAMAL/AFP via Getty Images With 35 days remaining before China's expanded rare-earth export-control suspension expires, House Republicans have assembled a four-bill legislative package designed to accelerate domestic mining, create
content:
Hector RETAMAL/AFP via Getty Images

With 35 days remaining before China's expanded rare-earth export-control suspension expires, House Republicans have assembled a four-bill legislative package designed to accelerate domestic mining, create a federally backed mineral stockpile, and shield defense programs from a supply chain that Beijing has proven it can switch off. The November 10, 2026 deadline is not theoretical: yttrium oxide — used in radar systems, semiconductor coatings, and jet engine thermal barriers — has already [risen approximately 140-fold in price](https://theoregongroup.com/commodities/rare-earths/rare-earth-prices-surge-as-china-keeps-export-restrictions/) outside China since Beijing imposed licensing controls in April 2025, a price shock that has temporarily halted production at two North American firms.

The four bills represent the most comprehensive congressional response yet to a vulnerability that has been acknowledged for years but addressed only in pieces. According to a January 2026 presidential proclamation, the United States was [100 percent import-reliant for 12 minerals](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202600025/html/DCPD-202600025.htm) deemed critical to national security and relied on imports for more than half of 29 others. For rare earth elements specifically, that dependence runs nearly 100% through Chinese processing facilities — even ore extracted from domestic mines typically travels to China for separation before returning as usable metal.

Together, the bills target three chokepoints that analysts have identified in the domestic critical minerals pipeline: slow permitting, fragile supply chains, and the absence of a strategic buffer against foreign supply disruptions.

### What's in the Package

The bundle draws together legislation advancing through House committees at varying speeds since late 2025. Four bills form its core:

**The Critical Mineral Dominance Act (H.R. 4090)** — the furthest along of the group — [passed the House 224-195](https://www.skillings.net/?p=80424), with some Democratic support, and now awaits Senate action. Sponsored by Rep. Pete Stauber (R-MN), the bill directs the Department of the Interior to address mineral supply chain vulnerabilities, including by accelerating and expanding mineral production on federal land — covering National Forest System land, public lands, and any land that may be leased for exploration, development, or production of hardrock minerals. Interior must identify priority mining projects on federal lands that can be immediately approved and take all necessary and appropriate steps to [expedite those priority projects](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/SAP-H.R.-4090.pdf).

**The Protecting Domestic Mining Act (H.R. 1501)**, sponsored by Rep. Jefferson Shreve (R-IN), [classifies mining as covered projects](https://nam.org/?p=40138) under the FAST Act, ensuring that such operations are protected under the federal permitting framework. The FAST-41 process — established under the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act — sets enforceable, publicly trackable timelines for federal environmental reviews through the [Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council](https://www.permitting.gov/newsroom/press-releases/first-fast-41-covered-mining-project-completes-federal-permitting). Previously available only to transportation and energy infrastructure projects, FAST-41 was extended to critical minerals by a March 2025 executive order; this bill would lock that extension into statute.

Under FAST-41, all federal agencies with a stake in a project review coordinate on a shared public timetable posted to the Federal Permitting Dashboard, with legally trackable intermediate deadlines. The process does not bypass the National Environmental Policy Act or reduce environmental review requirements — it enforces coordination so that agencies cannot sequentially delay a project that is waiting on each other. South32's Hermosa mine in Arizona (zinc, manganese) was the first mining project to complete the FAST-41 permitting process, finishing federal permitting in 2026 after about three years — compared to an industry average of seven to ten years for traditional federal mine permitting.

**The Critical Minerals Supply Chain Resiliency Act (H.R. 5929)**, introduced by Rep. Andy Barr (R-KY), treats actions taken by the Defense Department to support domestic critical mineral production as covered projects under the FAST Act. The bill extends FAST-41 eligibility specifically to projects funded under the executive order invoking the [Defense Production Act March 2025](https://www.skillings.net/?p=80424), which authorized direct federal investment in critical mineral mining and processing. It was reported to the House with an amendment by the Committee on Natural Resources in June 2026.

**The SECURE Minerals Act (H.R. 7126 / S. 3659)** creates a government corporation — the Strategic Resilience Reserve Corporation of the United States — to secure US access to critical minerals through domestic and partner-country production, stable pricing, and reduced reliance on foreign supply chains. A companion Senate version, introduced in January 2026 by Sens. Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) and Todd Young (R-IN), would establish a [$2.5 billion Strategic Resilience Reserve](https://www.axios.com/2026/01/15/congress-rare-minerals-reserve-proposal) — a domestic stockpile of critical minerals designed to insulate the American economy from price manipulation and supply shocks, with governance modeled on the Federal Reserve.

The reserve's seven-member board would be authorized to sell minerals for commercial and defense use, with proceeds reinvested to sustain operations. Allied nations willing to [contribute 100 million minimum](https://www.clarkhill.com/news-events/news/bipartisan-legislation-seeks-2-5-billion-strategic-minerals-reserve-to-counter-china/) in capital could participate in the stockpile structure.

"China's global dominance of critical minerals supply chains gives it significant leverage and leaves the US vulnerable to economic coercion," Sen. Young said at the bill's introduction.

### The China Problem — and Its November Deadline

The urgency behind the legislative push is inseparable from China's demonstrated willingness to use mineral dominance as a foreign policy lever. China now accounts for approximately 69% of global rare-earth mine production and [up to 91 percent processing capacity](https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2026/executive-summary) of refining and separation worldwide. For magnet rare earths specifically — the materials that make the permanent magnets in EV motors, wind turbines, and precision guidance systems — China controls roughly 91% of refined output and [94 percent sintered permanent magnet production](https://www.skillings.net/?p=101270).

The United States imported more than two-thirds of the rare earth elements it used in 2025, despite growing alarm in Washington over reliance on China. F-35 fighter jets and Virginia-class submarines both require rare earth materials that pass through Chinese processing.

Beijing moved to activate that leverage in April 2025, requiring companies in China to obtain government approval to export even small amounts of minerals including yttrium, dysprosium, and terbium. Shipments of those elements [fell roughly 50 percent](https://theoregongroup.com/commodities/rare-earths/rare-earth-prices-surge-as-china-keeps-export-restrictions/) from baseline levels in the months that followed. Japan — the largest rare earth magnet producer outside China — received just 4 percent of its normal dysprosium supply after the controls took effect; Germany received none.

In October 2025, China moved to expand those controls dramatically, announcing requirements that would have extended licensing obligations to foreign-made products containing even trace quantities of Chinese-origin rare earths — a provision that could have effectively brought most of the world's electronics supply chain under Beijing's export-licensing authority. China [suspended those October measures](https://www.cirs-group.com/en/chemicals/china-temporarily-suspends-export-controls-on-key-raw-materials-including-rare-earths-lithium-batteries-and-diamond) until November 10, 2026, as part of a trade truce.

But that reprieve has a hard stop — and the [April 2025 controls on seven elements](https://www.skillings.net/?p=99800) were never suspended at all. With the November 10 deadline now approaching, [three possible policy scenarios](https://www.mining-technology.com/news/china-rare-earth-export-pause-nears-expiry-amid-persistent-supply-concentration/) loom: Beijing could extend the suspension, selectively reactivate controls targeting specific elements or end uses, or fully restore the October 2025 measures.

The May 2026 Trump-Xi summit produced only limited concessions — the White House said China pledged to "address US concerns" about shortages of key rare earths including yttrium, scandium, and neodymium, but China's [export licensing regime remained intact](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/051826-us-claims-china-agreed-to-address-rare-earth-supply-concerns) and the earlier language about "effectively eliminating" export controls was dropped from the communiqué. No formal extension of the suspension was announced at any subsequent meeting, and analysis from Fitch Group's BMI concluded that China's dominance of the global rare earth supply is expected to stay firmly in place.

The International Energy Agency has warned that full implementation of China's expanded export controls — if Beijing decides to proceed — could put an [estimated 6.5 trillion dollars](https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2026/executive-summary) per year of downstream production outside China at risk across the automotive, high-tech, defense, and energy sectors. The automotive sector outside China could lose more than 3 trillion, with more than 40% of those losses falling on the United States.

### The Processing Bottleneck Congress Cannot Fix in 35 Days

Here is the constraint that even successful legislation cannot solve before the November deadline: the United States does not have the processing and refining infrastructure to convert domestically mined ore into the defense-grade rare earth metals and magnets its military and technology industries need.

The mine-to-magnet pipeline has four stages: mining the ore, separating it into individual rare earth oxides, converting oxides into metals and alloys, and manufacturing permanent magnets. China dominates not the first stage — rare earth ore exists in the United States, Australia, Canada, Brazil, and elsewhere — but stages two through four. China controls roughly 85-90% of global rare earth refining capacity. The United States and Europe together account for an [estimated 6 to 7 percent](https://www.skillings.net/?p=99262) of global rare-earth oxide separation capacity combined.

The Hermosa mine — the first to complete the FAST-41 permitting process — took approximately three years under the coordinated review. A mine starting the process today would not begin production until well into the decade. The processing and refining facilities that would receive that ore are being built, but the Pentagon's $439 million commitment to domestic rare earth supply chains and the EXIM Bank's Nebraska processing facility investment represent starting points, not solutions. Fabian Villalobos, an engineer and critical minerals expert at the [RAND Corporation think tank](https://www.rand.org/), has noted that building a complete mining and processing industrial chain like China's could take decades.

Yttrium illustrates the gap. The United States [imported 93 percent of its yttrium](https://www.miningmx.com/trending/63184-rare-earth-yttrium-surges-to-record-amid-china-curbs/) d

title: 蔡康永现身民进党活动遭中国抵制引爆台湾人对中国跨境镇压的反弹
summary: 台北 — 台湾知名主持人蔡康永现身台湾民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋的造势活动后，连三日遭中国网民出征后，引发台湾人对中国民主素养、“巨婴思维”和跨境镇压的反弹，同时，台湾官方也誓言积极修法反制。 蔡康永遭网攻只是近期中共对台湾跨境镇压的最新一例。与此同时，美国联邦调查局说，台湾总统赖清德在美国工作的长子赖廷被涉嫌在美国境内充当中国政府未登记代理人的华裔女子监视。分析人士说，这些事件凸显中共在塑造外部敌人，来对内激发民族主义，以巩固政权正当性的焦虑。 **蔡康永陷网攻和中企抵制*
content:
台北 —

台湾知名主持人蔡康永现身台湾民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋的造势活动后，连三日遭中国网民出征后，引发台湾人对中国民主素养、“巨婴思维”和跨境镇压的反弹，同时，台湾官方也誓言积极修法反制。

蔡康永遭网攻只是近期中共对台湾跨境镇压的最新一例。与此同时，美国联邦调查局说，台湾总统赖清德在美国工作的长子赖廷被涉嫌在美国境内充当中国政府未登记代理人的华裔女子监视。分析人士说，这些事件凸显中共在塑造外部敌人，来对内激发民族主义，以巩固政权正当性的焦虑。

**蔡康永陷网攻和中企抵制**

蔡康永星期天(10月4ㄖ)低调出席沈伯洋的台北竞选总部成立大会，离去前表明他只是来“听听各方的意见”，并希望“有机会访问到每一个候选人”，但消息一传至中国，马上引发中国网民质疑他对“台独顽固分子”的支持倾向。

沈伯洋曾被大陆国台办列入“台独顽固分子清单”，并遭中国公安机关立案侦查，蔡康永的出现格外受关注。

虽然蔡康永的经纪人随后证实，他准备采访两大党的台北市长候选人，但是，这依然阻挡不住中国网民对他的攻击，有人甚至大骂他是“同性恋+台独艺人”，且接连三天都有不同的负面话题冲上微博热搜榜首，如#蔡康永帐号清空取消关注#、#蔡康永多个作品下架#标签,分别吸引到逾5300万和3700万的阅读量。

蔡康永1962年出生于台北，后来以主持《康熙来了》走红，并担任中国大陆的综艺节目《奇葩说》导师，2001年，他公开了自己是同性恋的身份。

中国官媒《环球时报》前总编胡锡进星期一(10月5日)则在微博发帖直斥蔡康永“主动踩(红)线，而且是踩雷。”

他写道: 中国“不能允许个别台湾艺人或商人做双面人，既享受大陆广大的市场，又与岛内‘台独’势力勾勾搭搭。要全面孤立“台独”，这在大陆早已成为有广泛群众基础的社会共识。”

中企品牌也加入抵制行列，如领跑汽车发声明，与蔡康永切割，时尚杂志《时尚芭莎》删除其九月刊封面故事宣传，接着他的播客对话视频《新生PLUS》惨遭下架。

中国官媒如《北京时间》星期二(10月6日)更是口不择言地辱骂蔡康永“龌龊”。

**台湾民众支持蔡康永：“无需向任何人报备或抱歉”**

不过，除少数蓝营政治人物附和中国舆论，蔡康永在台湾内部的支持并未受到太大影响。

一般民众对他仍多持肯定，如高雄市民陈艺民在脸书(FB)留言称，蔡康永是台湾公民，有权参加任何活动，“也无需向任何人报备或抱歉!”

台北选民彭小美也在脸书留言称：“不论康永哥票投给谁…他投蒋(万安)或沈(伯洋)都是他自己的判断选择。”

国民党籍的现任台北市长蒋万安星期一(10月5日)也公开称，他尊重蔡康永的自由选择，且“不认同透过利益或任何形式来干预或影响每一个人选择的自由”，他还邀请蔡康永出席他的竞选活动，并安排在摇滚区座位。

根据台湾媒体，沈伯洋星期天晚出席会活动时，被问及蔡康永遭大陆网民抵制一事。他说，这真的是很可惜的一件事，因为蔡康永已经表明，其实是想聆听各式各样不同的声音。

沈伯洋说：“我觉得在民主社会，就是这样。他来这边，他并不是在这边跟着我们喊，他是来过来看说，欸，这个人讲什么？然后他接下来可能也想去看另一个人讲什么。”

沈伯洋也提到，如果只是在民主社会做这样的事情，“我觉得对我们来讲，应该是稀松平常的。”

蔡康永本人未正面回应风波，仅于脸书两度发文，一则感谢蒋万安的邀请，并允诺“将欣然前往观摩学习…尽可能遵循该场主人希望的服装方向去打扮，共塑派对气氛”，另一则发文仅是耐人寻味地大晒自己题有“一切只是过程”的版画照片。

美国之音以电邮邀约采访蔡康永，但截稿前，尚未获回应。

**黄逸豪:中共有“巨婴思维”**

蔡康永遭到来自中国的网暴和抵制只是中国对台跨境镇压的最新一例。据台湾陆委会星期一发布的统计，中共对台进行跨境镇压的人数已至少达126人、140人次，且对象不限政府官员、政治人物或特定人士，例如喜剧演员黄逸豪和引进《国有器官》电影的雄狮影视文化公司负责人管建忠都曾是受害人。

去年底，黄逸豪因嘲讽中共领导人习近平的维尼段子受到好评，今年5月底再度安排专场，但演出前，演出场地却遭到35岁的郭伟皓泼白漆和粪便警告，检调侦察后，9月底以恐吓和毁损等罪名起诉两名嫌犯，包括在台教唆犯罪的刘升杰，唯两嫌背后指使跨境暴力恐吓的中国籍影武者至今仍身分不明。

对于遭受暴力攻击，黄逸豪在接受美国之音采访时说，他颇感意外，因为自认“知名度低到…不会被盯上”，但现亲身经历过，才深刻了解到两岸在民主、自由、法治上的差异，虽然他早于2018年前赴中发展时，就曾因涉敏感议题被封杀，而认知到中国不是适合他发展的民主社会，且决定放弃中国市场。

他说:“我觉得中国，应该说，共产党的思维就真的很巨婴。全世界就必须要以它为中心，它想要什么就要得到什么；没有得到什么，它就开始哭、开始闹。”

黄逸豪还反讽，如果赚谁的钱，就必须要喊谁爸爸，那中国要赚美国的钱，不就该喊美国总统特朗普爸爸?

他也对怂中国小粉红:“这么爱中国，就好好待在中国就好了，不要出来。共产党希望你不要出来看外面的世界，你就待在墙里面好好生活。”

**管建忠:从恐惧到顶住压力**

管建忠也是另一个中国跨境镇压的受害者，他自2024年将《国有器官》电影引进台湾后，就不断收到有枪、刀、子弹的恐吓照片或扬言放置炸弹的恐吓信，近期还有人变相假冒他的名义，电话恐吓他人，让他疲于奔命，赶赴警局报到澄清。

管建忠在接受美国之音采访时坦承，一度恐惧到当年10月底就想停止播映，尤其八成的戏院受到中国跨境镇压的寒蝉效应影响，都拒播这部中共活摘中国人器官的电影时，其中包含一位18岁解放军人的现身说法。

但他说，正是因为中国“不断加柴火”迫害，让他愤而决定不屈服，持续“在戏院争言论自由”，也才惊觉自己原来是顶得住压力的人。

管建忠说：“没有人是局外人。和平从来不是沉默，沉默只有换来你无限的恐惧。”

管建忠语带沉重地呼吁全台戏院加入他的行列，他问:“中共在杀人，我站起来说话，我就被社会正常的机制拒绝?你(戏院)是执行外国政府的命令，还是你要维护善良的民主制度呢？”

他也呼吁全台观众支持《国有器官》，勇敢走进戏院，展现台湾人抵制威吓的决心。

**台湾陆委会:将积极修法反制**

对于蔡康永事件，台湾陆委会主委邱垂正星期二(10月6日)表示，这凸显台湾自由民主社会跟中国专制极权社会的截然不同，他也呼吁中国勿干预台湾选举，并提醒台湾艺人赴中发展，可能有“立场不同，利益归零”的风险。

另外，针对台湾总统赖清德之子赖廷与其家人在美国洛杉矶遭中共打手非法监视一事，邱垂正也谴责中共的跨境镇压行径，他说，台湾政府将推出一套全民指引，让台湾人了解中国跨境增压的本质和手法，及面对中共打压时，可取得的协助。

邱垂正还说，台湾早已建立机制，来预防和反制中国的跨境镇压，但针对法治不足处，将积极修改《反渗透法》和其他法律来强化。

台湾陆委会星期二也发布新闻稿，肯定台湾检警积极侦办日本资深媒体人矢板明夫于7月遭香港黑帮成员施暴的案件，台中地检署已将廖姓犯嫌提起公诉，并通缉其余4名共犯。

陆委会声明称，此案被告接受境外资助，除伤害特定被害人，更以“暴力钳制言论，侵害台湾民主制度及社会秩序”。

**中共靠催化民族主义来巩固政权**

针对中共日益升高的跨境镇压，政治大学国家发展研究所副教授黄兆年分析，这背后的结构性原因是，“中国威权统治的正当性逻辑正受到严重挑战”。

他说，2010年代以前，中国经济成长仍亮丽，人民也普遍乐观，经济成长可支撑中共统治的正当性，但这十多年来，中国经济成长力道逐渐走缓，产业转型升级不易，尤其近几年青年失业率居高不下，都让中共转而对外展现强硬，包括对全世界的战狼外交，以及对台湾在军事、外交和经济上的强硬手段，都是为了激发内部的民族和爱国主义，来巩固其执政的正当性。

黄兆年告诉美国之音:“这些都是强硬的对外作为，塑造一个外部敌人，可以在内部凝聚民族主义与爱国心…巩固(政权)正当性。”

他说，中国的跨境镇压也是一种强硬手段，手法包括入境中国的司法镇压或跨国引渡的长臂管辖，及对蔡康永之类艺人的经济胁迫或引诱，甚至对矢板明夫、黄逸豪和管建忠等反对人士的直接暴力恐吓等。

针对中国境内的司法镇压和海外的长臂管辖，黄兆年说，台湾政府只能对国民道德劝说并揭露赴中风险，或呼吁国际社会重新评估与中国的司法协定。

至于对反对人士的直接暴力，他呼吁台湾政府除强化法治外，应设计吹哨者的诱因机制，让中共收买和指挥在地协力者的隐蔽网络能有所揭露，以助攻检调侦办和依法究责。

content:
台北 —

中国船只近年不断出现在临近限制水域，让同处第一岛链的台湾和菲律宾，深受中国灰色地带骚扰之苦，促使两国海巡探索可行的合作模式。

中国科考船“嘉海科7号”9月底、10月初在菲律宾北部巴丹群岛海域徘徊多日，遭菲国海岸警卫队最大舰艇“特蕾莎·马格巴努阿号”(BRP Teresa Magbanua)驱离，在2艘中国海警船伴航下北移吕宋海峡。

菲律宾海岸警卫队发言人杰伊·塔里埃拉(Jay Tarriela)10月2日发布声明披露上述驱逐事件。值得注意的是，声明提及3艘台湾海巡船舰也现踪该海域，监控中方船舰。

**菲台中公务船齐聚敏感海域**

“该区域其他海上执法船只的出现也表明，不仅是菲律宾在关注这艘船(嘉海科7号)的动向。”声明写道。

声明称“嘉海科7号”是一艘海底勘测船，在关键海底电缆走廊穿越的水域停留了4天，甚至还伪造了自动识别系统(AIS)位置以隐藏其行踪。

有分析认为，中国很可能会试图破坏台湾周边的海底通讯电缆，寻求在冲突期间干扰台湾、菲律宾、美国和其他国家的通讯。

塔里埃拉10月3日在一场论坛上表示：“当中国科考船到达我们专属经济区边界时，我们也监测到3艘台湾海巡船也在等待这艘中国科考船驶出我们的专属经济区。令人惊讶的是，就连台湾海巡也在认真调查这艘中国科考船可能进行的非法海洋科学研究。”

塔里埃拉强调，菲律宾和台湾并未就监视中国船只一事进行协调。

分析人士则认为，菲律宾海岸防卫队于声明中提及台湾海巡船舰的存在，仍具有一定程度上的政治意涵。

台湾国防安全研究院战略与资源研究所所长苏紫云向美国之音表示：“台湾的船也在监控中共的海科船还有海警船，(台菲)双方有共同的敌人，但是还没有正式的合作。所以这一次的行动，我个人认为是一种安全的默契，未来(合作)当然是乐观其成。”

苏紫云认为，台湾海巡和美国、日本分别签有工作备忘录，因而得以展开各项交流合作。至于台菲之间虽然仅有渔业协定，但是包含重叠专属经济区内的多项执法要点，可以在此基础上催生两国海巡工作备忘录。

**台菲通过海巡 深化两国关系**

台湾东海大学中国大陆暨区域发展研究中心副执行长洪浦钊接受美国之音采访时指出，巴丹群岛位处的吕宋海峡距离台湾非常近，这里同时涉及重要航道、海底电缆、潜舰活动。中国科考船在这个区域搜集海洋与海床资料，台湾与菲律宾都有理由关切。

他表示，海巡已经成为台菲发展实质安全合作的重要管道，包括台湾退役海巡舰艇移交菲律宾，目前已在菲律宾南部服役，明年也规划由大型海巡舰赴菲敦睦。对台湾而言，海巡外交可以成为没有邦交下拓展区域安全合作的另一条道路。

在菲律宾政府的“一中政策”框架下，菲律宾和台湾借由海上安全事务，小心翼翼地取得实质关系进展。

台湾海巡上月将一艘500吨级退役巡逻舰捐赠菲律宾“我们保护我们的海基金会”(We Protect Our Seas, WPS)，再经由基金会赠予菲律宾海岸防卫队。10月2日，该舰以“沙兰加尼舰”(BRP Sarangani)的新身分在菲律宾南部服役。

为了避免中国借机挑事，菲律宾海岸防卫队发言人塔里埃拉特别强调，“沙兰加尼舰”并非来自台湾，而是来自基金会。菲律宾海岸防卫队没有接受台湾海巡署的捐赠。

《美国海军协会新闻网》(USNI News)引述菲律宾政府消息人士，称台北在2022年至2024年间就向马尼拉提交了一份船舰清单。台北和马尼拉之间透过非政府组织NGO转移物资，凸显了双方在国防和安全领域低调且缓慢发展的合作路径。

**睽违逾半世纪 台湾海巡百人团明年访菲律宾**

台湾海巡另外规划明年派舰访问菲律宾，执行为期约8天的“远洋敦睦计划”。这也是具备海上执法与军事性质的台湾公务船舰，睽违逾半世纪再度以敦睦名义正式访问菲律宾。

台媒《自由时报》报道，访问团成员包括海巡官兵与中央警察大学水警学系学生共计100人，这趟敦睦之旅在地缘政治上具有极高的指标意义，双方将在海上人道救援、打击海上犯罪等“非传统安全议题”上进行实质交流。

新加坡拉惹勒南国际研究院海洋安全专家许瑞麟(Collin Koh)以电邮回复美国之音表示，2013年菲律宾海巡舰开枪扫射台湾渔船的“广大兴事件”，促成菲律宾和台湾当局加强沟通与协调，但是双方关系仍多聚焦在业务层面而非政治层面。

许瑞麟进一步表示，近期台湾海巡赠船予菲律宾以及明年的公务访问，表明台菲两国海巡合作正在加强，尤其是在今年6月中国海警和科考船扩大在台湾东部沿海的活动之后。

洪浦钊指出，中国对台湾及周边海域施加压力，也增加区域国家与台湾合作的现实需求。台湾要做的，就是让更多国家清楚认识，台湾的安全与他们的利益密切相关。

content:
## “又来了”：美国海军陆战队员涉谋杀女性被捕 重燃日本冲绳抗议浪潮

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，美军驻日设施中，70%面积位于冲绳。

*       *   Author, 森来实（Kurumi Mori）
    *   Role, BBC驻日本记者

*   Published 6 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

长期居住在冲绳，52岁的佐藤爱（Ai Sato；音译）对BBC说：“老实说，我的第一反应是：‘怎么又来了？’”

“从我小时候到现在，甚么都没有改变。我们究竟还要重演多少次同样的事情，制造更多受害者，令他们的家人承受痛苦，最终让冲绳人民陷入悲伤？”

居住在宜野湾市，62岁的大城明美（Akemi Oshiro；音译）也有相同感受。

她向BBC表示：“我知道我们不应该对这种可怕的事情习以为常，但它们一再发生，我已经不再感到惊讶。”

冲绳拥有日本规模最大的美军驻紮力量，设有多个美军基地，并驻有数以万计的美军人员。

二十岁的美国海军陆战队下士德文·雅各布·巴拉德（L/Cpl Devin Jacob Ballard）星期日（10月4日）被日本警察逮捕。警方表示，调查仍在进行中，由于涉嫌罪行与官方军务无关，因此巴拉德目前由日本当局拘留。

美军人员当时[是否正在执行官方职务](https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/area/usa/sfa/pdfs/fulltext.pdf)，将决定哪个国家拥有主要司法管辖权。当日本拥有管辖权、但疑犯由美方羁押时，美方可在日本正式起诉前继续保留羁押权。

图像来源，EPA

图像加注文字，一些冲绳那霸市民众星期日聚集，抗议这宗劫杀案。

巴拉德隶属第三海军陆战队远征军（III Marine Expeditionary Force），驻紮于宜野湾市的普天间海军陆战队航空基地。

冲绳县警察表示，39岁的屋宜杏奈（Anna Yagi）于3日凌晨被发现陈尸于那霸市一间酒店房间内。

据称，闭路电视画面显示，一名相信是疑犯的男子与该名女子一同进入酒店，其后独自离开，并带走她的财物。当地媒体引述警方报导称，屋宜似乎被绳索勒颈致死。

日本首相高市早苗已向华盛顿提出正式抗议。但像佐藤这样的居民认为，这远远不足够。

“我对政府数十年来一再发表同样的评论感到非常失望，例如表示会提出抗议，或称高度重视这宗事件。”

她说：“我希望高市首相直接致电特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）总统。她一直强调自己与特朗普关系密切，我希望她能与他讨论具体措施，防止同类事件再次发生。”

涉嫌谋杀案的消息传出后，日本各地民众表达愤怒情绪，约100人分别在那霸及东京举行抗议活动。另有不少人透过社交媒体表达愤怒并要求伸张正义，其中一名用户写道：“够了。”

图像来源，Kyodo via REUTERS

图像加注文字，美国海军陆战队下士德文·雅各布·巴拉德因涉嫌犯下谋杀案而被捕。

过去几年，多宗事故及罪案令当地反对美军继续驻紮冲绳的声音日益高涨。

2016年，一名20岁冲绳女子遭强奸及杀害后，[数以万计示威者走上街头](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/world/2016/06/160619_japan_us_okinawa)，抗议当地庞大的美军驻紮规模。涉案的一名前美国海军陆战队员其后被判终身监禁。

目前约有5.5万名美军人员驻紮日本，其中最集中驻紮于这个亚热带群岛。冲绳虽然是日本面积最小的县份之一，但日本境内专供美军使用土地的70%位于冲绳。

1972年，在美军于第二次世界大战结束后占领冲绳群岛多年后，冲绳县重新回归日本管治。冲绳县政府资料显示，自那时起，已录得6,409宗涉及美军人员的刑事拘捕。

当地居民表示，大规模美军驻紮引发多方面不满，问题包括强奸、袭击及酒后驾驶事故等罪案，以及噪音和军机坠毁等对社区造成的滋扰。

1995年，三名美军士兵在一名12岁女学生从文具店步行回家途中将她绑架、殴打及强奸。

2025年，一名美国海军陆战队员因勒颈及性侵一名日本女子而被定罪。

育有两名儿子、48岁的宫城瞳（Hitomi Miyagi；音译）向BBC表示：“战争结束80年后，我们居住的冲绳仍然是一个令人惶惶不安的地方。”

“我们不会停止发声，希望迎来一个能够和平生活的冲绳。”

title: “九合一”台北市长选战：蒋万安的2028前哨战，沈伯洋能否靠“洋流”突围？
summary: 图像来源，AFP and gettyimages 图像加注文字，原先不被看好的沈伯洋（左），从9月开始声势高涨，给本享有执政优势的现任市长蒋万安（右）带来了挑战。 * * Author, 蒋曜宇 * Role, BBC中文特约记者 * Published 6 小时前 * 阅读时间: 5 分钟 台湾的“九合一”地方选举将于11月28日举行。 这场选举将奠定执政的民进党及在野的国民党、民众党之间的势力消长，不仅被视为是总统赖清德的“期中考”，更是2028总统大选的前哨战。 外界密
content:
图像来源，AFP and gettyimages

图像加注文字，原先不被看好的沈伯洋（左），从9月开始声势高涨，给本享有执政优势的现任市长蒋万安（右）带来了挑战。

*       *   Author, 蒋曜宇
    *   Role, BBC中文特约记者

*   Published 6 小时前

*   阅读时间: 5 分钟

台湾的“九合一”地方选举将于11月28日举行。

这场选举将奠定执政的民进党及在野的国民党、民众党之间的势力消长，不仅被视为是总统赖清德的“期中考”，更是2028总统大选的前哨战。

外界密切关注俗称“六都”的六个直辖市的选情。在首都台北，寻求连任的国民党籍现任市长蒋万安，被视作2028年总统大选的热门人选之一，这次选战打得是否漂亮，是他进一步问鼎中央的关键。

政治大学选举研究中心研究员蔡佳泓对BBC中文分析：“2028年民进党会由赖清德竞选连任，这是蛮确定的事情。那重点就在国民党。他们状况还不是很明朗，可能人选有蒋万安、卢秀燕、可能再加上郑丽文，有很多的说法。这也让大家更关注台北的选情。”

然而，原先不被看好的民进党籍候选人、现任立委沈伯洋，自宣布参选后大力改变形象，并从9月开始声势高涨，其竞选团队以“洋流”为号招炒热选情，给本享有执政优势的蒋万安带来了挑战。过去对选战采取冷处理策略的蒋万安团队，也开始积极进行攻防，使台北选战白热化。

## 蒋万安是谁？

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，蒋万安被视为“蒋家第四代”，但他的身世也备受争议。图为2024年蒋万安访问美国，在姊妹市波士顿发表演讲。背景中的华埠牌楼由台湾政府于1982年赠予波士顿。

今年47岁的蒋万安，被视为2028年、甚至2032年总统大选的热门人选之一。

蒋万安在台北成长，毕业于国立政治大学法律系，随后赴美取得美国宾州大学法学博士，在美国作为执业律师直到2013年返台。回台湾后，蒋万安致力于帮助台湾新创产业在矽谷做募资、并购及上市的咨询。

2015年，他放弃美国绿卡，以政治素人身份投入2016年立委选举并成功当选，正式踏入政坛。当时国民党因太阳花学运而受挫，蒋万安为该党带来新气象，隔年即高票当选国民党中常委，成为党内的政治明星。

2022年地方选举，他击败对手陈时中、黄珊珊等人，当选台北市市长，以43岁之龄成为历任最年轻市长。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2023年8月30日，台北市长蒋万安参观上海城市规划展示馆。

两岸立场方面，2019年蒋万安担任立委期间表示，认同总统蔡英文提出的“四个必须”，尤其是要对岸正视中华民国存在的事实；但他不能接受蔡英文“台湾从未接受九二共识”的说法。同年香港爆发反送中运动，他在脸书发文声援香港示威者，并称一国两制在台湾没有存在的空间。

在市长任内，他推动两岸稳定交流，曾两度赴上海参加上海台北双城论坛，也在台北接待上海市府访团。他批评民进党政府“逢中必反”的立场，呼吁尽快恢复两岸观光和人员往来。

近年来，蒋万安在多个场合强调，两岸关系越紧张，越需要沟通与交流。但他也回避提及“九二共识”与“两岸一家亲”等政治意涵较高的口号。

在市政层面，蒋万安就任三周年时表示，他最自豪的政绩包含台北大巨蛋的启用、捷运工程开发，以及修法协调让美国晶片大厂辉达（Nvidia）台湾总部成功落脚台北。后者将投入新台币400亿资金，预估带动超过一万个工作机会。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2026年5月27日，辉达（Nvidia）执行长黄仁勋与台北市长蒋万安握手

《天下杂志》2026年县市调查，台北市夺下“幸福城市”冠军，但蒋万安的首长满意度在六都中仅排名第四。其任内发生的食安事件、[虐童案件](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/c93l71xkdz2o/trad)及[鼠患](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/c5yerdxdvz6o/trad)，也引来民进党与反对者的批评。

值得留意的是，蒋万安2019年担任立委期间，在同婚法案中投下赞同票，是少数公开支持婚姻平权的国民党立委，他担任市长后也曾公开参加台北彩虹游行。这次选举前夕，[台北市警察10月3日突击搜索一间同志酒吧](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cmz98p0x525xo/trad)，引发性平团体批评及上百民众抗议，蒋万安作为市长的回应备受关注。

台北市一般被认为是蓝营大本营，在这次选举前期他也大幅领先对手。据TVBS民调中心5月报告，蒋万安获得58%的支持度，而沈伯洋只有30%；但信民协会最新9月民调却显示两人差距已缩小到1.2%，使台北选情升温。

对支持者而言，蒋万安是一个非传统的国民党政治人物。他清新、温和的首都市长人设，让他在蓝大于绿的台北市更容易巩固基本盘并吸引中间选民。其反对者则批评蒋万安为“背稿机”，在公开演说方面缺乏群众魅力。

个人生活方面，蒋万安的身世一直备受讨论。2005年，蒋万安的父亲、前总统府秘书长蒋孝严，透过多方文献佐证自己为蒋经国的私生子，并将姓氏从“章”改为“蒋”，蒋万安也因此随父改姓。

蒋万安曾在自传中提到，虽然从小就听过耳语，但他是到高中才从父亲那得知自己与蒋家的关联，称他们之间有“切不断的血缘关系”。蒋家第四代蒋友青则公开质疑蒋万安从未与他们进行DNA鉴定。

蒋万安与妻子育有三子。近期，其15岁的长子录取台北市教育局的公费赴美交换计画，引发舆论质疑市长是否利用特权且未主动利益回避。蒋万安对外说明，自己并无介入孩子的甄选过程，但也表示不会领取教育局的新台币7.5万元补助金。

## 沈伯洋是谁？

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，沈伯洋自宣布参选后大力改变形象，除了更换发型，其竞选主视觉也打破传统绿营色调，改以橘色为主底，分析认为是要淡化政党色彩、吸引中间选民。

今年44岁的沈伯洋，为目前台湾政坛上群众反应最极化的政治人物之一。

绿营支持者称赞他论述清晰且具国际观，认为他提升了台湾社会的防卫意识，是“抗中保台”的指标性人物；泛蓝选民则指他频繁将国内政治攻防归咎于“中共统战”，并认为他所推动的民防运动是在贩卖焦虑，视之为激进派。

沈伯洋在台北出生长大，毕业于台大法律学系，考上法律学研究所后曾以“扑马”为艺名任职补习班多年，专门教授刑法。他2007年赴美留学，取得宾州大学法学硕士及加州大学尔湾分校犯罪学与法律社会学博士学位，2017年放弃美国教职返台，任教于国立台北大学犯罪学研究所，研究中国对台统战及威胁。

他在2021年创办提倡全民防卫的“黑熊学院”，并曾在分析中国资讯战的台湾民主实验室担任理事长，是国际研讨会上的常客。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2023年11月18日，台湾民众在新北市一个公园参加“黑熊学院”举办的家庭活动，该组织致力于推广民防教育。

2024年，沈伯洋在立委选举中以不分区排名第二，成为民进党籍立委，正式步入政坛。在他当上立委的同一年，北京称他为“台独顽固分子”并加以制裁。

沈伯洋对中国大陆的强硬态度，使他卷入多起争议。

他曾表示，陆配参政前需明确放弃中国国籍，否则可能衍生国安危机，是要防范的“紧急事态”。国民党和反对者称其打压陆配参政权，使陆配被歧视。

中国国台办曾制裁沈伯洋父亲沈土城的贸易公司，称他与中国企业有商业往来。沈伯洋则对外表示，该指控为中国“认知作战”的一环，指父亲公司主要在中南美洲做贸易，中国只是多个进口来源之一。

2025年“大罢免”，民进党中央以“罢免投同意，反共更有力”作为号召，沈伯洋被视为这场运动的核心领军人物之一，反对罢免阵营批评他煽动社会对立。最终32起罢免案全数不通过，沈伯洋表示会负起责任，但称罢免团体为自主集结，不该因行使公民权利而被苛责。

大罢免后的同年10月底，中国重庆市公安局以涉嫌“分裂国家”为由对沈伯洋发布通缉令。中国官媒央视其后播出一段7分钟纪录片，指控沈伯洋传播“仇中”思想，其创办的“黑熊学院”三年内训练逾300万名“黑熊勇士”协助防卫台湾。沈伯洋回应指，中国无权在台湾行使司法管辖，自己绝不退缩。

图像来源，AFP

图像加注文字，10月4日，沈伯洋举行竞选总部成立大会，前总统蔡英文及现任总统赖清德站台。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，沈伯洋支持者出席其竞选总部成立大会

沈伯洋过去因推动“抗中保台”等被反对者认为“高仇恨值”，他自宣布参选台北市长后大力改变形象，首先剪去原本标志性的爆炸头，并将论述重点从国防与两岸转换到市政治理等社会议题，积极跑基层来弥补地方经营上的不足。其论述能力为他带来声量，外界关注他是否“破圈”取得非同温层支持者。

不过，遭对岸通缉的沈伯洋始终离不开两岸议题。近期被追问对双城论坛的看法时，他表示若当选，将重新评估双城论坛的效益，主张台北应与更多国际都市交流，不应限缩在两岸之间。他强调，只要无政治前提，他不排斥赴对岸交流，问题在对方要不要让他进去。

外界原本预期沈伯洋胜选机率低，但随着选情白热化，他与对手间的差距逐渐缩小。

台湾中央研究院政治学研究所研究员鲍彤（Nathan F. Batto）撰文指出，沈伯洋并没有照剧本演出他被分派的那个“毫无胜算、注定落败”的角色。相反，他掌握了整个选战的节奏，使蒋万安团队捉襟见肘。

“事情本来不应该这样发展的。但台北选战却出人意料地变得非常有趣。”鲍彤写道。

title: Hong Kong, Tibetan, and Chinese Groups Rally Against Transnational Repression - Vision Times
summary: TORONTO, Canada — On Oct. 1, protesters from Hong Kong, Tibetan, Uyghur, Chinese democracy and Falun Gong communities [gathered outside the Chinese Consulate](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/2026/10/05/1105675.html) in Toronto, using Ch
content:
TORONTO, Canada — On Oct. 1, protesters from Hong Kong, Tibetan, Uyghur, Chinese democracy and Falun Gong communities [gathered outside the Chinese Consulate](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/2026/10/05/1105675.html) in Toronto, using China’s National Day to take a stance against transnational repression and [call for accountability](https://www.rebelnews.com/_canada_don_t_trust_communist_china_anti_ccp_protesters_unite_outside_toronto_consulate) over human rights abuses and increasingly brazen attacks by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) on Canadian soil.

The demonstration opened with “O Canada,” followed by songs associated with participating communities, including the Hong Kong protest anthem “Glory to Hong Kong.” During the rally, protesters held photographs of political prisoners and chanted slogans including, “Free Hong Kong,” “Free Tibet,” while calling for freedom, transparency, and peace.

Hong Kong Muay Thai champion Kui Teng (second from left), his wife, and Hong Kong supporter Mr. Guo hold signs at the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally in Toronto, Canada on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image: Courtesy of Kui Teng)

**RELATED: [Toronto Attack on Falun Gong Practitioner Draws Calls for Federal Scrutiny](https://www.visiontimes.com/2026/09/28/toronto-attack-on-falun-gong-practitioner-draws-calls-for-federal-scrutiny.html)**

Organizers described Oct. 1, the anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) in 1949, as a “day of mourning” rather than celebration. Winnie Ng, co-chair of the Toronto Association for Democracy in China, said the date “is not a day of celebration. It’s actually a day of mourning. For us, it’s a day to resist, to organize, and as loud as we can say no to political repression.”

Winnie Ng, co-chair of the Toronto Association for Democracy in China, speaks at the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally outside the Chinese Consulate in Toronto on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image: Courtesy of the Toronto Association for Democracy in China)

She questioned why authorities in Hong Kong increasingly treat longstanding forms of political expression as threats. “Why has calling for an end to one-party dictatorship become a crime? Why has mourning the victims of the June 4 Tiananmen massacre also become a crime?” she said.

## Different communities, shared concerns

### SIGN UP FOR OUR FREE NEWSLETTER

##### For the best of our weekly content！

There is something wrong, please try again later

### Success

You are now signed up for our newsletter

### Success

Check your email to complete sign up

During the event, representatives from several communities addressed what they described as decades of political, religious, and cultural repression. Tenzin Kunsang, president of Students for a Free Tibet Toronto, spoke about Beijing’s policies in Tibet and the removal of Tibetan children into state-run boarding schools, arguing that Tibetan language, religion, and identity are increasingly endangered.

A group participating in the seventh annual Peace Rally Marathon for Tibet also arrived at the consulate after running from Ottawa. “We run for Tibet,” said 19-year-old Jigme Tsering, adding that preserving Tibetan identity and history is a responsibility shared by Tibetans in exile.

On Oct. 1, 2026, protesters from Hong Kong, Tibetan, Uyghur, Chinese democracy and Falun Gong communities gathered outside the Chinese Consulate in Toronto to take a stance on China’s National Day with calls for human rights’ accountability. (Image: Vision Times Staff)

Li Yanan, representing the Democratic Party of China’s Canada committee, told the crowd that participants came from different backgrounds but shared a common aspiration: a future without fear. “For freedom! For human rights! For hope! For a better future!” she said, leading the crowd in chants.

Li Yanan, a member of the Democratic Party of China’s Canada Committee, speaks at the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally in Toronto on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image: Courtesy of the Toronto Association for Democracy in China)

Representatives of the East Turkistan community similarly urged Canada and other democratic governments to continue scrutinizing Beijing’s human rights record and protect communities facing intimidation abroad.

On Oct. 1, 2026, protesters from Hong Kong, Tibetan, Uyghur, Chinese democracy and Falun Gong communities gathered outside the Chinese Consulate in Toronto to take a stance on China’s National Day with calls for human rights’ accountability. (Image: Vision Times Staff)

## September attack looms over rally

The Oct. 1 gathering took place at the same location where [two Falun Gong practitioners were confronted](https://www.visiontimes.com/2026/09/28/toronto-attack-on-falun-gong-practitioner-draws-calls-for-federal-scrutiny.html) by an angry protester on Sept. 22. Video from that incident showed the unidentified man wearing a jacket bearing the Chinese flag tearing down Falun Gong displays, insisting that the sidewalk was “Chinese territory” and making death threats toward practitioners.

The victim, 62-year-old Falun Gong practitioner Li Na, suffered a bleeding injury to her chin during the attack on Sept. 22, 2026. (Image: Video Screenshot Provided by Falun Gong practitioners)

One practitioner at the scene, Li Na, said she suffered an injury to her chin during the confrontation and was seen with a bleeding cut on her face following the clash. Toronto police have been investigating the incident. The episode was raised by several speakers at Thursday’s rally as an example of why foreign intimidation has become an increasingly urgent concern.

Chinese Canadian attendee Liu Chong said watching the video initially made her afraid to participate publicly because of possible repercussions. But she said remaining silent would only embolden those responsible. “We still have to bravely stand up,” Liu told Vision Times.

Toronto resident Liu Chong attends the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally with her teenage son, Ma Haorui on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image: Courtesy of Liu Chong)

[Falun Gong, also known as Falun Dafa](https://en.falundafa.org/), is a spiritual practice rooted in the principles of Truthfulness, Compassion, and Forbearance. Despite being peaceful in nature, the CCP launched a brutal campaign to eradicate the practice in July 1999 after seeing its rapid rise in popularity as a threat to its authoritarian regime. Since then, thousands of practitioners have perished at the hands of Chinese police, with many today still undergoing routine monitoring, arbitrary travel bans, and arrests.

Dozens of members of the Democratic Party of China’s Canada Committee attend the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally carrying handmade banners reading ‘End the CCP’ and ‘The CCP Is Not China.’ (Image: Courtesy of the Democratic Party of China’s Canada Committee)

Sunny Sonam, president of Students for a Free Tibet Toronto, led demonstrators in chants during the rally. Referring to the Sept. 22 confrontation outside the consulate, he said the attacker appeared intent on showing that he was “not afraid of the Canadian government,” and argued that such conduct, particularly against elderly protesters, was unacceptable in Canada and should be addressed seriously under Canadian law.

Sunny Sonam, president of Students for a Free Tibet Toronto, leads chants during the rally outside the Chinese Consulate in Toronto on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image: Courtesy of the Toronto Association for Democracy in China)

Canada’s own intelligence service has warned that the concern extends well beyond individual demonstrations. In a recent assessment, the Canadian Security Intelligence Service described the People’s Republic of China as the most active state conducting foreign interference in Canada “in scale and scope” and said Beijing will “almost certainly continue to engage in acts of transnational repression.”

Members of the Federation for a Democratic China’s Canada chapter attend the ‘National Day of Mourning rally’ on Oct. 1, 2026. From right: David Shao, Hou Shijun; second from left: Shi Jun. (Image: Vision Times Staff)

## Billboard truck returns

_Rebel News_ also returned to the consulate with a digital billboard truck displaying footage of the Sept. 22 confrontation. The outlet [first brought the truck](https://www.visiontimes.com/2026/09/29/threats-against-falun-gong-practitioners-spark-billboard-protest-outside-consulate.html) to the site on Sept. 28 as part of a campaign seeking information about the attacker to demand accountability. On Oct. 1, it again displayed footage alongside messages emphasizing that Chinese Canadians should have the same rights as other Canadians.

A Rebel News digital billboard truck returns to the Chinese Consulate in Toronto on Oct. 1, 2026, while covering the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally. (Image: Vision Times Staff)

“This is not Chinese territory on the sidewalk here. This is Canada, and you are allowed to practice whatever faith, belief system, or religion you want to in this country, and it has to stay that way,” _Rebel News_ reporter Scarlett Grace said.

The broader concern was echoed by Hong Kong participants at the rally. One participant, Dino Chan, said authorities still need to establish whether the Sept. 22 attacker had any connection to the Chinese government. “Whether there was authorization or instruction from the Chinese government is currently unknown. The Canadian government needs to investigate,” he said.

Hong Konger Mai Zixuan and his family attend the ‘National Day of Mourning’ rally in Toronto, Canada on Oct. 1, 2026. (Image: Courtesy of Kui Teng)

Another Hong Kong participant warned that rights lost gradually can be difficult to recover, saying he did not want “Toronto five or 10 years from now to become the Hong Kong of today.”

For protesters gathered outside the consulate, that concern linked otherwise distinct causes: Whether involving Hong Kong, Tibet, Uyghurs, Chinese dissidents or religious believers, they argued that political restrictions imposed elsewhere must not be permitted to determine what people can say or believe in Canada.

Outbound booking links in it are turned into paid links automatically by our affiliate network, Travelpayouts: if you book through one, we earn a commission from the booking company, at no extra cost to you. It never affects what we recommend. [Affiliate disclosure](https://www.beijingtourism.org/affiliate-disclosure/)

Ask ten people who have been to China recently whether their VPN worked and you will get ten different answers, all of them true for the week they were there. One sailed through a fortnight of video calls; another spent every evening in a hotel room watching a spinning wheel. That is the defining thing about a **VPN for China**: it is not a product that simply works or does not, but a moving target, and for most short-stay visitors in 2026 it is no longer the best tool for the job.

This page explains what a VPN does and does not solve in China, the legal position in plain terms, why VPNs fail, how to choose and set one up if you decide you need it, how to use it without upsetting your payment apps, and when a roaming eSIM makes the whole question go away. Rules and technical conditions were checked in September 2026 and change often. Everything here is a description of the situation rather than legal advice, and the decision is yours.

## The short version

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Do I need a VPN? | Not if you use a roaming eSIM on your phone. Possibly if you work on hotel WiFi or use a local SIM |
| Is it legal? | Only government-approved VPN services are authorised. Enforcement is aimed at providers and sellers |
| Can I download one after I arrive? | Realistically, no. Install and test it at home |
| What gets through the firewall? | Only obfuscated or “stealth” protocols, and not consistently |
| Plain WireGuard or OpenVPN? | Recognised and blocked |
| Free VPNs? | No |
| Should it be on when paying with Alipay or WeChat? | No. Turn it off, or exclude those apps |
| When is it least reliable? | Around politically sensitive dates, and in waves of blocking that nobody announces |

## First question: do you need one at all?

A VPN exists to get your traffic past the Great Firewall, the system of filtering that blocks a large part of the foreign internet inside China. For a visitor the blocked list that matters is short and painful: Google in all its forms, including Gmail, Maps, Drive and Translate, plus WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, Signal, Telegram and many Western news sites. Apple services generally work, and so do most Microsoft ones.

### What is blocked, and what to use instead

| Service | On a Chinese connection | What works instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google Search, Gmail, Drive, Photos | Blocked | Bing works; move essential emails and documents offline before you go |
| Google Maps | Blocked, and inaccurate in China anyway | A Chinese map app, or Apple Maps, which uses Chinese map data |
| WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram | Blocked | WeChat for local contacts; iMessage and FaceTime generally work |
| Instagram, Facebook, X | Blocked | None; post when you are on an eSIM or back home |
| YouTube, Netflix, Spotify | Blocked or not offered in China | Download before you travel |
| Wikipedia, Dropbox, most Western news sites | Blocked | Save what you need offline |
| ChatGPT and several other Western AI tools | Not available in mainland China | See the note below |
| Apple iCloud, most Microsoft services, Outlook | Generally work | No workaround needed |

A note on that AI row, because it catches people out. Several Western AI services do not serve mainland China or Hong Kong, and since most roaming eSIMs exit to the internet through Hong Kong, an eSIM may not reach them either. Your home network’s own roaming, which exits in your own country, generally does. It is a small thing until you need it for work.

But a VPN is no longer the only way past, or the easiest. A roaming eSIM carries your mobile data out of the mainland to a gateway in Hong Kong or Singapore before it reaches the internet, so the filtering never touches it, and Google and WhatsApp load normally with no extra software. [Our China eSIM guide](https://www.beijingtourism.org/china-esim-guide/) explains how it works and what it costs. Your home network’s own roaming does the same, at a higher price.

So the real question is which connections you will be using. The firewall only applies to Chinese connections: hotel WiFi, café WiFi, public networks and a local Chinese SIM.

| Your situation | Do you need a VPN? |
| --- | --- |
| Short trip, phone only, roaming eSIM | No |
| Short trip, using your home network’s roaming | No |
| Working on a laptop from the hotel | Either a VPN, or tether the laptop to your eSIM on a metered plan that allows it |
| Local Chinese SIM as your only data | Yes, or add an eSIM for blocked apps |
| A month or more, studying or working | Usually, or run a local SIM and an eSIM side by side |

For most people reading this, the first row applies, and the rest of this page is background. If you are in one of the other rows, read on.

Free official WiFi at a Chinese railway station. Networks like this are Chinese internet: fine for Chinese apps, blocked for Google and WhatsApp (Photo: MNXANL / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0)

## The legal position, plainly

China’s rules on VPNs are clearer on paper than in practice. Since a 2017 notice from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, cross-border VPN services have required government approval, which means that only licensed services, used mainly by businesses for their own networks, are lawful. The consumer VPN apps that travellers use are not licensed. Amendments to the Cybersecurity Law that took effect on 1 January 2026 raised penalties further, with the emphasis on those who build, sell and provide circumvention tools.

Enforcement follows the same emphasis. Action has overwhelmingly targeted providers and sellers. The cases against individual users that have become public have mostly involved Chinese residents, often alongside other alleged offences. There is no public pattern of tourists being fined or detained for using a VPN to read their email or message their family, and millions of foreign visitors, business travellers and residents use them.

That is a description, not a promise. The sensible attitude is to treat a VPN as a private convenience: do not discuss it at a hotel registration desk or with officials, do not use it for anything you would not want read, and do not assume that “nobody gets fined” means “nothing can happen”. If that uncertainty bothers you, the roaming eSIM is the lower-friction choice, because roaming is an ordinary licensed service.

## Why VPNs fail in China

The firewall does not just block websites. It inspects traffic, and it has become very good at recognising what a VPN connection looks like.

*   **Standard protocols are fingerprinted.** OpenVPN, plain WireGuard and IPsec each have recognisable signatures. They are identified and blocked or throttled, often within minutes of connecting.
*   **Obfuscation helps, inconsistently.** So-called stealth or obfuscated protocols wrap VPN traffic to look like ordinary encrypted web browsing. These are what still get through, some of the time, and providers that take China seriously build and maintain them.
*   **Blocking comes in waves.** It tightens around politically sensitive dates, including the National People’s Congress sessions in March, the 4 June anniversary and National Day on 1 October, and during major political meetings. In spring 2026, users widely reported a sharp crackdown that took many proxy-based services offline overnight.
*   **Speed suffers even when it works.** A VPN over hotel WiFi routes your traffic out of the country and back, through a system that deliberately slows suspicious connections. Video calls are the first thing to suffer.

The honest summary: anyone who promises a VPN that works all the time in China is selling something. The realistic expectation is a service that works most of the time, needs occasional fiddling, and has bad days.

### The dates when disruption is most likely

| When | What | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Early to mid March | The “Two Sessions”, China’s annual parliamentary meetings in Beijing | Tighter blocking and heavier security around Tiananmen |
| Around 4 June | The anniversary of 1989 | VPNs and some foreign services noticeably less reliable |
| 1–7 October | National Day and Golden Week | Disruption, plus the busiest travel week of the year |
| Autumn 2027 | The next national Party Congress, held every five years | Expect a prolonged tightening around the meeting |

None of these makes a trip impossible, and for a visitor with a roaming eSIM they are barely noticeable. They are simply the weeks not to depend on a VPN for anything important.

### Arriving through Hong Kong

If your route takes you through Hong Kong or Macau first, use the stop. The internet there is not filtered in the same way, so it is the last easy place to download a VPN app, install an eSIM profile you forgot about, update your apps or fix a login that has locked you out. An hour in a Hong Kong café before the train north can save a week of frustration.

## If you decide to use one: choosing

If you are in one of the situations above where a VPN makes sense, the choice matters more than it does anywhere else. The things to look for:

*   **Explicit China support**, with a named stealth or obfuscated protocol. Providers that do not mention China at all rarely work there.
*   **Servers close by**, in Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore or elsewhere in Asia, for tolerable speeds.
*   **Apps for every device you will bring**, and enough simultaneous connections for all of them.
*   **A money-back period** long enough to test it before you depend on it.
*   **Support reachable by email**, since the provider’s website will be blocked once you are inside China.

Avoid free VPNs. They are slow, many make their money from your data, and they almost never survive the firewall. Some long-term residents keep a second paid VPN from a different provider as a backup, because when one is being blocked the other often is not. For a short trip, a roaming eSIM is a better backup than a second VPN.

## Setting it up before you fly

This part is not optional. VPN providers’ websites are blocked from inside China, and Apple removed VPN apps from its China App Store in 2017, so whatever you plan to use must be installed, logged in and tested before you leave home.

1.   **Install it on every device** you are bringing: phone, laptop, tablet.
2.   **Log in on each one** and store the login details somewhere you can reach offline.
3.   **Switch on the stealth or obfuscated protocol** in the settings, and connect once with it to make sure it works.
4.   **Download any alternative apps or configuration files** the provider offers for restricted countries, while you still can.
5.   **Update the app** just before you go, so that you are not relying on an update from inside China.
6.   **Save the provider’s support email** and any instructions offline.
7.   **Check your two-factor authentication.** If your email or bank sends codes by text, keep your home line able to receive them. An authenticator app works offline, which is one less thing to depend on the firewall for.
8.   **Download what you cannot afford to lose** anyway: boarding passes, booking confirmations, offline maps, your hotel’s address in Chinese.

Whatever you plan to use in China, VPN or otherwise, gets installed and tested at home. The app stores and provider websites you would need are not reliably reachable once you land.

## Your accounts will think you are somewhere else

Whether you use a VPN or an eSIM, your online accounts will see you logging in from Hong Kong, Singapore, Tokyo or wherever your traffic leaves, and some of them will not like it. Google, Microsoft, banks and soci

title: VOA专访俞大㵢：美对台政策没有改变，中共篡改抗战史“冒领战功”
summary: 华盛顿 — 唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统与中国国家主席习近平在华盛顿举行峰会后，美台关系是否受到影响？美国对台军售又有哪些新的进展？驻美国台北经济文化代表处(TECRO)代表俞大㵢在接受美国之音(VOA)专访时表示，美国对台政策没有改变，双方不同层级官员在峰会前后密切交流。在台湾前总统蔡英文即将访美之际，人们关注现任总统赖清德是否有机会在年底前过境美国，对此俞大㵢回应：“如果有这样的计划，我们会和美国伙伴进行这些讨论”。 俞大㵢在10月2日的专访中除了谈到台
content:
华盛顿 —

唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统与中国国家主席习近平在华盛顿举行峰会后，美台关系是否受到影响？美国对台军售又有哪些新的进展？驻美国台北经济文化代表处(TECRO)代表俞大㵢在接受美国之音(VOA)专访时表示，美国对台政策没有改变，双方不同层级官员在峰会前后密切交流。在台湾前总统蔡英文即将访美之际，人们关注现任总统赖清德是否有机会在年底前过境美国，对此俞大㵢回应：“如果有这样的计划，我们会和美国伙伴进行这些讨论”。

俞大㵢在10月2日的专访中除了谈到台湾在超级智能时代扮演的关键角色，也对美国延宕已久的F-16V Block 70战机终于在特习会结束一周之后抵达台湾感到鼓舞。他强调台湾需要“以实力维护和平”，美国对台军售的规模也应与台湾面对的军事威胁相称。

俞大㵢在访问中特别强调台湾的战略价值不但超越地缘政治，而且是基于美台之间的共同历史，他批评习近平在白宫国宴上提及二战与“飞虎队”时刻意篡改史实，指责中共长期“操弄历史叙事”，试图“冒领战功”，并强调1937年至1945年对日作战期间，与美国并肩抗战的是中华民国，而非1949年才成立的中华人民共和国。

**美台持续沟通 若有赖清德过境计划 双方将会讨论**

当被问到在美中峰会之后他是否有收到美方官员的情况通报，以及特朗普总统曾在5月访问北京后表示将与台湾总统赖清德通话，俞大㵢未证实这通电话是否已经进行，只表示美台双方的沟通“持续、定期、而且非常密切”，并“在不同层级”的官员之间展开。

与此同时，台湾前总统蔡英文本周也将访美，俞大㵢表示，这反映出台北与华盛顿之间“持续的互动与交往”。

俞大㵢还被问到，考虑到即将举行的APEC和二十国集团(G20)峰会以及特朗普总统与习近平可能再次举行会晤，台湾现任总统赖清德是否有可能在今年年底前在出访友邦期间过境美国一事。他回答说：“如果有这样的计划，我们会和美国伙伴进行这些讨论。当然，这最终是由台北决定。”

**“特习会”后首批F-16V抵台 俞大㵢：美国正加快军备交付**

至于延宕已久的美国F-16V Block 70战机终于抵台交付，俞大㵢表示，两架首批F-16V抵达台湾是一个“非常令人兴奋、非常积极的事态发展”，美国政府和军火制造商正努力加快交付台湾已经采购的军事装备。

他指出，后续F-16V战机将随着生产和组装完成陆续交付。对于台湾而言，这批先进战机的到位，将进一步增强台湾空中防卫能力。

俞大㵢同时强调，特朗普政府第二任期已经批准约110亿美元的对台军售。他认为，美国历届不同政府以及美国国会长期以来都对台湾防卫保持支持，无论共和党还是民主党、参议院还是众议院，都存在对台湾安全的广泛支持。

他强调，美台关系仍以《台湾关系法》和六项保证为基础，美国对台湾安全的支持具有长期性，而且得到美国国会跨党派的支持。

美国驻中国大使庞德伟(David Perdue)10月5日在X平台发贴重审美国政府的台湾政策没有改变。

他的帖文说：“特朗普总统在台湾方面的立场是我所知的人当中最坚定的。他表示得非常清楚，我们的一中政策没有改变。我们支持《台湾关系法》、三个公报以及六项保证。习主席已经多次听到唐纳德·特朗普总统的表述。”

**俞大㵢：美对台军售规模须与中共对台威胁相称**

谈到台湾安全，俞大㵢指出，中国军机、军舰、海警和受官方指挥的民船几乎每天都在台湾周边活动，台湾面对来自对岸的军事压力持续存在。他说，台湾需要更多防卫性的武器、包括导弹防御和通信系统，以及适合“不对称作战“的军备“以实力维护和平”。”

俞大㵢认为，美国对台军售的规模应该与中共对台湾的军事威胁程度相称。如果台湾面对的军事压力持续增加，提供台湾足够的防卫装备就是维持台海和平的重要组成部分。

他也将台湾面对的安全挑战与乌克兰的情况相提并论，强调不能以绥靖方式应对潜在威胁。俞大㵢说，台湾并不是寻求冲突，而是希望维持现状、和平、稳定与繁荣。强化防卫能力的目的，是提高潜在侵略者发动攻击的成本，从而降低战争发生的可能性。

**超级智能时代的“硅盾” 俞大㵢：台湾价值不只是地缘政治**

在谈到台湾与美国的战略价值时，俞大㵢将焦点从传统军事安全进一步延伸到超级智能和半导体产业。他表示，随着美中在超级智能、也就是之前所说的人工智能领域加快竞争，台湾的战略重要性已经超越传统的地缘政治。他指出，台湾先进半导体产业及相关数据中心、AI服务器供应链，在全球人工智能产业中扮演关键角色。

俞大㵢认为，这使台湾成为美国及全球科技与国家安全体系中的重要伙伴，也进一步凸显所谓“硅盾”的战略意义。

对于台积电赴美投资，他认为，这不应该简单被理解为将台湾半导体产业外移，而应该被视为产能扩张，以及美国与台湾科技供应链进一步整合。

俞大㵢强调，台湾半导体产业真正难以复制的，不只是晶圆厂本身，还包括工程师、专业知识、产业经验以及完整的供应链体系。这些人才、技术和产业网络，是台湾半导体产业的重要核心，因此，即使中共控制台湾的企图得逞，也无法掌控台湾所拥有的关键技术。

**习近平在白宫国宴提“飞虎队” 俞大㵢批中共“冒领战功”**

针对习近平在白宫国宴上提及二战和“飞虎队”，称“中美两国人民80年前并肩作战，这份由‘血与火锻造的友谊’必将世代相传。” 俞大㵢批评中共试图操弄历史叙事，将抗战时期中华民国政府及军民的牺牲与贡献据为己有，并以英文中的“stolen valor”(冒领战功)来形容这种做法。

俞大㵢强调，1937年至1945年的抗日战争期间，代表中国与美国并肩作战的是中华民国政府，而中华人民共和国直到1949年才成立。他进一步指出，中共建政后不久，中美便在朝鲜战争中成为战场上的对手。他强调，从历史发展和事实来看，中共长期与美国处于敌对状态，中华民国才是那个一直以来与美国保持友好、并肩合作的朋友和盟友。

“80年前，我们是你们的朋友和盟友，80年后，我们依然是你们的朋友和盟友,” 俞大㵢对美国之音谈到美台关系历史时说。

**俞大㵢引富兰克林名言：感谢美国捍卫“自由与安全”**

俞大㵢在访谈最后也特别引用美国开国元勋本杰明·富兰克林(Benjamin Franklin)曾说过的名言: “那些以牺牲自由换取一时安全的人，既不配享有自由，也不配享有安全。”

俞大㵢强调，台湾对于美国政府、美国国会和长期支持台湾的美国朋友深表感谢。

他说：“我们非常赞赏和感激我们拥有与我们价值观相同的美国朋友。你们正在庆祝一个民主共和国成立250周年。而我们也正在庆祝台湾总统直选30周年。我们是自由和民主的，我们会捍卫自己的生活方式。我们非常赞赏美国站在我们这一边。”

title: 中国监视赖清德之子 台湾政府严厉谴责 FBI局长警告：“美国不是你们的游乐场”
summary: 台湾 — 加州一名华裔女子涉嫌受中国指示，监视台湾总统赖清德居住在美国的儿子一家。对此，台湾政府星期一(10月5日)严厉谴责中国的跨国镇压野蛮行径。 美国联邦调查局(FBI)刑事诉状指出，居住加州的张婉莹受中国政府官员指示，监视赖清德之子赖廷与。2025年9月，张婉莹前往西雅图，在赖廷与住家外守候拍摄。 **台湾政府谴责中国野蛮行径 逾百受害者受威胁** 台湾总统府发言人郭雅慧星期一表示，这是典型的跨国镇压，台湾对于这类无视人权与各国主权，目的在打压、威胁，甚至是伤害主张自由
content:
台湾 —

加州一名华裔女子涉嫌受中国指示，监视台湾总统赖清德居住在美国的儿子一家。对此，台湾政府星期一(10月5日)严厉谴责中国的跨国镇压野蛮行径。

美国联邦调查局(FBI)刑事诉状指出，居住加州的张婉莹受中国政府官员指示，监视赖清德之子赖廷与。2025年9月，张婉莹前往西雅图，在赖廷与住家外守候拍摄。

**台湾政府谴责中国野蛮行径 逾百受害者受威胁**

台湾总统府发言人郭雅慧星期一表示，这是典型的跨国镇压，台湾对于这类无视人权与各国主权，目的在打压、威胁，甚至是伤害主张自由民主人们或其家人的野蛮行径，表达最严厉谴责，这样的行为在文明世界不应被容忍。

郭雅慧另外感谢美国司法单位对于台湾民众的协助与保护。她强调，台湾也将持续与美国在内所有民主友盟合作，共同打击这类跨国镇压的非法行为。

> “这样的行为在文明世界不应该被容忍”，台湾总统府发言人郭雅慧10月5日针对涉嫌受中国指使监视台湾总统赖清德之子的加州女子的案件表示这是典型的跨国镇压。此前，美国联邦调查局(FBI)10月4日在洛杉矶国际机场逮捕了张婉莹，当时她正准备前往中国。当局指控她充当未注册的外国代理人。 https://t.co/U2a0PieE28
>
> — 美国之音中文网 (@VOAChinese) [October 5, 2026](https://x.com/VOAChinese/status/2107094106593800243?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

台湾陆委会通过[新闻稿](https://www.mac.gov.tw/cn/News_Content.aspx?n=05B73310C5C3A632&sms=1A40B00E4C745211&s=4F416D99C588CBC5)强调，中共在世界各地持续采行跨国镇压行为，其中，针对台湾进行的跨国境镇压人数至少已达126人、140人次。中共不断威胁当事人及家属安危，其目的不仅仅是针对台湾的元首或官员，而是对所有台湾人进行拙劣的集体威吓，制造寒蝉效应。台湾人坚决反对到底！

台湾民进党立委陈冠廷指出，中共过去曾针对特定人士及海外民运人士，采取类似的监控、骚扰与施压手段。这类行为也会波及当事人的家属，干扰日常生活，造成安全上的威胁。对于中共将压力延伸至境外的做法，台湾必须保持高度警惕，严肃看待每一起涉及海外国人安全的事件。

他说：“我们的国人在海外，如果遇到中共这样的骚扰或者是跟监的话，第一时间我们都要全力来去谴责中共的这种违法的作为，或者是跨境的这种镇压。那过去不管是对特定人士，或者是对他们的民运人士，中国都有类似这样的做法，所以我们必须非常警惕。 ”

**中国监视赖清德之子 引发国安隐忧**

中国全球跨国镇压案例层出不穷，但是这次锁定台湾领导人之子，值此两岸紧张关系持续升高之际，进一步引发国安隐忧。

国安战略学者、台湾开南大学副校长陈文甲以书面方式向美国之音表示，这起案件的本质不只是“监控赖总统家属”，而是涉及外国势力透过代理人，在第三国境内进行情报搜集与跨国政治监控，因此具有高度国安意涵。

陈文甲说明，借由住所、车辆、行踪及家庭成员等资讯，经系统性搜集后，可以建立完整的人员关系图谱与生活模式，进一步成为威胁评估、情报渗透甚至胁迫行动的基础。

据FBI干员凯文·何特(Kevin Holt)递交的刑事诉状中写道：“如果中华人民共和国(PRC)想在任何潜在冲突期间对台湾总统取得筹码，掌握台湾高级政府官员近亲的所在地及照片，包括住所和车辆的照片，都可能对中华人民共和国有所助益。”

台湾国防安全研究院副研究员王占玺接受美国之音采访时表示，赖廷与身为赖清德的儿子，敏感的身份也让这起跨国镇压案显得更加特殊，很可能成为威胁台湾政府高层的新手段。

分析人士指出，中共的目标已经不单是打压单一对象，而是借由跟监赖廷与，试图找出能在未来影响赖清德重大国政决策的武器，而这攸关到美国利益。

张婉莹星期天在洛杉矶国际机场欲出境被逮埔，被控未依法注册却充当外国政府代理人，预计星期一在洛杉矶联邦法院出庭。

值得注意的是，FBI局长卡什·帕特尔(Kash Patel)在X平台上针对此事件连续发文。帕特尔星期一上午在[X上](https://x.com/FBIDirectorKash/status/2107118665401278662)叫板外国对手：“外国对手请注意：美国不是你们的游乐场。”他表示，“在特朗普总统的领导下，联邦调查局都在追捕国家安全威胁，无论他们藏身何处，并把他们铐起来。”

帕特尔在稍早的另一篇[X贴文](https://x.com/FBIDirectorKash/status/2106910435878298056)中写道：“涉嫌为中国政府在美国境内监视外国领袖的家人，还想直接搭飞机溜回上海？没那么容易！现在的FBI不管威胁美国国家安全的人躲在哪里，都会把人找出来，移送司法审判。”

**FBI行动有战略吓阻效果**

王占玺认为，FBI干员递交的刑事诉状以及局长的宣示，充分反映出美国对抗中国跨国镇压行为的决心 。

他指出，尤其是在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)和中国国家主席习近平的峰会之后，美中两国在寻求平衡点之际，FBI并没有选择掩盖案情，相当于释放一个积极的信号给台湾：不论一般民众或者是领导人的家属，只要在美国遭遇到跨国镇压这种违反基本人权跟当地法律的不公平的对待，美国政府愿意出面维护当事人的基本权利。

王占玺说：“FBI这么明确地去点名，其实也有意涵去反映出来，美国政府其实在当前台湾问题的处理上面，其实仍然有他们相当重要的底线，不会让中国在不同的领域为所欲为。”

陈文甲认为，FBI行动具有战略吓阻效果，向外国情报行为者明确宣示，就是美国领土不能成为境外情报活动的安全纵深。未来台美合作应进一步深化反情报、反跨国镇压及情报共享机制，才能有效因应中国日益扩张的灰色地带安全威胁。

同时身为台湾立法院外交国防委员会召委的陈冠廷强调，台湾应透过与友邦及友好国家的情资交流管道，加强资讯分享与合作，及早掌握跨国骚扰、跟监及胁迫的动态，共同防范中共跨国镇压，让国人在海外能免于恐惧与威胁。

台湾外交部也通过新闻稿表示，将秉持“预防”、“保护”、“反制”三面向原则，持续与美国在内所有民主友盟国家密切合作，加强情报共享与安全防护机制，共同打击跨国违法威胁行为，坚定捍卫自由、民主与人权的普世价值。

title: 台北同志酒吧遭搜查 警员歧视言论惹争议

content:
## 台北同志酒吧遭搜查 警员歧视言论惹争议

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，有民众响应呼吁，抗议台北万华警方执法不当。

Published 2026年10月5日早上7点57分

最近更新： 8 分钟前

阅读时间: 3 分钟

台湾台北西门町同志酒吧“Commander D”周末遭搜查，其间现场警员被指发表歧视言论及执法不当，引起争议。

上周六（10月3日）下午的搜查中，负责人被拘捕，多名现场民众被带走。关注LGBT社群权益团体周日（4日）号召到西门町红楼前派出所抗议警察执法不当，逾百人出席。

当地警方一度澄清“并无对身障人士进行言语羞辱”，其后证实有警员言行不当已惩处，有六名警员被申诫；台北巿长蒋万安周一（5日）称，将要求警察局检讨。

台湾在2019年成为亚洲首个将同性婚姻合法化的地区，台北将于本月底举办东亚规模最大的同志游行活动，警方行动引发外界对当地自、开放形象的关注。

[跳过 Instagram 帖子](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cmz98p0x525xo/simp#end-of-instagram-content)

告知: BBC 不对外来网站内容负责

结尾 Instagram 帖子

## 警员在搜索期间做了什么？

图像来源，Provided

图像加注文字，现场画面可见，部份人士被戴上手铐。

综合台湾媒体报道，警方上周六下午突击搜查“Commander D”酒吧，从现场带走酒吧负责人钟姓男子及其他在场人士共52人，其中包括上半身赤裸的男性，并检获安全套、润滑油等。

“Commander D”为男同志 BDSM 主题酒吧，开业超过十年，BDSM 是指一种涉及束缚、支配调教、施虐受虐与感官刺激的性行为模式。

台北市警察局万华分局表示，已将钟男以涉嫌妨害风化罪嫌移送台北地方检察署（台北地检署）侦办，其余相关人等以涉嫌违反社会秩序维护法处罚。

搜查行动后，网络流传帖文，其中有[现场录音](https://www.threads.com/@greenparty_tw/post/DeFCGp-lkwJ)，有警员曾表示：“残障还可以在里面做爱喔？”

BBC中文未能独立核实录音内容。亦有影片显示，有警员称，在场人士[不能录影](https://www.threads.com/@jaychang0728/post/DeEnM70jnWD)。

侦查队队长陈怡凯一度澄清称，并无对特定身障人士进行言语羞辱。

警方表示，此案是经民众检举、合法蒐证，确认有妨害风化情事，有员警言行不当已惩处在案。警方亦证实，执法过程确有员警言行不当，已予以行政惩处，有6名警员被申，后续将持续加强教育训练，要求员警尊重多元文化、保障市民权益。

图像来源，Threads/@41027hcl

图像加注文字，有民众抗议警方执法不当行为，要求道歉。

## 民间发起游行抗议

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，集会的同志群体要求台北市警察万华分局道歉。

在西门町红楼前的派出所外举行的抗议活动上，自称曾被警方带走的民众温（Wen）先生对路透社表示：“他们很暴力地突袭，真的非常可怕。”

其中一名抗议者杨康（Kang Yang）表示，警方采取行动正值“骄傲月”（Pride Month），让他相当愤怒，他强调：“我不能接受这件事。这座城市过去曾自称对同志很友善。”

多个关注同志权益及人权组织[发起联合声明](https://www.amnesty.tw/node/25033)关注事件，指出执法机关有必要侦办特定案件，也须在法律授权的边界内，以最小侵害方式进行，提出五项诉求，包括独立调查、保留当时的执法纪录等。

中国国民党籍台北市长蒋万安周一被问及事件时说：“不论是什么年龄、性别、性倾向、身分族群或认同，都是我们共同要守护、享有相同权利的台北人。”

“对于被影响的人我也非常抱歉，那过程当中，执法的过程，如果有不当，当然就必须要严加的检讨。”

执政民进党立法委员，台北市长参选人沈伯洋说，警察依法执法大家都尊重，如果有违法的事情，应该依法处理，但依法执法不代表执法的方式不需要被检视。

沈伯洋说：“一座真正友善的城市，不只是欢迎你来，也让你知道，你可以安心地做自己。”

台湾将于11月底举行地方选举，现任台北巿长蒋万安竞逐连任，其他参选人有民进党沈伯洋、“台湾麻将最大党”郭玺、“台湾双语无法党”萧文干、三势团结促进联盟唐新民，以及无党籍林志成。

title: 美中稀土之争 美国打“组合拳”加速重建自主供应链

content:
九月底的“特习峰会”，两国元首将贸易休兵期仅推迟两个月，有分析人士指出，问题卡在稀土谈判，因为美国不满中国去年承诺的稀土出口量只履行了三分之二，因此拒绝大幅松绑贸易限制以持续施压。

中国自2025年以来，祭出收紧稀土的出口管制对美“卡脖子”后，如何突围成了美国的重中之重，也催生其重建“去中化”、自主的稀土供应链。

**美国的稀土磁铁矿链即将成形?**

虽然市场普遍认为，美国的这条“去中化”稀土矿链恐耗时5-10年才能成形，但白宫贸易与制造业高级顾问彼得·纳瓦罗(Peter Navarro)近期给出了最乐观的时间表。

他9月25日受访时表示，美国将在未来6-18个月内“实现稀土磁铁的自给自足，甚至有能力出口。”

纳瓦罗说，美国政府采“超高速”注资新创公司，再将其与既有大厂配对，来进行规模化生产，目前产出的氧化物和下游磁铁的成本可望比中国制品还低。

他还说，中共将稀土“武器化”是敲醒美国和全世界的警钟。

位于台北的中技社科技暨工程研究中心主任芮嘉玮，虽然对纳瓦罗的时间表存疑，但他在接受美国之音采访时表示，美国正多管齐下重建自主稀土矿链，以摆脱对中国的依赖。他说，以日本对中国的稀土依赖度从2010年的92%大降至今年的60%以下为例，美国走稀土自主的路虽耗时且困难，但“方向绝对是对的”。

**美国稀土自主的四大组合拳**

综合芮嘉玮和媒体的分析，美国布局自主稀土矿链的组合拳包括:

一、**120亿美元的金库计划(Project Vault)**：美国今年2月已启动类似石油战备储量的机制，来确保智能手机、电动车及战机等军工产品所需之镓、钴等稀土关键矿产的60天紧急供应量。

目前包括波音、通用汽车(GM)等十多家美企已加入，并承诺未来若发生重大断供危机，将在指定价格、定量和库存回补等条件下，预先提领战备库存使用。

二、**注资和保底价**：据[《华尔街日报》](https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/china-critical-minerals-supply-chain-charts-fbe4eb85)9月27日引述不具名的白宫官员报道，美国政府正积极对国内矿产项目注资，目前已完成180项的专案立案，该报道引述华府智库“战略与国际研究中心(Center for Strategic and International Studies)”的统计称，2025年至今年6月间，美国政府对稀土和磁铁项目的非股权投资增至76亿美元，是2020-2024年间投资总额的四倍以上。

另外，美国也透过股权投资和价格补贴大力扶持本土产业，例如，国防部2025年7月已斥资4亿美元，取得美企龙头芒廷帕斯材料公司(MP Materials)15%的股权，除成为最大股东外，还承诺承购其第二座磁铁厂未来十年的所有产能，并实施“价格保底”，以每公斤110美元的钕镨氧化物价格下限为例，几乎比中国制品的市价高出一倍，来确保该公司不再被中国的价格倾销战击垮，也凸显美国快速打造涵盖采矿、加工、回收和磁铁制造全产业链的战略企图。

除芒廷帕斯材料公司外，美国政府也拟斥资16亿美元取得另一家小型磁铁制造商美国稀土(USA Rare Earth)约10%的股权，唯目前联邦资金仍未拨付，因该公司尚未达成解锁资金所需的里程碑。

三、**稀土回收循环**: 芮嘉玮分析，美国也资助电子废弃物回收稀土的“城市采矿”计划，并推动《稀土循环利用法案》，要求制造商建立产品回收体系，也以税收优惠鼓励企业使用回收稀土，盼于2030年前达到回收稀土能满足国内20%需求的目标。

美企大厂中，如苹果(Apple)早于去年就与芒廷帕斯材料公司签下5亿美元的供应协议，委其以回收稀土的方式，为苹果提供稀土磁铁。

四、**国际结盟**:美国已启动涵盖55国的“资源地缘战略参与论坛(Forum on Resource Geostrategic Engagement)，简称FORGE联盟，并于7月正式接任主席国，分析人士认为，此联盟高度展现美国反制中国、夺回全球稀土定价权的战略策略。

对此，日本智库笹川和平财团(Sasakawa Peace Foundation)安全保障与日美事务小组的主任研究员小林祐喜(Yuki Kobayashi)告诉美国之音:“美、日和欧洲是昔日引进稀土精炼技术到中国的主要大国，其部分市占率虽小的公司仍保有稀土精炼和制造高效能磁铁的技术，因此，以美日为核心，重组这些技术是打破中国垄断的关键。”

不过，他说，稀土虽已跃居各国的国安战略问题，但企业和消费者可能更在意价格和采矿衍生的环境污染等问题，这将对各国打造自主稀土矿链带来挑战。

一位负责打造台湾自主稀土矿链的材料化工专家在不具名接受美国之音采访时也表示，美国有稀土矿，上游开采不是问题，但要重建包括中下游精炼和终端应用在内的矿链，代价较高，但若“不计成本一定做得到”。

他说，美国目前以绑融资金流、未来价格和客户的方式来确保自主稀土矿链的成功率，非常聪明，也应有机会反制中国的稀土倾销战。

**中国打稀土牌短多长空**

这位专家还说，中国大打稀土牌也有反作用力，据他了解，因出口管制，部分矿商中企的磁材稼动率(开工率)近期已降至三、四成，若按七大工业集团(G7)的共识:要将从单一国家(剑指中国)进口的稀土与永久磁铁比例，于2030年前降至60%以下，未来若真的达标，这代表中国恐将损失至少三成的全球市占率。

不过，据《路透社》7月引述十多位专家和分析人士的报道称，美国国防部明年1月起禁用中国进口的禁令恐跳票，因以最常见的稀土磁铁为例，美国2025年需求约4.8万公吨，国内供应量却仅300公吨；即使产能持续扩张，预计今年底也只能达到5,000公吨，约只能满足需求的一成。

稀土素有“工业维他命”之称，共包含镧(La)、铈(Ce)、镨(Pr)、钕(Nd)等17种金属元素，微量添加就能强化其他金属化合物的性能，因此，从手机、电动车到战机和核潜舰的制造都离不开它，其中最常见的终端应用是永磁磁铁，广泛用于马达相关制品。

稀土之稀贵不在蕴藏量，而在精炼之复杂过程。

美国在1990年代以前曾是全球最大的稀土制造和出口国，但基于环境污染和成本等因素，逐渐外移，让中国有机可趁，顺势构建起从开采到冶炼、再到磁材成品制造的全链条霸权，全球市占一度逾九成。

国际能源署(IEA)7月中旬曾[警告](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/chinas-rare-earth-curbs-endanger-65-trillion-western-industry-iea-says-2026-07-16/)，各国为建立替代性稀土矿链，投入的资金已暴增至650亿美元，也使得中国的稀土市占率略降至85%，“但关键稀土的供应链仍高度集中”，且若中国重启稀土的全面管制，“以汽车、高科技、国防及能源领域为主，中国以外的欧美地区规模约6.5万亿美元的下游生产，将面临断供危机，再度凸显全球关键矿物供应链的脆弱性。”

# 香港团体调查：逾三成半受访基层住户的单位不合简朴房标准 有人搬进无窗工厦

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月5日 14:43

香港民间团体劏房支援连线10月5日发表调查报告说，在今年3月2日至6月23日访问的647户基层住户中，35.4%住户的单位至少有一项不符合简朴房的要求，11.7%有两项以上不合规，最常见的是面积不足8平方米。《简朴房条例》今年3月起生效；团体担心，这些单位未必能获认证，住户可能要面对改建、加租、终止租约甚至搬迁，并估计2027年9月宽限期临近结束时会出现迫迁高峰。

调查还发现，近三分之一续租的住户曾被要求增加租金、水电费或其他杂费；逾百户的书面租约在2026年至2028年间到期。过去一年有59户搬过家，其中54户搬迁后仍住在不适切居所，19户搬进了工厦劏房、僭建单位、木屋或寮屋。

劏房支援连线调查的几个数字

| 调查发现 | 数字 |
| --- | --- |
| 单位至少一项不合简朴房要求 | 35.4% |
| 单位有两项以上不合规 | 11.7% |
| 续租时曾被要求加租或加杂费 | 近三分之一 |
| 过去一年搬过家 | 59户 |
| 搬迁后仍住不适切居所 | 54户 |
| 搬进工厦劏房、僭建、木屋或寮屋 | 19户 |

数据：劏房支援连线10月5日发表的调查报告（647户，今年3月2日至6月23日访问）

从事清洁工作的邓女士原本在荃湾租住一个约100呎、有窗的劏房，月租约4000元；70岁的业主说担心规管、不想花钱装修，干脆把楼卖了。她两个月内搬进一个一劏十一、不足100呎的工厦单位，月租连水电费约4000元。她对媒体说，单位没有窗、空气不流通，早上起床常感头晕，看了八个月中医。工厦单位不在简朴房规管范围内，改作居住用途本来就违反《建筑物条例》。

住在葵涌的单亲母亲May一家四口，今年7月收到业主通知，说因为简朴房规管要收回单位改装，限期四个月内搬走。她对媒体说，同区同类劏房的租金已涨到一万元以上，政府的租金津贴只有6000元，她已轮候过渡性房屋一年多。

房屋局局长何永贤10月初说，全港11万个分间单位中，已收到约7.38万宗简朴房登记，约占68%，42个单位已获认证。房屋局的六支地区服务队处理了86宗怀疑短时间内被迫迁的个案，主要在油尖旺和深水埗，已协助其中78户申请过渡性房屋，另外8户自行安排了住处。劏房支援连线成员赖建国说，还有三万多个单位没有登记，说明业主在观望，可能退出市场或把单位还原。

赖建国说，单位改成合规的简朴房后租金势必上涨，基层住户负担不起，最后会搬到工厦、寮屋、天台屋或新界的货柜屋等更隐蔽、火灾风险更高的地方。他还建议把工厦、寮屋和丁屋也纳入规管，并参考安老院舍买位的做法安置被迫迁的住户。

## 茉莉花观察

这一节是茉莉花的看法，依据是上文的事实。

我们的判断《简朴房条例》要淘汰不合格的劏房，但从调查看，搬走的基层住户多数没有住得更好，有的还搬进了条例管不到的地方。过去一年搬过家的59户里，54户仍住在不适切居所，19户搬进了工厦劏房、僭建单位、木屋或寮屋；工厦单位改作住宅本来就违法，火灾风险也更高。

不同看法 约68%的分间单位已经登记，房屋局的地区服务队还在迫迁通知发出前就上门，已协助78户申请过渡性房屋；条例本身就是要让人不再住面积不足8平方米的单位。我们同意条例的目标没有错，政府也在安置；但工厦、寮屋和天台屋完全在规管之外，搬进这些地方的住户，登记和认证的数字反映不出来。

接下来要看什么 宽限期结束前，还没登记的三万多个单位是登记、改建还是退出市场；政府会不会把工厦和寮屋纳入规管，并支援住在里面的人。

综合集志社 The Collective HK、Dimsum Daily报道
