title: Haze prompts school closures in Malaysia
summary: **KUALA LUMPUR** — Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country on Friday as haze from fires in neighboring Indonesia again plunged local air quality to among the world’s worst. Toxic smoke from peatland and forest
content:
**KUALA LUMPUR** — Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country on Friday as haze from fires in neighboring Indonesia again plunged local air quality to among the world’s worst.

Toxic smoke from peatland and forest fires has shrouded cities in the region for more than a month, sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing.

The school closures came as Malaysia’s leader discussed the choking smoke with his Indonesian counterpart and called for an urgent regional meeting.

*   [Trump: No new Iran attack before midterms](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/trump-no-new-iran-attack-before-midterms/2442642)

Air quality in Kuala Lumpur has been firmly in “unhealthy levels” this week, with a Swiss-based air quality monitor ranking the Malaysian capital among the world’s most polluted cities on most days.

Malaysia’s Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said she has instructed whole school closures in four states and two federal territories, as well as one partial closure in central Pahang state.

Malaysia’s king, Sultan Ibrahim, weighed in on the matter on Thursday, saying schools should be closed as air quality readings reached 150 or higher on the Air Pollutant Index (API).

Under Malaysian guidelines, API readings above 100 are classified as unhealthy, above 200 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous. Reading beyond 500 constitute the threshold for declaring a local emergency.

Kuala Lumpur on Friday showed a reading of around 170 API.

The city was the second-most polluted globally behind neighboring Singapore on Friday morning, Swiss-based air monitor IQAir said.

‘Worrying level’

Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday he discussed the fire situation with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

“The haze issue is indeed at a worrying level. And I have personally contacted President Prabowo,” Anwar said.

“And he also agreed to take the necessary steps,” the premier added, without going into specific details.

He said Malaysia has been taking measures to combat the haze, including increasing attempts to trigger rain via cloud seeding.

Experts said the flames were being fanned by a turbo-charged El Niño weather phenomenon, causing the worst pollution conditions in years.

Anwar said he had asked Malaysia’s Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to contact the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ secretariat for an urgent meeting between environmental ministers to discuss the matter.

“So these are all the steps we are taking, but we are monitoring and will try the measures that we ought to take next,” Anwar said.

Singapore’s air quality levels also dipped into the “very unhealthy” range, with a reading of 205 on the Air Quality Index (AQI), according to the IQAir website.

The AQI converts measurements of pollutants into a single figure indicating air quality and potential health risks.

Readings above 150 are classified as unhealthy, while levels above 300 are considered hazardous.

title: Xinjiang’s “Blue Miracle”
summary: A cold-water fish breeding base in Turpan, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, August 21, 2025. _Credit: Gou Lifeng/Xinhua via [Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/this-photo-taken-on-aug-21-2025-shows-a-cold-water-fi
content:
A cold-water fish breeding base in Turpan, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, August 21, 2025. _Credit: Gou Lifeng/Xinhua via [Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/this-photo-taken-on-aug-21-2025-shows-a-cold-water-fish-news-photo/2287190051?phrase=fish%20farm%20xinjiang&adppopup=true)_

China’s Xinjiang region, located on the country’s far northwest frontier, is a land of unforgiving extremes. At Xinjiang’s southwest border stands K2, the second-highest mountain in the world at 28,251 feet.

The Karakoram Range, where K2 is situated, is just one of four major ranges abutting, slicing through, or ringing Xinjiang. The Kunlun runs along the province’s southeastern border; the Altai is found in Xinjiang’s northern reaches, and the Tian Shan spans its center. Together, the mountains, while breathtaking to look at, work to keep much of Xinjiang starved of moisture. Barely six inches of rain fall every year across Xinjiang’s 600,000 square miles.

An aerial view of a small oil town in the Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang, China. _Credit: Zheng via [Adobe Stock](https://stock.adobe.com/images/aerial-view-of-a-small-oil-town-in-the-heart-of-the-taklamakan-desert-in-xinjiang-china/1844330384?prev\_url=detail)_

A huge swath of Xinjiang is taken up by China’s largest desert, the Taklamakan. The Taklamakan’s ever-shifting dunes can top 600 feet, taller than the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt.

In total, less than 10 percent of Xinjiang has ever been fit for human habitation. Those who have eked out an existence have mostly been nomadic herdsmen, with refuge for them and their families found around a modest number of oases fed by mountaintop glaciers in the Tian Shan and Kunlun. Historically, Xinjiang’s native populations have included Turkic Uyghurs, Han Chinese, Kazakhs, Mongols, and Tajiks.

Central Chinese authorities were long content to regard Xinjiang as a remote and rugged strategic buffer against an outside threat from the west. Shortly after the 1949 revolution, though, the state began to imagine Xinjiang as more than a wild outpost, and rather as a valuable territorial holding to be tamed and exploited, its people persuaded or conscripted to join China’s emergence into the modern world, and, in time, its campaign for global economic supremacy.

Exploratory wells, Tarim oilfield, Xinjiang. _Credit: SASAC_

Beginning in the 1950s, Chinese government geologists discovered oil and gas in three of Xinjiang’s topographical basins — the Tarim, Junggar, and Tuha — and mounted some of the deepest drilling programs ever seen. Xinjiang became the western anchor of what was called the West-East Gas Pipeline, a monumental project completed in 2004 that sends natural gas over 2,400 miles to cities such as Shanghai.

At the same time, the state reengineered the Tarim River, Xinjiang’s longest, in a bid to turn the province’s hard and dry soil into farmable land. Reservoirs were built on the Tarim’s tributaries; diversion gates measured and allocated flow, and lined canals carried water to what would become newly leveled farmland. The Tarim, once an unremarkable waterway prone to seasonal flooding in an otherwise parched landscape, was suddenly a highly regulated and reliable supply system. The controlled use of the Tarim would help jumpstart the growing of a range of crops in Xinjiang, including an aggressive push to plant and harvest cotton.

[Video 13](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Troops-Xinjiang.mp4)

Troops from the People’s Liberation Army entered Xinjiang in 1949. Demobilized troops became part of the XPCC, Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, established under a directive to “cultivate and guard border areas” in 1954. _Credit: VideoChinaTV, Channel 4_

Amid the discovery of natural resource riches and the marvels of technology, there was always the daunting human project of somehow creating a workforce for the state’s ambitions in Xinjiang. The Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps would handle that feat of reinvention. The XPCC is a corporate unit of the Chinese army, made up of former soldiers turned economic developers. They were sent to Xinjiang as the government agents meant to convert herdsmen into farmers. Land was seized, training programs were implemented and enforced, state-backed companies were launched, the reluctant were threatened with detention, and many were shipped out of Xinjiang to work in China’s larger eastern cities.

The company’s record of coercive tactics in Xinjiang has earned it a notorious international reputation. Over the past decade, the XPCC has seized more than half a million acres in Xinjiang to use for growing cotton, as well as for a variety of other industries, from fruit farming to solar fields. The company has also helped the government relocate more than 10 percent of Xinjiang’s population — over 2.5 million people between 2014 and 2019 — through labor transfers. If brutal, the XPCC’s work in Xinjiang has been effective. Today, Xinjiang produces roughly 20 percent of the world’s cotton supply and is a major source of export crops such as tomatoes, lavender, and wine grapes.

Left: Workers load cotton onto a truck in Alar, Xinjiang. Right: Farmers put harvested tomatoes on a sunning ground for air-drying in Yanqi Hui Autonomous County, Xinjiang. _Credit: IC Photo via Depositphotos_

Of all the successes in Xinjiang over the last 75 years none may be as remarkable as the latest: The Chinese are growing fish in Xinjiang, a place often referred to as the most landlocked spot on the planet.

> China’s desert fish farming project is actually as much a consequence of self-preservation as creative ingenuity… Aquaculture, a 2024 report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies explained, is central to Beijing’s efforts “to bolster food security.” As a result, China has been perhaps the most aggressive practitioner of fish farming.

It turns out that in China’s earliest efforts to pull oil out of Xinjiang, its government drilling teams were regularly turning up evidence of underground aquifers, including underneath the Taklamakan. Researchers knew that the Taklamakan had once been entirely underwater, connected to one of Earth’s oceans. The desert’s sand and soil were littered with ancient coral fragments, microscopic plankton, bivalves, and gastropods. The Taklamakan’s salty soil, in fact, helped explain why some of the world’s best-preserved mummies had been unearthed there.

[Video 14](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Sand-Dunes.mp4)

Qiemo County Shishixian Aquatic Products built a roughly eight-acre fish farm on the southeastern edge of the Taklamakan Desert in March 2024. Today, the farm raises golden pomfret, grouper, and mullet in two outdoor ponds and an indoor greenhouse with 68 tanks. _Credit: Xinhua_

The aquifers found beneath Xinjiang’s arid vastness would eventually be mapped, and tests would be done on the discovered water — to see both how pressurized and just how salty the water was. Initially, the tests suggested the waters under the Taklamakan and elsewhere across Xinjiang were too salty to be used for farming, too bitter to be consumed by humans. Chinese scientists eventually realized that the underground waters in Xinjiang could be adjusted to mimic seawater.

As a result, over 1,000 fish farms now dot Xinjiang, producing about 200,000 tons of seafood annually. Atlantic salmon, lobster, bass, carp, crab, shrimp — all of them and more raised in Xinjiang. Chinese media calls it the “Blue Miracle,” a maritime economy in a frontier home to what is known as the Eurasian Pole of Inaccessibility. [The Outlaw Ocean Project](https://theoutlawocean.com/), a news organization in Washington, DC, mapped these farms as part of a sweeping [investigation](https://foodforfeed.theoutlawocean.com/) showing how much seafood is reaching the U.S., including government facilities, in violation of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA).

In recent years, China has pushed fish farming into its arid and high-altitude far west, particularly in Xinjiang and across the Tibetan Plateau. [This map](https://chinafishfarms.theoutlawocean.com/) highlights more than 1,000 of these farms and provides access to a national database of over 63,000 sites. _Credit: [The Outlaw Ocean Project](https://chinafishfarms.theoutlawocean.com/)_

“Raising fish in the desert?” China’s state broadcaster CCTV wrote in a 2025 article. “It sounds impossible, but in Xinjiang, it’s becoming a reality.”

###### **FARMERS OF FISH**

Aquaculture is a global phenomenon. More than half of all seafood the world consumes now comes from aquaculture rather than wild catch. India alone produces some 11 million metric tons of farmed fish products every year. The raising of clams, oysters, scallops, and mussels — distinctive aquaculture marvels because they require no feed and very little freshwater — has driven much of the explosive growth. In a 2019 report, the Nature Conservancy argued that by 2050, sustainably managed fish farms should become humanity’s primary source of seafood.

A floating fish farm in Xiapu, Fujian, China._Credit: [Yujie](https://stock.adobe.com/images/aerial-view-of-the-sea-fish-farm-cages-and-fishing-village-in-xiapu-fujian-province-china/727202819?prev\_url=detail)_

Most ambitious fish farming falls into a small handful of models. In Asia, the dominant system is the freshwater pond: excavated basins stocked with hatchery-raised juveniles, fed daily, and aerated mechanically to prevent oxygen crashes. Along coasts, floating net pens hold fish in open water, relying on currents to disperse waste. Some fish farms operate fully enclosed recirculating systems, filtering and reusing water inside warehouses.

The $313 billion industry has generated varied and extraordinary benefits. In India, it is a major source of employment, particularly for women. In Bangladesh, the expansion of fish farming has helped drive down prices, making seafood more affordable for poorer households. The industry, even accounting for transporting the farmed fish around the world, is a far smaller source of carbon emissions than beef or pork.

Recent efforts to push the nature and reach of the business have wound up pushing the boundaries of the imagination and technology. The Norwegians have built enormous, semi-submersible structures in the open ocean, capable of holding volumes of water great enough to house 1.5 million salmon. The Chinese have built “aquaculture ships,” huge vessels sent to sea with 15 breeding cabins capable of holding 90,000 cubic meters of water.

[Video 15](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Fish-Farms-in-Desert.mp4)

On the southern rim of the Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang, two companies, Hotan Yujianjianglai and Qiemo Shishixian, began farming fish around 2024. Roughly 250 fish farms in and around the Taklamakan produce $100 million in desert seafood — including species like cod and grouper — every year. _Credit: Hotan Yujianjianglai Aquaculture, Xinhua News_

In Scotland, underwater robots are used to combat the threat of sea lice, a parasite that feeds on salmon. The robots identify the lice and fire laser pulses to eradicate them. The inventions have not been exclusive to major commercial farm fishing. Modest fish farms in Indonesia have been using smartphone apps to manage timed, more cost-effective feeding schedules at their ponds.

And then there is the engineering of the fish themselves. In the U.S., the seafood company AquAdvantage has won approval to raise cloned salmon. Fish farming, therefore, isn’t only about cages, pumps, and sensors anymore. It’s also about re-writing biology — treating growth rates and production timelines as variables that can be redesigned, not just managed.

But as with many feats of human ingenuity and profit-making, aquaculture is freighted with a multitude of downsides. Crowding millions of fish together produces

title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal
source: 菲律宾在中国紧张局势中加强其最北端的防御
summary: _Russia and China block US efforts to expand the Darfur arms embargo to cover all of Sudan amid ongoing conflict._ The United Nations Security Council extended the arms embargo on Sudan’s Darfur region by two months but failed to agree on a
content:
_Russia and China block US efforts to expand the Darfur arms embargo to cover all of Sudan amid ongoing conflict._

The United Nations Security Council extended the arms embargo on Sudan’s Darfur region by two months but failed to agree on a US proposal to widen it to the whole country, after permanent members Russia and China opposed it.

The 15-member council unanimously adopted Resolution 2830 on Thursday, extending the sanctions regime until December 11 to allow more time for negotiations.

## Recommended Stories

list of 3 items
*   list 1 of 3[The battle for Kordofan: The corridor linking Sudan’s east and west](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/1/the-battle-for-kordofan-the-corridor-linking-sudans-east-and-west)
*   list 2 of 3[Washington’s diplomacy in Sudan has backfired](https://www.aljazeera.com/opinions/2026/10/2/washingtons-diplomacy-in-sudan-has-backfired)
*   list 3 of 3[Sudan’s army says it captured RSF stronghold in North Kordofan](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2/sudans-army-says-it-captured-rsf-stronghold-in-north-kordofan)

end of list
It also extended the mandate of the panel of experts that monitors the measures until January 11, 2027. The UN described the text as a short-term “technical rollover”, after the regime was last renewed for one month on September 11.

The sanctions were first imposed in 2005 under Resolution 1591.

The council set up an arms embargo on [armed actors in Darfur](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/1/the-battle-for-kordofan-the-corridor-linking-sudans-east-and-west), a travel ban and an asset freeze on designated individuals and entities, and a five-member panel of experts to monitor them.

Despite weeks of discussion, the United States failed to secure approval to expand the embargo. Russia and China have argued for keeping the existing regime.

## ’20 years outdated’

“The current sanctions regime is over 20 years outdated, and is insufficient to address the realities of the war today,” US Ambassador Jeff Bartos told the council last month, urging it to “expand the arms embargo across the entire territory of Sudan”.

Russia’s deputy UN ambassador, Anna Evstigneeva, said at the time: “We will not allow even a hint of broadening the restrictions by the council on Sudan.”

Sudan’s UN ambassador, Al-Harith Mohamed, argued that a total embargo goes against the UN Charter’s guarantee of the right to self-defence.

The war between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which began in April 2023, has killed at least 59,000 people, though aid groups warn [the toll could be far higher](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/9/un-probe-finds-mass-killings-gang-rapes-by-sudans-rsf-amount-to-genocide).

It has also displaced about 13 million people and pushed parts of the country into famine.

The army holds central and eastern Sudan, while the RSF controls Darfur in the west and parts of the south.

Darfur, a region about the size of Spain, has seen some of the worst violence, with displacement camps attacked and repeated ethnic massacres killing thousands at a time.

SEOUL, Oct. 8 (Yonhap) -- The heritage authority said Thursday it has yet to decide whether to raise admission fees for its major palaces and royal tombs, with the planned increase still under review.

The Korea Heritage Service (KHS) had planned to announce the fee hikes in November so they could take effect in January 2027, citing the relatively low fees compared with those at major heritage sites abroad.

But the service said the timing of the fee increases remains "undecided," in a document submitted to Rep. Choi Min-hee for an annual parliamentary audit.

Gyeongbok Palace in central Seoul is crowded with visitors, in this file photo taken Sept. 24, 2026, the first day of the extended Chuseok holiday. (Yonhap)

[](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261008007900315 "Opens in new web browser window")

In the document, the service's Royal Palaces and Tombs Center said it will instead improve visitor services in January after reviewing the free admission programs for visitors wearing hanbok and the potential financial burden of the fee hike on the public.

"At present, there are not enough rest areas, information desks and facilities for people with disabilities, and the reservation systems are not sufficiently equipped," Huh Min, chief of the KHS, said. "We are currently addressing these shortcomings."

The admission fees have remained unchanged since 2005, despite growing visitor numbers and calls for better preservation of the heritage sites and improved visitor experiences.

Adult admission to Gyeongbok Palace and Changdeok Palace currently costs 3,000 won (US$2.20), while Changgyeong Palace, Deoksu Palace and Jongmyo Shrine charge 1,000 won. Fees for Joseon-era royal tombs range from 500 won to 2,000 won.

The service has considered a three-stage increase, including fees of 5,000 won for all palaces and Jongmyo, and 3,000 won for royal tombs, according to a separate document cited by Rep. Kim Jae-won of the minor opposition Rebuilding Korea Party.

About 17.81 million people visited South Korea's four major palaces, Jongmyo and the royal tombs in 2025, and some 69 percent of the visitors were admitted free of charge, according to figures from the agency.

title: Chinese Hackers Impersonate US Officials for AI Cyber Espionage
summary: Source: Pixels Hunter via Shutterstock [Chinese hackers](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/china-spies-russian-it-orgs) impersonated US policymakers in adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing campaigns aimed at stealing
content:
Source: Pixels Hunter via Shutterstock

[Chinese hackers](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/china-spies-russian-it-orgs) impersonated US policymakers in adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing campaigns aimed at stealing credentials from AI experts working for US think tanks, universities, and legal organizations.

Researchers from Proofpoint discovered the campaign, which occurred in July, and attributed it to [China-aligned](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/china-hijacks-captive-portals-spy-asian-diplomats) threat actor TA419, [according to a blog post](https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/hallucinating-credibility-china-aligned-ta419-impersonates-its-way-us-ai-policy)published last week. The activity is believed to be part of a broader [Chinese cyber-espionage](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/china-linked-hacker-ai-capabilities-apac-attack) effort to gather intelligence on US AI policymaking and planning.

"Proofpoint has observed TA419 conducting regular targeted credential phishing campaigns against individuals working for US- and Japan-based think tanks, defense contractors, universities, and law firms since at least April 2025," Proofpoint cyber-threat intelligence analyst Mark Kelly and the Proofpoint Threat Research Team wrote in the post.

TA419 impersonated multiple individuals in the campaign, including a former member of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy leadership team, and engaged with victims through a series of emails. The July campaign followed an earlier operation in February in which the same threat actor impersonated an Anthropic employee to target an AI policy expert at a US think tank, according to Proofpoint.

Related:[ClickFix Attacks Evolve to Better Hide Malicious Payloads](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/clickfix-attacks-evolve-better-hide-malicious-payloads)

"This activity likely supports wider Chinese intelligence objectives to better understand ongoing developments within the US AI policy and regulatory landscape and occurs amid intense strategic competition, accusations of model distillation, and export controls involving the US and China," the researchers wrote.

## Social Engineering Before the Phish

The attack combines [social engineering](https://www.darkreading.com/cloud-security/unc6692-social-engineering-malware-cloud-abuse)with extensive phishing infrastructure, but the technical attack comes later in the process. Rather than beginning with an obviously malicious email or attachment, TA419 first attempts to establish credibility with its targets.

The group [impersonated people](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/threat-actor-booking-com-clickfix-phishing-scheme) who appear to be legitimate contacts for AI policy experts at US think tanks, universities, and law firms. Once that relationship was established, the attackers introduced the phishing component.

On July 8, for example, the actor pretended to be Lynne Edwards Parker, the former principal deputy director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, and later impersonated Heidi Crebo-Rediker, a prominent economist and foreign policy expert.

"In both cases, the group opened with benign outreach, inviting targets to join a fictitious 'AI Policy Advisory Committee' or to contribute to a Senate Committee on Foreign Relations report on AI export controls and supply chains," the researchers wrote.

Related:[Alleged KillSec Ransomware Mastermind a 16-Year-Old](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/killsec-ransomware-mastermind-16-year-old)

The approach allowed the attackers to start conversations around subjects that were particularly relevant to their targets, including AI policy, export controls, and technology regulation. The strategy is notable because the attackers were not simply trying to convince victims to click on a [phishing link](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/attackers-livechat-phish-credit-card-personal-data). They first attempted to make the eventual link appear to be a legitimate part of an ongoing professional relationship.

## Technical Attack Begins With a Link

Once that [credibility](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/axios-attack-complex-social-engineering-industrialized) was established, the technical attack began with a link that appeared to lead to a legitimate Microsoft or OneDrive document or collaboration environment.

"If the target replied, TA419 followed up with a shortened URL that purported to share additional information," the researchers wrote. "The link ultimately led to a fake OneDrive AiTM credential phishing page designed to gain access to the target’s cloud account."

The URL used a multistage redirection chain before ultimately taking the victim to an AitM credential-phishing page. Proofpoint said the infrastructure used a customized version of the open source [browser-in-the-browser](https://www.techtarget.com/cybersecurity/definition/man-in-the-browser-MitB) (BitB) phishing tool Frameless BitB.

Related:[Warlock Ransomware Hits Large Spanish, Portuguese Orgs](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/warlock-ransomware-spanish-portuguese)

Rather than simply collecting a username and password, an [AitM attack](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/china-backed-apt41-attack-africa) places the attacker between the victim and the legitimate authentication service. This can allow the attacker to capture authentication information and, critically, the authenticated session, even while the victim can still complete multifactor authentication (MFA) and believe the login was legitimate, according to Proofpoint. The stolen session can potentially then be reused to access the account without requiring the attacker to complete MFA again.

“It should be noted that the technique used is particularly common for all email compromise attacks," observes Steven Swift, managing director of security firm Suzu Labs. "Most organizations are vulnerable to this attack, despite having confidence that their MFA will protect them."

However, it will not, because "the point of the attack is to let the user both click on a link and approve the MFA for the link that they just clicked on," Swift tells Dark Reading. "Because the user initiates the activity, everything feels normal from the user's perspective."

And though this type of attack "feels a lot like an [MFA bypass](https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/researchers-voidproxy-phishing-bypass-mfa/760017/) attack," technically, the MFA happens, he says. "It just happens at a point in the attack where it doesn't help," Swift notes.

## Recognizing Suspicious Relationship-Building

Proofpoint expects further attacks using similar impersonation and phishing techniques as TA419's activity becomes more widely understood. Indeed, [China](https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/china-botnets-cyberattacks-covert-networks-advisory/818309/) is known for conducting [cyber-espionage attacks](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/chinese-apts-asian-orgs-high-end-malware) against the US defense and energy industry, as well as foreign-policy makers, Swift observes. Going after AI policymakers appears to be "simply a logical extension of existing behavior," he says.

"That they're now also including AI policymakers is simply a reflection of where the industry is at. AI security overlaps meaningfully with national security, and it's only logical that state-sponsored groups are now including AI in the scope of their activities," Swift says. "We should expect [this activity](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/china-nexus-actor-us-researchers-undetected) to continue if not escalate, as AI continues to further integrate and mature."

The campaign also highlights why defending against [targeted cyber espionage](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/eu-sanctions-companies-china-iran-cyberattacks) requires more than teaching employees how to recognize a phishing page or suspicious email. In this case, the phishing attempt came after the attackers spent time establishing what appeared to be a legitimate professional relationship.

"Individual targets in scope of TA419 activity should treat unsolicited subject-matter outreach as a plausible pretext stage and seek to verify the legitimacy of such unexpected communications via another independent medium," the Proofpoint researchers wrote.

Organizations also should consider phishing-resistant, origin-bound authentication such as passkeys, Proofpoint recommended. The lesson for defenders is that the phishing link may be only the final stage of the attack, and the more difficult challenge may be recognizing that an apparently legitimate professional relationship is itself being used as the pretext for credential theft.

Contributing Writer

Elizabeth Montalbano is freelance writer, editor, and journalist with 30 years of professional experience and a master's degree from Arizona State University. Her areas of expertise include enterprise technology, cybersecurity, business, and culture. During her long career, Elizabeth has lived and worked as a full-time journalist in Phoenix, San Francisco, and New York City. She specializes in news coverage and analysis, using her years of experience to look at the current state of cybersecurity with a critical gaze. She currently resides in a village on the southwest coast of Portugal, where in her free time she enjoys surfing, hiking with her dogs, growing plants, and playing and performing as a singer and musician.

title: China urged to build ‘system’ to protect expanding overseas interests
summary: Beijing has been urged to do more to [protect its overseas interests](https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3295830/china-vows-protect-overseas-interests-hurdles-and-uncertainties-mount?module=inline&pgtype=article) with a cal
content:
Beijing has been urged to do more to [protect its overseas interests](https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3295830/china-vows-protect-overseas-interests-hurdles-and-uncertainties-mount?module=inline&pgtype=article) with a call for diplomatic engagement to reshape international rules and deeper security cooperation with other countries.

As China’s expanding global footprint comes under pressure from geopolitics and restrictions from the West, a Chinese analysis posted on the Global Security Research social media account has called for a major shift in strategy.

The author was not identified, but the account regularly posts analysis and commentary on Chinese national security ranging from nuclear issues to supply chains and technological sovereignty.

It called for Beijing to move beyond crisis management and focus instead on prevention and cooperation when it comes to the country’s interests abroad.

“The primary task is to build a systematic, complete and highly coordinated overseas interests security protection system,” said the analysis, which was posted last month.

To do that would require “streamlining responsibilities across diplomacy, commerce, security and military departments to form a unified national approach”, according to the analysis.

A construction project at the Port of Balboa in Panama City. It is one of two ports seized by the Panamanian authorities in February after Hong Kong-based CK Hutchison’s contract to run them was annulled following pressure from the United States. Photo: AFP

It highlighted the need to reshape international rules through diplomatic engagement, urging Beijing to “actively participate in global security governance and improve rule systems in the global investment, trade and maritime fields”.

The analysis also called on Beijing to deepen security cooperation with countries where China has interests – particularly [Belt and Road Initiative](https://www.scmp.com/topics/belt-and-road-initiative?module=inline&pgtype=article) partners – including on law enforcement, counterterrorism and transnational crime.

It said joint working mechanisms should be set up to protect Chinese companies and personnel on the ground.

By the end of last year, more than 50,000 Chinese companies were operating overseas across 190 countries and regions, according to Ministry of Commerce data.

The ministry data showed that China’s cumulative outbound investment has remained in the global top three for the past nine years. Outbound direct investment totalled US$174.38 billion in 2025 – a 7.1 per cent increase from a year earlier.

But as China’s overseas investment has increased, new dangers have emerged beyond the traditional and non-traditional security risks, according to the analysis. They include legal compliance risks, unpredictable policy changes and foreign sanctions, all of which “interweave and amplify each other, making responses increasingly difficult”.

It said “growing politicisation” of Chinese investment was also a concern for Beijing. The analysis said some countries used state power to suppress foreign enterprises and that national security was used as a pretext for protectionism, in an indirect reference to the United States.

all-inclusive edge to stay ahead on China news.

To access our exclusive content you’ll need to subscribe.

Already a subscriber?

LOG IN

“Previously, going overseas mainly meant competing on cost and service,” it said. “Now you also have to guard against major powers flipping the table.”

It comes as Chinese state-owned and private entities increasingly face foreign curbs ranging from export controls to investment screening and financial sanctions targeting Chinese enterprises globally.

In a case earlier this year, Panama [took control of two container ports](https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/article/3344379/panama-orders-control-canal-ports-operated-hong-kong-firm-after-supreme-court-ruling?module=inline&pgtype=article) on the Panama Canal after its Supreme Court annulled contracts that had allowed Hong Kong firm CK Hutchison Holdings to run them, calling them “unconstitutional”. The ruling came after pressure from US President Donald Trump.

03:35

Donald Trump goes light on China on Day 1, except where the Panama Canal is concerned

Beijing has sought to strengthen its legal arsenal to protect its interests overseas, most notably through its 2021 [Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law](https://www.scmp.com/topics/chinas-anti-sanctions-law?module=inline&pgtype=article) which enables authorities to penalise entities that enforce measures deemed harmful to Chinese sovereignty.

[Resource nationalism](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3346717/chinas-supply-chain-meets-wall-african-resource-nationalism?module=inline&pgtype=article) has also been an obstacle for Chinese mining investors. For instance, Indonesia’s 2020 ban on raw nickel exports forced foreign companies to process the metal onshore. That prompted Chinese investors to start scaling back their operations earlier this year and threatening to withdraw from the Indonesian nickel industry due to production quota cuts and foreign exchange controls.

Chinese mining operations face political and legal challenges across Latin America and Africa, while undersea cable projects have encountered resistance on national security grounds in multiple regions.

The US Federal Communications Commission enforces a presumption of denial for cable-landing licences linked to foreign adversaries, effectively blocking Chinese firms from connecting submarine cables to US territory.

The Pacific Light Cable Network – originally planned to link Hong Kong with Los Angeles – had its Hong Kong segment dropped entirely.

China’s vulnerability along key maritime routes was also highlighted in the analysis, which argued that the security of shipping lanes was critical to energy and mineral imports as well as supply chains.

“As Chinese supply chains have globalised, critical components, raw materials and production are now scattered globally,” it said, adding that they were exposed to geopolitical conflict, logistics disruptions and deliberate supply chain ruptures.

The analysis warned that disruption at chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz or the Strait of Malacca could affect China’s economic stability.

“We must strengthen technological support using big data, artificial intelligence and satellite remote sensing to build a global risk monitoring and early warning platform,” it said.

“This will enhance risk identification, assessment and warning capabilities, enabling dynamic monitoring of global hotspots, key projects and critical corridors.”

title: Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70s
summary: ## WAITING FOR MORE: The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite US reassurances * Staff writer, with agencies * * [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.c
content:
## WAITING FOR MORE: The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite US reassurances

*   Staff writer, with agencies

*       *   [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com)
    *   [_![Image 1](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/x.png)_](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Taiwan+receives+first+2+F-16V+Block+70s%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ffront%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F03%2F2003865308)
    *   [_![Image 2](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/facebook.png)_](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ffront%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F03%2F2003865308&t=Taiwan+receives+first+2+F-16V+Block+70s)
    *   [_![Image 3](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/line.png)_](https://lineit.line.me/share/ui?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ffront%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F03%2F2003865308?utm_medium=P&utm_campaign=SHARE&utm_source=LINE)

Taiwan yesterday took delivery of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 jets purchased from the US after years of delays, helping to strengthen an air force that has to scramble almost daily to shadow China’s military.

The aircraft, bearing tail numbers 6727 and 6728, landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County at about noon after departing from Hawaii and making a stop in Guam.

The two fighter jets had been expected to arrive in Taiwan by the end of August, but remained in Hawaii without explanation as US President Donald Trump prepared to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) late last month.

## An F-16V Block 70 fighter jet, one of two delivered to Taiwan from an order of 66 aircraft from the US, arrives at the Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County yesterday.

Photo: Yu Tai-lang, Taipei Times

The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite Washington saying there has been no change in policy.

President William Lai (賴清德) welcomed the arrival of the two aircraft.

“This is an important milestone in strengthening Taiwan’s air defense capabilities. It also demonstrates our resolve to bolster self-defense and ensure peace through strength,” Lai wrote in a social media post.

Lai said it was his administration’s “unwavering” goal to preserve peace in the Taiwan Strait, and that investing in national defense, which increases the cost of invading Taiwan and lowers the risk of miscalculation, helps further that aim.

Air Force Command said in a statement that it would carry out a planned transition training and gradually complete preparations for the new aircraft to ensure that their operational capabilities are brought online in phases.

The F-16V Block 70s would be operated by the 7th Tactical Fighter Wing, which was established on Dec. 1, 2023, it said.

The wing is being organized into operational squadrons in three phases, with air and maintenance personnel being sent to the US in batches for transition training, it said.

Some of the remaining F-16V Block 70s have reached the stage of being ready for delivery, it said, adding that it would continue coordinating with the US program office and managing the delivery and return of the aircraft to Taiwan according to the planned schedule.

Earlier in the day, Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo (顧立雄) told reporters at the Legislative Yuan that “there will be more than two jets delivered this year.”

The delivery dates of subsequent F-16V Block 70s would be determined in coordination with the US, he said.

Asked where the new F-16Vs would be stationed, Koo said that, in line with the military’s strategy, eastern Taiwan would be an important stronghold for preserving combat power. He did not elaborate.

The US approved the sale of 66 F-16Vs and related equipment to Taiwan in 2019 for about US$8 billion. Delivery was expected to begin in 2023 and be completed this year, but delays due to technical issues have pushed the timetable back.

The arrival of the first two aircraft yesterday also came almost exactly a week after Trump met Xi in Washington.

Trump said after meeting Xi in Beijing in May that he was holding a new US$14 billion package for Taiwan in abeyance, although he did approve one worth US$11 billion in December last year.

The F-16Vs have advanced avionics, weapons and radar systems to better counter the Chinese air force, including its stealthy J-20 fighters, though Washington has been unwilling to provide Taiwan its most advanced fighters such as the F-22 or F-35.

An upgrade program for Taiwan’s existing F-16s was completed in 2023.

The US is bound by law to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, but the two have no formal diplomatic relations.

“We continue to stand with friends and allies across the Indo-Pacific to advance our shared prosperity, security and values — that includes Taiwan,” a US Department of State spokesperson said when asked about the new F-16s.

Dozens of locals, some carrying binoculars and telephoto lenses, gathered near the air base’s perimeter fence to watch the highly anticipated arrival of the jets.

Kimi Chi, a salesman from Taichung, had traveled through the night to be able to photograph the aircraft landing in Taitung.

He was philosophical about the delays, saying “good things take time.”

“In terms of hardware capabilities, there will definitely be an improvement,” the 37-year-old told reporters.

“But what we are actually lacking the most right now is pilots. Of course, I hope the government can provide better additional allowances for these military pilots,” he said.

Former air force serviceman Eric Chan, 57, marveled at the improvements made to the F-16 over the past 30 years and said the fighter jets based in Taitung would “play a very important defensive role” against China.

“The threat from the Chinese Communist Party has always been there, so we definitely need to strengthen our defense capabilities,” Chan said.

title: 【袁红冰热点】独家内幕：习近平与太子党刀光剑影的政治搏杀！(视频)  -  内幕 - 李静汝
summary: 【看中国2026年10月12日讯】 （看中国记者李静汝采访报道）据悉，根据海外媒体最近的分析，中共[习近平](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%B9%A0%E8%BF%91%E5%B9%B3)经过十多年的执政与多次人事清洗，认为习近平已成功逐步削弱并瓦解了中共“太子党”（红二代）作为一个独立政治集团的影响力，将大部分红二代边缘化，使他们退出了中共的核心决策层。如何看习近平与中共太子党决裂对中共政权的影响？看中国记者就此采访
content:
【看中国2026年10月12日讯】 （看中国记者李静汝采访报道）据悉，根据海外媒体最近的分析，中共[习近平](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%B9%A0%E8%BF%91%E5%B9%B3)经过十多年的执政与多次人事清洗，认为习近平已成功逐步削弱并瓦解了中共“太子党”（红二代）作为一个独立政治集团的影响力，将大部分红二代边缘化，使他们退出了中共的核心决策层。如何看习近平与中共太子党决裂对中共政权的影响？看中国记者就此采访了旅居澳洲著名法学家、时常披露中共高层动向内幕的袁红冰教授。

## **陈云：太子党是中共长治久安的定海神针**

袁红冰在采访中首先谈到：“所谓中共的红二代，一般是指中共建政之初的军队少将以上、党政系统中的地市厅局级以上官员的子女。当然也有人是企图攀龙附凤，狗尾续貂，把中共县团级以上的建政官员的子女也归类为红二代。

上个世纪也就是二十世纪最后的二十年间，依据陈云等中共顽固派元老的一个信念，也就是权力还是掌握在我们自己子女手中可靠的这种权贵专制的信念，中共组织系统精心筹谋安排中共的红二代进入党政军和经济金融领域的各个要害部门。这就像是一张张开的庞大的蛛网，逐步控制了[中国](https://www.secretchina.com/)重要国家范畴的权力要害的节点。中共的红二代由此形成了具有整体性的统一的一种意志。这种意志曾经是中共暴政维持权力稳定的最后一道政治防线，最后一块政治基石。陈云曾经声称这是我们党的统治的中坚力量，也是我们党长治久安的定海神针。”

## **89六四中太子党密会、确定“杀20万、稳定20年”**

袁红冰披露了中共太子党在89六四期间的密谋所起到的决定性作用。“89六四那场全民反抗运动的最后结局也经典地证明了陈云的判断。89六四运动最终是以一种时代的悲剧落幕。它的主要的政治意志的原因固然是在于当时的中国知识分子，整体上处于改良主义思潮的控制之下，在历史的关键时刻，他们没有勇气和智慧引领全民反抗，走向颠覆中共暴政的人民起义。不过另外一个重要的原因就在于中共的太子党集团整体统一性的政治意志当时发挥出了逆转历史潮流的能量。50多个太子党当时共同开会，提出在天安门广场上‘杀20万人稳定20年’……太子党这样的政治意志最终被[邓小平](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E9%82%93%E5%B0%8F%E5%B9%B3)所接受。‘杀20万稳定20年’的这个罪不容诛的战略成为中共暴政89六四的主导性意志。

[![Image 1](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2024/11-2/p3556881a508884777.jpg)](https://naturexcels.com/language/zh/)

当时这个尽管红二代中也有诸如胡德平、罗点点、马晓丽这样的人格高贵的良知人士。六四运动的风起云涌就是源自中国民间对于大良知者胡耀邦的深切怀念。而罗点点等人更在六四过程中做出过巨大努力，试图阻止中共党卫军对民众的大屠杀。但是他们这些人只能拯救自己的良知。从总体的政治意志的角度来审视，中共太子党构成了最顽固、最冷血凶残也最为阴险狡诈的一支政治能量，在历史的关键时刻维护中共暴政的专制统治的稳定。

回顾历史，斯大林和[毛泽东](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E6%AF%9B%E6%B3%BD%E4%B8%9C)都是基于创建并维护个人的绝对独裁权威的这种逻辑，都在共产党内实施了刀刃向内的大清洗、大整肃。那么不同之处在于斯大林采取的是直接的肉体消灭的方式，对于苏共的高级官员实行大规模的清除，而毛泽东则主要是借助文化大革命的这种政治运动，通过政治迫害、精神摧残而非直接肉体消灭的方式，对背叛他的权威并投靠刘少奇的中共建政一代的官员进行批判斗争。当然这种批判斗争的整个过程是极其残酷，极其冷血的，而且极其违背人性的。正是由于斯大林对于高级官员及其子女亲属的祸连九族的这种大规模的肉体虐杀，使得苏联共产党历史中没有形成红二代或者太子党这种政治族群。

而毛泽东的大清洗的方式则为中共暴政保留了生成太子党的血脉。那么太子党之所以获得强大的政治能量，这也与他们在文化大革命中经历的苦难直接相关。文化大革命初期之时，红二代中爆发出歇斯底里的政治激情，在‘老子革命儿好汉’的这种红色血统论的癫狂之中，太子党形成了一种核心的政治价值观。那么这种价值观可以集中的表述如下，就是继承了红色血统的红二代是天之骄子，他们天命注定要以共产主义之名主宰中国的命运，并索要人类命运的主导权和所有权。中共政权是只属于他们的和他们家族的特权，中共太子党就是要实行国家权力的红二代所有制。

然而毛泽东认为由于由红二代的父兄所组成的中共党政系统的官员和部分的军队官员背叛了他，投靠了刘少奇，因此毛泽东发起以全面摧毁效忠于刘少奇的党政系统为目标的夺权运动。如此一来随着父兄的政治劫难，中共红二代也由天皇贵胄转瞬之间便沦为政治贱民。文化大革命十年，红二代中的绝大多数流落民间，经历了难以计数的苦难，饱尝人间的酸甜苦辣。毛泽东死后，随着一场宫廷政变，中共建政元老群体劫后余生，重返权力中心，红二代的命运也如影随形、鸡犬升天，跟随其父兄再次崛起，重新获得权力贵族的特权。

更重要的支点在于，经过从骄横之气冲天的这种红色贵族血统，到贱民命运之间的这一番跌宕起伏，中共太子党对专制权力的贪恋也得到进一步强化，甚至他们对失去权力的恐惧已经发展到了一种病态的状态。他们普遍意识到，失去权力就将失去一切。正是太子党对他们自己这种宿命逻辑的认知，所以他们才会在89六四过程中发出在天安门广场要‘杀20万人稳定20年’这样丧心病狂的罪恶的叫嚣。89六四之后，邓小平设计出中共权贵资本主义，并实行中共权贵寡头共和专制这种太子党和官二代联手主导的专制体系，其中太子党群体使这个体系的中坚力量，和陈云所谓的定海神针成为政治经济军事和文化的主宰性的意志。”

## **习近平为什么要毁掉他与中共太子党的联盟？**

据悉，有海外媒体分析指，进入2026年，习近平与中共“太子党”的关系进一步疏离……袁红冰对此进一步表示：“习近平踏上中共最高权力之后，他想要步独夫民贼毛泽东的后尘做共产皇帝，实行个人绝对独裁。为了达到这个目的，习近平就首先要废除中共太子党群体和官二代阶层共享专制特权红利的那种中共权贵寡头共和专制的体制，也就是中共自己所谓的集体领导的体制。如此一来，习近平的个人绝对独裁野心，与中共太子党这个维护中共暴政的最后一道防线之间就不可避免的处于白刃不相饶的敌对状态。

习近平借助人类万年历史间规模最庞大、组织最严密的特务系统，以反腐败的名义实施大清洗大整肃。在摧毁了[江泽民](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E6%B1%9F%E6%B3%BD%E6%B0%91)的上海帮和胡耀邦的团派势力之后，又对太子党群体实施离庭扫雪式的政治经济整肃。中共十九大之后到今天的九年间，习近平逐步从太子党和官二代的各大家族手中夺回了中共庞大的军工体系、银行金融体系、水利电力体系的控制权，更以整肃张又侠作为标志，最终剥夺了太子党家族对中共党卫军的控制权。同时通过摧毁肖建华、吴小晖等一大批中共太子党和官二代家族的白手套，瓦解了中共太子党群体的社会经济基础。中共太子党本就构成了中共暴政的最顽固的统治基石，习近平则渴望回归毛泽东原教旨主义，让自己成为独夫民贼毛泽东2.0，所以习近平与太子党之间的刀光剑影的政治搏杀是两种罪恶之间的你死我活。对此，中共太子党中的一位大哥大式的人物孔丹，曾经痛心疾首的哀叹，习近平的愚蠢胜过谈恋爱中的母猪，他是在自毁他赖以飞黄腾达的政治长城。”

## **中国人将面临如何选择未来生活方式**

袁红冰还就中国未来局势走向表达了自己的看法。“一段时间以来，围绕2027年中共二十一大的人事安排的预判，我们可以看到，中南海听床师们又进入了新一轮的癫狂。他们爆料出一系列的形色各异的所谓中共二十一大领导人的名单。中共暴政可以说是人类历史上狡猾和凶残都大于极致的极权专制。那么中国反抗运动理所当然的要重视同中共暴政之间的认知战、心理战的战略和策略的博弈。但是中南海听床师们爆料的价值取向，显然不能够归类为同中共暴政的认知战、心理战。因为他们喋喋不休、津津乐道的中共二十一大的所谓人事安排，至少在客观上是在向社会大众暗示，中共二十一大之后或者习近平之后，中共暴政还会稳定的持续存在。那么这样的一种论调，显然是在替中共暴政进行精神的维稳。

那么我们可以预判，在习近平已经毁掉了中共太子党整体的统一意志和中共狗官利益分享的中共权贵寡头共和专制体制之后，中共暴政由于丧失了维护中共政治稳定的最后的基石，那么在这种状态下，中共暴政陷于空前大混乱的前景无论进行怎样的人事安排都不可避免。中共的红三代、红四代都是骄奢淫逸的特权温室中养大的红草莓，根本没有能力稳定中共政治经济社会危机叠加的专制统治。当然中共空前大混乱之后，是会像俄罗斯那样陷于又一轮专制的轮回？还是彻底颠覆中共暴政？止终和一切这个专制的逻辑，使中国走向自由民主、实现人民主权，还取决于中国人的群体中是否有潜力再次涌现出辛亥英烈群体那样一代英雄人格、风云际会、慷慨悲歌，愿用生命与祭血为自由中国洗礼。”

## **中共元首外交受挫、未来外交重点？**

据《美国之音》近日报道，美国白宫官员再次强调，[川普](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%B7%9D%E6%99%AE)(特朗普)(Donald Trump)总统将在短时间内就新的对台军售方案做出决定。驻美国台北经济文化代表处(TECRO)代表近日在接《美国之音》专访时表示，川习峰会后，他预期美国将不会改变对台湾的政策。袁红冰对此做出了短评并预测了习近平当局未来外交的可能意图。“不久前举行的《川习会》，川普以超级礼遇的方式接待了习近平。这件事情实际上在国际政治中产生了一系列的效应。但是所有的这些效应都最终证明没有办法改变美国国家意志对于台湾海峡的政治立场。那么此前我们已经讲过，由于美国和中共暴政之间国家战略利益之间的不可调和的冲突，那么美国现在实际上已经形成了一种政治共识，那就是维护台湾独立于中共暴政的存在就是在维护美国根本的国家利益。这样的一种国家利益的形式它主要是通过美国的两个主要政党，以及美国的国会的主体的这个意志表现出来，这不是任何一个美国总统的个人意志可以改变的。

那么在这种情况之下，中共暴政原来试图通过这个所谓的元首外交，想要软化甚至改变美国国家意志在台湾海峡问题上的立场，这种元首外交的努力显然是失败了。但是这并不能改变习近平已经确定的通过发动台海战争、迈出共产极权主义全球扩张的关键一步这样一个基本的战略想定。那么他发动台海战争的时间节点，上次的采访中已经做过分析，在此就不再赘述。

那么面对这样的情况，我想中共暴政一定会在外交受挫的情况下做出下面几个方向的努力。第一，继续强化由中共暴政为核心，由俄罗斯、北韩、巴基斯坦和伊朗共同组成的当代这个邪恶的轴心国集团；第二，就是在俄乌战场上进一步强化对俄罗斯的支持，从而把北约的能量拖在欧洲方向；第三，就是进一步强化对伊朗的全方位的支持。从经济军事到国际政治外交各个方面的全方位的支持，使美国更加长期的陷于伊朗战争的这个困境之中，消耗美国的国家能量，吸引美国的国际政治关注的方向，从而使美国无力或者是弱化对台湾海峡局势的关注；那么第四点就是中共将进一步通过各种隐秘的方式，强化对美国的芬太尼前端产品的输入，试图强化美国国内的社会危机；第五，中共将通过它的长臂管辖和跨境迫害，在美国和西方国家包括台湾在内制造恐怖的气氛，为它发动台海战争创造进一步的条件。”

## **伊朗战争是美国与中共在中东的决战**

据悉，川普(Donald Trump)总统近日排除了在下月初中期选举前对伊朗采取新一轮军事打击的可能性。之前，川普(Donald Trump)曾表示，他下令对伊朗神权统治者采取军事行动。有猜测中期选举后美国会对伊朗神权政权采取彻底的军事行动。袁红冰对此明确认为：“因为在伊朗战争问题上，川普已经多次做出一些表态，然后又收回一些表态。所以很难引起人们的真正的重视。我觉得现在关于伊朗战争，应当重视的是如果美国再次发动对伊朗的军事打击，它会不会改变此前它的战略考量？我们以前说过，美国和伊朗的这场战争，并不是美国和伊朗之间的单打独斗。站在伊朗后面的是一个以中共暴政为核心的包括俄罗斯、北韩、巴基斯坦在内的这个邪恶的轴心国集团。美国实际上是在和中共暴政进行一场在中东的决战。

从另一个角度讲，就是伊朗实际上在相当程度上在为中共暴政打一场代理人战争。所以如果下一次的川普对伊朗的军事行动仍然像以前那样，只把作战的战略安排和策略安排，集中到和伊朗的单打独斗上，那他不可能取得胜利。川普只有做出重大的战略调整，明确地面对伊朗以及站在伊朗背后的这个邪恶的轴心国集团主要是中共暴政，正视这样的一个战略现实，并采取相应的积极主动的军事行动，那么他对伊朗的作战才有可能取得最后的胜利。”

左起：毛泽东、李德、朱德、吴莉莉。（网络图片）

按：延安时**[毛泽东](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E6%AF%9B%E6%B3%BD%E4%B8%9C)**的情人**吴莉莉**嫁给国民党军人张研田，中共篡政后随夫去了台湾。张研田曾任台湾农学院院长，台糖董事长、兼职经济部政务次长，对台湾土地改革有杰出贡献，逝于一九八六年。有关其妻子吴莉莉曾赴延安结识毛泽东的秘闻，张研田留在大陆的长子张依群曾有记述。

我的父亲朱亚英是一个国民党的起义将领，在镇压反革命运动中被定为历史反革命，判处死刑，缓期执行二年。直到“文革”末期，特赦最后一批在押的国民党县团级以上人员时，才把他释放出来，安排在河北省邢台劳改农场就业，月薪三十二元。后来经过我们子女上诉，找到有关证明人作证，在一九八○年北京市中级人民法院重审，认定这是一起错案，恢复了他的起义人员身份，安排在北京市人民委员会任工作员和北京市人民政府的参事，月薪五十六元。

父亲回到北京时，已是一个瞎了一只右眼、半身不遂的七十四岁老人，生活不能自理。当时我们一家三口（我和妻子，一个两岁的儿子）挤在一间九平方米的小屋，实在无法容纳父亲。只好把他安顿在北京东郊管庄的一家农户，答应把他的全部工资交给人家，这家人才肯照料这样一个瘫痪的老人。我又用退还给他的没收财产费（折合人民币二千多元），给他买了一台十四英寸的黑白电视机，供他解闷度日。平时我每周骑车从城里到管庄看望他一次，从家里做些他爱吃的饭菜，如饺子、红烧肉、炸酱面等，给他解解谗，再陪他聊聊天，略尽一点子女的心意。

[![Image 2](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2025/7-29/p3676411a560438137.jpg)](https://www.naturenergy.us/)

## 回忆儿时认识的张伯母

一九八○年十月的一天，我正和父亲一块看电视，一边聊天，他对我述说了一件往事，我终生难忘。

那天正好审判“四人帮”的江青，江青出场后，态度十分嚣张，桀骜不驯。父亲看了，感叹道：“中国落在这么一个女人手里，老百姓不倒霉才怪。要是换了[吴莉莉](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%90%B4%E8%8E%89%E8%8E%89)，中国这段历史可能要重写了。”“爸爸，您说的这话是什么意思？吴莉莉何许人也？她怎么可能改变中国的历史，这不是胡言乱语吗？”

“还记得你张伯母不？”

“记得，当然记的。她不是妹妹的干妈吗？小时候，因为她长得美极了，我们都叫她天下第一美人。”

“她是你妈妈的好朋友，你张伯伯又是我的好朋友。所以咱们两家走得很近。你妹妹小时候长得活泼可爱，她特别喜欢，就收下做了干闺女。你母亲病死后，又是她给我介绍的续弦，也就是你的继母王慧敏。所以你张伯母和咱们家的关系不一般。”

父亲说的张伯母就是吴莉莉，毛泽东的情人。

我的眼前马上显现了张伯母的形象。

张伯母有着中等偏高的身材，皮肤白皙，有对大而有神的眼睛，对人态度冷漠，不大爱说话，她有一头波浪飘逸的卷发，常常穿着一身将校呢的军装：上身是紧身夹克，下身是马裤，足蹬长统马靴，右手食指上晃荡着一个钥匙链，那是她开的吉普车钥匙。那时在众多身穿旗袍、浓妆艳抹的国民党官太太中，她显得“鹤立鸡群”。当时小汽车还很少见，但张伯伯是胡宗南手下中央军校第七分校的政治部主任，自然有办法给她弄来车子。

在她的身上，存在着两种截然相反的东西，常使人迷惑，给我的印象很深。比如说，当时我母亲病重，我们家便由王曲搬到了西安，以便就医。那时我才是个小学二、三年级的学生，父亲却把我送到王曲的国民党军官子弟学校——中正小学住校，这也是张伯母所支持的。

她对父亲说：“亚英兄，你放心。星期天就让孩子来我家过，我给他改善生活。”

张伯母见到我便问：“汉生，学校的生活好不好？吃得怎么样？”

我回答：“一点也不好。吃的是黑面馒头和咸菜，馒头都馊得发酸了；老师动不动就动手打人。”

她一本正经地教训我：“住校就是为了让你从小得到锻炼，能吃苦耐劳，适应集体生活。一个小孩子不能娇生惯养。”

过了没一会儿，她又问我：“汉生，你没发现我们家里有什么变化吗？”

“没有。”

“你看看，我们家屋里全都铺上了地砖，这样就干净漂亮多了，小孩子应该培养观察力，你怎么连这么明显的变化都没发现！”

她对我教育很严；自己却追求生活的舒适和讲究（在抗日战争时期，一般的住房都是土地）。

这就是张伯母的为人。

## 思想激进与史沫特莱去延安

父亲开始和我讲起了张伯母的故事。

张伯母原名叫吴宣晨，也叫吴光伟，吴莉莉是她的艺名。她是北京师范大学外语系的学生，张伯伯叫张研田，是她北师大的同学。

后来，她去美国留学，思想激进，认识了海伦･斯诺和史沫特莱等人。“七七事变”后，她回国参加抗日，就和史沫特莱一起去了延安。在延安时期，她在“鲁艺”自编、自导、自排、自演了高尔基的名著《母亲》，引起了轰动。

后来史沫特莱觉得延安的生活太单调，就建议毛主席在延安推广交谊舞。征得毛同意后，在延安城郊一所废弃的基督教堂里办起了跳舞训练班。老师就是史沫特莱和她的翻译——年轻貌美的吴莉莉，她是一个离过婚的老练演员。

毛主席经常来到史沫特莱的窑洞，在这里史沫特莱对他进行采访。吴莉莉也是须臾不可或缺的翻译。他们一谈就是几个小时，一整天，有时吃饭也在这里。他们海阔天空，无所不谈，从革命、抗日、苏联、美国、德国到浪漫主义的爱情，英国诗人济慈的诗……毛是个诗人，文学家，浪漫主义者。“精神上十分寂寞和孤独”，吴莉莉作为一个外国文学的爱好者，给他介绍和讲解了济慈……

作为翻译和舞伴，她和毛泽东就这样相识了，很快两个人就恋爱了，双双堕入爱河，并且打得火热。

这件事自然瞒不过[贺子珍](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E8%B4%BA%E5%AD%90%E7%8F%8D)的眼睛。有天半夜，毛主席来到吴莉莉的窑洞。贺子珍跟踪而来，这下可捅了大娄子。

据史沫特莱说，她上床睡觉的时间不久，忽然听到隔壁吴莉莉的窑洞门前响起了熟悉的毛的脚步声。接着，像猫一样的尖叫声划破了夜空。史沫特莱冲进了隔壁窑洞，看见毛坐在吴的炕头挡住妻子的拳头。贺子珍站在一边，对毛大叫大喊，毛默默地承受了她一阵子责备，然后给了她一记耳光，要她停止。于是，贺子珍冲向缩在墙角的吴莉莉，一把抓住她的头发，用手指甲抠她的脸。史沫特莱过来干预，贺子珍开始大骂史沫特莱，说她是帝国主义分子，在这个革命根据地败坏了共产主义道德。史沫特莱反驳她，说她不配当中国共产党主席的夫人，并且给了贺子珍一个耳光。这时，还有另一种说法，说愤怒欲狂的贺子珍拔出手枪，要射杀吴和毛（此事只是当事人吴莉莉所说，史沫特莱并未提及，故史料不全，难以确定）。此时史沫特莱指责贺子珍说，你出于疑心和嫉妒而攻击革命领袖，犯下了反革命罪行。最后只好由毛的警卫员把贺子珍强行拉走。一路上都有人偷偷观看，议论纷纷。

 毛泽东和贺子珍因为“吴莉莉事件”，被“精神病”而送往苏联治疗。（网络图片）

## 吴莉莉被送出延安内幕

这件事发生后，毛和贺的婚姻彻底破灭了，很快就把她途经西安送往苏联，治疗“精神病”。吴莉莉也无法再在延安待下去，被强行送往西安……一说法是：[周恩来](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%91%A8%E6%81%A9%E6%9D%A5)怀疑吴莉莉是美国中央情报局派来的战略情报人员，危害极大，就和叶剑英派人强行劫持了吴莉莉，把她送往西安，不让她再和毛见面。吴莉莉到了西安之后，自然受到国民党特务的注意，拘捕了她。但在此时，一直追求她的大学同学张研田，已经当上了胡宗南第七分校的政治部主任。把她救了出来，两个人结了婚。

婚后二人生了一个儿子张小芒和一个女儿张小菲，但感情一直不好，吴莉莉根本不爱张研田。他们的夫妻关系很奇特：虽然在人们面前，夫妻二人卿卿我我，亲密和谐。但是一关上家门，就形同路人，谁也不再理谁。就连张研田在外面终日和两个歌女鬼混，吴莉莉也不闻不问，置若罔闻。

## 吴莉莉一九四九年从成都去台湾

吴莉莉始终不能忘情于毛泽东......竟然泣不成声，连手中的烟卷熄灭了，烟灰跌落在白锻子旗袍上都不知道。后来竟然失声痛哭起来。

一九四九年解放前夕，张研田一家在成都，和张光祖家同住在一个大院里，后来张研田带着两个孩子坐飞机去了台湾，吴莉莉竟然拒绝前往，躲在了好友雷锦章家，张研田到台湾一个月后，有一天，一队国民党士兵突然闯入张光祖和雷锦章的家，从卧室的大衣柜里把吴莉莉揪出来，她虽然竭力挣扎，哭哭啼啼，最终还是被强行拖上汽车带走，送到了台湾。但是，吴莉莉在张家却留下一个手提箱没有被拿走，其中就装着毛写给她的四十多封信件和那本有毛亲笔题词的线装书《聊斋志异》。

毛对吴莉莉是一往情深，可能吴是他一生中最爱的女人......直到康生又给毛介绍江青，取代了吴莉莉，毛的情绪才恢复正常。由此内心中郁结了对周恩来的极端不满，结下了个人恩怨。这也是他不断整治周恩来的原因之一。

......毛专门派人来找张光祖和雷锦章夫妇，把那些书信收走了，并严词警告：“此事不许告诉任何人！”

......我听了父亲的这段述说，当时心中很不以为然。我确信吴莉莉和毛主席谈过恋爱这是事实。但说是因为周恩来把吴赶走，并由此结下毛、周之间的个人恩怨，以至解放后毛不断地整周，我不相信。我认为这件事肯定是党中央的集体决定，而毛批判周，是出于政治观点和政策上的分歧。一个伟大的无产阶级革命家怎能为个人情爱而和亲密战友结下死仇呢？另外，如果假设当初毛泽东和吴莉莉结了婚，吴当了“第一夫人”，就因为她曾留学美国，比较亲美，就会影响到毛主席不会搞亲苏的“一边倒”和抗美援朝运动？简直是荒诞不经。

我当时就和父亲争论起来，说他这完全是唯心史观，世界观没有改造好。

父亲感叹道：“你小孩子，懂得什么？”

“我都三十多岁了，经过这么些年党的教育，我是个马列主义的历史唯物论者。”

父亲苦笑了笑，再没说话。

## 吴莉莉与丈夫张研田的下落

一九九二年，我随中国电视艺术代表团访问台湾，曾讬我在台湾的表弟陈良打听张研田夫妇的下落。在“文革”时期，我有一次在《参考消息》上看到一个消息，提到张研田是当时台湾驻日的“亚东关系协会”理事长。

后来，表弟陈良告诉我：张家人丁凋零。张研田夫妇均已过世，他们的儿子张小芒也死于帕金森病；女儿张小菲现在美国，是一位经营中药材的富商；吴莉莉的死，好像是在毛逝世的前一年，她今天如果还活着，应该有九十六岁了。

回过头来，再看这段历史，不知为什么，我忽然觉得当初父亲的看法，不无道理。

content:
2026年10月9日，在广东省深圳市的一家展厅内，一辆Maextro V800豪华MPV亮着车灯陈列展示。（图片来源：Cheng Xin/Getty Images）

【看中国2026年10月12日讯】（看中国记者李德言综合报导）日前，懂车帝对华为尊界V800做紧急制动测试，发现三辆车的刹车踏板支架都出现断裂，相关视频一度被全网封杀，而中共当局的态度也极度诡异。新疆政府发文《回应产品安全问题能不能说人话》被下架，隔天浙江省政府也发文间接批评华为尊界，同一天，《人民日报》发表题为《四部门联手，对“速成车”说不！》的文章。事件出现再度反转，引发外界对华为乃至[任正非](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%BB%BB%E6%AD%A3%E9%9D%9E)处境的猜测。

## **懂车帝实测[华为](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%8D%8E%E4%B8%BA)尊界视频被封杀**

2026年10月9日，据陆媒快科技、澎湃新闻报导，近日，字节跳动旗下的汽车内容平台“懂车帝”汽车安全内容负责人东门健男带队，对三辆全新的尊界V800做时速100公里至零的紧急制动测试，三辆车的刹车踏板支架都出现断裂，而断裂位置和断口形态也高度相似，其中一辆测试车总里程只有3公里。

10月8日，相关测试视频公开后，引发网络高度关注与持续发酵。10月8日晚9点08分，[尊界](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%B0%8A%E7%95%8C)汽车官方微博发布《关于尊界汽车制动踏板支架底座相关问题的情况说明》，称将进一步对相关部件的设计进行优化，并为已交付的用户提供免费的升级选择。说明中也提到尊界汽车的制动系统按照高于国家及行业标准的要求完成的开发和验证过程，而且自首批车辆交付以来，用户的实际使用中没有发生制动踏板支架底座出现断裂故障的现象。

[![Image 2](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2024/11-2/p3556881a508884777.jpg)](https://naturexcels.com/language/zh/)

但尊界在声明中并没有具体解释三辆测试车接连出现相似断裂的原因，也没有进一步公布调查结果。

据[中国](https://www.secretchina.com/)大陆网络媒体及网友发布的截图显示，10月8日晚9点多，中共党媒新华社曾在微博和公众号转载尊界汽车的情况说明，诡异的是，新华社随后删除了相关内容。也有一些网友表示，才过了一段时间，就无法查看新华社发布的转载内容。

10月8日晚11点，有网友发帖表示，中国大陆哔哩哔哩平台“[懂车帝](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E6%87%82%E8%BD%A6%E5%B8%9D)实测”帐号发布的尊界V800测试主视频，已经无法查看。

10月9日下午，有中国大陆网友表示，懂车帝抖音帐号中的相关视频已打不开，懂车帝自己的App里无法正常播放相关视频。

懂车帝的测试视频在微博、B站和微信视频号等平台被全面封杀。外界质疑，这背后似乎有势力介入，想压下对华为不利的消息，“懂车帝尊界视频已经全网化灰”的词条也冲上了微博热搜。

对此，网友纷纷表示：“真牛啊，不处理问题，先处理视频，下次不会先处理车主吧”；“从另一面证实了，确实质量有问题”；“现在下架视频等于在捂嘴啊”；“脊背发凉”。

而事件又出现反转。

## **新疆政府发文下架 浙江省政府发文再批评**

2026年10月10日，新疆政府新闻办公室官方微信公众号“新疆发布”，发布题为《回应产品安全问题能不能说人话》的文章，称三台崭新的尊界V800，在懂车帝的百公里紧急制动测试中，刹车踏板支架先后出现断裂。尊界回复，测试属于“非标准的极端测试工况”，下一步将优化部件设计、为已交付用户免费升级等说法。

文章指出，“问的是结不结实，答的是‘我合规’。这一问一答之间，隔着的正是公众和这家企业之间全部信任的距离……话说得滴水不漏，唯独不回答你问的那个问题。”“可企业真不会说人话吗？看看他们卖车的时候是怎么说的。”

文章继续批评说：“卖车的时候，全是能听懂的大白话，一个零件恨不得掰开揉碎讲给你听；出事的时候，话锋一转，全成了‘高于国标行标’‘非标准极端工况’。同一拨人，两副面孔，换的不是词汇量，是心态。”

10月10日下午6时左右，这篇文章被“新疆发布”在微信上隐藏。

2026年10月11日，浙江省政府官方公众号发表文章“应对舆情的六个误区”，称“有些企业在产品质量受到公开质疑时，不是认真回应消费者的核心困惑，网上的许多帖子反而消失不见，令人疑窦丛生”。“部分单位问题短板被曝光后，首先想的不是整改问题、回应公众，而是捂盖子、压消息、隐实情”。

文章罕见声称“没有能捂住的事”，越遮掩只会让公信力流失得越快等。

## **中共四部门联手 罕见对[速成车](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E9%80%9F%E6%88%90%E8%BD%A6)集体表态**

10月11日当天，中共党媒《人民日报》也发表题为《四部门联手，对“速成车”说不！》的文章，称这几天，舆论广泛关注尊界V800刹车踏板支架断裂的事件，讨论焦点是汽车尤其是“速成”新能源车的安全问题。

文章表示：“尽管事件有待权威的调查结论，但有一点毋庸置疑：一辆汽车的刹车踏板，绝不应该在驾驶中出现‘断裂’！”“对于消费者而言，车辆可以不具备顶尖的加速性能或智慧配置，但绝不能在关键时刻，在最基础的安全问题上‘掉链子’。”多家陆媒随后也集体转发了这篇文章。

中共党媒舆情的反转引发关注。

其实，早在10月10日，中共工业和信息化部就会同中共公安部、生态环境部、市场监管总局联合发布了征求意见稿《关于进一步加强汽车产品创新设计和研发测试验证有关管理工作的通知》，对汽车制动系统等关键结构件、可靠性与耐久性验证，零重力座椅创新设计和隐藏式门把手等都提出了相关要求。

党媒文章指出，“速成车”是对那些为抢占市场份额、过度压缩研发周期、删减实车验证流程而推出的车型统称。文章引用北京现代总经理李凤刚的说法称：“有的品牌为了追求上市速度，很多该做的实验没有做，消费者成了‘试车员’。”

文章提到：某新能源品牌做新车门把手测试，标称是一万次，而真正拿实物测试的只有两千次，剩下的八千次测试靠电脑模拟。文章指，删减验证科目、跳过验证流程的偷工减料由消费者买单。

文章再举例说，2026年夏，重庆持续出现40℃以上的极端天气，不少某品牌新能源车主发现，车在行驶时出现空气弹簧漏气、车身单侧塌陷情况，导致无法继续开车。

X平台网友对此纷纷留言表示：“四个部门这么快一起发文，看得出来这次是真压不住了。”“从传任老头（任正非）出逃到三个刹车，会不会是组合拳？”“假如国外市场先发现把这个刹车踩断了，那这个事情有多大？”“现在重点不是在国内市场，而是开拓电动车的外销市场。再包庇下去在国际上就太难看了，而且同时间还有马来西亚在行驶中整组后轴连同两颗后轮直接脱落事件，再继续卷价格不顾品质，外国人敢买吗?就算买了，有问题又不召回，到时出事死了人，再一次受到打击，步上机车外销市场的后尘是迟早的。”

## **网友猜测华为尊界事件背后的中共用意**

有网友指出：“4部门的意见稿在10月8日应该都差不多会签完了，不可能是因为这个事临时搞出来的。不要说4个部委完成全流程，这时间连在一个部委送到第一位副部长办公桌上都不够。更大可能是懂车帝提前就知道这份文件。这不奇怪，这文也没什么要保密的，可能早就征求过很多业内人士的意见。这可能也是懂车帝为什么敢发的原因。”“在体制内待过的朋友都知道，多部门联合发文都会花非常多的时间，因为经手的人太多，而且本身效率就不高，往往得几个月以上。这次如此迅速的四部门联合发文，看来这次上面是真的急了，舆论压不下去了！！！”

X平台博主“李承鹏（大眼哥）”发帖表示，人民日报开始批华为了：一辆汽车的刹车踏板，绝不应该在驾驶中出现“断裂"！突然有一种胡雪岩被做空的感觉……

> 人民日报开始批华为了：一辆汽车的刹车踏板，绝不应该在驾驶中出现“断裂"！有的品牌为了追求上市速度，很多该做的实验没有做，消费者成了“试车员”。 突然有一种胡雪岩被做空的感觉…… https://t.co/8yjxbuBKnc
>
> — 李承鹏（大眼哥） (@dayangelcp) [October 11, 2026](https://x.com/dayangelcp/status/2109241457391644909?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

X平台网友表示：“胡雪岩？你还真抬举华为了，胡雪岩何曾助纣为虐过？”“这里面有没有政斗的影子？”“上面不知道放了啥风，各大媒体从来没有过这样的现象，而且没有丢出谁曾经也这样过的论调，这是唱啥戏”？“感觉到暗流涌动”。

## **中共官媒集体转口径 华为与任正非处境引猜测**

2026年10月11日，X平台博主“新高地”发帖评论说：“华为已经出事无疑。前不久，网传华为任正非孟晚舟失联并非空穴来风，他们当时应该正在接受调查，后来看到舆情凶猛，只好放任出来露个脸。任家父女出事是早晚的事，这些年华为贿赂了不少地方官员，东窗事发是必然的。另外，当下各级政府都在打劫富豪，任家显然难以独善其身，他若不积极配合，就必然会查他个底朝天。如今官媒集体对华为速成车开火，只是为下步公布任家罪行作前期铺垫。”

> 新高地评：华为已经出事无疑。前不久，网传华为任正非孟晚舟失联并非空穴来非，他们当时应该正在接受调查，后来看到舆情凶猛，只好放任出来露个脸。
>
> — 新高地 (@5xyxh) [October 11, 2026](https://x.com/5xyxh/status/2109324256832111049?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

2026年9月11日，在中共出入境新规生效前夕，网上一张涉及华为内部对话的聊天截图被广泛传播，内容显示华为董事长梁华自称连续两天无法联络上任正非，因担心任正非或发生意外，因此联络华为副董事长孟晚舟，希望了解情况，但据说任家十多口人疑似同时失联，甚至传出他们可能由海路离开中国的说法。

2026年9月14日，任正非的小女儿、演员姚安娜出席在北京举行的优酷人文《非遗之城．守护季》定档发布会，被指是间接辟谣。

9月20日，网上传出姚安娜在某地片场现身的视频，她声称“收工了回家休息”，并对着视频镜头展示她穿着印有“不信谣不传姚老师”字样的白色T恤。疑似再次进行间接辟谣。

据中国大陆《21世纪经济报导》报导称，2026年9月22日，东风汽车总经理、党委副书记冯长军到深圳，与华为创办人任正非和华为高层代表进行会谈。东风汽车微信公号也发布了任正非与冯长军的合照。

任正非这次公开现身，被指是为关于他们举家逃亡的传闻进行辟谣。

2026年9月23日，旅美独立时评人蔡慎坤发帖说：“全网都在津津有味传任正非举家外逃，各种故事惊悚又刺激，我在视频中就提到这种可能性近乎于零。只是任正非真能忍，憋了11天才露面辟谣，让外网喧闹了半月之久。”

评论区网友热议：“也有可能不是在忍，是这十多天任、孟、余等人都在参加某个闭门会议，出不来。”“事肯定是有事，或大或小而已；跑是跑不掉了，一个都别想！”“有没有一种可能，他是被中共控制了，他们家自己释放谣言，倒逼放人”。

任正非此前全家出逃的说法传得沸沸扬扬，时隔将近一个月，华为尊界V800刹车踏板断裂事件又出现反转，引发外界关注的同时，也有人指出：“以前被抓的谣言难道是遥遥领先的预言？”“从竹知了开始，华为在舆情上好像一直在受挫，应该是有神秘力量在敲打。”

content:
1956年5月，北京街头两位青年人抬着**斯大林**巨幅画像。（图片来源：Pictorial Parade/Archive Photos/Getty Images）

## 百年忧患与俄罗斯的阴影

其实，中国伟大的**三民主义**者[蒋经国](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E8%92%8B%E7%BB%8F%E5%9B%BD)对中国过去100年的历史，以及未来长时期的发展方向，是看得很清楚的。在这里，综合他的有关论述以飨读者。

蒋经国说，目前最重要的敌人，是攫取我们整个大陆的俄国——赤色帝国主义了。林则徐说：“亡中国者，终为[俄罗斯](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%BF%84%E7%BD%97%E6%96%AF)！”这是金石之言！

100年来，我们中国的积弱，固然由于大多数人民失却了“民族自信心”，但重要的，也还是由于列强帝国主义对于我们不断的侵略和压迫——尤其是比邻的日、俄两国，更迭为害。日本没有力量的时候，俄国就来了；俄国打败了，日本又起来；现在日本倒下去了，又成了俄国人的天下。真是“前门拒虎，后门进狼。”日本的田中意一说：“要征服亚洲，必先征服中国。”日本的野心，已由日本人自己的口中说出，这是容易明白的。而俄国人则不同，他们口口声声是“扶植弱小民族”，帮助殖民地民族的解放运动，援助中国革命；其实绝对是口是心非，变相的侵略主义而已。蒋经国从他与其父[蒋介石](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E8%92%8B%E4%BB%8B%E7%9F%B3)有关的部分入手，阐述苏俄对中国侵略的行动和方法，不外运用如下三种方式：一、组织亲俄第五纵队，制造内乱。二、破坏中国与友邦的关系，使中国处于孤立。三、直接明目张胆地用武力来侵略。

[![Image 2](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2024/11-2/p3556881a508884777.jpg)](https://naturexcels.com/language/zh/)

## “联俄”背后的第五纵队

蒋经国说，关于第一点，开始自民国（1921）年，共产国际特派维丁斯基到中国来活动。维丁斯基在上海勾结了陈独秀，创立“马克思主义研究会”，作为苏俄的宣传机关的代理人。民国十年初，又派了赤色职工国际代表李特洛斯克及殖民地问题委员会秘书长马林为代表来华，协助陈独秀筹画党务工作。同年宣布了正式成立“中国共产党”，积极进行苏俄在中国第五纵队的活动。一面马林又到桂林晋谒国民党总理孙中山先生，表示苏俄政府同情中国革命运动，希望与国民党合作。并建议：一、改组中国国民党，联合社会各阶层，尤其是农工大众。二、创办军官学校，以为建立革命武装的基础。三、与中国共产党合作。民国十一（1923）年，中山先生特派廖仲恺先生至日本与苏俄代表会商，结果双方同意，从此国民党就开始与苏俄政府合作。因为这种关系，在民国十二（1924）年八月，其父蒋介石就奉派到莫斯科去考察。经过四个月的考察之后，对于苏俄内部的情况，了如指掌。回国的时候，便秘密向孙中山报告：第一、苏俄的共产主义，实行起来，一定要为害人类；第二、今日的“朋友”苏俄，正是我们未来的最大的“敌人”。当时为着避免和俄国分裂，所以这个报告没有公布。

蒋介石的慧眼，老早就发觉了俄帝的阴谋。

民国十五（1927）年三月二十日，中共党员李之龙，以当时海军局局长的地位，率领中山舰，实行武装叛乱。蒋介石于先期得到报告之后，即以迅雷不及掩耳的手段，将俄共在广州所有的机关，有关工会、农会、乃至苏联顾问住宅，均予派兵监视；俄共的阴谋立归失败，马上对国民党表示让步。同年四月初，蒋介石建议中央：“整军肃党，准期北伐”，以后全国相继实行清党。

但俄共除原有的东方大学、列宁学院及一般军事学校，收容中国左倾青年入学，受布尔塞维克的思想训练之外，并特别在莫斯科创设中山大学，专收中国学生，希图大量地训练和制造各种各式的第五纵队。其对中国的阴谋，无孔不入。

## 一幅画像里的帝国旧梦

俄国对于中国的侵略，到了[斯大林](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E6%96%AF%E5%A4%A7%E6%9E%97)时代，登峰造极。斯大林的侵略主义，是继承俄国的历史传统；他的政策，也可以说，就是执行彼得大帝的政策。什么“社会主义”、“共产主义”、“民族自决”等等的口号，不过是欺人的幌子罢了。

蒋经国举出一个实例：当他于民国二十四（1936）年到莫斯科去看斯大林，谈话完毕出来的时候，他的秘书顺便问蒋经国：“你有几年没有到莫斯科来了，你有什么新的发现？”蒋经国对他说：“我今天下午才到莫斯科，晚上就来看你们；所以我还没有发现什么东西。不过有一件事，我要请教你，1931年，我也在这个地方看见过斯大林，现在办公室的一切，都和从前一样，只有一点不同；从前斯大林的书桌背后，是挂一张列宁站在坦克车上面，号召人民暴动的油画，这次却不见了，换了另外一幅彼得大帝的画像；这就是我今天所发现的新事物。”这个秘书听了笑一笑地说：“当然是新的，此一时，彼一时。”

斯大林跟列宁从事“革命”，把彼得大帝的余孽沙皇尼古拉打倒了；现在他却用彼得大帝的画像，取他自己所崇拜的列宁的画像而代之。这就是正宗的布尔什维克主义的真实内容，这对于他们的马克思主义是何等讽刺！

在中国北伐时期，也就是国共尚在“合作”和国民党“联俄”的时期，张作霖在北京搜查了苏俄大使馆；搜出的秘密文件中，竟发现了莫斯科苏联共产党打电报给当时尚是中国革命政府顾问的鲍罗廷说：“我们的人帮助南方军队北伐，但却不能让南方军队占领全国；我们的目的，是要用这一个军事行动，来牵制其他帝国主义的力量，使他们不能从东方来打苏联。”

这，就是苏联“同情”中国革命和“援助弱小民族自决”的铁证！

抗战时间，苏联也有飞机和“志愿队”派到中国来助战。有一天，驻兰州的俄国飞行队里一个队员，因为多喝了几杯酒，对蒋经国露出真言说：“我们到中国来打仗，最主要的目的，是要找一点日本的新式武器做对象，来练习练习。”他们把中国流血争取独立生存的战争，当作他们练习武器的试验场所。但经过“练习”之后，飞机不来了，坦克也不来了。最后，更把东北接收来的日本的武器交给亲俄派，来打倒中国的国民政府了。

## 雅尔塔的阴影与莫斯科的交锋

民国三十四（1942）年二月，美国因为要苏联参战，提早结束对日战争，罗斯福总统与斯大林订了雅尔塔协定。中国当时为着要打退压境的强敌——日本，只好委曲求全，根据雅尔塔协定，和苏联政府谈判，签订中苏条约。在谈判的时候，美国方面有人主张：“要结束战争，必须苏联参加，要苏联参加，他当然要提出对他有利的条件，等到他提出之后，中国政府应该考虑给他好处。”到了今天，外蒙古、中东铁路、旅顺、大连的军港，乃至整个大陆，苏联都攫取去了。

民国三十四（1942）年，美国还没有把雅尔塔协定公布以前，国民政府派员到莫斯科去进行中苏谈判，蒋经国也参加。这次的交涉，是由当时的行政院长宋子文领导的。到了莫斯科，第一次和斯大林见面，他的态度非常客气；但是到了正式谈判开始的时候，他的狰狞的面目就显露出来了。蒋经国记得非常清楚，当时斯大林拿一张纸向宋子文面前一掷，态度傲慢，举动下流；随着说：“你看过这个东西没有？”宋子文一看，知道是雅尔塔协定，回答说：“我只知道大概的内容。”斯大林又强调说：“你谈问题，是可以的，但只能拿这个东西做根据；这是罗斯福签过字的。”谈判中间，有两点双方争执非常剧烈：第一、根据雅尔塔协定，有所谓“租借”两个字眼。蒋介石给指示：“不能用这两个字，这两个字，是帝国主义侵略他人的一贯用语。”第二、所有问题都可以逐步讨论，但是必须顾到中国的国家主权和领土完整。后来，斯大林同意不用“租借”两字，对于中东铁路、旅顺、大连这些问题，也肯让步；但关于外蒙古的独立问题——实际就是苏联吞并外蒙古的问题，他坚持决不退让。这时蒋介石打电报要蒋经国以个人资格去看斯大林，转告他为什么中国不能让外蒙古独立的道理。蒋经国遂以私人资格去见斯大林，斯大林问他：“你们对外蒙古为什么坚持不让他‘独立’？”蒋经国说：“你应当谅解，我们中国七年抗战，就是为了要把失土收复回来，今天日本还没有赶走，东北、台湾还没有收回，一切失地，都在敌人手中；反而把这样大的一块土地割让出去，岂不失却了抗战的本意？我们的国民一定不会原谅我们，会说我们‘出卖了国土’；在这样情形之下，国民一定会起来反对政府，那我们就无法支持抗战，所以，我们不能同意外蒙古归并给俄国。”斯大林说：“你这段话很有道理，我不是不知道。不过，你要晓得，今天并不是我要你来帮忙，而是你要我来帮忙；倘使你本国有力量，自己可以打日本，我自然不会提出要求。今天，你没有这个力量，还要讲这些话，就等于废话！”

## 外蒙古之争：地图背后的战略算盘

他说话时态度非常倨傲，露骨地表现帝国主义者的真面目。蒋经国也就开门见山地问他说：“你为什么一定要坚持外蒙古‘独立’？外蒙古地方虽大，但人口很少，交通不便，也没有什么出产。”他干脆地说：“老实告诉你，我之所以要外蒙古，完全是站在军事的战略观点而要这块地方的。”他并把地图拿出来，指着说：“倘使有一个军事力量，从外蒙古向苏联进攻，西伯利亚铁路一被切断，俄国就完了。”蒋经国又对他说：“现在你用不着再在军事上有所忧虑，你如果参加对日作战，日本打败之后，他不会再起来；他再也不会有力量占领外蒙古，作为侵略苏联的根据地。你所顾虑从外蒙进攻苏联的，日本以外，只有一个中国；但中国和你订立‘友好条约’，你说25年，我们再加5年，则30年内，中国也不会打你们；即使中国要想攻击你们，也还没有这个力量，你是很明由的。”

斯大林立刻批评蒋经国的话：“你这话说得不对。第一、你说日本打败后，就不会再来占领外蒙古打俄国，一时可能如此，但非永久如此。如果日本打败了，日本这个民族还是要起来的。”蒋经国就追问他说：“为什么呢？”他答道：“天下什么力量都可以消灭，唯有‘民族’的力量是不会消灭的；尤其是像日本这个民族，更不会消灭。”蒋经国又问他：“德国投降了，你占领了一部分；是不是德国还会起来？”他说：“当然也要起来的。”

蒋经国又接着说：“日本即使会起来，也不会这样快；这几年的时间你可以不必防备日本。”他说：“快也好，慢也好，终局总是会起来的；倘使将日本交由美国人管理，五年以后就会起来。”蒋经国说：“给美国人管，五年就会起来；倘使给你来管，又怎样的呢？”他说：“我来管，最多也不过多管五年。”

后来他不耐烦了，直截地表示：“非要把外蒙古拿过来不可！”

谈话一直继续下去，斯大林又很正经地向蒋经国说：“我不把你当做一个外交人员来谈话，我可以告诉你：条约是靠不住的。再则，你还有一个错误；你说，中国没有力量侵略俄国，今天可以讲这话；但是只要你们中国能够统一，比任何国家的进步都要快。”

这的确是斯大林的“肺腑之言”，他所以要侵略我们，还是害怕我们强大起来：因此只顾目的，不择手段，用尽千方百计来压迫、分化和离间中国。

最后，经过许多次的谈判，《中苏友好条约》终于签订了。不过，蒋介石当时对于签订这个条约，有个原则上的指示：“外蒙古允许‘独立’，但一定要注明，必要经过公民投票；并且要根据[三民主义](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%B8%89%E6%B0%91%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89)的原则来投票。”这原则，斯大林总算是同意了。但这个《中苏友好条约》，经俄帝彻底破坏之后，国民政府已经明白宣布其“无效”；依理依法，外蒙古仍然是中华民国领土的一部分。

## 条约成废纸 边疆留伤痕

在雅尔塔协定中，规定东北的行政权及一切主权，都归中华民国政府。可是，苏联的军队来了，一切都等于废纸了。他们向民国政府口口声声称道“友好关系”，可是，日本关东军缴来的武器，就不肯给。经根据条约一再向他们交涉，到他们没有办法抵赖的时候，他们说：“对不起！关东军的武器原来是放在火车站，因为装车装错，运到莫斯科去了。”后来，民国政府去了一个公文质问，他们满不在乎地回一个公文来说：“你们的信，我们收到了；现在根据同盟友好的关系，我们把关东军的武器，交给你们。共计步枪3000枝，马刀148把，东西现存哈尔滨，你们自己去收回。”……

俄国不但要侵略中国，并且时时刻刻企图离间中、美两国的关系。但俄国挑拨离间的卑劣手段，并没有成功。直到今天，台湾不但一贯地维持国际道义，反而更进一步与美国合作无间。

至于俄国人用武力来侵扰中国边境，自满清入关以后，就开始了；直至民国三十六年伊宁事件为止，不知若干次。自1644年起到1949年，俄国掠夺中国边疆的土地，先后共有54次之多。中国领土被占的面积，包括外蒙古在内，共有6578820平方公里，约为我原有领土的1/3；而与我们现有领土1200万平方公里比较，则已有一半的土地被俄国占领去了。这样大的仇恨，中国是永远忘不了的！

蒋介石曾说：“像我们这样4亿5000万人口，1200万方公里土地的国家，无论是跌下去，或是站起来，对于世界人类总是一番大震动。无论是敌人或是友人，都要先看他自己所受的影响，才敢确立他对我们中国的方针。”

蒋氏父子一生，就是为着民族国家的生存，为着维护真理而努力的一生。“汉奸必亡，侵略必败”，是蒋氏父子昭示我们的历史铁则。

title: Lai outlines plans for tougher drug-driving penalties in National Day address - Focus Taiwan

content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) outlined plans Saturday to toughen penalties for drug-impaired driving, as part of a National Day address setting out measures to strengthen public safety and support families.

"The government will strictly enforce the law and show zero tolerance," Lai said in his address outside the Presidential Office.

Under proposed legal amendments, first-time offenders caught driving under the influence of drugs will face fines of up to NT$150,000, while those who refuse roadside testing will face a NT$270,000 fine, he said

Repeat offenders will face unlimited fines, license revocation and vehicle forfeiture. Passengers riding with drug-impaired drivers will also be subject to fines, he said.

The government will step up drug enforcement, strengthen rehabilitation and education, trace drugs to their source, and introduce rapid saliva tests at roadside checks to identify drug-impaired drivers.

On fraud prevention, Lai said the Executive Yuan's anti-fraud command center has become a permanent body, coordinating efforts to disrupt scams, from online advertising to the movement of money.

Turning to Taiwan's declining birthrate, Lai said the government plans to introduce a monthly allowance of NT$5,000 (US$156) starting next year for every child from birth until age 18.

The allowance will be accompanied by expanded childcare services, more family-friendly workplaces and housing assistance, he added.

"Families should not have to raise children all on their own. To support a family is to safeguard Taiwan's future," Lai said.

Through the Healthy Taiwan initiative, the government will seek to help people live healthier lives, he said, highlighting cancer screening and in-home care as well as improvements in working conditions for medical staff.

The Long-term Care 3.0 plan launched this year is intended to bring medical and community services together so older people can receive care in familiar surroundings, while easing pressure on family caregivers, he said.

On housing, Lai said the government will continue its program supporting 1 million renter households by expanding supply and providing rental assistance.

A larger proportion of social housing will be reserved for newlyweds and families with young children, and the government will raise the amount those families can borrow under the Preferential Housing Loans for the Youth 3.0 program, he said.

Lai pledged to advance gender equality, noting that Taiwan was the first country in Asia to legalize same-sex marriage. No one should be excluded because of gender, ethnicity, background or identity, he said.

He celebrated Taiwan's athletes at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, thanking them for showing the world the country's resilience and pride.

Lai praised Yu Kai-wen (余凱文) and Huang Shih-yuan (黃詩媛) for winning Taiwan's first gold medal of the Games in soft tennis mixed doubles.

He highlighted swimmer Wang Kuan-hung's (王冠閎) gold, Taiwan's first Asian Games swimming gold medal in 28 years, and high jumper Fu Chao-hsuan's (傅兆玄) victory, the nation's first men's athletics gold at the Games in 60 years.

Boxer Lin Yu-ting's (林郁婷) second consecutive Asian Games gold and Taiwan's gold-silver sweep in women's tennis doubles were among the other achievements Lai praised. Hsieh Su-wei (謝淑薇) and Liang En-shuo (梁恩碩) won gold, while Chan Hao-ching (詹皓晴) and Wu Fang-hsien (吳芳嫺) took silver.

With local elections approaching, Lai urged voters to choose capable leaders and resist threats and inducements. Political competition and differing opinions should not divide Taiwan, he said.

A president's authority comes from the people's trust, he added, noting that his responsibility is to unite their strengths and lead the country forward.

(By Chao Yen-hsiang)
