title: Why the US-China trade truce matters
summary: **NEW YORK —**Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington in September produced no major new agreement. But it did result in an extension of the trade truce that Xi and US President Donald Trump struck in Busan, South Korea, la
content:
**NEW YORK —**Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington in September produced no major new agreement. But it did result in an extension of the trade truce that Xi and US President Donald Trump struck in Busan, South Korea, last October. Instead of expiring on Nov. 10, the truce will expire on Jan. 10, 2027. Though modest, this achievement has given an unstable world economy a reprieve.

The core agreement is simple enough: China will refrain from enforcing the export controls on rare earths and related materials that it unveiled last October, and the United States will refrain from raising tariffs further, holding the overall duty on Chinese goods near the 47 percent level reached in Busan (down from 57 percent beforehand). Both sides have grumbled about compliance, but neither wants the truce to lapse before the presidents meet again, first in Shenzhen in November, then the following month in Miami.

China clearly has a great deal of leverage in dealing with Trump. It accounts for roughly 60–70 percent of global rare-earth mining and 85–90 percent of rare-earth processing (the step that turns mixed ores into the oxides used in many critical technologies). And when it comes to the heavy rare-earth elements, China’s grip is even tighter. Processing of dysprosium and terbium, essential ingredients in electric-vehicle magnets, wind turbines, and missile-guidance systems, is carried out almost exclusively in China.

*   [Quo haec patria tendit?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/quo-haec-patria-tendit/2443321)

On a detailed element-by-element accounting, the US and its allies have meaningful non-Chinese extraction capacity for only seven or eight of the 17 rare earths, but essentially no processing capacity. That could change in the next two years, with the processing figure growing to five elements. The Australian miner Lynas and the US-based MP Materials already ship commercial volumes of lighter elements like neodymium and praseodymium, and within ten years, non-Chinese extraction could cover nearly all light elements and most heavy ones.

But even then, the processing figure may reach only nine elements, with dysprosium and terbium remaining overwhelmingly under Chinese control. While future innovations in processing, or in designing rare earths out of manufactured goods altogether, could alter the picture, such scenarios are harder to predict.

It is also useful to question the belief that “de-risking” from China would leave the US and Europe unambiguously better off. Recent geopolitical developments suggest otherwise. Now that the US no longer wants to be bound by international rules that it considers inconvenient, rare-earth leverage is one of the few remaining restraints on US protectionism and economic warfare.

Since the Trump administration seems oblivious to the cost of tariffs on US households, there is no guarantee that the next round of tariffs would stop at a level Americans can comfortably bear. In fact, by threatening to reduce, but not eliminate, the rare-earth supply, China may be saving Trump from himself, at least in the short term.

The European Union faces a similar situation. It has been more cautious than the US about raising tariffs on Chinese goods, partly because European industry is heavily reliant on Chinese inputs. Although the EU’s own Critical Raw Materials Act targets 40 percent domestic processing by 2030, its auditors reported in February that actual capacity remains near 25 percent. Tellingly, although Japan has spent over a decade and roughly $1.2 billion diversifying away from China since a 2010 rare-earths dispute, its heavy rare-earth imports collapsed by 70–80 percent in early 2026.

Export controls were not invented by the Chinese. The US Commerce Department’s Entity List has grown roughly ninefold over the past decade, to nearly 1,200 entries, while China’s own retaliatory lists have grown only through the occasional addition of a few dozen entities at a time. On this measure, the US and the EU currently maintain considerably longer control lists than China does.

Although export controls are nominally aimed at military applications, the national-security rationale is not always as clean as advertised, and the civilian collateral damage often rivals the intended effect. In the case of the US and Chinese export controls, one unintended consequence has been a reduction in US exports and Chinese imports. This is probably because export controls cut off Chinese customers from US suppliers, who mostly failed to find replacement buyers and instead suffered a loss of revenue, profitability, and employment. Whereas Oxford Economics estimates that export controls cost China a cumulative 0.8 percent of GDP in 2024–26, a 2023 input-output study concludes that the US has, in relative terms, lost more, with Japanese, South Korean, and European firms capturing the resulting market share.

In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, a fragile status quo stabilized by mutual leverage is probably better than unilateral acts of dominance or chaos. If the zero-sum wrangling ultimately inspires a return to multilateral negotiation, so much the better.

title: Songshan: The ups and downs of Taipei's 'other airport' - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) waded into a long-running debate last week with a proposal to close Songshan Airport and build an "AI park" in its place. With the airport's future again under discussion, CNA has compi
content:
Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) waded into a long-running debate last week with a proposal to close Songshan Airport and build an "AI park" in its place.

With the airport's future again under discussion, CNA has compiled a short history of the 90-year-old airport, which, especially in the last half-century, has seen its fortunes rise and fall in response to various events in Taiwan's development.

## Early days

Songshan Airport was opened during Japanese rule in 1936 as Taihoku Airfield, becoming the first airport in Taiwan.

When the Kuomintang (KMT) government relocated to Taiwan in 1949 after losing the Chinese Civil War, it reestablished the airport as Taipei International Airport on April 16, 1950.

Operations at the facility gradually expanded over the following years, eventually handling flights by 14 international airlines.

## Eclipsed by Taoyuan

That began to change in 1979, with the opening of the larger Chiang Kai-shek International Airport (renamed Taoyuan International Airport in 2006) in Taoyuan outside Taipei.

As international flights were gradually relocated, Songshan Airport shifted to focus on domestic flights, while facing a steep decline in passenger volume.

However, after Taiwan's government launched its "open skies" policy in 1987, deregulating the airline industry, Songshan's fortunes were revived, as new carriers opened and domestic flights rapidly expanded.

By 1997, passenger volume at Songshan Airport reached an annual high of 15.39 million people.

## High-speed rail and the decline of domestic air travel

As the 2000s began, several factors -- including airline consolidation, the expansion of the highway system and the opening of Taiwan High Speed Rail -- caused a contraction in domestic air travel.

In 2002, annual passenger volume at Songshan fell below the 10 million mark, while the opening of Taiwan High Speed Rail in 2007 led to the cancellation of many flight routes across western Taiwan.

The following year, passenger volume at Songshan plummeted to 3.1 million.

## Cross-strait, international flights offer a new lifeline

In 2008, regular weekend charter flights were launched between Taiwan and China, with Songshan being among the airports from which such flights were allowed.

Two years later, in 2010, Songshan Airport announced the launch of direct flights to and from Shanghai's Hongqiao Airport in June, followed by the opening of a direct service to Tokyo Haneda Airport in October.

In recent years, Taiwanese carriers have increasingly utilized Songshan for short-haul flights to destinations such as Japan and South Korea.

As of 2025, total passenger volume at Songshan stood at 5.62 million, with the number of passengers on international and cross-strait flights (3.02 million) exceeding those on domestic flights (2.60 million) for the second consecutive year, Civil Aviation Administration data showed.

Because of its location in central Taipei, Songshan is also frequently used by high-profile visitors to Taiwan, such as the 2022 visit by then-U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and visits by Nvidia founder Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) on his private jet.

## Current status

Supporters of removing Songshan Airport have noted that the airport sits on valuable real estate, and has limited Taipei's growth by forcing building height restrictions to be imposed over large swathes of the city.

In 2022, a Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) candidate running in the by-election for Chiang's old legislative seat attracted attention with a proposal to replace the 213-hectare airport with a giant park.

In a statement on Oct. 8, however, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications defended Songshan Airport as an important hub for international flights connecting Taipei with Seoul, Tokyo and Shanghai, as well as domestic flights from Taipei to eastern Taiwan and outlying islands.

The airport also hosts Air Force deployments and the National Air Service Corps -- a key part of Taiwan's emergency rescue operations -- and thus plays an important role in air transport in Taiwan, the ministry said.

(By Yu Ting-hsuan and Matthew Mazzetta)

title: Alyssa Valdez celebrates PVL decade-long journey amid retirement speculations
summary: **MANILA, Philippines**—Philippine volleyball icon Alyssa Valdez remains thrilled that, years after her career-defining stint with the Ateneo Blue Eagles, she is still playing the sport she loves. On the Premier Volleyball League’s (PVL) 10
content:
**MANILA, Philippines**—Philippine volleyball icon Alyssa Valdez remains thrilled that, years after her career-defining stint with the Ateneo Blue Eagles, she is still playing the sport she loves.

On the Premier Volleyball League’s (PVL) 10th anniversary, Valdez, who has been playing volleyball for nearly 20 years—sees her decade-long involvement in the league as a personal milestone.

“It’s a very, very huge milestone for me because, in my career, I never really thought I would still be playing this long after graduating from college. And I never imagined that I would enjoy and love volleyball this much even after 10 years or more,” she said after Creamline’s win over Akari on Saturday night at the SM Seaside Arena Cebu.

“I think the legacy… what we always practice in our Creamline team… I hope they see that when you enjoy doing what you love, everything will follow naturally—the wins and everything,” she added.

Valdez’s rise to stardom started with Ateneo as she guided the team to consecutive titles in 2014 and 2015, with her explosive back-row attacks and precise cross-court swings soon earning her the nicknames “The Phenom” and “_Bagyong Baldo._”

With over 19,000 spectators showing up for PVL’s opening day, Valdez did not anticipate that the league would fill the arena.

“We were talking about how coach (Sherwin Meneses) said it would be really cold inside tomorrow because it’s a new arena and everything. But when we stepped in, that’s when it sank in for us how many people there were, and how hot it already was. So we’re really overwhelmed too.”

title: Major earthquake destroys buildings, roads in Panama
summary: **PENONOMÉ, Panama**— A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake rocked Panama on Friday, causing buildings and roads to collapse in the center of the country but no immediate reports of casualties. The shallow tremor was felt across the Central A
content:
**PENONOMÉ, Panama**— A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake rocked Panama on Friday, causing buildings and roads to collapse in the center of the country but no immediate reports of casualties.

The shallow tremor was felt across the Central American nation of around 4.5 million people, according to the National Civil Protection System.

It lasted for around a minute.

*   [Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/outrage-over-plan-to-livestream-us-military-firing-squad-execution/2442977)

In Panama City, about 200 kilometers from the epicenter, there were scenes of panic as people rushed to evacuate from the city's emblematic skyscrapers.

"I was scared because the shaking was very strong and prolonged. Heavy objects like dressers, the bed, and all the kitchen items were shaking," Salomon Andion, 46, told AFP after evacuating his 15-story building for the second time following aftershocks.

A video widely shared on social media showed water falling from the rooftop pool of a building that's over 20 stories tall.

Another showed a bridge over the Panama Canal shaking violently but remaining upright as vehicles travelled across it.

"We are facing a major disaster," President Jose Raul Mulino said, adding that some roads had "completely collapsed."

*   ![Image 1: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

"It was horrible, like nothing we ever experienced. My daughter was trapped in school," Juana Alveo, a 38-year-old cashier at a store in the city of Penonome in central Cocle province told AFP.

The US Geological Survey said the quake struck at 1756 GMT with an epicenter 10 kilometers (6 miles) from the small town of Pitaloza Arriba in central Herrera province.

The USGS initially estimated it to be a magnitude-8.0 quake before revising it to 7.7.

A tsunami warming was issued for the eastern Pacific but later lifted.

*   ![Image 2: No first-round bye for projected No. 13 seed Eala at Wuhan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253937.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[No first-round bye for projected No. 13 seed Eala at Wuhan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/sports/no-first-round-bye-for-projected-no-13-seed-eala-at-wuhan/2442979)

The Panama Canal Authority said shipping through the channel, which connects the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, was unaffected and operating "as normal."

Mulino travelled to Penonome to coordinate the disaster response.

Health Minister Fernando Boyd said the most affected areas were the provinces of Herrera and Cocle as well as Los Santos in the southeast.

He said the town of Tonosi in Los Santos was completely cut off.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

"We are trying to figure out how to get there by air, because it's impossible by land," he said.

Panama City's international airport, a major hub for the region, was temporarily closed.

Several flights were diverted to other airports as a precaution, according to the Civil Aeronautics Authority.

The leaders of Colombia, Ecuador and Guatemala all sent messages of solidarity and offers to send aid.

**Over 80 aftershocks**

Earthquakes are rare in Panama and usually occur in the western Chiriqui province, bordering Costa Rica.

Former president Ricardo Martinelli posted pictures on Instagram of his house in the town of Sona in Veraguas province which collapsed.

A church and a hotel in Penonome also suffered extensive damage, images shared on local media showed.

Over 80 aftershocks, one above magnitude 6.0, were recorded by the local geosciences institute.

Writing on X, Mulino called for calm.

"What happened should not be used to generate alarms and disorder," he said, adding that he had called for a report on the damage.

The education ministry announced the suspension of classes in schools nationwide.

The Panamanian quake is at least the fourth quake this year in Latin America surpassing 7.0 in magnitude, after devastating back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela's Guaira in June and a powerful earthquake in western Colombia in August.

title: The Real Reason Xi’s Trump Meeting Was So Short - Domino Theory
summary: Xi Jinping’s (習近平) visit to Washington last month was heavy on pageantry but light on substance. Why? According to conventional wisdom, the reasons were strategic. China wanted time to shore up vulnerabilities in its economy. The U.S. was c
content:
Xi Jinping’s (習近平) visit to Washington last month was heavy on pageantry but light on substance. Why?

According to conventional wisdom, the reasons were strategic. China wanted time to shore up vulnerabilities in its economy. The U.S. was cowed by the threat of another Chinese crackdown on rare earth exports. Combine that with Trump’s emphasis on personal relationships in foreign policy, and a summit devoid of tough conversations on real issues makes sense.

But a string of recent reports suggests that something else might have been going on.

Reporting from Beijing, the South China Morning Post revealed on Tuesday that China’s repeated efforts to plan a more substantive itinerary were rebuffed by U.S. officials.

“Beijing suggested Xi could engage with the American business community and public, pushed to raise dozens of diplomatic and security issues with Trump, and proposed talks on artificial intelligence between Chinese and American executives,” the newspaper [reported](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3369774/beijing-wanted-more-xis-washington-state-visit), citing “people with knowledge of the matter.”

The U.S. side apparently rejected those suggestions, according to the report, arguing that the visit should be equivalent to Trump’s three-day summit in Beijing in May, where the leaders also sipped tea and toured historic sites.

But Dennis Wilder, a former senior U.S. intelligence official, was skeptical. “This SCMPNews story looks fanciful,” he [wrote](https://x.com/dennisw5/status/2107407375900590110) on social media. “I think anonymous sources in Beijing are trying to beat back the stories of Xi’s frailty by claiming he sought a robust US visit. Seems pretty transparently propaganda to me.”

The backstory is this. On Monday last week, The Wall Street Journal published a [story](https://www.wsj.com/world/china/xi-jinping-health-caf250f1) with the headline: “Unusual Rest Breaks for Xi Jinping Sucked Hours Out of Summit With Trump.” According to the article, Beijing requested a private room inside the West Wing for Xi to take rest breaks between events.

That request, along with the Chinese side rejecting a U.S. suggestion that Trump and Xi hold a working lunch, as they had in Beijing, contributed to the summit’s thin schedule. When Trump took Xi to visit the National Archives on the final day of the visit, the Chinese leader only spent about 10 minutes inside, according to the Journal’s sources.

The Journal’s report, like the South China Morning Post one that followed it, was based on unnamed sources. And presumably the information on Xi’s rest breaks came from people on the U.S. side.

But it also quoted Wilder, who said that the hold-room arrangement in the West Wing was unprecedented. Wilder also found the length of substantive discussions during the summit, which totalled only a few hours, unusually brief. “That’s amazingly short for a summit like this,” he said.

Wilder’s suspicion that Chinese officials are using anonymous tips in the South China Morning Post to shape the narrative around Xi comes in the aftermath of a summit that left many observers underwhelmed.

It also sheds light on media coverage of a related issue: Why didn’t Xi give a speech at the United Nations while he was in the U.S.?

Trump addressed the General Assembly on September 22, a day before Xi arrived in Washington. Had Xi come a day earlier, he could easily have delivered a speech of his own.

According to a [report](https://asia.nikkei.com/spotlight/trump-xi-summit/xi-skips-un-address-to-show-china-as-equal-to-rival-us) from Nikkei Asia, Xi chose to skip the U.N. to send a signal that China is the United States’ equal. “Beijing limits leader’s visit to 3 days, mirroring Trump’s trip in May,” the article’s subheadline read.

“According to the Chinese government source, Beijing prioritized sending a message to the rest of the world that China was on an equal footing with the U.S.,” the article read.

It’s not clear how Xi skipping the U.N., where Trump himself gave a speech, signals that China is on an equal footing with the U.S. And if the point is that Xi will only travel to the U.S. for bilateral summits, then it’s hard to explain Trump’s planned visit to Shenzhen for APEC next month.

Let’s review. The South China Morning Post’s Beijing sources say China wanted a much longer trip, but the U.S. side wouldn’t agree. Nikkei Asia’s Beijing sources say China limited the length of the visit to show that Xi is Trump’s equal. One of these anonymous sources isn’t telling the truth.

As for The Wall Street Journal’s reporting, one could argue the Washington sources are playing the same manipulation game they play in Beijing. But it’s hard to ignore the images of Xi walking down the ramp at Joint Base Andrews, holding on for dear life to his wife’s hand.

America is no stranger to aging leaders who stumble around, clearly in the grips of physical decline, yet surrounded by a loyal cadre of advisors who insist nothing is wrong. Look how that turned out.

content:
*   By Hollie Younger / Staff writer

*       *   [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com)
    *   [_![Image 1](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/x.png)_](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Survey+shows+strong+Chinese+support+for+limited+attack+if+Taiwan+declares+independence%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F07%2F2003865564)
    *   [_![Image 2](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/facebook.png)_](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F07%2F2003865564&t=Survey+shows+strong+Chinese+support+for+limited+attack+if+Taiwan+declares+independence)
    *   [_![Image 3](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/line.png)_](https://lineit.line.me/share/ui?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F07%2F2003865564?utm_medium=P&utm_campaign=SHARE&utm_source=LINE)

About 77 percent of Chinese surveyed supported military operations against Kinmen and Lienchiang (Matsu) counties if Taiwan declares independence, the latest China Pulse survey found.

About 24 percent supported a full-scale military attack on Taiwan if it were to declare independence, rising from 21 to 29 percent following the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) in May, China Pulse said in the survey published on Friday last week.

China Pulse publishes a twice-annual survey of Chinese public opinion on international relations conducted by the Carter Center and Emory University in the US.

## Chinese People’s Liberation Army soldiers march with a national flag in an undated photograph.

Photo: Reuters

The latest survey was fielded between April 16 and June 26 — during the Trump-Xi summit in May and ahead of their second meeting of the year last month — gathering responses from 2,500 Chinese across the demographic spectrum.

The proportion of those who oppose the use of force to unify Taiwan "under any circumstances" increased from 32 percent to 40 percent following the summit, it found, although the majority disagreed with that statement.

However, were Taiwan to make an official declaration of independence, 24 percent supported using military force, 59 percent supported a military blockade on commercial shipping and maritime traffic in the Taiwan Strait and 56 percent supported imposing economic sanctions on Taiwan, it found.

A summary for the Carter Center's US-China Perception Monitor publication said that, within China, it is believed that a declaration of independence from Taiwan would amount to an act of war to which Beijing must respond.

However, a narrow majority of 51 percent of respondents believed that the use of force against Taiwan would worsen the issue of cross-strait relations, the survey found.

The most popular non-coercive approach to cross-strait relations was cultural exchange, with an 83 percent support rate, while support for reciprocal economic exchanges increased to 82 percent from 78 percent late last year.

Support for official negotiations on a peaceful agreement increased from 52 percent to 66 percent since the last survey, although support for unilateral concessions decreased from 27 to 15 percent.

The article suggested that the increase may be a reaction to Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun's (鄭麗文) highly publicized visit to China in April, during which she met with Xi in Beijing.

The survey began just four days after her visit concluded, it said.

Meanwhile, Chinese favorability toward Taiwan ranked at 61 out of 100, higher than any other country or region in the survey, including Russia and Singapore, the survey found.

Asked why Taiwan is important, 82 percent said that "both sides of the Strait share the same cultural heritage and are like one family," up from 67 percent in the last survey, while 77 percent said that unification with Taiwan would symbolize resolving a long-standing historical issue.

About 63 percent said Taiwan's strategic location is important for China to break through US strategic containment, 53 percent said the advanced semiconductor industry is important to Beijing's long-term technological development and 48 percent said Taiwan's open and inclusive society would provide China with a "useful reference" for social development, it found.

Belief in the importance of shared cultural heritage seems to have increased since Cheng's visit, while recognition of Taiwan's semiconductor industry rose "significantly" after the Trump-Xi summit for all demographics, except college-educated Chinese, the article said.

The survey "did not reveal a Chinese public eager for a preemptive attack on Taiwan to force unification," it said, although it revealed a widening gap between those who oppose the use of force and those who do not.

For the Chinese public, improvement of cross-strait relations by diplomatic means is possible, but the consequences of any sudden action could be severe due to belief in cultural and historical nationalist positions on Taiwan that are intensifying amid the US-China artificial intelligence race, it said.

apps](https://www.chinatradingdesk.com/post/china-s-new-draft-rules-for-apps-what-they-signal-for-marketing-adtech-and-dsps-in-2026),[China Strengthens Online Protection for Minors.](https://www.chinatradingdesk.com/post/china-strengthens-online-protection-for-minors-what-marketers-need-to-know)

China’s regulation of artificial intelligence is moving further from broad principles towards active, platform-level enforcement.

In our previous article, **“China Strengthens Online Protection for Minors: What Marketers Need to Know,”**we examined how China’s “Clear and Bright” initiatives are placing greater attention on the digital environment surrounding younger users. That campaign addressed harmful content, unsafe online interactions, inappropriate commercial practices, recommendation systems and the effectiveness of minor-protection modes. It also highlighted AI-generated material as an emerging area of concern, particularly where automated content could expose children and teenagers to misleading, disturbing or inappropriate information.

The latest regulatory development extends this broader direction of online governance into AI applications themselves. The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) has moved into the **second phase of its separate “Clean and Clear: Rectifying Disorder in AI Applications” campaign**.

### **From AI System Compliance to AI-Generated Content**

Phase One focused heavily on whether AI platforms and developers had appropriate safeguards in place.

The CAC targeted areas including failure to complete required large-model filings, inadequate safety and content-filtering systems, problematic model-training data, AI data poisoning, insufficient implementation of **AI-generated content identification requirements**, misuse of AI technologies and inadequate security management of open-source models.

By July, authorities reported action against more than **14,000 non-compliant AI products, websites, applications and intelligent agents**, alongside the removal of more than six million pieces of non-compliant information and action against over 26,000 accounts.

Phase Two goes further into the **AI-generated content ecosystem**.

According to the CAC’s September update, more than **5.61 million pieces of illegal or non-compliant information have been removed, over 49,000 accounts have been dealt with and more than 2,400 websites and applications have faced action**during the second phase.

Instead of concentrating mainly on how AI systems are developed, trained and technically governed, regulators are examining how AI is being used to produce false information, low-quality content, synthetic identities, inappropriate material and artificial online engagement.

For global brands, advertisers, agencies and digital marketers operating in China, the campaign provides a clearer picture of how **China AI regulation in 2026**is moving from technical compliance towards the everyday production and distribution of AI-generated content.

### **Seven AI Misuse Categories Targeted in Phase Two**

The CAC has specifically identified **seven forms of inappropriate or non-compliant AI use**under the second phase of the campaign.

**1. Using AI to distort classic works and create “digital swill”**

Authorities are targeting the use of generative AI to substantially alter classic literature, traditional culture, historical figures and well-known entertainment works for attention or traffic.

Examples include changing established characters, inserting vulgar or violent storylines and mass-producing low-quality content with confused logic, little meaningful value or distorted cultural representations.

**2. Creating and distributing false information with AI**

The second category concerns **AI-generated misinformation and synthetic fake content**.

Regulators have taken action against the creation of fabricated disaster scenes and rescue footage, false social news, misleading information around public events and other synthetic content presented as authentic.

The scope also covers misleading use of **AI digital humans**, including synthetic presenters used to make false promotional or commercial claims.

**3. Using AI to impersonate other people**

AI-powered **face swapping, voice cloning and digital impersonation**are another focus.

The campaign targets the unauthorised use of AI to imitate public figures or other individuals, including synthetic images, videos and audio created for misleading communication or commercial purposes.

This means brands using AI avatars, virtual spokespersons or synthetic voices should pay closer attention to authorisation, identity management and the way generated content may be interpreted by audiences.

**4. Producing violent, vulgar or inappropriate AI-generated content**

The CAC is also targeting the mass creation and distribution of AI-generated material containing **violent, frightening, grotesque, vulgar or sexually suggestive elements**.

This applies across formats including images, videos, written content and other synthetic media.

**5. Using AI-generated content in ways that harm minors**

Protection of minors remains a significant component of China’s wider approach to **AI content governance**.

The CAC identified AI-generated depictions of minors involved in situations inconsistent with their age, including pregnancy and fighting, as well as disturbing animations, abusive content and so-called “cult” videos based on characters or imagery familiar to children.

Authorities stated that such content can damage or distort the image of minors and affect their physical and mental wellbeing.

**6. Using AI-managed accounts for fake engagement and “online water army” activities**

Another focus is the use of **AI automation to imitate human social-media activity**.

This includes using AI-managed accounts to simulate real users, automatically operate social accounts, generate comments and interactions, mass-produce repetitive content or artificially influence traffic and online discussion.

**7. Non-compliant AI products, services and applications**

The final category focuses on **AI applications and services themselves**.

Authorities have identified AI agents, applications and services containing pornographic, inappropriate or otherwise harmful content, including information considered harmful to minors.

Where operators refuse to make corrections, measures can include warnings, fines, application removal or closure.

### **Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang and Guangdong Strengthen Local AI Governance**

The second phase is also being implemented through targeted measures by local cyberspace authorities.

**Beijing**has guided online platforms to upgrade their content-review strategies and improve their ability to identify and manage new variations of non-compliant content.

**Shanghai**has instructed platforms to strengthen internal reviews and corrective measures, increase action against illegal content and accounts, and introduce an AI application “knowledge package” to help the public identify potential risks.

**Zhejiang**has adopted a more platform-specific approach, providing tailored compliance guidance to major local platforms, encouraging improvements to internal governance systems and taking action against problematic AI applications.

**Guangdong**has held working meetings with major platforms and conducted targeted corrective supervision of applications with identified compliance issues.

These measures indicate that **AI compliance in China is increasingly being implemented through both national policy and local platform supervision**.

### **Chinese Platforms Are Strengthening AI Content Detection**

Major Chinese digital platforms are also expanding their technical controls.

Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, Tencent, Baidu, Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, Zhihu, Douban and Taobao have been upgrading **multimodal AI detection models**, expanding facial, voiceprint and violation-sample databases and introducing functions such as real-time facial-content governance systems.

Platforms have also published **46 AI governance notices**during the campaign.

Chinese AI platforms including **Doubao, Yuanbao, Qwen and ERNIE**have tightened reviews of source material, restricted prohibited outputs and strengthened implementation of AI-generated and synthetic content identification requirements.

At the application-distribution level, **Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo**have introduced stricter developer admission and application-listing requirements, while conducting inspections and retesting applications already available in their app stores.

### **What China’s AI Regulation Means for Marketers**

For businesses using **generative AI in China marketing**, the latest campaign reinforces the need to consider compliance throughout the entire AI content workflow.

AI-generated images, videos, copy, digital humans and social-media content should be reviewed before publication. Brands should verify factual claims, establish appropriate controls around face and voice generation, monitor AI-generated content labelling requirements and review how automated tools are being used for social engagement.

Protection of minors should also remain part of the approval process, particularly for campaigns distributed through **Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Weibo, WeChat and other Chinese digital platforms**, where content can reach audiences beyond the advertiser’s original targeting assumptions.

The same principle applies to influencer marketing and content automation. Generative AI can improve production efficiency, but mass-generated low-quality content, synthetic engagement and automated account behaviour may create additional compliance concerns.

title: Trump’s Taiwan Arms Calculus: Bargaining with Beijing, Reassuring the Region
summary: The Trump administration's handling of Taiwan arms sales points to a broader shift in the way Washington is managing its China policy. A roughly USD 14 billion package for Taiwan, primarily air-defence systems, missiles and counter-drone ca
content:
The Trump administration's handling of Taiwan arms sales points to a broader shift in the way Washington is managing its China policy. A roughly USD 14 billion package for Taiwan, primarily air-defence systems, missiles and counter-drone capabilities, has reportedly been kept in abeyance, with Trump describing it as a “very good negotiating chip” with Beijing. The message is unmistakable: Taiwan's security assistance is no longer being treated simply as an element of US deterrence policy, but also as an instrument in the wider US-China bargain. That approach may offer Washington tactical leverage. But it also creates strategic uncertainty for Taiwan and, more importantly, for US allies and partners across the Indo-Pacific.

## Taiwan As An Instrument

Congress advanced the roughly USD 14 billion package earlier in 2026, but Trump has yet to give final approval. Following his May summit with Xi Jinping in Beijing, he said the package was being held “in abeyance” and that its fate “depends on China.” He also acknowledged that Taiwan arms sales had been discussed with Xi in considerable detail.

This is significant because it moves beyond the traditional logic of US arms transfers to Taiwan. The Six Assurances, alongside the Taiwan Relations Act, have long provided the framework within which Washington has maintained Taiwan's defensive capacity while avoiding an explicit commitment to Taiwanese independence. Consulting Beijing over the timing or substance of arms deliveries risks giving China a degree of influence over a policy that Washington has historically sought to keep within its own strategic calculus.

> The Six Assurances, alongside the Taiwan Relations Act, have long provided the framework within which Washington has maintained Taiwan's defensive capacity while avoiding an explicit commitment to Taiwanese independence.

The administration has offered more than one explanation for the delay, including the desire to retain leverage with Beijing and pressure on US munitions stocks because of military operations involving Iran. These explanations need not be mutually exclusive. But from the perspective of allies, the important issue is not merely why a particular package is delayed. It is whether future security commitments can similarly become contingent on unrelated negotiations with Beijing.

A previous package of roughly $11 billion was approved in late 2025, underscoring that the administration has not abandoned arms transfers to Taiwan. The question, therefore, is less about an immediate rupture in policy than about the emerging pattern of conditionality.

## The China Arms-Sale Episode

The reported remarks by US Ambassador to China David Perdue add another layer of uncertainty. Last week, following Xi's state visit to Washington, Perdue said on _Fox News_ that Trump had at one point asked Xi whether China would like to buy US weapons, arguing that Washington sells arms to countries around the world. The White House and State Department quickly rejected the suggestion that there was an actual offer or plan to sell weapons to China, pointing to US law prohibiting such sales. Trump himself disputed Perdue's characterisation, suggesting that the ambassador may have been referring to Taiwan and saying that China would probably prefer superior American equipment, while adding that such a sale had not been discussed.

The episode is therefore best understood as a contested account rather than evidence of an actual US plan to arm China. Yet the fact that the remark required such rapid clarification is itself revealing. Strategic signalling is not simply about what governments intend; it is also about what allies and adversaries believe Washington is prepared to contemplate.

## The Alliance Problem

For US allies, Taiwan is not an isolated issue. Japan, Australia, the Philippines and South Korea all have an interest in the credibility of American deterrence in the western Pacific. A conflict over Taiwan would have consequences for regional sea lanes, military deployments, supply chains and the broader balance of power. This makes the handling of Taiwan arms sales a test of alliance confidence.

If Washington can temporarily suspend a major Taiwanese arms package to gain leverage with Beijing, allies will inevitably consider what this means for their own security relationships with the United States. The concern is not necessarily that Washington will abandon Taiwan. Rather, it is that security commitments could become increasingly transactional, with their implementation conditioned by the demands of a larger US-China bargain.

That perception could encourage greater hedging. Japan and Australia may accelerate indigenous defence capabilities; Southeast Asian partners may diversify security relationships; and governments across the region may become more cautious about aligning themselves too closely with Washington during periods of intensified US-China competition.

> The wider US problem of competing munitions demands, from Europe and the Middle East to the Indo-Pacific, only reinforces these pressures.

The practical consequences are also important. Taiwan already faces long delivery timelines for many American systems. Additional delays thus have effects beyond the immediate political signal. They complicate defence planning and force modernisation and the sequencing of military capabilities. The wider US problem of competing munitions demands, from Europe and the Middle East to the Indo-Pacific, only reinforces these pressures.

## Beijing's Opportunity

For China, the episode offers both a diplomatic and informational advantage. Beijing has consistently opposed American arms sales to Taiwan, which it regards as part of its territory, and has sought to constrain or delay such transfers. If Chinese objections can contribute to postponing US weapons deliveries, Beijing gains something more consequential than a single policy concession: evidence that diplomatic engagement with Washington can influence the operational tempo of American support for Taiwan.

Chinese state media has already used Trump's comments to question the reliability of American backing for Taipei. Such narratives serve Beijing's broader objective of persuading Taiwan that dependence on the United States carries risks, and that accommodation with China may ultimately be unavoidable. The strategic question, therefore, is whether Beijing is being given a de facto role in determining the timing of US military assistance to Taiwan. That would represent a significant shift in the regional balance of signalling.

## The Larger Dilemma

The central tension is between transactional diplomacy and strategic consistency. Trump's approach places a premium on using every available instrument-trade, agriculture, aircraft purchases, military sales and diplomatic engagement - to shape Chinese behaviour. From that perspective, delaying Taiwan arms sales can be presented as pragmatic statecraft rather than abandonment.

But deterrence depends not only on capabilities; it depends on expectations. Allies and adversaries must have some confidence that commitments will survive changes in the diplomatic weather. If weapons deliveries to Taiwan become another variable in summit negotiations with Xi, the United States risks creating uncertainty precisely where deterrence requires clarity.

The distinction between a temporary delay and an indefinite freeze is thus crucial. A short postponement linked to logistics, stockpile management or immediate diplomatic circumstances is one thing. A prolonged delay explicitly conditioned on Beijing's satisfaction would send a very different signal.

For Washington's partners, the issue is consequently larger than the USD 14 billion package itself. They will be watching whether the package, or a modified version of it, eventually moves forward, whether the administration continues to reaffirm the Taiwan Relations Act and Six Assurances, and whether future US-China summits produce similar conditionality.

The reported discussion about possible US arms sales to China, even after being denied and disputed, adds to the uncertainty. At a time when the Indo-Pacific is already adjusting to a more contested balance of power, Washington's challenge is not simply to negotiate effectively with Beijing. It is to ensure that the pursuit of a better US-China relationship does not generate doubts among the very partners whose confidence underpins American strategy in Asia.

* * *

content:
这个尾号为0252的美国银行账户并非你想象的那样。

它不属于某个人或某家企业。事实上，账户里的钱不属于任何单一实体。

账户汇集了众多浙江稠州商业银行客户的钱款。这家地区性银行位于中国东部城市义乌。

《纽约时报》对数千份金融文件和银行交易的分析发现，稠州商业银行的客户包括俄罗斯的幌子公司。它们作为规避西方制裁的庞大行动的一部分，已潜入全球金融体系。

稠行提供所谓的代理行服务。这是一种常见的银行业务，允许本地银行无需在海外开设分行，就能为客户提供多种货币的国际服务。

在西方银行不愿服务的地区，许多机构充当中间人，找到了有利可图的业务，稠行便是其中之一。通常，较小的银行会聘用像稠行这样在华尔街大公司拥有代理账户的银行，从而在金融系统中形成一种套娃效应，可以掩盖非法活动。

时报分析显示，自四年前入侵乌克兰以来，寻找并利用代理行系统中的薄弱环节已成为俄罗斯规避美国经济限制努力的重要组成部分。

除了合法客户外，2025年前四个月向俄罗斯出售受限电子产品、工业化学品及其他商品和服务的50多家公司也在稠行持有账户。

时报审阅的许多文件来自 总部位于莫斯科的金融服务公司[A7](https://www.nytimes.com/video/world/europe/100000011077984/how-russia-evades-sanctions.html)。黑客在网上发布了该公司2025年初的大量记录。此外，时报还获取并分析了数千笔商业交易和其他文件，这些来自该公司在网上未受保护的内部数据库。稠行在文件中反复出现，为代理行服务在制裁规避中所起的作用提供了一个详细例证。

A7未回应置评请求。[时报上个月报道](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/24/business/russia-sanctions-evasion-a7.html)，A7通过将资金汇往国外购买商品，帮助俄罗斯企业规避经济限制，通常是通过除了掩盖此类采购外 别无其他目的的空壳公司。

通过一家在稠行持有账户的银行，一家在吉尔吉斯斯坦代表A7工作的空壳公司在此期间进行了超过1000万美元的受限采购。

还有一些俄罗斯公司购买了工业产品，包括可用于制造武器部件的精密磨床。

交易文件显示，2025年1月，一家俄罗斯公司购买了价值7.3万美元的组件，用于制造电子战系统。贸易数据显示，这些部件由一家有向俄罗斯买家销售历史的香港分销商供应。

为完成这笔交易，阿联酋的第一阿布扎比银行安排将资金汇至稠行在美国银行的账户。

按照代理行交易的标准做法，美国银行收到了汇款指令，但不会得到有关采购本身的细节。这使得货物的性质以及买家的身份在交易通过国际银行系统进行时得以被掩盖。

2025年6月，美国银行在没有解释的情况下终止了与稠行的关系，关闭了0252账户。该账户的存在曾在一家吉尔吉斯斯坦银行网站上披露。时报发现，稠行继续通过花旗银行、摩根大通和渣打银行为数十家原本无法直接进入美国金融系统的银行提供美元通道，其中包括与俄罗斯有密切经济联系的国家。

稠行未回应详细的置评请求。9月下旬在迈阿密举行的一次银行业会议上，本报得以面见该行代理行部门的一位经理，对方拒绝置评。

美国银行、花旗集团、渣打银行和第一阿布扎比银行的代表均表示，他们与执法官员和政府密切合作。这些代表补充说，他们的银行定期监控代理行活动，并向当局报告可疑活动，以识别并帮助破坏非法银行网络。

尽管花旗和第一阿布扎比的发言人都表示不会对特定客户置评，但四家银行均强调，他们保持着严格的内部控制，以打击洗钱、制裁规避和其他金融犯罪。摩根大通拒绝置评。

**必不可少的基础设施**

作为国际金融的支柱，代理行系统是一个不透明且陈旧但又必不可少的金融管道。它在使美元成为国际贸易主导货币以及赋予美国在金融交易中无可比拟的影响力方面发挥了至关重要的作用。

其运作方式如下：想象一下，中国农村的一家面料出口商想向海外客户出售商品。对于该出口商，甚至其当地银行来说，在客户可能想要使用的每个国家和每种货币中维护账户是不切实际的。

代理行解决了这个问题。出口商的当地中资银行在少数全球银行持有美元、欧元和其他货币账户。通过这些账户，中资银行获得了这些国际银行的广泛网络，使其客户能够收发国际支付，并将收益兑换成本地货币。

然而，代理行系统本质上会在大银行与试图规避其控制的小公司之间增加距离。大银行通常将客户和交易的审查委托给代理链下游的小银行。

2001年9月11日袭击后为阻断恐怖主义资金渠道而实施了新规，银行随即开始在全球范围内削减代理行关系。

被美国列为支持恐怖主义国家的苏丹受到的打击尤其严重。许多银行停止处理来自该国的付款，引发其被隔绝于全球金融体系之外的担忧，哪怕国民的最基本需求都被迫要转向影子银行网络。

自那以后，监管机构一直试图在制裁规避风险与保持美元在全球使用这一目标之间取得平衡。2016年，美国财政部发布指引称，银行无需逐一审查其代理行客户——也就是所谓“了解你的客户的客户”的原则。

当交易通过美国银行时，美国财政部拥有广泛的管辖权来监管和监督该活动。例如，上个月，美国政府对外国银行实施经济限制，这两家银行利用代理行系统帮助伊朗进入美元体系，以便为伊斯兰革命卫队洗钱和规避制裁。

即使仅作为另一家金融机构的代理行处理受限交易，美国银行也可能面临法律责任。然而，美国财政部对追查哪些案件拥有自由裁量权。

据一位未获授权公开谈论执法程序的前财政部高级官员称，很难想象一家美国银行会因在复杂的制裁规避计划中无意中发挥作用而受到处罚，具体要看非法活动的情节和银行尽职调查的水平。

**一条关键的生命线**

稠州商业银行于1987年在义乌成立，随着这座中国中型贸易城市发展成为向世界各地输送商品的制造业中心而成长。

据时报获得的文件以及代理行合规平台BankCheck的数据，多年来，通过向西方官员认定为洗钱或制裁规避高风险的数十个国家的银行提供代理行服务，这家银行开辟了一个利基市场，这些国家包括阿富汗、也门和南苏丹。

稠行在吉尔吉斯斯坦、格鲁吉亚和乌兹别克斯坦尤其活跃，这些国家与俄罗斯有密切经济联系，已成为改道贸易的重要枢纽。

根据BankCheck数据，稠行为近70家其他银行提供美元账户通道，其中大多数原本无法直接进入美国金融系统。这些银行反过来又向客户推销美元账户。

相比之下，按资产计全球最大的银行中国工商银行为20家银行提供美元通道。BankCheck数据显示，伦敦的汇丰银行仅向其他银行提供七个美元代理账户。

根据一份债券招股说明书，2024年，稠行处理了超过2000亿美元的国际交易，将近其总资产的四倍。但这可能只是其当前活动的一小部分：在上个月迈阿密的金融服务会议上，稠行宣传其与1000多家银行保持着关系，有能力处理27种货币支付。

据[新闻稿](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2024/02/07/major-chinese-bank-halts-all-settlements-with-russia-vedomosti-a84001)和贸易文件，稠行于2024年初停止直接处理与俄罗斯和白俄罗斯银行的交易。但它继续与被视为俄罗斯制裁规避高风险国家的客户和银行合作。

BankCheck数据显示，去年美国银行终止与稠行的关系后不久，这家中国银行在花旗银行和渣打银行开设了两个新的美元账户。

这些账户至今仍正常使用。

title: Philippines opens largest OFW service center in Taipei, eyes expansion - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) The Philippines opened its largest overseas Filipino worker (OFW) service center in Taipei on Sunday, with hopes of establishing two more in central and southern Taiwan over the next two years, according to the country
content:
Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) The Philippines opened its largest overseas Filipino worker (OFW) service center in Taipei on Sunday, with hopes of establishing two more in central and southern Taiwan over the next two years, according to the country's Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA).

Speaking to CNA after the opening ceremony, OWWA Administrator Patricia Yvonne Caunan said the OFW Global Center-Taipei is the third such facility worldwide, following centers in Hong Kong and Kuala Lumpur. It is also the largest to date.

The center is located in the same building as the Manila Economic and Cultural Office (MECO), the Philippines' de facto embassy in Taiwan in the absence of formal diplomatic ties, in Taipei's Neihu District.

It is designed as a one-stop hub where Filipino migrant workers in Taiwan can access government services, welfare assistance and training without returning to the Philippines.

The facility includes training spaces, a café offering free coffee, a karaoke room and areas for government services. Planned activities include Mandarin classes, financial literacy programs, computer and artificial intelligence training, and courses on content creation and entrepreneurship, according to Caunan.

"Skills are the best protection for migrant workers. You can never take away skills," Caunan said, adding that the training can help workers pursue new career opportunities or start businesses after returning to the Philippines.

The administrator also highlighted the emotional challenges faced by migrant workers living away from their families, saying the center will provide counseling and opportunities for social interaction to help address feelings of homesickness.

"Just walk in and make sure that you make yourself comfortable in our café," Caunan said when asked how Filipino migrant workers can access the center's services.

Plans for expansion

Regarding plans to expand the service network in Taiwan, Caunan said the OWWA hopes to establish similar centers in Taichung and Kaohsiung, in central and southern Taiwan, respectively, over the next two years, with feasibility studies underway.

"We don't want our OFWs in Kaohsiung to travel all the way to Taipei just to experience this," Caunan said, adding that the proposed centers will likely be located near MECO's offices in the two cities.

MECO Chairperson Corazon Avecilla-Padiernos said the new center in Taipei reflected the Philippine government's commitment to supporting its citizens overseas.

"Wherever our Filipinos may be, the care and support of our government must remain within their reach," she said in her remarks at the opening ceremony.

OFWs welcome new center

Among those welcoming the center was Geraldine G. Domingo, 54, a Taipei-based caregiver who has worked in Taiwan for 12 years.

"This is very convenient now because everything is here already, what a Filipino overseas worker needs," Domingo said.

She was particularly interested in Mandarin classes to help Filipino workers communicate with Taiwanese employers and friends, and also supported opening centers elsewhere in Taiwan.

Judith Vidal Mendoza, 37, another Taipei-based caregiver who has worked in Taiwan for eight years, said the facility would make Philippine government services more accessible.

"For me, as an OFW, it is very important for us to have access," Mendoza said, referring to document processing services that Filipino workers need while living abroad.

She said migrant workers often have to take time away from their jobs to handle administrative procedures and hoped the center would offer faster document processing and additional services.

Taiwan had around 191,000 Filipino blue-collar migrant workers as of the end of August, including more than 61,000 in Taipei, New Taipei and Taoyuan, three special municipalities in northern Taiwan, according to the Ministry of Labor.

(By Sunny Lai)

Enditem/AW

The FBI has arrested a “Chinese foreign agent” at Los Angeles International Airport accused of spying on the Taiwanese president’s son.

Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, was arrested on Sunday before her planned departure to China, the first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California, Bill Essayli, said in a post on X.

Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with acting as an unregistered foreign agent.

Zhang surveilled Taiwanese President William Lai Ching-te’s son, the FBI said. The agency did not directly name Zhang’s alleged target, but later shared a news article identifying him as Lai Ting-yu.

The US Justice Department said Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the behest of Chinese officials. She sent photos, video and license plate information of the Taiwanese leader’s son and his family to China.

Essayli called Zhang a “Chinese foreign agent” and said she “used tradecraft to avoid detection”.

“She never notified the Attorney General she was acting for a foreign government, a federal offense,” he added.

Essayli said Zhang will appear in a Los Angeles federal court on Monday.

William Lai Ching-te and his Democratic Progressive Party say that [Taiwan](https://www.aljazeera.com/where/taiwan/) is already an independent country separate from China. Beijing views the island as Chinese territory.

Washington does not have ⁠formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but the US is bound by law to provide the island with the means to ‌defend itself.

Earlier this week, the US[delivered](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2/us-delivers-f-16v-fighter-jets-to-taiwan-as-island-eyes-threat-from-china) two F-16V ⁠Block 70 fighter jets to Taiwan as the island seeks to build its defence capabilities to deter a feared attack by [China](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/101-east/2026/8/15/is-china-seeking-to-copy-irans-strait-of-hormuz-blockade-around-taiwan).

title: <div bis_skin_checked='1'>European, Chinese automakers launch product blitz at Paris car show<div bis_skin_checked='1'>
summary: PARIS — European and Chinese automakers were expected to unveil as many as 60 new models at the Paris car show on Monday, as competition for buyers on the continent continues to intensify. The show comes days after the European Union (EU) a
content:
PARIS — European and Chinese automakers were expected to unveil as many as 60 new models at the Paris car show on Monday, as competition for buyers on the continent continues to intensify.

The show comes days after the European Union (EU) announced a deal with China to cut imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc, with a cap of 350,000 units a year, according to a European Commission official on Monday. It is still not clear how the agreement will be implemented, though it was welcomed by the region’s manufacturers.

The flood of hybrid imports into the EU is “not sustainable” for Europe, said Renault CEO Francois Provost, with the current deal “better than a trade war.”

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

Around 20 Chinese brands are attending the show, including BYD and Chery, double their presence at the last Paris car show in 2024 as they face a grueling EV price war and falling sales at home.

Chinese brands have gained share rapidly in Europe in the last three years, while total Chinese exports of hybrids to the EU’s 27-member states tripled to $7.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese customs.

The EU-China deal could hit BYD, Chery, and state-owned SAIC’s MG brand hardest, as between them they accounted for 90 percent of Chinese brand hybrid sales in the EU in the first eight months of 2026, said analysts at Jefferies on Sunday.

Speaking at an event on Sunday evening, Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume welcomed the progress in EU-China talks, adding: “Those who sell here should compete under comparable conditions and create jobs and value here in Europe too.”

The German carmaker’s deliveries fell 14.3 percent in the third quarter, the steepest quarterly drop in four years, dragged down by a further decline in demand in its top market, China, it said on Monday. Deliveries also fell in North America and Western Europe.

*   ![Image 1: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

As part of its bid to regain lost market share in Europe, world No. 4 automaker Stellantis is launching six new models across its European brands at the show and unveiling nine concept cars, a remarkable turnaround after years of maintaining a low-key presence at shows on the continent.

During a high-profile event on Sunday evening, Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa promised attendees they would “witness the reinvention of a European icon,” with an affordable retro electric version of the iconic Citroen 2CV aimed at fending off Chinese competition — which drew huge crowds as the show got underway.

“Our great brands never stand still,” Filosa said.

The company is also learning from the Chinese to go faster, Chief Technology Officer Ned Curic said, outlining plans to build small EVs in Pomigliano, Italy, based on the e-car platform being developed with China’s Leapmotor at Fiat’s plant in Mirafiori, Italy.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

**‘If they drop exports they die’**

Like other Western car shows, Paris had been in decline until Chinese automakers started showing up in Europe in force four years ago.

Alongside the likes of BYD and Chery, this year’s show will feature new Chinese brands like Aito, while state-owned automaker Changan will launch two new brands — Nevo and Avatr.

The EU imposed tariffs on Chinese-made fully electric vehicles in October 2024. The European Commission is also working on legislation that would include “Made in Europe” provisions, mandating minimum local content in EVs to gain access to large parts of the EU’s car market.

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Agreement between France and Germany on the provisions is “imminent,” French President Emmanuel Macron said at the show.

“Preserving this European sovereignty and our capacity to manufacture within Europe is crucial for us,” he said, adding that despite a “difficult” European market, companies on the continent were “innovating, advancing and accelerating.”

Major Chinese automakers have been looking for European production ahead of “Made in Europe,” often in partnership with legacy automakers.

**In July, China’s Geely Auto said it will produce electric SUVs at a Ford Motor factory in Spain.**

Speaking at an event on Sunday evening, Geely Auto CEO Alex Nan emphasized the automaker’s deepening partnership with French automaker Renault and the company’s “commitment to Europe.”

Car sales in China, the world’s largest car market, fell 20 percent in the first half of 2026, increasing the pressure on Chinese automakers to grow sales overseas.

As the US market is effectively closed to China’s auto industry, Europe is the top priority for its automakers.

“If they drop exports in Europe, they die because they can’t make the money elsewhere,” said Francois Roudier, secretary general of the International Organization of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers. REUTERS

title: The not so lost years
summary: **_First of two parts_** THERE is a dearth of detail on the life of the Brains of the Katipunan Emilio Jacinto after his leader, friend and mentor Andres Bonifacio’s death on May 10, 1897. But he left papers that give us an idea of the life
content:
**_First of two parts_**

THERE is a dearth of detail on the life of the Brains of the Katipunan Emilio Jacinto after his leader, friend and mentor Andres Bonifacio’s death on May 10, 1897. But he left papers that give us an idea of the life he led of continued service to the people while apparently pursuing personal happiness.

From his personal papers we found the he was eventually stationed in Santa Cruz, Laguna, where he produced two sets of rules in his own handwriting that may appear odd. One establishes a government in the “Hukuman ng Silangan” (Eastern Area) which places itself under the leadership of the Provisional Constitution of the Philippine Republic attested to at Biak-na-Bato on Nov. 1, 1897. Now this government was of course led by Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo, or Emiliong Matanda (Older Emilio, as opposed to Jacinto, Emiliong Bata or Younger Emilio), the one who approved the sentence of death on Bonifacio. How does this paper tell us that Jacinto submitted himself to Aguinaldo and formed a branch of the latter’s government?

*   [Paper is not proof](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/paper-is-not-proof/2443919)

The other set of rules talked about establishing a People’s Association for Commerce in Santa Cruz, Laguna, where they could put forward agricultural, industrial and commercial interests that could sustain the needs of the people. In the early biographies, details and testimonies are scant about these two movements Jacinto was trying to build, but we may have some clues.

It can be said that he continued to have some fighting men under his command, but whether or not he was under the direct command of or in contact with Aguinaldo is something that cannot be proven in the present. What can be ascertained was that in mid-1897, not Feb. 27, 1898 as some secondary sources say, he was traveling on horseback at night with 20 of his men traversing the fields and the woods when members of the elite light infantry unit of the Spanish colonial army called Cazadores saw them. They clashed and because of the sound of gunfire the horses panicked. Jacinto fell from his horse, was hit by a bullet which shattered the bones of his foot.

He hid in the mud until the morning when he decided to let himself be carried away by the river, and by the afternoon, tired, hungry and suffering pain because of his wounds, he began crying for help. An old man saw him and went to the town center to tell a Spanish lieutenant, who then went out to get him and took him to the convent of Magdalena. They preserved a corner near the stairs of the convent where he was supposedly placed when they arrived.

To avoid detection as he was being interrogated, he produced a cedula or a tax certificate of an undercover he previously killed, Florentino Reyes. He made up a story that he was an escaped captive of the “insurrectionists” as he called them. Because of this, a doctor was sent to him to check him. Fortunately, the initial plan to sever his foot was averted.

While recovering, according to the historian Jim Richardson, Jacinto was in prison in Santa Cruz, Laguna, in a Dec. 21, 1897 report by agent Tito David found in the spy documents of the Cuerpo de Vigilancia, “our forces treated him very well.” He was given a desk job and even lived at the prison. Despite this, he wrote two poems in Spanish “A la Patria,” where he wrote that his “soul’s vehement desire” was to see the land “without the Spanish yoke” (el yugo español). “To relieve, o Patria, your suffering, your sorrows,” he proclaims, “I would gladly give all the blood in my veins....” He signed it with one his pen names, Dimas Ilaw (he who cannot be blinded) followed by his real initials “E.J., 3 October 1897. Sta. Cruz – Laguna – (C.P.),” the C.P. meaning Cárcel Publica or Public Jail. In another poem, “A mi querida madre,” he wrote, “for in my chest a volcano blazed when I saw my Motherland wounded and enslaved, and when I saw her sorrow, I took up arms.” Talk about being careless.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

After some time, Jacinto left the jail house. And when he did, the Spaniards found out right away that they had been duped. He went into hiding in Manila but returned to Laguna after some time. As for the economic society, apparently he became a successful businessman in Laguna, a meat merchant and found time to marry someone. More on this next week. As we can see, Jacinto was an idealist, but when needed, we can also see some sense of practicality and pragmatism in his actions.

VIVANT Energy retail electricity supplier COREnergy has signed a retail electricity supply agreement with Dedon Manufacturing Inc., the Philippine manufacturing arm of one of the world’s leading luxury outdoor furniture brands.

The two-year agreement, covering a contracted capacity of 0.55 megawatts, marks an important first for COREnergy as Dedon is the inaugural customer of the company’s new Sunshine Plan — an innovative electricity solution that combines stable daytime rates backed by solar generation with flexible market pricing during off-peak hours, giving businesses a way to align their electricity costs with how and when they actually operate.

Founded in Germany in 1990, Dedon has built a global reputation for redefining outdoor living through award-winning furniture that combines pioneering material innovation with exceptional craftsmanship.

Just four years after its founding, the company chose Cebu as its manufacturing home, recognizing the island as home to some of the world’s most skilled weavers.

Today, its Cebu production facilities remain at the heart of Dedon’s global operations, producing handcrafted furniture for luxury residences, hotels, resorts, yachts, and hospitality destinations in more than 100 countries.

title: Cheong Wa Dae says Lee ordered rescue operations for Daegu incident while on golf course
summary: SEOUL, Oct. 11 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung was indeed playing golf when a supermarket ceiling collapsed in the southeastern city of Daegu over the weekend, his office confirmed Sunday, while insisting that the president immediately
content:
SEOUL, Oct. 11 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung was indeed playing golf when a supermarket ceiling collapsed in the southeastern city of Daegu over the weekend, his office confirmed Sunday, while insisting that the president immediately ordered rescue operations after receiving updates on-site.

Cheong Wa Dae took an unusual step of proactively confirming Lee's out-of-office schedule after Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) earlier announced plans to hold a press conference to reveal that Lee had been on the links during the incident.

Large sections of ceiling finish material collapsed on the second floor of a four-story building in Daegu on Saturday morning, injuring 38.

In a statement, Cheong Wa Dae said Lee visited Taeneung Country Club in northern Seoul with his family Saturday and was briefed on the Daegu incident while there.

The presidential office said Lee got on the phone with Kim Jong-cheol, acting chief of the Korean National Police Agency, and received "detailed updates" on casualties and damage.

"President Lee then instructed relevant agencies to deploy all available resources for rescue efforts and ensure swift and safe recovery measures," Cheong Wa Dae added, indicating that Lee's outing at the golf course did not prevent him from performing his duties as head of state.

The announcement by the presidential office appears to be a preemptive response against what it regards as a politically charged attack linking Lee's golf outing to an incident that caused multiple injuries.

Cheong Wa Dae apparently sees practicing golf serves a diplomatic purpose since Lee may play a round with U.S. President Donald Trump, an avid golfer, on the sidelines of the Group of 20 summit in Miami, Florida, in December.

This Oct. 5, 2026, photo shows the presidential office Cheong Wa Dae. (Yonhap)

Sources said some in the presidential office believe legal action must be taken against Joo over security breaches if the lawmaker were to release photos or videos of the president's security detail and official vehicles.

"As a rule, we do not confirm the president's undisclosed or private weekend activities, but we are making an exception this time to prevent an unnecessary controversy," Cheong Wa Dae said. "We express regret over attempts to exploit the president's private schedule for a political battle."

At his press conference at the National Assembly, Joo claimed that Lee left the golf course at 4:49 p.m. Saturday and described his outing as "an imperial round of golf."

Joo demanded a minute-by-minute account of Lee's response to the incident and called on the presidential office to explain how Lee's round was funded.

"They only begrudgingly admitted to the golf outing only 10 minutes before my press conference because I had secured photos," Joo said while demanding an apology from Lee and a special investigation into the situation.

The ruling Democratic Party (DP) dismissed Joo's allegations as "irresponsible political maneuvering."

"As the presidential office said, President Lee took immediate measures to fulfill his duty to protect citizens' lives," DP spokesperson Cho Gye-won said in a statement, adding that playing golf was part of Lee's preparation for a round with Trump.
(END)

summary: For most of Gabe Norwood’s adult life, basketball dictated the rhythm of his world: practices, games, flights, seasons, championships, losses and the constant preparation that comes with being a professional athlete. For his wife, Lei, it m
content:
For most of Gabe Norwood’s adult life, basketball dictated the rhythm of his world: practices, games, flights, seasons, championships, losses and the constant preparation that comes with being a professional athlete. For his wife, Lei, it meant building a life around that rhythm too.

Now, with Gabe’s retirement from the Philippine Basketball Association (PBA), the Norwoods are entering a season unlike any they have had before. Their schedule is different, their priorities are shifting, and for the first time in years, they have more freedom to decide what comes next.

“It feels exciting, unfamiliar, and a little surreal all at once,” Lei says. “Basketball dictated so much of the rhythm of our lives for so many years. Now there’s a little more freedom to ask, ‘What do we want this next chapter to look like?’ Not just for Gabe, but for all of us.”

*   [Diplomats, public servants honored at Asia’s Modern Hero Awards 2026](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/the-sunday-times/filipino-champions/diplomats-public-servants-honored-at-asias-modern-hero-awards-2026/2443069)

For Gabe, the transition does not mean leaving basketball behind. The game has been part of his life for as long as he can remember, and his connection to it reaches beyond his years as a player.

“The playing part ended,” he says. “The relationships, the lessons, the love for the game, those don’t end.”
