content: 茉莉花深度报道 文 / 魏臻 国际事务撰稿人 英国军情五处9月30日第一次独立公开发布间谍活动警报，点名中国通用技术研究院替中国国家安全部资助学术研究，100多名与英国有联系的学者参与过它资助的项目。从这一天起，还和这家机构合作的英国学者再也不能说自己不知道它和国家安全部的关系；按《2023年国家安全法》第3条，理应知道也可能构成犯罪。 9月30日，英国军情五处发布了一份“间谍活动警报”，点名中国通用技术研究院。警报说，这家机构与中国国家安全部有“非常密切的联系”，它的主要目的是资助能直接提升国家安全部间谍技术能力的学术研究；100多名与英国有联系的学者参与过国家安全部通过它资助的项目，涉及人工智能、网络安全、隐蔽通信和隐写术，其中一些人可能并不知道这家机构在项目中的角色。这是军情五处第一次独立公开发布警报。这份警报对还在和这家机构合作的英国学者意味着什么？ 答案是：从警报公开那一天起，他们再也不能说自己不知道这家机构和国家安全部的关系。军情五处在警报里专门提醒大学和研究人员注意英国《2023年国家安全法》第3条。按这一条，一个人的行为可能实质性地协助外国情报机构开展与英国有关的活动，而他知道、或者根据他所知的其他情况理应知道这一点，就构成犯罪，最高可判14年。BBC中文网指出，这意味着没有立即采取行动的英国学者，最终可能触犯法律。 一家关系被刻意模糊的出资方 军情五处说，许多学术机构和个人是“出于善意”与这家机构合作的，因为它和国家安全部的联系被刻意弄得模糊不清。中国通用技术研究院和中国国家自然科学基金委员会从2015年起共同设立联合基金，这个联合基金2026年仍在发布项目指南；基金说明称，它要重点解决中国通用技术研究院“在服务国家、履行职能中的”重大科学问题和关键技术问题。 英国《每日电讯报》查明，剑桥大学生物物理学教授米凯莱·文德鲁斯科洛（Michele Vendruscolo）参与的一项2024年发表的研究，得到过这个联合基金的资助；文德鲁斯科洛对该报说，他本人和剑桥大学都没有拿到这笔钱，那项研究也不涉及情报、安全、人工智能、网络安全或隐蔽通信。这类资助可以经由国家自然科学基金的联合基金发出。军情五处建议学者和中国机构合作时查清最终的资金来源，并“强烈建议”各校立即审查与这家机构正在进行或计划中的合作。负责安全事务的大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）说，他已写信给各大学负责人，要求终止与这家机构的关系。 中国驻英国使馆发言人说，英国情报部门的指责“纯属捕风捉影、无中生有”，并敦促英国情报部门停止散布谣言、破坏中英教育交流和科研合作。 不必再证明中国是“敌人” 《2023年国家安全法》第1至第3部分在2023年12月20日生效。第3条规定，可能构成协助的行为，包括直接或间接提供信息、物品、服务或经济利益。警报还提醒大学注意第17条规定的从外国情报机构获取物质利益罪。这部法已有涉华的判例：在英国替中国监视香港民主派人士的Chi Leung Wai和Chung Biu Yuen，被裁定犯有协助外国情报机构罪，2026年6月被判入狱。 旧法下的一起涉华间谍案没能审下去。2023年3月被捕的克里斯托弗·卡什（Christopher Cash）和克里斯托弗·贝里（Christopher Berry），2024年4月被控违反《1911年官方保密法》，罪名是收集或传递可能对“敌人”有用的信息；2025年9月15日，皇家检控署撤销了指控。检察长帕金森（Stephen Parkinson）说，政府补充提供的证人陈述，没有一份说明中国在案发时对英国国家安全构成威胁。取代旧法的《2023年国家安全法》不再要求证明当事人是在替“敌人”国家工作。两件事都关系到英国人有没有为中国情报机构提供帮助，不同的是，那起案子要先证明中国是敌人，政府拿不出这样的证词；这次警报援引的第3条不问对方是不是敌人，问的是当事人知不知道、该不该知道自己的行为可能协助外国情报机构。 美国起诉个人，荷兰筛查所有人 美国司法部2018年11月1日启动“中国行动计划”。哈佛大学化学教授查尔斯·利伯2021年12月被裁定六项重罪成立，其中两项是就他与武汉理工大学和中国“千人计划”的关系作虚假陈述。据《麻省理工科技评论》2021年12月的统计，在这个计划下被起诉的个人和机构只有约四分之一被定罪；2022年2月23日，美国司法部宣布终止这个计划，主要原因是它被指对华裔进行种族定性。荷兰走的是另一条路：2025年4月公布的《知识安全筛查法》草案，要求接触人工智能、量子、芯片等敏感知识的研究人员和硕士生事先接受政府筛查，预计每年约8000人，荷兰人也在其中；2026年6月，教育部长莱切特致函议会说，大范围筛查不可行，暂不实施。 英国这次两样都没有做。和美国相比，它不必先证明哪一个学者隐瞒了什么；和荷兰相比，它不必去审查每一个研究人员。它点名一家出钱的机构，把查清资金来源的责任交给各校和学者本人。此前的警报，军情五处发给的是议会：2022年1月，它发出干预警报，指李贞驹为中共中央统战部从事政治干预活动，由下议院议长转发给议员，调查权力法庭2024年驳回了她对军情五处的全部诉讼请求；2025年11月，它又向议员发出警报，点名领英上替国家安全部活动的两名猎头。军情五处总监肯·麦卡勒姆在年度威胁评估讲话中说，在秘密技术转移方面，军情五处正在应对接连不断的引诱英国学术专家的企图。 大学的钱和政府自己的名单 从几项统计看，中国仍是英国大学最大的生源国之一，在读人数减少，申请人数增加。英国高等教育统计局的数据显示，2024/25学年在英国高校就读的中国大陆学生有143,200名，比上一学年少约4%，入学新生连续第二年减少；英国大学招生服务中心的数据显示，截至2026年1月，来自中国的本科申请人增加约10%，到34,380人；英国内政部的数据显示，截至2026年6月的一年里，中国公民仍是获批英国学生签证（主申请人）最多的国籍，共86,368份。2024-25年度，国际学生的学费收入占英国高校总收入的23%；英国学生事务办公室说，这一年超过三分之一（35.8%）的英格兰高校出现赤字，预计2025-26年度升到42.7%。情报公司Strider的一份报告说，2020年以来超过5,000名英国研究人员与解放军关联机构合著了超过8,000篇论文。英国大学联合会说，它正在研究这份警报，帮助各校评估对现有和未来合作的影响。 2006/07至2024/25学年进入英国高校的国际新生人数，按来源地：中国新生连续第二年减少 政府自己的做法和警报并不一致。贾维斯此前在下议院说，中国等国家正试图影响英国大学的独立研究；可是2025年生效的外国影响登记计划，加强级至今只列了俄罗斯和伊朗，中国不在其中。德国之声报道，英国政府还批准了中国在伦敦建设其在欧洲最大使馆的计划。在政府的名单上，中国还没有和俄罗斯、伊朗放在同一档；防范中国通用技术研究院，眼下靠的是一份警报和各校自查。 如果警报之后仍有学者继续与这家机构合作，检方却以无法证明当事人理应知道为由不起诉，就说明警报没能让学者失去“不知道”这个理由，本文的判断就错了。接下来有三件事要看。第一，如果英国政府把中国列入外国影响登记计划的加强级，就说明政府在法规上也把中国放到了和俄罗斯、伊朗同一档；如果加强级仍然只有俄罗斯和伊朗，就说明防范中国仍主要靠情报机关的警报和学者自查。第二，如果有学者因警报后继续与这家机构合作而依第3条被起诉，就说明这份警报就是起诉前的告知；如果一直没有人被起诉，就说明警报的作用主要是让各校自己切断合作。第三，如果有英国大学公开宣布终止或审查与这家机构的关系，就说明大学接受了查清资金来源是自己的责任；如果各校都不公开表态，就无法知道警报落实了多少。 军情五处的这份警报，改变的是每一位还在和这家机构合作的英国学者的处境：从9月30日起，他们再也不能说自己不知道这家机构和国家安全部的关系；按第3条，理应知道也可能构成犯罪，最高可判14年。 茉莉花深度报道独立调研、撰写。 参考报道：ICEF Monitor（数据来自英国高等教育统计局）（5月20日） · The Guardian（摄影：Peter Nicholls/Reuters）（9月30日） · The Guardian（摄影：Leon Neal/PA）（9月30日） · BBC中文网（9月30日） · 德国之声中文网（10月1日）

title: In the Online Age, PRC Foreign Intelligence Evolves
summary: Executive Summary: Chinese intelligence efforts are increasingly moving away from human intelligence (HUMINT) collection to digital operations launched from within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The Ministry of State Security (MSS),
content: Executive Summary: Chinese intelligence efforts are increasingly moving away from human intelligence (HUMINT) collection to digital operations launched from within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The Ministry of State Security (MSS), military intelligence, and others have started to employ online recruiting to replace face-to-face contact for foreign assets. Beijing likely adopted the new model in response to the 2018 arrest of Xu Yanjun—the first MSS officer to be tried and convicted in the United States—which highlighted counterintelligence risks facing officers operating outside PRC borders. The MSS is using LinkedIn en masse to recruit and develop assets overseas. These operations frequently involve headhunter-style approaches and commercial pretexts to collect resumes and gather intelligence. Traditional HUMINT remains an important component of MSS tradecraft. MSS agents have started to integrate face-to-face contact in the PRC for managing their overseas contacts while their assets abroad deploy digital tools to facilitate operations. Beijing’s intelligence services are increasingly using massive, scattershot methods amenable to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to recruit foreign sources without sending their own officers abroad. They rely largely but not exclusively on online platforms, commercial consulting arrangements, and third-country intermediaries to identify, assess, and recruit targets, all while reducing the risk of counterintelligence detection. Meanwhile, People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence officers and agents continue to employ traditional face-to-face human intelligence (HUMINT) methods outside of the PRC when they pose a better chance of success. Numerous cases have surfaced in the last few months that indicate the scale and breadth of these espionage efforts. On the digital side, these include the seizure by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) of 13 Internet domains used to target U.S. citizens, including those with security clearances, as well as of additional domains used to target U.S. critical infrastructure (DOJ, June 10 , August 26 ). On the HUMINT side, examples include the DOJ sentencing of a former senior adviser for the Federal Reserve Board of Governors to over three years in prison for “funneling sensitive Federal Reserve information to Chinese spies,” and a former U.S. Army soldier pleading guilty to sending information on U.S. weapon systems to the PRC (DOJ, July 15 , September 16 ; CNBC , September 30).  [1] Beijing may have perceived an inflection point beginning in 2018 when Xu Yanjun (徐延军), the first Ministry of State Security (MSS) officer to be extradited to the United States, was arrested ( Reuters , November 21, 2022; National Security Archive , accessed October 1). With advancements among foreign counterespionage services, the PRC’s intelligence services may have concluded that recruiting and handling assets are best conducted from within the PRC’s borders. Prisoner Exchanges Highlight Risk and Suggest Change Xu Yanjun was convicted in 2021, and his operative, Ji Chaoqun (季超群), was convicted shortly thereafter in 2022 ( CNA , March 9, 2023; Guancha , Nov 28, 2024). In November 2024, however, both men were released and repatriated to the PRC, well before the end of their sentences. This was the first known instance where Beijing negotiated to recover intelligence personnel captured by the United States ( Chicago Tribune , November 27, 2024; VOA Chinese , November 28, 2024) In exchange, Beijing released two U.S. citizens convicted of “espionage” and one under a death sentence for drug trafficking. The lack of evidence from the Chinese side about these cases raises the possibility that Beijing decided to take the three individuals as hostages to trade for their nationals in the United States.  [2] This swap was particularly notable as it marked the return of PRC intelligence personnel apprehended in the United States for the first time.  [3] As far as is publicly known, Beijing had previously eschewed efforts to recover its captured spies. In one prominent case, Chi Mak (麦大志), who ran a highly effective and longstanding technology theft operation in southern California for 20 years before he was apprehended, was ignored after his 2007 conviction. He died there in October 2022 at age 82 ( Substack/HUMINT , November 21, 2025; Sina.com , May 1, 2007).  [4] Commercial Platforms Keep Intelligence Officers at Home Since the U.S.–PRC negotiated swap, PRC intelligence techniques have emphasized technology-enabled recruitment and handling, suggesting that Beijing views prisoner swaps as a tool only to be used on rare occasions. The MSS has developed a workflow that allows officers to remain within the PRC’s borders, mitigating the risk of identification by hostile security services. As noted by the Belgian security service, the recruitment and handling of “individuals of interest” now “is often carried out in China or from China” ( VSSE , January 14, 2025). Five Eyes nation assessments covering cases across North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific between 2019–2026 describe a similar evolution in intelligence operations conducted by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA). Chinese services increasingly conduct spotting and assessment at industrial scale through LinkedIn and other professional networking platforms, encourage targets to undertake seemingly legitimate paid consulting work as an initial step, and employ third-country and private-sector intermediaries as operational cut-outs. In this form, they have adopted the semiconductor industry’s commercial talent-recruitment model ( Five Eyes , March 6). The U.K. Security Service (MI5) has separately and specifically attributed comparable LinkedIn headhunter-style tradecraft—including two accounts identified as “Amanda Qiu” and “Shirly Shen”—to the MSS itself, indicating the online-recruitment shift spans both the civilian and military intelligence services rather than being unique to either ( BBC , November 18, 2025). The recruitment of former CIA and Defence Intelligence Agency officer Kevin Mallory in 2017 by the MSS was a precursor. Mallory, who was in financial difficulty, was approached on LinkedIn by a contact posing as a representative of the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences—a think tank with documented ties to Chinese intelligence—and offered a paid “consulting” role. The relationship subsequently developed through in-person meetings in Shanghai rather than the United States ( DOJ , May 17, 2019). Although Mallory was arrested before he could establish a long-term espionage operation, the case appears to have inspired, rather than discouraged, Beijing’s confidence in remote recruitment methods. Security services across Europe report similar patterns. MI5 Director General Ken McCallum disclosed in 2023 that approximately 20,000 Britons had been approached through LinkedIn by Chinese recruiters, more than double the roughly 10,000 users MI5 had said were being targeted online by all foreign intelligence services and criminals two years earlier ( The Guardian , October 18, 2023). The Canadian Security Intelligence Service has separately warned that Chinese intelligence services advertise employment opportunities through front companies, leading applicants to unknowingly work on behalf of a hostile intelligence service. Comparable warnings have also been issued by Germany’s Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV), the Netherlands’ General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD), and Czechia’s Security Information Service (BIS) ( BfV , 2020; AIVD , February 8, 2022; Euronews , September 16, 2024; CSIS Public Report, 2025). Such approaches continued this year, as demonstrated by the 2026 Kevin Zhang/Oriental Consulting operation, which reportedly netted substantial NATO and EU intelligence information ( Hong Kong Free Press , March 28). These industrial-scale approaches are particularly amenable to the deployment of artificial intelligence. AI systems can search and classify large numbers of publicly available professional profiles, identify combinations of access, expertise, foreign travel and possible financial or career vulnerability, and rank prospective targets for human review. Generative AI can then draft individualized approaches in the target’s language, vary the supposed recruiter’s identity and commercial pretext, and sustain preliminary conversations with many candidates simultaneously. The U.K. National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) assesses that AI already provides a “capability uplift” in reconnaissance and social engineering, making both more effective; it also enables more convincing approaches without the linguistic mistakes that traditionally exposed foreign phishing and influence efforts ( NCSC , January 24, 2024). Human Recruiters Remain Valuable Despite this growing reliance on online recruitment—likely enhanced by AI—traditional human intelligence operations have by no means disappeared. Instead, they complement digital approaches and are employed when they present the best chance of success. Two recent cases show how human recruitment is fused with technology-enabled tradecraft. Singaporean academic Dickson Yeo was recruited by Chinese intelligence contacts he met while giving a talk in Beijing, then set up a fictitious political consulting firm and used LinkedIn’s contact-suggestion algorithm to identify and approach potential sources almost daily; he received more than 400 resumes, roughly 90 percent from people with U.S. military or government security clearances, before he was caught ( Straits Times , April 2, 2025). Estonian national Gerli Mutso travelled to the PRC for coordination with PLA intelligence officers who used the cover identity of a fictitious “Beijing Information Association”; she then returned to Europe and recruited Tarmo Kõuts, an Estonian scientist with access to NATO’s Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation, who subsequently supplied classified defense-research material to the PRC. Mutso was convicted in 2022 and sentenced to eight and a half years; Estonia’s Supreme Court upheld her sentence in 2023 while partially annulling other elements of the conviction ( ERR News , June 17, 2023). Even with the shared linguistic background between the PRC and Taiwan, PRC intelligence officers follow a comparable trajectory over time. The Ministry of National Defense (MND) has noted that PRC tradecraft moved from direct in-person contact to introductions via third parties met outside Taiwan, to an increasing recent focus on online recruitment ( CNA , April 22, 2025; MND , April 23, 2025). This suggests the shift toward remote, intermediary-based recruitment is a general trend rather than one confined to harder-target Western countries. Conclusion PRC intelligence officers increasingly direct foreign recruitment from the safety of the PRC, relying on online platforms, commercial intermediaries, and locally based facilitators to conduct much of the initial contact and relationship building that was traditionally done abroad. The result is a model that reduces, but does not necessarily eliminate, operational exposure for Chinese intelligence personnel while allowing recruitment efforts to expand simultaneously, even exponentially, across multiple countries. Notes [1] Other examples include an MI5 warning that over 100 U.K.-linked academics had contributed to research projects funded by the MSS via a proxy ( MI5 , September 30); the arrest by Belgian authorities of both a man suspected of stealing semiconductor technology and an intern at NATO headquarters for spying for the PRC ( CBC , July 29; Reuters , September 7); the arrest by Korean authorities of two PRC citizens accused of intercepting fighter jet communications and reportedly obtaining training materials from U.S. bases ( Korea JoonAng Daily , September 29); the indictment of a man in Taiwan for leaking classified documents to PRC spies, and of another three former military personnel for collecting military secrets since 2020 ( Taipei Times , August 18; Focus Taiwan , October 1); and the sentencing of an Australian businessman for compiling reports for PRC intelligence ( ABC , September 10). [2] Hostage taking is part and parcel of Beijing’s playbook when dealing with foreign governments and institutions ( China Brief , May 11, 2017; Substack/Strategic Narratives , July 31, 2025). [3] The only other known example since the CCP’s 1949 victory was a genuine spy swap in 2015 between the PRC and Taiwan. In an agreement enabled politically by the meeting that November between President Xi Jinping and Taiwan’s then president Ma Ying-jeou (馬英九), the PRC released two Taiwanese military intelligence officers, Colonels Chu Kung-hsun (朱恭訓) and Hsu Chang-kuo (徐章國) in exchange for a Chinese intelligence officer, Li Zhihao (李志豪) ( Taiwan Ministry of National Defense , November 30, 2015; China Taiwan Net , December 1, 2015). [4] Beijing similarly ignored Larry Wu-tai Chin (金无怠) and his wife. Having confessed to the FBI that he had spied for the PRC over the course of four decades, Chin allegedly committed suicide in jail before sentencing ( Sohu.com , August 19, 2024). Years later, unofficial mainland sources began to laud his achievements as a “mole” inside the U.S. Intelligence Community (Red Song Network, January 26, 2018 , October 27, 2025 ; Sina.com , April 8, 2020; Zhihu , March 26, 2024). The post In the Online Age, PRC Foreign Intelligence Evolves appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Taiwan’s First F-16 Block 70s Have Finally Arrived
summary: After nearly seven years of waiting, Taiwan has received the first two aircraft from its long-delayed purchase of 66 new-build F-16C/D Block 70 fighters from the United States. The two single-seat F-16Cs, serials 6727 and 6728, touched down
content: After nearly seven years of waiting, Taiwan has received the first two aircraft from its long-delayed purchase of 66 new-build F-16C/D Block 70 fighters from the United States. The two single-seat F-16Cs, serials 6727 and 6728, touched down at Chihhang Air Base near Taitung on October 2. They are the first factory-new fighter aircraft delivered to Taiwan in 25 years and mark the beginning of the aircraft acceptance and integration phase of the Republic of China Air Force’s (ROCAF) so-called Peace Phoenix Soaring project. The two jets have also had an unusually eventful trip to Taiwan. They began their journey to the island on August 17, flying from Lockheed Martin’s production facility in Greenville, South Carolina, to Hawaii. The aircraft were subsequently forced to remain there for more than a month after an unexpected issue prevented them from continuing across the Pacific as planned. The reasons for the delay have been the subject of considerable speculation, including weather and tanker availability. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6727 arrive in Taitung. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press The two jets finally departed Hawaii again on October 1, stopping in Guam before making the final leg to Taitung today. Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo said today that more of the aircraft will arrive before the end of the year, although he did not provide a specific number. Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70 fighter jets Taiwan took delivery Friday of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 fighter jets purchased from the United States, with the aircraft landing at Chihhang Air Base in the eastern county of Taitung at around noon. pic.twitter.com/hbqdV6io26 — Focus Taiwan (CNA English News) (@Focus_Taiwan) October 2, 2026 The 66-aircraft purchase is worth approximately $8 billion. Taiwan originally expected deliveries to begin much sooner, but production-line adjustments, supply-chain problems, and software issues contributed to delays. COVID, too, had an impact on the production line. The program’s delivery schedule has slipped repeatedly . Defense Minister Koo said in March, May, and again through his deputy in June that the first aircraft were expected to arrive by the end of September. That deadline passed without an F-16 reaching Taiwan. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6727 touches down earlier today. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense acknowledged in late September that development and production of the aircraft’s new electronic warfare self-protection system had also been a factor. The Block 70s are being equipped with L3Harris’ AN/ALQ-254(V)1 Viper Shield electronic warfare suite , and the system was not yet fully through its development and production process when the first aircraft were otherwise ready for delivery . L3Harris announced on September 3 that it had completed production of the first 35 Viper Shield systems, underscoring that the electronic warfare equipment was itself still moving into production as Taiwan’s fighters were approaching delivery. Taiwan chose to acquire the AN/ALQ-254 rather than the AN/ALQ-257 electronic warfare system used on U.S. Air Force F-16s. Lawmakers have questioned whether the system meets requirements associated with earlier work to modernize earlier F-16A/B Block 20 fighters to the F-16V standard . Meanwhile, Defense Minister Koo argued that those requirements applied to the earlier Block 20 upgrade rather than the new Block 70 purchase. Other international F-16 Block 70 operators are also using Viper Shield. Taiwanese officials have defended the decision, citing the specific requirements of Taiwan’s F-16 fleet and associated procurement considerations. The system is intended to provide the new fighters with a modern electronic warfare and self-protection capability against increasingly sophisticated radar and missile threats. There are also still questions about when the Viper Shield system itself will be fully ready. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6727. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press Weapons deliveries have also not kept pace with the aircraft themselves. Taiwan is receiving AIM-120C-8 AMRAAM air-to-air missiles as part of the F-16 package, with 200 ordered. The C-8 version incorporates upgrades from the U.S. Air Force’s Form, Fit, Function Refresh (F3R) effort, including new electronics and improved electronic-counter-countermeasures intended to make the missile more capable in a heavily contested electromagnetic environment. For Taiwan, the missile will provide the new F-16s with a modern beyond-visual-range air-to-air weapon that can be cued by the aircraft’s AN/APG-83 Scalable Agile Beam Radar (SABR), as well as other sources of targeting information through the F-16’s networked systems. An AIM-120 AMRAAM is prepared to be loaded onto an F-16V at Chiayi Air Base, in Chiayi on January 28, 2026. Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP The AIM-120C-8 is particularly relevant as Taiwan fields more F-16s against China’s increasingly capable fighter fleet, which includes aircraft equipped with long-range air-to-air missiles such as the PL-15 . Taiwan’s F-16 Block 70 package also includes the AGM-88 High-speed Anti-Radiation Missile (HARM), intended for attacks against enemy air defense systems. According to Roy Choo , a defense journalist and TWZ contributor, the first of the new AGM-88F missiles arrived in Taiwan back in 2022. The major gap is the AGM-154C Joint Standoff Weapon (JSOW). The precision glide weapon is intended to give Taiwan a longer-range strike capability against ground targets without requiring the launching aircraft to fly directly over heavily defended areas. According to the latest reporting from Taiwan, deliveries of the AGM-154C have been held up by delays on the U.S. production line and may not begin until 2027 or 2028 at the earliest. Existing stocks of these weapons were also heavily used in Operation Epic Fury . The two aircraft now sitting at Chihhang are significant for another reason. Unlike Taiwan’s existing F-16V fleet, they are new-production aircraft rather than older fighters that have been upgraded. Taiwan received 141 F-16A/B Block 20s that were upgraded to the F-16V configuration under a separate modernization program completed in 2023. The new Block 70s incorporate many of the same technologies — including the APG-83 — but are built from the ground up as new aircraft. A Taiwan Air Force F-16V taxis out during a spring military exercise at Chiayi Air Base, in Chiayi on January 28, 2026. Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP The Block 70s will also bring a significant new passive-sensing capability to Taiwan’s F-16 fleet. Under a $328.5-million U.S. Foreign Military Sales contract awarded to Lockheed Martin in February, Taiwan is receiving the company’s IRST21 Legion-ES infrared search and track system. Designed specifically for the F-16, the long-wave infrared sensor can passively detect and track airborne targets without emitting radar energy. That gives the aircraft another way to search for and track threats while reducing its own electromagnetic signature. The IRST21 also gives the F-16s a passive way to detect and track low-observable targets, potentially providing another means of finding Chinese stealth aircraft without relying solely on radar. In 2019, Lockheed Martin displayed a model of a Block 70 F-16 with what appeared to be a podded IRST system on one of its chin stations at the biennial Taipei Aerospace & Defense Technology Exhibition in Taiwan: The mysterious IRST pod at TADTE – https://t.co/avpx5djZMM pic.twitter.com/86lqxu6fN6 — Alert 5 (@alert5) August 16, 2019 The new fighters will therefore complement Taiwan’s upgraded F-16A/Bs while expanding the overall number of modern F-16s available to the ROCAF. The timing matters. People’s Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft operate around Taiwan on an increasingly routine basis, forcing the ROCAF to maintain a persistent air-defense posture. The additional F-16s will provide more aircraft for missions ranging from air defense and counter-air operations to maritime strike . Ground crew prepare to load AGM-84 Harpoon anti-ship missiles in front of an F-16V during a drill at Hualien Air Force base on August 17, 2022. Photo by SAM YEH/AFP via Getty Images The F-16V fleet is also being tested for a more specialized intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance role. The ROCAF has recently been conducting flight and systems integration testing of the MS-110 advanced reconnaissance pod, part of its Phoenix Scout project. The service plans to acquire six pods to replace older reconnaissance equipment . Based on the DB-110 digital sensor architecture, the system combines visible-light and infrared imaging with long-range, day-and-night reconnaissance, and real-time image transmission, allowing imagery to be passed more rapidly to ground command and intelligence elements. Integrating the pod with the F-16 and associated ground systems will give Taiwan another means of monitoring activity around the island and its surrounding waters. A ROCAF F-16V carrying an MS-110 reconnaissance pod. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press But Taiwan remains heavily outnumbered across the Taiwan Strait. China is fielding an increasingly sophisticated combat aircraft fleet that includes the J-20 and J-35 stealth fighter, large numbers of advanced fourth-generation fighters, airborne early warning and other force-multiplier aircraft , and a growing variety of uncrewed systems . A J-20 fighter during the Changchun Air Show on September 22, 2025 in Changchun, Jilin Province of China. Photo by Zhang Xiangyi/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images And the F-16s will face the same fundamental problem as Taiwan’s other combat aircraft in a major conflict: staying operational. China possesses extensive missile and air capabilities that could threaten Taiwan’s airbases, aircraft shelters, fuel supplies, command-and-control infrastructure, and other elements needed to keep fighters flying. You can read more about how the ROCAF would likely go to war with China in this previous in-depth feature. Basing the new F-16s at Chihhang Air Base, operated by the 7th Tactical Fighter Wing, is significant, Choo told us. “The basing of the aircraft at Chihhang allows the ROCAF to readily project air power south and eastwards, especially over the Bashi Channel , which is one avenue PLA can gain access to the Philippine Sea and beyond.” He explained. “Previously, ROCAF fighters from other bases maintain QRA detachments there” A new F-16C Block 70 lands at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung on October 2, 2026. Photo by CHENG Yu-chen / AFP The F-16 delivery today is only the beginning of a much larger effort to get all 66 aircraft into Taiwanese service. According to the latest information from the ROCAF, 63 F-16C/D Block 70s remain in various stages of production and delivery in the United States, with some already moving through the handover process. The remaining aircraft will be delivered according to production, flight-test, and acceptance milestones before being ferried to Taiwan. Once the full order is delivered, Taiwan will operate more than 200 F-16s when the new Block 70s are combined with its existing fleet. That will give the ROCAF a considerably larger force of modern F-16s, with substantial commonality between the upgraded F-16V fleet and the new-production Block 70s. The aircraft will still need to go through Taiwan’s acceptance procedures, while pilots and maintenance personnel complete the necessary conversion and training work. The new jets will then be progressively incorporated into the ROCAF’s operational units. Remarkably, the arrival of the first Block 70 fighters today marks the first delivery of new fighters to Taiwan since 2001, when the last of the 150 F-16A/B Block 20s were delivered. “The ROCAF’s surviving fleet of 139 F-16s, 53 Mirage 2000s , and 129 F-CK-1s was largely inducted in the 1990s, when Taiwan held the upper hand in the cross-Strait air-power balance,” Choo explined. “Even then, there remained a requirement for additional fighters, prompting the island’s first formal request to purchase 66 F-16C/Ds during the 2006 Monterey Talks.” F-CK-1s taxi for takeoff during a scramble as part of a combat readiness exercise at Ching Chuan Kang Air Base in Taichung on January 7, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP “By the late 2000s, these fighters were approaching the limits of their combat effectiveness as the PLA air fleet expanded in both size and capability. Fortunately, substantial upgrades began to be rolled out to the F-CK-1s and F-16s from the 2010s.” In the wake of the 2019 acquisition of the F-16C/D Block 70s, questions arose over the aircraft’s asymmetric value as the Taiwan military increasingly focused on developing a plan for asymmetric capabilities in response to the PLA’s growing combat power. “However, developments in recent years have underscored the continued importance of a capable fighter fleet not least for policing Taiwan’s airspace amid the PLA’s sustained gray-zone air operations around the island,” Choo added. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6728. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press The timing of today’s arrival is also notable. The aircraft reached Taiwan just days after U.S. President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. The delivery comes amid questions in Taipei about the future pace of U.S. arms transfers, after Trump said in May that a proposed $14-billion Taiwan arms package was being held in abeyance. He had approved an $11-billion package in December 2025. Washington continues to say that its policy toward Taiwan has not changed. Beijing, for its part, continues to oppose U.S. arms sales to Taiwan and regards the island as part of Chinese territory. It has taken nearly seven years to get the first two F-16C/D Block 70s, to Taiwan. But their arrival marks the first step in a major modernization of the ROCAF’s F-16 fleet, adding new-production fighters with improved radar, electronic warfare, sensors, and weapons to a force that is already operating upgraded F-16Vs. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Taiwan’s First F-16 Block 70s Have Finally Arrived appeared first on TWZ .

content: “李南央状告海关案”跟进报道（146） ——继续通知、继续跟进 上期 “跟进”中 ，我说中国国家图书馆没有对美国地方法院 “李锐资料归属案” 的裁决提起上诉，应该是主管此案 李锐资料134专案组（LimsTim134） 的决定。这个推测在本月以无论如何大开脑洞也想不到的方式得到了证实。 9月19日，在东欧游历半个多月后，我们从法兰克福乘美联航班机飞回旧金山。我的座位是一排靠窗，巴悌忠的座位在我后面。正在整理行囊，身后飘过一声有些犹疑的招呼： “ Ms. Li. ”我下意识地 回头寻声，简直不能相信自己的眼睛，咫尺相对的会是张玉珍/中国国家图书馆的美国代理律师福赛特。他的座位与我同排，在走道的另一侧。我看着他那双显然也有些不敢置信的眼睛脱口而出： “ 世界怎么会这么小！上天居然为我的书准备了如此精彩的情节！ ” 福赛特似乎仍处在错愕之中不知如何回应。我抓住了这不可思议的天赐良机，迅即提问： “ 我有个问题，你如果觉得不方便不必回答。 ” 他秒回： “什么问题？” 我秒接： “不上诉是谁的决定？是你建议他们那么做，还是他们自己决定这么做？” 没有些许的踌躇，他说： “ 跟我没有关系，是他们自己的决定。 ” 我的嘴角翘了起来： “谢谢你让我知道。” 对话间，我看到福赛特旁边座位有位女士一直站立着望向我们，脸拉得有点长。我问： “这位是你的夫人？” 福赛特侧过身，让我和那位女士直接相对，说： “是，她是我的妻子。” 我冲福赛特的妻子笑了笑：“很高兴遇到你。” 她却有些不悦地问福赛特： “她是谁呀？” 福赛特 只回答了两个字： “ Li Rui’s Daughter （李锐的女儿）。” 显然，她知道老公曾经手的案子，一脸的无法相信： “世界真是太小了！” 大约察觉到妻子的不悦，福赛特对我笑笑，低下头摆弄起座位上的枕头、毯子。我转向坐在我后面的悌忠，他说：“这简直是百万分之一的机率！不信有上帝之手都不成！” 有心的读者可能会记得我在“跟进144”中提到地方法院裁决的最后一条： “作为本案胜诉方斯坦福和李南央有权根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第 54(d)(1) 条追回其合理费用。”这里的“合理费用” 指的是我方聘请专家证人、取证证人等费用。斯坦福向中国国家图书馆提了支付请求吗？答案是 “没有。”作为胜诉一方斯坦福的立场是：“相对整个案件而言，这些费用数额相当有限。为了以非对抗性的方式推进事态，斯坦福/胡佛方面决定不提交相关申请。” 在 “李锐资料归属权案”的初始 ，我对斯坦福大学不愿因这个案件影响她在北京大学内的斯坦福中心的运作而举棋不定是完全不理解的。结案后的今天，斯坦福大学在我方完胜之后不对中国国家图书馆穷追猛打，这个选择我认同。 这次在欧洲游历，我们在波兰首都华沙参观了位于瓦津基公园的美希莱维茨基宫内曾经的中美华沙会谈厅。厅内的介绍牌子上写着： 1958年至1979年间，在瓦津基皇家公园梅西莱维茨基宫，中华人民共和国和美利坚合众国政府代表举行过数十次会谈。这是当时中美之间对话沟通的主要途径，对两国建立互信、维护和平发挥了重要作用。 可以说，没有中美华沙会谈，就不会有后来1971年的尼克松宣佈访华和最后1979年的中美建交。很难想象，在视资本主义为万恶之源、美帝国主义为中国人民头号敌人的毛泽东年代，中美之间会在一座波兰的前王宫中一间佈置的绝不无产阶级化的厅内举行过会谈，而且不是一次，是数十次。联想到几天前美国国务卿鲁比奥回答各方对总统川普高规格接待习近平的质疑的回复： “对于两个拥有庞大经济和军事体量的强国而言，直接沟通是必要的。”他将川普与习近平的会谈与 冷战时期美苏之间的会谈进行了类比。 在十多个小时的航行途中，我和张玉珍的律师福赛特没有再说过一句话，商务仓的小包座将乘客隔在互不打扰的各自空间。直到飞机平稳落地旧金山机场，乘客纷纷起身去取头顶行李舱内的箱子，我与福赛特不可避免地再次直面相对。 我微颔告别说： “很高兴遇到你。” 他颇真诚地回应： “我也是。” 我又说： “我正在写案子的书，书中当然提到了你。你若愿意看，出版后我会告知你。” 他说： “请一定，很期待。” 换到八年前，我想我能忍住不对张玉珍的美国代理律师怒目而视就不错了。现在，我对美国独立于政治之外的法律体系有了更多的理解，我也从斯坦福的律师那儿学会了看问题的不同视角。是的，世界上有那么多的国家，那么多的国家又有那么多不同的制度、信仰、意识形态、文化、历史……即使是无可避免、迫在眉睫的你死我活，留有沟通渠道、保持对话、不把事情做绝，似乎是持有常识的政府、抑或个人的睿智选择。 回到我的 “状告海关案” 。上期 “跟进” 发出后，一位读者来电说： 祝贺您，南央大姐！您终于胜利了，正义终于胜利了！ 但愿您还剩下的一个案件能够在您和我们的有生之年也得到胜利！！ 我回复说： 是真相胜利了。在美国真相是可以获胜的。在那边，真相是可以被伪造的。“海关案”若获开庭日，或许是“真相”可以不再被伪造或掩饰的开端。 9月10日，北京第三中级法院向我发出了第32次“延审通知”。他们继续“通知”，我继续“跟进”。 2026年9月30日

Aboitiz Power Corp. (AboitizPower) was among the organizations commended by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) for its exemplary contribution to the region’s energy sector, particularly on its cooperation on nuclear energy technologies, information sharing, and capacity building.

[![Image 19: ABOITIZPOWER PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255877.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255877.jpg)

 ABOITIZPOWER PHOTO

To recall, AboitizPower signed a memorandum of understanding with Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power Co. Ltd. in Gyeongju, South Korea last July to explore the potential applicability of nuclear energy technologies in the Philippines, including conducting joint pre-feasibility studies. AboitizPower President and CEO Danel Aboitiz (center) receives the commendation during the 44th Asean Ministers on Energy Meeting (AMEM) at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City, Metro Manila. AMEM gathers Asean energy leaders, industry representatives and key stakeholders for high-level discussions, knowledge exchange and regional collaboration.

title: PH to host 2026 East Asia Cup at RMBS
summary: THE crack of the bat will once again echo through the storied walls of the Rizal Memorial Baseball Stadium (RMBS) as Manila hosts the East Asia Cup 2026, presented by the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) from Dec. 7 to 13. For one week, s
content:
THE crack of the bat will once again echo through the storied walls of the Rizal Memorial Baseball Stadium (RMBS) as Manila hosts the East Asia Cup 2026, presented by the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) from Dec. 7 to 13.

For one week, six nations headlined by host Philippines, Singapore, Hong Kong, Thailand will converge on the capital, turning the historic venue into a hub of competition and sports tourism.

For the first time since its opening in 1934, the RMBS has undergone a major facelift, a transformation that promises to restore its past grandeur and elevate Philippine baseball to global standards.

*   [Eala suffers worst loss of 2026 season, falls to world No. 217 Shi](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/sports/eala-suffers-worst-loss-of-2026-season-falls-to-world-no-217-shi/2443990)

“Our objective is to finish the facelift as soon as possible and bring the stadium to global standards,” said PSC Chairman Patrick Gregorio, noting that the grandstand will be retrofitted to seat 10,000, complemented by a digital scoreboard mounted on the historic outfield wall and an all-weather artificial turf built to international specifications.

“This is about giving Filipino baseball a true home worthy of its history and future,” Gregorio added.

Immediately after completion, the stadium will host the East Asia Cup organized by the Philippine Amateur Baseball Association (PABA), sanctioned by the Baseball Federation of Asia (BFA).

“This renovation is a turning point for Philippine baseball,” emphasized PABA Secretary General Mike Asuncion. “Hosting the East Asia Cup in a world-class stadium will inspire our athletes and show the region that we are serious about competing at the highest level.”

Asuncion added that the PSC-PABA partnership extends beyond RMBS, with plans to build additional baseball fields nationwide to nurture young talent and expand grassroots development.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

The RMBS is a shrine to baseball’s global heritage. In its inaugural exhibition game in December 1934, Lou Gehrig hit the stadium’s first-ever home run, followed by Babe Ruth with the second. Their feats remain etched on the stadium’s walls, reminders of Manila’s place in baseball lore.

Hataw Pilipinas, the official moniker of the 24-man Philippine national team that captured the Southeast Asian Games gold medal against host Thailand, enters the East Asia Cup with confidence.

Team captain and pitcher Romeo Jasmin, who will soon pass the baton to the next generation of Filipino baseball players, leads the charge, determined to prove that Filipino baseball is ready to step up its game.

Veterans such as Ferdinand “Bong” Liguayan Jr., catcher Mark Steven Manaig, leadoff hitter Jenald Pareja, and rising star Mark Beronilla likewise anchor the squad. TMT

title: 刘军宁：中华民国国歌里，藏着列宁的先锋队
summary: 刘军宁 X @liujunning · Oct 11, 2026 换个场景想想。美国的共和党趁执政把保守主义写进宪法，或者民主党把自由主义写进去，然后要求全体国民“必信必忠、贯彻始终”。然而，孙中山与国民党，就是这个做的。他们把一个人的主义、一党的党歌强加给所有的政党和全体民众。这就是国民党与孙中山应该被拒绝的最重组的理由。 —————— 忠诚不绝对，绝对不忠诚。这不是从李鸿忠开始的，是从孙中山开始的。他一再要求：入党党员必须按指印、立誓约，宣誓“绝对服从总理（孙中山）一人”
content: 刘军宁   X @liujunning · Oct 11, 2026 换个场景想想。美国的共和党趁执政把保守主义写进宪法，或者民主党把自由主义写进去，然后要求全体国民“必信必忠、贯彻始终”。然而，孙中山与国民党，就是这个做的。他们把一个人的主义、一党的党歌强加给所有的政党和全体民众。这就是国民党与孙中山应该被拒绝的最重组的理由。 —————— 忠诚不绝对，绝对不忠诚。这不是从李鸿忠开始的，是从孙中山开始的。他一再要求：入党党员必须按指印、立誓约，宣誓“绝对服从总理（孙中山）一人”。蒋介石则在此基础上，于1943年的《中国之命运》中正式将这一模式总结并升华为“一个国家、一个政党、一个领袖、一个主义”的政治纲领。 中华民国国歌里，藏着列宁的先锋队  我先讲一个每年双十都能看见、却没多少人留意的细节。 国歌一响，总统府前的台上站着一排人。有的从头唱到尾。有的嘴在前两句不动，等到第三句“以建民国”才开口。还有人更巧，只把“吾党”两个字滑过去，别的照唱。 民进党的县市首长和党籍公职人员这么干，已经干了很多年。问他们为什么，答案也不绕：那两句明摆着是党歌，跟国民党分不开，没法当成纯粹的国家象征。 我感兴趣的不在这儿。我想知道的是：那两句到底写了什么，能让一群靠自由选举上来的人，宁可在国歌里闭嘴。 这首歌歌词要的是绝对忠诚 你把歌词摊开，会发现撑着整篇的是四个字：宗、从、信、忠。 这四个字在汉语里从来就不是政治词。它们是宗教词。“宗”是宗奉，把什么东西奉成终极；“从”是顺服；“信”和“忠”，字面就是信与忠。 问题出在它们后面跟的宾语。只有一个：主义。 所以这不是一首描述国家的歌。它要求的是归顺。形式是属灵的，对象是属世的。偶像就是这么来的——拿敬拜的纳粹手势，去对待一个受造之物。 三民主义的历史位置我不否认。孙中山把西方的民族主义、民权、民生揉在一起，做成一套世俗的政治方案。可它是方案，不是启示。它要去的那个“大同”，说到底是人用政治工程盖起来的乌托邦，跟圣经里神所立的国度，完全两码事。 第一诫不许人把受造之物当终极权威。第二诫不许人替自己雕像。而观念做的像，比木头石头做的更麻烦。它没有形状，所以从来没人指着它说一句：那是个像。 第五句的来历 说到第五句，我头一回注意到的时候，愣了一下。 “咨尔多士，为民前锋。” 对，前锋（Vanguard） 列宁主义最硬的那块建制，叫先锋队——党是群众的先锋队，觉悟得由党从外头灌进去。 而这八个字写在1924年。那一年国民党联俄容共改组。地点是黄埔军校开学典礼，底下坐着一屋子马上要去当党军骨干的年轻人。苏联顾问就在现场。 我不是说它像先锋队。它就是先锋队理论的文言版。 再往上翻一层。孙中山把人分三等：先知先觉的创造发明，后知后觉的仿效推行，不知不觉的竭力乐成。有了这个分法，“训政”就立住了——党先把人民训好，等人民够格了再行宪。党自然排在国前面、压在国上头。党歌通向国歌，一点都不奇怪。 时间线也简单。1928年定党歌，1937年定国歌，1943年立法确认。你去查，从头到尾拍板的都是一个政党的中央机构。没有哪一次经过全民，连议会那一关都没走。 所以国民党和共产党在组织形式上，不存在谁先谁后。同一个顾问团，同一年，同一套文件。 这就是暴政 换个场景想想。美国的共和党趁执政把保守主义写进宪法，或者民主党把自由主义写进去，然后要求全体国民“必信必忠、贯彻始终”。 这还叫民国（共和）吗。 暴君的要害其实不在残暴。有的暴君脾气还挺好。要害在于他把自己的意志当成了法律的源头。 政党的纲领本来是能吵的，能投票的，能被推翻的。写进国家的终极信条，就吵不动了。吵不动的东西，已经不叫政纲。那叫教义。 中共把马列主义写进宪法序言，国民党把三民主义写进国歌。两家的意识形态内含有别，手上的动作一模一样。 官方后来有个辩解，说“吾党”在古汉语里可以当“吾辈”讲。这个训诂就算能接受。可“主义是从”那四个字怎么办。训诂救不了它。 罢唱的不同意 回到开头那几位在前两句闭嘴的人。 他们做的不只是摆个政治姿态。在一首规定了必须唱的歌里，他们替自己留下了罢唱的不同意。 一首歌该怎么唱，是台湾人自己的事，轮不到海峡这边的人指手画脚。我只想把一件事说明白：那支先锋队从来不是共产党的专利。它1924年在广州上岸，分成两路，一路往北京，一路去了台北。 北京那一路，到今天还在路上。 台北那一路，人们已经学会在唱到第二句的时候闭嘴。 光是这件事，就把自由政体和党国之间的全部距离量出来了。 虽然同根同源，只是海峡那一边，没有这个选项。 附： 现行中华民国国歌歌词（1924年孙中山黄埔军校训词） 三民主義，吾黨所宗     San Min Chu-i, our aim shall be 以建民國，以進大同      To found a free land, world   peace be our stand 咨爾多士，為民前鋒      Lead on, comrades, vanguards ye are 夙夜匪懈，主義是從      Hold fast your aim, by sun and star 矢勤矢勇，必信必忠     Be earnest and brave, your country to save 一心一德，貫徹始終     One heart, one soul, one mind, one goal

title: 梅艳芳骨灰失窃至今未找回，事件荒诞程度令人咋舌
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 以前是人质被绑架，现在没想到骨灰也可以被绑架了。 10月10日，梅艳芳63岁冥诞。 本该是静默追思的日子，歌迷会一纸声明，曝光了一桩沉寂三个月、细思极恐的怪事。 今年7月18日，有歌迷前往香港大屿山宝莲禅寺祭拜。 走到梅艳芳灵位前，所有人瞬间失语、心底发凉。 安放骨灰的牌匾螺丝被人为撬开，摆放二十余年的骨灰瓮，空空如也。 梅艳芳的骨灰，不见了。 现场是24小时监控、专人值守的灵塔园区，本是逝者最安稳、最清净的归宿。 可就是在这样严密的防护之下，有人精准潜入、精准下手、悄无声息
content: 以前是人质被绑架，现在没想到骨灰也可以被绑架了。 10月10日，梅艳芳63岁冥诞。 本该是静默追思的日子，歌迷会一纸声明，曝光了一桩沉寂三个月、细思极恐的怪事。 今年7月18日，有歌迷前往香港大屿山宝莲禅寺祭拜。 走到梅艳芳灵位前，所有人瞬间失语、心底发凉。 安放骨灰的牌匾螺丝被人为撬开，摆放二十余年的骨灰瓮，空空如也。 梅艳芳的骨灰，不见了。 现场是24小时监控、专人值守的灵塔园区，本是逝者最安稳、最清净的归宿。 可就是在这样严密的防护之下，有人精准潜入、精准下手、悄无声息带走一切。 事发当天，歌迷立刻报警，香港重案组介入调查。 无线索、无嫌疑人、无任何进展。 走投无路的歌迷，只能选择公开求助，将这件荒诞又悲凉的事，公之于众。 很多人不知道，为了让梅艳芳死后安宁，家人早已做到了极致。 灵位不写梅艳芳，不放照片，不留任何名人痕迹，只剩下最普通、最朴素的乳名——珠女。 不仅如此，她的生忌、死忌，全部刻意避开公历，只用农历低调记录。 不宣传、不纪念、不声张。 家人的心意简单又心酸： 你生前热闹了一辈子、辛苦了一辈子、为别人活了一辈子。 死后，只想让你做回普通女孩，无人窥探，无人打扰，静静长眠。 本以为，低调至此，便能一世安稳，可人性的恶意，从来不分场合，不分生死。 而更让人心酸的是，7月梅艳芳骨灰被盗，8月梅艳芳的母亲也撒手人寰。 梅妈生前想和女儿合葬在一起，但女儿的骨灰下落不明，她的事情也一直悬而未决。 目前梅艳芳哥哥已经发出悬赏，希望早日找到骨灰，让她得以清净。 这个事件在网上曝光后，全网猜测四起。 其实这并不是香港第一起骨灰被盗案了。 2025年到2026年，香港沙田宝福山出过一连串吓人的事： 盗贼用专业手法撬开骨灰龛，取走骨灰，再把外观复原。 日常巡查看不出异样，像没人来过。 宝福山创办人冯成的骨灰也被偷。 盗贼发来骨灰盒照片，开价狠到离谱： 刘家良案里，翁静晶被勒索6000万港元； 其他个案里，传言每位家属索100万美元。 翁静晶回得硬：“一毛钱都不会给。” 后来警方介入，2026年2月，刘家良、向华胜骨灰寻回，有人被控串谋勒索，但同伙还在外头。 也就是说，在如今这个时代，骨灰已经不只是骨灰，它是软肋，是筹码，是一个人死后被拿去勒索其家人的重要武器。 但在梅艳芳这个案件中，警方公布了细节，整整三个月，没有一通勒索电话，没有任何人索要钱财。 不谈判、不示威、不露面，不知道对方是怕被抓不敢露面，还是想等风声过后再敲诈梅艳芳的家人，又或者不是绑架事件。 如果排除绑架的可能性，那剩下的几种可能性，都让人背脊发凉，细思极恐。 有网友说是极端执念的私生粉丝，偏执疯狂，妄图独占念想，不择手段带走逝者骨灰； 更有人说出了最阴暗、最惊悚的可能：配阴婚。 在一些灰色阴暗的角落，名人逝者的骨灰，被视作稀缺筹码，尤其是没有结过婚的梅艳芳，很容易沦为不法分子牟利的工具，用来交易配阴婚、做玄学勾当。 如果是这样，那这个远比明面上的敲诈勒索，更加阴毒、更加恐怖。 时至今日，真相依旧成谜。 我们无从知晓，到底是谁，对一个离世二十余年的逝者，痛下狠手。 但唯一确定的是：梅艳芳，终究没能逃过世人的打扰和消耗。 世人总说：死者为大，入土为安。 原来，入土为安从来不是天生的权利，对一些人来说，这竟然都是一种奢侈品。 回看梅艳芳这一生，愈发让人意难平。 四岁登台卖唱，替家里还债，小小年纪扛起整个家的生计； 年少成名，红遍华语乐坛，手握万千荣光，却从未为自己活过一天； 她重情重义、慷慨坦荡，圈内人人尊称一声“梅姐”，帮扶后辈、仗义疏财，待人赤诚温热； 可善良换不来善待，仗义换不来安稳。 生前，被原生家庭无休止索取、捆绑、消耗，一生为家人奔波兜底，受尽牵绊； 活着时，被舆论消费、被流言重伤，一举一动都被放大解读，身不由己； 离世二十二年后，本该尘埃落定、归于安宁，最后连一捧骨灰，都无法保全。 她明明已经退到“珠女”了，世界还是追进来。 这实在是让人愤怒和惋惜。 鬼有什么好怕的，我带你见见这世间的人心。 愿所有盗取骨灰的作恶者，都受到法律的严惩。 如果一个人连死后都得不到安宁，如果一个环境连别人的骨灰都想着去换取利益，那我们这个社会该烂成什么样子啊？ 梅艳芳事件发生后，有人在网上问，梅艳芳的骨灰值多少钱？ 停一停，别再问骨灰值多少钱了。 梅家现在最需要的，不是看热闹的心态，而是行车记录仪、是7月前后宝莲寺一带的可疑身影、是有人是否见过类似骨灰瓮的器皿，是让梅艳芳早点回家。 我始终认为，人活着，总得敬畏一点东西。 不是为了求回报，不是为了求善待，而是为了获得内心的安宁。 这份敬畏，保护的不只是逝去的人，也是活着的我们。 人质绑架，要挟的是活生生的人； 而盗取骨灰，瞄准的是生者心底最后的思念。 施暴者看准了逝者无法开口，没有反抗之力，便肆无忌惮地闯入生死边界，拿一捧尘土当做筹码。 生死，本是人间最后的分界线，活着的纷争，到这里本该落幕。 可当恶意跨过生死，连长眠都要被打扰，击穿的是整个社会最基础的文明底线。 梅艳芳一生，从梅姐到珠女，她放下了所有光环，只想安安静静退场。 可人间的执念与贪婪，依旧追了过来，这也是全国网友最愤怒的地方。 惟愿警方能够早日寻回线索，让漂泊的她回家，让一对母女，终能如愿相伴长眠。 也希望相关部门能以此为契机，推动立法的前进，狠狠打击这样的行为。 《女人花》里唱，缘分不停留，像春风来又走。 春风来过，温暖过无数人。 不该在落幕之后，还要承受世间龌龊。 《女人花》里唱，缘分不停留，像春风来又走。 春风来过，温暖过无数人。 不该在落幕之后，还要承受世间龌龊。

title: Who should pay capital gains tax?
summary: Dear PAO, In sale of real properties, who is really liable to pay the capital gains tax and how is it computed? Are all real properties sold subject to this kind of tax? Que * [Effect of minor discrepancies between testimony in court and af
content:
Dear PAO,

In sale of real properties, who is really liable to pay the capital gains tax and how is it computed? Are all real properties sold subject to this kind of tax?

Que

*   [Effect of minor discrepancies between testimony in court and affidavit of the complainant](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/legal-advice/effect-of-minor-discrepancies-between-testimony-in-court-and-affidavit-of-the-complainant/2442784)

Dear Que,

Capital gains tax (CGT) is a tax imposed on the presumed gains realized from certain transactions involving capital assets. With respect to the sale of real property, Section 24(D)(1) of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) of 1997, as amended, provides for a final tax rate of six percent (6%) on the presumed capital gains from the sale, exchange, or other disposition of real property located in the Philippines, and classified as capital assets.

Being a tax on the presumed gains, the party who stands to profit or be benefitted from the transaction—i.e. the seller, is liable to pay the CGT. Note, however, that while our laws imposed upon the seller the obligation to pay the same, in reality, the burden may shift from either the buyer or the seller, depending on the agreement of the parties. (Section 24[D][1], National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended) In computing the amount of CGT payable, the law adopts a presumed-gain system and uses the gross selling price, the current fair market value as shown in the schedule of values of the Provincial or City Assessors, or the zonal values as determined by the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, whichever is higher, as the tax base. (Ibid.) Finally, not all real properties sold are subject to CGT. Only those real properties classified as capital asset are subject to said 6% tax, while real properties classified as an ordinary asset are generally subject to the applicable ordinary income tax and creditable withholding tax rules instead. Section 2 of Bureau of Internal Revenue Regulations No. 7-2003, which was issued on December 27, 2002, distinguishes capital assets from ordinary assets in this wise: SEC. 2. Definition Of Terms. — For purposes of these Regulations, the following terms shall be defined as follows: a. Capital assets shall refer to all real properties held by a taxpayer, whether or not connected with his trade or business, and which are not included among the real properties considered as ordinary assets under Sec. 39(A)(1) of the Code.

b. Ordinary assets shall refer to all real properties specifically excluded from the definition of capital assets under Sec. 39(A)(1) of the Code, namely: 1. Stock in trade of a taxpayer or other real property of a kind which would properly be included in the inventory of the taxpayer if on hand at the close of the taxable year; or 2. Real property held by the taxpayer primarily for sale to customers in the ordinary course of his trade or business; or 3. Real property used in trade or business (i.e., buildings and/or improvements) of a character which is subject to the allowance for depreciation provided for under Sec. 34(F) of the Code; or 4. Real property used in trade or business of the taxpayer. Real properties acquired by banks through foreclosure sales are considered as their ordinary assets. However, banks shall not be considered as habitually engaged in the real estate business for purposes of determining the applicable rate of withholding tax imposed under Sec. 2.57.2 (J) of Revenue Regulations No. 2-98, as amended.

The classification of the property is therefore essential in determining the proper tax treatment. The mere fact that a property is land or a building does not automatically mean that the 6% CGT applies. Ultimately, the nature and use of the property, as well as the status and activities of the seller, must be considered in determining whether the property is a capital asset or an ordinary asset.

# China denies obstructing PCG medical evacuation

[![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/allen-limos "author image")

 October 11, 2026

 80

*   ![Image 21: font icon small](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-small.svg)Small
*   ![Image 22: font icon medium](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-medium.svg)Medium

[![Image 24: Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/google-preferred-source.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=manilatimes.net "Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google")

CHINA denied allegations that the China Coast Guard (CCG) intentionally obstructed the medical evacuation conducted by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in the Ayungin Shoal, accusing Manila of distorting facts.

On Oct. 8, the CCG vessel 5306 delayed a PCG medical evacuation at Ayungin Shoal by nearly 10 hours by using a water cannon on a PCG ship.

In a statement on Friday, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning asserted that it was the PCG that entered Beijing’s territory without permission.

*   [‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

Mao added that the CCG took “legitimate and reasonable measures” before ultimately allowing the evacuation to proceed on humanitarian grounds.

“After communication between the two sides, out of humanitarian considerations, China gave timely permission to the Philippine side to evacuate injured personnel by small boat and provided necessary facilitation,” Mao stated.

“Instead of acknowledging China’s facilitation, individual Philippine officials have distorted facts and wrongfully accused China without showing the whole picture to the public,” Mao added.

title: Cebu City landslide kills 3 family members; mother survives
summary: **CEBU CITY** — A landslide buried a family of four inside their home at Sitio Kandarong Riverside, Barangay Pulangbato, on Friday, killing two children and their 60-year-old grandmother while the mother survived. Rescue teams from the bara
content:
**CEBU CITY** — A landslide buried a family of four inside their home at Sitio Kandarong Riverside, Barangay Pulangbato, on Friday, killing two children and their 60-year-old grandmother while the mother survived.

Rescue teams from the barangay, the Cebu City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, and the Bureau of Fire Protection in Cebu City spent nearly six hours retrieving the victims as persistent rain and unstable soil hampered operations.

The fatalities were identified as Xian Caballero, 5; Kyden, 6; and their grandmother, Judith, 60. Their mother, Jolly Pearl Andamon, 38, survived and was rushed to a hospital for treatment.

*   [DENR pushes bamboo planting in Tarlac](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/regions/denr-pushes-bamboo-planting-in-tarlac/2443091)

Rescuers recovered Xian at around 1:45 p.m. and brought him to a hospital, where he later died despite emergency treatment.

They pulled Andamon out from the rubble alive shortly afterward. Rescuers then recovered Kyden at around 4:24 p.m. and Judith at 5:43 p.m. Both had died by the time rescuers retrieved them.

The shifting ground and continuing rainfall made the rescue dangerous, forcing responders to work cautiously and temporarily suspend operations from time to time over safety concerns.

Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival expressed his condolences to the bereaved family.

“Our deepest prayers and sympathies are with the family during this painful time,” Archival said.

The landslide also forced 35 families, or 137 people, to leave their homes. The incident completely destroyed two houses and prompted residents of 29 other houses to evacuate.

The city government sheltered the evacuees at the Pulangbato Gym and pledged to provide relief goods and hot meals throughout their stay.

Archival also urged residents in landslide-prone areas to remain alert and take precautions amid the continuing rains.

He asked the public to stay away from the site and keep access roads clear for emergency vehicles and heavy equipment.

*   ![Image 2: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)

The city government committed to giving P20,000 in financial assistance to the relatives of each deceased victim and another P20,000 to the owners of houses damaged by the landslide.

title: 一场新的太空竞赛提出了一个关键问题：任何人能否拥有月球？
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 德国科学家测试新开发的宇航服，随着人类登陆月球竞赛加速，测试正在进行中。（美联社：马丁·迈斯纳） 20 世纪点燃了一场美国和苏联之间的太空竞赛。 但在这个世纪，一场新的竞赛正在诞生，亿万富翁和主要世界强国为了控制月球而展开竞争。 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克希望在十年内在月球上建造一座自我生长的城市，研究人员表示，由于缺乏水，这一梦想可能几乎不可能实现。 与此同时，蓝色起源的杰夫·贝佐斯也表达了他殖民月球的愿望。 随着关于在月球上建造核反应堆的竞赛的报道出现，美国与俄罗斯 –
content: 德国科学家测试新开发的宇航服，随着人类登陆月球竞赛加速，测试正在进行中。（美联社：马丁·迈斯纳） 20 世纪点燃了一场美国和苏联之间的太空竞赛。 但在这个世纪，一场新的竞赛正在诞生，亿万富翁和主要世界强国为了控制月球而展开竞争。 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克希望在十年内在月球上建造一座自我生长的城市，研究人员表示，由于缺乏水，这一梦想可能几乎不可能实现。 与此同时，蓝色起源的杰夫·贝佐斯也表达了他殖民月球的愿望。 随着关于在月球上建造核反应堆的竞赛的报道出现，美国与俄罗斯 – 中国联盟之间的旧冷战紧张局势似乎正在重演。 这引发了一个问题：任何人实际上都能拥有月球吗？ 贝佐斯拥有的蓝色起源新格伦航天器的艺术构想，旨在帮助在月球和太空中建立定居点。（提供：蓝色起源） 始于冷战条约 1967 年的《联合国外层空间条约》（OST）诞生于冷战高峰时期，当时一枚搭载苏联国旗的苏联火箭于 1959 年坠毁在月球表面。 这在西方引发了关于苏联对月球主权主张的担忧。 虽然苏联的主张从未实现，但这确实开启了月球属于所有人的理念。 美国总统林登·B·约翰逊（最右侧）坐在国务卿迪安·腊斯克身旁，签署 OST。（维基媒体共享资源：ITU） OST 的一项关键裁决是，月球应“仅用于和平目的”，禁止在其表面进行武器测试或军事用途。 其他与月球相关的关键条款如下： OST 获得了联合国大会的一致通过，但自那以来，其限制也受到了挑战。 1969 年历史性登月后，阿波罗 11 号登月舱“鹰号”拍摄的地球景象。（路透社：档案） 漏洞使问题复杂化 正如悉尼大学空间法专家胡赛因·巴德雷丁解释的那样，OST 的问题在于该条约“非常笼统和广泛”。 值得注意的是，OST 没有关于开采月球的规定。 1979 年，联合国《月球协定》试图通过裁决“月球及其自然资源是全人类的共同遗产”来解决这一问题。 然而，只有 18 个国家（包括澳大利亚）批准了该条约。 美国和俄罗斯不在其中。 巴德雷丁博士表示，各国需要许可证开采月球，并将费用分摊给人类这一建议，被一些美国公司视为“试图将月球社会化”。 相反，2015 年，一项法案授予美国公民和私人实体拥有和销售太空资源的能力。 卢森堡、阿联酋和日本也制定了类似的立法。 另一位空间律师卡桑德拉·斯蒂尔（Cassandra Steer）对 OST 的持久性持更乐观的态度。 她曾撰文阐述其优点，并表示她坚信“该条约的长期持久性，因为将其视为宪法最为有用”。 “‘非占有原则’在第二条中确实面临压力，但似乎正在发生的是围绕条约的新解释的趋同，而不是废除条约。” 美国、卢森堡、阿联酋和日本的行动是“拓宽了可能性的解释”，她说。 联合国表示，全球太空产业正朝着 2030 年价值一万亿美元的方向发展。（路透社：NASA/金·希夫莱特） 影响力等于控制权吗？ 澳大利亚和新西兰空间法理事会主席雷贝卡·康诺利（Rebecca Connolly）认为“月球正成为地缘政治竞争的下一个前沿”。 她说这是一场竞争，其中“率先到达很重要”。 “‘在月球上建立基础设施和持续运营的国家可能会获得相当大的影响力，以决定未来活动的进行方式，’康诺利博士表示。” 国际法的漏洞引发了关于谁将控制月球及其资源的访问的担忧。（路透社：NASA/新闻稿） 斯蒂尔博士表示，SpaceX 可能控制月球上的访问和资源的风险是“让我整夜睡不着的事”。 “‘美国无法到达月球，除非有 SpaceX，但 SpaceX 可以在没有美国、甚至没有政府合同的情况下做到这一点，’她说。” “‘即使 SpaceX 被 NASA 承包，仍然可能存在 SpaceX 率先登陆资源丰富的月球房地产，并利用人工智能和机器人技术建立足够的采矿基础设施，从而拒绝第二到达者的访问，这是一个真正的担忧。’” 目前，一次 SpaceX 火箭坠毁已在月球上凿出一个陨石坑。（NASA 通过美联社） 和平的持久希望 美国正在建立一套新的、非约束性的月球探索指导原则。 由 NASA 领导的《阿尔忒弥斯协定》希望重申对 OST 的支持，并在太空碎片和太空资源的使用方面建立护栏。 目前已有 76 个国家签署，但俄罗斯和中国拒绝了它们。 这就是为什么巴德雷丁博士更喜欢一个“在联合国框架下”的条约，专门解决军事活动、资源开采和环境问题。 “‘该条约必须详细，并应在联合国的主持下谈判，而不是在联合国之外，’他说。” 联合国外层空间事务厅确实有一个工作组，正在为太空资源推荐法律原则。 其今年 4 月的最后一轮草案建议称，月球及其资源不能成为任何国家或组织的财产。 它还重申了月球和平的必要性，这一信息比以往任何时候都更为贴切。 始于人类迈出的一小步，如今已成为太空领域的一个巨大的“如果”。（提供：NASA） 上周，美国国防部长皮特·海格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）宣布了武器创新的计划，指出需要主宰“从地球之下到月球之上的任何未来战场”。 这在美国首次确认已在太空部署武器之后。 与月球不同，太空没有同样的和平护栏。 但任何在月球上的战斗都是对 OST 原则的“公然”违背，斯蒂尔博士表示。 “‘这也可能违反《联合国宪章》，’她说。” “‘但这对现任政府来说都不重要。’” “‘从这个意义上说，外层空间条约的强度取决于其他国家希望国际法在多大程度上有效。’”

title: French students eye more protests as UN voices concern
summary: **MIAMI, Florida** — Isaias strengthened to a Category 2 hurricane on Thursday as it headed toward the United States Gulf Coast, the US National Hurricane Center said, prompting mandatory evacuations and disrupting oil and gas production. T
content:
**MIAMI, Florida** — Isaias strengthened to a Category 2 hurricane on Thursday as it headed toward the United States Gulf Coast, the US National Hurricane Center said, prompting mandatory evacuations and disrupting oil and gas production.

The first hurricane of the Atlantic season, Isaias is forecast to make landfall in Florida, Alabama or Mississippi on Friday night or early Saturday, the NHC said.

Isaias comes unusually late in the season, which began on June 1, partly due to a strong El Niño weather phenomenon.

*   [Trump: No new Iran attack before midterms](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/trump-no-new-iran-attack-before-midterms/2442642)

El Niño causes strong vertical wind shear, dry air and sinking air over the Atlantic Ocean, hampering storm formation and intensification in the area.

Mandatory evacuation orders have been issued for coastal areas in four counties in Florida, while states of emergency are in place in parts of Alabama, Florida and Georgia.

A hurricane warning was in effect from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Gulf County Line in Florida, the NHC said in its latest update.

A storm surge warning, which brings the danger of “life-threatening inundation,” was in effect for the mouth of the Mississippi River to the Suwannee River, it said.

title: Arms race for world peace?
summary: WILL war break out soon? Judging from war and peace-related news headlines, it would seem that countries are preparing for a high-tech war. Figure out the following: “China increases construction rate of amphibious assault ships with landin
content:
WILL war break out soon? Judging from war and peace-related news headlines, it would seem that countries are preparing for a high-tech war. Figure out the following: “China increases construction rate of amphibious assault ships with landing platform decks”... “Qatar to become first advanced medium-range air-to-air missile-extended range user”... France launched its first Barracuda nuclear-powered attack submarine”... “India launches combat game linked to Pakistan crisis”... “Sudan has the largest force in the Arab coalition”... “Iran credited new indigenous surface-to-air missile systems with Golden Hawk unmanned aerial vehicle shootdown”... “North Korea fires 2 more nuke missiles”... “Toughening up: Developing rugged military hardware and software”... “Nuclear war threat back”...

In our part of the world, there is an Asean (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) resolve to take greater responsibility for our own maritime security as the South China Sea (SCS) militarization issue gains worldwide attention and concern. In Brunei Darussalam, German-made offshore patrol vessels have considerably enhanced the navy’s operational capabilities. Indonesia has a marine base in Sulawesi island and is making submarine purchases. Its guided missile frigate Raden Eddy Martadinata has been fitted to accommodate anti-air missiles, anti-ship missiles and torpedoes for anti-submarine warfare. Singapore, which has the most potent military in the region, confirmed it will field 16 m-class unmanned surface vehicles on its future multirole combat missiles. It has the region’s first submarine rescue capacity.

The Philippines is also on a procurement drive. As part of its long-awaited military modernization program, the country is continuously acquiring weapons and equipment like frigates and aircraft, including jet fighters. Medium-lift transport and surveillance aircraft, new anti-submarine helicopters, fast support vessels have also been received. As Vietnam’s economy improves so does its defense procurements. Fighter aircraft, submarines, coastal radar system, maritime patrol helicopters and fast patrol vessels for its coast guard are now in its arsenal.

*   [The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

To upgrade its military hardware and material, Malaysia received its first Scorpene submarines as well as its military transport aircraft while Thailand, the first in Southeast Asia to acquire an aircraft carrier, has purchased a Saab Crippen fighter aircraft. It procured diesel-electric submarines to enhance its subsurface capabilities. Myanmar, despite the Tatmadaw’s (armed forces) preoccupation with an unending ethnic conflict, pursues its military modernization drive with allies Russia, China and India.

With the acquisition of modern military arms and equipment, naval exercises between and among Asean countries significantly increased to improve professionalism, develop exchange experience and draw lessons from fellow navies. Likewise, Asean countries have also committed to defense and diplomacy forums among its confidence-building activities. One such is the Asean Plus-Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADM-Plus), the Plus being Australia, China, India, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, Russia and the United States. To improve interoperability capabilities, there is an Information Fusion Center at the Singapore Navy manned by a bevy of multinational naval officers.

# Wipe Away Su Lee's Tears from her Composing Nights

Dear friends, music lovers, and new music supporters,It’s me, Su Lee, and I am currently working on my dissertation concert (for my Ph.D. in composition) which will be held on Sept. 9th 2019 Monday at 7:30pm in Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall at University at Buffalo.The title of my dissertation composition and concert is Die Radikalen Tasten (The Radical Keys) in terms of aesthetics, Klang (sound), and theme.I am writing a concerto for organ with keyboard ensemble, namely for our own tremendous Fisk Op.95 organ at UB. It will involve organ soloist with 1 assistant, 2 pianos (1 quarter-tone flat piano), 2 harpsichords (1 quarter-tone flat harpsichord), and 2 vibraphones which is a very rare instrumentation for microtonal new music. The 1st half of the program features significant keyboard works from the 20th century such as Messiaen's solo organ work and Ives's quarter-tone piano pieces. As a special request from Dr. Fuller, who was in charge of the installation of the Fisk Op.95 organ at UB, I'm playing my very first organ transcription of Wagner's orchestral work.The 2nd half of the program features my own 'radical' politically inspired compositions including a choral piece with organ accompaniment (dedicated to the UUCB Choir family) and my dissertation organ concerto. Both works are based on the Korean Democratic Uprising in May 1980 and the protest song written for the victims of the subsequent Gwangju massacre - a song that has became widely popular for activists and protesters, including those participating in the on-going Hong Kong protests.Overall, it is a very colorful and unique combination and a rare program which is a you-don’t-want-to-miss concert.I am modestly asking you for a little or big help in making my dissertation concert happen smoothly, especially given my financial struggles in not being able to even work legally for money off campus in America due to my visa status.Your generous donation will be spent towards, (besides helping me wipe away all my tears and whining from composing numerous nights over the past few months and rehearsing in the upcoming days and nights):Nine Musicians’ Performance Fee, about $3,000 – 3,300Rent/Labor for Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall, about $1,000Other concert related costs; buying performing materials, copying/binding score/parts, printing poster/program book, audio/video recording, photographing, tuning, reception, etc. about $1,200 – 1,500In Total $5,200 – 5,800Fortunately, I got awarded the MDRF (research fund) for $3,000 at UB so that I can be reimbursed afterwards, but I need money upfront now to pay first, and possibly more, to pay my dream team musicians fairly and to cover other costs.Your genuine help means SO MUCH to me being an international Ph.D. student with many restrictions on earning money (3 months summer break without job, seriously!), as it will lighten my financial burdens and psychological anxiety when I absolutely need to focus more on my creative activities. Simply speaking, you are contributing to a potentially "fabulous" new music piece, stimulating my further musical activities and making me believe that life (and the world) is so beautiful!Every single one of your names will be acknowledged in my concert program book, and to thank you all, but not nearly enough, I like to give you in return as below:$1~$49: a thank-you-card with a cover of a handwritten excerpt of my score$50~$99: a thank-you-card like above AND a dvd of my dissertation concert (after my concert)$100~$199: a thank-you-card AND a dvd like above, PLUS the autographed full score of my dissertation composition$200~$299: EVERYTHING above AND one additional dvd of my Masters organ recitals (your choice of “Über den Namen B-A-C-H” or “Celebrating Lou Harrison’s 100th Birth-Year at Thunder Night”)$300 or more: EVERYTHING above, PLUS a gift pack of Korean snacks/sweets/tea etc.Please write me an email with your home address!I am really excited to prepare my dissertation concert. Though I feel like this is sadly going to be my last self designed concert during my time in Buffalo (at UB), so I cannot wait to see many of you there!Thank you so much for reading this and considering your donation. I promise to pay you back with my "fabulous" new compositions and my performance, with the great help of my dream team of musician fellows!Please feel free to spread the link to your social pages like Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter, or to emails, to help get the word out! FYI, I am collecting your donations from now till October and GoFundMe takes 2.9% for transaction fee plus $0.30 PER Donation. Or you can donate by sending me a check to my place (email me for asking my address please!)Fondly,Su Lee

title: Microsoft brings more AI to PCs to challenge Apple
summary: SAN FRANCISCO, California — Microsoft unveiled on Wednesday an artificial intelligence (AI) coding model that can run directly on personal computers and new security technology to prevent AI agents from accessing data without permission, ch
content:
SAN FRANCISCO, California — Microsoft unveiled on Wednesday an artificial intelligence (AI) coding model that can run directly on personal computers and new security technology to prevent AI agents from accessing data without permission, challenging Apple’s push to bring more AI into personal devices.

The software company also presented at the event in San Francisco a high-powered Surface laptop called Ultra powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark chips. Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft is seeking to turn Windows into a platform for AI agents to handle tasks such as writing computer code or tackling complex business projects on desktops and laptops.

For Microsoft, the move represents a bet that some work that currently happens in its costly Azure cloud computing data centers can shift to high-powered Windows machines in businesses and homes, a market where the firm retains a stronghold — and where its customers foot the hardware bills. It is a market opportunity rival Apple is also chasing with new Mac computers.

*   [Semirara: Revised auction rules unfair](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/business/corporate-news/semirara-revised-auction-rules-unfair/2441199)

For Nvidia, cracking the Windows PC market could help it go after one of the last major markets dominated by Intel and Advanced Micro Devices.

As a guardrail against increasing­ly autonomous AI agents that have created security risks, Microsoft said it was releasing Microsoft Execution Containers, a tool to prevent agents from accessing data and doing unauthorized tasks when running on a laptop or desktop machine. Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia will use the tools, said Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president for Windows and devices.

**“We needed to make the desktop the most secure place for agents to execute,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said.**

Davuluri said new tools would let IT departments set rules for agents, and the Windows operating system would enforce those rules on each employee’s machine.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who joined Nadella on stage, said Microsoft’s new execution container technology, which goes by MXC for short, “is going to revolutionize how agents are built and deployed.”

“Without it, [agents are] a complete nonstarter,” he said.

Nvidia is trying to prevent a repeat of the hack of AI hub Hugging Face, while Apple is looking to tighten up the process for giving AI agents full access to a Mac computer’s hard drive.

**AI moves to the PC**

Microsoft also unveiled AI models that previously required cloud access but can now run locally on high-powered Windows desktops and laptops, including Nvidia’s open-source Nemotron model. Davuluri said a version of Chinese AI firm DeepSeek’s V4 model can run on machines with at least 60 gigabytes of memory and outperform OpenAI’s GPT-5 on some coding and reasoning tasks.

Microsoft is taking a similar approach with its own Copilot AI assistant, splitting tasks between the cloud and individual laptops. “Copilot will still use the cloud for the hardest tasks, but for times when cost or privacy matter more, it can delegate down to local models that run directly on your computer,” said Microsoft’s Copilot chief Jacob Andreou.

Davuluri also said Meta’s Muse personal assistant will come to Windows devices as a native app, using some of Microsoft’s new security tools, and that OpenClaw, the open-source AI agent system, can also work with those security tools.

title: VIDEO | Shielding illegal fishers? Manila hits out as Chinese vessels block operation
summary: An illegal fishing vessel intercepted by Philippine forces near Thitu Island in the South China Sea Jay Tarriela / Philippine Coast Guard [![Image 1: Reuters](https://media.assettype.com/bairdmaritime%2F2024-12-02%2F7e0yqzaz%2Freuters_logo_
content:
An illegal fishing vessel intercepted by Philippine forces near Thitu Island in the South China Sea Jay Tarriela / Philippine Coast Guard

[![Image 1: Reuters](https://media.assettype.com/bairdmaritime%2F2024-12-02%2F7e0yqzaz%2Freuters_logo_icon_170782.png?w=48&auto=format%2Ccompress)](https://www.bairdmaritime.com/author/reuters)

Published on:

05 Oct 2026, 10:23 am

The Philippine Coast Guard said on Sunday Chinese vessels obstructed a Philippine law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near the Manila-held Thitu Island in the South China Sea.

It described the presence of a Chinese navy helicopter as an "unnecessary act of intimidation". It was the latest in a series of recent maritime confrontations between Manila and Beijing.

The operation involved personnel from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Philippine Navy and Philippine National Police Maritime Group responding to a report of suspected blast fishing near Sandy Cays two and three, about three nautical miles west of Thitu Island, known in the Philippines as Pag-asa.

The PCG said two China Coast Guard vessels sounded their horns, radio-challenged the Philippine team and later shadowed and blocked its boats. A People's Liberation Army Navy helicopter also circled above the Philippine personnel four times.

The Philippine team ordered the foreign fishing vessel to stop and radioed it several times, but the vessel ignored the orders and sailed southwest towards Subi Reef, one of seven artificial islands China has built in the Spratlys to support its sovereignty claims.

Philippine authorities ended the pursuit for safety reasons and returned to Thitu.

The PCG said the China Coast Guard had "no law enforcement authority" in the territorial sea of Thitu and said its actions, "made it easier for a suspected violator to escape". It also rejected any Chinese claim that its vessels had been expelled from the area.

At just 37 hectares (0.14 square miles), the coral-fringed Thitu is the largest and most prized of the nine Philippines-held features in the Spratly archipelago, located 450 kilometres (280 miles) from the mainland.

Separately, the military said a Chinese J-16 fighter jet repeatedly approached and manoeuvred close to a Philippine patrol aircraft over the disputed Scarborough Shoal on Saturday, creating an aviation safety risk.

The Armed Forces of the Philippines said the incident was part of a "recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behaviour" against Philippine vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations.

The Chinese Embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the weekend incidents.

_(Reporting by Karen Lema ; Additional reporting by Greg Torode; Editing by Sonali Paul)_
