title: Minimum wage for HK domestic workers rises 2.35%, but advocate says still ‘far from’ a living wage
summary: Hong Kong has raised the minimum wage for the city’s more than 380,000 foreign domestic workers by 2.35 per cent, from HK$5,100 to HK$5,220 per month, the government has announced. Domestic workers in Central. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The
content: Hong Kong has raised the minimum wage for the city’s more than 380,000 foreign domestic workers by 2.35 per cent, from HK$5,100 to HK$5,220 per month, the government has announced. Domestic workers in Central. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The government also said on Friday that the food allowance for domestic workers – which employers must pay if they do not already provide free meals – will remain unchanged at no less than HK$1,236 per month. The new minimum wage will apply to all contracts signed on or after Saturday, October 3. The government said it had carefully assessed the views of employers and domestic workers before coming to the decision of the 2.35 per cent increase. Last year, the minimum wage was upped by 2.2 per cent. “This year’s socio-economic factors are more favourable than those at the time of last year’s review,” a government spokesperson added. ‘Far from’ living wage But the rise fell short of demands by groups representing domestic workers, who have called for an increase in the minimum wage to HK$6,172 – a 21 per cent hike. The Asian Migrants Coordinating Body (AMCB) has also demanded that the monthly food allowance be more than doubled to HK$3,123 – equivalent to roughly HK$100 per day. AMCB spokesperson Sringatin said on Friday that the HK$120 increase was a result of the collective struggle of migrant workers’ movement in the city. However, “the HK$5,220 is far from the HK$6,172 living wage in Hong Kong,” she told HKFP. “The piecemeal increase will give a very little relief with our long-standing sufferings and burden because of the rapid increase of inflation and standard living [in Hong Kong],” she said. “While no increase in food allowance will mean more expenses and loss in the wage of [domestic workers] who have no food at employer’s house,” she added. See also: Hong Kong workers see real salary growth slow to 1.1% in post-pandemic low The government typically announces the adjustments to domestic workers’ minimum wage in September following an annual review, but this year’s announcement was delayed . The government says it takes into account an array of factors, such as Hong Kong’s economy, labour market conditions, affordability for employers and basic living needs of domestic workers, when reviewing the minimum wage.

title: Greenpeace urges HK gov’t to cut Po Pin Chau visitor quota after Nat. Day overcrowding
summary: Environmental NGO Greenpeace has urged the government to review its ecotourism policies and reduce visitor quotas for a popular Sai Kung trail after finding overcrowding and damage on the first day of the Golden Week holiday. Tourists stand
content: Environmental NGO Greenpeace has urged the government to review its ecotourism policies and reduce visitor quotas for a popular Sai Kung trail after finding overcrowding and damage on the first day of the Golden Week holiday. Tourists stand on the Po Pin Chau viewing platform on October 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The green group said in a statement that Sai Kung’s Po Pin Chau trail saw overcrowding on Thursday, which marked China’s National Day and the beginning of a weeklong holiday for the mainland. This comes in spite of a recently established reservation system for the hiking hotspo t. Crowds caused erosion along the trail, the NGO said, with plants trampled underfoot and rampant littering in the form of plastic bottles, tissues, and food remains. Some tourists were suspected of defecating on the natural beauty site, the group added. Littering on Po Pin Chau, Sai Kung on October 1, 2026. Photo: Greenpeace. Hong Kong’s Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), which looks after the territory’s country parks, introduced a real-name booking system for the trail last month to curb overtourism. Under the scheme, visitors planning to visit between 9am and 5pm on weekends and public holidays from September through October 7 must book in advance, with entry capped at 2,000 visitors per day. Authorities earlier announced that some days of the National Day Golden Week holiday were already fully booked . The AFCD said on Facebook that around 1,160 people visited the Po Pin Chau trail on Thursday, and the overall situation was “generally smooth and well-ordered.” However, Greenpeace staff inspected the site at 8am on Thursday and found that many tourists rushed up the mountain before 9am to beat the restriction. “Some ignored safety warnings and climbed over fences to take photos, creating dangerous situations,” Greenpeace said in a Chinese-language statement. “Some took shortcuts off the main trail for convenience, trampling and damaging adjacent vegetation, and some visitors were even found defecating by a cliffside beach, raising serious hygiene concerns.” Greenpeace notices tourist suspected of defecating in Po Pin Chau, Sai Kung on October 1, 2026. Photo: Greenpeace. At around noon on Thursday, the NGO counted 64 people on the Po Pin Chau viewing platform, which was designed for only 25 people. HKFP has reached out to the AFCD for comment. ‘Conservation-first ecotourism policy’ Greenpeace has urged the government to reduce the current daily limit of 2,000 reservations for the Po Pin Chau trail, and to consider temporarily closing down damaged sections of the site or even seasonal closures to let the area recover. Tourists on the Po Pin Chau trail on October 1, 2026. Photo: Greenpeace. The group said authorities should adopt “a conservation-first ecotourism policy.” “This should include carrying-capacity studies on ecologically sensitive areas across Hong Kong to formulate corresponding management measures and ensure truly sustainable ecotourism,” the Greenpeace statement stated.

title: (EDITORIAL from The Korea Times on Oct. 13)
summary: Pitfalls of Lee's social media outreach President must focus on message of unity, not division President Lee Jae Myung has expressed his willingness to strengthen direct communication with the Korean public, saying he will use social media
content:
Pitfalls of Lee's social media outreach
President must focus on message of unity, not division

President Lee Jae Myung has expressed his willingness to strengthen direct communication with the Korean public, saying he will use social media more actively than before.

An aide explained that Lee was inspired by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum. During his recent summit with the Mexican leader, Lee reportedly learned that Sheinbaum makes it a rule to hold four press conferences and conduct three on-site visits every week to interact with citizens. Her active public outreach has become a source of inspiration for Lee.

A president's efforts to engage directly with the public are encouraging and desirable. Such communication can help dispel public misunderstandings about government policies and give citizens a better understanding of the administration's objectives.

Despite these benefits, however, Lee should remember that presidential social media accounts are not private chatrooms. They are platforms through which a president should convey messages of hope and unity, rather than provoke division or controversy.

For politicians, direct communication with the public is a double-edged sword. Depending on how it is used, it can make or break their political careers. Used wisely, it can help politicians explain and defend their policies effectively and persuade the public of their merits.

Direct public engagement can also reflect a politician's confidence and command of the issues. Politicians who communicate directly with citizens often face situations in which they must respond quickly to unexpected questions or criticism. The better informed they are, the more readily they can provide convincing answers.

The opposite, however, is also true. Given the weight of presidential rhetoric, impromptu remarks can be risky because a president's words are difficult to retract once they have been made public. This is one of the pitfalls of direct, on-the-spot communication by political leaders.

Lee is already an active social media user. So far this month, he averaged six posts a day on X (formerly Twitter), publishing 65 posts between Oct. 1 and 11. On Saturday, he vowed to continue sharing his views on social media despite criticism from those who consider his online activities inappropriate. "I will continue to visit back alleys and do my direct communications with the public," he wrote.

Lee also invoked the late former President Roh Moo-hyun to draw a parallel between their experiences. He noted that Roh, too, faced criticism and even ridicule while engaging with a social media user who challenged him. On Sunday, Lee wrote that the late former Seoul Mayor Park Won-soon had reminded him of the importance of social media as a means for politicians to communicate with citizens.

Yet Lee's social media posts have often generated controversy rather than fostered constructive and healthy debate on policy issues. On Oct. 9, he criticized a group of unnamed politicians for harboring excessive ambitions despite their limited qualifications.

"They are radical. This is relatively an insignificant problem, compared to the fundamental one they had. They wanted highly coveted positions which go far beyond their capabilities. They turned into critics from within after their requests were ignored," he wrote.

Although Lee did not identify the individuals, his remarks appeared to target hard-liners within the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) who criticized what they described as his "lukewarm" and "passive" approach to prosecutorial reform. Rep. Kim Yong-min, a DPK lawmaker regarded as one of the hard-liners, responded swiftly on social media, saying he had entered politics not to secure a plum job but to achieve prosecutorial reform.

On Sunday, Lee criticized another unnamed politician for allegedly ignoring the hardships and basic needs of working-class citizens. He said the politician had cut welfare spending intended for working-class families. Once again, Lee did not name the person, but his remarks appeared to be directed at Gyeonggi Province Gov. Choo Mi-ae who had cut the child care budget, citing a shortage of financial resources.

So far, Lee's social media-driven politics has raised eyebrows because his posts have been overly personal and confrontational. Rather than promoting constructive discussion, they have fueled divisions within the ruling party and risked deepening political polarization. What does Lee stand to gain if his social media posts repeatedly trigger controversy?

A president's social media account is not a private space. As the head of state and government, Lee must recognize that his online presence carries official weight. Every word he posts can have political consequences and shape public perceptions of his administration. He should therefore exercise caution and prudence in his online communications.

Direct engagement with citizens can be a valuable tool for a president, but its purpose should be to build trust and bring people together. Lee should use social media to promote national unity, not deepen divisions.
(END)

title: America’s Adversaries Are Attacking Sideways
summary: America’s Adversaries Are Attacking Sideways bbert@hudson.org Mon, 10/12/2026 - 09:59 SVG Commentary Oct 10, 2026 The Hill America’s Adversaries Are Attacking Sideways Peter Rough Senior Fellow and Director, Center on Europe and Eurasia Pet
content: America’s Adversaries Are Attacking Sideways bbert@hudson.org Mon, 10/12/2026 - 09:59 SVG Commentary Oct 10, 2026 The Hill America’s Adversaries Are Attacking Sideways Peter Rough Senior Fellow and Director, Center on Europe and Eurasia Peter Rough Commentary Caption Russia's President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian hold a meeting in Turkmenbashi on October 8, 2026. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print When the U.S. imposed tariffs on China in April 2025, Beijing  restricted exports  of rare earth elements and magnets, threatening allied supply chains around the world in a campaign that continues to this day.  When the U.S. and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February, Tehran  expanded the battlefield  to the Gulf states.   Last month, European Union defense ministers  gathered in Brussels to grapple with the rising threat of grey-zone attacks. Even the normally taciturn Swiss government is  raising the alarm about Russian actions. The August discovery of an  explosive-laden drone  at Germany’s Leipzig Airport underscores the larger pattern: Beijing, Tehran and Moscow are increasingly using horizontal escalation to challenge U.S. influence.   Horizontal escalation — the expansion of a conflict to new geographic regions or domains of competition — presents a vexing challenge for American policymakers. Washington tends to organize its policies vertically, into separate domains: NATO, trade policy and Taiwan. America’s adversaries are going sideways, operating across these domains rather than solely within them.  China, Russia and Iran differ greatly in their capabilities and objectives, but each seeks to overturn the U.S.-built international order.   Xi Jinping often  speaks of  “major changes unseen in a century.” In 2023, Xi famously invoked this same idea while standing beside Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow,  exhorting  the Russian leader, “Let’s push it forward together.”   To pursue their aims, America’s opponents sometimes cooperate. Tehran supplied Moscow with  key drone capabilities  when Russia was at its weakest in Ukraine. Russia, in turn, has provided Iran with sophisticated military assistance. Moscow is   reportedly helping Tehran develop supersonic cruise missiles. China has helped blunt U.S. pressure on both Russia and Iran by  supplying  Moscow with essential dual-use items for its defense industry and by remaining a major buyer of sanctioned Iranian oil. But U.S. adversaries support each other even without coordinating formally. Russia’s war consumes Western air defense missiles. Iran ties down American aircraft, ships and interceptors in the Middle East. China’s military buildup forces Washington to preserve scarce capabilities for a possible contingency in the South China Sea. Each of these efforts absorbs American resources that cannot be deployed somewhere else. This exposes a vulnerability of American power. U.S. alliances multiply American strength and expand its reach. But a global system of allies also presents Washington’s adversaries with more targets. An opponent that is unable or unwilling to confront the U.S. directly can threaten a weaker ally, sabotage its infrastructure or disrupt its supply chains.  To meet this challenge, the U.S. and its allies must first deny adversaries easy opportunities for horizontal escalation. Diversify what is vulnerable, harden what cannot be diversified, build deeper stocks of scarce military capabilities and require allies capable of carrying more of the burden to do so.   But resilience should not be the only strategy. The U.S. cannot defend every vulnerability at all times, and trying to do so would hand its adversaries a permanent advantage. Instead, Washington and its allies should develop horizontal escalation options of their own.   Russian acts of sabotage against European infrastructure should trigger costs in domains the Kremlin values — weapons transfers to Ukraine, restrictions on Russian finance, seizures of sanctions-busting assets. An adversary may choose where to apply pressure, but it should not be allowed to choose where the consequences fall.  As EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius  explained , “if we are facing painful hybrid threats or actions, our answer should be painful in a similar way … Not similar means [necessarily], but pain should be at the same level.” In the wake of the Leipzig incident, for example, Germany announced that it had shipped additional IRIS-T air defense missiles and attack drones to Ukraine.   This same logic should shape competition with China and Iran. Economic coercion need not be answered only with economic measures, and gray-zone attacks need not be met only at the site of the attack. America’s responses should create uncertainty in adversaries’ minds about where and how the U.S. and its allies will respond.   Horizontal escalation can also strengthen the bonds that connect U.S. allies. By imposing costs on countries other than the U.S., America’s adversaries may inadvertently provide Washington’s disparate partners with a common cause.  When China retaliated against U.S. tariffs by cutting European supply chains, Washington responded by forging a new  critical minerals partnership  with Europe. China’s support for Iran and Russia’s assistance to North Korea can likewise push the Gulf states and America’s Asian allies to reassess their relationships with Beijing and Moscow. In trying to expand a conflict horizontally, America’s adversaries may also be expanding the coalition arrayed against them.   Combating horizontal escalation will require Washington’s allies to guard against sabotage and coercion, assume a greater share of the deterrence burden and coordinate more closely to protect critical technologies and supply chains. But it also requires American leadership and dependability to ensure that openness remains a source of power for the West rather than a vulnerability.  America’s adversaries have learned to go sideways. The U.S. and its allies must show a willingness to do the same.    Read in The Hill. Enjoyed this analysis? Subscribe to Hudson’s newsletters to stay up to date with our latest content. title: Yonhap News Summary
summary: The following is the second summary of major stories moved by Yonhap News Agency on Monday. ----------------- ■ Lee's move to Cheong Wa Dae residence planned for this year SEOUL -- President Lee Jae Myung's move to the official presidential
content:
The following is the second summary of major stories moved by Yonhap News Agency on Monday.

-----------------

■ Lee's move to Cheong Wa Dae residence planned for this year

SEOUL -- President Lee Jae Myung's move to the official presidential residence at Cheong Wa Dae is being planned for this year, an official said Monday.

Lee and first lady Kim Hea Kyung have been living at the official residence used by former President Yoon Suk Yeol in Seoul's Yongsan Ward while refurbishments take place at Cheong Wa Dae.

[https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012007500315?section=national/politics](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012007500315?section=national/politics)

-----------------

■ Unification minister says S. Korea-U.S. alliance intact despite conflicting interests

SEOUL -- Unification Minister Chung Dong-young dismissed concerns Monday that the South Korea-U.S. alliance is weakening, saying the two allies share common values even when their interests diverge.

Chung made the remarks during a meeting with reporters, as the opposition has accused him of undermining the alliance, citing controversy over U.S. restrictions on intelligence-sharing with South Korea following his remarks about a suspected North Korean uranium enrichment facility in Kusong and other issues.

[https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012005300315?section=national/diplomacy](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012005300315?section=national/diplomacy)

-----------------

■ (2nd LD) Seoul shares plunge over 3 pct on tech sell-off amid Mideast, inflation woes

SEOUL -- Seoul shares plunged more than 3 percent Monday, extending their losing streak to a fourth session, as a massive sell-off in technology stocks fueled by inflation concerns weighed on the market amid elevated oil prices.

The Korean won rose against the U.S. dollar.

[https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012007400320?section=economy-finance/finance](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012007400320?section=economy-finance/finance)

-----------------

■ Military manpower agency chief voices regret over Asian Games footballers' gloating about military exemption

SEOUL -- The head of South Korea's military manpower agency voiced regret Monday over South Korean footballers glorying in their exemption from mandatory military service following their win at the recent Asian Games.

Military Manpower Administration (MMA) Commissioner Hong So-young made the remarks during a parliamentary audit, after some of the gold medalists gloated about their exemptions in media interviews and on social media, sparking strong public backlash and reigniting calls for policy overhaul.

[https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012005100315?section=national/defense](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012005100315?section=national/defense)

content:
2026年10月10日，台湾总统赖清德在台北总统府举行的“双十节”庆典上发表演说。（图片来源：I-Hwa Cheng / AFP via Getty Images）

【看中国2026年10月10日讯】（看中国记者李净瑶报导）今天（10日）是中华民国115年国庆，赖清德总统发表国庆演说表示，在战争与威权扩张、全球秩序快速变动的时代，[台湾](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%8F%B0%E6%B9%BE)应勇敢自信打造“山巅之城”，这不是对自己的赞美，而是对国家未来的期许，也是台湾愿意承担的责任。台湾不求霸权，也不追求支配他人，台湾深知冲突的代价，因此选择以坚持和平为己任，做国际社会可信赖的稳定力量。

中华民国国庆大会10月10日上午在台北总统府前广场登场，[赖清德](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E8%B5%96%E6%B8%85%E5%BE%B7)总统以“台湾 山巅之城，地上的盐，世上的光”为题，发表国庆演说，议题触及少子女化、能源、毒品、区域和平、美中关系、五大信赖产业等。这也是赖清德发表就职总统以来第三次国庆演说。

以下为赖清德致词全文：

[![Image 2](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2025/7-29/p3676411a560438137.jpg)](https://www.naturenergy.us/)

大会主席立法院韩国瑜院长、萧美琴副总统、行政院卓荣泰院长、史瓦帝尼王国恩史瓦帝三世国王陛下、祖玛王妃殿下、“日本台湾友好议员联盟”古屋圭司会长、友邦、友好国家的庆贺团团长、各国驻台使节、海内外贵宾，现场以及收看电视和直播的国人同胞，大家好！

今天，我们齐聚在总统府前，一起庆祝中华民国国庆，共同为台湾喝采，祝福我们的国家，生日快乐，国运昌隆！

此时此刻，无论我们人在台湾，或身处世界不同角落；无论我们来自不同世代、不同职业，抱持不同的政治立场，我们都立足在同一个台湾；也共同承担一份责任，就是让我们的国家更安全、社会更安定、人民生活更美好，让下一个世代对未来充满希望。

今年，是台湾总统直选30周年。30年前，面对飞弹威胁，台湾人民依然勇敢走进投票所，完成台湾人民“当家作主”的百年追求，用手中的选票告诉全世界：这个国家的主人，是人民；台湾的未来，要由台湾人民自己决定。

30年来，我们走过民主转型，经历政党轮替，也承受许多挑战。今天，我们更加确信，自由民主与经济发展不会背道而驰。台湾越是拥抱民主、迎向世界，就越能创造繁荣，也越有能力为世界做出贡献。

过去一年，世界并不平静。战争与威权持续扩张，全球经济面临关税、能源以及红色供应链的多重挑战。然而，台湾没有退缩，反而在变局中站稳脚步，展现令人骄傲的韧性。

就像台湾健儿在亚运表现精采。余凯文跟黄诗媛在软网场上，一球又一球拚出第一面金牌；王冠闳在泳池里破浪，游出我们28年的期望；还有傅兆玄，在大雨里腾空一跃，跃出田径60年来最荣耀的一刻。林郁婷也不负所望，连续两届勇夺金牌。谢淑薇与梁恩硕、詹皓晴与吴芳嫺更在网球女双金包银，所有的运动选手，表现都非常精彩，谢谢你们，让世界看见台湾的韧性与骄傲。

感谢百工百业的打拚，经济表现也非常亮眼。今年，光是上半年，最新的经济成长率，达到百分之14.15。而全年的经济成长率更有望突破百分之11，创下39年新高；今年，我们的人均GDP，预估也将达到4万5,332美元，几乎是2016年的两倍。我们的台股指数冲上4万9千点，成为全球第四大股市。

在外交上，台湾也一步一步走得更远。

今年，我前往史瓦帝尼王国进行国是访问，感谢恩史瓦帝三世国王陛下的热情接待，以及王母陛下与全国人民的热烈欢迎，见证双方在能源、农业、医疗、妇女赋权以及教育文化上的合作；萧美琴副总统访问帕劳，深化医疗、农渔业、基础建设以及永续观光的成果，并应邀赴意大利出席文托泰内欧洲自由与民主论坛，让台湾的声音在象征欧洲自由与民主的重要场域被世界听见。

而在今年瑞士洛桑管理学院的世界竞争力排名中，台湾在“经济表现”、“政府效能”、“企业效能”与“基础建设”都名列前茅，一举冲上全球第四最具竞争力的国家，创下有史以来最好的成绩。

这些成就，毫无疑问，属于两千三百万台湾人民；也是政府携手无数台湾人民，多年来不分领域，共同努力，一点一滴所勤奋打拚的成果。我要邀请所有国人同胞，再次用热烈的掌声，为自己喝采。

在战争与威权扩张、全球秩序快速变动的时代，台湾应该成为什么样的国家？

我的答案是：勇敢自信的打造“[山巅之城](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%B1%B1%E5%B7%85%E4%B9%8B%E5%9F%8E)”!

这不只是对自己的赞美，而是我们对国家未来的期许，也是台湾愿意承担的责任。

各位国人同胞，山巅之城，是建造在护国群山之上，是民主治理的美好成果，让人民在坚实的基础上安心生活；因此，一座山巅之城不能只有耀眼的天际线，更要有稳固的地基。

台湾的地基，就是人民的生活。国家是否进步，不能只看产值与出口，更要看劳工待遇有没有提高、家庭负担有没有减轻、长辈是否受到照顾，以及年轻人是否相信，努力就能创造更好的未来。

因此，我们以务实治理，推动加薪、减税、增福利、少负担，让这个国家里的每一个人，都能站得稳、过得好。

面对少子女化，政府在“0到6岁国家一起养”的基础上，提出“台湾人口对策新战略—家庭支持篇”，从生育、养育到教育，以加补助、减负担、多弹性、增照顾，建立更完整的家庭支持。

我们规划从明年开始，推动0到18岁成长津贴，每个孩子每月5千元，并结合生育给付、人工生殖补助、平价托育、友善职场与婚育住宅，让工作与家庭，不再成为年轻人被迫二选一的难题。

养育孩子，不应该是一个家庭孤军奋战。支持一个家庭，就是守护台湾的未来。

面对超高龄社会，我们推动“健康台湾”国家政策，从癌症筛检、智慧医疗、在宅照护，到改善医疗工作环境与护理人力，让国人不只活得长寿，也要活得健康。

今年上路的长照3.0，进一步整合医疗、社福、社区与科技，让长辈在熟悉的生活圈获得照顾，也让上有老、下有小的三明治世代，多一分支持，少一分辛苦。

面对居住压力，我们持续推动“百万租屋家庭支持计划”，透过直接兴建社会住宅、包租代管、租金补贴，还有新增都市更新分回及容积奖励等多元方式增加供给，并调升婚育宅比例、实施青安3.0，提高婚育家庭贷款额度。安居才能乐业，安居也才能让年轻人勇敢成家，追求梦想。

面对缺工与人才不足，我们推动“跨国劳动力精进方案”，坚持本国劳工为主、跨国劳动力为辅，以加薪连动增聘人力，放宽资深移工转任技术人力的留用限制，并推动国对国直接聘雇。

我们也修正《外国专业人才延揽及雇用法》，扩大国际人才与外籍生来台、留台的机会。让企业补足人力，也让劳工提高待遇；让人才愿意来，也愿意留下来。

社会安全，同样是这座山巅之城不可动摇的根基。

面对诈骗，我们将行政院打击诈欺指挥中心列为常设性任务编组，整合内政、法务、数发与金融监理力量，串联检察、金融及平台业者，从广告、通讯、帐户到金流，阻断犯罪链。

面对毒品与毒驾，政府持续推动“新世代反毒策略行动纲领”，强化缉毒、验毒、戒毒、识毒与防毒，向上追查毒品来源，并运用唾液毒品快筛加强路检，即时阻止危险驾驶。人民辛苦累积的财产、每一个家庭珍贵的生命，政府都要全力守护。

政府也积极推动修法，毒驾初犯最高罚15万；拒绝临测，重罚27万；累犯罚款不设上限，一律吊销驾照，强制没入车辆，同车乘客，也将连带受罚。政府会从严执法，绝不寛贷。

面对能源与气候挑战，我们以稳定供电、能源安全以及净零转型为目标，推动多元绿能、储能、节能与电网强韧建设，也会依科学证据、法定程序及安全标准，务实评估各种能源选项。

能源政策不能建立在口号上，必须建立在安全、专业和责任上；我们不为意识形态排除选项，也不会为短期利益牺牲世代永续。

山巅之城的高度，不是政府自己宣告的，而是由人民的生活，一层一层筑起。我们要让世界看见，民主不只有选择的自由，更有解决问题、照顾人民的能力。

各位国人同胞，山巅之城，必须固若金汤，全民团结一心，是维护印太和平与稳定的关键力量。

就像盐虽然微小，却能调和百味、防腐保鲜。台湾的国土不大，但我们守护民主、自由、人权及法治，不让威权侵蚀珍贵的普世价值。

我们不求霸权，也不追求支配他人。我们深知冲突的代价，因此选择以坚持和平为己任，做国际社会可信赖的稳定力量。

然而，和平不能只靠愿望，包容也不能成为侵略者得寸进尺的理由。

中国持续以军事与灰色地带行动施压，企图改变台海现状。面对威权扩张，台湾的坚持，不只关乎自己的生存，也关乎国际社会是否仍然相信：武力不能凌驾规则，强权不能剥夺人民决定未来的权利。

因此，我们持续推动国防改革，强化不对称战力，发展国防自主产业，让半导体、资通讯与精密制造的优势，转化为守护国家的力量。

我们也透过全社会防卫韧性的准备，整合中央、地方与民间量能，提升能源、通讯、交通、金融、粮食与医疗的持续运作能力。让危机来临时，社会能够稳定运作，人民知道如何保护自己、协助彼此。

我要感谢所有国军官兵、后备军人、警察、消防、医护、民防，以及参与演练的国人。你们每一次认真的准备，都是为台湾的和平，多筑起一道防线。

我们增加国防投资，不是为了挑衅，而是为了吓阻战争；我们强化自我防卫，不是放弃对话，而是确保对话能在对等、尊严的基础上进行。

我们乐见美中透过对话来管理竞争，降低冲突及战争的风险，但是，我们也必须指出，要维护区域的安全、和平与稳定，不但要正确理解历史的发展，绝不容许扭曲二战历史，也要尊重台湾人民生存的权利，更要结合印太地区民主国家的共同力量，不让区域和平稳定的现状被改变。

台湾珍惜和平，但不会放弃自由；台湾愿意交流，但不会接受矮化。

台湾展现决心，不让威权侵蚀民主，不让恐惧取代自由，以坚定而负责任的行动，守护台海与印太的和平稳定现状。

各位国人同胞，山巅之城，城门要向世界自由开放，让世界的光照进城里；城中的光，则以创新、平等与良善，为世界带来希望。

光，不只照亮自己，也让他人看见方向。台湾的光，来自人民的智慧与勤奋，来自产业的创新，也来自我们愿意与世界分享成果的选择。

从传统产业到先进半导体，台湾用实力证明，一个资源有限的国家，也能成为全球繁荣不可或缺的力量。

但我们不会停在今天的成就，行政院正加速推动13项核心战略产业，涵盖半导体、人工智能、军工、安控、次世代通讯等五大信赖产业；以及矽光子、量子运算、机器人等AI新十大建设所聚焦的三大核心科技，还有关键矿物、生技医疗、亚洲资产管理中心、基础公共建设及都市更新、文化创意、兆元观光等6项重点产业，来确保台湾下一个世代的竞争优势；也透过千亿元规模的中小微企业多元振兴发展计划，提供融资、人才培训、数位转型、净零升级与国际通路支持。

科技产业要继续向前，也要带着传统产业一起走；龙头企业要走向世界，也要带动供应链在台湾扎根。台湾不能只有一座护国神山，而要让百工百业共同成为护国群山。

经济的光，也必须照进人民的生活。我们连续11年调升基本工资，军公教10年来5次调薪，也在今年调升专业与主管加给，透过加薪诱因与社会支持，让成长转化为更好的待遇、更少的负担；也规划在明年财政稳健的基础上，普发每人1万元AI红利；老农津贴每人每月1万元，国民年金每人每月5千元；弱势家庭等六大社福津贴，也全面提升，让全民共享经济发展的成果。

台湾的光，不只来自科技，更来自我们如何对待每一个人。

亚洲第一个实现同性婚姻合法化的国家就是台湾。我们要继续推动性别平权，让每个人不因性别、族群、背景或身分而被排除，都能有尊严地生活，自由地追求幸福。

在国际上，我们以医疗、农业、能源、科技、教育与永续发展合作，回应伙伴的需要。台湾的专业与善意，化为改善生活的实际行动。

“Taiwan Can Help”，不是一句口号，而是我们愿意分享能力、承担责任的承诺。台湾的光，要跨越国界，让更多需要帮助的人，感受到温暖与希望。

亲爱的国人同胞，再过不久，我们将迎来九合一地方选举，选贤与能、不受威胁利诱是我们共同的责任；政党可以竞争，意见可以不同，但我们立足的台湾，不应因此被分割。

山巅之城，不是因为没有分歧才发光，而是因为即使意见不同，我们仍然尊重彼此，相信制度，也愿意共同守护国家。

总统的权力，来自人民的讬付；总统的责任，就是凝聚力量，带领国家继续向前。

我会以务实治理，筑起山巅之城；以坚定的民主与防卫力量，成为守护和平的盐；以创新、平等与良善，成为温暖世界的光。

各位国人同胞，让我们团结一起，为下一个30年的台湾：

打下更坚实的基础，

更有竞争力的优势，

让下一代站得更稳、走得更远。

中华民国加油！台湾加油！

谢谢大家。

# HELP BRING MY SON BACK HOME

My name is Nelson Wells, Sr. and I write to you on behalf of my wife, Cynthia Wells, and our family, asking for your assistance in our fight to bring home our son, Nelson Wells, Jr., who has been unjustly imprisoned in China for more than eight years. We are natives of Louisiana, who have served our country for decades. I served in the United States Army for more than 20 years, and Cynthia, served at the Department of Defense for nearly 28 years. We’ve traveled all over the United States and world and have a host of extended family and friends, who join us in the fight for our son. This includes Nelson’s wife and three children, who are desperate to have him returned to our family unit. Like us, Nelson, Jr. loved to travel, and it was this love of travel that inspired him to live in Japan and visit China. Unfortunately, it was on one of these visits there that Nelson was arrested and later convicted on a drug charge with little evidence of his guilt, opportunity to defend himself, or due process prior to this conviction and incarceration. He was stripped of his freedom without the opportunity to tell his story. Indeed, it took months for us to learn what happened to him. We’ve fought for years to help our son, working behind the scenes with advocates, lawyers and diplomatic officials in the United States and China. We were told that this quiet strategy was the best strategy to keep him safe, but after nearly a decade with little progress, we’ve decided to tell our story, Nelson’s story. It breaks our heart to say it, but Nelson is now sick. The weight of incarceration has taken a toll on his physical and mental health. As you can see from the photos, our child has gone from a healthy man to an emaciated one, who has lost more than 100lbs and is in poor health. He is suffering from life-threatening medical problems in a prison in Chongqing Southwest China far from us, far from his wife and children. Indeed, we have not seen him during these eight long years. We are sustained by periodic calls from him, and for that, we are thankful to God, the United States State Department, and the Chinese government and prison officials. Still, we fear that he will not last much longer. It is time to bring Nelson home, perhaps through medical parole. Whatever the pathway, getting help for him is more urgent now than ever and so we are turning to the public for help with legal fees and welfare support on his behalf. No amount is too small, and we promise that your donations will only be used to directly secure the release and return of our son. We also invite you to leave a comment alongside your donation with a note of inspiration that we can share with Nelson, a personal reflection about Nelson for those who know him, or a testimonial about why you are deciding to join our fight. Thank you for considering this request. Thank you for your thoughts and prayers for Nelson. Thank you, in advance, for your generosity. Even the act of creating this go fund me page and sharing our story publicly has given us – including Nelson – purpose and hope for the future when we can be reunited. Until then we are heartbroken, but we fight on. Mr. Nelson Wells, Sr. and Mrs. Cynthia Wells Louisiana

# Fund Independent Reporting In Richmond Virgina

We have a state of emergency declared in Virginia!And right now we’re seeing what looks like a massive police state closing in on the state capitol where there will be a huge rally on Monday.This is a very divisive issue that’s generating a lot of media spin and disinformation. And chaos could break out in Richmond.It is crucial that there be independent, on-the-ground reporting in Richmond, especially given what happened in Charlottesville — where many people argue police actually instigated some of the violence and things definitely got out of hand.In the past, when massive Yellow Vests protests were taking place in Paris, I was there reporting on the ground and risking safety as protesters were losing eyes due to police brutality. I have also been to places like Somalia, Venezuela andCheran, once the most violent, dangerous area in Mexico. And more recently, I reported on the ground amid huge protests in Hong Kong.Now lots of people are asking me to go to Richmond, so they can get the truth about what’s happening there.So I’ve decided to go, if we can raise enough funds for it.A trip to Virginia isn’t as expensive as going to Hong Kong, where I provided you in-depth, on-the-ground reports on one of the world’s most important protest movements.But it’s not free either. I still need to cover airfare/gas, hotel and equipment expenses. And I’m planning on hiring a cameraman and video editor. I estimate this will cost around $1,500.If you value reporting on the events in Virginia that is free of spin and manipulation and provides a real, honest look at what is happening, then your support is essential.Thank you so much for funding independent media and for allowing me to continue doing the job I love!

This is a very divisive issue that’s generating a lot of media spin and disinformation. And chaos could break out in Richmond.

It is crucial that there be independent, on-the-ground reporting in Richmond, especially given what happened in Charlottesville — where many people argue police actually instigated some of the violence and things definitely got out of hand.

In the past, when massive Yellow Vests protests were taking place in Paris, I was there [reporting on the ground](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hTzwJqUPeqk) and risking safety as protesters were losing eyes due to police brutality. I have also been to places like [Somalia,](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UooepLs3Fqs)[Venezuela](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UOQb7Y5QVO8) and[Cheran](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r3qRm3sXVRU), once the most violent, dangerous area in Mexico. And more recently, I reported on the ground amid huge protests in Hong Kong.

Now lots of people are asking me to go to Richmond, so they can get the truth about what’s happening there.

So I’ve decided to go, if we can raise enough funds for it.

A trip to Virginia isn’t as expensive as going to Hong Kong, where I provided you in-depth, on-the-ground reports on one of the world’s most important protest movements.

But it’s not free either. I still need to cover airfare/gas, hotel and equipment expenses. And I’m planning on hiring a cameraman and video editor. I estimate this will cost around $1,500.

If you value reporting on the events in Virginia that is free of spin and manipulation and provides a real, honest look at what is happening, then your support is essential.

Thank you so much for funding independent media and for allowing me to continue doing the job I love!

# Legal Defense for Hong Kong Democracy Activists

The Lantos Foundation for Human Rights & Justice stands with the people of Hong Kong on the front lines of the fight for freedom & democracy.Courageous Hong Kong democracy activists have been protesting for months against a dangerous Chinese extradition bill that would have undermined their independence and freedom. Though the bill has now been formally withdrawn, the fight is not over. Since June, thousands of protesters have been attacked and injured by police and mainland gangs and over 1,100 people have been detained. Those arrested for peacefully protesting have been charged with offenses that could put them in jail for many years.Hong Kong Democracy protesters have won the first huge victory in the court of public opinion, but the next victories will need to be won in the courts of law.Just a few months ago, the Lantos Foundation was proud to give our highest award to the most recognizable leader of the democracy movement – Joshua Wong. While such leadership is important, all of the brave democracy crusaders deserve more than our admiration. We must equip them to defend themselves against the crushing apparatus of the Chinese communist state. This legal defense fund aims to support Joshua and his compatriots as they defend themselves against false accusations that could land them in prison for years to come.Our hope is that we can match their courage and determination in the form of financial support that will ensure they have fair representation. It is critical that the rule of law be upheld at this pivotal moment in Hong Kong's history. The eyes of the world may be on Hong Kong, but the eyes of history will be on those of us enjoying our own freedom and democracy - let us match our words and good wishes with the resources to defend those on the front lines of this fight for freedom.These legal defense funds will be officially disbursed through the Lantos Foundation's Front Line Fund grant program.

title: Navigating GPU Export Controls And AI Use Restrictions In Data Center Operations
summary: There have been a number of notable changes in the AI and data center regulatory landscape in 2026. As AI has dominated business decisions around the world, the race for AI leadership has reshaped the global geopolitical landscape. The broa
content:
There have been a number of notable changes in the AI and data center regulatory landscape in 2026. As AI has dominated business decisions around the world, the race for AI leadership has reshaped the global geopolitical landscape. The broad consequences of AI have confounded — and at times, captivated — policymakers at all levels, and now, leaders in Washington, D.C., must grapple with harnessing AI’s capabilities while defending against malign use of AI to harm America’s strategic interests.

While there remains a general bipartisan interest in controlling exports of strategic technologies, especially regarding China, the Trump administration’s actions to date reflect the balance between national security controls on exports and the need to maintain a dominant global market share in AI technologies. Since its announcement that the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule would not be enforced, the Trump administration has taken some actions to increase the accessibility and availability of graphics processing units (GPUs) to U.S. partners. Perhaps the earliest harbinger of this policy shift came in late May 2025, when the United States inked deals with the UAE and Saudi Arabia to allow for significant exports of advanced American semiconductors to each country. Given years of security concerns related to semiconductor exports to the region, the deals included strict security and reporting requirements for a select group of end users.

Two months later, the White House released [America’s AI Action Plan](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Americas-AI-Action-Plan.pdf), a comprehensive strategy that combined both offensive and defensive policies to win the global AI race. Alongside the AI Action Plan came [an executive order](https://www.mondaq.com/redirection.asp?article_id=1852140&company_id=18524&redirectaddress=https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2025/12/trump-administration-issues-executive-order-on-national-ai-policy-framework) that eventually led to the American AI Exports Program, which aimed to boost the export of the full American AI stack to global customers.

Then in December 2025, the Trump administration departed from previous policy expectations on semiconductor exports and technology security by approving exports of certain advanced U.S.-origin chips to customers in mainland China.

Amid reports that diverted and smuggled American semiconductors may be aiding China’s rapid AI advancements, broad bipartisan support has emerged in Congress for strict export controls on American AI technology. In 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee passed with overwhelming support measures that would codify export controls on advanced American semiconductors (AI Overwatch Act), direct BIS to require location tracking mechanisms for exported advanced semiconductors (Chip Security Act), and ensure that our allies match U.S. controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment or face the imposition of extraterritorial controls on such technology (MATCH Act). Companion versions for each of these bills were included in the Senate’s annual defense authorization bill through a manager’s amendment.

This GT Advisory considers how data center operators that host GPU servers might navigate this evolving regulatory environment, providing an overview of current U.S. export and use restrictions and identifying compliance considerations for participants in this sector.

As detailed below, a strong foundation of export control compliance, supply chain relationships, and contract terms may help companies position themselves to absorb and adapt to potential changes in the U.S. regulatory regime.

### Why GPU Hosting Creates Export Control Risks for Data Centers

Within data centers, GPUs have emerged as key components, transforming how complex computations are handled. GPUs are employed for their exceptional ability to perform parallel data processing, making them ideal for a range of tasks, including scientific computations, machine learning algorithms, and processing large-scale data. As demand for infrastructure capable of supporting AI model training and inference has grown, the ability to host GPU servers has become increasingly important for data centers.

The massive increase in processing power provided by GPUs as compared to central processing units (or CPUs) has, however, given rise to considerable disquiet amongst Western governments. In particular, the United States — where the biggest producers of GPUs are based — has expressed concern over their potential application for military and malign uses, and the Biden administration in January 2025 introduced comprehensive restrictions on the export and use of GPUs (the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule). The Trump administration has also emphasized, as a policy imperative, the continuation (and even tightening) of these restrictions and has revoked the Biden-era restrictions and indicated that it would be replacing them with new restrictions, which, as of the date of this briefing, have not yet been issued. This regulatory uncertainty leaves industry in an interim phase questioning how best to manage current and possible future restrictions on GPU exports and use.

Historically, data center operators that merely hosted the GPU servers of their tenants (rather than exporting or providing GPU as a service) may have assumed these U.S. export controls were not a material compliance concern. That assumption, however, may no longer be appropriate. U.S. export controls apply to the items themselves — meaning that even non-U.S. operators may face liability under the EAR if restricted GPUs, controlled technology, or sanctioned end users are present in their facilities, even indirectly through tenants or sub-tenants. As regulators focus increasingly on the downstream use and custody of advanced computing hardware, data center operators must be prepared to demonstrate robust compliance measures and control frameworks. This includes knowing what GPUs are being hosted, who owns and accesses them, and for what purposes they are used.

### U.S. Restrictions on GPU Exports and AI Model Use

**_Overview of U.S. Export Controls on GPUs_**

*   U.S. export controls currently regulate the physical export of GPUs from the United States and re-export from third countries. The January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule, and possible replacement regulations, may also seek to control post-delivery use of the GPUs for certain AI models.
*   Under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) that BIS administers, some U.S. export controls are based on the export control classification number (ECCN) of particular goods, software, and technology (to country destination, to nationality of recipient, to nationality of temporary custodians or lessees).
*   In addition, the EAR also has restrictions and license requirements that are based on the particular end user, such as end users identified on the BIS Entity List.
*   Currently, most GPUs are classified under ECCNs 3A090 and 3A991, which carry varying degrees of export license requirements. Under the EAR, various license exceptions are available for GPUs exports. Related computers and equipment may be controlled under ECCNs 4A090 and 5A002. These require a fact specific, case-by-case analysis and may involve notifications or certifications to BIS.
*   If a license is required and no exceptions are applicable, the U.S. exporter (or third country reexporter) may apply to BIS for a license. BIS’s review typically looks at the parties involved, and, in the case of GPU exports or other computing technology, the potential for the exported goods to be diverted to China and/or used for the development of advanced AI or military capabilities.
*   It is a violation of the EAR (even for non-U.S. persons or entities) to proceed with a transaction knowing that U.S. export controls have been, or will be, violated. For example, it would be a violation for a data center operator to knowingly purchase GPUs that were exported without an appropriate license, even if the GPUs were already outside the United States. Thus, in procuring GPUs, data center operators may wish to conduct diligence on all parties in the chain of custody and to verify that appropriate export licenses have been sought and obtained.
*   Liability and penalties under U.S. export controls and economic sanctions:

- Most export controls and economic sanctions are subject to strict liability, meaning it is irrelevant to a finding of violation whether the person knew or intended to violate the law. However, whether the specific offense includes a knowledge or intent element, enforcement agencies typically view intent or knowledge of a violation as an aggravating factor when assessing heightened penalties. In the most egregious cases, BIS and OFAC may make criminal referrals to the U.S. Department of Justice.

- Current potential penalties are civil monetary penalties for a U.S. economic sanctions or export controls violation, which can reach approximately USD $370,000 per violation or twice the value of each violation, whichever is greater. If U.S. sanctions or export control violations are prosecuted as criminal offenses, the criminal penalty can reach up to USD $1 million and for individuals, imprisonment for up to 20 years, though criminal referrals generally occur only in the most egregious cases (circumvention, evasion, willful pattern of conduct with high-risk technologies and end users). Additionally, egregious violations may result in denial of export privileges, or designation to the Entity List as a prohibited recipient of items subject to the EAR.

- The responsibility for seeking export licenses (or determining the applicability of exceptions) falls on the exporter of record from the United States (and/or reexporter from a third country). Recipients or intermediate consignees have a responsibility to prevent diversion of the items to unauthorized destinations or end users.

For operators, understanding who owns and uses the GPUs in their facilities, and taking reasonable steps to verify their compliance measures, may be a beneficial risk management component.

**_Overview of Restrictions on AI Model Use of GPUs_**

*   The January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule placed new restrictions on the export of GPUs and related equipment (under ECCNs 3A090, 4A090, and 5A002), but also on certain services and the use of AI technology itself.
*   Specifically, the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule applied significant export restrictions to closed-weight AI models trained with 10^26 computational operations or more. Additionally, the rule created a new foreign direct product rule that applied these controls to certain model weights produced abroad using advanced computing chips made with U.S. technology or equipment. Accordingly, even AI models developed outside of the United States with controlled U.S. technology were subject to the EAR end-use controls (which, for example, prohibit exports for the use of certain weapons development).
*   The rule established a framework of license exceptions and allocations that depended on the destination country of the above-referenced chips and services. It separated countries into three groups: 1) U.S.-allied countries eligible for broad license exceptions (specifically, Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Republic of Korea, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, United Kingdom, and the United States); 2) restricted, arms-embargoed countries that are subject to stringent licensing requirements with a presumption of denial (China, Macau, Afghanistan, Belarus, Burma, Cambodia, Central African Republic, DRC, Cuba, Cyprus, Eritrea, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Lebanon, Libya, Nicaragua, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Venezuela, and Zimbabwe); and 3) all other countries, a broad group that includes many countries in Southeast Asia.

title: China exit ban risk for US citizens hinges on open disputes
summary: ### Quick summary China’s exit-entry rules changed on September 15, 2026, when **State Council Order No. 841** took effect and widened the grounds for barring a foreign traveler from leaving. Security, criminal, and export-control matters n
content:
### Quick summary

China’s exit-entry rules changed on September 15, 2026, when **State Council Order No. 841** took effect and widened the grounds for barring a foreign traveler from leaving. Security, criminal, and export-control matters now count toward that decision. The shift is procedural and quiet, which is exactly what makes it consequential for anyone with unfinished business in the country.

Enforcement is discretionary, and outcomes vary from case to case. For U.S. and Canadian travelers, the practical question is narrower than a destination-level advisory implies, and it turns on what you carry into the country.

In this article

*   [Who faces exit-ban risk: the if-then test](https://www.airtraveler.club/intel/china-exit-ban-risk-us-citizens-hinges-open-disputes/#atc-toc-1)
*   [What Chinese authorities actually check](https://www.airtraveler.club/intel/china-exit-ban-risk-us-citizens-hinges-open-disputes/#atc-toc-2)
*   [Exceptions: when the risk is minimal](https://www.airtraveler.club/intel/china-exit-ban-risk-us-citizens-hinges-open-disputes/#atc-toc-3)
*   [Settle the record before you fly](https://www.airtraveler.club/intel/china-exit-ban-risk-us-citizens-hinges-open-disputes/#atc-toc-4)

U.S. citizens have spent years inside China, unable to board a flight home under an _exit ban_. The State Department ties that exposure to disputes, investigations, and security-linked cases rather than to the _Level 3_ destination label itself. An advisory that covers an entire country, from Beijing boardrooms to Chengdu teahouses, says almost nothing about one traveler’s odds. Clearing immigration on arrival is not the same as being free to leave, and that gap is where the risk lives.

For U.S. and Canadian travelers weighing a 2026 trip, the split is clean: business, legal, or regulatory exposure raises the stakes sharply, while a leisure itinerary with no China ties sits at the opposite end. As of October 2026, that split matters more than the advisory number.

Discover more

Travel

travel

Buy Maps

## Who faces exit-ban risk: the if-then test

Business travel carries the clearest if-then. Holders of business visas who travel on commercial matters are the group the State Department flags for movement restrictions. A criminal charge is not required. **Unresolved commercial, legal, or regulatory disputes** can support a ban on their own.

Read that list literally. A contract under dispute counts. A tax matter under review counts. A regulatory or customs disagreement counts. None of them is a crime, and each can keep a traveler in the country for as long as it stays open.

At the other end sits the traveler with nothing to litigate. A tourist with no China business ties, no property, and no pending matter falls outside the exit-ban language the advisory carries. The trip is not risk-free, but the person is not in the targeted group.

_Dual nationals_ deserve their own line. A second passport does not simplify matters, because the advisory’s exit-ban caution concentrates on dual nationals as well as business-visa holders. Anyone with ties on both sides of the border sits in the group to watch.

[![Image 1: Superdeals to Asia preview](https://www.airtraveler.club/wp-content/uploads/superdeals-airports-world.png)](https://www.airtraveler.club/)
Superdeals cover departures from North America, Europe and Australia.

## Flight deals most people never see

Air Traveler Club monitors thousands of routes for pricing anomalies that traditional search engines miss. With ATC Superdeals [members save up to 80% on each flight](https://www.airtraveler.club/) vs. regular fares.

Too good to be true? Check it out yourself. It's free.

Delivered weekly. Unsubscribe anytime.

## What Chinese authorities actually check

At the border, the first check is your entry basis. China’s **240-hour visa-free transit** lets eligible travelers stay **up to 10 days** in permitted areas, provided they arrive through designated ports with a confirmed onward ticket, according to the [National Immigration Administration](https://www.nia.gov.cn/Enquiry/publish/showQuestion.jsp?MZ=GNZmkGUfJq6VUthCbueKsw%3D%3D).

Departure is a different examination. Officers assess the traveler, not the itinerary. A ban tied to security, criminal, or _export-control_ grounds can run as long as **three years**, and authorities may **withhold written notice** when they determine that disclosure would affect security or an investigation.

Civil disputes, business investigations, and alleged security violations all sit inside the framework, and the digital trail a traveler leaves can form part of the picture. The wider mechanics of [how exit bans attach to disputes and monitored communications](https://www.airtraveler.club/intel/china-exit-bans-risk-business-travelers-north-america/) are covered in this explainer.

## Exceptions: when the risk is minimal

The low-risk case is real. A traveler with no China business ties, no property, and no pending matter sits outside the group the advisory’s exit-ban language targets. Tourism fits there, and so does a short family visit.

Entry stays open to a wide field: the same visa-free transit program covers **57 countries**, the United States and Canada among them. The count shifts as new states are added, and the National Immigration Administration’s guidance is the version to trust.

Risk is also time-bound. A short stay in a _permitted area_, with a clean record and a confirmed onward ticket, looks different from a months-long business posting with unresolved matters on the mainland.

## Settle the record before you fly

The window that matters opens well before departure: the 240-hour transit clock starts on arrival, while an unresolved dispute follows its own timetable.

*   **Read past the headline** — the State Department’s China advisory carries the current Level 3 language, and the exit-ban section is the part that applies to business travelers.
*   **Close open matters first** — commercial, tax, and regulatory disputes are the exact conditions that raise exposure, so get a China-qualified lawyer’s read before booking.
*   **Carry the entry proof** — the confirmed onward ticket and designated-port details your visa-free transit eligibility depends on.
*   **Keep a reachable trail** — leave your itinerary and movements with family, as the advisory recommends.
*   **Watch:** a change to the China advisory level, or fresh exit-entry guidance from Beijing, would shift the calculus for everyone, not only business travelers.

Most leisure trips need no change at all. The ones that do are the ones with an open matter attached, and that is a question worth answering before the aircraft door closes.

Reporting by

ATC Intelligence

[ATC Intelligence](https://www.airtraveler.club/about) is the research division of Air Traveler Club. Backed by 15 years in Asia-Pacific aviation, we don't just report on the regional market; we live and work in it. By pairing AI-driven data with strict human fact-checking, we provide actionable, trustworthy journalism designed to make your trips to Asia smarter and more affordable.

Follow our daily coverage on Google News, Google Discover, and social media.

## Questions? Answers.

Is it safe for U.S. citizens to travel to China in 2026?
Risk tracks what a traveler carries in, not the country as a whole. Business disputes, regulatory exposure, or an open investigation raise the chance of exit restrictions sharply; ordinary tourism with no China ties carries a much narrower risk.

What countries are at Level 3 travel warning?
For this topic, the operative warning is the exit-ban risk the China advisory flags for certain travelers, rather than a uniform threat level applied evenly to every visitor.

Is China allowing U.S. citizens to enter?
Yes. U.S. citizens who arrive at a designated port with a confirmed onward ticket meet the conditions for the 240-hour visa-free transit, which is built for short stays.

Is there a travel alert for American citizens in 2026?
Yes. Arbitrary enforcement, exit bans, and the risk of unjust detention remain the core warnings, and the China advisory was reissued in September 2026.

What should a business traveler do before going to China?
Put the question to a China-qualified lawyer before booking, and ask whether any open tax, contract, or regulatory matter could be read as grounds for a restriction. If the answer is yes, the trip waits.

title: US defense experts to participate in meetings, war games in Taiwan joint assessment program
summary: * By Huang Ching-hsuan and William Hetherington / Staff reporter, with staff writer * * [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com) * [_![Image 1](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/x.png
content:
*   By Huang Ching-hsuan and William Hetherington / Staff reporter, with staff writer

*       *   [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com)
    *   [_![Image 1](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/x.png)_](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=US+defense+experts+to+participate+in+meetings%2C+war+games+in+Taiwan+joint+assessment+program%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F06%2F2003865473)
    *   [_![Image 2](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/facebook.png)_](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F06%2F2003865473&t=US+defense+experts+to+participate+in+meetings%2C+war+games+in+Taiwan+joint+assessment+program)
    *   [_![Image 3](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/line.png)_](https://lineit.line.me/share/ui?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F06%2F2003865473?utm_medium=P&utm_campaign=SHARE&utm_source=LINE)

US defense liaisons are to take part in 130 meetings and map-based war games in Taiwan under an expanded joint assessment program, the Ministry of National Defense said in a report.

Sources have previously said that the Pentagon would station personnel at the ministry under a joint program that is to run from this year through 2028.

That program would involve officials from the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Policy and researchers from the Institute for Defense Analyses, a US nonprofit research organization that conducts national security studies, the ministry report said.

## The Pentagon building in Arlington, Virginia, is pictured on April 21, 2023.

Photo: Bloomberg

Each organization would assign one representative to work at the ministry’s headquarters in Taiwan.

The Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Policy advises US defense leaders on national security and defense policy, while the Institute for Defense Analyses conducts federally funded research and analysis on national security and science policy.

The ministry plans to hold 50 in-person meetings and 80 videoconferences this year under the program, which runs from this year through 2028, the report said.

The ministry has allocated funding for the initiative since 2022. Under the arrangement, the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Policy commissions the Institute for Defense Analyses to coordinate experts from the US military and research organizations, including the US Indo-Pacific Command, the Defense Intelligence Agency and the National Ground Intelligence Center.

The US liaisons work with the ministry, General Staff Headquarters and the armed services to assess defense and operational issues and provide policy recommendations.

Findings from the program’s first three years have been incorporated into the annual Han Kuang military exercises and training assessments conducted by each service, the ministry said.

Beginning this year, the US is expanding the scope and depth of the assessments and increasing their frequency, the report said.

The ministry said it has budgeted NT$471 million (US$14.82 million) over three years for the program. The NT$152.5 million allocated for next year would cover an expanded research team, the 130 meetings and the costs of stationing the two US liaisons in Taiwan.

The meetings would bring US experts together with Taiwan’s joint staff, service headquarters and frontline units for discussions, on-site inspections and map-based war games, as well as qualitative and quantitative assessments using simulation models, it said.

title: 阿布都热依木.艾尼（Abdurihim Gheni）："专制政权必将倒台！"——阿姆斯特丹举行抗议中共政权成立77周年集会
summary: 阿布都 热 依木 . 艾 尼 (Abdurehim Gheni Uyghur ) 阿姆斯特丹， 10 月 3 日 — 在荷 兰 阿姆斯特丹 历 史悠久的达姆广 场 （ Dam Square ）， 举 行了一 场 大 规 模抗 议 集会，反 对 中共 专 制政 权 建立 77 周年。 此次抗 议 活 动 由荷 兰 支持西藏 组织 （ Tibet Support Group NL ）、支持 维 吾 尔 人基金会（ Stichting Support Uyghurs ）、反中共之
content: 阿布都 热 依木 . 艾 尼 (Abdurehim Gheni Uyghur ) 阿姆斯特丹， 10 月 3 日 — 在荷 兰 阿姆斯特丹 历 史悠久的达姆广 场 （ Dam Square ）， 举 行了一 场 大 规 模抗 议 集会，反 对 中共 专 制政 权 建立 77 周年。   此次抗 议 活 动 由荷 兰 支持西藏 组织 （ Tibet Support Group NL ）、支持 维 吾 尔 人基金会（ Stichting Support Uyghurs ）、反中共之声（ Voice of Anti-CCP NL ）以及南粤独立党（ Cantonia Independence Party ） 联 合 发 起和 组织 。   来自中共占 领 下的 东 突厥斯坦 维 吾 尔 人、西藏人、南蒙古人、南粤人、广西人、 满 洲人，以及人 权 活 动 家、中国基督教 组织 代表和支持正 义 的荷 兰 民众等 80 多人 积 极参与了此次活 动 。   活 动 主持人、荷 兰 支持西藏 组织 主席次仁姜巴（ Tsering Jampa ）致开幕 词 ， 强 烈 谴责 中共政 权 77 年来的 扩张 主 义 政策、侵犯人 权 及种族 灭绝 罪行。   同 时 ，各民族及 组织 代表也在活 动 中 发 表了 讲话 ： * 西藏、南蒙古、南粤及广西代表： 强 调 必 须团结 一致，共同反 对 中国政府在其家园 实 施的殖民主 义 、 强 制同化、种族 灭绝 以及跨国 镇压 政策。 * 中国基督教 组织 代表： 批 评 了中共 对 基督教徒的迫害，并呼吁国 际 社会和正 义 力量共同抵抗中国政府的暴政。   活 动 期 间 ， “ 支持 维 吾 尔 人基金会 ” 创办 人 阿布都 热 依木 . 艾 尼 （ Abdurihim Gheni Uyghur ） 发 表 讲话 ，指出中共政 权 对 世界构成威 胁 ，呼吁西方国家 团结 起来，共同抵制中国的 扩张 主 义 和种族 灭绝 。   示威者在舞台前献上白玫瑰及西藏 传统 白色哈达，向所有在中共 专 制暴政下 牺 牲的受害者致敬。   在集会尾声， 现场进 行了引人注目的 戏剧 性表达。南粤活 动 人士刘 飞龙 戴着 习 近平的面具，穿上橙色囚服并戴着手 铐 出 现 在广 场 上。他手中拿着一 张 印有 “END CCP” （ 结 束中共）和中文 “ 遗 臭万年 ” 字 样 的 习 近平 头 像。 阿布都 热 依木 . 艾 尼 用 绳 子拴住其 颈 部，在达姆广 场 上一 边牵 着他高喊 “ 恐怖分子 习 近平！法西斯 习 近平！ ” 。 这 一幕吸引了达姆广 场 上大量游客和当地民众的 强 烈关注，众人 纷纷 拍照和 录 像，将当天的活 动 推向了高潮。   阿布都 热 依木 . 艾 尼 针对 中共政 权 77 年来的侵略与同化政策 发 表的 讲话 全文：   " 尊敬的聚在阿姆斯特丹达姆广 场 的正 义 民众、 亲爱 的同胞 们 、合作 组织 及人 权 活 动 家 们 ！   今天，我 们 聚集在荷 兰 的心 脏 —— 历 史悠久的达姆广 场 ，表达我 们对 中共 专 制政 权 成立 77 周年的 强 烈抗 议 。   今天来到 这 里的，有遭受中国占 领 的 东 突厥斯坦人、西藏人、南蒙古人、南粤人、广西人，以及所有反 对 暴政的正 义 人士。今天，我 们发 出共同的声音，反 对 中共政 权 77 年来的侵略、暴政、种族 灭绝 和国 际 威 胁 ，要求正 义 ！   自 1949 年 10 月 1 日中共政 权 建立以来，在被占 领 的 东 突厥斯坦、西藏、南蒙古、南粤、广西和 满 洲等土地上，数以百万 计 的无辜民众遭到系 统 性屠 杀 、关押和流放。我 们 的身份、信仰、母 语 和文化正在通 过 强 制同化政策被抹去，企 图 将我 们 作 为 一个民族 彻 底消 灭 。   今天，在 东 突厥斯坦，数以百万 计 的 维 吾 尔 人和其他突厥 语 系民族正受尽集中 营 、 强 迫 劳动 和 监狱 的折磨。家庭被撕裂，母 亲 与孩子被迫分离， 妇 女被 强 制 绝 育。不 仅 如此，中国政府 还 利用今年 7 月 1 日 实 施的所 谓 《促 进 民族 团结进 步条例》， 试图 将其 镇压 延伸至境外， 为 其在民主国家 镇压 人 权 活 动 家和流亡自由 战 士 寻 找合法借口。他 们 通 过 跨国恐吓和 绑 架家人作 为 人 质 ，企 图 扼 杀 全球的自由之声。   尊敬的国 际 社会和荷 兰 人民！   今天，我 们 在 这 个广 场 向全世界 发 出 紧 急警告：中国的侵略和 扩张 主 义 政策不会 仅仅 停留在被占 领 的民族身上。他 们对 国 际 法的践踏、 对邻 国的威 胁 以及 对 民主价 值 的破坏，是 对 世界和平的重大威 胁 ！   因此，今天我 们 在阿姆斯特丹的天空下共同 挥 舞旗 帜 ，向全世界 发 出明确信号：我 们绝 不屈服！我 们 将 为 家园的自由、独立以及我 们 人民的正 义进 行不懈的斗争！   我 们 呼吁世界上所有的民主国家、人 权 组织 和正 义 人士，面 对 中国的 压 迫不要保持沉默， 维护 国 际 法，与我 们 站在一起！   专 制政 权 必将倒台！ 自由与正 义 必 胜 ！   我 谨 代表支持 维 吾 尔 人基金会向大家表示感 谢 。 " 日期： 2026 年 10 月 6 日 編輯：江培坤(Jiang Peikun)
