content: 近日，关注陈伟杰先生案件的人士发现，其羁押信息已无法在美国移民执法机关公开查询系统中检索到。鉴于相关信息变化，目前外界担忧其可能已进入遣返程序，案件进展情况亟需得到进一步说明和确认。 陈伟杰先生经历坎坷。其父母因贫困及疾病早年离世，其幼年便成为孤儿。成长过程中又亲历了哥哥一家以及其他亲属因宗教信仰等问题遭受中国当局的迫害，受此影响他开始逐步走上了反抗中共极权政权的道路。陈伟杰先生曾在深圳、香港等地从事健身教练工作，并曾参与香港社会公共事务和“反送中”运动。此后基于对自身政治立场及未来处境的担忧，离开香港并前往美国。 抵达美国后，陈伟杰先生持续公开参与民主、人权及公民社会活动，担任多个海外民主组织职务，并参加集会、抗议活动、公开演讲及媒体采访、常到使领馆举牌抗议，其公开活动记录可供查证。 鉴于陈伟杰先生长期公开反对中国共产党的一党专制统治，并持续参与中国民主、人权与公民社会活动。如果被遣返回中国，他既往公开的政治表达和参与的社会活动，将使陈伟杰面临中国当局拘押、酷刑、审查、政治迫害的风险及其他严重的后果。基于国际人权保护原则及“禁止遣返原则”（Non-Refoulement Principle），上述风险应得到充分审查和评估。 因此，我们郑重提出以下请求： 一、请求美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）、美国国土安全部（DHS）、负责案件审理的移民法庭、相关救济机构在涉及陈伟杰等人士被遣返相关政治迫害、人身安全风险以及其他严重后果未得到充分全面、独立和客观的审查、评估之前，停止对陈伟杰等采取遣返措施。 二、请求美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）、美国国土安全部（DHS）、负责案件审理的移民法庭等确保陈伟杰先生获得完整、公平的法律程序保障，包括律师协助、案件审理及救济机会。 三、请求美国作为世界最强大的民主国家，依据国内法及相关国际人权原则，审慎处理陈伟杰案件，避免出现不可逆的人道后果。继续依法履行国际责任与国际义务，继续作为世界的人权领导者与民主、自由的灯塔，带领人类走向更加光明的未来。 最后，鉴于陈伟杰先生目前状态不明，其羁押信息已无法公开查询，而遣返决定一旦执行往往具有不可逆性，因此本次呼吁具有高度时效性和紧迫性。故，我们也诚挚地紧急呼吁所有关心民主、自由、人权与法治的人士、团体关注陈伟杰先生当前处境，并以签名联署、提交证词、提供相关资料或其他合法方式表达支持。每一份关注和发声，都有助于维护基本人权、程序正义及人道主义价值。 发起单位: 中国民主人权联盟 美国民阵联合总部 中华共和党 2026年10月4日 联署名单： 1、金秀红 2、盛雪 3、陈维明 4、朱虞夫 5、史庆梅 6、姚戈 7、 张勇 8、房兰峰 9、司书良 10、王明义 11、李海风 12、郑杨 13、魏立斌 14、倪金芳 15、胡景 16、劉蔚鋒 17、暨智敏 18、邹劲 19、何兴强 20、高辉 21、占智能 22、贺瑞忠 23、卢超 24、陈娟 25、刘傲 26、Zegang yuan 27、张振振 28、蔡守奇 29、郑光信 30、范英龙 31、贾会刚 32、劳绍海 33、杨长兵 34、郑伟 35、钱家发 36、陈立群 37、温绍英 38、李聪玲 39、周志刚 40、郑喜宾 41、马相平 42、惠汝涛 43、刘世杰 44、杨毅杰 45、范发群 46、韦江红 47、林岳明 48、金月花 49、王永红 50、李家麟 51、Zhao Xiling 52、方正 53、方鹊 54、索罗门.李 55、白洁敏 56、林立伟 57、王西朋 58、台湾周伯 59、翟成松 60、刘双源 61、李树青 62、周清明 63、卫仁喜 64、王家伟 65、李青 66、李中平 67、林暖 68、潘贤要 69、陈峰林. 70、李元喜 71、李学政 72、熊燕 73、王斌 74、查理 75、司徒戴 76、管琴宇 77、莫逢节 78、郭城 79、黄奔 80、李海 81、刘微 82、陈新海 83、界立建 84、袁哲 85、李任興 86、廖文浩 87、方硕 88、Daniel Chan 89、刘敏 90、王志军 91、陈冲 92、王本学 93、陳翔威 94、陈新海 95、界立建 96、袁哲 97、李任興 98、廖文浩 99、方硕 100、Daniel Chan 101、刘敏 102、王志军103、陈冲 104、石淑萍105、郭贵祥 106、周君红107、牛葫芦 108、白楊109、陳翔威 110、楚向發 111、刘栋玲（丹麥） 112、石淑萍 113、 楊佳 （馬來西亞） 114、孫志剛 115、吴立新

title: UNGA81: Key human rights issues at the Third Committee in October – November 2026 - ISHR
summary: The Third Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA81) will meet in New York from **October 1 to November 20 2026**. The Third Committee is the General Assembly’s principal committee dealing with human rights and social
content:
The Third Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA81) will meet in New York from **October 1 to November 20 2026**.

The Third Committee is the General Assembly’s principal committee dealing with human rights and social and humanitarian issues. This year it is expected to consider approximately 47 thematic and country-specific resolutions and hold dialogues with 88 human rights experts, UN officials and entities. Its decisions can strengthen international human rights standards, respond to serious violations, and shape the work and resources of the UN human rights system.

**UNGA81 takes place at a moment of mounting pressure on the international human rights system and the institutions that underpin it.** States should use the session to reaffirm their commitment to human rights multilateralism and to translate into action the commitments made by more than [90 States in the cross-regional statement at HRC61](https://ishr.ch/latest-updates/over-80-countries-pledge-to-defend-human-rights-multilateralism-at-the-un/).

This means defending independent human rights mechanisms and those who serve them from intimidation and reprisals, responding collectively to the growing threat of transnational repression, including by acting on the recommendations of the recent [joint statement by over 130 UN human rights experts](https://ishr.ch/latest-updates/over-130-human-rights-experts-issue-global-call-for-states-to-end-transnational-repression/), and standing firmly behind international accountability mechanisms and officials facing threats and attacks.

It also requires ensuring that the UN human rights pillar has the resources to deliver: chronic underfunding and the liquidity crisis continue to impede UN human rights bodies from doing critical human rights work and help the most vulnerable, making it imperative that States deliver on the Pact for the Future commitment to provide adequate, predictable, increased and sustainable financing for human rights. Against this backdrop, the Third Committee should also reaffirm the indispensable role of human rights defenders and strengthen their protection, including through a strong and forward-looking resolution on human rights defenders.

**Stay up-to-date:** Follow @ISHRglobal and #UNGA81 on X and @ishr.ch on BlueSky, and look out for our Human Rights Monitor.

## ISHR thematic priorities:

### **Human rights defenders**

At UNGA81, Norway will lead the now triennial resolution on human rights defenders, providing an important opportunity for the General Assembly to reaffirm the essential role of defenders and strengthen their protection. The resolution comes at a time of shrinking civic space and increasing pressure on defenders in many parts of the world, including through threats, attacks, criminalisation, surveillance and other forms of intimidation and reprisal. **ISHR urges States to support a strong and forward-looking resolution that responds to the evolving risks faced by defenders, protects and expands the space in which they work, and strengthens implementation of the UN Declaration on Human Rights Defenders and**[**Declaration +25**](https://ishr.ch/25-years-un-declaration-on-human-rights-defenders/)**. In particular, the resolution should strengthen protections for defenders in the digital sphere, including against unlawful surveillance and spyware, misuse of AI and biometric technologies, internet shutdowns and technology-facilitated gender-based violence; respond to the growing threat of transnational repression; and recognise the particular risks faced by women human rights defenders and other defenders at heightened risk, while ensuring effective safeguards, accountability and remedies.**

### **Reprisals**

Each year at the Third Committee, Ireland and Uruguay deliver **[a joint statement](https://www.ireland.ie/en/un/newyork/news-and-speeches/speeches-archive/joint-statement-on-reprisals-for-cooperation-with-the-united-nations-2026/) condemning intimidation and reprisals against those who cooperate with the United Nations.** This year’s statement sent a strong message in support of the right of civil society and human rights defenders to engage safely and freely with the UN and its mechanisms, and ISHR welcomes and thanks the States that lent their voices to it. At the same time, the continued decline in the number of States joining the statement is deeply concerning at a time when reprisals remain widespread and are taking increasingly diverse forms, including transnationally. **ISHR urges States to translate the commitments expressed in the statement into concrete action to prevent, investigate and ensure effective follow-up and accountability for reprisals, and calls on more States to add their voices to this collective stand in future.**

The Third Committee’s interactive dialogue on 15 October with the **Assistant Secretary-General for Human Rights**, who leads the UN’s system-wide response to intimidation and reprisals, is also a critical opportunity for States to **raise individual cases of reprisals, including cases documented in the Secretary-General’s annual report, and press for their resolution and follow-up**. **ISHR encourages States to raise cases highlighted through our**[**#EndReprisals campaign**](https://ishr.ch/campaigns/endreprisals2026/), helping ensure that defenders who face retaliation for engaging with the UN are not forgotten and that perpetrators are held accountable. This year’s campaign focuses on human rights defenders who face reprisals through transnational repression, as States seek to silence criticism beyond their borders.

### **Defending gender equality and countering anti-rights initiatives**

UNGA81 takes place amid intensifying attacks on gender equality and the rights of women, girls and LGBTIQ+ persons — both through unilateral policy measures and coordinated efforts to roll back established language in multilateral negotiations. At CSW70 this March, the US tabled eight amendments targeting gender and SRHR language and a draft resolution seeking to redefine ‘gender’ in restrictive terms; all were defeated, but these tactics may be replicated in the Third Committee.

The precedent from UNGA80 is particularly concerning. An OIC-led amendment to delete the first-ever SOGI reference in the resolution on the rights of persons with disabilities was narrowly defeated in the Third Committee but was reintroduced and adopted in the General Assembly plenary, resulting in the deletion of the reference from the final resolution. This means defending inclusive language in Committee is no longer sufficient — States must be prepared to defend it through to the plenary.

These efforts are becoming more institutionalised. In September 2026, on the margins of the General Assembly, the United States and a group of Latin American and other States announced the formation of a new coalition — framed around ‘life and family’ — explicitly positioning itself as a counterweight to the Pro-LGBTI+ Core Group, signalling a more coordinated approach to opposing gender equality and SOGI language in UN negotiations.

**ISHR urges States to reject hostile amendments targeting****established****language****on****gender equality, SRHR and SOGI across all Third Committee resolutions; defend agreed language through to plenary adoption**; **and****oppose any attempt to redefine ‘gender’ in restrictive or exclusionary terms.**

At UNGA81, Finland will lead the biennial resolution on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, which has long recognised the heightened risk of unlawful killings faced by particular groups, including persons targeted because of their sexual orientation or gender identity (SOGI) and those exercising the right to defend rights. Maintaining this explicit protection is particularly important this year, especially given the ultimate removal of the SOGI reference from the resolution on the rights of persons with disabilities. This underscores that established inclusive language cannot be taken for granted and must be defended consistently throughout the General Assembly process. ISHR urges States to defend the integrity of the EJE resolution, reject any attempt to remove or weaken its established SOGI language, and ensure that the resolution continues to explicitly recognise and protect all those at heightened risk of unlawful killings.

### Strengthening the human rights treaty body system

At UNGA81, Iceland and a cross-regional group of States will lead the biennial resolution on the human rights treaty body system, providing an important opportunity to strengthen the effectiveness and sustainability of the treaty bodies. The resolution comes at a critical moment, as severe resource constraints, growing backlogs and the UN liquidity crisis are undermining the system’s ability to carry out its mandated work. This context demands an ambitious response from Member States that recognises the challenges facing the system and takes concrete steps to safeguard its effective functioning. ISHR urges States to support a stronger, adequately and predictably resourced treaty body system, including predictable review cycles, greater alignment of working methods, and accessible and inclusive modalities that enable the meaningful participation of civil society and other stakeholders, while safeguarding the independence of the treaty bodies. We urge all States to ensure that treaty bodies have adequate and predictable financial and human resources to carry out all their mandated activities fully and effectively, and to allocate the necessary resources through the Fifth Committee. The resolution should also build on and give practical effect to the previous resolution’s invitation to expand the use of digital technologies, by ensuring that hybrid modalities are systematically available to facilitate the meaningful and accessible participation of civil society and other stakeholders in treaty body activities.

### **Special Procedures reporting to the General Assembly**

Efforts to reduce the Third Committee’s workload have led to significant [cuts to Special Procedures reporting](https://ishr.ch/latest-updates/general-assembly-reporting-cuts-to-special-procedures-mandates-an-analysis/) to the General Assembly. Decisions taken at HRC60–62 will result in five fewer reports to GA81 and 17 fewer reports across GA81–83, already exceeding the reductions initially envisaged under the Third Committee working-methods roadmap. Of particular concern, some mandates are being moved to biennial reporting, risking making these cuts permanent and reducing opportunities for engagement with mandate holders in New York.

States from the Western Europe and Others Group (WEOG) have led these reductions, often through cross-regional initiatives involving one or more WEOG members. **ISHR urges States to assess any further changes on a case-by-case basis, preserve meaningful engagement with the General Assembly, and ensure that efficiency measures do not weaken the visibility, effectiveness or independence of Special Procedures.**

### **Civil society participation**

Civil society plays an important role throughout the session by briefing States and UN experts, providing information on human rights situations and individual cases, proposing technical expertise on resolutions being negotiated, and organising side events. Severe physical barriers prevent physical access to UN premises including those related to timely granting as well as delays in processing requests for ECOSOC accreditation. Even NGOs in ECOSOC status often face barriers in engaging at the Third Committee due to severe delays in approving requests for groundspasses.

**ISHR encourages States to enable effective and meaningful civil society engagement during the Third Committee by enabling inclusive participation in-person and through online and hybrid participation. We urge resolution penholders to facilitate meaningful civil society pa

title: China’s four new ‘global initiatives’: Attempting to change the global order
summary: Image generated using Artificial Intelligence * * * ## Executive summary * The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has established four initiatives aimed at aligning the international order with its preferences: the Global Development Initiative,
content:
Image generated using Artificial Intelligence

* * *

## Executive summary

*   The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has established four initiatives aimed at aligning the international order with its preferences: the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilisation Initiative, and the Global Governance Initiative.
*   Using these initiatives as ‘pillars’, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) aims to challenge the United States (US)-led free and open international order. This includes expanding its influence in forums such as the United Nations and World Trade Organisation, and establishing alternatives such as the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and BRICS.
*   The PRC advocates for greater influence for developing countries – referred to by the CCP as the ‘Global South’ – and positions itself as a member of the ‘Global South family’. In doing so, it aims to align developing countries with its vision for a reshaped international order.

* * *

## Introduction

In June 2026, the State Council Information Office (SCIO) of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) announced that in autumn that year, the PRC would host an inaugural Global Governance Forum to discuss reforming and improving global governance.[[1]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn1) The Chinese government and its think tanks have long been in overdrive, as they promulgate the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) own views and aims for change in global governance.

Over the past five years, Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CCP, has introduced and expanded upon the architecture of ‘a community with a shared future for mankind’ and its four supporting pillars. These are the **Global Development Initiative** (GDI), the **Global Security Initiative** (GSI), the **Global Civilisation Initiative** (GCI), and the **Global Governance Initiative** (GGI).

Xi considers reworking the international order and global governance an essential prerequisite for achieving the PRC’s ‘Second Centennial Goal’, namely, by the centenary of the establishment of the PRC in 2049, becoming ‘a great modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious, and beautiful’ – in short, to become the leading global power. With some justification, the CCP sees the system established after the Second World War as benefiting the interests of, and aligning with the values of, the United States (US) and its allies. Without this changing, achieving the ‘great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation’ – a slogan encompassing the intent of the ‘Second Centennial Goal’ – will not be possible.

The intention is not to replace the United Nations (UN) and other global institutions, but to refashion them. By canvassing the support of developing countries – often referred to by the CCP as the ‘Global South’[[2]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn2) – the PRC is working to set up new regional and global organisations and groupings more closely aligned with its own interests and values. It also aims to have a major say in drawing up international regulations and norms in new areas, such as space, the polar regions, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). The border between alignment and control is sometimes unclear.

This long Explainer uses CCP instructions and explanations to its own members to elucidate the architecture of the ‘common destiny’ and four global initiatives. Nevertheless, the terms retain a degree of woolliness. The CCP does this deliberately, both to allow flexibility in the present and to accommodate developments in the future.

As argued in previous papers by the Council on Geostrategy, anti-Americanism is the wellspring of the PRC’s foreign policy, and also informs much of its domestic policy.[[3]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn3) The CCP believes – correctly – that the US is trying to contain and repress its rise, so that the PRC will be unable to attain ‘national rejuvenation’ or ‘China’s modernisation’ (another codeword for the PRC becoming the world’s dominant power). This study aims to show how, in the area of global governance, under the guiding principle of anti-Americanism, this intention is being translated into action in pursuit of long-term goals.

If liberal, democratic international norms and values are not to lose their ‘dominant position’ – a phrase that Xi uses to define his own ambitions – greater unity and purpose are required, not least because reforms of the global governance system are indeed needed. Free and open countries should also engage better in the propaganda war that the CCP has launched.

## **‘Xi Jinping thought on foreign relations’: The architecture**

The CCP continues to refine ‘Xi Jinping thought on foreign relations’. The overarching concept is to ‘build a community with a shared future for mankind’. Initially, this concept was supported by three pillars, which, starting in 2022, emerged at the rate of one a year: the GDI, the GSI, and the GCI. Liu Jianchao, then Head of the International Department of the CCP (in practice, a more important body in setting the PRC’s foreign policy than the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [MFA]), made this clear in 2023:

> From the perspective of historical logic, the ‘three major global initiatives’ are closely related to the three major themes of the progress of human society, and together constitute the ‘three pillars’ of the building of a community with a shared future for mankind.[[4]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn4)

At the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in September 2025, Xi announced a fourth pillar: the GGI. He has also talked of the Global Artificial Intelligence Governance Initiative (GAIGI), but this lacks the status of the other four. At the BRICS summit on 12th-13th September 2026, Xi announced that ‘China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open-source community.’[[5]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn5) He also proposed the ‘BRICS initiative of AI-empowered new industrialisation’.[[6]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn6) It would not be surprising if Xi were to announce a Global Technology Initiative in the future.

Together, ‘the four major global initiatives are organically unified and mutually reinforcing, collectively constituting important strategic measures for promoting the building of a community with a shared future for mankind.’[[7]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn7) This and other similar pronouncements do not mention the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). The BRI receives less emphasis than in the past, but it will not be allowed to disappear – not least because the CCP has managed to insert it into UN and other international documents. Reduced mention of the BRI may also reflect reduced willingness to pour the large sums of the past into future BRI projects. The newer GDI label fits the more targeted approach that the CCP has brought to projects abroad.

## **An arch and four pillars**

The definitions of the ‘community of a shared future’ and the four global initiatives have evolved over time, retaining their degree of woolliness in order to cater for future global events. They are also important vectors for the CCP’s propaganda war against the US and its allies.

### **Building a community with a shared future for mankind**

First used by Hu Jintao, then General Secretary of the CCP, in the context of Taiwan at the Party Congress of 2007, the concept has been requisitioned by Xi as his own, not least in international speeches: in Moscow (March 2013), in New York (September 2015 at the UN), and in Geneva (January 2017 at the UN). Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the PRC and Politburo member, set out its developed form in November 2025, listing six constituents:

1.   Advocating a multipolar world of equality, order, and economic globalisation, which is universally beneficial and inclusive;
2.   Deepening integration of development with neighbouring countries and safeguarding regional peace and stability;
3.   Maintaining overall stability in major actor relations (e.g., with Russia, the US, Europe, and emerging nations);[[8]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn8)
4.   Deepening solidarity and cooperation with developing countries;
5.   Implementing the four ‘global initiatives’;
6.   Promoting the building of a world of lasting peace, universal security, common prosperity, openness and inclusiveness, and cleanness and beauty (i.e., environmental issues).[[9]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn9)

Few would disagree with these six elements as a prescription for global stability and prosperity; all would want to know what they mean in practice. The four global initiatives provide more – but not full – elucidation.

### **The Global Development Initiative (September 2021)**

According to the SCIO in September 2023, the fundamental aim of the GDI is to accelerate the implementation of the UN’s 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.[[10]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn10) Xi told the ‘BRICS+’ leaders’ dialogue in Kazan in October 2024:

> We should play an active and leading role in the global economic governance reform, and make development the core of international economic and trade agenda.[[11]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn11)

The SCIO echoed this sentiment in June 2026:

> With more than 130 countries and international organisations supporting participation in the initiative and over 80 countries joining the Group of Friends of the Global Development Initiative…China has signed more than 80 cooperation documents on implementing the initiative with other developing countries, international organisations, and financial institutions.’[[12]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn12)

In 2024, Xi claimed that since its introduction in 2021, the GDI had helped to make available nearly US$20 billion (£15.1 billion) of development funds and had launched more than 1,100 projects.[[13]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn13) By June 2026, ‘more than US$23 billion [£17.4 billion] of development funds of various types have been mobilised’, and the PRC had ‘launched more than 1,800 cooperation projects, and completed the training of 80,000 people within the framework of the initiative’[[14]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn14) – representing a considerably lower commitment of funds in the past two years than the preceding three.

Such claims require caution: it is not clear how much funding represents new money as opposed to existing projects repackaged under the GDI label. Additionally, findings by AidData, an aid and development research institute, show that the PRC’s grant aid (as opposed to loans) is a very small total of its foreign funding. Recently, the bulk of the PRC’s overseas investment has gone not to developing countries but to _developed_ ones, as the CCP pursues its aim of dominating new technologies.[[15]](https://www.geostrategy.org.uk/all-research/chinas-four-new-global-initiatives/#fn15) In pushing the GDI, the CCP frequently attacks or stresses the contrast with the US, often referred to as ‘some countries’.

### **The Global Security Initiative (April 2022)**

Xi often draws on his predecessors’ ideas, even if his burgeoning personality cult credits him alone for all aspects of the ‘thought’. In the case of the GSI, Jiang Zemin, then General Secretary of the CCP,

title: 澳前总理陆克文：2028年是台海局势“尤其危险的一年”，有效威慑是关键

澳大利亚前总理陆克文(Kevin Rudd)近日表示，2028年可能是台海局势“尤其危险的一年”，他强调有效威慑仍是避免冲突的关键。对美国实力，陆克文同时说，中国领导人习近平对美国的实力的看法比较“辩证”：一方面不会低估美国的军事、经济科技和美元实力，另一方面又可能从马克思主义历史观出发，将美国的国内分裂等现象视为西方相对衰落的迹象。

他是在10月2日布鲁金斯学会举行的名为“美中关系下一步：与陆克文对话”的活动上提出了上述观点。活动举行之际，美中领导人刚刚结束新一轮峰会。讨论围绕两国如何管控竞争、降低冲突风险、寻找合作空间，以及双边关系能否建立更稳定的基础展开。

**2028年可能成为风险窗口 应对核心靠威慑**

在谈及台湾问题时，陆克文称2028年可能是“尤其危险的一年”。

他说，2028年1月将举行台湾选举，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)届时处于总统任期最后一年，而习近平也可能获得连续第四个任期。如果民进党再次赢得选举，“这会不会在习近平心目中成为一个触发点，成为对台湾采取某种军事行动的触发因素？我认为这一风险有所升高。”

他反复强调，应对这一风险的核心仍是“威慑、威慑、威慑”。

“为什么？因为它行之有效。我们非常务实地看待这些问题。如果毛泽东1949年能够拿下台湾，他当时就会这么做。台湾从1949年到2026年一直没有被拿下，是因为采取行动的风险超过了冒这些风险所能获得的收益。这就是威慑的本质，” 陆克文说，“威慑之所以如此重要，成为我们在这一地区国家安全架构的支点，是因为它是战略稳定的基石，而战略稳定又是整个地区持续经济发展的基石。”

陆克文说，一旦威慑失效、战争爆发，影响将远远超出台海。

日本、韩国以及美国其他盟友将如何反应？美国主导的地区秩序是否会受到根本冲击？全球贸易和投资流动将发生什么变化？世界经济是否可能陷入衰退甚至萧条？陆克文认为，这些后果都需要被纳入考量。

他表示，要让威慑继续发挥作用，必须同时具备两个要素：能力和意图。他还指出，“威慑”在中国军事理论中同样是一个既有概念。他认为，相互威慑可以成为维持战略稳定的一种方式。

**习近平对美国实力的看法“辩证”**

当被问及习近平会如何评估特朗普政府治下的美国，陆克文说，基于他与习近平交往的经历，习近平的判断中存在一种“辩证张力”。

他说：“当他看美国时，他仍然看到支撑美国实力的三大支柱：美国的军事实力、美国的经济和科技实力，以及美元的力量。”

“他是一个敏锐的权力观察者。”陆克文说。按照他的分析，习近平不会因为华盛顿一时的政治争论而忽略美国的现实实力，而是会判断这些支柱本身是否发生了实质变化。

另一方面，陆克文认为，习近平也会透过马克思列宁主义历史观观察美国。美国国内的政治分裂、在印太地区以外的军事投入，以及围绕人工智能监管的争论，都可能被他解读为美国和西方出现“结构性衰退”的迹象。

陆克文说：“当他透过美国国内政治的视角，看到这里的政治分裂，看到美国专注于印太地区以外的战争和军事行动，例如伊拉克、阿富汗和伊朗，再看到美国国内甚至还在争论如何监管和约束硅谷的人工智能巨头时，他会透过这样一种视角来看待这些现象，认为它们体现了美国结构性衰退的一些因素。”

陆克文认为习近平“百年未有之大变局”和“东升西降”等表述，其实是体现马克思主义历史观的一种暗语。

陆克文说：“意思是这个单极世界正在变成一个多极世界。而更深一层的含义是，世界正在变成两极世界，然后成为由中国主导的世界，而且这种变化正在发生。”

“一方面，他以一种深刻的现实主义视角看待支撑美国实力持续存在的因素；另一方面，他又以马克思主义历史观看待美国和西方，认为美国和西方正在衰落。” 陆克文说。

title: If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead
summary: If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead bbert@hudson.org Mon, 10/05/2026 - 12:14 SVG Commentary Oct 2, 2026 The Hill If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead Rebeccah L. Heinrichs Senior Fellow and Director, Keystone Defense Initiative S
content: If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead bbert@hudson.org Mon, 10/05/2026 - 12:14 SVG Commentary Oct 2, 2026 The Hill If America Wants to Prosper, We Must Lead Rebeccah L. Heinrichs Senior Fellow and Director, Keystone Defense Initiative Senator Rick Scott Rebeccah L. Heinrichs & Senator Rick Scott Commentary Caption Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping enter the hall during a signing ceremony on May 20, 2026, in Beijing, China. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print Last week at the United Nations General Assembly , President Trump issued a “challenge for every nation in this room” to “go forward strong and united against the enemies of all humanity” and, by doing so, “make this world a far better and safer place.” While it is tempting to write Trump’s words off as rhetorical fanfare, the mission they describe is real, critical and — unfortunately — now being dismissed by many in the U.S. Lately, a foolish worldview is growing in popularity among elected leaders in Washington. You hear it from voices ranging from Tucker Carlson to Hasan Piker. Some on the left and right have become convinced that solving America’s domestic issues requires our retreat from leadership on the world stage. Their narrative requires us to ignore history and believe that America is in irreversible decline and has shriveled in form from her former greatness. But America’s best days are ahead, and we can and must stay energetically engaged in foreign policy to protect Americans and our way of life. And so, we must be clear about what a U.S. retreat would mean and how American life would look if we allowed Communist China to write the rules and our enemies to establish a New World Order. These views, often sold as populist ideas, are nothing new. Nearly a century ago, America faced similar choices as evil around the world began to threaten our security. In the fall of 1939, the devastation caused by the Great Depression hung like a dark cloud over the lives of many Americans while Nazi Germany invaded Poland. While the news out of Europe was troubling, there were plenty of “leaders” in Washington telling hardworking families that America couldn’t possibly be worried about the security of Europe when our own citizens couldn’t guarantee the security of their own jobs. These are the same arguments being sold today as young Americans worry about grocery bills, the cost of electricity, and how they are going to afford to raise a family. Of course, the choice between global leadership and domestic prosperity is a false one. The American Dream depends on the United States’ leadership in the world, where we set rules in a way that protects the American people, secures our economy, and advances our goals. America First is not possible if America surrenders its position on the world stage. We want an America strong enough to deter our enemies and win a war if an adversary starts one. That does not mean getting entangled in forever wars and needless regime change operations with no goal and no endgame. What the Tucker-Piker camp fails to understand is that America still has enemies. Communist China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba have created an anti-American coalition — an authoritarian alliance — to undercut us as the global superpower and sever the ties between the U.S. and the Western coalition. And it doesn’t end with China — Russia is waging a war of choice in Ukraine to test the resolve of NATO and to scare Americans into believing that they must surrender peace among their oldest and most prosperous Western democracies or risk catastrophic war. Those powers — supported by authoritarians in Iran, North Korea and Cuba — are consolidating with one goal: undermine the United States, replace its influence with those of authoritarian powers, and undermine the world that the West has built. This is happening at different levels and with different methods. The Chinese Communist Party is leveraging economic dependence against the West to bend our allies toward its interests. Russia is attempting to break NATO to claim territory from sovereign democratic nations. Iran is destabilizing the Middle East and global trade. Meanwhile, North Korea is investing in its illegal nuclear missile program while providing soldiers to Russia for its war against Ukraine . All four nations are collaborating in various ways, and aim to push the U.S., its forward deployed bases, and its influence out of their regions. In our own, Cuba has proven to be the greatest destabilizing force in the Western Hemisphere for decades. I have no doubt our foreign adversaries see a useful domestic asset in Islamist-Socialist Hasan Piker — an American via birthright citizenship only — who wants capitalists dead , believed 9/11 was justified , and campaigns for socialists in our elections. It cannot be any clearer: the authoritarian alliance desires the destruction of the postwar order, and the rights and prosperity generations have died defending. If we retreat and allow this authoritarian alliance to take hold, America will suffer. Communist China and its accomplices will starve us, isolate us, and deprive us of every resource possible until America is weak and dependent. We will have no autonomy, no opportunity, and no freedom. Our financial markets will be powerless to fuel innovation, our business will shutter, and the American Dream will die. President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio understand what’s at stake, and they’ve shown that there’s a smarter way to do it than the mistakes we’ve seen this century. They showed the world America is not giving up. President Trump made NATO allies recommit to the alliance and have encouraged others outside the alliance to join the cause. They also understand the need to reduce our exposure to our enemies, especially via trade. Every dollar we send to Beijing — and the rest of the authoritarian alliance — is capital for them to hurt us and our allies. Retreating from the challenges to our power will not appease them; it only increases the cost of confronting them down the road. Strong leadership creates the environment for domestic security and economic prosperity. Without it, America and her allies remain vulnerable to criminal regimes who hate our way of life. We cannot sacrifice national and global security to a false dilemma of domestic versus overseas issues. It is not a zero-sum equation. To believe it would destroy a century of American greatness and the American Dream itself. Americans deserve a future that is safe, prosperous and free. For that to happen, America must lead. title: Cardinal Zen, singer Denise Ho and 3 other trustees take 2019 protest fund convictions to top court
summary: Five pro-democracy figures convicted of failing to register a fund linked to the 2019 protests and unrest have taken their case to Hong Kong’s top court, after losing an appeal last month. Cardinal Joseph Zen (centre) appears at the High Co
content: Five pro-democracy figures convicted of failing to register a fund linked to the 2019 protests and unrest have taken their case to Hong Kong’s top court, after losing an appeal last month. Cardinal Joseph Zen (centre) appears at the High Court alongside, from left, scholar Hui Po-keung, barrister Margaret Ng, ex-lawmaker Cyd Ho, and singer-activist Denise Ho, on September 3, 2026. Photo: Hans Tse/HKFP. Cardinal Joseph Zen, barrister Margaret Ng, former lawmaker Cyd Ho, scholar Hui Po-keung, and singer-activist Denise Ho were listed on the Court of Final Appeal website’s list of forthcoming appeals when HKFP checked on Monday. The five were trustees of the since-disbanded 612 Humanitarian Relief Fund , which provided financial assistance to protesters arrested during the anti-extradition protests and unrest in 2019. The assistance was used to pay for protesters’ legal, medical, or other fees. The five were found guilty in November 2022  of not registering their fund as a society under the city’s Societies Ordinance, and were each fined HK$4,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts. Last month, the Court of Appeal upheld the convictions . The five had lodged an appeal arguing that the fund was established as a trust rather than a society. They also argued that the ruling implied nearly all groups holding activities must be registered as societies, infringing upon the freedom of association. The Court of Final Appeal. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. In the judgment, three Court of Appeal judges said the fund was indeed a society, and therefore it had to apply for registration or an exemption under the law. Chief Judge of the High Court Jeremy Poon called the fund more than “a mere sum of moneys held by the appellants,” and said that the appellants had used the fund to appeal for and collect donations to support the 2019 protests. According to local media, the guilty verdicts mark the first time there has been a conviction for this offence. The fund’s trustees announced in August 2021 that it would disband because it no longer had a bank account it could use. At the time, Ng said it was a “matter of deep regret” that the fund had to cease operations, but that it was “already a remarkable achievement for Hong Kong civil society that we have come this far.”

content:
## SHIFTING COOPERATION: With the new arrangement, US representatives would be able to participate directly in defense discussions, including weapons procurement

*   By Lo Tien-pin and Fion Khan / Staff reporter, with staff writer

*       *   [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com)
    *   [_![Image 1](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/x.png)_](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=US+to+assign+liaisons+in+MND%3A+sources%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ffront%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F04%2F2003865354)
    *   [_![Image 2](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/facebook.png)_](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ffront%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F04%2F2003865354&t=US+to+assign+liaisons+in+MND%3A+sources)
    *   [_![Image 3](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/line.png)_](https://lineit.line.me/share/ui?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ffront%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F04%2F2003865354?utm_medium=P&utm_campaign=SHARE&utm_source=LINE)

Taiwan-US military cooperation is deepening, with the Pentagon expected to station personnel at the Ministry of National Defense (MND), sources said.

The NT$470 million (US$14.77 million) joint program is scheduled to run from this year through 2028, under which the Pentagon would dispatch representatives from the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy and the Institute for Defense Analyses, a senior military official said on condition of anonymity, adding that one representative from each organization would be stationed at the ministry’s headquarters.

The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy is one of the US’ bodies responsible for formulating national security and defense strategy, and would help align policy coordination between Taipei and Washington, they said.

## The US Pentagon’s logo is pictured in the briefing room at the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, in an undated photograph.

Photo: Reuters

The Institute for Defense Analyses is a defense think tank known for using data analysis and mathematical modeling to conduct complex defense simulations and operational assessments, they added.

The arrangement would place US personnel closer to Taiwan’s defense policymaking process and allow them to assist with policy coordination and combat capability assessments, elevating bilateral military integration to the highest level, they said.

The move supplements the presence of hundreds of US military instructors in Taiwan who have assisted with military training.

US defense personnel have long maintained a presence in Taiwan, usually in less visible roles, an anonymous military official said.

The American Institute in Taiwan’s (AIT) security cooperation and technical offices are staffed by active-duty US military personnel and civilian defense officials responsible for coordinating arms sales and logistics cooperation, they said.

The US’ Defense Innovation Unit has also over the past few years assigned liaison officers to the AIT to help integrate Taiwan’s drone and technology supply chains to address technological warfare and cross-strait tensions.

However, the new arrangement differs, because US representatives would work directly with Taiwan’s defense ministry rather than through AIT, the sources said.

That signals a shift in Taiwan-US military cooperation from tactical training to higher-level strategic planning and wargaming, they said.

US instructors usually focus on operational training and weapons employment, while the new arrangement would allow US experts to participate more directly in discussions on overall defense planning and asymmetric warfare tactics, such as providing on-site advice during the Han Kuang exercises and major weapons procurement evaluations, they added.

The move also reflects concrete efforts to institutionalize and normalize security cooperation between Taiwan and the US through legislation, such as the Taiwan Enhanced Resilience Act and successive US national defense authorization acts, they said.

However, the presence of US personnel within the core of Taiwan’s defense establishment would require stricter mechanisms governing the sharing of classified information, confidentiality procedures and cybersecurity protections, the sources said.

title: Xi’s rest breaks cut hours from Trump summit schedule - WSJ
summary: Simon Mugo Fri, October 2, 2026 at 11:14 p.m. EDT **Investing.com --** Chinese officials sought unusually long rest periods for President Xi Jinping during his recent Washington summit with U.S. President Donald Trump, cutting hours from th
content:
Simon Mugo

Fri, October 2, 2026 at 11:14 p.m. EDT

**Investing.com --** Chinese officials sought unusually long rest periods for President Xi Jinping during his recent Washington summit with U.S. President Donald Trump, cutting hours from the leaders' schedule, the Wall Street Journal reported exclusively.

Beijing's requests included a private room inside the West Wing where Xi could rest between events, with only his wife, Peng Liyuan, permitted to join him, according to people familiar with planning for the visit.

Chinese officials also declined a planned working lunch between Xi and Trump on Sept. 24, the summit's only full day, saying they preferred additional downtime for Xi. The scheduling changes resulted in a roughly five-hour gap in the agenda during a visit lasting less than two days.

No activities were arranged for Xi on the evening of his arrival following a roughly 14-hour flight from Beijing. His visit to the National Archives on Sept. 25 lasted about 10 minutes, shorter than U.S. officials had planned.

The Journal said Xi's team also structured the schedule around considerations including how long he could stand and walk and when he would need breaks. Dennis Wilder, a former senior China director at the National Security Council, described the private room arrangement as unusual compared with previous state visits he helped organize.

The bilateral meeting at the White House on Sept. 24 began close to noon and ended by early afternoon. Xi then left the White House and returned for the state dinner that evening, limiting the time available for substantive discussions.

The report pointed to visible caution in Xi's movements during the visit, including holding Peng's hand as he descended aircraft stairs and climbed steps at the National Archives.

The Journal said some scheduling changes could be explained by jet lag. It also cited analysts who said they saw no signs of cognitive decline in Xi's public appearances.

Questions surrounding China's leadership succession have attracted attention because Xi has not designated a successor. He holds China's three major leadership positions as Communist Party general secretary, president, and chairman of the Central Military Commission.

title: Xi’s Purge and the War Over Taiwan
summary: Executive Summary: Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia’s expulsion from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) was politically motivated; Chairman Xi Jinping’s purge of the PLA high command is best explained by his dissa
content: Executive Summary: Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia’s expulsion from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) was politically motivated; Chairman Xi Jinping’s purge of the PLA high command is best explained by his dissatisfaction with senior officers’ assessments of an operation against Taiwan and their willingness to act on Xi’s orders. The Fujian-based generals Xi once trusted most, as well as the leadership of the Equipment Development Department and Rocket Force, and Zhang himself shared a professional caution about a cross-Strait war. Xi appears to have read their warnings as cowardice and resistance to the 2027 military readiness goal. The purge shows political will emphasized over military professionalism. Military conflict is less likely in the short term while new officers enter their posts, but gray-zone pressure will likely escalate. A leadership consisting of compliant subordinates makes war increasingly likely over time. Editor’s note: Jiang Lin is a former Lieutenant Colonel in the People’s Liberation Army and served as a reporter for the PLA Daily for 27 years. Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia’s (张又侠) time as Xi Jinping’s number two at the top of the Chinese military came to an end at the beginning of 2026. It was only in late September, however, that he was finally expelled from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Zhang, whose political failings were put front and center in the official announcement of his purge, is now set for a military prosecution ( Xinhua , September 21; China Brief , September 23). The official record divulges little information about the precise nature of Zhang’s crimes—political or otherwise. Part of what makes it so difficult to uncover the facts of his case is that the official record itself is unreliable. The Party’s pronouncements follow a logic of their own, and truth is far from a necessary criterion. The initial notice announcing that Zhang was under investigation was followed by an editorial in the PLA Daily that accused Zhang of being involved in five offenses. These included gravely betraying the trust and heavy responsibilities placed on him by the Party Central Committee and the CMC, severely trampling upon and undermining the CMC Chairman responsibility system, and seriously fueling political and corruption problems ( PLA Daily , January 25). The seriousness of these offenses indicated that corruption alone could not have been the root cause of the accusations. As the September announcement now suggests, Zhang’s crimes were ultimately political in nature. Mass Purges are a Response to Political Crimes Xi is not the first to remove disagreeable generals before forging ahead with hostilities. In 1938, for example, Adolf Hitler used the Blomberg–Fritsch affair—a scandal that was partly real and partly concocted—to reshuffle his high command and accrue more direct power over the military. Xi is also not the only PRC leader to do so, either. In 1962, Mao elected to attack India, not long after a shake up of the PLA high command following the dismissal of Peng Dehuai (彭德怀), his top military officer throughout the 1950s ( Foreign Affairs , July 18, 2025). The Party leadership’s most prominent purge of senior People’s Liberation Army (PLA) officers for political crimes took place between June 1989 and mid-1992, following the Tiananmen Square Massacre, when the CMC purged or sidelined key generals who had initially opposed the intervention, replaced six of the seven military region commanders, and engineered a complete turnover of PLA representation on the Central Committee ( People’s Daily , November 10, 1989; CSIS , February 24).  [1] Some research indicates that an estimated 3,500 PLA officers were purged for disobeying orders (Wall Street Journal, October 9, 1991).  [2] Only political reasons could have driven such a large purge. General Secretary Xi Jinping’s similarly dramatic purge appears likewise to have been motivated by political factors. In his case, the most likely explanation for his actions is dissatisfaction over both the readiness and willingness of senior officers to stage operations targeting Taiwan. Unification with Taiwan has been of central importance to Xi since he first came to power. From the start, his principal political objective, which he referred to as the “China dream” (中国梦), had subsuming Taiwan as its main military component. Responsibility for that component of Xi’s agenda falls principally on the PLA. The enormous reforms he launched to both the military and other Party and state institutions during his first term, and his successful efforts to amend the constitution and allow for indefinite tenure as state president, were intended to mobilize the entire system toward the achievement of this primary political objective.  [3] The massive purges seen throughout the PLA in recent years very likely relate to what Xi views as a lack of meaningful progress toward attaining this goal, as others have argued ( China Brief , January 26; AEI , January 28; CSIS , February 24). They began in the early days of Xi’s PLA reforms with the removal of those who opposed his agenda, such as the CMC vice chairs Guo Boxiong (郭伯雄) and Xu Caihou (徐才厚) ( The Diplomat , April 7, 2016). These were followed by the discovery of corruption issues within the Equipment Development Department (EDD) and the Rocket Force during efforts to improve capabilities for a Taiwan scenario. The larger-scale purge that occurred subsequently was driven more by political and military strategy than by issues with reform and corruption. Since 2022, 36 PLA generals and lieutenant generals have been formally purged, while another 65 high-ranking officers have disappeared from public view or may have faced purges ( CSIS , February 24). Of the seven members of the CMC present at the end of 2022, besides Xi Jinping only one remains. Xi Seeks Less Cautious Generals The purge of Zhang and other senior figures most likely represented a clash between Xi’s political strategy and a military community that was cautious about a potential war over Taiwan. When the absolute authority of a Leninist party comes into conflict with the physical realities of modern, professional warfare, this is the only possible resolution if the regime is to persist (China Brief, January 26 , February 11 ). Many believe that former CMC vice chairman He Weidong (何卫东) and officers from the former 31st Group Army were Xi’s most trusted allies in the PLA ( The Diplomat , October 20, 2025). Based in Fujian, Xi came to know them during his nearly 20 years working in the province. If they had been involved in corruption alone, Chinese political tradition indicates that they would likely have received only light punishment, not the unusually harsh treatment that ended up being administered. Those closest to the Taiwan Strait best understand the hard military realities, unlike the political officers in Beijing. They are aware of Taiwan’s strong defensive advantages, such as its difficult terrain, dense anti-ship missiles, and air defenses. They also realize that huge air and sea superiority, as well as long supply lines, would be needed to land large forces successfully, and that U.S. and Japanese intervention, however brief, would cut off any PLA troops who managed to make it ashore. In other words, their caution comes from professional judgment ( China Brief , March 20). When Xi demanded the PLA complete its preparation to attack Taiwan by 2027, the generals’ realistic assessments of high costs and risks sounded like fear and a lack of determination by Xi ( U.S. Department of Defense , November 29, 2022). Although Xi promoted these former Fujian subordinates because he thought they understood the Strait and would obey his command, he expected them to build a fast, powerful force using modern brigades that could quickly disable Taiwan. In a system that demands absolute loyalty, their subsequent claims of immature technology or a lack of readiness was reinterpreted as double-dealing and deliberate deception. Xi concluded that the generals never intended to fight and used professional concerns mainly to mask cowardice and protect themselves. This sense of betrayal was deeper than ordinary corruption, so no graceful exit was allowed ( PLA Daily , October 18, 2025). The final target, Zhang Youxia, shared key traits with the purged Fujian-faction generals on Taiwan strategy issues. As one of the few commanders who had actually led troops in battle, he had a deep, instinctive caution about the brutality of war and the gap between theory and real combat effectiveness ( ISDP , January 30). When frontline Fujian generals—who had spent years war-gaming a Taiwan Strait landing—warned against hasty action based on professional judgment, Zhang agreed and supported them as a fellow professional soldier. Their shared caution about war became a common professional language ( China Brief , January 26). They may have seen some of Xi’s goals, including tight force-building timelines, as unrealistic, and resisted them on professional military grounds. Analysts have speculated that part of Zhang’s downfall could be attributed to his long stint as head of the CMC EDD, which appears to have been a locus of a high degree of corruption ( Global Security/Zhang Youxia , accessed October 1). A more likely reason why this could be a contributing factor to his demise, however, is that the department fully adhered to Zhang’s cautious stance, and many senior officials who were later purged, such as Li Shangfu (李尚福), were subordinates that Zhang had promoted during his tenure there. This led to a situation—that for Xi was unacceptable—in which officials in charge of weapons development (the EDD and Rocket Force), frontline combat preparation (Eastern Theater Command and Fujian faction), and overall military oversight (Zhang himself) developed a strong shared understanding of tactical pragmatism with regard to a possible Taiwan Strait war. Together, they were seen as systematically using technical excuses and equipment shortcomings to resist Xi’s unification strategy passively. A strong indicator of this is Zhang’s assertion, in the pages of the PLA Daily in late 2025, that 2035, not 2027, would be the year by which the military would acquire all-domain operational capabilities ( People’s Daily , November 12, 2025; China Brief , January 26). Conclusion Xi’s purge appears to be a decisive victory of political will over military professionalism. The removal of seasoned veterans who valued professional caution about war could lead to replacements who are less likely to push back on Xi’s demands ( CSIS , February 2024). This could propel the Taiwan Strait situation along a more dangerous path. Though Xi’s purge reduces the short-term probability of a kinetic conflict, as promoted officers familiarize themselves with their new billets, gray-zone warfare is likely to continue to escalate. The greatest danger is that the information cocoon created by submissive subordinates, coupled with Xi’s arbitrary exercise of power, creates the conditions that make war across the Taiwan Strait increasingly likely once the new PLA leadership team is formed. Notes [1] As a victim of that purge, one of us can verify that it was indeed politically motivated ( NYT , May 28, 2015; NYT Chinese Edition , May 29, 2019; NYT Chinese Edition , June 3, 2019). Numerous generals involved in defying the martial law order were sentenced, dismissed, or demoted—such as Xu Qinxian (徐勤先), commander of the 38th Army ( The Guardian , December 24, 2025), He Yanran (何燕然), Commander of the 28th Army ( CND , December 31, 2025), Li Lianxiu (李连秀), Commander of the People’s Armed Police Force ( RFA , June 9, 2023), and Xu Feng (许峰), Commander of the 116th Division of the 39th Army ( DW , June 4, 2018). [2] Chong-Pin Lin. “China’s Restive Army.” Wall Street Journal , October 9, 1991. [3] For analysis of Xi’s structural reforms to the military over the last decade, see: Miller, Frank, Tung Ho, Kenneth Allen, and Arran Hope, eds. The People’s Liberation Army as Organization Volume 3.0 . Washington, D.C.: The Jamestown Foundation; Vienna: Exovera, 2025. The post Xi’s Purge and the War Over Taiwan appeared first on Jamestown .

content: 李承鹏（大眼哥）   X @dayangelcp · Oct 2, 2026 我的油管第11期：《 中美历史恩怨合订本——十大美好瞬间和十大交恶时刻 》。 历史每天都很正确，就是不能看合订本。郭德纲老师说，凡事就怕同行衬托。别看宴会上你侬我侬唱你问，我爱你，有多深……你爱我有多深，得看合同签几分。 历史就这么诡异，当年要是乒乓球运动员科恩没上错大巴，老毛晚上安眠药剂量再大一点，基辛格表演肚子疼没成功……中美指不准啥时候才能建交，老百姓指不准啥时候才能看上电视、冰箱。 1979年大年初一，邓小平在飞往美国的专机上说：回头看这几十年，凡是和美国搞好关系的国家，都富起来了。 在肯尼迪中心，200名美国孩子用中文合唱《我爱北京天安门》……你看，美国早就让孩子唱中文歌接待中国元首了。邓小平竟然还跑上台去亲吻孩子，用洋范儿动作争取西方世界的接纳。你很难把这温馨一幕跟十年后下令广场开枪的屠夫联想起来。 卡特说“送10万人来！”邓小平马上给美国送去一大批留学生，其中就有王沪宁…… 邓小平戴上女骑手献上的白色牛仔帽，向全场挥帽致意。临别时他对卡特说：“我们不怕美国的制度，美国也不必怕我们。” 但对美国制度骨子里的恐惧很快暴露，四年后中美交恶，因为19岁的网球女子运动员——胡娜出逃，寻求政治庇护。坊间狗血传说，邓小平怒斥里根，其中一条是拐骗了我的干女儿。 中美价值观迥异，现实需求却是刚需。里根放宽对华技术出口，承诺执行“一个中国”政策，中国再次掀起赴美浪潮。这一年，一位年轻的中国县委书记随农业考察团来到小城马斯卡廷。他衣着整洁、每次准时，很有好奇心，住进了当地一户农民家。他，就是习近平…… 老布什在长城饭店举行答谢宴会，邀请了中国异见知识分子方励之夫妇，但方励之夫妇在路上被警察堵住了。“六四”发生，枪声和坦克履带声打碎了幻想……老布什带头全面制裁中国，中美关系再次降到冰点。 中美就像一场虐恋。克林顿称：只要中国经济发展了，民主就水到渠成。1997年，正式邀请江泽民访美，在夏威夷，老江愉快地弹起夏威夷吉他……蜜月又回来了。中美总是规律性的一会儿蜜月，一会儿交恶。 1998年6月，克林顿访华，在人民大会堂的全球记者会上，在中央电视台全程直播中，全国人民都看见了——克林顿公开表示：“六四事件中使用武力、造成人命损失是错误的”，他还力挺达赖……而江泽民竟然在央视全程直播中，跟美国总统碰撞六四、西藏、台湾这些极敏感的话题，这是中国元首史上唯一一次。 惊喜不惊喜，意外不意外。所以，当看到小白们因为这次会谈上唱了中国歌就激动不已，我这老登真想拍着您的肩膀说：年轻人，图漾图森破…… 两天后，克林顿去北大与学生辩论自由和人权问题，央视竟然播出画面。克林顿引用胡适的话说：个人争取自由，也是在为国家争取自由。北大中文系女生马楠反驳……几年后她移民美国，嫁给美国人。 经历过那个时代的我，也被这段历史给惊呆了，中国元首竟然跟美国总统在央视直播辩论六四、西藏，人权。美国总统竟可以窜访北大……回首往事，恍若隔世。就请问：您怀不怀念那个时代，而那个时代，正是中美之间最好的时代。 结论是：一定要和美国搞好关系，和美国关系好的时候，就是中国最开放的时代。 点击进入： —————————————————— 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 5h 寓言般的画面是：马斯克，黄仁勋，库克，苏姿丰和她老公，与美国总统、中国元首坐一张桌吃饭。你能想像马云、马化腾、雷军、潘石屹跟习近平坐在一张桌上吃饭？ 要啥自行车？让你活着就是皇恩浩荡。当年马云挥斥方遒跟马斯克对谈。五年后，马云消失，马斯克成了世界首富，马斯克问：马云在哪儿…… 马斯克公开骂川普，还当世界首富，还是川普座上宾……任志强写了一封内部信，就判了十八年，生死不明…… 据说一批中国企业家到了华盛顿，没等到通知，稍息、立正，就地解散，从“随行商界代表团”变成“自由行”，跟旅游团大妈打卡去了。而川普用空军一号拉着一群商人到北京吃国宴，又拉着他们在白宫吃国宴，中国商人跟元首一张桌吃饭？ 这还叫社会主义吗，红旗还要不要打？美国商人跟总统吃饭时，中国商人正想着补税和外逃，想着从香港还是越南走更安全，后备厢够不够大，女朋友能不能装下…… 制度DNA差异。商业立国，谁本事大谁上桌。领导立国，让谁上桌才能上桌，鱼头冲谁，霍金见着领导，渐冻症也得好了，站起来“我先干了，领导您随意”。 中国经济能不能好起来，你的生活能不能好起来，取决于中美关系能不能好起来。 点击进入： https:// youtu.be/4vg_xrPIQRs?si =ORQKc4R5TyEUG1CV

title: Alcaraz through in straight sets in Shanghai Masters
summary: **SHANGHAI**— A mustached Carlos Alcaraz beat Juan Manuel Cerundolo, 6-3, 6-3, to kick-start his title bid at the Shanghai Masters on Saturday, days after winning the Tokyo Open for his first trophy since returning from injury. The Spanish
content:
**SHANGHAI**— A mustached Carlos Alcaraz beat Juan Manuel Cerundolo, 6-3, 6-3, to kick-start his title bid at the Shanghai Masters on Saturday, days after winning the Tokyo Open for his first trophy since returning from injury.

The Spanish star, seeded second, put on a dominant show to brush aside the 55th-ranked Argentinian in the second round in just 66 minutes.

“Really, really happy with the way I played today. It wasn’t easy,” said the 23-year-old former number one.

Sporting a fresh moustache, Alcaraz signed a camera “Moustache Team” following his win.

Medvedev was defaulted from his semifinal against Novak Djokovic in Beijing for hitting a spectator with a ball and ended the 500-level event with zero ranking points and no prize money.

title: Hunger stalks Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
summary: KHAN YUNIS, Palestinian Territories — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family. It has been a year since a ceasefire between
content:
KHAN YUNIS, Palestinian Territories — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.

It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.

Masri has little choice. Without the kitchen run by humanitarian groups, she and her eight children would have “nothing at all”, the 35-year-old told AFP.

Each day she sets out early in the morning and returns in the afternoon, this time bringing four containers of rice, lentils and a little chicken, which the family throws itself at.

Among them is her husband, wounded in both legs by an airstrike, meaning he “cannot go and fight with the others” to get food.

[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

But Shaun Hughes, of the UN’s World Food Program, was less sanguine.

The food security situation, he said, “is still extremely serious”.

The most recent figures, from July, show that “1.4 million out of the population of about 2.1 million people are acutely food insecure”, he said, with 200,000 of them “just one step below famine”.

‘Shameful’

*   ![Image 4: Malacañang accepts Aguda resignation – Remulla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254517.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Malacañang accepts Aguda resignation – Remulla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/national/malacaang-accepts-aguda-resignation-remulla/2443171)

While some food is getting in, a lack of sufficient nutritional variety continues to pose a health threat.

“Dietary diversity is a major food security issue in Gaza,” said Hughes.

“You cannot survive on dry goods and wheat flour and bread alone. Particularly children, particularly pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, they need the micronutrients that come with high protein foods, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits,” he explained.

Masri said that her children, aged between three and 14, “dream of eating fruit” but the family doesn’t have the means to buy any.

She said one of her sons suffered from malnutrition during the 2025 famine, although “little by little, his condition is improving”.

Malnutrition isn’t only caused by a lack of food, but also essential nutrients. It weakens the immune system of children, making them vulnerable to illnesses and stunting their growth.

“Repeated bouts of acute malnutrition amongst children is something that human beings just don’t recover from,” said Hughes.

Cognitive and physical impairments “continue into later life”, he added.

At Khan Yunis’s Nasser hospital, the head of the malnutrition unit, Israa al-Najjar, told AFP she had “observed an increase in syndromes and conditions” linked to malnutrition that affect the immune system.

In a report published on Thursday, the day after the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war, Medecins du Monde published a study that found 93 percent of pregnant or breastfeeding women had symptoms of anaemia, which is closely linked to malnutrition.

Just 17 percent had a sufficiently varied diet to meet their nutritional needs, the group found.

All the while, Masri has kept visiting the community kitchen, despite asthma leaving her exhausted.

Her children spend their days collecting “pieces of nylon, bits of cardboard and chunks of foam” to try and reinforce their tent, which is in a poor state.

She said it was “shameful” that her children had to do so.

“I swear to God, this isn’t normal.”

title: Major cities in Taiwan hold flag-raising ceremonies for National Day - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Major cities around Taiwan held flag-raising ceremonies Saturday morning to celebrate the 115th National Day of the Republic of China (ROC), Taiwan's official name. For several of the mayors, it was their last National
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Major cities around Taiwan held flag-raising ceremonies Saturday morning to celebrate the 115th National Day of the Republic of China (ROC), Taiwan's official name.

For several of the mayors, it was their last National Day ceremony in office. Taiwan will hold local elections on Nov. 28, and mayors who have served two consecutive four-year terms cannot run again; their successors take office on Dec. 25.

In Taichung, Mayor Lu Shiow-yen (盧秀燕) presided over a ceremony at which a drone carrying the national flag flew over the plaza in front of city hall, as the crowd looked on.

Lu, who is completing her second and final term, said she was proud of her administration's achievements, including improvements in air quality, the reinstatement of health insurance premium subsidies for senior citizens, and the construction of the Taichung International Exhibition Center.

As mayor, she said, she had always emphasized cooperation between the city government and the city council to keep public works projects on track.

Whoever succeeds her should ensure that the city keeps prospering and its residents keep living well, Lu said.

In Taipei, Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安), who is seeking a second term in the November elections, led attendees in singing the ROC national anthem in front of city hall.

The Taipei City government also set up an entertainment area where visitors who took photos at designated spots, including a 6-meter-tall sculpture of the city's mascot, Bravo Bear, could claim free ice cream.

Speaking to reporters, Chiang said he wished the ROC prosperity and happiness, and hoped that people living and working on the island could enjoy peace and contentment.

Taipei must seize key opportunities to usher in a golden age of artificial intelligence (AI) and establish itself as an international city, he said.

In Tainan, the ceremony opened with an energetic performance by the marching band of Kang Ming Senior High School.

Tainan Mayor Huang Wei-che (黃偉哲), who will also leave office in December, joined residents in front of city hall to pay tribute to the national flag and wish the country prosperity and strength.

Huang said Tainan was reaching a turning point in its development, with the first phase of its underground railway project nearing completion.

The project is expected to improve transportation by better connecting urban areas on both sides of the railway and to spur the city's development, he said.

Given Tainan's rich cultural heritage and strong technological capabilities, the city government will combine resilience with innovation to make the city a more harmonious, progressive, sustainable and livable place, Huang said.

In New Taipei, Mayor Hou Yu-ih (侯友宜) presided over his last National Day flag-raising ceremony after eight years in office.

It was the first time the city had held the ceremony at its second administrative center in Sanchong District, instead of at its main one in Banqiao.

Most of the city's government offices and services have been concentrated in Banqiao, in southwestern New Taipei, Hou said. The second center, which is meant to promote more balanced development, is scheduled to open at the end of this year.

New Taipei, Taiwan's most populous city, also plans to establish a third administrative center in the Wenzijun redevelopment area and a fourth serving Tucheng, Shulin, Sanxia and Yingge districts, he said.

In Kaohsiung, Mayor Chen Chi-mai (陳其邁), who is also in his final months in office, said at the flag-raising ceremony that he would always be proud to have been part of the city, which he said had made significant progress during his six years as mayor.

Chen took office after winning a by-election in 2020, held after then-Mayor Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜) was recalled by voters, and won a full term in 2022.

During that period, Kaohsiung attracted NT$2.7 trillion (US$84.71 billion) in investment, including from contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), helping to expand the city's AI ecosystem and create about 100,000 jobs, Chen said.

Kaohsiung has also benefited from increased revenue from more concerts held in the city, he said, citing 471 concerts held in the city from 2023 through July 2026. The events attracted more than 5 million concertgoers and generated NT$18.9 billion in revenue.

(By Chao Li-yen, Yeh Chen-yun, Chang Jung-hsiang, Tsao Ya-yen, Hung Hsuen-kuang and Frances Huang)

Enditem/sfj

title: Speaker Han makes 3 wishes for Taiwan, calls for political compromise - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜) on Saturday wished for a secure Taiwan, prosperity for its people and a thriving democracy, while urging the government and the opposition to resolve their differences through compr
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜) on Saturday wished for a secure Taiwan, prosperity for its people and a thriving democracy, while urging the government and the opposition to resolve their differences through compromise.

Speaking at the National Day ceremony in his capacity as chairman of the National Day Preparatory Committee, Han said just as people make wishes on their birthdays, everyone could join in making three wishes for the Republic of China (ROC), Taiwan's official name, on its 115th birthday.

His first wish was for Taiwan's security. The country must never descend into war, he said.

He urged political leaders not to deepen divisions over national identity and called on them to defend the ROC, protect democracy and freedom, maintain ties with the United States and preserve peace across the Taiwan Strait.

His second wish was for greater prosperity for the people.

He urged the government to ensure that older manufacturing industries, tourism, the cultural and creative sectors, health care, agriculture and fisheries also benefit from Taiwan's economic growth, so that high-tech industries do not thrive while other sectors struggle.

His third wish was for democracy to thrive. Taiwan's democracy was built through generations of effort, Han said, and protecting it is a shared responsibility of the ruling and opposition parties and the public.

Han said Taiwan's democracy was showing signs of strain, citing last year's recall campaigns against opposition lawmakers, which he described as "political persecution," and the executive branch's refusal to countersign bills passed by the Legislature.

He warned that the standoff between the Executive Yuan and the Legislative Yuan could damage Taiwan's international reputation as a democracy, saying Taiwan must not be seen by the world as a "fake democracy, real dictatorship."

President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) and Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) must help resolve the standoff through dialogue and compromise, he said.

Quoting former President Chen Shui-bian (陳水扁), he said, "Politics inevitably involves conflict, but compromise leads to progress."

Han expressed confidence that the Cabinet and opposition parties could work together to advance Taiwan's democracy.

## Responses to Han's remarks

Chuang Jui-hsiung (莊瑞雄), chief executive of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) legislative caucus, said national celebrations should unite the public and not be used as an occasion for political attacks, adding that the speaker should build bridges instead of deepening divisions.

Chuang said the DPP supports Han's three wishes but accused him of inflaming tensions by using terms such as "political persecution" and "fake democracy, real dictatorship."

The speaker should lead by example if he wants political parties to overcome their differences, Chuang said.

Legislator Hung Mong-kai (洪孟楷), of the opposition Kuomintang, backed Han, saying the Cabinet's repeated refusal to countersign bills passed by the Legislature raised serious questions about the separation of powers and the proper functioning of Taiwan's constitutional order.

Lai should rise above party politics and help resolve the impasse between the executive and legislative branches, Hung said, stressing that democracy requires respecting institutions, not making decisions that merely serve the ruling party's interests.

He praised Han's remarks as an important reminder to the government of its responsibility to safeguard Taiwan's security and democracy.

Taiwan People's Party Legislator Hung Yu-hsiang (洪毓祥) also praised the remarks, saying democracy is about more than elections and voting and requires those in power to accept scrutiny and abide by the Constitution.

(By Wang Cheng-chung and Ko Lin)

Enditem/sfj

title: 'Human-authored' book labels gain ground amid AI scandals
summary: FRANKFURT, Germany — Initiatives to label books as written by humans, and not artificial intelligence, are gaining ground following a string of scandals where authors were suspected of using the technology without admitting it. Several labe
content:
FRANKFURT, Germany — Initiatives to label books as written by humans, and not artificial intelligence, are gaining ground following a string of scandals where authors were suspected of using the technology without admitting it.

Several labelling schemes, including from Britain, France and Germany, were being showcased at the world's biggest book industry fair in Frankfurt this week, where the challenges posed by AI were hotly debated.

Among recent cases where authors allegedly used AI, the most high-profile is that of Haitian-Canadian author Thelyson Orelien, which has rocked the French-language literary world. He has denied the claims.

The affair was a "real earthquake" for the French book trade, Charlotte Allibert, co-founder of Librinova, a self-publishing company and literary agency, told AFP.

The French group runs a scheme under which authors can get their books assessed and then labelled as a "human creation" for a small fee, with about 200 works so far given the stamp.
