Writers who want the label have their works run through AI detection software and undergo an interview with an auditor, who also checks the book personally.

**"It's reassuring for authors to know that we're committed to this issue," said Allibert.**

"More and more, authors are afraid of being suspected of using AI -- self‑published authors even more so."

*   ![Image 1: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

**- 'Organic literature' -**

Another scheme is from British startup Books By People, which this week announced its certification mark for human-authored works had been registered by the country's intellectual property office.

To get the stamp, titles have to meet the group's "organic literature" standards, which require the writing to originate from its author while allowing limited use of AI for tasks such as spelling or grammar checks.

"We want to create a comprehensive, transparent, reliable framework that publishers and authors can fall back on," Esme Dennys, the initiative's co-founder, told AFP.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

"Anxiety around undisclosed AI use has increased in recent months -- we have been getting a lot more interest from people all over the world."

Publishers sign up to the scheme for a fee, and can then request to get their authors' books labelled with the Books By People mark.

The scheme launched with five independent publishers and is set to announce more members in the coming months.

In the United States, writers group the Authors Guild has introduced a "human authored" certification mark.

*   ![Image 3: No first-round bye for projected No. 13 seed Eala at Wuhan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253937.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[No first-round bye for projected No. 13 seed Eala at Wuhan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/sports/no-first-round-bye-for-projected-no-13-seed-eala-at-wuhan/2442979)

It is a self-certification system which requires authors to sign a license agreement, and so far around 6,500 titles have received the stamp.

**- Mounting scandals -**

The controversy surrounding Orelien erupted last month when an anonymous X account alleged the 38-year old used AI to write his debut novel "It Was Either That or Die", based on analysis of excerpts by AI-detection websites.

He has denied the claims and believes the attacks on his work are racially motivated, although the scandal led to him being dropped from France's top literary prize.

There have also been a string of other cases in recent times.

Earlier this year publisher Hachette cancelled the release of horror novel "Shy Girl" by Mia Ballard in the United States and withdrew the book from sale in Britain over allegations of AI use.

In comments to the New York Times, Ballard denied personally using AI but said that an acquaintance she hired to edit the book, which was originally self-published, had used AI.

**Despite the mounting scandals, some in the book trade view the idea of labels with skepticism.**

Current schemes mostly allow a minimal use of AI, for example for research and grammar checks, but there are worries this could be open to interpretation.

There are also concerns it could be too easy to circumvent checks in the fledgling initiatives, and pass off AI-produced books as human-written.

Sebastian Guggolz, head of the German Publishers and Booksellers Association, said the book trade was struggling with what approach to take.

"There's no simple 'with AI' or 'without AI'," he said at the book fair, adding that basic schemes to categorise how much AI was used to produce a title could fall short.

"The question has to go deeper. It has to be addressed to each individual and to the entire industry: how do we want to make our practices transparent?"

title: Mike Ditka, the quintessential Chicago Bear and a Pro Football Hall of Famer, dies at 86
summary: CHICAGO — Mike Ditka, who personified the toughness and grit of Chicago in a Hall of Fame career as a player and coach of the Bears and the leader of arguably the most dominant team in NFL history, has died. He was 86. **Ditka's family anno
content:
CHICAGO — Mike Ditka, who personified the toughness and grit of Chicago in a Hall of Fame career as a player and coach of the Bears and the leader of arguably the most dominant team in NFL history, has died. He was 86.

**Ditka's family announced his death on Friday in a statement.**

“It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka,” the family said. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.”

*   [Flydubai co-pilot intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, UAE prosecutor says](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/flydubai-co-pilot-intended-to-crash-plane-into-tel-aviv-airport-uae-prosecutor-says/2442894)

Nicknamed “Iron Mike” as a player, Ditka helped revolutionize the tight end position and in 1988 was the first to play at the spot to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He then moved to the sidelines and later took over as Chicago’s coach. His 1985 team featured one of the game’s most dominant defenses ever. It also had enough outsized personalities to record a rap video, “The Super Bowl Shuffle,” and back up their boasting in the championship game three months later.

He was arguably the NFL's most recognizable — and imitated — personality during his time as Chicago's coach with his thick but neatly groomed mustache and sweater vest with “BEARS” emblazoned across the chest. The iconic look is still mimicked by fans at Bears games decades later. That along with his fiery, red-faced sideline tantrums inspired the popular “Da Bears” skit on “Saturday Night Live” during the 1980s.

After retiring as a coach, Ditka became a restaurateur, pitchman and TV personality, as well as a forceful advocate for improved medical and retirement benefits for former players.

Ditka was tough and gruff, the quintessential Chicago Bear. He did everything from order off the menu to knock defensive backs on their butts with a growl. His adopted hometown reveled in every minute.

Revered as "Da Coach," Ditka was the ringmaster of the 1985 Bears, one of the most dominant and perhaps the zaniest Super Bowl-winning team in league history.

*   ![Image 1: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

“When I got to Chicago in the summer of 1985, Mike Ditka and the Chicago Bears were king,” former President Barack Obama wrote on X. “Coach Ditka set the tone for a team that was punishing, dominant, and fun — and the city loved him for it. I’m thinking of the Ditka family and Bears fans everywhere on the passing of a legend.”

Ditka was enshrined in the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame and the Bears said during a ceremony in 2013 that his "No. 89" jersey will be the last one retired by the team.

“Player. Coach. Legend,” the Bears wrote in a tribute on social media. “Mike Ditka embodied the spirit of Chicago and will be deeply missed.”

Ditka was the first person enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio, who had won Super Bowls as a player, assistant coach and head coach. Tom Flores, inducted in 2021, is the only other person to accomplish the feat.

**NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said Ditka “epitomized football over so many years” during his career.**

“He brought intensity, authenticity and an unmistakable personality to everything he did,” Goodell said in a statement. “As a Hall of Fame player, Super Bowl-winning coach with his beloved and iconic Bears, and as a broadcaster, Mike served as an ambassador for the game and inspired generations of fans. Through his work with the Gridiron Greats Assistance Fund, Mike was a champion for taking care of those who helped build our game. We extend our deepest condolences to Diana and the Ditka family.”

#### **Ditka got his “Iron Mike” nickname during his western Pennsylvania upbringing**

He was born in Carnegie, Pennsylvania, the son of a welder who changed the family name from Dyczko. He grew up in nearby Aliquippa — which also later produced fellow Pro Football Hall of Famers Ty Law and Darrelle Revis — close to the coal-mining and steel-manufacturing plants that dotted the western part of the state, a big, talented, three-sport athlete and All-American at Pitt whose bruising style made his first nickname, "Iron Mike," a good fit.

“When our players see Mike Ditka’s name, I want them to understand how he competed," current Pitt football coach Pat Narduzzi said in a statement. “He gave everything he had and expected the same from the guys beside him. That’s Pitt. He showed us that tough people find a way through tough times and taught us to fight for the names on the front and back of our jerseys.”

Selected fifth overall by flinty Chicago owner George Halas in the 1961 draft, Ditka went on to Rookie of the Year honors, multiple Pro Bowl trips and the 1963 NFL Championship. He and Baltimore's John Mackey changed the tight end position and offensive schemes forever. He was a battering ram of a blocker, but Ditka was just as likely to catch a short pass and pinball through an entire secondary or outrace a lone safety on a deep touchdown throw.

He left Chicago in 1966, playing briefly for Philadelphia and Dallas.

# China Coast Guard harasses Ayungin medical evacuation

[![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/2328_1768617959.jpg)![Image 21: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/2328_1768617959.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/franco-jose-c-barona "author image")

CHINESE coast guard vessels used water cannon and dangerous maneuvers to delay the medical evacuation of a Philippine Navy sailor from Ayungin Shoal by nearly 10 hours on Thursday, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said on Friday.

The sailor, who was stationed aboard the derelict BRP Sierra Madre that had been beached at the shoal, was eventually transferred to a PCG vessel and was reported in stable condition after receiving initial medical treatment. He was being transported to the port of Buliluyan in Palawan for further treatment.

The PCG said the BRP Cabra had sailed from Lawak Island, about 9 nautical miles north of Ayungin Shoal to fetch the sailor.

At around 7:30 a.m. on Thursday, the China Coast Guard (CCG) vessel 5306 approached the Cabra.

The PCG said CCG 5306 came to about 400 yards of the Cabra while firing its water cannon. The Cabra was not hit, but it moved farther from the shoal to protect its crew and maintain coordination with the personnel stationed at the Sierra Madre.

The PCG initially planned to pick up the stricken navy man at a rendezvous point about 2.5 nautical miles northeast of the Sierra Madre.

Chinese coast guard vessels, however, prevented the Cabra from reaching the rendezvous point, forcing it to remain about 13 nautical miles north of the shoal for several hours.

The CCG 5306 again challenged Cabra by radio, prompting the Philippine vessel to transfer to a location farther from the Sierra Madre.

*   ![Image 26: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The Cabra launched a rigid-hull inflatable boat (RHIB) carrying a member of its Maritime Security Team and medical personnel.

The Chinese coast guard deployed its own RHIB to harass the Philippine boat.

The Sierra Madre detachment launched two rubber boats, one of which was carrying the patient.

Advertisement

The patient and his companion were successfully transferred to the PCG RHIB. During the RHIB’s return trip to the Sierra Madre, another CCG vessel maneuvered about 500 yards off the Philippine boat’s starboard, while CCG 5306 positioned itself about 600 yards off its port quarter, the PCG said.

[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

A PCG medical officer checked the sailor’s vital signs and administered intravenous fluids.

The PCG said it monitored three CCG vessels as well as the Chinese maritime militia vessel Qiongsanshayu 00119 and the People’s Liberation Army Navy warship 628 during the operation.

PCG commandant Adm. Ronnie Gil Gavan called on the Chinese coast guard to respect the humanitarian nature of medical evacuation missions.

Advertisement

“When a life is at stake, there should be no water cannon, no obstruction and no delay,” Gavan said.

Ayungin Shoal, also known internationally as Second Thomas Shoal, is within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ) in the South China Sea.

The 2016 arbitral award upheld the Philippines’ maritime rights in its EEZ, although it did not determine sovereignty over the shoal.

The Tropang 5G is not in the safest position. They carry an even 4-4 win-loss slate and will need as many wins as possible in the next few weeks.

Only the top four teams per group will advance to the quarterfinal round after the double-round elimination group stage format.

In the quarterfinal round, it will be a crossover playoffs where the top teams from each group will face the No.4 seeds of the opposite group. The second-seeded squads of the two groups will meet their counterparts in the opposite group.

Every game is crucial now and the Tropang 5G will be pinning their hopes for now on Hornsby, the well-travelled reinforcement, who last saw action in the Canadian Elite Basketball League while playing for Edmonton Stingers.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Once RHJ returns to action, he will restore his role as the gold standard among imports playing in the PBA.

With Justin Brownlee still doubtful to play after Barangay Ginebra coach Tim Cone disclosed during the Senate hearing that he has a heart condition and high blood pressure that forced him to miss the recent Asian Games campaign and the previous window event of Gilas Pilipinas in the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers, much will be expected on Hollis-Jefferson as his stiffest competition is likely to miss the tournament.

But whether Hollis-Jefferson will still play with the same overall impact like he did three times when he led TNT to the promised land or will he become a few steps slower remains to be seen, but knowing that the Tropang 5G will have their old reliable back in harness is very encouraging.

The Philippines has been home for Hollis-Jefferson the past four years. He was regarded as the only import who was able to beat Brownlee in a finals confrontation. Three times when they met in the championship showdown, the TNT reinforcement was able to get the better end of his match up with the beloved Barangay Ginebra import.

*   ![Image 3: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

Except when he lost to Brownlee in the Asian Games in China three years ago when Gilas Pilipinas defeated Jordan in the gold medal game, Hollis-Jefferson had been lording it over against his old nemesis and his import counterparts in the PBA.

TNT is not panicking. It has Hollis-Jefferson at its disposal and it will only be a matter of time before the Tropang 5G will rediscover their old, deadly championship form.

They believe they can never go wrong with RHJ, who has some unfinished business to fulfill.

title: PVL celebrates 10th year with triple-header in Cebu
summary: PREMIER Volleyball League (PVL) celebrates a decade of high standard volleyball action with a one of a kind triple-header to open the All-Filipino Conference at the newly opened SM Seaside Cebu Arena on Saturday. For the first time, the men
content:
PREMIER Volleyball League (PVL) celebrates a decade of high standard volleyball action with a one of a kind triple-header to open the All-Filipino Conference at the newly opened SM Seaside Cebu Arena on Saturday.

For the first time, the men’s counterpart — Spikers’ Turf — joins the PVL schedule on the same play date with a game sandwiched by two women’s matches.

It is also the first time the PVL opens a season at the SM Seaside Cebu Arena and the first major professional volleyball event staged at the venue.

*   [St. Benilde extends win streak to four](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/sports/st-benilde-extends-win-streak-to-four/2442657)

The triple-header action features Capital 1 Solar Spikers and Choco Mucho Flying Titans at 1 p.m. followed by Spikers’ Turf teams Alpha Insurance Protectors and Savogue Aesthetics at 3:30 p.m. and the much-awaited match between Creamline and Akari at 6 p.m.

The All-Filipino Conference features a new format, built on three series.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The first round, referred to as Siklab, is slated from Oct. 10 to Dec. 4 and is a single round-robin with a mandatory “all-to-play” rule requiring every declared and available player in the team to see action.

The top four teams will advance to the semifinals where the two best teams in the elims having the twice-to-beat advantage.

The championship showdown is a best of three affair.

*   ![Image 1: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

The second round is slated from January to March with the same format but without the all-play requirement, allowing coaches to have full flexibility.

And for the final round, points from the first two series determine seedings for a stepladder-style finale where the first-ever Philippine grand champion will be crowned.

To kickoff the opening day, Capital 1 will be bannered by prize acquisition and national team standout Bella Belen, together with former Cignal Super Spikers stars Vanie Gandler and Erika Santos.

The lethal trio aims to upscale the young franchise, which was founded in 2024.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

However, the Solar Spikers need to brace for the heavy favorites Choco Mucho, bannered by Sisi Rondina and setter Deanna Wong, who both have Cebu roots.

Rondina, who was out from the previous season as she was serving her national team duties, returns to the court with Choco Mucho star Eya Laure.

After their match, the men’s team Alpha Insurance Protectors and Savogue Aesthetics begin their campaigns.

For the final game, Creamline begins its quest for a record-stretching 12th championship after a fourth-place finish in the 2026 Invitational Conference.

*   ![Image 3: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

The Cool Smashers will be bannered by stars Alyssa Valdez, Jia de Guzman, Bernadeth Pons, Michele Gumabao, and Jema Galanza.

Creamline, which historically dominated Akari, needs to brace for the fortified team powered by captain Justine Jazareno and setter Mars Alba.

The Chargers achieved rare victories over Creamline in the Reinforced and All-Filipino Conferences, and aim to pull another upset.

title: The ecological debt: What humanity owes the future
summary: **_Last of seven parts_** THE philosophy of time, if there were such a thing (St. Augustine of Hippo said time exists only in the mind), may be the grand avenue for understanding ecological debt. Ordinary debt connects past, present and fut
content:
**_Last of seven parts_**

THE philosophy of time, if there were such a thing (St. Augustine of Hippo said time exists only in the mind), may be the grand avenue for understanding ecological debt. Ordinary debt connects past, present and future. Somebody borrowed yesterday.

Someone repays tomorrow. Ecological debt creates a strange moral relationship among the dead, the living and the unborn.

*   [US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

Our ancestors made choices whose consequences remain with us. We are now making choices whose consequences will remain with people who do not yet exist. It means history is not finished merely because the people who made it are dead.

All things are created twice, says my civil engineer boss. Let’s create this scenario a second time. Industrialization continues to exist in the atmosphere. Colonial extraction continues to influence economic structures. Deforestation continues to influence ecosystems. Nuclear waste continues beyond political generations. Climate consequences can persist for centuries.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

And now: We are writing obligations into the future. That makes ecological debt not merely an environmental concept, but a philosophy of inheritance, responsibility and time.

**Intergenerational justice**

The unborn can neither vote, nor lobby, nor demonstrate, nor sue, nor participate in markets, nor attend international conferences, nor negotiate treaties. Yet they will inherit the consequences of today’s decisions.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

This creates a profound democratic paradox. Some of the people most affected by our decisions do not yet exist. The political system is overwhelmingly designed around people who are alive now.

The ecological crisis forces us to ask what Laudato Si’ blows in the wind: How can a democracy represent the interests of people who cannot yet represent themselves? CST then makes everything political.

**What development should mean**

Populorum Progressio challenges the conventional equation where development means more. Instead, it proposes that development should mean greater human flourishing within ecological limits. The crucial word is not growth. It is flourishing. This allows economics, ecology and human dignity to meet.

*   ![Image 2: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Sollicitudo Rei Socialis gives us the concept of structures of sin. We ask: What happens when structures created by previous generations systematically transfer ecological costs to future generations?

The structures of ecological debt can suggest that individuals may be decent. Yet their systems can still produce excessive extraction, waste, emissions, inequality, resource depletion, etc.

This shifts the question from “Who is personally guilty?” to “What structures make ecological irresponsibility normal?”

Ecological debt also introduces justice between regions. Those who benefited most from industrialization are not necessarily those who suffer the greatest consequences. This creates a profound moral asymmetry: Those who accumulated the benefits of ecological exploitation and those who bear its costs are not always the same people, complicating the idea of responsibility.

*   ![Image 3: The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253556.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

Let Bob Dylan ask the questions: Who benefited? Who paid? Who continues to pay? Who inherited the benefits? Who inherited the damage? Who has the capacity to repair it?

We may know the answers. And the choice of whether to act or not is also ours.

Taken together, the papal encyclicals introduce a compelling moral category. They provide a coherent justification for limiting the choice to the one that serves humanity.

Every person has dignity (Pacem in Terris). Every person deserves authentic development (Populorum Progressio). Human beings are interconnected (Sollicitudo Rei Socialis). Economic and technological power requires moral responsibility (Caritas in Veritate). Humanity is embedded within an ecological community (Laudato Si’). And humanity must rediscover fraternity (Fratelli Tutti).

Surely, the answer to the question, “What kind of humanity deserves to inherit the power it has acquired?” should give occasion for uniting ecology, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, economics, politics, religion, philosophy and intergenerational justice.

It is no longer as simple a question as “How do we solve climate change?” We need to confront ourselves with “What kind of civilization are we becoming?”

A tentative proposition is that moral transformation is required for human power to become planetary, aware of ecological debt and intergenerational justice. The transformation can lead the path for the debt to be viewed not only as an economic spreadsheet but as something that civilization morally owes.

Lest the nagging slows down, these questions need to be raised again.

Who owes whom? Can the dead owe the living? Can the living owe people who haven’t been born? Can a nation inherit a debt it didn’t personally incur? Can a species owe something to other species? Can humanity owe something to the Earth?

What happens when a civilization becomes extraordinarily good at calculating what things are worth, but extraordinarily bad at calculating what things are owed? What does one generation owe another when it plants something whose greatest gifts will be enjoyed by people it will never meet?

My parents planted something whose greatest gifts came later. Theirs is a love that keeps on giving.

Theirs was a symbol of an alternative model of civilization. They didn’t simply consume the land. They left something alive. And that is the opposite of ecological debt.

Those who enjoy the shade of a mango tree, those who freely pick the fruits of santol trees without knowing who planted the tree, may or may not realize that nature and human work are the love that keeps on giving. But when they do come to that realization, paying that love back to the next generation becomes easier. There can be less carbon in the sky, doves can freely sail, mountains are kept from being washed into the sea, etc. It will only take one person to go through a genuine moral transformation for the rest of the world to follow.

Yet civilization has miles to go before humanity sleeps.

The debt is real. The inheritance is damaged. But the account is not yet closed.

There are still tables to build. There are still trees to plant. There are still promises to keep.

Fr. John Carroll, SJ, said in one of his works that reform takes time. And precisely because it takes time, there is no time to lose. The work starts now.

_email@aberia.xyz_

title: Donate to Fighting for legal fairness, organized by David Xia
summary: **Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)** Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China. Mr. Xia has
content:
**Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)**

Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.

Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.

Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.

Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.

Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.

Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.

Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.

We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!

Yeliang Xia and his team of volunteers

Sept 15, 2018

征集律师费援助捐款公告

原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。

夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。

郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。

夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。

夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。

请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

感谢各位的关注、鼓励、支持和帮助！

夏业良与募捐团队

2018年9月15日

content: 先知书店  先知书店店长荐书  2026年10月5日 杨小凯，一位超越时代的思想家，很多人可能还没听说过他，但他的思想却是打开中国现代化之门的钥匙。 他被两度提名诺贝尔经济学奖，是离诺贝尔经济学奖最近的华人。事实上，他的贡献已不能是否获得诺奖来衡量。  杨小凯是一个传奇。他生于内战时期，长于癫狂的岁月，在监狱里“念完大学”。然而，就连世界级的学者布坎南、克鲁格曼等人，也不敢轻视他的思想。 他一直走在思想界最前沿，堪称1840年以来中国知识界与思想界第一人。他关于“经济与社会”的三种新范式，不仅适用于中国，在全世界也具有普遍意义。 >>> 01 重塑经济学的新范式：以数理逻辑捍卫古典经济学 诺贝尔经济学奖得主布坎南曾说：“全世界最重要的经济研究，就是以杨小凯为主的对分工的分析。” 现代主流经济学家，擅长适用集合论、拓扑学、线性代数等数学工具进行经济学理论分析，但却越来越缺少古典经济学的灵魂，有的甚至完全成为政治的附庸。然而，不论他们得出的结论是对是错，都很难从其推理过程中找到短板。 率先打破这种现状的，正是杨小凯。他将数学分析工具进一步升级，以更加严谨、更加全面、更加贴近现实世界的数理逻辑，指出主流经济学分析的漏洞，并将亚当·斯密的古典经济学分工理论复活。 简而言之，杨小凯是直接可以和亚当·斯密对话的现代经济学者，他回归斯密，又超越了斯密；他让经济学回归源头，不再有宏观与微观之分。 我们可以大胆预测，如果他再多活几年，一定可以获得诺奖，并能进一步升级他的理论。可惜天妒英才，世间再无杨小凯。 >>> 02 后发国家转型的新范式：制度转型优于经济变革 杨小凯说：“中国人对共和了解太少，对民主讲得太多，对自由讲得太少......民主简单地说就是少数服从多数，而共和或自由则是要保护和尊重少数。” 大约从1990年代开始，杨小凯通过对世界政治经济史的系统研究，总结出两种后发国家的“转型范式”： 第一种：大规模引进先进技术，实现经济快速增长，即先发展经济，后社会转型。 第二种：通过制度改革，建立自由市场制度，实现经济、社会同步转型。 杨小凯认为：后发国家如果只沉溺于“经济奇迹”，无视制度转型，结果一定会形成路径依赖，最终反噬经济成果。明治维新后的日本、二战前的德国、洋务运动时期的清朝，都证明第一种范式行不通。 杨小凯将其概括为“后发劣势”，并进一步指出：落后国家模仿技术比较容易，模仿制度比较困难，因为改革制度会触犯一些既得利益。但是，模仿技术虽然可在短期内取得快速发展，却会给长期发展留下许多隐患，甚至长期发展可能失败。 >>> 03 超越“唯制度论”的新范式：信仰是制度的第一因 2001年9月，杨小凯被确诊为肺癌晚期，在生命的最后几年，他完成了一场“自我革命”，皈依基督，每日祷告，直到去世。 杨小凯说：“脱离文化与信仰的土壤，认为仅仅依靠制度转型就能包治百病，是肤浅的。信仰才是制度的第一因。” 历史不仅证明了“只模仿技术，不改革制度”行不通；历史还证明了“只模仿制度，不重铸观念地基”的“唯制度论”也行不通。 人的行为，受观念的支配；任何制度，不过是对特定观念的表达。因此，唯有基于观念共识的制度变革，才可能激活制度的力量；缺乏观念地基的制度，终究是无源之水。 信仰决定个人行为→个人行为形成社会秩序→社会秩序要求相应的制度安排。因此，信仰处于这个链条的最前端，是制度变革的根本源头。杨小凯的这一洞察，超越了自新文化运动以来，绝大多数中国知识分子对社会转型的认知。 从经济到制度再到信仰，杨小凯用仅仅56年的人生，抱着向死而生的态度，创造了一个又一个的奇迹。无论这位先知的传奇人生，还是他的主要思想遗产，仅凭碎片化的提炼是远远不够的，需要系统的梳理。 更重要的是，如今，他对中国与世界很多先知般的“预言”，正在一一应验： 后发国家转型的瓶颈、经济发展的陷阱、文明演进基础崩塌、世界秩序愈发撕裂，各种事关家国命运、文明走向的“大问题”层出不穷，越来越难以解决。 破解这些难题，更绕不开杨小凯——不仅仅是他诺奖级别的经济学贡献，还有关于后发劣势、关于信仰是制度第一因的洞察，以及他向死而生的精神力量。 遗憾的是，最能呈现杨小凯思想全貌的著作，因种种原因已无处可觅。 为此，先知书店在对杨小凯思想近十年学习和积累的基础上，经过半年时间策划，推出迄今市场上较为全面、系统、深入讲解杨小凯的传奇人生及主要思想的线上视频讲座——《被时代追赶的先知——杨小凯及其思想六讲》，让更多人以全新形式重新认识并读懂杨小凯。 该课程由六个模块组成，从最传奇的中国知识分子、最接近诺奖的华人经济学家、向死而生的生命高度、保守主义的思想家等六个角度还原真实的杨小凯，系统打捞杨小凯最重要的思想遗产以及精神力量。 为了保证讲座品质，我们邀请到或最熟悉杨小凯、或长期研究杨小凯的导师团授课，包括政治学者任剑涛，杨小凯学生梁捷（经济学博士）、王珞（博弈论教授），财经学者李炜光，经济学者刘业进、王小鲁。 为辅助学员更精细化的理解相关内容，在讲座前中后期，还安排了课程助理领学，以及研究杨小凯多年的资深编辑全程伴读，负责日常答疑。 所有关注杨小凯的朋友，关心现代化转型与个人命运、追求道德信仰与自由秩序的深度思考者，都能有所收获。扫描下方二维码，即可报名。

title: How will new longer-range aircraft boost Manila’s South China Sea surveillance?
summary: The [Philippine](https://www.scmp.com/topics/philippines?module=inline&pgtype=article) Coast Guard will receive three longer-range aircraft from the US, two of them modified for improved surveillance, giving Manila greater reach and enduran
content:
The [Philippine](https://www.scmp.com/topics/philippines?module=inline&pgtype=article) Coast Guard will receive three longer-range aircraft from the US, two of them modified for improved surveillance, giving Manila greater reach and endurance to monitor [Chinese coastguard](https://www.scmp.com/topics/chinas-coastguard?module=inline&pgtype=article), naval and research vessels across the [South China Sea](https://www.scmp.com/topics/south-china-sea?module=inline&pgtype=article).

Under a US$39.6 million contract awarded by the United States Navy on September 28, the three second-hand, extended-range King Air 350-series aircraft will be fitted with extended-range fuel systems, upgraded Garmin avionics and high-frequency radios.

Two will also carry King Air Maritime Domain Awareness intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance systems. The work is expected to be completed by September 2028.

03:31

China and the Philippines trade accusations after clash in South China Sea

Observers said the twin-turboprop aircraft could allow the coastguard to reach distant patrol areas – such as Scarborough Shoal, the Spratly Islands and waters around Batanes in the northern Philippines – more quickly, and remain over them for longer.

The agency is already deploying aircraft to such areas to monitor and challenge Chinese activity. On September 27, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) sent the Cessna 208 Grand Caravan PCG-2081 to locate and challenge China Coast Guard vessel CCG-3303 near Cabra Island, Occidental Mindoro province, visually confirming the ship and issuing repeated radio challenges.

Raymond Powell, executive director of the SeaLight Foundation, noted that while the PCG’s existing single-engine surveillance aircraft could locate Chinese vessels, it had “little endurance or sensor capability to stay and observe” them.

He said the two King Airs fitted with mission suites would allow crews to “loiter, evaluate, document completely and return home with time-stamped evidence” – even if Chinese military aircraft forced them away from the immediate area.

The King Air aircraft could extend the PCG’s surveillance reach into the Luzon Strait and around Batanes, where it had historically been able to devote “almost no persistent surveillance” to the movement of PLA Navy and Chinese research vessels, according to Powell.

The three King Airs would make it easier to have aircraft available, even during training and maintenance operations, said Michael Bosack, director of the Parley Policy Institute.

This additional capability would allow the PCG to respond “more consistently, swiftly and effectively to vessels that are further afield”, he said.

Peter Layton, a visiting fellow at the Griffith Asia Institute and a former Royal Australian Air Force officer, said the King Air’s two engines would provide an added safety margin on long overwater flights. He also expected the aircraft to have “a much better nighttime capability”, which could extend coastguard surveillance into the night.

Washington’s move to support its Southeast Asian ally comes as Philippine surveillance flights continue to encounter Chinese military aircraft around contested waters.

On October 3, a Philippine Air Force C-208 Caravan patrolling near Scarborough Shoal encountered two Chinese military aircraft. Manila said one, a J-16 fighter, repeatedly manoeuvred dangerously close to the smaller plane.

Beijing said the C-208 had “illegally intruded” into what it called the territorial airspace over Huangyan Island, its name for Scarborough Shoal. The People’s Liberation Army’s Southern Theatre Command said Chinese forces tracked and monitored the aircraft and issued warnings to expel it, accusing Manila of “provocative acts”.

Bosack said Beijing could similarly seek to curtail King Air operations through “radar lock incidents, unsafe manoeuvres around the aircraft or deployment of flares” once they entered service.

Timothy Heath, director of China and security research firm Perceptum, said the King Airs were unlikely to significantly change Beijing’s response given that China could continue sending military aircraft to challenge Philippine flights around disputed areas.

He said the King Airs had “longer duration and potentially more surveillance capabilities” but added that their addition “doesn’t fundamentally change the situation”.

Detecting Chinese activity does not necessarily give the Philippines the surface assets needed to respond, and while the King Airs could help Manila decide which incidents warrant deploying its limited surface assets, they cannot stop Chinese grey-zone activity.

The PCG “simply cannot dispatch ships to address every Chinese boat in its maritime areas of responsibility”, Bosack said.

However, Heath noted that improved surveillance could provide “earlier warning” of Chinese operations and help Manila determine which coastguard or military assets to send, reducing the chances of Philippine forces being surprised or outmatched.

Powell said evidence gathered during longer surveillance flights could help Manila “strip away deniability” by providing a more complete record of Chinese activity, strengthening its ability to challenge Beijing’s account of disputed encounters.

01:50

Chinese fighter jet flies close to Philippine plane over disputed shoal in South China Sea, Manila says

The King Air programme is the latest example of foreign partners helping Manila fill gaps in its maritime monitoring and enforcement.

Australia has provided the Philippine Coast Guard with drones and training. Japan, which has already financed 12 PCG vessels, is funding a further five and France is supporting Manila’s purchase of 40 OCEA patrol boats through export-credit insurance and direct market-rate loans.

Heath noted that wider foreign involvement could ultimately matter more than the aircraft themselves because “the more the other countries aid the Philippines, the more likely that they will take an interest” in what happens in contested waters.

This mattered because information gathered by Philippine surveillance aircraft could also provide US forces with “useful data” on PLA activity during a Taiwan crisis, he said.

title: Industry Advisory: U.S. and China Target $30B in Reciprocal Tariff Relief via Board of Trade Framework
summary: The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) and Chinese trade officials have released preliminary frameworks under a newly established bilateral Board of Trade (referred to in Beijing as the Trade Council) to grant tariff relief acro
content:
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) and Chinese trade officials have released preliminary frameworks under a newly established bilateral Board of Trade (referred to in Beijing as the Trade Council) to grant tariff relief across an estimated $30 billion in annual trade on each side. According to official statements from Beijing, more than 90% of the covered product categories are designated to see previously imposed punitive tariffs eliminated, reverting duties back to standard Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) rates.

For logistics managers, customs brokers, and supply chain directors, the plan offers targeted relief for major consumer hardlines while leaving high-volume soft goods and complex tariff classifications untouched.

### Key Tariff Reductions: High-Volume Winners

The USTR designated 77 Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) codes for tariff adjustments. While the list spans dozens of subheadings, the vast majority of the $30 billion in import value is concentrated in a handful of high-volume consumer goods categories:

*   **Toys & Children’s Products:** Representing the single largest line item, toy imports accounted for $9.8 billion in 2025. Unlike other segments, toys were preserved under broader subheadings without narrow eight-digit restrictions. Child safety seats, high chairs, and booster chairs account for an additional $2 billion in relief.

*   **Small Domestic Appliances:** Major kitchen categories represent several billion dollars in volume, including countertop microwaves ($1.2B), blenders and food processors ($704M), electric kettles and coffee makers ($378M), toasters ($102M), and other small appliances ($1.7B). Commercial and residential floor polishers add another $1.1 billion.

*   **Plastics & Drinkware:** Insulated vacuum flasks (such as popular stainless-steel tumblers) accounted for $1.3 billion. Plastic dinnerware, utensils, and bowls ($3B) alongside plastic beads ($3.8B) are also slated for duty reductions.

In exchange, China agreed to lower barriers on an equivalent $30 billion portfolio of U.S. exports. Key sectors receiving reciprocal market access include bulk agriculture (beef, poultry, seafood, corn, wheat, sorghum, and cotton) and high-value medical technology (MRI equipment, X-ray machinery, ultrasound systems, ventilators, pacemakers, and orthopedic devices).

### Technical Pitfalls: Narrow HTS Specifics and Scope Limits

Importers must scrutinize product descriptions and material breakdowns before adjusting landed-cost models. The list was strictly capped to meet the $30 billion ceiling, leading to granular HTS carve-outs:

*   **Textile Restrictions:** Eligible bed linens and curtains must explicitly exclude majority cotton or synthetic blends, with curtains requiring specific knit constructions.

*   **Selective Sporting Goods:** Tennis balls and nets are slated for relief, yet tennis rackets are excluded; conversely, racquetball and squash rackets qualify.

*   **Seasonal Decor:** Wooden and glass holiday ornaments, nativity sets, and select lighting are covered, while plastic ornaments are entirely excluded.

*   **Minority-Sourced Commodities:** Several categories on the relief roster—including playing cards, electric shavers, and fishhooks—represent lines where China holds a minority share of total U.S. import volume.

### Critical Exclusions: Apparel and Footwear Left Out

Despite aggressive lobbying from the American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA)—which submitted requests covering over 600 product codes—no apparel, footwear, or travel goods were included in the relief package. The AAFA noted that roughly 97% of domestic apparel is imported, warning that ongoing Section 301 duties will continue to put direct pressure on retail margins and consumer prices.

### Implementation Timelines and Peak Season Impact

From an operational standpoint, the announcement carries key timing constraints:

1.   **Peak Season Has Passed:** The National Retail Federation (NRF) highlighted that the bulk of holiday 2026 merchandise, including toys and holiday decor, has already entered domestic distribution channels. With peak ocean shipping winding down, duty relief will have minimal impact on goods already cleared through customs.

2.   **Administrative Runway:** USTR has not yet published an effective implementation date, standard operational procedures, or a public comment calendar. Both Washington and Beijing must finalize domestic regulatory reviews before customs agencies update tariff schedules and entry processing systems.

Importers and shippers should consult their trade compliance teams and licensed customs brokers to verify HTS classifications against the formal 77-code annex and monitor official Federal Register notices before altering entry filing procedures.

title: Lost in tabulation: Diverging US-China trade data point to tariff evasion
summary: The United States and China share one of the world's largest and most closely monitored bilateral trading relationships. Yet the official statistics used to assess that relationship are sending sharply different signals. China reports expor
content:
The United States and China share one of the world's largest and most closely monitored bilateral trading relationships. Yet the official statistics used to assess that relationship are sending sharply different signals. China reports exporting more goods to America than the United States says it imports—particularly since early 2025, when the Trump administration sharply increased tariffs on China. Among possible reasons for the gap, the evasion of US tariffs appears to be an important contributor. As a consequence, US bilateral import data for China appear to have become less reliable. The reported decline in US imports from China should not be treated as a clean measure of either economic decoupling or the effectiveness of US tariffs.

From January through July 2026, the US Census Bureau recorded $158.3 billion in merchandise imports from China (including Hong Kong). Over the same period, China reported $258.1 billion in merchandise exports to the United States. The $99.8 billion difference was equivalent to 63 percent of reported US imports from China. This share was nearly five times its 2021–24 average. If the average monthly gap observed from January through July persists for the rest of the year, the cumulative gap for 2026 will exceed $170 billion.

Figure 1 shows how China's reported goods exports to the United States compare with America's reported goods imports from China since early 2024: Both declined sharply starting in February 2025 following US tariff increases.[[1]](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftn1) Their subsequent trajectories diverged. By July 2026, China reported monthly exports to the United States about 4 percent below their 2024 average. By contrast, US-reported imports from China were 26 percent below their 2024 average, indicating a more persistent contraction in bilateral trade.

## Why have US-China trade statistics diverged?

US-China bilateral trade statistics have never fully aligned. Before 2020, the gap was negative: The United States generally reported more imports than China reported as exports to the United States. The pattern reversed in 2020. The gap became positive and averaged roughly 13 percent of US imports during 2021–24. Federal Reserve researchers [estimated](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/did-the-us-bilateral-goods-deficit-with-china-increase-or-decrease-during-the-us-china-trade-conflict-20210621.html) that tariff evasion accounted for about $55 billion of the $88 billion shift in the reporting gap between 2018 and 2020. The tariffs [imposed](https://www.piie.com/research/piie-charts/2019/us-china-trade-war-tariffs-date-chart) in 2025 were substantially higher and covered more goods than the 2018–20 measures.

Tariff evasion can take several forms. Firms may misstate a shipment's country of origin to take advantage of lower bilateral tariff rates or reclassify goods when rates differ across product categories. They may also understate the reported value or quantity of imports. Because import and export declarations are filed separately, underinvoicing can create a gap between reported exports and imports. A recent _New York Times_[analysis](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/07/us/politics/tariffs-trade-import-fraud.html) found that the average value of merchandise per shipping container from China fell by around 40 percent between January 2025 and February 2026. In some cases, Chinese exporters may be responsible for the US customs entries. For example, a Nikkei Asia [investigation](https://asia.nikkei.com/spotlight/policy-asia/china-s-formidable-logistics-sector-challenges-trump-tariff-enforcers) describes allegations that logistics providers used shell companies as importers of record and manipulated invoices to reduce the duties owed. Nikkei separately [reports](https://asia.nikkei.com/economy/trade-war/trump-tariffs/us-scrutiny-deters-some-chinese-tariff-refund-claims-as-others-cash-in) that some Chinese companies have been reluctant to claim US tariff refunds because renewed scrutiny could expose irregularities in the underlying entries.

The effects of tariff evasion are not confined to US-China trade data. False declarations of origin create two gaps in bilateral trade data: a positive gap for the true country of origin, as observed with China, and an offsetting negative gap for the false country of origin. Relabeling of Chinese exports through Vietnam appears substantial. As New York Federal Reserve researchers [note](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/05/in-what-ways-has-u-s-trade-with-china-changed/), its reporting gap runs in the opposite direction from China's (figure 2). From January through July 2026, the United States recorded $149.6 billion in imports from Vietnam, while Vietnam's customs agency reported $105.0 billion in exports to the United States. The resulting $44.6 billion discrepancy is consistent with some Chinese goods being relabeled as Vietnamese, although aggregate data cannot establish exactly how much relabeling occurred.[[2]](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftn2)

## Do other factors explain the current US-China gap?

Other developments have contributed to the gap, but they appear much less significant than tariff evasion. First, the emergence of a positive gap in 2020 coincided with rapid growth in low-value shipments entering under the US _de minimis_ exemption, which [allowed](https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/national-media-release/de-minimis-value-increases-800) eligible imports valued at $800 or less to enter duty free with reduced documentation. China and Hong Kong accounted for roughly two-thirds of US _de minimis_ shipments around this time, [according](https://gava.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/FY2018-2021_De-Minimis-Statistics-update.pdf) to US Customs and Border Protection (CBP). The Congressional Research Service [estimates](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/IF12891.html) that Chinese low-value e-commerce exports to the United States rose from $1.4 billion in 2018 to $22.9 billion in 2024. Since these exports were [more likely](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2025/02/u-s-imports-from-china-have-fallen-by-less-than-u-s-data-indicate/) to appear in Chinese than US reporting, they contributed to the gap.[[3]](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftn3)

However, the United States [ended](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202500424/pdf/DCPD-202500424.pdf) duty-free _de minimis_ treatment for shipments from China in May 2025 and [suspended](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/eo-14324.pdf) it globally that August. China's Ministry of Commerce also issued [guidance](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zwgk/zcfb/art/2024/art_6261fd8d73e745368da54e2b37022514.html) in June 2024 encouraging e-commerce retailers to use overseas warehouses for fulfillment, shifting goods from individual parcels into bulk shipments subject to ordinary customs reporting. The value of global imports entering the United States under the _de minimis_ exemption [fell 26 percent](https://www.cbp.gov/trade/basic-import-export/e-commerce) in fiscal year 2025. This should have narrowed the reporting gap.

Chinese customs data through 2026 reinforce this conclusion. Although the categories shown in figure 3 cover a narrower range of goods than the CBP estimates, their trend remains informative. Chinese exports to the United States in these categories peaked in 2024 and declined thereafter. The US series for low-value imports from China requires a different interpretation. It shows a clear structural break in May 2025, when the _de minimis_ exemption ended and additional entry and reporting requirements took effect. Its subsequent rise likely reflects improved coverage rather than growth in low-value trade. Convergence with the Chinese series should have further narrowed the portion of the overall gap attributable to low-value shipments.

A second possible cause of the US-China reporting gap stems from Chinese exporters artificially inflating export values to claim tax rebates from the Chinese government. The Fed [analysis](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/did-the-us-bilateral-goods-deficit-with-china-increase-or-decrease-during-the-us-china-trade-conflict-20210621.html) cited earlier estimated that changes in Chinese tax incentives accounted for about $12 billion of the $88 billion shift in the reporting gap between 2018 and 2020. There are two reasons to think this was not a major contributor to the gap's recent growth. First, China [eliminated or reduced](https://www.china-briefing.com/news/navigating-chinas-latest-export-tax-rebate-adjustments-implications/) export rebates for selected products beginning in December 2024 and [announced](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/global/china-cut-export-tax-rebates-ease-global-trade-tensions) further cuts in January 2026. This contrasts with the 2018 episode, when it increased rebates to offset US tariffs. Second, Chinese authorities have [intensified](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202604/17/WS69e216b7a310d6866eb44173.html) tax enforcement since 2024, inspecting more than 130,000 firms suspected of fraudulent invoicing.

## Conclusion

The exact causes of the reporting gap remain uncertain. Still, tariff evasion appears the most likely explanation for its recent growth. To better counter tariff evasion and tax fraud, more systematic sharing and matching of transaction-level customs data could benefit both the United States and China. A [framework](https://www.state.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/13029-China-Law-Enforcement-Customs-4.9.1999-1.pdf) for such cooperation already exists, but implementation appears limited. More broadly, the episode illustrates the limits of using discriminatory tariffs to address bilateral trade imbalances. As argued in a recent PIIE [Policy Brief](https://www.piie.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/pb26-12.pdf) by Mary E. Lovely and Christine Y. Wan, such tariffs can redirect trade through third countries without substantially reducing US reliance on Chinese content or China's role in global production. Addressing trade imbalances instead requires [domestic adjustment](https://www.imf.org/en/blogs/articles/2026/07/30/rising-global-imbalances-underscore-need-to-confront-domestic-distortions) on both sides: The United States needs to rein in its large fiscal deficits, which contribute to its trade deficit, while China needs to stimulate domestic consumption and reduce industrial overcapacity.

## Notes

It remained elevated at 24 percent in 2026, through July, compared with a 6 percent average effective rate for imports from other countries.

title: Bears manager moving starter Logue to bullpen for KBO postseason
summary: By Yoo Jee-ho SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Doosan Bears manager Kim Won-hyong announced Monday his American starting pitcher Zach Logue will pitch out of the bullpen during the upcoming South Korean baseball postseason. With one final regular
content:
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Doosan Bears manager Kim Won-hyong announced Monday his American starting pitcher Zach Logue will pitch out of the bullpen during the upcoming South Korean baseball postseason.

With one final regular-season game left Monday evening, the Bears have long clinched the fifth seed in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) and a spot in the wild card round. It will start Wednesday against the No. 4 seed -- either the Kia Tigers or the LG Twins, who were to play each other Monday with the winner grabbing the third seed and the loser finishing in fourth place.

The lower-seeded team will be at a disadvantage in the wild card phase, as it will have to win two straight games on the road. The higher-seeded team, though, only needs a tie or a win in two tries to advance to the next round.

With that arrangement in mind, Kim said he saw no point in saving starting pitchers for later rounds, when the immediate goal is to get past the wild card stage.

Doosan Bears starter Zach Logue pitches against the Samsung Lions during the clubs' Korea Baseball Organization regular-season game at Daegu Samsung Lions Park in the southeastern city of Daegu on Oct. 5, 2026, in this photo provided by the Bears. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

"We have to win two straight games and we cannot afford to get ahead of ourselves," Kim told reporters before hosting the Lotte Giants at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul. "In postseason games, you can never predict what can happen. Maybe our starter will be roughed up after just a few innings. In that case, we will need someone to eat up multiple innings in the middle. We will need every pitcher available other than our potential Game 2 starter."

Gwak Been, the regular-season leader in ERA and strikeouts, is the no-brainer choice as Game 1 starter in the wild card round. Either Wes Benjamin or Choi Min-seok, both coming off strong regular seasons, will likely take the mound in Game 2 if the Bears force that.

Logue had an up-and-down second season in the KBO this year, going 8-7 with a 4.27 ERA before Monday -- compared to a 10-8 record and a 2.81 ERA last year. Logue also saw his walk rate go up and strikeout rate fall this year compared to 2025.

In a conversation with Yonhap News Agency prior to Kim's media scrum, Logue attributed his lack of consistency to an increased familiarity among KBO hitters against him.

"I feel like I threw a lot of strikes and I wasn't walking guys. I think there is definitely an aspect of luck for that," he said. "Also, I have pitched against a lot of these hitters for several games now so they have seen my stuff. That is not an excuse but it just makes things a little bit more difficult and I need to be a little bit more precise sometimes. There have been probably times where I wasn't as precise as I needed to be and I paid for it."

Doosan Bears manager Kim Won-hyong (L) greets his player Park Chan-ho after Park scored a run against the Samsung Lions during the clubs' Korea Baseball Organization regular-season game at Daegu Samsung Lions Park in the southeastern city of Daegu on Oct. 5, 2026, in this photo provided by the Bears. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

On the flip side, Logue also noted making adjustments against certain hitters to enjoy better success against them than a season ago.

And after the Bears missed the postseason in 2025, Logue said he was looking forward to playing some meaningful baseball in October, regardless of his role.

"It has been a lot more fun for me to be a part of a winning team. So I am really looking forward to going into the postseason and seeing what we can do," he said. "I think our team stacks up really well so I am excited to get there and hopefully make a little run. I think our pitching can pitch well against anybody. We are ready to go wherever and a really good pitching staff I think is what ultimately wins you a championship."

The left-hander has some experience pitching in relief both in the majors and minors in the United States. Kim said Logue volunteered to come out of the bullpen at some point during Monday's game.

"We have to think about the best pitching strategies that can help us win two games in the wild card round," Kim said. "If we are successful that way, then someone will emerge from the pile as a strong option."

Kim insisted he had no preference as to which of the Tigers or the Twins he would rather face in the wild card stage.

"What we do is more important than who our opponent will be," Kim said. "Of course, maybe they will both use a lot of pitchers tonight and their bullpen may be gassed. But you just never know in baseball. You always have to be careful. We are the fifth seed, after all. We are in no position to be picky."

jeeho@yna.co.kr
(END)

title: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame
summary: ALAN Peter Cayetano has a formidable adversary in the impeachment trial of Sara Duterte: Alan Peter Cayetano. The senator who once made accountability sound beautifully simple now makes it sound impossibly complicated. His own words from Re
content:
ALAN Peter Cayetano has a formidable adversary in the impeachment trial of Sara Duterte: Alan Peter Cayetano. The senator who once made accountability sound beautifully simple now makes it sound impossibly complicated. His own words from Renato Corona’s impeachment return as an indictment of the political convenience masquerading as principle in his present conduct.

During Corona’s impeachment, Cayetano asked: “Why do we complicate what is so simple?”

Indeed, senator. Why?

When Corona stood accused, Cayetano understood that public office carried obligations beyond the clever deployment of legal defenses. Today, watching him rationalize restrictions and procedural detours favorable to Duterte, one wonders whether his celebrated conscience came with an expiration date.

Explaining his vote to convict Corona, he acknowledged: “Technicalities should protect the rights of people, and I don’t blame this court for sticking to technicalities because this is supposed to protect the rights of people.”

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

That acknowledgment matters. Cayetano did not reject due process. He recognized its purpose. Rights deserve protection, and an impeachment respondent deserves a fair hearing. But fairness requires a tribunal willing to examine evidence, not senator-judges behaving as though their assignment were to discover increasingly ingenious reasons why evidence should remain unexplored.

Cayetano warned the Corona impeachment court: “Pero somehow in this country, it is being used to protect people who plunder this country.”

Those were his words. They are not finding that Duterte has plundered anything. Her liability must be determined from the evidence. They are, however, a devastating standard against which to measure a senator’s conduct when procedural solicitude repeatedly benefits the powerful official whose accountability he is supposed to judge.

In July, Cayetano questioned whether impeachment could reach acts preceding Duterte’s current term, raising the issue as the prosecution sought bank and tax records. But a limitation on the acts charged does not automatically render earlier records irrelevant to proving a present omission, tracing assets or assessing an explanation. Evidence and impeachable conduct are distinct questions.

A senator-judge should insist that distinction be addressed. A defense advocate benefits when it disappears. Cayetano increasingly invites the latter description because his interventions appear directed toward narrowing the prosecution’s path while expanding the respondent’s protection. That is a criticism of observable conduct, not a claim to know his private intentions.

His verdict on Corona came with this ringing declaration: “If your client cannot explain, I cannot abstain. If you did not disclose, we have to depose. And if you are not fit, you cannot sit.”

Explanation mattered then. Disclosure mattered then. Fitness mattered then. Now the public deserves to ask why the same senator seems more animated by obstacles to examination than by the imperative that an official satisfactorily account for what the evidence reveals.

The contradiction became particularly embarrassing in September. Cayetano sought to defer the conviction threshold issue to the Supreme Court. Pia Cayetano, Imee Marcos, Bong Go, Robinhood Padilla and Camille Villar supported that move. After its rejection, those six did not participate in the threshold vote. The senator whose refrain was that he could not abstain now belongs to a bloc that declined to vote.

The threshold dispute has constitutional substance. Disagreement alone proves neither dishonesty nor partiality. But Cayetano cannot demand that the public forget his earlier moral absolutism while he retreats into procedural positioning. He marketed refusal to abstain as courage. He should explain why withholding participation now deserves a nobler label.

His sister Pia also expressed reservations about the subpoenas for Duterte’s financial records, as did Imee Marcos and Camille Villar. Padilla opposed their issuance. The cumulative impression is disgraceful: Senator-judges supplying a protective chorus around a respondent who already has lawyers paid or appointed to defend her.

Bong Go’s participation in Cayetano’s threshold maneuver strengthens that impression. Each intervention must be judged on its merits, but the Senate loses credibility when its members seem eager to anticipate the defense’s needs instead of testing both sides with equal rigor.

Camille Villar may be less conspicuous than the others. That makes proportional criticism appropriate, not exemption. A quieter contribution to the protective bloc remains a contribution. Judicial responsibility does not diminish with speaking time, family pedigree or the relative intensity of one’s political performance.

Before a similar tribunal in Corona, Cayetano also offered a personal commitment: _“For myself, gagawin ko po ito. Pag ako inimbestigahan ng Ombudsman, papayag po ako na buksan ang aking account. OK po ako sa waiver. Wala dapat ikatakot pag walang itinatago.”_

Cayetano offered openness as the answer to suspicion. Where is that insistence now? Why does the confidence that once celebrated opening accounts now coexist with such anxiety over the reach of financial scrutiny?

A waiver is voluntary; legal rights do not vanish because an official refuses one. Nor does refusal establish guilt. But Cayetano chose to make willingness to disclose a badge of integrity. Political honesty requires him to explain whether he still believes his maxim, or whether it applied only when somebody else’s removal was politically convenient.

The most offensive spectacle is his invocation of impartiality while inviting doubts about his own. In September, he emphasized that an impartial tribunal is essential to accountability. Correct. He should begin by applying that insight to himself. Impartiality demands discipline when loyalty urges intervention, and restraint when a defense argument tempts a judge to become its salesman.

Sara Duterte is entitled to counsel. She is not entitled to senators who effectively supplement counsel while retaining the authority to decide her case. The public is entitled to judges who hear explanations, examine disclosure and assess fitness without treating political friendship as an unwritten exemption.

Cayetano’s old speech supplies the standard. His present conduct supplies the embarrassment. Nobody forced him to proclaim those principles; nobody should let him discard them now. He can still choose consistency: facilitate scrutiny, weigh evidence fairly and stop making accountability sound like an attack that the powerful must be rescued from.

Otherwise, his famous rhymes will survive as evidence of something uglier than inconsistency: a conscience eloquent against Renato Corona, unabashedly partisan for Vice President Sara.

_The author is a professor at the University of the Philippines Los Baños and vice chairman of the board of PTVNI._

title: 《初信牧养系列》第十篇：基督住在我们里面
