content:
**第十篇：基督住在我们里面**

主题：认识基督如何住在信徒里面，经历基督作生命、作人位，并在日常生活中活基督。

**壹、基督徒最大的奥秘，就是基督住在我们里面**

歌罗西书一章二十六至二十七节：「就是历世历代以来所隐藏的奥秘，但如今向祂的圣徒显明了；神愿意叫他们知道，这奥秘的荣耀在外邦人中是何等的丰富，就是基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。」

哥林多后书十三章五节：「你们要试验自己是否在信仰中；你们要验证自己。岂不知你们自己里面有耶稣基督么？除非你们是经不起试验的。」

这两处经文启示一个极其宝贵的真理：基督不仅是为我们死而复活的救主，更是今天住在我们里面的生命。许多初信者知道主耶稣为我们的罪死在十字架上，也知道祂已经复活、升天。但是，他们可能还不清楚，今天这位复活的基督，竟然住在每一个真实相信祂的人里面。这就是神历世历代所隐藏、如今向圣徒显明的奥秘。

歌罗西书一章二十七节说：「基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。」神不仅要赦免我们的罪，更要把基督分赐到我们里面，使祂成为我们的生命、供应和荣耀的盼望。

**生活中的例子**

一个人拥有一本介绍丰富食物的书，虽然知道许多营养知识，却仍然需要实际吃进食物，才能得到生命的供应。照样，我们不仅需要知道基督的丰富，更需要实际接受并享受基督。

属灵应用：

每天早晨，我们可以向主宣告：「哦，主耶稣！谢谢你不仅是我的救主，更是住在我里面的生命！」

**贰、基督如何住在我们里面？——借着复活成为赐生命的灵**

哥林多前书十五章四十五节下半：「末后的亚当成了赐生命的灵。」

约翰福音十四章十六至十八节：「我要求父，祂必赐给你们另一位保惠师，叫祂永远与你们同在，就是实际的灵，乃世人不能接受的，因为不见祂，也不认识祂；你们却认识祂，因祂与你们同住，且要在你们里面。我不撇下你们为孤儿，我正往你们这里来。」

罗马书八章九至十节：保罗告诉信徒，神的灵住在他们里面；有基督的灵，就属于基督，并且基督是在他们里面。

这几处经文告诉我们，基督今天能够住在信徒里面，是与祂的死而复活，以及圣灵的内住密切相关的。主耶稣在地上时，是神成为肉体，住在人中间。祂经过十字架的死，又从死人中复活。哥林多前书十五章四十五节告诉我们，末后的亚当，就是基督，成了赐生命的灵。

按照李常受弟兄关于经过过程并终极完成之三一神的职事，复活的基督作为赐生命的灵，将祂自己分赐到相信的人里面。这并不是说父、子、灵之间没有区别，乃是强调复活的基督借着那灵，能够真实地住在我们里面，成为我们的生命。

**生活中的例子**

空气虽然看不见，却能够进入人的身体，维持人的呼吸。照样，我们虽然不能用肉眼看见住在里面的基督，却可以借着信心、祷告和操练灵，实际接触并经历祂。当然，基督不是物质的空气；这个例子只是帮助我们认识，看不见不等于不存在。

属灵应用：

我们不需要到遥远的地方寻找主。当我们转向祂、呼求祂时，就能够在灵里接触这位住在我们里面的基督。

**叁、基督住在我们里面的地方，是我们重生的灵**

提摩太后书四章二十二节：「愿主与你的灵同在。愿恩典与你们同在。」

罗马书八章十六节：「那灵自己同我们的灵见证我们是神的儿女。」

哥林多前书六章十七节：「但与主联合的，便是与主成为一灵。」

这三处经文给我们看见，基督住在我们里面，与我们人的灵有特别密切的关系。按照圣经，人有灵、魂、体三部分。（帖前五23）身体是我们接触物质世界的器官。魂包括心思、情感和意志，使我们能够思想、爱好和选择。灵是神所创造、使我们能够接触并接受神的器官。

当我们相信主耶稣时，圣灵使我们的灵得着重生。如今，主与我们的灵同在。基督不仅在天上作我们的救主，也在我们重生的灵里作我们的生命。

**生活中的例子**

一个人遇到困难时，天然的反应可能是立刻担心、着急或发脾气。但是他里面有主。当他停下来，简单呼求：「哦，主耶稣！」他就开始从忙乱的心思转向灵里的主。这就是操练灵、接触主的开始。

**属灵应用**

初信者可以每天操练三件事：呼求主名、向主祷告、将心思转向灵。不必追求特别的感觉，只要凭信接触主。

**肆、基督住在我们里面，是要作我们的生命**

歌罗西书三章四节：「基督是我们的生命，祂显现的时候，你们也要与祂一同显现在荣耀里。」

约翰福音十四章十九节：「还有不多的时候，世人不再看见我，你们却看见我，因为我活着，你们也要活着。」

约翰福音十章十节下半：「我来了，是要叫羊得生命，并且得的更丰盛。」

这些经文告诉我们，基督住在我们里面，首先是要作我们的生命。什么叫作基督作生命？就是我们不再仅仅靠自己的天然能力，努力过一个外面良善的生活，乃是学习凭里面基督的生命生活。

例如：我们天然的生命可能缺少忍耐，但基督是我们的忍耐。我们天然的生命可能没有足够的爱，但基督是我们的爱。我们天然的生命可能常常忧虑，但基督能够成为我们的平安。

这不是说我们不需要作任何选择，而是我们需要学习转向主，与祂合作，让祂的生命在我们里面运行。

**生活中的例子**

一位姊妹在家里照顾孩子，整天忙碌，非常疲倦。当孩子不听话时，她很容易发脾气。但是她想起基督住在她里面。于是，她简单祷告：「主耶稣，我没有忍耐，但你是我的忍耐。求你在我里面活着。」这样的祷告，就是学习经历基督作生命。

属灵应用：

遇到自己不能胜过的软弱时，不要只靠意志努力，更要转向基督，接受祂生命的供应。

**伍、基督不仅作我们的生命，更要作我们的人位**

加拉太书二章二十节：「我已经与基督同钉十字架；现在活着的，不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着；并且我如今在肉身里所活的生命，是我在神儿子的信里，与祂联结所活的，祂是爱我，为我舍了自己。」

以弗所书三章十七节上半：「使基督借着信，安家在你们心里……」

这里我们需要认识一个更深的真理。基督住在我们里面，不仅要作我们的生命，还要作我们的人位。生命是使我们能够活着的。人位则涉及我们的思想、爱好、选择、决定和生活方向。基督作生命，是祂成为我们生活的供应；基督作人位，是我们让祂在我们里面作主，支配我们的思想、爱好和决定。

**生活中的例子**

一个人买了一栋房子，却只允许新主人使用客厅，不允许他进入卧室、厨房或书房。虽然新主人已经进了房子，却还没有完全安家。照样，基督已经住在我们重生的灵里，但我们可能仍然不愿意让祂管理我们的心思、情感和意志。

我们可能愿意在主日聚会时爱主，却不愿意在家庭生活、金钱使用或个人选择上让主作主。因此，以弗所书三章十七节说，基督要借着信安家在我们心里。这说明基督不仅要住在我们里面，更要在我们心的各部分逐渐得着地位。

**属灵应用**

每天作决定以前，可以先问主：「主耶稣，你喜欢我这样作吗？主啊，我愿意让你作我的人位。」

**陆、如何经历「不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着」？**

腓立比书一章二十一节上半：「因为在我，活着就是基督……」

哥林多后书四章十至十一节：保罗告诉我们，他常常在身体上带着耶稣的治死，使耶稣的生命也显明在他的身体上。

这说明活基督不是单单学习模仿耶稣外面的行为，乃是借着十字架的工作，使基督复活的生命从我们里面活出来。

我们可以从三个方面操练。

第一，学习否认自己。

当我们天然的意见、脾气和喜好与主的引导相冲突时，愿意放下自己。

第二，学习转向灵。

借着呼求主名、简短祷告，将心思从天然的反应转向里面的基督。

第三，学习顺从里面生命的感觉。

当主光照我们需要道歉、饶恕别人或停止某种不合宜的行为时，愿意顺服。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄在工作中受到同事批评。他天然的反应是立刻反驳。但他里面感觉需要安静，先听清楚对方的意见。于是，他在心里呼求：「哦，主耶稣！求你作我的人位。」他没有立即发脾气，而是温和地回应。这不只是外面的修养，更可以是他在具体环境中学习经历基督的结果。

属灵应用：

每天至少在一件事情上操练：不立即凭自己反应，而是先转向主，让祂在我们里面活着。

**柒、基督住在我们里面，是为着生命长大与身体建造**

以弗所书三章十六至十九节：保罗祷告，求父照着祂荣耀的丰富，借着祂的灵，用大能使信徒得以加强到里面的人里，使基督借着信安家在他们心里，并使他们被充满，成为神一切的丰满。

以弗所书四章十五至十六节：这两节经文告诉我们，我们需要在爱里持守真实，在一切事上长到元首基督里面，并借着各部分的功用，使基督的身体在爱里把自己建造起来。神将基督分赐到我们里面，不只是为了改善我们个人的生活，更是为了完成祂永远的经纶。

基督住在我们里面，要逐渐扩展到我们全人。祂要更新我们的心思，变化我们的性情，使我们在生命里长大。当众圣徒都这样经历基督，基督的身体就得着实际的建造。

**生活中的例子**

在召会生活中，一位弟兄可能习惯坚持自己的意见。但当他学习让基督作人位时，就开始愿意听取其他圣徒的交通，学习配搭，并顾到身体的感觉。这样的生命变化，不仅使他个人蒙恩，也使基督的身体得着建造。

属灵应用：

我们不仅要在个人生活中经历基督，也要在家聚会、小排聚会和主日聚会中，学习让基督作我们的生命和人位。

**捌、基督在我们里面，是荣耀的盼望，最终完成新耶路撒冷**

歌罗西书一章二十七节：「……就是基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。」

罗马书八章二十九节：「因为神所预知的人，祂也预定他们模成神儿子的形像，使祂儿子在许多弟兄中作长子。」

神为什么要使基督住在我们里面？不仅是为了叫我们今天有平安、有喜乐、有供应，更是为了使我们在生命里长大，最终被模成基督的形像。

基督今天住在我们里面，是生命。祂天天在我们里面运行，使我们得着更新与变化。将来，祂还要使我们身体得赎，进入荣耀。最终，所有蒙救赎、得重生、被变化并得荣耀的圣徒，要成为新耶路撒冷，作神永远团体的彰显。

按照神永远经纶的启示，神成为人，为要使人在生命和性情上成为神，却无分于神的神格。而这一切，都是借着基督不断将祂自己分赐到我们里面而实现的。

基督住在我们里面，是神经纶的中心经历；基督安家在我们心里，是生命变化的过程；基督从我们里面活出来，是神人生活的实际；新耶路撒冷，是这生命分赐与建造的终极完成。

**玖、结束的话——基督徒生活的秘诀，就是让基督在我们里面活着**

亲爱的弟兄姊妹，今天我们认识了一个极其宝贵的真理：基督住在我们里面！祂不是一位遥远的神，也不是一位只存在于历史中的救主。祂是经过死而复活、今天借着那灵住在我们里面的基督。祂住在我们重生的灵里，作我们的生命。祂还要借着信安家在我们心里，成为我们的人位。

因此，正常的基督徒生活，不是单单靠自己的努力做好人，乃是天天转向里面的基督，享受祂、经历祂，并让祂从我们里面活出来。

当我们发脾气时，让基督作我们的忍耐。当我们缺少爱时，让基督作我们的爱。当我们忧虑时，让基督作我们的平安。当我们需要作决定时，让基督作我们的人位。当我们参加召会聚会时，让基督成为我们彼此交通、配搭和建造的实际。

我们越让基督在里面活着，就越能活出基督；越活出基督，就越能在生命里长大，并与众圣徒一同建造基督的身体。最终，这身体要完成于新耶路撒冷，成为神与人永远团体的彰显。愿我们每天都能宣告：「现在活着的，不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着！」阿们！

**拾、简短应用祷告**

「哦，主耶稣！谢谢你住在我的灵里，作我的生命。主啊，求你借着信安家在我心里，管理我的思想、爱好和选择。使我天天转向你、享受你、经历你，不再凭自己而活，乃让你从我里面活出来。阿们！」

title: (EDITORIAL from Korea JoongAng Daily on Oct. 9)
summary: Unification minister downplays North Korean mine provocation Military investigators called the blast a deliberate provocation, while Unification Minister Chung Dong-young instead described it as an accident. The Ministry of Defense has conc
content:
Unification minister downplays North Korean mine provocation
Military investigators called the blast a deliberate provocation, while Unification Minister Chung Dong-young instead described it as an accident.

The Ministry of Defense has concluded that North Korean troops deliberately planted land mines south of the military demarcation line (MDL), seriously injuring three Korean soldiers in a clear provocation that violated the Armistice Agreement.

The conclusion followed investigations by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) and United Nations Command (UNC). At a parliamentary audit yesterday, the JCS chairman declared, "I have never once considered it anything other than a provocation."

Yet Unification Minister Chung Dong-young told lawmakers Wednesday that the incident could not yet be classified as a deliberate mine attack. He instead described it as fundamentally a land mine explosion accident.

That the unification minister refuses to accept the military's findings illustrates the confusion surrounding the Lee Jae Myung administration's North Korea policy.

North Korea has been installing fences and minefields along the MDL under its declared policy of fortifying its border.

Military authorities believe hundreds of North Korean mines may already have been planted south of the demarcation line. Areas have also been identified where North Korean fences are suspected of crossing the MDL. Korean and UNC authorities are preparing on-site investigations.

The mine explosion occurred amid North Korea's apparent efforts to push the boundary gradually southward. Describing deliberate mine placement as an accident effectively grants Pyongyang an excuse for its provocations.

Chung further stirred controversy by suggesting during the audit that allowing the UNC and North Korea to reconfirm the MDL without Korean participation could contribute to peace and stability. The MDL has served as a crucial boundary preventing military clashes between the two Koreas.

With Pyongyang defining inter-Korean relations as those between two hostile states and apparently encroaching southward, voluntarily diminishing Korea's role in determining the boundary is dangerous and irresponsible.

The government's adoption of the North Korean expression "Joseon-Hankook relations" to describe relations between the two Koreas is similarly ill-advised.

The military's preparedness also requires scrutiny. In September last year, the JCS identified an area south of the MDL under the jurisdiction of the Army's 25th Infantry Division in Paju as a suspected mine-laying site using satellite imagery.

It reported its findings to the JCS chairman and defense minister, warning of possible further incursions. Authorities must establish who made decisions following that warning and what preventive measures were taken.

The government must hold North Korea accountable for its provocation. Equally important, it must thoroughly investigate whether military commanders failed to respond appropriately despite receiving advance warnings of the danger a year earlier.

National security demands consistent judgments, clear accountability and coordinated responses across government agencies, particularly when soldiers' lives are at risk.
(END)

title: Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini
summary: Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7
content: Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Implementation of 2027 G CTF Workshop in Eswatini American Institute in Taiwan Opportunity number: GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 Application deadline: November 7 , 202 6 , at 11:59 p.m. (Taipei Time)   A. Basic Information 1. Overview Funding Instrument Type: C ooperative agreement . Cooperative agreements include substantial involvement of the bureau or embassy in program implementation of the project. Examples of substantial involvement are included in section C.2 below. Project Performance Period : Proposed projects should be completed by May 31 , 202 7 . This notice is subject to availability of funding. The Public Diplomacy Section reserves the right to award less or more than the funds described under circumstances deemed to be in the best interest of the U.S. government, pending the availability of funds and approval of the designated grants officer. 2. Executive Summary The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement to support the planning and implementation of a Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) regional franchise workshop in Eswatini in the first or second quarter of 2027. Subject to the availability of funding, AIT intends to award one cooperative agreement of approximately USD 200,000 to implement this program. The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform that brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, academics, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experiences and strengthen cooperation in addressing regional and global challenges. The GCTF was established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015 and has since expanded to include Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom as Partners. The proposed workshop, “Strengthening Cybersecurity and Digital Governance in Southern Africa,” is expected to take place in Eswatini during the first or second quarter of 2027. The program will focus on strengthening cybersecurity resilience, improving digital governance, protecting critical digital infrastructure, addressing emerging cyber threats, and promoting secure and trusted digital transformation. It will provide a platform for participants to exchange practical experiences, identify common challenges, and strengthen professional networks and regional cooperation. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with a particular emphasis on regional participation from Southern Africa. Approximately 60 to 80 participants are expected to participate in the first day of the program, which will feature plenary discussions, expert presentations, and practical exchanges. A smaller group of approximately 40 participants is expected to participate in the second day, which may include focused technical discussions, interactive exercises, working-group sessions, and/or relevant site visits. The program is expected to bring together government officials, cybersecurity and digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from participating African countries. Subject-matter experts from the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF Partners, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, may also be invited to contribute relevant international expertise and practical experience. The selected recipient will serve as AIT’s implementation partner and will be responsible for comprehensive program and logistical support, including venue and lodging coordination, participant management, travel arrangements for designated participants and speakers, ground transportation, interpretation and audiovisual services, workshop materials, vendor coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and required grant reporting. Travel expenses for U.S. Government officials invited by the U.S. Government and Taiwan-supported speakers will be funded separately and should not be included in the recipient’s proposed budget. AIT and GCTF partners will provide overall policy guidance, strategic direction, and substantive oversight throughout program planning and implementation. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, think tanks, private-sector organizations with relevant international program management experience, public international organizations where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations, and other eligible organizations with demonstrated capacity to organize international conferences or capacity-building programs and administer U.S. Government assistance awards. This cooperative agreement is intended to strengthen practical cybersecurity capacity and digital governance cooperation in Southern Africa, expand professional and institutional connections among participating countries, and advance the GCTF as a platform for practical international capacity building, technical exchange, and sustained regional cooperation. B. Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants The following organizations are eligible to apply: Not-for-profit organizations , including non-governmental organizations (NGOs), think tanks, and civil society organizations Educational institutions , including universities and research institutions Professional associations and nonprofit organizations with demonstrated experience managing international conferences or capacity-building programs Private-sector organizations with demonstrated experience organizing international conferences or implementing international exchange programs Public international organizations , where eligible under applicable U.S. Government regulations Organizations may sub-contract with other entities, but only one entity, from the eligible categories of organizations listed above, can be the prime recipient of the award. When sub-contracting with other entities, the responsibilities of each entity must be clearly defined in the proposal. For more information on the difference between sub-contract and sub-recipient, please refer to 2 CFR 200 .331 . 2. Cost Sharing or Matching Cost sharing is not required . 3. Other Eligibility Requirements All organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) issued via SAM.gov as well as a valid registration in SAM.gov. Please see Section D.3 for more information. Individuals are not required to have a UEI or be registered in SAM.gov. Applicants are only allowed to submit one proposal per organization. If more than one proposal is submitted from an organization, all proposals from that institution will be considered ineligible for funding. 4. This opportunity will not support: Projects relating to partisan political activity; Charitable or development activities; including direct social services such as medical, psychological, and/or humanitarian support Construction projects; Projects that support specific religious activities; Fund-raising campaigns; Lobbying for specific legislation or programs Scientific research or surveys; Commercial projects; Projects intended primarily for the growth or institutional development of the organization; Projects that duplicate existing projects; Illegal activities C. Program Description 1. Project Background, Goals, and Objectives Project Background The Global Cooperation and Training Framework (GCTF) is an international capacity-building platform established by Taiwan and the United States in 2015. Japan joined as a full partner in 2019, followed by Australia in 2021, Canada in 2023, and the United Kingdom in 2025. Through workshops and other capacity-building activities, GCTF brings together government officials, technical experts, industry representatives, and civil society representatives to exchange practical experience, strengthen professional networks, and develop approaches to shared regional and global challenges. As governments and societies become increasingly dependent on digital technologies and interconnected systems, cybersecurity and effective digital governance have become important elements of economic development, public-service delivery, critical infrastructure resilience, and public trust. Recent research documents that scam syndicates displaced from Southeast Asian epicenters, including Myanmar, Laos, and Cambodia, are actively pivoting to Africa, with documented raids in nine African countries and growing evidence of scam infrastructure, including online gambling platforms used as cover for fraud operations, gray business Telegram groups openly advertising scam facilities, and unregulated cryptocurrency services establishing footholds across the continent. Countries across Southern Africa face evolving cybersecurity and cybercrime challenges while also seeking to expand digital services, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop governance frameworks that support secure and trusted digital transformation. The proposed GCTF regional workshop in Eswatini will provide a platform for government officials, cybersecurity and the digital governance practitioners, technical experts, private-sector representatives, academics, civil society representatives, and other relevant stakeholders from across Africa to exchange practical experiences and strengthen professional and institutional connections. The workshop is expected to include representatives from at least eight African countries, with particular emphasis on participation from Southern Africa. The program will draw on expertise and practical experience from participating African countries as well as the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partners, as appropriate. Through expert presentations, policy and technical discussions, interactive exchanges, and other practical activities, the workshop will address shared challenges and identify approaches that participating countries may adapt to their respective national and institutional contexts. Strengthening cybersecurity capacity and secure digital governance in Southern Africa also advances U.S. security and economic interests. Cyber threats, cyber-enabled crime, and vulnerabilities in interconnected digital systems increasingly cross-national borders and can affect American citizens, businesses, and critical infrastructure. By strengthening the ability of partner countries to prevent, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats, this program can help reduce vulnerabilities that may be exploited by transnational criminal networks and other malicious cyber actors. The workshop will also strengthen U.S. engagement with African partners on secure and resilient digital ecosystems, promote cooperation and information sharing among governments and technical experts, and expand relationships between African stakeholders and the United States and other GCTF partners. Through practical capacity building and sustained professional networks, the program will support a more secure and resilient regional digital environment while advancing shared interests in cybersecurity, economic security, and trusted digital development. Project Goal: The goal of this project is to strengthen cybersecurity resilience and digital governance capacity in Southern Africa by facilitating practical knowledge exchange, regional cooperation, and sustained professional engagement among participating countries and international partners, while advancing shared U.S. and partner interests in a more secure, resilient, and trusted digital environment. Project Objectives: The project will pursue the following objectives: Strengthen Cybersecurity Capacity and Resilience: Enhance participants’ knowledge of practical approaches to preventing, preparing for, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity threats and incidents, with a specific focus on basic cyber hygiene, national cyber resilience, digital trust, and the development of a secure digital ecosystem aligned with global standards and best practices. Advance Effective and Secure Digital Governance: Promote the exchange of policies, practices, institutional approaches, and lessons learned that support secure, trusted, resilient, and inclusive digital governance and digital transformation. Promote Regional Cooperation and Information Sharing: Strengthen professional and institutional connections among participating African countries and encourage greater cross-border cooperation, information sharing, and coordination in addressing shared cybersecurity and digital governance challenges. Facilitate Practical International Exchange: Connect African policymakers and practitioners with relevant expertise and practical experience from participating African countries, the United States, Taiwan, and other GCTF partner countries, including Japan, Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, as appropriate to the workshop agenda. Support Sustainable Professional Networks and Follow-on Cooperation: Encourage participants to identify practical opportunities for continued professional engagement, knowledge sharing, and future cooperation beyond the workshop. 2. Substantial Involvement This award will require substantial involvement from the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT ) and the U . S . Embassy in Eswatini . AIT will approve all key aspects of the workshop, including but not limited to venue selection, flight and hotel arrangements, ground transportation, lodging, visual designs, agenda, site visit locations, speaker and participant lists, catering and menus, conference room layout, lighting, and audio-visual setup. D. Application Contents and Format Please follow all instructions below carefully. Proposals that do not meet the requirements of this announcement or fail to comply with the stated requirements will be ineligible. Content of Application Please ensure: The proposal clearly addresses the goals and objectives of this funding opportunity All documents are in English All budgets are in U.S. dollars All pages are numbered, including budgets and attachments All documents are formatted to fit 8 ½ x 11 paper All documents are single-spaced, 14-point New Times Roman font, with 1-inch margins. Captions and footnotes may be 10-point New Times Roman font. Font sizes in charts and tables, including the budget, can be reformatted to fit within 1 page width. All applicant authorized signatures are provided where indicated on the various, required forms. The following documents are required: 1. Mandatory application forms SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance – organizations) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424A (Budget Information for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . SF-424B (Assurances for Non-Construction programs) at https://grants.gov/ or https://www.ait.org.tw / . (note: the SF-424B is only required for individuals, organizations exempt from registration, and for organizations not required to fully register in https://sam.gov/ ) 2. Proposal (10 pages maximum) The proposal should contain sufficient information that anyone not familiar with it would understand exactly what the applicant wants to do. You may use your own proposal format, but it must include all the items below. Proposal Summary: Short narrative that outlines the proposed project, including project objectives and anticipated impact. (Attachment: Recommended Proposal Template ). Introduction to the Organization : A description of past and present operations, showing ability to carry out the program, including information on all previous grants from the State Department and/or U.S. government agencies as well as experience with and expertise in areas related to those described in the NOFO. Applicants are encouraged, but not required, to use the attached Applicant Organization Information Survey form to provide this information (Attachment : Recommended Applicant Organization Information (AOI) Survey Template ). If the applicant chooses not to use the attached form, all of the requested information from the form will still need to be addressed in the application package. Problem Statement: Clear, concise and well-supported statement of the problem to be addressed and why the proposed program is needed Program Methods, Design, Activities, and Deliverables: The “goals” describe what the program is intended to achieve. The “objectives” refer to the intermediate accomplishments on the way to the goals. These should be achievable and measurable. Describe the program activities and how they will help achieve the objectives. Proposed Project Schedule and Timeline: The proposed timeline for the program activities. Include the dates, times, and locations of planned activities and events. Key Personnel: Names, titles, roles and experience/qualifications of key personnel involved in the program. What proportion of their time will be used in support of this program? Project Partners: List the names and type of involvement of key partner organizations and sub-awardees (if applicable). Future Funding or Sustainability: Applicant’s plan for continuing the program beyond the grant period, or the availability of other resources, if applicable. Monitoring & Evaluation Plan: Proposals must include a draft Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP). The M&E PMP should show how applicants intend to measure and demonstrate progress towards the project’s objectives and goals. The key components to the PMP are as follows: Monitoring and Evaluation Narrative: In narrative form, applicants should describe how they intend to monitor and evaluate the activities of their award. In addition, the applicant should describe any M&E processes, including key personnel, management structure (where M&E fits into the overall program’s staff structure), technology, and as well provide a brief budget narrative explaining any line-item expenditures for M&E listed in the program’s budget. If the proposal is from a prior grantee, the proposal discusses how the grantee has adapted, improved or otherwise modified their approach based on learning from previous experience. This narrative is limited to two pages. Theory of Change Diagram: Applicants are expected to submit either a Theory of Change diagram or an If-Then Statement that illustrates how project activities will lead to intended outcomes. Monitoring and Evaluation Datasheet: The applicant must include their proposed activities and their expected outputs and outcomes as well as the goals and objectives as written in the NOFO. The datasheet’s purpose is to explicitly illustrate how a project’s activities lead to tangible results (such as increased beneficiary skills, knowledge, or attitudes) that ultimately address a PDS objective. The selected applicant’s M&E PMP is subject to review and approval before any award will be issued under this NOFO. The selected applicant will be required to work with the Public Diplomacy Section’s Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to ensure the applicant’s M&E PMP achieves an expected level of expertise and meets PDS objectives. Expenses directly associated with monitoring and evaluation are considered allowable. The suggested template includes a space to list the portion of the total budget amount directly associated with monitoring and evaluation activities. 3. Budget Justification Narrative Detailed Budget – Applicants must submit a detailed line-item budget. Applicants are encouraged to utilize the template provided with the funding opportunity but are not required to do so (Attachment: Recommended Budget Narrative Template ). Line-item expenditures should be listed in the greatest possible detail. The budget must identify the total amount of funding requested, with a breakdown of amounts to be spent in the following budget categories: personnel; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; supplies; consultants/contracts; other direct costs; and indirect costs. See Annex Section I for a description of the types of costs that should be included in each category. Personnel salaries should include the level of effort and the rate of pay, which should cover the percentage of time each staff member will dedicate to grant-based activities. If an organization is charging an indirect cost rate without a NICRA, it must apply it to the modified total budget costs (MTDC), refer to 2CFR § 200.1 . Budgets shall be submitted in U.S. dollars and final grant agreements will be conducted in U.S. dollars. Budget Justification Narrative – Applicants must submit a budget justification narrative to accompany the detailed line-item budget. The purpose of the budget justification narrative is to supplement the information provided in the detailed budget spreadsheet by justifying how the budget cost elements are necessary to implement project objectives and accomplish the project goals. The budget justification narrative is a tool to help AIT staff fully understand the budgetary needs of the applicant and is an opportunity to provide descriptive information about the requested costs beyond the constraints of the budget template. Together, the detailed budget spreadsheet, the budget justification narrative, and the SF-424A should provide a complete financial and qualitative description that supports the proposed project plan and should be directly relatable to the specific project components described in the applicant’s proposal. Additional Budget Notes: Curing venues, managing logistics, catering, etc. are allowable. Audit Requirements: Please note the audit requirements for Department of State awards in the Standard Terms and Conditions https://www.state.gov/federal-assistance-policies-appeals, Subpart F – Audit Requirements. The cost of the required audits may be charged either as an allowable direct cost to the award OR included in the organization’s established indirect costs in the award’s detailed budget. Visa Fees: Include all visa application and related fees in your budget as applicable. Please note DS-2019s for post-funded programs must be submitted directly by the award recipient. If you anticipate your program will include the DS-2019 visa processing, your organization must be a registered Designated Sponsoring Organization. For more information go to: https://j1visa.state.gov/sponsors/become-a-sponsor/ 4. Attachments Key Personnel Resumes : A résumé, not to exceed one page in length, must be included for the proposed key staff persons, such as the Project Director and Finance Officer, as well as any speakers or trainers (if applicable). If an individual for this type of position has not been identified, the applicant may submit a 1-page position description, identifying the qualifications and skills required for that position, in lieu of a résumé. Letters of support from program partners: Letters of support should be included for sub-recipients or other partners. The letters must identify the type of relationship to be entered into (formal or informal), the roles and responsibilities of each partner in relation to the proposed project activities, and the expected result of the partnership. The individual letters cannot exceed 1 page in length. Indirect Costs : If your organization has a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) and includes NICRA charges in the budget, your latest NICRA should be included in the application submission. Proof of Non-profit Status: Documentation to demonstrate the applicant’s non-profit status (e.g., U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their 501(c)(3) Internal Revenue Service determination letter, and non-U.S. organizations should provide evidence of non-profit status issued by a government entity). Proof of Registration: A copy of the organization’s registration should be provided with the proposal application. U.S.-based organizations should submit a copy of their IRS determination letter. Taiwan -based organizations should submit a copy of their certificate of registration from the appropriate government organization. Other items NOT required/requested with the application submission, but which may be requested if your application is approved to move forward in the review process include: Copies of an organization or program audit within the last two (2) years Copies of relevant human resources, financial, or procurement policies Copies of other relevant organizational policies or documentation that would help the Department determine your organization’s capacity to manage a federal grant award overseas Documentation that demonstrates the recipients’ plan and/or policy to safeguard PII of participants and beneficiaries. It is the responsibility of the recipient to ensure protection of personally identifiable information (PII) and safeguard PII when collecting, maintaining, using and disseminating such information Information to determine what financial controls and standard operating procedures an organization uses to procure goods and services, hire staff and track time and attendance, pay for grant-related travel, and identify other financial transactions that may be necessary to undertake the project activities AIT reserves the right to request any additional programmatic and/or financial information regarding the proposal. E. Submission Requirements and Deadlines 1.Address to Request Application Package Application forms required above are available at https://www.ait.org.tw/ , grants.gov, MyGrants, etc. 2.Department of State Contacts If you have any questions about the grant application process, please contact: AITGCTF@state.gov . Question Deadline: For questions on this solicitation, please contact AITGCTF@state.gov . Questions must be received before October 28, 2026 , at 23:59 p.m. (Taipei Time) . Applicants should not expect an email response to questions, as questions received before the deadline will be answered in a question-and-answer document and posted at http://www.grants.gov and https://www.ait.org.tw/ . 3.Unique entity identifier and System for Award Management (SAM.gov) Required Registration: All organizations, whether based in the United States or in another country, must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and an active registration in SAM.gov. A UEI is one of the data elements mandated by Public Law 109-282, the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA), for all Federal awards. An applicant must maintain an active registration while it has a proposal under review by the Department and must continue to keep the registration active for the entire duration of the period of performance of any Federal award that results from this NOFO. The 2 CFR 200 also requires subrecipients to obtain a UEI. Please note the UEI for subrecipients is not required at the time of application but will be required before an award is processed and/or directed to a subrecipient. Note: The process of obtaining or renewing a SAM.gov registration may take anywhere from 4-8 weeks. Please begin your registration as early as possible . Organizations based in the United States or that pay employees within the United States will need an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and a UEI prior to registering in SAM.gov. Organizations based outside of the United States and that do not pay employees within the United States do not need an EIN from the IRS but do need a UEI prior to registering in SAM.gov. Organizations based outside of the United States that do not intend to apply for U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) awards are no longer required to have a NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code to apply for non-DoD foreign assistance funding opportunities. If an applicant organization is mid-registration and wishes to remove an NCAGE code from their SAM.gov registration, the applicant should submit a help desk ticket (“incident”) with the Federal Service Desk (FSD) online at www.fsd.gov using the following language: “I do not intend to seek financial assistance from the Department of Defense. I do not wish to obtain an NCAGE code. I understand that I will need to submit my registration after this incident is resolved in order to have my registration activated.” Organizations based outside of the United States and that DO NOT plan to do business with the DoD should follow the below instructions: Step 1: Proceed to SAM.gov to obtain a UEI and complete the SAM.gov registration process. # 加州一对华裔夫妇被控虐待至少14名代孕子女

Play video, "'House of Horrors': California couple accused of abusing surrogate-born children", 节目全长 1,07 01:07

视频加注文字，“恐怖之屋”：加州夫妇被控虐待代孕子女 (英文影片）

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 奥莉薇亚·爱尔兰（Olivia Ireland）

*   Published 1 小时前
*   阅读时间: 2 分钟

美国加州一对夫妇被控多项罪名，包括虐待至少14名代孕出生的孩子（其中一些只有两个月大）以及妨碍证人作证。

洛杉矶县地区检察官内森·J·霍克曼（Nathan J Hochman）在一份声明中称：“遭受这种骇人听闻的虐待的儿童人数之多，前所未有。”

美国媒体称，宣国军（Guojun Xuan，音译）和张思薇（Silvia Zhang，音译）是一对夫妇，两人于周二在阿卡迪亚（Arcadia）的豪宅中被捕。

据BBC的美国合作媒体哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）报道，夫妇二人在帕萨迪纳（Pasadena）法院拒绝认罪。

](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/ws/640/cpsprodpb/4102/live/be6f94a0-c228-11f1-b7d8-6f930589c871.jpg.webp)
图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，来自中国的夫妇二人在加州的豪宅被捕，但拒绝认罪。

66岁的宣先生和39岁的妻子张女士被指控合谋，对家中16名儿童中的15名多次施以身体虐待。

此前，已有21名儿童于去年被带离这对夫妇的监护。

根据美国刑事诉状，这对夫妇经营自己的代孕机构，并被指控向至少两名代孕女性作出虚假陈述，暗示张女士难以怀孕。

截至2025年5月，张女士在一份电子表格上记录了21名孩子的情况，其中包括代孕所生的孩子。

官员表示，调查始于当月，当时张女士带着一名头部受伤的两个月大男婴到医院就诊，并告诉医护人员孩子是从床上摔下来的。

据CBS洛杉矶电视台报道，这对夫妇的律师米切尔·克雷姆斯（Mitchell Krems）说，根据他审查的证据，这一指控是对事实的“错误描述”。

加州医院工作人员当时通知了执法部门。警察到达他们的豪宅时，发现了三个不同的房间，被称为“学习中心”，由多名保姆监管，霍克曼将其描述为“恐怖屋”。

据称，这栋大房子装有32个移动感应摄像头，霍克曼说，这对夫妇用这些摄像头监控保姆对孩子的管教情况。

据称，录像显示保姆对孩子打屁股、掌掴或殴打。

一名保姆李春梅（Chunmei Li，音译）被指控殴打一名两个月大的婴儿，导致婴儿在被送往医院前两天头部受伤。

CBS洛杉矶电视台还报道说，克雷姆斯称，事发后，李姓保姆很快就被解雇了。

现年58岁的李姓保姆被控一项重罪，罪名是虐待儿童，且虐待行为可能造成严重人身伤害或死亡。

对此，检察官霍克曼表示，这名保姆目前在逃，法院已发出10.5万美元的逮捕令。

2025年7月，这对夫妇的家首次遭到美国警方搜查，警方将21名儿童带走，交由州政府监护。

阿卡迪亚警察局当时表示，这对夫妇的住所遭到突袭搜查时，孩子们的年龄从两个月到13岁不等，但大多数孩子在一至三岁之间。

15名孩子被从这对夫妇的大房子中带走，另外6名孩子住在别处，后来也被带走。

克雷姆斯强调，他的委托人宣先生是无辜的。

title: China’s crackdown on house churches: An interview with Su Ziming, wife of detained Chinese pastor Wang Lin
summary: On 9 October 2025, Pastor Wang Lin was taken away by police during a crackdown on Zion Church. Zion Church is a “house church” – in other words, one of the primarily protestant churches in China that operate independently of the state-appro
content: On 9 October 2025, Pastor Wang Lin was taken away by police during a crackdown on Zion Church. Zion Church is a “house church” – in other words, one of the primarily protestant churches in China that operate independently of the state-approved religious system and therefore lack official registration. Wang Lin’s case highlights ongoing concerns about religious freedom for independent Christian communities in China. In the months that followed Wang’s arrest, his wife Su Ziming and their young son and daughter endured constant surveillance and harassment, restrictions on their ability to leave China, and prolonged family separation. Today, Su and her children live in the United States, while her husband remains detained in China. Here, Su tells Amnesty International how the crackdown changed the course of her family’s life and describes the wider repression faced by China’s “house churches” and its faith-based communities . How did your husband end up a faith leader? Before becoming a pastor, Wang Lin worked as a lawyer. In 2006, after he became a Christian, he left the legal profession, enrolled in seminary, and spent several years in the US pursuing theological studies. We returned to China at the end of 2017 and Wang Lin became a faith leader at Beijing Zion Church. As a pastor, his greatest joy came from being with others. In 2018, the Chinese authorities shut down Beijing Zion Church. What happened next? After the shutdown, many members were driven out of Beijing by authorities through harassment, including coerced evictions, or concerns about their jobs. A congregation that had once worshipped together found itself scattered across the country. During the COVID-19 pandemic, believers stayed connected through Zoom services and online Bible studies. Gradually, the church became a network spanning multiple provinces rather than a single congregation based in Beijing. And did the authorities allow this? No! At the same time this network developed, surveillance and repression intensified. I think the authorities have tried for a long time to bring house churches fully under their supervision. When house churches refuse government control and wish to exercise their beliefs freely, the governments see this as a problem. And they’re not afraid to use trumped up charges under existing criminal law to solve that problem. At the end of the day, whatever charges they use, their ultimate goal is to crush the church and make it disappear. What are some of the tactics used by the authorities to target the Zion Church? In the case against Zion Church, authorities accused church leaders of receiving “fraudulent proceeds”, treating believers’ tithes and offerings as unlawfully obtained funds. They also characterized church training programmes and seminary courses were deemed as engaging in “illegal business activities.” My husband Wang Lin has been charged on both counts. I think the charges against Zion Church reflect a broader trend in recent years. While some church leaders, like many human rights defenders, are prosecuted on national security charges, authorities have increasingly used charges such as “fraud” and “illegal business operations” to target the normal actions and management of the institutions and communities themselves. What activities are being targeted with these allegations? In the Zion case, the authorities have defined believers’ voluntary offerings as money obtained through fraud. They see it as money that was obtained from people through deception. And as to the theology courses, this was a discipleship training programme within the church. It was never intended to make money. I don’t think this was about actually finding problems with our financial activities; it was aimed at faith communities themselves. What’s been the impact of these allegations? A lot of human rights activists, and very high-profile church leaders, face serious criminal charges like “inciting subversion of state power”. But a lot of damage can be done with these ordinary or more “minor” criminal prosecutions. Not least because it affects the ability of parishioners and believers to exercise their right to freedom of religion. These charges not only stigmatize normal religious activities but also obscure the broader issue of freedom of religion. By treating voluntary offerings as “fraudulent proceeds” and church training programmes as “illegal business activities”, the authorities are effectively criminalizing the peaceful exercise of religious freedom, making it easier to target church leaders and entire faith communities. What about the family members of those targeted – how has it affected you and your family? Even before my husband’s arrest, we were living under immense pressure. We had to move repeatedly, we’d get evicted for no reason, we couldn’t finalize a contract to buy our own home. Wherever we went, it seemed like someone was watching. The most painful thing was seeing our children unable to get an education. Su Ziming Obviously, this had an effect on our children, too. But the most painful thing was seeing our children were unable to get an education. One afternoon, a teacher packed up all of our children’s books and supplies and sent them home. My son asked: “Mom, why do we always have to take our things home?” Even he had begun to realise that this was not the first time our family had faced such disruption. How can I explain? It’s terrible that in China today, simply because of their father’s work, my children don’t have the right to go to school. And so, you decided to leave? Yes. When I tried to leave with our two children in November 2025, we were stopped after entering the airport in Shanghai. The airport security took me aside and escorted me to an interview room; they said I was under an exit ban. They refused to show me any legal documents to justify their actions until hours later – at around 4 in the morning, when I copied down the details of the restriction. Our children were there and saw everything: their mother confronting a room full of police officers. Following sustained international attention and pressure, the authorities eventually lifted the exit ban, allowing us to leave China. But I know this experience has taken an emotional toll on our children. Even here safe in the US, the trauma remains. They often ask: “What if you get arrested too?” It’s a question no mother ever wants to answer. Why have you and other family members decided to go public with this case and the challenges facing Christians, among many faith communities, in China? There have been other church cases that received little public attention over the years, and we have heard reports that people detained then were subjected to abuse and mistreatment. Another house church leader, Yang Rongli, was sentenced to 15 years in prison on fraud charges. But we think that if a case becomes internationally known, authorities often become more cautious in how they treat those in custody. This would be important for the family members of Zion Church, but also to other house churches and believers facing persecution because of their faith. You – international NGOs, governments, the media, the UN – your voices can be the strongest support. Would you like to share a message for your husband? Our children and I will stand with you. I will always believe in you. And no matter if you get sentenced, or for how long, our children and I will wait for you. Amnesty International continues to document the ways in which human rights defenders and others, including faith-based leaders, are targeted with punitive measures by the authorities – and the ways this extends to their family members, despite them not being accused of any crime themselves. Amnesty is concerned about the new Entry-Exit Regulations and the risk that they codify a persistent use of de facto travel and exit bans to constrain freedom of movement for activists and their families. # 喝多醉才算醉？康奈尔轮奸案指控揭“同意法”漏洞争议

Play video, "'I'm very shocked' - College students react to Cornell University rape investigation", 节目全长 1,10 01:10

视频加注文字，“我非常震惊”：大学生谈康奈尔大学强暴案调查重启事件（英文影片）

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 玛德琳·哈尔珀特（Madeline Halpert）

*   Published 3 小时前
*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

美国一名女子对康奈尔大学（Cornell University；康乃尔大学）兄弟会（fraternity）成员提出性侵犯投诉，处理方式引发强烈反弹，凸显了专家们认为美国多个州现行有关性侵与饮酒法律所存在的问题。

该女子在法律文件中以“Jane Doe”（女性无名氏）代称，上月提出诉讼，指控自己于2024年在纽约州康奈尔大学遭数名男子下药及强奸。

Doe表示，在据称事发当晚较早时间，她曾饮酒，其后前往一间兄弟会会所。她指称，多名男子施压要她吸食氯胺酮（ketamine），并不断让她饮酒，之后更在群组讯息中宣传与她进行一次“免费”性接触。

她表示，在据称事发期间自己处于醉酒状态，无法作出有效同意。

End of content

根据现行纽约州法律，若一个人是自愿饮酒或吸毒，而非在违反本人意愿下陷入醉酒或药物影响状态，法律并不会自动认定其失去性行为同意能力。

美国媒体广泛将此称为“自愿醉酒漏洞”（voluntary intoxication loophole）。

纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔（Kathy Hochul）上周表示：“自愿醉酒不构成性侵或轮奸的许可证。”她并表示，将与州议会合作堵塞这个“漏洞”。

但部分专家认为，外界对法律存在误解，相关法例并不会阻止自愿饮酒或吸毒的人提出性侵指控。不过，这些人需要证明自己当时已严重失去行为能力，以至无法作出身体上的同意，而这一门槛高于单纯醉酒。

这种区分反映出美国社会持续存在的争论，即一个人在饮酒后，应如何界定其同意能力。

前性犯罪检察官丹·肖尔（Dan Schorr）向BBC表示，纽约州法律仍然保护那些自愿饮酒或吸毒后遭受性侵的人。

“如果一个人因饮酒或吸毒而无法表达同意或拒绝同意，那么任何与其发生的性行为都属于非自愿，无论其摄入酒精或毒品是自愿还是非自愿的，”肖尔说。肖尔现在亦协助大学审核性侵案件。

他表示：“我曾检控许多针对自愿醉酒人士实施性侵的人。”

他补充说：“我让他们被定罪了。他们被判入狱。”

## 何谓“失去行为能力”（incapacitated）？

一些人认为，现行法律的问题在于，认定一个人因醉酒而无法同意性行为的法律门槛设得过高。

包括纽约州在内，至少19个州都采用较高标准，要求当事人的醉酒程度达到特定水平，才会被认定为失去行为能力、无法作出同意。

纽约州法律规定，若一个人“失去知觉，或因其他原因在生理上无法表达对某项行为的不愿意”，则不能对性行为作出同意。

肖尔表示，这项规定同样适用于因饮酒而严重丧失行为能力、无法作出同意的人。

但另一名接受BBC访问的法律专家表示，这类情况可能难以证明。

曾任检察官、处理过性贩运案件的米切尔·埃普纳（Mitchell Epner）表示，一些检察官“可能不会提出起诉，或者被告可能获判无罪，因为当事人是在醉酒状态下‘表示同意’，但并未完全失去行为能力”。

他表示，在其他法律门槛较低的州份，如果一个人已“受到影响”（impaired）或“严重受到影响”（significantly impaired），便不能作出有效同意；而醉到无法驾驶汽车，便可能被视为已达到这个程度。

大学校园对同意的标准则与刑事法律有所不同，康奈尔大学亦是如此。

该校采用“积极同意”（affirmative consent）标准，将其定义为“所有参与者在知情、自愿及共同决定下进行性活动”。

康奈尔大学表示，沉默或缺乏反抗并不构成同意。

## 推动修法

埃普纳支持修改纽约州法律的提议，以扩大认定一个人因醉酒而无法作出同意的适用范围。纽约州参议院已多次通过相关法案，但州众议会一直未将其提交表决。

该法案规定，如一个人因受到某种物质影响，以致“暂时无法判断或控制”自己的行为，而另一方已知或理应知道该情况，则该人不能作出有效同意。

宾夕法尼亚州亦曾尝试修改相关法律，希望让醉酒受害者更容易证明自己遭受性侵。

“如果一个人醉到不能开车，那他也醉到不能做其他事情了——你可以自行填上任何动词，”埃普纳说。

选区涵盖康奈尔大学的州议员莉亚·韦布（Lea Webb）向BBC电视新闻台表示，她与其他议员正推动相关立法，而法案已经历多次修订。

她表示，纽约州现行法律“将举证责任放在受害者身上”。

另一方面，肖尔及一些刑事辩护律师批评有关修改纽约州性侵法律的建议。

纽约州刑事辩护律师协会（State Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers）在发给 BBC的声明中表示，纽约州现行法律已经足够，而且“在受害人属自愿醉酒的案件中，已有被告被裁定强奸罪成”。

该组织表示，使用“无法判断或控制其行为”等措辞，“过于模糊，难以公平执行”，并指出法案没有清楚说明何种程度的醉酒才构成无法进行性行为。

肖尔表示，要界定一个人究竟在何时因醉酒而失去同意能力，并非容易回答的问题。

他补充说：“法律应该如何处理这个问题？要找到一个清晰而且能够一致适用的标准，是非常困难的。”

“这是一场我们作为一个社会、一个州，应该共同讨论的对话。”

# 蔡康永现身民进党选举造势活动遭砲轰 盘点大陆商界“割席台独”案例

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，蔡康永在民进党竞选集会现场称，如果能访问到台北市长选战每一位候选人“会很棒”。

Published 26 分钟前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

台湾将于11月底举行地方选举，台湾知名主持人蔡康永周末现身民进党竞选活动，引来中国大陆网民强烈反应，曾合作的大陆品牌也警告“保留追究法律责任权利”。

蔡康永周日（10月4日）现身立法委员沈伯洋台北市长竞选总部成立大会。蔡康永回应提问时称“就是来见识一下”；其经纪人表示，目前正在考虑访问台北市长两大候选人，会尽可能了解其历程及意见。

沈伯洋是“黑熊学院”创办人，长期推动民防训练，并研究中国认知作战；中国国台办将其列入“台独顽固分子”名单，重庆市公安局更以“分裂国家罪”立案侦查沈伯洋。

蔡康永的举动引发中国网络反弹及商界切割。“蔡康永现身台独分子竞选会场”登上[微博热搜](https://s.weibo.com/weibo?q=%23%E8%94%A1%E5%BA%B7%E6%B0%B8%E7%8E%B0%E8%BA%AB%E5%8F%B0%E7%8B%AC%E5%88%86%E5%AD%90%E7%AB%9E%E9%80%89%E4%BC%9A%E5%9C%BA%23&topic_ad=&t=31)；曾与其合作的零跑汽车发声明否认蔡康永为其代言人，并称已下架与其相关内容。

## 蔡康永是谁？

蔡康永现年64岁，是台湾知名主持人，与台湾艺人“小S”徐熙娣合作的电视节目《康熙来了》极受华语圈欢迎，亦是台湾公众人物中少数公开出柜的同性恋者。

蔡康永生于台北，父母来自上海，是外省人第二代，早年在美国读书后回台，任影评人和编剧，其后跨足广播影视圈，并着有多本作品，近年工作往中国发展。

蔡康永周日被拍到戴着帽子、口罩现身民进党沈伯洋竞选总部成立大会，他坐在台下，手持现场旗帜及加油棒。离场面对记者提问时，蔡康永表示，“就是来见识一下”，也想要听听各方的意见，又指“如果有机会的话，访问到每一位候选人会很棒”。

蔡康永透过经纪人表示，目前正在考虑访问台北市长两位候选人，会尽可能了解其历程及意见。

## 中国网络及商界如何反弹？

消息曝光后，“蔡康永现身台独分子竞选会场”登上[微博热搜](https://s.weibo.com/weibo?q=%23%E8%94%A1%E5%BA%B7%E6%B0%B8%E7%8E%B0%E8%BA%AB%E5%8F%B0%E7%8B%AC%E5%88%86%E5%AD%90%E7%AB%9E%E9%80%89%E4%BC%9A%E5%9C%BA%23&topic_ad=&t=31)；有网民涌进蔡康永的抖音及小红书帐号留言，如宣扬“台湾永远属于中国”，关注何时封号，以及提出工作“你这样一搞谁还敢工作邀约你啊？”

中国大陆目前仍是“十一”长假期，在微博上拥有176万粉丝的军政博主“终南剑客”彭迪周一（5日）[发表播客影片](https://www.weibo.com/7092883638/RlgmWsIvX)，宣称“全网都在骂蔡康永，把高高兴兴大过节的我们大家都气到不行”，提出“光骂不够，得打，而且得打疼，打出威慑，打出效果⋯⋯杀鸡儆猴”。

被一些中国官方媒体形容为“军事大V”的彭迪并未说明要如何具体“打出威慑”，但该影片在微信上收获超过9600个赞好，被转发超过1700次。

网络有说法指蔡康永的微博同被清空。蔡康永的微博目前有约3600万粉丝，只见标注为“博主设置了仅展示半年内的微博”，但未见任何公开帖文，亦无关注任何帐号。

目前不确定微博内容是否因应近日事件而遭清空，[惟来自2022年底的报导指出](https://www.setn.com/news/1220050)，蔡康永微博当时已经清空；[他后来曾公开受访说明](https://www.mirrordaily.news/story/89629)，整理微博已经长达一年多。

浙江零跑汽车[周日深夜发声明](https://weibo.com/5872290888/Rla8Q5Su0)，重申“一个中国”原则，坚决反对任何形式的“台独”分裂活动及一切伤害民族感情的言行。

声明强调蔡康永并非代言人，只是过往合作内容的参与艺人，目前已下架与其相关内容，保留追究法律责任权利，又指会进一步加强合作方背景与立场审核。

据报，知名时尚杂志《时尚芭莎》删除蔡康永9月份的专访。

中共官方《人民日报》旗下《环球时报》前总编辑胡锡进[发文称](https://weibo.com/1989660417/RlhqBxRI4)：“来大陆发展的艺人不得支持‘台独’，是一条绝对的红线，任何人都踩不得，我认为这是所有台湾艺人来大陆发展应有的高度警觉。”

## 现身后牵扯的选举议题

现任中国国民党籍台北巿长蒋万安将在11月的选举中竞逐连任，民进党的沈伯洋被视为其主要对手。

蒋万安回应蔡康永出席沈伯洋集会争议时，呼吁大陆尊重台湾自由民主生活方式，不要因为政治倾向而有任何差别待遇，又指如有节目邀约，幕僚团队会规划，也会邀请蔡康永出席其竞选总部成立活动。

蔡康永其后在社交平台转载蒋万安受访片段，指收到具体邀约后会“欣然前往观摩学习”，“尽可能遵循该场主人希望的服装方向去打扮，共塑派对气氛”。

沈伯洋则指，蔡康永到场是想聆听各式各样不同的声音，“他来这边，他并不是在这边跟着我们喊，他是来过来看说，欸，这个人讲什么？然后他接下来可能也想去看另一个人讲什么”，认为在民主社会做这样的事情“应该是稀松平常的”。

台北市长其他参选人有“台湾麻将最大党”郭玺、“台湾双语无法党”萧文干、三势团结促进联盟唐新民，以及无党籍林志成。

## 施压事件屡发

台湾演艺文化界人士因被中国大陆一方认为支持“台独”或政治立场有争议，而遭受陆方官方舆论与商业施压的事件，时有发生。

2021年，与蔡康永合作无间的“小S”徐熙娣，于东京奥运期间[以“国手”形容中华台北选手](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/chinese-news-58116399)，亦遭大陆网民砲轰其支持“台独”，至少四家大陆品牌与之解约“割蓆”。

2023年，“小S”女儿许韶恩回答网民提问时说“英文是母语”，大陆网民高呼抵制，遭一家大陆女装品牌解除广告合作。

其他具代表性的案例还包括：2016年周子瑜因挥舞中华民国国旗卷入政治争议，其演艺事业一度受冲击；2022年田馥甄因社交媒体帖文及歌词惹议，其歌曲遭部分平台下架，多项商演受影响。

电影界亦有类似情况。2018年台湾纪录片得奖导演傅榆的“台独致辞”引发政治风波，中国官方下令暂停中国电影人赴台。

同样在2021年，活跃台湾的马来西亚华人歌手黄明志与澳洲马来西亚华裔歌手陈芳语合作发表单曲《玻璃心》，[内容遭大陆官媒批评为“侮辱中国人民”](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/chinese-news-59386956)，陈芳语称[曾收到“死亡威胁”](https://www.setn.com/news/1024759)，又称对遭中国大陆封杀[感到遗憾，但并不后悔](https://www.abc.net.au/chinese/2021-10-29/china-bans-australian-singer-kimberley-chen-fangyu-mocks-xi/100578866)。

与此同时，过去有不少台湾艺人会在中国特定日子、10月1日中共建政周年或解放军阅兵时转贴官媒帖文。台湾大陆委员会（陆委会）曾约谈部分艺人，并警告他们若“配合陆方宣传矮化、消灭我国家主权”，会依据《两岸人民关系条例》惩处。

title: 世界正滑向“黑帮天堂”，怀旧越来越不现实
source: 中国民主转型研究所（每季度一次刊物）
summary: * 作者：Hal Brands（约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院亨利·A·基辛格全球事务杰出教授） * 本文系编译，完整内容请阅读原文 * 原文来源： https://foreignpolicy.com/2026/09/09/hal-brands-rules-based-order-great-power-politics-geopolitics/ 冷战结束之初，人们曾经相信世界正在变得更加文明。美国及其盟友建立的规则体系，让贸易可以通过世界贸易组织解决，让国家边界和航行
content: * 作者：Hal Brands（约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院亨利·A·基辛格全球事务杰出教授） * 本文系编译，完整内容请阅读原文 * 原文来源： https://foreignpolicy.com/2026/09/09/hal-brands-rules-based-order-great-power-politics-geopolitics/   冷战结束之初，人们曾经相信世界正在变得更加文明。美国及其盟友建立的规则体系，让贸易可以通过世界贸易组织解决，让国家边界和航行自由拥有共同认可的规范，也让美国的军事力量成为维系秩序的“警察”。在这种体系里，开放经济似乎能够带来共同繁荣，大国竞争也可能随着相互依存而逐渐缓和。 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院亨利·A·基辛格全球事务杰出教授哈尔·布兰兹（Hal Brands）在《外交政策》2026年秋季号封面文章中直言：那是一个鼓舞人心的愿景，却终究是幻觉。今天的世界正滑向“黑帮天堂”，越来越只看实力，越来越不讲规则。 随着俄罗斯重新寻求势力范围、中国迅速崛起，以及美国自身越来越厌倦承担全球秩序的成本，这套体系开始松动。俄罗斯在后苏联地区改变边界，中国利用全球化带来的财富扩充军力、争夺未来产业，并强化在南海的影响力；与此同时，美国经历中东战争和金融危机后，也越来越怀疑自己是否还应继续充当全球“治安官”。从2013至2014年前后，美国对叙利亚化武问题的“红线”没有真正兑现，对俄罗斯第一次入侵乌克兰的反应也相当有限。美国社会由疲惫走向失望，尤其是中国崛起让越来越多美国人认为，开放的世界经济反而掏空了本国制造业、壮大了竞争对手。 如今，变化已经不仅发生在安全领域，也发生在经济领域。世界贸易组织长期陷入停滞，保护主义和关税重新抬头，美国和中国甚至把供应链变成了经济与地缘政治斗争的武器。与此同时，战争、领土争端、军备竞争和军控体系的衰退，让国际规则越来越像一层薄膜。文章甚至借用了一个非常形象的比喻：世界正面临变成“gangster’s paradise”——一个规则越来越不重要、越来越只讲拳头大小的“黑帮天堂”。但布兰兹同时强调，眼下国际社会还不是1930年代那种全面无政府状态，很多联盟和国际制度依然存在，但世界正在变得更加黑暗、混乱，也更加不宽容。 那么，在这样的世界里如何生存？布兰兹首先提醒人们：怀旧不是战略。不能把特朗普视为一切问题的唯一来源，也不能幻想换一位美国总统，世界就会自动恢复到过去。北京和莫斯科早就在挑战旧秩序，而特朗普只是更深层力量变化的表现之一。真正需要改变的，是各国自己的心态。 第二个关键词是“自助”。在一个保障越来越少的世界里，不能把国家安全完全寄托于某个大国、某份国际条约或某个国际机构。文章特别提到波兰和日本：前者正在突破旧有财政和政治限制，大幅增加国防投入，并强化与欧洲前线国家的合作；后者则积极发展与澳大利亚、菲律宾、印度、越南等国家的安全关系。这里的“自助”并不是完全孤立，而是在继续保留与美国合作的同时，为未来建立更多替代方案。 第三，布兰兹并不看好由众多“中等强国”联合起来拯救旧秩序。加拿大总理马克·卡尼（Mark Carney）曾在达沃斯提出“中等强国时刻”，希望这些国家联合维护规则体系，但布兰兹认为，权力现实决定了这很难成功。更现实的做法，是让规模较小、利益更一致的国家形成紧密合作，降低自身对单一市场和单一安全来源的依赖。 第四，联盟仍然不可替代，但联盟关系会越来越交易化。即使美国变得更加自利，它仍然需要欧洲、中东和亚洲的盟友；而这些国家也仍需要美国提供安全保障。文章甚至把这种关系延伸到人工智能领域：美国拥有先进的AI能力，却离不开荷兰、台湾等掌握关键技术和供应链节点的伙伴。未来的联盟，可能不再建立在单纯的价值共同体之上，而更多建立在明确的利益交换之上。 第五，所有国家都必须学会为“风险溢价”付钱。过去全球化追求的是效率，未来则需要更多考虑韧性。霍尔木兹海峡、能源运输、关键矿产、粮食供应链，都可能成为地缘政治武器。因此，一条更昂贵但更安全的替代管线，一份更大的战略储备，都可能值得付出成本。效率不再是唯一标准，避免被别人“卡脖子”同样重要。 有意思的是，布兰兹最后也把警告送给那些正在拆除旧规则的国家。俄罗斯和中国或许会在短期内从“弱规则、强实力”的世界获益，但长期而言，它们也可能成为这种新环境的受害者：日本重新武装，波兰和德国增强军事力量，核扩散风险上升，全球贸易和航运受损，最终都可能反过来威胁自身安全。 所以，文章真正想说的并不是“规则已经死了，因此实力才是一切”，而是既然旧秩序正在瓦解，就不要沉湎于旧时代的安全感，而要学会在不确定性中建立自己的韧性。更重要的是，美国同样不能误以为强大就意味着可以肆无忌惮。因为一个国家真正长期的力量，不只来自军舰、关税和武器，也来自盟友对它的信任。今天若为了短期利益只奉行黑帮逻辑，把世界变成丛林，明天就可能发现，自己失去的恰恰是曾经放大自身力量的那张网络。

title: 国会指出美中科研合作的国家安全隐患后，NASA暂停4千万美元拨款项目

content:
众议院中国问题特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)星期五(10月2日)赞扬美国国家航空航天局(NASA)加强科研安全执法。在该委员会今年发布一份报告后，NASA最近采取重大步骤，加强对《沃尔夫修正案》(Wolf Amendment)的执行力度，并暂停总计4000万美元的40个拨款项目，以着手处理报告指出的安全隐患问题。

这位密歇根州共和党籍联邦众议员在声明中说：“NASA采取重要步骤保护美国的科研与创新，理应受到肯定。”

今年5月，穆勒纳尔领导的众议院中国问题特设委员会公布了一份报告，题为《美国太空未来的研究安全：NASA对《沃尔夫修正案》的执法情况》(Research Security for America's Future in Space: NASA's Enforcement of the Wolf Amendment)，检查NASA的安全合规问题以及对《沃尔夫修正案》的执行情况。

《沃尔夫修正案》是2011年通过的法律，禁止NASA在没有国会和联邦调查局批准的情况下出资与中国展开双边研究与活动。

该报告发现有几百个NASA支持或资助的出版文献有美中人员共同署名或机构合作，有可能违反《沃尔夫修正案》。

前弗吉尼亚州共和党籍联邦众议员弗兰克·沃尔夫(Frank Wolf)是《沃尔夫修正案》的推出者。他在那份报告的前言中写道，美国科研环境的开放促进创新，加强美国领导力，“然而，开放并不意味着没有规则。当纳税人资助的研究与国家安全风险发生交集时，美国既有权威也有义务划定明确的界限。《沃尔夫修正案》确立了这些界限。本报告表明，必须采取更多举措来坚守这些界限。”

中国问题特设委员会主席、来自密歇根州的共和党籍联邦众议员穆勒纳尔(左)和来自艾奥瓦州的共和党籍联邦参议员格拉斯利(右)。

今年2月，穆勒纳尔与艾奥瓦州的共和党籍联邦参议员查克·格拉斯利(Chuck Grassley)曾联名致函NASA负责人，对这家美国宇航机构可能资助了“与中国实体的双边合作”提出质疑。众议院中国问题特设委员会还在当时发表声明说，“NASA资助的研究永远也不应依赖与中国军工综合体有关联的实体。”

在该委员会5月份发布那份报告后，NASA对总额超过4000万美元的40个正在进行的研究拨款项目进行审议，检查与中国机构开展双边研究合作时可能存在的违反《沃尔夫修正案》规定的问题，在审议期间，这些拨款项目被暂停。

NASA还启动了行政执法行动，并在其研究安全办公室与监察长办公室之间建立了一项协调机制，以便将经证实的违规行为移交有关机构作进一步调查，而且有可能移交司法部采取执法行动。

此外，NASA制定并实施了一项自动化流程，以主动识别可能涉及违禁或高风险合作的论文成果，并对接受拨款的人员制定了额外的审查程序，以确保合规。

穆勒纳尔在声明中说：“这对主动识别违禁合作并将其移交进行适当执法至关重要。我赞赏NASA领导层和特朗普政府采取这些必要的具体步骤，以保护由纳税人资助的研究工作。”

在众议院中国问题特设委员会对美中科技合作问题提出关切后，美国战争部今年1月采取措施，阻止在美运营的被列为“中国军事企业”的实体接受该部资助的基础研究资金，美国国家科学基金会(NSF)则在今年7月推出新政策，禁止将其科研资金用于与被纳入美国政府各个受限制清单的实体开展合作。

title: Mynt IPO oversubscribed
summary: INVESTOR demand for Mynt Inc.’s initial public offering (IPO) exceeded share allocations at several brokerages, with one firm reporting subscriptions more than four times its assigned quota, as investors bet on the growth prospects of GCash
content:
INVESTOR demand for Mynt Inc.’s initial public offering (IPO) exceeded share allocations at several brokerages, with one firm reporting subscriptions more than four times its assigned quota, as investors bet on the growth prospects of GCash’s parent company ahead of its stock market debut.

AB Capital Securities Inc., which handles subscriptions through GCash’s GStocks PH platform, reported that its allocated shares were 165.11 percent oversubscribed as of Friday. Regina Capital Development Corp. head of sales Luis Limlingan, meanwhile, said his firm’s allocation was oversubscribed four times.

Domestic trading participants and retail investors were allocated 2.41 billion shares, equivalent to 30 percent of the base offering of about 8.03 billion shares, according to the offering details.

*   [Trade dept welcomes Mitsubishi-Ayala deal](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/business/corporate-news/trade-dept-welcomes-mitsubishi-ayala-deal/2443998)

COL Financial Inc.’s head of research April Tan attributed the strong investor interest partly to the participation of about 22 cornerstone investors along with the attractive offer price.

“And the price is also good, not expensive,” she added.

In a client memo issued Monday, COL Financial said Mynt retained significant growth potential through GCash, which had 41.5 million monthly active users, equivalent to 56 percent of the country’s adult population.

The brokerage noted that digital payment adoption in more developed markets typically reaches 70 percent to 80 percent of the adult population, suggesting room for GCash to expand its user base.

GCash also had 7.5 million active borrowers, representing about 18 percent of its monthly active users, indicating potential to expand its lending business, COL Financial said.

*   ![Image 1: Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256345.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

The platform could also grow through merchant acquisition and overseas remittance services for overseas Filipino workers.

SeA Focus Portfolio hedge fund manager Eric Jurado said the P6.60-per-share IPO price did not require Mynt to sustain its historical earnings growth rate to justify its valuation.

He said the offer price assumed annual growth of 15 percent from Mynt’s 2025 net income of P17.15 billion, or a 25.8 percent growth rate from 2026 to 2028, which he considered achievable based on the company’s historical performance.

“Given GCash’s market leadership, 41.5 million monthly active users, expanding financial ecosystem, and continued shift toward digital payments in the Philippines, I believe that is a realistic hurdle,” Jurado said.

*   ![Image 2: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

He added that investors could benefit if Mynt’s earnings growth exceeded the rate implied by the offer price, potentially prompting the market to recognize greater earnings capacity.

COL Financial estimated that at P6.60 per share, Mynt would be trading at 21.7 times its projected 2026 earnings and 17.1 times its projected 2027 earnings, well below regional peer averages of 33.3 times and 24.2 times, respectively.

Mynt wrapped up its IPO on Monday and is scheduled to list on the Philippine Stock Exchange on Oct. 20 under the ticker symbol GCASH.

The base offering comprises 1.61 billion primary shares and 6.42 billion secondary shares for a total of about 8.03 billion shares, with an additional 1.2 billion secondary shares available through an over-allotment option.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

At P6.60 per share, the base offering could raise about P53 billion, with total proceeds reaching approximately P60.9 billion if the over-allotment option is fully exercised.

Mynt expects to receive P10.6 billion in gross proceeds from the primary share offering, of which it plans to allocate 60 percent to its credit technology business, 20 percent to product innovation, and the remaining 20 percent for general corporate purposes.

title: TSMC to get 6th straight record profit quarter
summary: TAIPEI — TSMC, the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector. Analysts say de
content:
TAIPEI — TSMC, the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector.

Analysts say demand for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s AI chipmaking capacity, as well as its advanced chip packaging technology, CoWoS, remains strong.

That has catapulted Asia’s most valuable company, a key supplier to Nvidia and Apple, to new heights. Its market capitalization is almost double that of South Korean rival Samsung Electronics at around $2.1 trillion.

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

On Thursday, TSMC is expected to report a 65-percent surge in third-quarter net profit to ⁠NT$746.3 billion ($23.4 billion), according to an LSEG SmartEstimate compiled from 16 analysts. SmartEstimates place greater weight on forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate.

**An earnings call at which it will provide fourth-quarter and updated full-year guidance is scheduled for 0600 GMT.**

Any result above NT$706.56 billion would mark the company’s highest-ever quarterly net income, as well as its 11th consecutive quarter of profit growth.

Last Thursday, it posted a 50-percent year-on-year rise in third-quarter revenue, beating market forecasts and hitting a new record high.

In an Oct. 6 report, Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan said he expected TSMC to raise its full-year revenue growth forecast to the low-to-mid 40-percent range from its current guidance of more than 40 percent, driven by strong demand for its 3-nanometer chips.

**Texas expansion prospects**

TSMC is investing $265 billion to ⁠build chip factories in the US state of Arizona, including an additional $100 billion that was unveiled in July.

In September, Reuters reported that TSMC was evaluating a potential investment in Texas. Tesla CEO Elon Musk also said last week that his companies would build and operate the Terafab AI chip complex, with TSMC potentially subleasing a part of it.

**Analysts expect TSMC to address questions about its potential expansion plans in Texas.**

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

In his report, Chan ⁠said an expansion in Texas could become necessary given growing customer demand and limited space at TSMC’s Arizona site in five years’ time.

Phelix Lee, senior equity analyst at Morningstar, however, saw limited urgency for TSMC to expand into Texas, given that some of its planned fabs in ⁠Arizona have yet to be built.

“Texas is a good location for a 2030s or 2040s expansion grand plan, given its long history of semiconductor ecosystem and talent pool,” Lee said. “It may be a dangling carrot to preempt potential US trade and other policies.”

On ⁠its July earnings call, the company raised its capex forecast for this year to between $60 billion and $64 billion from a previous prediction at the high end of $52 billion to $56 billion.

title: PH warned of repeated Chinese deployments
summary: THE repeated deployment of a Chinese maritime militia vessel accompanied by dozens of small boats near Kota Island raises concerns over China's continuing efforts to assert its claims in the West Philippine Sea, national security expert and
content:
THE repeated deployment of a Chinese maritime militia vessel accompanied by dozens of small boats near Kota Island raises concerns over China's continuing efforts to assert its claims in the West Philippine Sea, national security expert and civil society leader Jose Antonio Goitia said.

The same Chinese Maritime Militia Vessel (CMMV) 9622 returned to the waters near the Philippine-held island on Oct. 9 with 22 sampans, just 11 days after it was reported in the area with 24 similar boats.

The latest incident involved an alleged attempt by the Chinese vessel to assert control over the area and order Filipino personnel to leave as Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) personnel, supported by the Philippine Marine Corps and Philippine Navy, moved to address the Chinese presence.

*   [Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

Goitia said Filipino defenders had the right to remain in Philippine waters and carry out their duties despite the Chinese vessel's reported demand.

“Our Coast Guard, Marines, and Navy have every right to perform their lawful duties in Philippine waters. No foreign vessel can simply order them to leave. They were there to protect our interests, and they had every reason to stay,” he said.

According to the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS), one of the 22 sampans approached within about 250 meters of Kota Island's shoreline.

The Chinese mothership maneuvered around and encircled Philippine boats, claimed the area as Chinese territory and directed the Filipino team to leave.

The PCG and NTF-WPS said the coordinated Philippine response resulted in all the Chinese vessels leaving the island's territorial sea.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

The task force also accused the Chinese boats of engaging in unauthorized fishing and dumping waste at sea.

The return of CMMV 9622 so soon after its previous deployment highlights the recurring presence of Chinese maritime militia vessels and small boats near Philippine-held features in the disputed South China Sea.

Kota Island, also known as Loaita Island, is part of the Kalayaan Island Group in Palawan. Its territorial sea falls under Philippine sovereignty.

The NTF-WPS said the reported activities violated Philippine laws, including Republic Act 12064, or the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, and Republic Act 8550, or the Philippine Fisheries Code, as amended by Republic Act 10654.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

China claims most of the South China Sea, including areas disputed by the Philippines.

A 2016 arbitral ruling under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea rejected the legal basis of China's expansive historic-rights claim insofar as it exceeds the maritime rights allowed under the convention. Beijing rejected the ruling.

title: Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first
summary: ASTON Martin has expanded its DBX lineup with the new DBX GT, a more comfort-focused version of its high-performance SUV that places greater emphasis on refinement, craftsmanship, and daily usability while retaining the same 727PS twin-turb
content:
ASTON Martin has expanded its DBX lineup with the new DBX GT, a more comfort-focused version of its high-performance SUV that places greater emphasis on refinement, craftsmanship, and daily usability while retaining the same 727PS twin-turbo V8 used in the DBX S.

The DBX GT is aimed at buyers who want a quieter and more understated interpretation of the brand’s SUV. Aston Martin says the model combines improved ride comfort, lower cabin noise, and a more luxurious interior with the same performance capability expected from the DBX range.

*   [Geely Monjaro EM-i takes on Philippine roads](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/fast-times/geely-monjaro-em-i-takes-on-philippine-roads/2443717)

Despite its stronger focus on comfort, the DBX GT retains the performance hardware and chassis capability expected from Aston Martin’s high-performance SUV range.

“DBX GT is aimed at customers who prefer assured elegance over sporting aggression and demand a higher degree of luxury,” Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark said.

“By refining the visual drama and elevating the interior with new elements of craftsmanship, the DBX GT delivers a true ultra-luxury experience; one which comes with no sacrifice in performance,” he added.

Exterior changes are intended to give the DBX GT a more restrained appearance than the sportier DBX S. The most noticeable update is a new double-vane grille, offered in bright or dark finishes, with the split metal vanes extending toward the outer vents and daytime running lights.

The SUV also receives a new two-piece metal side strake with polished and satin finishes inspired by traditional watchmaking. The lower front bumper, side sills, and rear diffuser are painted in body color as standard, while new quad exhaust finishers are arranged horizontally at the rear.

*   ![Image 7: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

A new 22-inch forged wheel with a Satin Titanium diamond-turned finish is standard, paired with all-season tires selected to improve ride comfort and reduce road noise. Buyers can also choose an optional 23-inch wheel and tire package.

Inside, Aston Martin has redesigned both the front and rear seats with additional cushioning, revised bolsters, and new comfort contours.

A 10-mm memory foam layer has been added to the seat cushions, while the rear cabin now features two individually sculpted seating positions designed to provide greater lateral support without sacrificing five-seat capacity.

The DBX GT also comes with a panoramic glass roof, semi-aniline leather, deep-pile floor mats, and GT-specific upholstery combinations. Aston Martin says each front seat uses 691 meters of thread, 3,297 perforation holes, and required more than four and a half hours of craftsmanship to complete.

*   ![Image 8: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

The cabin also receives anodized metal switchgear and a new drive-mode controller, while additional sound-deadening materials, improved body sealing, and acoustic laminated rear side glass have been used to reduce outside noise. Aston Martin claims a 13-percent improvement in its Articulation Index measure, which evaluates how easily occupants can hold a conversation while the vehicle is moving.

Performance

remains unchanged

Despite the stronger focus on refinement, performance remains unchanged from the DBX S.

*   ![Image 9: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

The 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 produces 727 PS and 900 Newton-meters (Nm) of torque, using turbocharger technology shared with the Valhalla supercar. Aston Martin claims a 0-60 mph time of 3.1 seconds and a top speed of 193 mph, or about 311 kph.

Stopping power comes from carbon-ceramic brakes measuring 420 mm at the front and 390 mm at the rear. The DBX GT also uses the faster steering ratio from the DBX S, while retaining a 12-meter turning circle.

The suspension receives its own GT-specific calibration, including revised damper settings and new internal damper valves designed to better filter small, high-frequency road imperfections. Spring behavior also changes according to the selected drive mode to balance ride comfort with body control and steering response.

Aston Martin has also recalibrated the throttle and nine-speed wet-clutch automatic transmission for smoother and more progressive responses in everyday driving. A revised transmission mount and additional longitudinal dampers between the body and rear subframe are intended to improve structural refinement over rough roads and large suspension movements.

The exhaust system also receives a dedicated GT tune. In GT mode, the system is calibrated for quieter progress, while Sport and Sport+ modes restore a more aggressive exhaust note.

“The challenge with DBX GT was achieving meaningful improvements in comfort and refinement in everyday use cases, but keeping the same class-leading reserves of performance and handling we have achieved with the DBX S,” Aston Martin Chief Technology Officer Ian Hoban said.

The DBX GT joins the DBX range as its most comfort-oriented and understated variant while retaining the same headline performance figures as the DBX S.

First deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: With contract expiring, KBO club manager recounts fond memories at old home stadium
summary: By Yoo Jee-ho SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Ahead of his final game at Jamsil Baseball Stadium, a historic Seoul ballpark set to be demolished after this year, Lotte Giants manager Kim Tae-hyoung on Monday recounted some fond memories at the v
content:
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- Ahead of his final game at Jamsil Baseball Stadium, a historic Seoul ballpark set to be demolished after this year, Lotte Giants manager Kim Tae-hyoung on Monday recounted some fond memories at the venue over his playing and coaching career.

"My first game here came as a college player during the 1988 Olympics," Kim said, before facing the home team Doosan Bears in the two teams' regular-season finale. "Then I joined Doosan. I played for them and later managed the team for years. All told, I have probably spent 30 years of my baseball life here."

Kim spent his entire 12-year playing career with the Bears but did not leave much of a mark as mostly a backup catcher. As the Bears' manager, though, Kim had a wildly successful run, reaching the Korean Series every year from 2015 to 2021 and winning titles in 2015, 2016 and 2019.

"Those were some happy times," Kim said with a smile.

Asked if he felt sad that the stadium, which opened in 1982, will be replaced after this season, the 59-year-old cracked, "I am not really a sentimental type. Plus, I have my own future to worry about. I am not getting emotional about a stadium."

Lotte Giants manager Kim Tae-hyoung tips his cap toward the crowd after defeating the Hanwha Eagles 7-0 in a Korea Baseball Organization regular-season game at Daejeon Hanwha Life Ballpark in the central city of Daejeon on Sept. 22, 2026, in this file photo provided by the Giants. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

It provided a rare moment of levity in a season that has given Kim and the rest of the Giants little to celebrate.

Kim's three-year contract will expire after this year and the Giants are expected to go in a new direction after failing to make the postseason in all three years under Kim.

"If they wanted to keep me around beyond this year, they would have told me already," Kim said. "I guess we will find out in a couple of days."

This year, the Giants had gone 63-77-3 (wins-losses-ties) before Monday, eighth place in the 10-team Korea Baseball Organization.

"It is just disappointing overall. We did not make one postseason during my three years here. That is the frustrating part," Kim said, turning more serious. "I can sit here and talk about so many different things. But the bottom line is we just never won enough games.

"When I signed my three-year deal, I promised I would turn this team into a championship contender," Kim continued. "And I didn't get it done. I don't want to make excuses. Someone has to take the responsibility. If I had taken this group of players to the postseason, then it would have improved my own stock. But it is my responsibility as manager that I didn't get it done in my three years here."

jeeho@yna.co.kr
(END)

title: Leaders and Their Movements - Discussing Themes of Progress in World History, Sun, Oct 18, 2026, 3:00 AM   | Meetup

content:
## Details

**Dawns** is a community for history enthusiasts interested in understanding the big picture of human history.
 The way it works is that there is a different theme each month:

*   January: **the natural world** (kinship or commodity)
*   February: **industrial modernisation** (industrial revolutions 1-4)
*   March: **"the axial age"** (Moses, Buddha, Socrates, Laozi, Zoroaster)
*   April: **literary history** (oral to internet)
*   May: **energy** (from muscle to nuclear)
*   June: **different modes of living** (e.g. pastoralists, fishing)
*   July: **history of science** (Aristotle, Newton etc)
*   August: **politics and power** (tribes to superpowers)
*   September: **art history** (who and what is art for?)
*   October: **cradles of civilisation** (Egypt, Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Yellow River, Olmecs and Chico Norte)
