5年過去了，彷彿一切烽煙已經在時間中沈沒，然而有些人仍然選擇不去遺忘。

Five years have passed since Hong Konger's last attempt to maintain their freedom, and it seems that all dust has settled. However, some people still choose not to forget.

經過多方努力，我們在Yermo的自由雕塑公園（Liberty Sculpture Park）建立起了香港地，用藝術去銘記香港人的意志不滅。

After many efforts, we have established Hong Kong Corner in the Liberty Sculpture Park in Yermo, using art to remember the unyielding will of the Hong Kongers.

香港地的維護和創作需要長期的投入，我們亟需你的支持。不論捐款多少，都代表著你對香港所出的一分力。

The maintenance and creation of Yermo's "Hong Kong Corner" requires long-term investment, and we urgently need your support. Any donation, no matter the amount, represents your contribution to the undying spirit of Hong Kongers.

希望有一日我們能在自由的香港相見！

We hope to meet in a free Hong Kong someday.

捐款用途有三

Donation serves 3 main purposes.

1. 現時香港地有四件展品，沙漠氣候極端，冬寒夏焰，烈日風沙，我們要定期維修，提供防曬材料予連儂牆， 令他們可以日久維新。

1. Currently, Hong Kong Corner has four exhibits. We need to perform regular maintenance for some of the art works and provide sun & water protection sealants in the harsh desert weather condition.

2. 香港抗爭者的雕像現時沒有任何解釋。 在我們維修的過程當中，經常見到美國本地人到訪，但他們對於2019抗爭一事並不了清楚。希望可以籌款建立一塊金屬牌匾， 刻上中英文描述，令到到訪者了解究竟發生了什麼事。

2. The statues of Hong Kong Protesters currently have no explanations. During our maintenance work, we often see local Americans visiting, but they are not familiar with the 2019 protests. We hope to raise funds to establish a metal plaque with descriptions in both Chinese and English to help visitors understand what happened.

3. 自由雕塑公園的創辦人陳維明老師亦為香港地建立了新牆，我們希望可以籌款聘請來自香港的專業藝術家，以壁畫描繪出香港的景況。

3. Mr. Chen Wei Ming, the art creator of Liberty Sculpture Park, has also built a new wall for Hong Kong Land. We hope to raise funds to pay for the expenses of hiring a professional artist from Hong Kong to depict the situation in Hong Kong with a mural.

**Hillary Johnson**

# Hong Kong Photojournalism Trip

Hi everyone, my name is Hillary Johnson, and I’m a photographer living in Chicago, working all over the Midwest and in Hong Kong. I have two main threads to my photography practice, photojournalism and fine art. Though it feels awkward, I confess, I’m pushing ahead because I need your help. I’m going to Hong Kong on November 12 to cover the protest and the election of a new cabinet in Hong Kong. You might wonder why bother giving money to me or why my voice particular needs to be added to this news event, or even why this matters to you at all. I hear that and I’ll do my best to answer your questions. I’ll also explain what you can do if you’re interested in helping out. A little bit about me: in addition to being a photographer I’m also someone who studies a martial art called Ving Tsun. This art is extremely popular in Hong Kong for various reasons that I won’t go into right now but if you’re curious you can ask me and I’ll be happy to answer. It was the practice of this martial art that introduced me to my husband, Matt Johnson who runs a kung fu school here in Chicago. This martial art has a code of ethics that involves being a good citizen, being humble, promoting peace, and standing up for what is right and protecting those who need protection from bullies and so forth. I made my first trip to Hong Kong a couple of years ago and I’ve been back a few times since then. Though I’m someone who likes spend a lot of time in remote locations being quiet and letting the busyness of my mind and heart settle down, I felt 100% in love with the city of Hong Kong, it’s culture, it’s people, and of course with my kung fu family there. As a result it has been difficult watching the news and worrying about this place I love so much and the people who live there. My concern for all of this led me to do a story for the Chicago Reader. Here's a link to that: https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/photos-hong-kong-protest-freedom/Content?oid=73815391I’m extremely grateful to the reader for giving me the time and space that it did. I made all the photographs, did all the interviews, and wrote all the text with guidance from the amazing Reader staff. In the process of working on that story I began to see, that much that was going on in Hong Kong seems to not quite be making it into the news. This made me want to go to Hong Kong and do more. The stories we have been seeing her only the tip of the iceberg. I’m interested in the stories of ordinary people, their everyday life, and what they do. What are their day jobs? How do they prepare for protesting? How do they support each other in the midst of such extreme difficulty? I want to understand the impact of what’s happening in this interaction between the Beijing mainland Chinese government in the city of Hong Kong in the Hong Kong people. It’s interesting that Hong Kong has roots and connections stretching out from the city, all over the globe. While working on the story I’ve met many people here in Chicago who have a deep connections to Hong Kong. I want to go and photograph an interview to help amplify the voices of those people not being heard as much as they might be. Why do the events Hong Kong matter to you wherever you might live? Here are a few reasons: Number one. Hong Kong people are simply asking for fundamental human rights to be recognized. Number two. The Hong Kong people are asking for the promises made by the Chinese government to be kept. Number three. The Hong Kong people want their freedom. All people everywhere around the world want their fundamental human rights, they want promises to be kept and they want freedom. If we all look into our own hearts I believe we will see this truth is self evident. What’s happening in Hong Kong matters to all of us, because all of us want the same things; freedom, respect- both given and received, dignity, and agency. Further, for those of us living in other parts of the world, if we think that what’s happening in Hong Kong cannot happen to us wherever it is that we happen to live, I think if you forgive me, that view is naïve. The road to tyranny is a slippery slope. First one right is eroded, then another, then another. For this trip to Hong Kong all the groundwork is in place. Because of the network being built up over the years and as a result of my recent work, there are people on the ground in Hong Kong ready to help with making connections, translation, safety and getting around and so forth. My intention is to get to Hong Kong do my work at the photographer and then do my best to get those stories out into the world so that everyone can know what is going on. But I need help with the expenses. Here is a list: Airfare and hotel around $2100-2400 depending on flight detailsTransportation in Hong Kong When the MTR is shut down taxis may be necessary - estimating maybe $300Money to pay translators and other fixtures and facilitators estimating $300-500A laptop to process photos while I’m there so I can send them out to editors at various news outlets - around $200-300I’m hoping to raise $3500. to cover all of that as well as some of my bills while I’m away so that the lights and heat are still on when I return home. Addition I’ll provide links to news outlets as well as the story I did for the reader so that you can get more information about the situation over there. I’ll also link or attach a video that I made about the story. As things when I’m planning to offer in addition to publicly thinking everyone who supports this is the creation of a private Facebook group where I post updates photos and video from my time in Hong Kong. This content will be exclusively for anyone who supports this trip. I’m excited to announce that someone already made a first donation of $500 before even launched this campaign which let me adjust the amount needed to $3500Honestly I wasn’t even planning on doing this but so many people said to me that they wanted to support the trip and believe in the mission of supporting truth and openness and democracy, that I pushed past my own discomfort and jumped in. I want to thank all of you in advanc

title: 特习峰会上特朗普据报敦促习近平改善日中关系，但习反应冷淡

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)9月下旬与中国国家主席习近平在白宫举行的峰会已经过去多时，但是围绕此次峰会的传闻和相关报道仍然不绝于耳。

香港《南华早报》星期四(10月8日)援引消息人士的话报道说，特朗普总统在与习近平会晤时，曾敦促他改善与美国盟友日本的关系，并解除中国对日本实施的一些出口管控。

这篇受到日本媒体高度关注的报道还透露，特朗普告诉习近平，中国针对包括稀土在内的输日商品实施的出口限制，对“依赖日本供应商的美国产业”构成了威胁，并称此举“间接违反了”去年10月在韩国达成的美中贸易休战协议。

据报道，习近平对特朗普的这些呼吁和要求“反应冷淡”。他对特朗普说，北京与东京之间的争端应与美中关系分开处理，不应影响后者。习近平还警告称，“日本军国主义的风险正在上升”。

日本首相高市早苗去年11月7日在国会接受质询时表示，如果发生“台湾有事”，可能构成日本可行使集体自卫权的“存亡危机事态”，日本自卫队不排除进行武力干预。高市早苗的这番发言导致日中关系持续恶化、跌入谷底。

中国声称台湾是中国领土，并誓言将其置于自身控制之下，必要时不惜动用武力，并表示绝不容许外部势力干涉其所谓的内政。

中国政府要求东京撤回高市在国会的发言，但是遭到拒绝。日方只愿重申“政策不变”，而这无法平息北京的愤怒。中方随后逐渐加大对日本的政治和经济施压力度，包括对制造各种高科技产品所需的稀土实施贸易限制。

中国商务部将多家日本实体列为出口管制对象，禁止向它们出口任何可能用于军事用途的物资。北京还批评了高市早苗政府的扩军政策，声称日本国内“新军国主义”正在抬头。

在习近平抵达白宫进行国事访问之前，高市早苗利用前往纽约出席联合国大会的机会，抢先与特朗普总统举行了双边会晤。高市在启程赴美前曾对记者表示，她希望日美首脑会谈能够在美中首脑会谈之前举行，除了强调美日同盟的牢固之外，还能与美方就对华立场达成共识。

有分析认为，日本担心特朗普总统可能会与习近平在台湾问题上达成一项重大协议，即美国在获得经济让步的同时，默许北京在台湾问题上的部分立场。

特习峰会结束后，双方一直等到习近平回到北京，才同时发布此次白宫峰会的具体成果。成果清单中并没有提到中日关系，也没有点日本的名，但是双方都提到两国元首忆及美中“是二战盟友，并肩作战赢得战争胜利”。

蒋介石领导的中华民国政府是美国二战时的盟友，而目前日本已经成为美国在东亚最重要的盟友。分析人士认为，习近平与特朗普回忆美中二战时的盟友关系当然是为了敲打日本。美方的确也在声明中确认了中方的说法，而且措辞与中方几乎一致，这可能是特朗普安抚习近平之举，只不过美方将这一条排列在靠近末尾的位置。

分析人士认为，如果《南华早报》的报道属实，那就显示，特朗普在安抚习近平，回忆美中二战盟友关系的同时，也在帮东京的忙，那就是敦促习近平改善与日本的关系，解除对日本的出口管制。

美国之音分别联络白宫和美国国务院，寻求对特习峰会中有关日中关系讨论的评论。但是截止发稿，尚未收到白宫或国务院立即的回应。

中日关系恶化之后，东京一直在推动两国高层官员恢复交往，甚至举行双边高峰会，但是一直遭到北京的拒绝。

《南华早报》还报道说，日本曾推动高市早苗与习近平在下个月于中国南部城市深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会期间举行双边会谈，因为特朗普总统届时也将访问深圳，并在出席亚太经合组织峰会期间再次与习近平举行双边峰会。但北京拒绝了日方的这一请求。

中方仅愿意安排高市早苗与中国国务院总理李强会面，但东京表示无法接受这一安排。

新加坡南洋理工大学公共政策与全球事务副教授古贺庆(Kei Koga)接受《联合早报》采访时表示，特朗普除关注经济利益，也须顾及美国作为盟友的可信度。这也促使他在会晤习近平时寻求缓和中日紧张关系。

但他认为，特朗普推动中日对话的能力有限。北京坚持将中美与中日关系分开处理，意味着“华盛顿能与北京保持沟通，并不等于能说服中国与日本举行峰会”。

title: Russia’s Invasion Spurs PLA Casualty Evacuation Developments
summary: Executive Summary: The “life-saving chain” developed by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Joint Logistics Support Force (JLSF) to evacuate and treat casualties is part of the wider lessons it gained from observing the ongoing Russian war i
content: Executive Summary: The “life-saving chain” developed by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Joint Logistics Support Force (JLSF) to evacuate and treat casualties is part of the wider lessons it gained from observing the ongoing Russian war in Ukraine. Drones and other unmanned platforms provide the JLSF units with an increased capacity to evacuate wounded personnel to field hospitals and other medical sites for treatment. The use of intelligent equipment such as electronic casualty tags and telemedicine surgery capabilities enhances the JLSF’s ability to effectively treat wounded personnel. The JLSF’s live-saving chain would likely face some limitations, such as developing an overreliance on unmanned platforms that can be jammed, and which emit substantial electromagnetic signatures that can assist targeting. In mid-September, Chinese news outlets celebrated the 10th anniversary of the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Joint Logistics Support Force’s (JLSF) establishment. State media highlighted how the JLSF has established an integrated joint support capability over the last ten years focused on logistics, medical support, and transportation ( CCTV , September 13). It has also expanded the scope of its logistical operations, shown by various exercises that subordinate units, such as the Shenyang Joint Logistics Support Center (JLSC), conducted using drones and other intelligent equipment ( CCTV , September 13). The JLSF’s use of drones and intelligent equipment to transport and treat injured soldiers is part of a “life-saving chain” (生命救援链) ( CCTV , September 13). The PLA has developed this evacuation process for transport and care at medical facilities as part of wider lessons it gained from observing Russia’s war in Ukraine. Life-Saving Chain Employs Unmanned, Intelligent Equipment The JLSF’s life-saving chain deploys a transportation capability to evacuate wounded soldiers from the battlefield and move them to medical facilities for treatment. The JLSF developed these tactics and procedures to retrieve and treat casualties by leveraging various drones and intelligent equipment, which enhances the effectiveness of evacuations ( CCTV , September 13; China Brief , September 15). Heavy use of unmanned platforms in the chain is also a response to the increased presence of loitering munitions, precision guided munitions, first-person view (FPV) drones, and sensors that now exist on the battlefield. Drones and sensors introduce new risks for medical and support personnel when completing missions behind the frontlines. The PLA views the use of drones to evacuate wounded soldiers as a solution to this obstacle. Tracked and wheeled unmanned ground vehicles (UGV) would have the ability to transport casualties from the frontlines to medical sites located in the rear; robot wolves and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) would conduct searches for injured personnel and deliver medical supplies on the battlefield as they wait for evacuation ( Xinhua , September 12). Drones would also conduct resupply missions to deliver medical supplies to medics stationed with frontline units. These auxiliary missions would increase soldiers’ chances of survival as they wait for UGVs and unmanned helicopters to bring them to aid stations and other frontline medical facilities ( CCTV , September 13). Drones would also be used as supplementary transport to move casualties for follow-on treatment at medical sites with more substantial resources. Casualty tracking and remote treatment are the successive stages of the JLSF’s life-saving chain. The chain uses intelligent equipment such as “wearable smart monitoring systems” (可穿戴智能监护系统), which would allow medical staff to rapidly examine a soldier’s vital signs during the triage and treatment processes ( CCTV , September 13). It also used improved “dynamic electronic casualty tags” (动态电子伤票) to provide enhanced care for wounded troops ( CCTV, September 13). These tags would enable medics to input personal data, injuries, treatments, and other information about casualties, likely using an improved interface compared to the second-generation system. They would also prevent doctors and nurses from administering redundant treatments or tests. Past iterations allowed medical staff to rapidly access the medical history of injured personnel ( PLA Daily , June 9, 2009). The system can likely sync with existing electronic casualty tags to continuously upload medical information. Medical staff would also leverage the PLA’s “military-wide telemedicine information network” (全军远程医学信息网) built upon “5G-plus dedicated long-range Internet line communications technology” (5G+互联网专线远程通信技术) to provide enhanced medical care by remotely conducting surgeries and other procedures at field hospitals and frontlines ( The Paper , September 11; CCTV , September 13). Conclusion The life-saving chain enhances JLSF evacuation capabilities by providing the branch with the ability to move casualties from the frontlines to receive treatment at field hospitals. Its employment of unmanned platforms and intelligent equipment in the evacuation process enables the PLA to increase the survivability of its troops by reducing the threat posed by FPV drones, loitering munitions, and sensors. Drones would also increase the survivability of troops by providing them with additional medical supplies as they wait for UGVs and unmanned platforms to evacuate them from the battlefield. Intelligent equipment, such as the smart monitoring systems and electronic casualty tags, would complement drone evacuations by enabling medical personnel to effectively continue treating the wounded soldiers. The chain would be employed at the tactical level by individual brigades to enable their medical units to play a role in the wider process. The life-saving chain would likely have limitations that decrease its ability to evacuate and care for casualties from the frontlines. One limitation is the potential for drones to be jammed or disabled using electronic warfare techniques. This vulnerability would prevent targeted drones from conducting evacuation operations. Another is that the heavy electromagnetic signatures that drones and intelligent equipment emit could be used by enemy forces to locate field hospitals and other medical sites. This information would be used to locate frontline positions and other viable military sites for targeting by artillery, long-range missiles, and other stand-off weapons. The post Russia’s Invasion Spurs PLA Casualty Evacuation Developments appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Missing the Forest for the Trees in Taiwan’s Defense Preparations
source: 害怕军事上软弱的中国——外交官
summary: In recent years, Taiwan’s military issues have received considerable discussion, from changes in Taiwan’s annual large-scale [Han Kuang exercises](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/han-kuang-42-learning-to-fight-after-things-go-wrong/)to [
content:
In recent years, Taiwan’s military issues have received considerable discussion, from changes in Taiwan’s annual large-scale [Han Kuang exercises](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/han-kuang-42-learning-to-fight-after-things-go-wrong/)to [recommendations on equipment procurement](https://www.cnas.org/publications/reports/hellscape-for-taiwan). These are all quite important areas of change, but the most core issue seems to have received much less discussion: how exactly the Taiwan military may fight. The aforementioned changes in exercises and equipment procurement, in the end, are all meant to serve the kind of war Taiwan is prepared to fight. Taiwan has had some developments in this area that have received limited attention and discussion, but their importance is definitely no less than the developments in exercises and equipment.

The key is to comprehensively understand Taiwan’s efforts and preparations from the strategic level, using what the Taiwan military most often says about what kind of war to fight, what equipment to have, what kind of force structure is needed, and what training to conduct. Taiwan has moved from its past concepts of defeating the enemy on the opposite shore or seeking a decisive battle in the littoral area to actually carrying out an erosion strategy and sustained operations in recent years. To that end, Taiwan has continued to strengthen the army’s active-duty combat power in the northern region to build a layered defensive network and regional force superiority. Meanwhile, the cumulative duration of large-scale exercises in 2026 has already accumulated to nearly one month. There is also something that many people might have noticed but not realized: the significant expansion of Taiwan’s navy in recent years.

At the same time, these developments also bring out the current difficulties Taiwan faces in joint operations across the services. This is one of the most critical areas to watch in Taiwan’s future defense development. In recent years, experts have paid considerable attention to the Taiwan military’s efforts toward decentralization, but in practice, joint command and control is the key to whether Taiwan’s combat capability can be improved.

**Further Concentration of Forces in Northern Taiwan**

The key to an erosion strategy and sustained operations is to delay and strike enemy forces through layered forces. Although Taiwan emphasizes decentralized command and control, this means emphasizing that a single operational unit can continue to carry out assigned actions based on higher-level operational objectives when command and control is disrupted. In terms of military operations, strategically concentrating forces to make it difficult for the enemy to break through and advance is quite important. And this is also what Taiwan is doing.

Northern Taiwan is where the political center is located, and it also concentrates important operational command organizations and transportation hubs. More than one-third of Taiwan’s population lives there. More than about half of the Taiwan active-duty brigade-level forces of the Republic of China (ROC) Army and Marine Corps are normally stationed in the northern region (north of Miaoli and Yilan), including the main combat forces, [combined arms brigades](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/4939409), Army Aviation units, and Marine Corps forces.

In particular, in recent years Taiwan has continued during exercises to additionally move units from other regions into the northern region to conduct reinforcement missions. This makes the forces concentrated in the northern region possibly reach nearly two-thirds of Taiwan’s active-duty ground forces. During the 2025 Han Kuang Exercise, the main reinforcement was carried out by units from the Marine Corps 99th Brigade moving north from southern Taiwan to reinforce Taoyuan and the greater Taipei area. The [2026 Han Kuang Exercise](https://www.storm.mg/article/11154520) further expanded the reinforcement forces, including forces under the Marine Corps 99th Brigade and Army 564th Combined Arms Brigade from southern Taiwan, and the Army 586th Combined Arms Brigade from central Taiwan, which moved and deployed to the northern region.

Map by K. Tristan Tang and H. Rion Wu based on information collected and compiled from Military News Agency and Liberty Times.

This kind of deployment and training concentrates forces in northern Taiwan and is, to a considerable degree, a focus of Taiwan’s current sustained defensive operations. In September 2026, during the ROC Army’s annual large-scale Lu Sheng exercise, Maj. Gen. Lin Shih-wei, deputy commander of the Army Education, Training, and Doctrine Development Command, clearly stated at a press conference that this exercise was centered on the concept of successive resistance and sustained operations under Chief of the General Staff [Admiral Mei Chia-shu’s erosion strategy](https://www.mnd.gov.tw/en/Publication/87871). Most importantly, the exercise area was changed to northern Taiwan in order to conform with the focus on defensive operations and allow troops to become familiar with key terrain in the area of operations and the deployment and employment of troops and firepower.

**Nearly One Month of Large-Scale Military Exercises**

Another development deserving more attention is that in recent years the Taiwan military has begun extending the training duration of various live-force exercises. In addition to extending existing exercises such as the nationwide Han Kuang exercise and the brigade-level Lu Sheng exercise, it has also added [several large-scale exercises](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5486834).

The accumulated time of these military exercises has led the Taiwan military this year to spend almost an entire month participating in various live-force exercises, far more than in the past few years. This includes the five-day [Immediate Combat Readiness Exercise](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5479192) in June, the five-day [Joint Defense Exercise](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5510468) in July, the 10-day [Han Kuang Exercise](https://udn.com/news/story/10930/9692402) in August, and the 10-day [Lu Sheng Exercise](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202609060058.aspx) expected in October.

Besides allowing units to have more time to complete continuous training events that could not be conducted in the past, this also allows participating units to become familiar with scenarios related to long-duration sustained operations during a future Taiwan conflict. The longer training and exercise duration allows units to validate operations under prolonged combat scenarios, as well as the maintenance of combat capability and [coordination with civilian sectors](https://www.ey.gov.tw/Page/448DE008087A1971/ba09b5ff-9d3b-4eb4-b778-2b401f20cc7d) in the use of civilian resources, including manpower and material mobilization.

**Taiwanese Navy’s Expanded Mission**

Another aspect worth attention in recent years is that the ROC Navy has been playing more and more roles in Taiwan’s current defensive operations. In the past, the Taiwan government mainly planned naval units in wartime as [fleet task forces](https://www.mnd.gov.tw/NewUpload/%E6%AD%B7%E5%B9%B4%E5%9C%8B%E9%98%B2%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A%E6%9B%B8%E7%B6%B2%E9%A0%81%E5%B0%88%E5%8D%80/%E6%AD%B7%E5%B9%B4%E5%9C%8B%E9%98%B2%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A%E6%9B%B8%E5%B0%88%E5%8D%80.files/%E5%9C%8B%E9%98%B2%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A%E6%9B%B8-98/%E5%9C%8B%E9%98%B2%E5%A0%B1%E5%91%8A%E6%9B%B8-98-%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87.pdf). In recent years, there have been three notable changes.

First, the Marine Corps under the Navy has undergone a major transformation in recent years, shifting from a force responsible for offensive amphibious operations and power projection in the past to a defensive force for urban areas. In recent years, Taiwan’s Marine Corps has gradually given up its tanks and self-propelled artillery[in favor of drones and anti-tank equipment](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5503669). As the [strategic reserve](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5111857) directly under the General Staff Headquarters, the Marine Corps has been deployed to the Taipei area, with its mission shifting to become a defensive force for [the capital garrison area](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202503210321.aspx).

Second, the ROC Navy this year established a new [Coastal Operations Command](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5532902) within the service. Its commander holds the same vice admiral rank as the Fleet Command commander, and it integrates units related to shore-based anti-ship missiles, shore-based radar, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), and unmanned aerial systems, with the goal of establishing a coastal operations system across units and platforms.

Third, Taiwan’s Coast Guard this year added [one new deputy director-general position](https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/politics/paper/1741878), and in late September formally appointed [a vice admiral](https://www.president.gov.tw/NEWS/40387) from the Navy to the position. The purpose is to bring the Navy’s tactical thinking into the Coast Guard, inject key new momentum into the Coast Guard’s transition from peacetime to wartime, effectively connect communication channels between the military and Coast Guard, and deepen joint maritime-air defense and response mechanisms.

In addition, Taiwan’s Coast Guard has also begun, during the military’s annual exercises, to expand training events related to [the transition from peacetime to wartime](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5533323), allowing its Coast Guard vessels to undertake part of the sea-denial strike missions during wartime. Specifically, this year’s Han Kuang exercise had the Coast Guard conduct exercises under [the control of the Navy’s Coastal Operations Command](https://def.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5532902).

These changes all show that the ROC Navy is playing an increasingly important role in Taiwan’s current defensive operations. This includes sea denial and coastal operations, and also includes the capital garrison mission during the defense-in-depth phase.

**Policy Implications**

Taiwan’s current defense preparations are not only changes in concepts and efforts in equipment procurement, but have also seen quite significant developments in military training and deployment validation. More importantly, as the relatively weaker side in the cross-strait military balance, Taiwan must necessarily concentrate its resources to a greater degree and use them more efficiently. Therefore, we can also notice that there is now more Navy involvement in maritime and coastal denial operations, and even in the land-based attrition strategy and the defense-in-depth phase. The Coast Guard is also practicing the transition from peacetime to wartime,

But at the same time, these changes also point to a more critical area to observe in the future, which is whether Taiwan’s joint operations across the services, especially its command and control preparations, are in place. In the past, land operations were usually considered something for the Army to handle by itself. In a hypothetical scenario where the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) would be able to conduct an amphibious assault on Taiwan and then offload follow-on forces, it was typically assumed to mean that Taiwan’s air and naval combat power had already been largely paralyzed, while China had air and sea superiority. Now, this situation has changed to a considerable degree. Navy shore-based units and Air Force air defense units will also play important roles during the defense-in-depth phase, and therefore preparations for joint operations become quite important.

The first question mark is the joint command and control capability under the concentration of large numbers of forces, including Army and Navy forces concentrated in the northern region, as well as Ai

title: America’s Defense Industrial Base Begins at the Mine
source: Small Wars Journal by Arizona State Univ
summary: Abstract The U.S. defense industrial base depends not only on the factories that produce weapons, but also on the mines, refineries, supply chains, and corporate structures that provide their critical inputs. This article examines how China
content: Abstract The U.S. defense industrial base depends not only on the factories that produce weapons, but also on the mines, refineries, supply chains, and corporate structures that provide their critical inputs. This article examines how China’s position in critical minerals creates strategic dependencies for the United States, focusing on cobalt, copper, rare earth elements, and other materials essential to defense production. It argues that supply-chain security cannot be assessed solely by the geographic location of mines or refineries. Ownership, financing, governance rights, offtake agreements, and the potential for future changes in corporate control can also shape who ultimately influences strategically important assets. Drawing on several recent cases, the article illustrates how these vulnerabilities can affect U.S. supply-chain security, and outlines a strategy combining domestic production with allied supply chains and government-backed financing. Confronted by significant bottlenecks , the U.S. faces a sobering reality: The military power that has for so long underpinned its global leadership only obtains its robustness insofar as the defense industrial base is capable of replenishing it. One notable vulnerability arises in the procurement of aircraft parts, missiles, drones, radars, satellites, precision-guided systems, batteries, and communications networks. These necessary components of the military supply chain have a strict reliance on critical raw materials that are concentrated in a few localities around the globe, and are difficult to substitute. Turning traditional strategic considerations in the defense industry upside down, an adversary may no longer have to defeat superior American weapons systems to gain victory. Disrupting the supply chains in service of the U.S.’s defense industrial base – potentially at as early a stage as extraction – would prove sufficient. This is something that China has understood for years. The best evidence for this is its robust mining, processing and refining infrastructure , which Beijing has supplemented with reliable sourcing partnerships and other minerals projects abroad. China controls between 60% and 90% of the production of most key materials essential for defense, renewable energy and modern computer technology worldwide. This advantage is not simply the result of competitiveness, but emerged in large part due to the symbiotic relationship between China’s state-capital system , its industrial leaders and its national strategic objectives. The lesson for Washington should be clear: access to resources is just as critical as securing the industrial capacity and corporate structures that are capable of turning those resources into the strategic capabilities the U.S. military relies on. A good example of securing a controlling interest in both mining and refining in the cobalt and copper supply chains is provided by the commercial relationship between China and the Democratic Republic of Congo. On one side of the relationship, CMOC Group Limited (formerly called China Molybdenum) acquired an 80% ownership stake in the DRC’s Tenke Fungurume Mining copper-cobalt project, which makes up roughly 38% of global cobalt production. Simultaneously, on China’s side, significant processing capabilities were developed at home. China now refines more than 79% of the world’s cobalt. This one supply chain alone creates significant dependencies for the U.S. in a number of strategic sectors. Cobalt is used in the production of lithium-ion batteries that power electric vehicles, drones and other energy-storage systems. It is also an integral part of the superalloys used in jet engines and other high-performance aerospace applications. Disruption to cobalt supplies in the defense sector in particular would negatively impact the production of batteries, aircraft engines, missiles and other military systems that depend on these materials. While Washington has increasingly tried to expand its domestic mining and refining capabilities, and worked with allies including Japan, Australia and South Korea to build “friend-shored” supply chains diversified away from China, another challenge is the ownership and control structures of strategically important companies. A characteristic of modern capital markets has made national security screening more difficult. U.S. mechanisms are generally adept at asking whether a strategic asset is controlled by China, but less experienced in uncovering private-equity structures, financing by multiple institutional investors, and the consequential differences between ownership and control over the operations of firms. The absence of apparent direct Chinese ownership no longer guarantees the lack of Chinese influence in a trade or joint venture relationship. The attempted acquisition of Lattice Semiconductor illustrates this risk. In 2016, U.S.-based private equity fund Canyon Bridge agreed to acquire the U.S. chipmaker for $1.3 billion. Its sole investor was a unit of China Venture Capital Fund, whose funding was ultimately traced to China’s State Council. In September 2017, President Trump blocked the deal following a CFIUS recommendation, citing the Chinese government’s role in the transaction and the potential transfer of semiconductor technology. The recent and ongoing battle of corporate control over Korea Zinc may be another example. Korea Zinc produces strategically important minerals including zinc, lead, copper, and a range of other non-ferrous and strategic metals, including indium, bismuth, and antimony. To strengthen American critical minerals supply, the U.S. government and Korea Zinc formed a joint venture under the name Crucible Zinc Inc., specifically to decrease America’s reliance on Chinese refining. The Department of Defense took a significant stake in the $7.4 billion smelter project in Tennessee, and the federal government also backed the project with a direct grant under the CHIPS and Science Act. While Washington and Korea Zinc’s leadership under Chairman Choi are trying to build a more resilient Western and allied supply chain, the company has become embroiled in a prolonged battle for control. The Young Poong Group and the Jang family that leads it have maintained a shared governance model with the Chois for decades – an agreement that collapsed only in recent years. This may have been an opening for China. In 2024, Young Poong officially partnered with private equity firm MBK Partners and launched a bid for Korea Zinc shares. MBK Partners’ explicit focus on the Chinese market and their history of mutual investments – with MBK acquiring China’s largest car rental firm, CAR Inc. and China’s sovereign wealth fund, the China Investment Corporation contributing to MBK’s sixth buyout fund – deserve scrutiny. As part of the broader control battle, the MBK-Young Poong alliance has been presenting itself as America’s operational partner for Crucible after unsuccessfully opposing the project in the Korean court on the grounds that it puts Korea’s national core technology under U.S. influence. The Crucible JV holds a 10% stake in Korea Zinc that currently supports the incumbent management; securing that stake’s support would significantly boost the alliance’s takeover attempt. Thus, in the context of Korea Zinc’s control, Washington should carefully examine the financial and corporate networks that can determine who supplies capital, owns governance rights and makes decisions in the future, especially when these maintain direct connections to the Chinese government and Chinese state capital. The defense industry’s reliance on rare earth mining far exceeds only Korea Zinc’s promised importance in the refining of gallium, germanium, and antimony. Rare Earth Elements (REEs) are also essential components of virtually all defense-related products. The transaction between China’s Shenghe Resources , Australia’s Peak Rare Earths and the Ngualla project in Tanzania presents a case in which a single mining deal could lock up the operations of an entire critical mineral supply chain from mine to market. Shenghe has become Peak’s largest shareholder with a nearly 20% stake in the company while also securing a 100% offtake agreement for all rare earths produced at Ngualla. This strategic positioning has essentially created a fully integrated, China-centric pipeline for the production of certain REEs. China’s success in critical minerals demonstrates that supply chain security cannot be measured by where a mine or refinery is located. A resource deposit in an allied country can still feed a China-centric supply chain if Chinese firms control the offtake, processing, financing or key corporate decisions. Similar restrictions may arise from a refinery being built on American soil. Washington therefore needs to complement its push for domestic production and “friend-shoring” with a more rigorous concept of trusted control. This approach could examine ultimate beneficial ownership, financing, governance rights, offtake agreements and the possibility of future changes in control. Shutting out allied or private capital is not necessary, but it requires attention paid to who has the ability to influence the assets which American military power depends on. The defense industrial base does not begin at the weapons factory. It reaches back to the refinery, the mine and, increasingly, the shareholder register. A more resilient strategy would see a strategic combination of reliable domestic production, coupled with a network of allied supply chains. Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom are all partners with access to vast mining resources alongside processing and refining knowledge. Continued support from government-backed financing and long-term offtake agreements would facilitate the creation of strategic stockpiles, giving producers a certainty they sorely lack today, and allowing them to develop projects which they otherwise would not be able to manifest in competition with Chinese-backed capital. Washington has a range of issues which it must also address at home, including the impact of lengthy permitting delays, high capital costs and limited downstream processing capacity. Enabling the production of more minerals is an easy policy solution to argue for, however the United States needs to build alternative capacity across the entire chain. The tremendous scope of American defense procurement would guarantee ongoing demand for strategically important materials. This could potentially create a a supply chain in where no single foreign government or company could control the critical link between mine and military product. Friend-shoring is thus an integral part of this process. “Friendly” however, means more than simply the flag under which a mine or refinery operates; we must also account for who owns the asset, who finances it, who controls its output. This necessarily impacts who has the ability to disrupt the supply chain. The post America’s Defense Industrial Base Begins at the Mine appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

title: 「沒有國慶，只有國殤」——中共建政77週年 各族群齊聚阿姆斯特丹水壩廣場抗議
summary: （荷蘭反共之聲・阿姆斯特丹報道）2026年10月3日（星期六）下午1時至3時，約百名在荷蘭的西藏人、維吾爾人、南蒙古人、滿洲人、廣東人、晉蘭人代表，以及中國異見人士、家庭教會及全能神教會基督徒，在阿姆斯特丹水壩廣場舉行聯合集會，抗議中共建政77週年。集會由荷蘭西藏支持小組（Tibet Support Group NL）、支持維吾爾人基金會（Stichting Support Uyghurs）及荷蘭反共之聲聯合主辦。 一條橫幅，七面旗幟 主辦方荷蘭西藏支持小組租用了一輛6米長
content: （荷蘭反共之聲・阿姆斯特丹報道）2026年10月3日（星期六）下午1時至3時，約百名在荷蘭的西藏人、維吾爾人、南蒙古人、滿洲人、廣東人、晉蘭人代表，以及中國異見人士、家庭教會及全能神教會基督徒，在阿姆斯特丹水壩廣場舉行聯合集會，抗議中共建政77週年。集會由荷蘭西藏支持小組（Tibet Support Group NL）、支持維吾爾人基金會（Stichting Support Uyghurs）及荷蘭反共之聲聯合主辦。 一條橫幅，七面旗幟 主辦方荷蘭西藏支持小組租用了一輛6米長的流動舞台車，車下懸掛同樣長6米的橫幅，寫著「沒有國慶 只有國殤 1949-2026 Oct 1st, it is NOT our National Day」。現場飄揚著西藏雪山獅子旗、東突厥斯坦藍色星月旗、香港光時旗、南粵獨立旗、台灣獨立旗、滿洲旗及晉蘭旗。廣場地面鋪開一排海報，展示中共建黨以來造成的人道災難；全能神教會的基督徒則手持教會旗幟、遇難信徒的照片和資料，以及要求停止宗教迫害的標語牌。法輪功學員亦在廣場另一側同場表達訴求。 白玫瑰與哈達 集會由藏人次仁強巴（Tsering Jampa）主持開場。她強調，今天大家團結在一起，反對的不是中國人民，而是中國共產黨和習近平領導層。她指出，西藏在1950年遭解放軍入侵，東突厥斯坦和南蒙古亦有相同遭遇；兩天前中共在天安門大張旗鼓閱兵慶祝，但對西藏人、維吾爾人、南蒙古人和香港人而言，10月1日不是慶典，而是哀悼日。她亦提到，西藏被稱為「亞洲水塔」，亞洲五大河流均發源於此，中共在西藏修建水壩、濫用水資源，影響的是下游數以百萬計的人。 隨後，格西桑丹（Geshe Samten）為世界和平誦經祈禱，全場默哀兩分鐘，悼念所有在中共統治下受苦和罹難的人。主辦方準備了30支白玫瑰和白色哈達，次仁強巴率先將玫瑰與哈達放在台前的椅子上，參與者隨後逐一上前獻花，緬懷1921年以來的中共受害者。 各族代表輪番發言 粵國獨立黨代表劉飛龍以荷蘭語發言。他說自己已流亡五年，流亡讓人失去家園、家人和母語，卻失去不了聲音。他表示中共壓迫的不只是邊疆民族，而是所有想要自由的人，並聲援台灣：「你們可以佔領我們的土地、禁止我們的語言、關閉我們的教堂，但永遠摧毀不了我們追求自由的意志。」 支持維吾爾人基金會主席阿布都熱依木·艾尼（Abdurehim Gheni）指出，數以百萬計的維吾爾人和其他突厥民族正被關押在集中營、強迫勞動設施和監獄中，家庭被拆散，婦女被強制絕育。他表示，今年7月1日生效的所謂「民族團結進步」法律，試圖為中共把鎮壓延伸到境外提供法律框架，以挾持海外流亡者國內親屬等手段壓制自由的聲音。他警告國際社會，中共的擴張政策不會止步於被佔領的民族，呼籲各民主國家不要沉默。 歐洲東突厥斯坦教育協會主席阿布力卡斯木·阿布都阿齊茲（Abulqasim Abdulaziz）回顧，1949年10月1日是東突厥斯坦歷史的轉折點，1955年故土被北京更名為「新疆」，意即「新的疆土」。他說，今天維吾爾青年被送往內地工廠強迫勞動，兒童被關進寄宿學校同化，但他們從未放棄希望，終將重建獨立的東突厥斯坦。 南蒙古大會駐荷蘭代表額勒貝勒圖·孛兒只斤（Elbereltu Borjigin）說，77年前的10月1日，標誌的不是一個國家的誕生，而是人民深重苦難的開始。他歷數大躍進、大饑荒、文化大革命和三年嚴苛的疫情封控，指南蒙古在文革中是受打擊最嚴重的地區之一，如今大規模稀土開採又令草原和水源遭到毀滅性破壞。他呼籲國際社會依國際法追究中共官員的責任。 滿洲人代表江虹表示，中共建政後，滿洲淪為「資源殖民地」，煤礦被挖空、森林被砍光，資源耗盡後又被拋棄成為「鐵鏽地帶」，年輕人背井離鄉，語言文化瀕臨滅絕。她環顧廣場上的各族旗幟說，大家的苦難相通，敵人是同一個，並帶領全場高呼「拒絕極權，團結抗爭」「獨裁必亡，自由必勝」。 全能神教會基督徒代表侯永傑引述該教會2025年度迫害報告的不完全統計稱，僅2025年就有至少19,191名信徒被抓捕，2,291人被判刑，至少23人被迫害致死，被捕者中年紀最大的93歲。他說，即使逃到海外，信徒仍面對監視、跟蹤和國內家屬被施壓：「一個人到底要逃到哪裡，才能真正擁有自由？」 來自河南的流亡基督徒王群濤、孫心愛夫婦亦先後發言。王群濤說，從大饑荒、文革到六四，再到今天的西藏、新疆和香港，這個政權雙手沾滿同胞鮮血，「中共不等於中國人，暴政不等於國家」。孫心愛則講述各地十字架被拆、家庭教會被查封的情況，並提到成都秋雨聖約教會牧師王怡被判刑九年。她說，所謂宗教「中國化」，實質是要信仰服從政黨，「良心不能被登記，也不能被審批」。 「每一分每一秒都重要」 集會尾聲，次仁強巴總結說，在場者民族、語言、文化和宗教各不相同，但可以共同做到一件事，就是團結。她表示，藏人在達賴喇嘛尊者領導下，七十多年來一直尋求以非暴力和對話解決漢藏衝突，雖未成功，但絕不放棄。她呼籲路過的市民主動去了解西藏、東突厥斯坦和南蒙古的處境，並代表各地被關押的政治犯，感謝在場者記住他們。 西藏國民大會黨成員仁增（Rinzin）最後上台，呼籲各族不要只在集會時聚在一起、回家後便停下來，派傳單、向身邊人講述自己的故事同樣重要，「如果你是自由戰士，每一分每一秒都重要」。 集會在「Bhö Gyalo（西藏必勝）」「自由西藏」「自由東突厥斯坦」「自由南蒙古」「自由廣東」的口號聲中結束。 （文／荷蘭反共之聲 攝影／江培坤） 更多現場圖片：

title: The Card Congress Can Still Play on the Iran War
source: 个人自由、自由市场与和平
summary: Katherine Thompson President Trump wants Congress to deliver both a $1.5 trillion defense budget and emergency funding for the Iran war this year. As the midterms loom, Congress shows no appetite to give the president what he wants. Members
content: Katherine Thompson President Trump wants Congress to deliver both a $1.5 trillion defense budget and emergency funding for the Iran war this year. As the midterms loom, Congress shows no appetite to give the president what he wants. Members from both sides of the aisle continue to raise concerns about  munitions shortages , the war’s  objectives and expected length , and the effect on readiness for deterring China.  In most areas of national security policy, Congress has ceded its powers and prerogatives to the president. But its most powerful card, control of the nation’s budget, remains intact and available. Through the power of the purse, Congress holds leverage to limit the president’s prosecution of the Iran war and course-correct the strategic trajectory of the United States. The time to play the ace is right now, before course correction is no longer an option. Recent reports from the  Congressional Budget Office (CBO) and the  Department of Defense (DoD) Inspector General (IG) paint a grim picture of the consequences the US now faces because of the Iran war. CBO pegs the overall cost of the war thus far at $38 billion. Even more jarring, CBO estimates that if the conflict continues even at a low intensity, the US is still staring down the barrel of a minimum of $2 billion a month. The Trump administration’s pressure on Congress for supplemental funding is only going to increase as  operations and maintenance accounts, currently being used to pay the bills, run dry.  An additional  $67 billion in emergency funding for the war, on top of the president’s desired $1.5 trillion defense budget, is a tough sell. Most Americans believe the war is not making the US safer and feel the “America First” president is trading away affordability promises for overseas adventurism.  Proponents of both spending measures argue moving them through without delay is necessary to support US forces in the field. However, Congress always retains the option to scale down the requests and pass funds for personnel and other immediate needs without rubber-stamping full multi-billion-dollar packages. Congress, just a few weeks out from the midterm elections, cannot afford to be out of step with constituents by cutting large checks for an endless war with no accountability.  Cost is one layer of consideration for Congress. Strategy should be another. The president’s  National Defense Strategy puts deterring a conflict with China as the nation’s top security priority outside of defending US borders. Soon, the US may lack the resources to keep deterrence on the table as a credible option.  Resource decisions for the Iran war today undercut US strategy in the Pacific tomorrow.  CBO’s analysis revealed the US is facing a critical munitions “shortfall” for the next several years, and the opportunity cost that comes with the shortage hits readiness in the Pacific the hardest. Recently,  Secretary Rubio justified delays in arms sales to Taiwan due to more urgent US needs.  The DoD’s IG report on Operation Epic Fury noted that since the war began, “six warships were re-tasked from the Pacific to the Middle East.” Earlier this year,  testimony from Pacific Command officials also confirmed munitions and some critical system components were also moved from the Pacific to the Middle East. The report also highlighted that between January and June of this year, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE received high-value munitions and system parts, including for the Patriot and THAAD systems, from the United States. Most of these “emergency” sales bypassed congressional review entirely. Using the Pacific as the bill payer for war in the Middle East, and the risks to readiness incurred as a consequence, deserve significant scrutiny from Congress.  Members of Congress from both parties struggle to accept that limits exist on America’s military resources. It is easier to reach for quick fixes like emergency funding, larger defense budgets, or avoiding strategy debates entirely. However, the colossal costs and strategic implications of the Iran war are too big to ignore. After the midterms, the pressure from the current administration is going to be overwhelming to massively increase the defense coffers. Congress can and should resist. Safeguards for protecting munitions, alignment and protection of U.S. strategic aims in the Pacific, and reporting requirements on the administration to outline an end to the Iran war should all be on the table before any funding measure can move forward.  By asserting its prerogative over the nation’s purse, Congress can put America’s defense dollars back in line with an America First defense strategy.

title: 雪铁龙复兴 2CV，以迎接电动时代
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 法国汽车制造商雪铁龙（Citroen）推出了其 2CV 品牌，旨在在充满挑战的市场中提升电动汽车的销量。 这款新车型于巴黎车展亮相，是一款具有复古风格的小型城市用车，灵感源自该公司最著名的设计之一。 作为一款旨在展示雪铁龙未来方向的“概念车”，它目前尚未准备上市，但计划于 2028 年在展厅推出相应版本。 面对来自中国制造商的日益激烈的竞争，雪铁龙和其他欧洲品牌正利用其历史遗产作为销售现代汽车的手段。 农民的最爱 雪铁龙首席执行官 Xavier Chardon 将这款新车描述
content: 法国汽车制造商雪铁龙（Citroen）推出了其 2CV 品牌，旨在在充满挑战的市场中提升电动汽车的销量。 这款新车型于巴黎车展亮相，是一款具有复古风格的小型城市用车，灵感源自该公司最著名的设计之一。 作为一款旨在展示雪铁龙未来方向的“概念车”，它目前尚未准备上市，但计划于 2028 年在展厅推出相应版本。 面对来自中国制造商的日益激烈的竞争，雪铁龙和其他欧洲品牌正利用其历史遗产作为销售现代汽车的手段。 农民的最爱 雪铁龙首席执行官 Xavier Chardon 将这款新车描述为“对明日出行挑战的一种现代、巧妙且令人耳目一新的回应”。 最初的雪铁龙 2CV 于 1948 年推出，当时欧洲正从第二次世界大战的破坏中恢复。它被设计成一种廉价、坚固的方式，让法国农民和乡村居民出行。 该车拥有高轮拱和软悬挂，使其能够穿越犁过的田野或崎岖的道路——正如传说所说，而不会弄碎一盘鸭蛋。 其高车顶让驾驶员可以在驾驶座上戴帽子。它易于驾驶，且维修简单。 该车如此受欢迎，生产时间超过 40 年。随着时间的推移，它从一种乡村实用工具演变为一种 cult classic（ cult 经典），并成为嬉皮士和反文化人士的最爱。 雪铁龙 2CV 的粉丝每年都会举办此类聚会，例如这次在瑞士德莱蒙特的泥泞集会 现在，雪铁龙希望利用这一遗产来销售一款预计售价约为 13,000 英镑的电动小型城市车。 新 2CV 的外观可能会随着雪铁龙设计的发展而演变。但就目前而言，它与著名的前身共享了许多设计特征。 高外扩的轮拱、高耸弯曲的车顶以及类似眼睛的前大灯，都是对原始”deux chevaux”（即”两匹马”）的提醒。 通过利用旧车的记忆来销售新车，雪铁龙正在走一条被广泛验证的道路。 VW 在 20 世纪 90 年代末曾试图重新推出甲壳虫，但效果有限。 BMW 的 Minis 一直保留着致敬非常英国原版的设计。Fiat 在过去二十多年里一直销售具有复古风格的 Fiat 500。 复古怀旧 但近年来，复古怀旧趋势正在加速，因为汽车制造商正在寻找向怀疑的消费者销售电动汽车的方法。 雪铁龙的法国竞争对手雷诺（Renault）一直走在前列。它始于 Renault 5 E-Tech，其外观呼应了原始 Renault 5 独特的方盒子风格，后者曾是法国街道上随处可见的景象。此后，它还复兴了 Renault 4 和 Twingo 品牌。 VW 拥有独特的 ID-Buzz 小型货车，这是对经典 T2 Transporter 的致敬，而 Ford 正在开发一款新电动车，普遍预期将被命名为 Fiesta。 Autocar 杂志高级编辑 Rachel Burgess 认为这是一种完全合理的策略。 “它是一款与全新汽车品牌截然不同的亮点，”她说。“年长一点的受众可能会记得原版并对其感到亲切，而年轻一点的受众可能会发现复古方面的吸引力。” 在面临来自中国品牌日益增长竞争的同时，寻找新的方法来使汽车更具吸引力变得比以往任何时候都更重要。 “行业中的许多人认为，欧洲的主要汽车制造商……正面临来自中国激进制造商的非常严重的生存威胁，”Global Data 汽车编辑 David Leggett 说道。 回到未来：VW 在设计其 ID-Buzz 小型货车时借鉴了过去 在这种充满敌意的商业环境中，历史遗产和怀旧情绪可能会成为老牌品牌的强大武器，汽车研究者和作者 Dr Paul Nieuwenhuis 认为。 “在一个可信、质量良好的中国电动车涌入欧洲的世界里，将欧洲设计与其历史联系起来，同时使用最新的动力总成技术，是中国人无法做到的，”他说。 “中国人可以建立新的设计趋势，但那里缺乏历史。” 但 Leggett 认为，雪铁龙需要更多的怀旧气息才能将其新车打造成畅销车。 “重新构想的雪铁龙 2CV 应该向其祖先致以崇高的敬意——特别是在价格和设计的简单性方面，以及视觉线索方面，”他说。 “但它也必须是一款在功能和功能方面可信的现代电动车，具有广泛的吸引力。”

title: 中国篮球小将逾期滞留两年，在机场被 ICE 逮捕，DHS 确认其已接受自愿离境
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 密西西比河谷州立大学（Mississippi Valley State University）一名来自中国的篮球运动员庞清方，因涉嫌签证过期被美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）拘留，目前仍关在路易斯安那州。 律师表示，庞清方从高中开始就在美国读书，后来进入大学篮球队，他自己都不知道签证过期了。目前正在申请紧急保释听证会，希望恢复学生签证，以便回校继续打球。 官方记录显示，庞清方身高6英尺9英寸（约2.06米）。高中的时候在纽约布鲁克林就读，大学初段在纽约州门罗大学打篮球，场均得到
content: 密西西比河谷州立大学（Mississippi Valley State University）一名来自中国的篮球运动员庞清方，因涉嫌签证过期被美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）拘留，目前仍关在路易斯安那州。 律师表示，庞清方从高中开始就在美国读书，后来进入大学篮球队，他自己都不知道签证过期了。目前正在申请紧急保释听证会，希望恢复学生签证，以便回校继续打球。 官方记录显示，庞清方身高6英尺9英寸（约2.06米）。高中的时候在纽约布鲁克林就读，大学初段在纽约州门罗大学打篮球，场均得到7.3分和3.8个篮板。随后被密西西比河谷州立大学招募。 一位知情人士表示，此事可能与学校方面文件处理延误有关，导致他的学生签证过期。 庞清方的律师马库斯·塞申斯（Marcus Session）表示，庞清方从门罗大学转到密西西比河谷州立大学的手续还不明朗，包括不知道自己住在哪里，因此他于9月29日试图搭乘飞机返回纽约，与一位家庭朋友团聚，这位朋友是庞最初的担保人，自他来美国后一直帮助指导他，没想到在机场被ICE逮捕了。 塞申斯说：“据说他不知道自己的签证已经过期了。他不知道该怎么办。” 根据ICE在线被拘留者信息，庞清方于9月29日被拘留后，现已转移到路易斯安那州里奇伍德（Richwood）的里奇伍德惩教所（Richwood Correctional Facility）。 密西西比河谷州立大学在一份声明中表示：“学校已获悉我校一名学生的情况，并对该学生的安危深表关切。该学生是密西西比河谷州立大学的全日制注册学生。校方正在密切关注事态发展，并将根据情况提供相应的支持。” 律师塞申斯说，庞对拘留已经感到疲惫。“他厌倦了被拘留。你知道，他厌倦了觉得自己像个罪犯。他就是这么表达的。” 塞申斯已提交紧急保释听证会申请，但表示法院系统尚未有进展。“我们只是想确保他有机会及时在移民法官面前陈述自己的情况。” 塞申斯表示，庞目前正在努力恢复学生签证。律师说，他希望重返校园并继续打大学篮球。“他想继续上学。他想打大学篮球。他想成为一个21岁的年轻人，努力为自己创造美好的生活。” 然而，国土安全部 (DHS) 的一位发言人在声明中表示，庞于 2023 年 11 月 17 日合法进入美国，获准停留至 2024 年 9 月 5 日，但他逾期滞留。“他接受了自愿离境，在被遣返前将继续被移民及海关执法局拘留，本届政府绝不会无视法治。”声明中说。 律师马库斯·塞申斯则说，庞是被迫在自愿离境文件上签字的，已申请紧急保释听证，希望尽快在移民法官面前陈述。 律师马库斯·塞申斯则说，庞是被迫在自愿离境文件上签字的，已申请紧急保释听证，希望尽快在移民法官面前陈述。

title: Lai's National Day speech steady, avoided provoking Beijing: Scholar - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te's (賴清德) National Day address maintained a steady stance on cross-strait issues while reaffirming Taiwan's commitment to peace, a political science scholar said Sunday, adding that the speech gave
content:
Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te's (賴清德) National Day address maintained a steady stance on cross-strait issues while reaffirming Taiwan's commitment to peace, a political science scholar said Sunday, adding that the speech gave Beijing no pretext for military coercion or provocation.

In the speech, titled "Taiwan's Future: A City upon a Hill, the Salt and Light of the World," delivered Saturday, Lai said Taiwan should bravely and confidently build a "city upon a hill" amid an era marked by wars, authoritarian expansion and rapid changes in the global order.

He said the vision represented an aspiration for Taiwan's future and a responsibility the country is willing to undertake, rather than an act of self-praise.

Chen Shih-min (陳世民), an associate professor in National Taiwan University's Department of Political Science, said Lai used the metaphor to highlight Taiwan's decades of efforts and achievements in becoming a model of democracy, freedom and economic development.

Chen said the speech reflected three key principles: maintaining stability, expressing a clear stance, and reaffirming Taiwan's role in safeguarding peace.

Lai has consistently adopted a pragmatic approach in major speeches, focusing on domestic achievements, Taiwan's international role and cross-strait relations, Chen said, adding that the latest address did not give Beijing an excuse for military coercion or provocation.

On U.S.-China relations, Chen said that while outside observers have often believed strategic competition between the two powers benefits Taiwan, Lai made clear that Taiwan also welcomes dialogue between Washington and Beijing to manage competition and reduce the risk of conflict in the Taiwan Strait.

Lai's reaffirmation that Taiwan is a guardian of peace, and that strengthening defense capabilities is intended to deter war rather than provoke conflict, also countered claims that Taiwan is a destabilizing force, Chen said.

Separately, Tsai Jung-hsiang (蔡榮祥), a professor of political science at National Chung Cheng University, said Lai's speech focused on three areas: reaffirming the definition of peace, clarifying historical narratives and strengthening ties with the international community.

Tsai said Lai emphasized that peace must be maintained through strength, including the development of asymmetric weapons, enhanced defense capabilities and cooperation with Indo-Pacific partners.

Tsai also cited Lai's remarks on Taiwan's economic performance, including projected annual economic growth of more than 11 percent, trade with the United States exceeding that with China and Hong Kong, and the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index reaching 49,000 points, making it the world's fourth-largest stock market in terms of market capitalization.

These figures showed that Taiwan's economy has continued to thrive and become more closely connected with the world despite reduced economic dependence on China, Tsai said.

(By Wang Yang-yu and Evelyn Kao)

Enditem/AW

title: Opposition leaders criticize DPP, Lai in National Day remarks - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Kuomintang (KMT) Chairperson Cheng Li-wun (鄭麗文) on Saturday urged voters to help her party win local elections in southern Taiwan, while Taiwan People's Party (TPP) Chairman Huang Kuo-chang (黃國昌) called on President La
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Kuomintang (KMT) Chairperson Cheng Li-wun (鄭麗文) on Saturday urged voters to help her party win local elections in southern Taiwan, while Taiwan People's Party (TPP) Chairman Huang Kuo-chang (黃國昌) called on President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) to promulgate laws passed by the Legislature.

The two opposition party leaders made their remarks separately on National Day.

Speaking at a flag-raising ceremony in Kaohsiung's Guomao community, Cheng accused the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) of heightening cross-strait tensions and undermining Taiwan's democracy.

She urged voters to support KMT candidates in Kaohsiung, Tainan and Pingtung County in the Nov. 28 local elections.

Cheng said peace across the Taiwan Strait was essential to safeguarding Taiwan's democracy, freedom and prosperity, arguing that dialogue and contact could reduce the risk of conflict and allow future generations to benefit from peace.

She also criticized the DPP government's energy policies and called for a resumption of nuclear power generation.

Economic growth should benefit older manufacturing industries, services, agriculture and fisheries, and not be concentrated in the high-tech sector, she said.

KMT Kaohsiung mayoral candidate Ko Chih-en (柯志恩), Tainan mayoral candidate Hsieh Lung-chieh (謝龍介) and Pingtung County magistrate candidate Su Ching-chuan (蘇清泉) attended the event, along with former Legislative Speaker Wang Jin-pyng (王金平) and other KMT officials.

In Taipei, Huang spoke before attending the National Day celebrations with eight TPP lawmakers.

He said the executive branch had no right to refuse to promulgate, or formally enact, laws that had cleared a third and final reading in the Legislature, or to refuse to implement them.

Huang was responding to Lai's call for lawmakers to swiftly review and pass the central government's 2027 budget and a supplementary budget for this year.

The Legislative Yuan, where the KMT and the TPP hold a combined majority, has not yet begun committee review of the budgets, Huang said, accusing Lai of creating the misleading impression that lawmakers were deliberately delaying their passage.

The TPP would support a budget that benefited the public but would not tolerate corruption or waste, he said.

Huang also urged Lai to honor his campaign pledge to build 130,000 social housing units and to address high housing costs, the rising cost of living and wealth inequality.

Lai has declined to promulgate several bills passed by the opposition parties.

The Cabinet has said the bills could strain the central government's finances, favor specific groups, or provide a legal basis for the government, political parties or the military to invest in private media outlets, potentially influencing their operations.

In one of the highest-profile cases, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) last year refused to countersign a law that would increase the share of tax revenue allocated to local governments, after raising doubts over its constitutionality.

(By Wang Cheng-chung and Sean Lin)

title: Store-in-store targets to revive Marikina shoes one step at a time
summary: Gen X who grew up wearing school shoes made in Marikina will remember how sturdy and seemingly indestructible they were despite the paces students put them through daily. For decades, Marikina Shoe Expo located in Cubao was the place their
content:
Gen X who grew up wearing school shoes made in Marikina will remember how sturdy and seemingly indestructible they were despite the paces students put them through daily.

For decades, Marikina Shoe Expo located in Cubao was the place their parents took them for a new pair at the start of the school year. That space has since been converted into a warren of small stores, restaurants and bars collectively known as Cubao Expo (Cubao X).

On Sept. 24, a new venue inside Spatio at Opus Mall was launched with the intention of reintroducing shoppers to Marikina-made footwear. Shoe Avenue is a partnership of Spatio with Zapateria and features a curated mix of independent Filipino footwear brands.

“We wanted to revive the glory days of Marikina’s shoe industry. We’re working closely with Unyx Sta. Ana of Zapateria on the brands to be featured at Shoe Avenue,” Martin de Leon, deputy general manager of Spatio told The Manila Times.

At the moment, Shoe Avenue occupies a sizable corner of the open-floor setup at Spatio. Unlike other department stores, Spatio features local independent brands ranging from bags and apparel to footwear and novelty items.

De Leon said that as a fifth-generation member of Zapateria, Sta. Ana already had an idea which Marikina-made footwear brands to tap and could deliver.

“I worked with her on the mix but she had a hand in coming up with the best assortment for the launch. There were several things to consider such as the capacity of a brand to produce since some of them are relatively small,” de Leon said.

The eight brands now available in store range from tiny Velcro sneakers for pint-sized clients from Wumwum to easy-to-slip-on flats for women from Posh Pocket and formal men’s shoes from Bucroe. Aside from Zapateria which anchors the space, the other brands include Alunsinag, Hayo, Bida Loca and Charis.

“Shoe Avenue is our way of honoring what came before us, drawing inspiration from what continues to be made today, and envisioning what Philippine footwear can still become,” Sta. Ana said in a statement. “Together with Spatio, we’re creating a platform where these stories can be experienced by more people.”

**Jelly for your feet**

Fun footwear brand Melissa launched two collections of colorful footwear including a new jelly set that pays tribute to the brand’s legacy as the jelly shoe pioneer, and its fall-winter 2026 collection set, Delirium.

Since launching its Aranha sandal in 1979, Melissa has transformed the classic fisherman’s sandal into a favorite fashion staple. The new Jelly Collection reworks this legacy with contemporary silhouettes. Each piece is crafted using the brand’s proprietary Melflex, a flexible cruelty-free and 100 percent material.

The year-end collection Delirium, meanwhile, is an attempt to push the envelope on where the brand’s signature jelly material can go next. Among the standout styles are the Melissa Aranha 79 II, a revival of one of the brand’s most beloved classics.

Other styles include slides, Mary Janes and T-strap sandals now available in store and online.

title: Donate to Support the Anti-Communist Film Festival Book, organized by Mark Judge
summary: A Book about Anti-Communist Movies We are on the eve of the announcement of the lineup at the first annual Anti-Communist Film Festival. Our headline film is **The Lives of Others.** I’ve spent over a year talking to Hollywood studios about
content:
A Book about Anti-Communist Movies

We are on the eve of the announcement of the lineup at the first annual Anti-Communist Film Festival. Our headline film is **The Lives of Others.**

I’ve spent over a year talking to Hollywood studios about licensing, visiting movie theaters to make my case (as you might expect, some were not thrilled with the idea), and finally getting a sponsor with the great folks at the Victims of Communism Foundation.

**There’s one more thing I’d like to do. I have a 20,000-word essay about my favorite anti-communist movies, and I'd like to publish it next year as a book and companion to the film festival.** Excerpts from the essay have been published on Hot Air, Chronicles, and on the Victims of Communism website. I’d like to publish the entire essay in paper format, something that people can hold. A samizdat, which during the Cold War was a book or pamphlet that was forbidden in communist countries and was passed around from hand to hand by dissidents.

**Most importantly, what I am calling Freedom’s Fury: A Guide to Anti-Communist Movies would be something that cannot be digitally erased.**

In his forthcoming book Reds: A Global History of Communism, journalist Paul Mason explores how communists want us to forget the past:

I do not want to “take control” of the memory of Marx, any more than the memory of the Russian Revolution or the Spanish Civil War. But I do want to prevent the Communist Party of China from taking control of them. Because, as [philosopher Walter] Benjamin reminds us: “not even the dead are safe from the enemy.” Just as postwar fascism fought to expunge the facts about the Holocaust, we are now seeing—in Putin’s Russia, Xi’s China, and political movements aligned to them in the global south—systematic distortions of the events described here. And it will get worse. In occupied Ukraine, new statues of Lenin are being erected. In Russia, plaques commemorating victims of the Great Purge are being torn down, and the last museum of the Gulag has been closed. In China, all critical writing about Mao is dismissed as “historical nihilism.”

Mason then notes how his own book may be censored:

As you read each chapter, I want you to imagine how it might be written in a future dominated by the brain-frozen clichés of Chinese communism. The Beijing propaganda machine has been busy eradicating the truth about the Tiananmen Square Massacre for nearly forty years. What might it achieve if given the unchallenged right to curate the facts about 1848, 1917, or indeed 1789? Far from being yesterday’s problem, the struggle for the truth about the history of communism may have only just begun. If so, Benjamin’s words on the eve of its darkest and finest hours bear repeating: Every line we succeed in publishing today—no matter how uncertain the future to which we entrust it—is a victory wrested from the powers of darkness.

**American communists would like nothing more than to censor the Anti-Communist Film Festival and forget it ever existed, even before it begins.**

title: 21 岁中国篮球运动员因赴美练球多年遭 ICE 拘留，父母同为运动员，如今面临遣返
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 10月8日，年仅21岁的中国篮球运动员因移民身份问题遭美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）拘留，目前被关押在路易斯安那州的一处移民拘留中心，甚至可能被迫离开美国。 这名球员就是来自深圳的庞清方（Qingfang Pang）。 庞清方身高约2.06米，从小学习篮球，十几岁来到美国，先后在美国高中和大学球队打球。 今年，他刚刚获得密西西比河谷州立大学（Mississippi Valley State University）的篮球奖学金，成功进入NCAA一级大学篮球队。 原本11月就要迎
content: 10月8日，年仅21岁的中国篮球运动员因移民身份问题遭美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）拘留，目前被关押在路易斯安那州的一处移民拘留中心，甚至可能被迫离开美国。 这名球员就是来自深圳的庞清方（Qingfang Pang）。 庞清方身高约2.06米，从小学习篮球，十几岁来到美国，先后在美国高中和大学球队打球。 今年，他刚刚获得密西西比河谷州立大学（Mississippi Valley State University）的篮球奖学金，成功进入NCAA一级大学篮球队。 原本11月就要迎来新赛季，谁也没想到，比赛还没开始，他却先被ICE拘留了。 事情发生在9月29日。 当天，庞清方正准备从密西西比州杰克逊市乘飞机前往纽约，却被ICE执法人员拦下。 他的律师Marcus Session表示，庞清方此前已经知道自己的学生身份出了问题，但一直没能解决。 他准备返回纽约，找一位多年来帮助照顾自己的家庭朋友，希望对方能够协助处理身份相关手续。 没想到，还没抵达纽约，他就被拘留了。 根据ICE的在押人员数据库，庞清方目前被关押在路易斯安那州里奇伍德（Richwood）拘留中心。 更麻烦的是，美国国土安全部（DHS）已经表示，庞清方同意自愿离境，目前正在等待离境安排。 根据DHS提供的信息，庞清方于2023年11月17日合法进入美国，但获准停留的期限在2024年9月5日就已结束。 不过，庞清方的律师对此有不同说法。 律师表示，庞清方是在ICE要求下签署了自愿离境文件，目前律师团队正在申请保释，希望能够争取机会解决他的身份问题。 与此同时，事件还牵出了两所大学之间的学生身份记录转移问题。 庞清方此前在纽约门罗大学（Monroe University）打球，今年才转入密西西比河谷州立大学。 对于持F-1学生签证的国际学生来说，转学不仅要办理普通入学手续，还必须完成SEVIS学生身份记录的转移。 然而，门罗大学透露，学校从今年春季开始就准备好转移庞清方的记录，只等新学校提出正式申请。 令人意外的是，直到10月7日，门罗大学才收到这份申请。 可见，庞清方9月29日被ICE拘留时，两所大学之间的相关记录转移手续尚未完成。 密西西比河谷州立大学已经发表声明，表示非常关心庞清方的处境，正在密切关注案件进展。 而庞清方的律师则希望能够尽快让他获得保释，重返校园。 对于已经在美国打球多年的庞清方来说，这场意外无疑打乱了他原本的人生计划。 而如果回顾他的成长经历，就会发现，这名21岁的中国年轻人，为了走上美国大学篮球赛场，已经努力了十多年。 庞清方来自中国深圳，出生于一个篮球家庭。 2023年1月，美国篮球媒体Pro Insight曾对他进行过一次专访。 当时，他还是一名正在美国高中打球的年轻球员。 在这篇采访中，庞清方用中文介绍了自己的家庭背景。 他的母亲曾经是中国省级篮球队的运动员，父亲也有篮球运动经历，还曾代表国家队参加过一次世界赛事。 父母都是篮球运动员，庞清方从小自然也与篮球结下了不解之缘。 他8岁开始打篮球，在深圳接受训练多年，随后来到美国，希望接受更高水平的训练和比赛。 来到美国后，他先后在新泽西州和纽约的高中就读，包括新泽西州的St. Benedict's Preparatory School，以及纽约皇后区著名的Christ the King High School。 后者在纽约高中篮球界颇具名气，培养过不少优秀球员。 庞清方还曾效力于纽约青年篮球俱乐部NY Renaissance，与多名受到美国大学篮球界关注的年轻球员一起训练、比赛。 对一个十几岁就来到美国的中国年轻人来说，这意味着不仅要适应新的语言和生活环境，还要努力适应美国篮球的训练方式、比赛节奏和身体对抗。 2023年接受采访时，庞清方曾表示，自己的目标是获得美国篮球名校肯塔基大学的招募机会，未来希望进入NBA，也不排除回中国CBA打球。 他认为，美国篮球的节奏和身体对抗更强，但可以通过训练弥补差距。身高超过2米的他，对自己的运球和投篮技术也颇有信心。 生活中，他喜欢玩NBA 2K游戏，最欣赏的球星是詹姆斯和威斯布鲁克。 高中毕业后，庞清方并没有如愿进入肯塔基这样的顶级篮球大学，而是去了纽约门罗大学继续发展。 2025—2026赛季，他代表门罗大学出战31场比赛，其中27场首发，场均贡献8.3分、4.4个篮板和1.1次助攻。 作为一名身高约2.06米的大前锋，他逐渐在球队中站稳脚跟。 今年，密西西比河谷州立大学向他提供了篮球奖学金，让他得以进入NCAA一级大学篮球联赛。 从8岁开始打球，到十几岁远赴美国，再到如今站上更高水平的大学篮球赛场，这条路他已经走了十多年。 原本，新赛季将在11月拉开帷幕，他也将迎来新的挑战。 谁能想到，距离开赛仅剩一个多月，他却因为移民身份问题被ICE拘留，甚至面临离开美国的可能。 十多年的努力，如今看来要因为一纸身份文件被迫中断了。

content: * 原文作者：黄宣颖（国立阳明交通大学医疗人类学家） * 本文系编译，请在这里阅读原文完整内容： https://madeinchinajournal.com/2026/03/09/political-depression-and-the-afterlives-of-neurasthenia/ 2019年夏天，“政治性抑郁”（政治性抑郁）开始进入中国网络话语，并在新冠疫情期间广泛传播。最初，这一说法与公众对武汉疫情应对失当的愤怒和绝望有关；此后，随着“动态清零”政策长期持续，人们的无力感与疲惫感进一步加深。与“丧”、“内卷”、“躺平”、“润”等网络热词类似，“政治性抑郁”表达了威权社会中不断累积的消极情绪。但它的特殊之处在于，既明确将痛苦指向政治，又借用了精神医学中的“抑郁”概念，试图说明个人的情绪困境可能具有政治根源。 这一概念并非单纯的网络流行语。其早期传播与青年活动人士小卡及其创办的公益组织有关。这类组织通过公众教育、心理社会支持等方式推动心理健康议题，强调精神疾病不仅是医学问题，也是社会问题。这种实践为讨论政治与心理困境的关系提供了空间。 然而，抑郁症成为中国社会熟悉的疾病概念，经历了漫长的历史转变。精神病学家兼人类学家阿瑟·克莱曼（Arthur Kleinman）1980年和1983年在湖南开展研究时，发现当地常见的诊断并非抑郁症，而是当时在西方已逐渐式微的“神经衰弱”。该病最初由美国医生乔治·比尔德（George M. Beard）于1869年提出，用来描述现代化社会中与疲劳、焦虑、失眠、易怒及身体不适有关的疾病。20世纪初，这一诊断传入中国，并在此后获得广泛认可。 克莱曼的湖南研究后来形成《社会起源：现代中国的抑郁、神经衰弱与疼痛》（ Social Origins of Distress and Disease: Depression, Neurasthenia, and Pain in Modern China ）一书。研究的重要问题是：不同文化中的精神疾病是否具有普遍一致的表现？他指出，中国患者往往通过疲劳、头晕和疼痛等躯体症状表达痛苦，而美国患者则更习惯直接诉说内心的悲伤与情绪困扰。因此，神经衰弱和抑郁症不仅是不同的诊断类别，也与各自社会中表达、理解痛苦的方式有关。 克莱曼进一步按照当时美国《精神障碍诊断与统计手册》第三版（ Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders , DSM-III）的标准重新评估神经衰弱患者，发现其中多数也符合抑郁症的诊断标准。这一发现被部分中国精神科医生理解为中国存在诊断错误，并推动了神经衰弱向抑郁症的转变。但克莱曼研究的意义并不止于诊断比较，更在于揭示痛苦的社会起源。 《社会起源》通过患者的生命经历，呈现了文化大革命期间的审讯、酷刑、公开羞辱、下乡经历以及家庭分离等政治创伤。克莱曼认为，个人在家庭、工作单位和人际关系中承受的长期压力固然重要，但文化大革命造成的宏观社会创伤具有更深刻的影响。神经衰弱的身体症状因而不仅是疾病表现，也可能承载社会记忆，成为人们在压抑环境中表达痛苦、间接批评现实的方式。 随着全球化的精神医学标准进入中国，抑郁症逐渐取代神经衰弱，并从专业诊断进入公共话语。然而，克莱曼担忧，新的生物医学诊断可能无法完整承载旧诊断所包含的历史创伤。1999年，他追问：神经衰弱的消退，是否也意味着人们忽略了中国政治失败带来的深层疏离、失去正当性与内心痛苦？ 疫情期间兴起的“政治性抑郁”，似乎重新提出了这一问题。它借助抑郁症的语言，表达源于政治现实的疲惫、绝望与无力。不过，小卡也曾指出，这一概念逐渐成为吸引流量的标签，其内涵可能被稀释，难以支撑持续而深入的讨论。 原文作者最终提醒，“政治性抑郁”虽然广为流行，但其政治化潜力仍然脆弱。它能否像克莱曼夫妇所期待的那样，成为唤回历史记忆的工具，使被压抑的社会痛苦重新获得表达，仍有待观察。

content: 美国司法部宣布，正寻求撤销两名涉及中国间谍活动人士的美国公民身分，包括曾在美国海军服役、因间谍罪被定罪的魏金超（Jinchao Wei），以及因涉嫌为中国政府充当未注册代理人而被判刑的佛罗里达州居民李平（Ping Li）。两人被列入司法部近期提出的40宗撤销入籍案件，是特朗普（Donald Trump）政府上台以来规模最大的一批相关诉讼。 司法部指出，相关案件属民事程序，目前仍在审理中，法院尚未就责任或是否撤销公民身分作出裁决。司法部也强调，提出诉讼本身并不会自动导致当事人失去美国公民身分。 针对魏金超的诉讼9月30日向加州南区联邦地方法院提出。魏金超2025年8月因间谍罪及违反出口管制法规被陪审团定罪，今年1月被判处200个月徒刑，即16年8个月。不过，陪审团同时判他自然化入籍诈欺罪名不成立。 检方在审判期间指出，魏金超曾服役于美国海军两栖攻击舰“埃塞克斯号”（USS Essex），期间向一名中国情报人员提供照片、技术手册及其他敏感的海军资料，并收取超过1万2000美元。 司法部目前主张，魏金超在2022年5月透过军人服役途径取得美国公民身分时，隐瞒了自己的犯罪活动。此外，司法部也指出，他在尚未完成5年符合荣誉条件的服役年限前，即以“不符合荣誉条件”的方式退伍，并以此作为撤销其入籍资格的依据之一。 李平的案件则于10月1日向佛罗里达州中区联邦地方法院提出。李平2024年11月因共谋在未通知美国司法部长的情况下，替中国充当代理人，被判处4年监禁。 根据李平的认罪协议及法院文件，检方表示，他承认至少自2012年起便接受中国国家安全部指挥，并向中方提供与中国异议人士、民主倡议者及法轮功修炼者有关的资料。此外，他也曾提供从电信及资讯科技业雇主处取得的资讯。 美国司法部认为，李平的相关行为显示，他在申请入籍时未能符合美国宪法所要求的效忠条件，因此有理由寻求撤销其公民身分。 美国法律规定，如果入籍是以违法方式取得，或申请人隐瞒重大事实、故意提供虚假陈述，法院可依法撤销其自然化公民身分。不过，司法部提出民事诉讼后，仍须经法院审理及裁决，不能直接取消公民资格。 司法部公布这批案件前一天，联邦调查局（FBI）才在洛杉矶国际机场逮捕中国出生的美国公民张婉莹（Zhang Wanying），指控她替北京充当未注册代理人。执法人员指称，她曾在西雅图监视一名台湾政府官员的近亲，外传是台湾总统赖清德儿子。不过，相关指控目前尚未经法院证实，张婉莹也不在司法部此次公布的撤销入籍案件名单内。 司法部表示，此次40宗案件是特朗普政府迄今最大规模的撤销入籍诉讼行动，反映当局正加强处理被指透过隐瞒或不实陈述取得美国公民身分、其后又涉及危害美国国家安全活动的案件。

# CNN: US, China discussing reciprocal nuclear site visits

2 hours ago

*   [Copy link](javascript:void(0);) [![Image 11: Share](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_share.svg)](javascript:void(0);)

US media outlet CNN says that the administration of US President Donald Trump has discussed beginning reciprocal nuclear site visits with Beijing amid concerns over China's rapid military buildup.

CNN on Tuesday quoted a source familiar with the matter as saying that the idea was initially proposed by China earlier this year.

The source reportedly said visits to the US Department of Energy national labs and to China's equivalent fities were discussed by officials. The source was also quoted as saying the US would be open to discussing visits to nuclear testing sites.

In September, the White House announced that Trump advocated for trilateral arms control negotiations between the United States, Russia and China. But CNN quoted a US official as saying Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping did not discuss the possibility of site visits during their summit talks last month.

The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute has said in its latest report that the US was estimated to have 5,042 nuclear warheads, while China likely has 620.

The US Defense Department released a report last year saying that China is on track to have over 1,000 nuclear warheads by 2030.

Register for Event Outcompeting China Through Technology, Industry, and Allied Power with Senator Dave McCormick In-Person Event Hudson Institute October 16, 2026 Register for Event Share: Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Caption Senator David McCormick (R-PA) speaks to an audience on June 2, 2025, in Boston, Massachusetts. (Getty Images) 16 October 2026 FRIDAY 2:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. In-Person Event Event will also air live on this page.   Inquiries: nhuergo@hudson.org . Register for Event Speakers: Senator David McCormick United States Senator, Pennsylvania Mike Gallagher Distinguished Fellow Mike Gallagher is a distinguished fellow at Hudson Institute. Full Bio Share: Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the White House on September 24 amid uncertainty across the Indo-Pacific. Leader-level diplomacy will continue at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, in November and the Miami Group of 20 summit in December. Yet Washington needs to balance these negotiations with the need to maintain deterrence across the region. Outcompeting China in artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and critical supply chains will require close, integrated cooperation with American allies, including Japan and the Republic of Korea. Cooperation is essential to maintain America’s lead in advanced technology, turn AI innovation into economic gains at home and abroad, rebuild defense industrial capacity, and reduce Chinese leverage over global economic chokepoints. Join Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA), who recently visited Japan and Korea, and Distinguished Fellow Mike Gallagher for a fireside discussion on United States–China relations, the role of allies and partners in America’s Indo-Pacific strategy, and how the US can harness technology, industrial capacity, and allied strength to prevail in the defining strategic competition of our time.   Related Events See More See More Related Research See More See More

title: 习近平访美特殊休息时间让他与特朗普的峰会缩短数小时
summary: 华尔街日报：据熟悉此次访问筹备工作的人士透露，中国官员提出了一项不同寻常的要求，即美国方面应在习近平与特朗普总统举行峰会期间，满足习近平的休息需求，这罕见地揭示了这位73岁领导人日益显现的身体限制。 发表时间： 03/10/2026 – 14:35 7 分钟 浏览时间 2026年9月25日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平及其夫人彭丽媛在美国华盛顿特区国家档案馆博物馆入口处合影。 REUTERS – Kylie Cooper 中方主要的要求
content: 华尔街日报：据熟悉此次访问筹备工作的人士透露，中国官员提出了一项不同寻常的要求，即美国方面应在习近平与特朗普总统举行峰会期间，满足习近平的休息需求，这罕见地揭示了这位73岁领导人日益显现的身体限制。 发表时间： 03/10/2026 – 14:35 7 分钟 浏览时间 2026年9月25日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平及其夫人彭丽媛在美国华盛顿特区国家档案馆博物馆入口处合影。 REUTERS – Kylie Cooper 中方主要的要求是在白宫西翼为习近平安排一间私人房间，供他在活动间隙休息，且仅允许其妻子彭丽媛陪同。中国代表团的其他成员均不得使用这个被称为“休息室”的房间——就连习近平的办公厅主任蔡奇也不例外。 知情人士透露，在习近平启程访美大约一个月前，其先遣团队拒绝原定于9月24日（峰会唯一完整的一天）举行中美领导人工作午餐的安排。今年5月，特朗普访问北京时，两位领导人曾在中南海领导人驻地共进了工作午餐。 约5小时空档 知情人士称，北京官员向美方表示，希望习近平在华盛顿访问期间有更多时间休息。结果是峰会议程中出现了约五小时的空档。在仅持续了不到两天的访问中，这段空档显得格外漫长。 此外，知情人士称，中方在习近平抵达当晚没有安排任何活动，而在访问的最后一天（9月25日），这位中国领导人仅在美国国家档案馆内停留了大约10分钟——远少于美国官员的计划。 当然，习近平刚结束从北京出发的约14小时飞行，时差这一因素足以解释部分日程调整，尤其是在抵达当晚。 而现年80岁的特朗普今年早些时候赴北京参加峰会时，其团队安排了为期两天的行政时间段。美国政府的活动摘要显示，特朗普利用部分空闲时间接受了福克斯新闻的采访。 习近平享受了国是访问的全部礼遇：21响礼炮、美国战斗机和隐形轰炸机的空中飞行表演，以及一座大型白头鹰雕像作为礼物。但知情人士透露，在这些精心策划的场面背后，他的团队正在根据他能站立多长时间、能走多远以及何时需要休息来安排行程。 曾任美国国家安全委员会中国事务高级主任、在小布什政府期间组织过三次国事访问的丹尼斯·怀尔德表示，这种在候见室等候的安排史无前例。他说，在安排日本首相小泉纯一郎、澳大利亚总理约翰·霍华德以及习近平的前任、中国国家主席胡锦涛的访问时，“我们从未做过类似的事情。这很不寻常。” 华尔街日报这篇报说，关于习近平健康状况的质疑并非新鲜事。2019年他结束欧洲之行后，曾出现过类似的猜测——当时有视频显示他走路时略有跛行，并扶着椅子的扶手来保持平衡。六年多过去了，习近平依然牢牢掌控着中国。 而习近平的健康状况的影响远不止于其个人福祉。他掌握的权力超过了自毛泽东以来的任何一位中国领导人，且尚未指定继任者。中国实际上并没有一套制度化的程序来选拔一位同时拥有习近平这三个重要头衔的领导人：中国共产党总书记、国家主席和中央军事委员会主席。

title: Recovering from Religion Support Group Meeting - South Carolina Chapter, Wed, Oct 28, 2026, 6:30 PM   | Meetup
summary: The South Carolina Chapter Recovering from Religion support group will meet the fourth Wednesday or each month at 6pm Eastern. **This meeting will be held in-person at the We Are Family community room located at 3265 North Carolina Avenue,
content:
The South Carolina Chapter Recovering from Religion support group will meet the fourth Wednesday or each month at 6pm Eastern. **This meeting will be held in-person at the We Are Family community room located at 3265 North Carolina Avenue, Suite 202 in North Charleston.** Attendees are welcome to share, but may also decide to remain anonymous if they so choose.

Light refreshments will be provided. Please contact one of the event hosts if you have any questions or concerns ahead of the meeting.

The primary focus of a Recovering from Religion support group is to provide ongoing support to individuals as they let go of their religious beliefs. This transitional period is an ongoing process that can result in a range of emotions, as well as a ripple effect of consequences throughout an individual’s life. As such, the support meetings are safe and anonymous places to express these doubts, fears, and experiences without biased feedback or proselytizing.
 We are here to help each other through this journey.

There is no cost to attend this support group but, if you feel so inclined, donations can be made at [www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate](http://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate)

If you'd like to provide confidential feedback for this meeting, click here [https://forms.gle/yhC7frShmyrRS56G7](https://forms.gle/yhC7frShmyrRS56G7)

If you find you need to talk with someone before the next support meeting, RfR has a hotline and online chat for that express purpose. Call [844-368-2848](http://tel:+18443682848/) to speak with someone. To chat online, go to [www.recoveringfromreligion.org](http://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/) and click on the green chat bubble in the lower left corner of the site.

If you are in need of professional help, we can recommend the Secular Therapy Project to provide options to connect with a professional therapist. All therapists have been thoroughly vetted by our organization and offer only evidence-based and non-religious treatment. Connect with them at [www.seculartherapy.org.](http://www.seculartherapy.org./)

Like what RfR does? Why not volunteer! There are quite a few options. Head over to [RfR Volunteer Form](https://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/volunteer) for more info.
